english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds carry dry air that quickly sucks moisture out of pepper leaves faster than the roots can draw water from the soil, causing the plant to shed leaves to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei ajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow much taller when I plant them where groundnuts grew last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa babaoo beni midu amɛ yɛ he ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to feed the maize that comes after.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farm soil get hard and stop producing good crops if I burn the dry bushes every year before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni ekpaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji mishã jwɛi lɛ daa afi dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning bushes destroys useful soil organisms and burns away organic matter that keeps the soil soft and moist. Over time, this leaves the soil dry, packed hard, and lacking nutrients.
ga: Tsoi ni ashã lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni amɛshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ewa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves at the very bottom of my corn stalks turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the corn plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil, so it pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my young maize leaves filled with small ragged holes and brown powder inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekumɔ ni eyɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf funnel of young maize during the day to eat the tender leaves and leaves behind its waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai amli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ni amɛshi jwɛi.

english: Why are there tiny green insects gathered under my cabbage leaves, making the leaves wrinkle up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ? Abua naa yɛ mi kaabeji baai lɛ ashishi Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: Those are aphids, tiny pests that suck the liquid nutrients out of the leaves. As they feed, they cause the cabbage leaves to weaken, curl, and turn yellow.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Amɛhaa cabbage baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water, because extreme heat damages the flower pollen and prevents fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ, ni ehaaa aduawai afee.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and soft if I leave them in the ground after heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains start, cassava plants stop storing starch in their roots and start using that energy to sprout new leaves, making the tubers watery and easy to rot.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ baakpa starch ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Ni obɔi nakai hewalɛ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni okɛwo baai heei. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ oya.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand easily underground. Hard, packed soil or stones block their path, forcing the tubers to bend or stay small.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ gbɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo efeɔ bibioo.

english: Why do the cut branches on my cassava or tomato plants rot if I prune them during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni afo yɛ mi-cassava loo tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mifo amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fresh cuts on plants are like open wounds on human skin. Wet weather carries invisible germs (bacteria and fungi) straight into these open plant tissues, making the plant sick and rotted.
ga: Pilamɔ hee ni yɔɔ tso nɔ lɛ tamɔ pilamɔ ni agbele yɛ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ helai ni anaaa baa. (bacteria kɛ fungi) boteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni agbele nɛɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do chemical crop treatments actually protect my vegetables from getting sick?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ tsei ahe nii lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crop treatments work like medicine on the plant's surface. They destroy invisible germs before those germs can enter open parts of the plant and cause rot or leaf sickness.
ga: Tso tsamɔi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa yɛ tso lɛ hiɛ. Amɛfiteɔ helai ni anaaa lɛ dani amɛboteɔ tso lɛ fãi ni agbele lɛ amli ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo baai hela baa.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly if they get scratched or cut during digging?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsɔ mli loo afo mli yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: A yam's skin acts as a barrier keeping out soil infections. Once damaged, the opening allows rot-causing germs to enter and decay the yam from the inside out.
ga: Sweet potato hewolo tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji efite Openings lɛ haa helai ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. ni ogbala sweet potato lɛ mli kɛjɛ mli kɛya kpo

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shield themselves from harsh heat. Shrinking their leaf surface helps the plant trap moisture inside so it does not dry out.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he. Baa lɛ hiɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when heavy rain leaves standing water on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu tara ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water floods the soil for too long, the roots choke, stop taking in nutrients, and cause the leaves to yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa amɛná niyenii kpakpai. ni oha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the afternoon sun even when the soil around them is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it up. The plant droops temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, usually recovering as the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu kroko ni baafite lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu.

english: Can using dirty gutter or river water to irrigate my crops cause them to get diseases?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji loo faa mli nu ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba?

english: Yes, dirty water contains harmful germs that can enter natural leaf openings or tiny root wounds, spreading rot and stem diseases through your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ abote adebɔɔ mli baai lɛ amli loo pilamɔi bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli, ni egbɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ fitemɔ helai ashwã kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I plant them in full sunlight without plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong sun. Planting fast-growing plantains nearby provides essential shade and moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: When planted too tightly, crops compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into thick stems and big cobs, the plants stretch upward to reach light.
ga: Kɛ adu babaoo tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baawo tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji amli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, tsei ɔmɛ pee jã konɛ la ɔ nɛ ba mi.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry weather, pests, or poor soil nutrients. Shedding extra flowers helps the tree save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni fata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi wala mli.

english: Should I throw away the outer skins and shells of my groundnuts after shelling, or can I mix them back into my farm soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashɛrɛ mi-peanuts lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mafɔ̃ beni migbe naa lɛ sɛɛ? Aloo manyɛ makɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Groundnut skins and shells break down into valuable organic matter. Plunging them back into your field feeds beneficial soil organisms, adds nutrients, and helps the soil hold water for your next crop.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie ŋmɔ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii afata he ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it true that planting groundnuts in my field makes the soil richer for my maize during the next planting season?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmei lɛ shweremɔ be ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, groundnuts belong to the legume family. They pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots, leaving natural nitrogen in the soil that helps future crops like maize grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii weku lɛ mli. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa wɔsɛɛ tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems under the soil instead of growing nuts up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ashishi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ŋmeii yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a special growth habit called pegging. Once the flower is pollinated, the stem bends down and pushes into the earth so the nuts can safely develop underground away from heat and birds.
ga: Peanuts yɛ dalɛ su krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fixation. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ okpoi bɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my groundnut plants fold up and close tightly every evening when night falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ daa gbɛkɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: This natural leaf movement helps the plant conserve moisture, regulate its temperature during the cooler night, and protect itself from heavy night dew.
ga: Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli baa lɛ nyiɛmɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kudɔɔ dɔlɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ ni obuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ bɔ́ ni naa wa ni baa shi gbɛkɛ lɛ he

english: Why do groundnut plants spread low across the dirt instead of growing tall like corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts grow low to form a dense green cover over the soil. This acts like a living mulch that shades the ground, suppresses weeds, and stops the hot sun from drying out the soil.
ga: Peanuts daa shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbeɔ jwɛi, ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my groundnut plants turning light yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on key nutrients like nitrogen or iron, or the ground is overly waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo dade bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my harvested groundnut pods turn out completely empty inside when I crack them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pods ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ mli kɛ migbele amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty pods—often called 'pops'—happen when the soil lacks calcium or moisture during the period when the underground pods are filling up, causing the seed inside to fail to form.
ga: Pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi pods lɛ eyiɔ obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ko.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to dig up my groundnuts so they do not rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii koni amɛkafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Observe the leaves; when they start turning yellow and dropping off, dig up a sample plant. If the insides of the shells have dark brown veins and spots, your groundnuts are mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tso ko he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: If I leave my freshly harvested groundnuts in the strong sun to dry, will the heat spoil the seeds inside?
ga: Kɛ mishi ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ koni amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani latsaa lɛ baafite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Gentle sun drying is necessary to remove moisture and stop mold growth during storage, but leaving seeds out in extreme heat for too long can destroy their ability to sprout when planted next season.
ga: Hulu ni egbiɔ blɛoo he hia koni ejie fɛ̃i ni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashi dumɔwui yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ adu yɛ be kroko mli lɛ.

english: Can I safely feed the leftover green leaves and stems of my groundnut plants to my sheep and goats after harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha tooi kɛ tooi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, groundnut vines and leaves are rich in protein and make high-quality animal feed that helps goats and sheep grow healthy and gain weight.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei kɛ baai lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ protein ni eji niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa tooi kɛ tooi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow so much faster between June and September compared to other times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa oya waa yɛ June kɛ September teŋ lɛ? kɛ akɛto afi lɛ mli bei krokomɛi ahe

english: During June to September, the major rainy season provides continuous water combined with warm temperatures. This triggers rapid photosynthesis, allowing the maize plants to absorb soil nutrients quickly and grow at their peak speed.
ga: Yɛ June kɛyashi September nyɔji lɛ amli Nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ yɛ nu ni yaa nɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ. Enɛ haa fotosintɛsis baa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn dry and yellow as soon as the rains slow down in September?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ September mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have massive leaves that lose water rapidly. When soil moisture drops at the end of the rainy season, the plant intentionally sheds its outer leaves to conserve remaining water for its stem and growing fruit cluster.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Tsei lɛ baajɛ amɛtsui mli amɛshwie amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ aduawai akui ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I get my cassava plants to grow bigger tubers so I can harvest a much larger yield this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji? Bɔni afee ni anyɛ akpa nibii babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Cassava tubers expand best in loose, well-drained soil. Mound the soil high around the stems, avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen which creates too many leaves, and clear surrounding weeds early so root energy isn't stolen.
ga: Cassava shishifãi daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Okɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ato ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he, ni baaha tsei lɛ ahe afee shoo. ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee mli Bɔni afee ni akaju shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ.

english: Flower drop happens when plants experience stress from sudden heat changes, uneven watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping soil moisture consistent and planting flowers nearby to attract bees helps fruit set properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni agbala ŋmɔtɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ koni aduawai lɛ afee nɔ ni sa.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly humid conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow onto the trunk helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba tso lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need for green growth. It can also mean the soil is waterlogged from heavy rain, which suffocates roots and stops them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ miibolɔ kɛmiitao nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why do market prices for my crops drop so low immediately after the main harvest period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jara ni akɛheɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest at the same time between July and September, the market experiences excess supply. Because fresh crops spoil quickly, buyers pay less; storing crops properly allows you to sell later when supply drops and prices rise.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli yɛ July kɛ September teŋ lɛ. Jarayelihe lɛ baaná nibii ni fa fe nine. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei heei fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli beni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from naturally getting eaten by weevils while stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ahe be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moisture and oxygen. Dry your maize until the grains are very hard, then store them in airtight hermetic bags which suffocate insects and keep moisture out without needing heavy chemicals.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye kɛji amɛná fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Gbimɔ o-corn lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli, ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops whenever heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local soil. They have aggressive root systems that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops, which is why clearing weeds early gives crops a fair chance.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops still look weak even after I spent money putting fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so roots can drink it in. If applied during dry spells or on highly acidic soil, the fertilizer gets locked up in the dirt and the plant roots remain unable to digest it.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛ akɛwo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo shikpɔŋ ni acidity babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ.

english: How can I tell if the maize seeds I bought from the local market seller are genuine improved seeds or just regular grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ loo dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa?

english: Genuine certified seeds usually come in sealed, official packages with a government certification tag or logo. Regular market grain might look identical in the bag, but certified seeds are tested to germinate evenly and produce much higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ baa yɛ kotoku mli ni maŋ nɔyeli he odaseyeli okadi loo okadi. Ekolɛ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayelihe lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ kome yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Shi akaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo kwraa.

english: I planted pepper seeds two weeks ago, but only a few sprouted. How do I know if the seeds were bad or if I planted them wrong?
ga: Midu pepper dumɔwui otsii enyɔ ni eho nɛ. Shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ kwɛ̃. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ehiii loo midu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ?

english: You can test seed quality before planting by placing ten seeds in a wet cloth for a week; if fewer than seven sprout, the seeds are old or poor quality. If the seeds pass this test, then poor sprouting in the field is likely due to planting them too deep or inconsistent soil moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ ahe okwɛ dani odu kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli otsi kome lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui ni shɛɛɛ kpawo kwɛ̃ɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo amɛhe ehiaaa. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ ho kaa nɛɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ ni ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my newly sprouted cassava plants showing yellow leaves even though the stem cuttings looked fine when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani nine lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lolo beni adu lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young cassava usually mean the planting material was infected with a hidden virus or that excess water is suffocating the young roots. Stems can look healthy on the outside while carrying disease internally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ yucca bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ emɔ tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ amli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso ko baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ yɛ be mli ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ eji hela tsɔne kɛjɛ emli.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into fruit. What is happening to them?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Mɛni ba a nɔ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Protecting the plants with partial shade and keeping soil moisture steady prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛ hulutsoo fã ko kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin with tiny, empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? He ko ni nɔ ko bɛ?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. This overcrowding causes them to stretch tall and weak, leaving them without enough energy to fill out full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel on the tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in heavy shade and high humidity. It is a crop disease rather than a sign of poor soil, and clearing excess shade trees and weeds helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Eji tso hela fe shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ he okadi. Ni tsei kɛ jwɛi ni haa hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Will applying extra fertilizer make my crops grow bigger and produce twice as much yield?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer can burn root systems and cause rapid leafy growth without producing heavy cobs or fruits. Crops only need the correct balance of fertilizer at the right growth stage.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ ada oya ni ekɛ cob loo aduawai ni tsii baaa. Tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa pɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni sa mli.

english: I sprayed chemical pesticide on my cabbage, but caterpillars are still eating the leaves. Did the chemical vendor sell me fake product?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie kaabɛji lɛ anɔ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ lolo. Ani tsofafeelɔ lɛ miihɔɔ amale nibii mii?

english: Not necessarily. Pests often hide under leaves or deep inside cabbage heads where sprays cannot reach, or they may have built resistance to that specific chemical. Using incorrect water mixture ratios also reduces how well the spray works.
ga: Jeee nakai kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ashishi loo yɛ kaabe yitsei amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Aloo amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ nakai tsofa pɔtɛɛ lɛ. Nu ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings wilt and die within a day after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi kome mli beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved suddenly into hot, bright sunlight. Exposing seedlings to direct sun gradually over a few days before planting, and transplanting late in the afternoon, helps them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ transplant shock mli kɛji trukaa Move kɛtee hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo hulu la mli blɛoo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli dani odu ni okɛwo he kroko yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my harvested cassava root turn dark and rot within just two days of digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ ediŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots naturally spoil quickly after harvest because exposure to air triggers a rapid breakdown process inside the root. Processing or consuming cassava within 48 hours, or keeping unpeeled roots buried in damp soil, stops this quick spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fiteɔ oya. Kasava he nitsumɔ loo yeli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli loo shishifãi ni ajieee amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa nɛkɛ fitemɔ ni yaa nɔ oya nɛɛ.

english: Why do buyers sometimes reject my cocoa beans even when they look healthy from the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mi-kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ?

english: Buyers test cocoa beans for hidden chemical residues left behind by unapproved or poorly timed sprays. If chemical traces remain inside the bean, international chocolate makers cannot buy them due to safety regulations.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa kookoo yibii lɛ amɛkwɛɔ kɛji tsofai ni eshwɛ ni akɛtee kɛtsɔ spray ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsofai ni eshwɛ lolo yɛ kɔfi yibii lɛ amli lɛ Maŋsɛɛ tsokolatefeelɔi nyɛŋ ahe yɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai ahewɔ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a farm product leaves no residue on my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ extension official ko kɛɛ okwaayeli mli nibii ko eshiii nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: It means the product breaks down safely after protecting your plant, leaving no chemical traces on your cocoa. This keeps your harvest safe to eat and makes it easy to sell to buying companies.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ obu otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, nɔ ni akɛfee lɛ baafite shweshweeshwe. ni okɛ tsofa ko akashi yɛ o-cocoa lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ. ni eha efee mlɛo akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ aha nitsumɔhe ni heɔ lɛ

english: Is it safe for me to spray my cocoa trees right before I harvest the pods?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ dani akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: No, spraying right before harvest leaves heavy chemical residues on the pods because the product does not have enough time to wash away or break down, making your crop unsafe for market.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani akpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baashi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ nɔ ni akɛfee lɛ enáaa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafɔ loo ebaafite. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why should I use researched products on my cocoa instead of buying whatever is cheapest at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nibii ni atao mli lɛ atsu nii kɛ mi-kookoo lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he nɔ́ nɛ e he jua wa pe kulaa ngɛ jua a nɔ ɔ.

english: Researched products are tested specifically to ensure they improve yield without damaging your trees, harming the soil, or leaving chemical traces that prevent licensed buying companies from purchasing your beans.
ga: Akwɛɔ nibii ni ataoɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni ana akɛ amɛhaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni amɛfiteee tsei, amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ, loo amɛshiii tsofai ni tsiɔ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni amɛheɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahe o-nuts lɛ.

english: Why does applying fertilizer to my cocoa farm make the pods grow heavier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Fertilizer replaces nutrients that have been washed away from the soil, giving the tree the energy it needs to feed developing pods so they grow larger and yield heavier beans.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are hungry and need plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-cacao lɛ ni ehe miihia ni eye tsei niyenii?

english: When cocoa trees lack nutrients, their green leaves begin turning yellow, flowering drops drastically, and any pods that grow remain small and weak.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ Ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ. Fofɔi lɛ baa shi waa. Ni ŋmeii ni miida lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by nutrient shortages, insect damage, or lack of water. Proper soil feeding and spray protection help flowers mature into strong pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ hebuu yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads easily when air humidity is high. Applying approved protective cocoa sprays before heavy rains helps stop the fungus from killing your pods.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ kookoo naa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo ohe dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafite o-pods lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees give me fewer pods when the branches grow too bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ be mli ni amɛniji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overgrown branches block sunlight from reaching the main trunk where flowers grow, and they trap excess moisture that causes pod-rotting diseases to spread faster.
ga: Niji ni eda fe nine lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso titri ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ he. ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni haa pod rot hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ mli

english: Why do young cocoa trees struggle to grow when planted in wide open fields without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Shade crops like plantains protect young cocoa from direct sun and preserve soil moisture so the trees can establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than your main crops and will steal the fertilizer you apply, preventing your crops from getting the nutrients they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ, ni amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by intense heat, prolonged dryness, or attacks by insects like mirids. Lack of shade or poor soil nutrients can also cause the tree to shed flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Gbimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ tamɔ ashwishwɛi, hulutsoo ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or severe stress from high heat and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa.

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when the soil holds too much water without proper drainage during heavy rains, allowing soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ titri kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Planting cassava too close forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small tubers instead of a big harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii waa baa yɛ ŋmaa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The sunlight helps the leaf produce food, which is then sent down to build big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni abaamaje shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my young crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot days, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers to save water and energy until weather conditions become cooler and safer.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshi fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee mlɛo ni shweshweeshwe.

english: Plantain trees fall over when pests like banana stem borers or tiny root worms weaken the roots underground, leaving the heavy plant without a firm hold in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi tamɔ banana tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo shishifãi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ba. Ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow leaves. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away from the soil, or weeds might be stealing it. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛjeee nakai lɛ, jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aju lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted around them to block the harsh sun and keep the soil moist until their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but why are the tubers underneath so small when I harvest?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen food in the soil or too much rain early on, it uses all its energy to grow tall branches and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below. Trimming extra branches can encourage the plant to swell its roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha ŋmei niyenii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shishijee mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ atsake tso lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Water your tomatoes regularly at the roots so the plant stays calm and turns those blossoms into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Okɛ nu awo otomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe daa koni tsei lɛ afee kpoo ni amɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks as soon as they start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛji ebɔi kwɔɔ pɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food. If the vines lie flat on the hot soil, they can easily catch diseases, get covered by weeds, and will not produce big, heavy yams underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛji wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, helai baa amɛnɔ oya. jwɛi ehà nɔ ni ebaawooo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to cut before sending it to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afolɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Plantain is ready to cut when the individual fingers lose their sharp, flat edges and become round and plump, but are still completely green. Cutting them at this stage ensures they stay firm enough during transportation and ripen nicely later.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ beni inchi fɛɛ inchi ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Shi fɛɛ ji eŋɔli lolo. Kɛji akɛ afo amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ, ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the top leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice. Spraying the leaves with soapy water or diluted neem oil helps control these insects so new leaves grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ pepper tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni ekɛfee baai heei lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts improves the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to help crops like maize grow bigger in the next planting season.
ga: Peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmei, ni amɛdara yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right when they are about ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ tswaa trukaa beni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split open when they absorb a sudden lot of water after a dry spell. The inside grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst. Watering your farm evenly throughout the growing season prevents this.
ga: Kaaba yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji amɛmu nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. cause rupture Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers turn soft and rot when heavy rains fall during flowering time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi gardenia fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall washes away the pollen needed to make pods and creates wet conditions where fungal mold quickly attacks the tender flowers. Timing your planting so the cowpeas flower near the end of the rainy season keeps the blossoms dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ pollen ni he hiaa koni afee pods lɛ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni ŋmei lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ oya. Be ni akɛduɔ koni tsina fɔfɔi lɛ abɛŋkɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting to get a good harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he kɛjɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu koni maná yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Spacing maize seeds about 25 to 30 centimeters apart within rows and 75 centimeters between rows gives each plant enough space, nutrients, and sunlight to grow strong stalks and produce full cobs.
ga: He ni ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ ŋmeii amli kɛ sɛntimita 75 yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Is it really necessary for me to put stakes or sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni makɛ tsei loo tsei ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight and prevents soil-borne diseases, which helps the plant manufacture enough energy to build larger underground tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei tsu nii kɛwo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them out in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sun. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees during their first two to three years to protect their delicate leaves from burning and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baabu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Excessive leaf growth with small tubers usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or if the plants are heavily shaded, causing the cassava plant to focus its energy above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa Enɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ lɛ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Leaving too many shoots (suckers) forces the main plant to share water and soil nutrients with them, leading to smaller bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures larger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi suckers (tsoji) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ nakai tsei lɛ agba nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ suckers ni mli wa kome loo enyɔ pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii babaoo aba.

english: What does it mean when the lower leaves of my maize start turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Abɛi lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ V su mli. Mɛni enɛ ɔ tsɔɔ?

english: A yellow V-shape pattern starting from the leaf tips on lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil, meaning the plant needs nitrogen fertilizer or manure to continue growing healthy green leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant nutrients in the soil through their roots, leaving rich fertilizer behind for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, usually caused by a lack of calcium uptake in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and then gets flooded.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my pepper plants without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when soil moisture fluctuates too drastically, or due to a lack of proper nutrients, which causes heat stress and prevents pollination.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ loo yɛ niyenii kpakpa ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa ni etsĩɔ pollination naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my garden egg plants curling up and feeling sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni kɛ́ mɔ ko ta he lɛ, enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and sticky residue are clear signs of tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, which weakens the plant and stunts fruit growth.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies miinu nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daamɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly at first before suddenly sprouting big green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli dani trukaa lɛ, baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: In the early weeks, crops focus their energy underground building strong roots. Once the roots are established, the plant quickly absorbs nutrients and water, causing the upper leaves to expand rapidly into a deep green canopy.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛma shishitoo ni wa. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ ja lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oyayaayai aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell if the leafy green color of my crops means they are truly healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Healthy crops display an even, rich green color across their leaves without yellow edges, dark spots, or curling, which shows they are getting enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jieɔ su eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kpo yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ amli ni amɛhe bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to plant my crops in straight rows with exact spacing instead of scattering seeds freely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni gbɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã heyeli mli lɛ

english: Precise spacing ensures that each plant gets its fair share of sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors, making weeding easier and resulting in bigger harvests.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa egbɛfaŋnɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ sũ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Enɛ haa jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa.

english: Is it beneficial to plant two different types of crops together in the same farm field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting compatible crops together, like maize and cowpeas, helps cover the soil surface, prevents weed growth, improves soil fertility, and provides a secondary crop if weather conditions change.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ naa Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa tsei ni ji enyɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsake.

english: Why does my farm land look so different and clean once the crop canopy closes over the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ feɔ srɔto ni ehe tse waa kɛ́ sũ ehà ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: As crops mature, their leaves spread out and meet each other to cover the ground, which shades out weeds, prevents topsoil from drying out, and gives the farm a uniform, healthy green look.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ shade Tsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa koni ekagbi. ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does thorough soil preparation before planting change how well my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake tsei lɛ adalɛ?

english: Proper land preparation breaks up hard soil, buries weeds, and allows roots to penetrate deeply, helping the land hold moisture and support strong crop development.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli, efuɔ jwɛi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What key features make harvested crops attractive and easy to sell to buyers at the local market?
ga: Mɛni ji sui titrii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ mlɛo ahaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Market buyers prefer produce that is uniform in size, vibrant in color, free from insect damage or disease marks, and harvested at the right stage of maturity.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ nibii ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, ni su mli tse, ni kooloi fiteee loo efiteee nɔ ko. ni akpaa yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli

english: How does careful planting and weeding directly affect the price I get at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Careful farm management prevents crop stress, leading to larger, cleaner, and higher-quality fruits and grains that command top market prices compared to stunted or damaged yields.
ga: Okwaayeli nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe haomɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai kɛ ŋmaa lɛ daraa, amɛhe tseɔ, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ. ni hiɛ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ akɛto nibii ni egbɔjɔ loo efite lɛ ahe.

english: How can my family divide farm tasks so we complete planting accurately before the rainy season starts?
ga: Te weku lɛ baaja okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ bɔni afee ni adu nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Dividing labor—such as having one person measure and dig planting holes while another places seeds and covers them—ensures precise planting depth and covers more land quickly.
ga: Nitsumɔ mlijaa, tamɔ ni mɔ kome aaasusu ni efo dumɔ bui yɛ be mli ni mɔ kroko lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ mli ni ehaa nɔ. Ebaaye ebua bo ni odu nii kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: What visual signs on my farm show that my planting methods are working well?
ga: Okadi ko ni anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛji gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mikwɛɔ nii lɛ miitsu nii loo etsuuu nii.

english: A successful field will show even crop height across the rows, minimal weed growth, vibrant foliage, and consistent plant populations across the whole land.
ga: ŋmɔ ni ye omanye lɛ baatsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔlɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ fioo lɛ baa ni hiɛ wala kɛ tsei ayibɔ ji ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it always so dark under mature cocoa trees, and is that healthy for my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ewoɔ duŋ yɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani no hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ?

english: Mature cocoa trees form a dense leafy canopy that naturally blocks sunlight to suppress weeds. However, if it becomes too dark, sunlight cannot reach the inner branches, which reduces flower formation and overall pod yield.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ, hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm has too much shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo?

english: If your farm stays dark and very damp even in the afternoon, or if you see very few flowers and new pods forming, your farm has too much shade and needs branch pruning or thinning of nearby trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ waa ni edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli po. Aloo kɛji ona fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be babaoo ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ loo afee amɛ bibii.

english: Should I keep tall forest trees inside my cocoa farm, or clear them all?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahã koo mli tsei kakadaji lɛ ahi mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo majie amɛ kwraa?

english: You should keep a few tall shade trees to protect your cocoa from harsh dry winds and extreme sun, but remove excess trees so enough sunlight reaches the cocoa leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei kakadaji ahi shi. Shi tsei fioo komɛi koni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa egbiɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, mo kpa tsohi nɛ a he hiɛ ɔ konɛ hulu la nɛ sa nɛ e su kookoo ba ɔmɛ a nɔ.

english: Which animals usually bite or damage green cocoa pods on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ loo amɛfiteɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Squirrels, monkeys, rats, and fruit bats frequently chew open cocoa pods to eat the sweet white pulp inside, especially if the farm is near wild bush or overgrown areas.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ŋmɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii koni amɛye loo yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ jwɛi, kooi loo hei ni tsei ekwɛ̃ fe nine.

english: How do I stop squirrels and small pests from eating my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa?

english: Keeping your farm weeded, clearing overgrown brush around the perimeter, and harvesting ripe pods immediately will remove hiding spots and reduce pest attraction.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ni akpa jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni mɛi ehiɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛjɛ mli, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi.

english: How can I tell whether an animal or an insect is damaging my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo kooloi bibii miifite mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Animals leave large chew marks, split husks, or hollow pods on the ground, whereas insects like mirids leave small dark punctures, sap oozing, or cause young pods to shrivel.
ga: Koolooi shĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ he okadii wuji, ŋmɔtɔ ni ekumɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo muji yɛ shikpɔŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ glase ni edɔ lɛ shiɔ okadii bibii ni tsuɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ muji. loo eha ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbo

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the farm stays very dark and damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ waa lolo ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Dark and humid conditions help fungal spores like Black Pod disease spread quickly. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight in, keeping the farm dry enough to prevent rot.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli efɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi bɔ ni sa koni ekafite.

english: Why do I need to prune my cocoa trees regularly instead of letting them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli daa moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches, opens up the farm for light and airflow, makes it easier to spot pests early, and encourages the tree to put energy into growing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. Gbelemɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ kane kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana tsɛŋemɔ helai mra. ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ awo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli

english: Why is my cocoa yield low even though my trees are tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibiiwoo lɛ faaa yɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ mi-cocoa tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai?

english: When cocoa trees grow too tall and bushy, energy goes into leaf growth instead of pod growth because light cannot penetrate to trigger flowering along the trunk.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da tsɔ ni efee ŋmɔji lɛ, Hewalɛ yaa baai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la nyɛɛɛ abote mli ni ekanya fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How do I protect young cocoa seedlings from dying in the hot sun during their first year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need partial shade to survive. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides cover from direct heat until they mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to make leaves green and healthy, or that the soil is waterlogged, preventing roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia koni baa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which prevents individual plants from growing strong leaves and full-sized produce.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ni tsiɔ tso fɛɛ tso naa koni ekawo baai ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo baa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward direct sunlight to create food, which then travels down to build and grow a large underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aya nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei agbo ko ni eda.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade from taller trees or shade crops like plantains to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does the soil in my vegetable garden dry out so quickly during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture rapidly from uncovered soil. Covering the dirt around your plants with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, shields the soil from dry air and traps moisture near the plant roots.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ oya. Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ Tsei ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi he, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long due to poor soil drainage, starving the roots of air and allowing soil fungi to infect the plant.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛyeɔ tsei anɔ helai

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani eyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dry spells, or excess nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa he haomɔ mli. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the whorls of my young maize stalks and eating the fresh leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the soft center whorl of maize plants to feed on tender growing leaves before the cob develops.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii dani ŋmãa lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck the sap out of leaves, often transmitting viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, egbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees snap or fall over at the root when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees naturally have shallow roots, and pests like root nematodes or stem weevils can weaken them further, making the heavy plant topple over easily once fruit cobs form.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ root nematodes loo stem weevils baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji aduawai ŋmeii ba.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden poles to climb on instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for big underground tubers. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes leaves to light while keeping them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow bottom leaves mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what is left from old bottom leaves to feed top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why don't my groundnuts need as much chemical fertilizer as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa mi ŋmãa lɛ tamɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which forms partnerships with tiny natural organisms in the soil to pull nitrogen gas out of the air and turn it into plant food.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ tsei aniyenii.

english: What happens to my soil if I burn the bush before planting instead of clearing it by hand?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishã mi tsei bibii lɛ dani midu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ minine baajie amɛ?

english: Burning destroys the top layer of organic matter that holds moisture and feeds good soil organisms. Over time, burning leaves your soil dry, hard, and easily washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niyenii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ewa, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho oya.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my sandy farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Manure acts like a natural sponge. In sandy soil, it binds the small particles together so water and nutrients stay in the root zone longer instead of washing deep underground.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ekɛ nibii bibii fiɔ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi shishifã lɛ he be babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How do I know which way to push cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni ooofee otsi ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look at the small raised nodes where leaves used to grow; these 'eyes' must point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes weak shoots and reduces your tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni awó nɔ ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ‘hiŋmɛii’ nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or drought stress. The plant lets go of its blossoms to conserve energy and survive until conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when dry spells and heavy rains make it hard for roots to absorb calcium steadily.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium lɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the center funnels of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni tɔmɔ yɔɔ he akɛ maye bu bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mikɛwo mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide in the central whorl of young corn. They target tender leaf tissue where the plant is growing newest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ateŋ. Amɛ kwɛɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ, ni no ji he ni tso lɛ dalɛ hee lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa seedlings from intense heat and keeping the soil moist until the trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants rolling up into tight tubes during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: When the weather is too hot and dry, maize plants roll their leaves inward to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating into the air. It is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to survive dry spells.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ, Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the farm without draining, it smothers the roots by taking away oxygen, which allows soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Be mli ni nu yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu homɔ bɛ mli. Nu eyiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve into a form that plant roots can drink up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn and damage the roots, and the nutrients will stay locked away from the plant.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite. ni niyenii mli hewalɛ baafee nɔ ni kɛ tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ

english: Why is it important for me to pick off black, rotten pods from my cocoa tree even if they are already ruined?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii diji ni egboi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛfite momo po lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads through rain splashes and wind. Leaving ruined pods on the tree allows the fungus to keep producing spores that infect healthy pods nearby.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekumɔ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ hela.

english: Why do the maize seeds I stored from my last harvest sprout poorly compared to fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds stored in warm or damp farm structures lose their internal energy and are often damaged by invisible insect larvae, while certified seeds are properly dried and treated to ensure strong sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato ni akɛto ŋmɔ mli tsũi ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛmli hewalɛ ni bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Yɛ be mli ni agbiɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.
