english: When temperatures get extremely high or water is irregular, tomato plants experience stress. To save their own energy to survive, they drop their blossoms instead of producing tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tomato tsei lɛ baahao. koni amɛkɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi No hewɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tomato.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds the current crop and enriches the soil for the next planting season.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ hewalɛ, ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Why must I train my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for expanding the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tuber lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii helai akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do small insects ruin my harvested grain inside the storehouse even when I don't see any bugs on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite ŋmaa ni akpa yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Insects often lay invisible eggs inside the grain while it is still in the field. When warm, damp conditions occur inside your storage barn, those eggs hatch into hungry larvae that feed on the stored crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmãa mli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ba otsu lɛ mli lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops when rainwater collects and stays on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by suffocating them of air. Without air in the soil, the roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and eventually decay.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ amɛmumɔ ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I protect my crop field from getting flooded during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nu afua akabote mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can dig shallow drainage channels around and through your farm to redirect excess water away from your crops, and plant on raised soil beds so the plant roots stay above standing water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ mli ni mli ekwɔɔɔ koni okɛjie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. ni odu tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my root crops like yam and cassava spoil inside the soil before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Root crops spoil underground when the soil holds too much excess moisture for long periods. Damp, waterlogged soil encourages fungal and bacterial rot that destroys the tubers before you can harvest them.
ga: Tsei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baagbe ŋmeii lɛ ahe hewalɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil has too much water for planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil in your palm; if water squeezes out easily like a soaked sponge, the soil is too saturated for planting and needs time to drain so seeds do not rot.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko yɛ onine nɔ. Kɛji nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tamɔ spunji ni efɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu tsɔ ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ nii, ni ebaabi ni be atsɔ mli koni dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: If I start planting late after the rain season has already begun, will my crops still grow well?
ga: Kɛji oje dumɔ shishi yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Planting late often lowers your yield because crops may not get enough steady water during their critical flowering and fruiting stages before the dry season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ odu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning pale yellow after a week of continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsi kome ni nugbɔ enɛɔ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away soil nutrients like nitrogen and soak the root zone, making it impossible for the plant to draw up foods needed to keep its leaves healthy and green.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha ebaa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli.

english: Why do crops planted on low, flat farmland often grow poorly compared to crops on gentle slopes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ okwaayeli hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ gɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Low, flat farmland easily traps runoff water, leading to soil compaction and root rot, whereas gentle slopes allow excess water to flow off naturally while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋshɔ lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to contact an agricultural extension officer about my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko agba sane yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: You should contact an extension officer as soon as you notice strange plant behavior, unexpected pest attacks, or persistent drainage problems that you do not know how to solve on your own.
ga: Esa akɛ oya o-extension agent lɛ he pɛ kɛji ona tso lɛ subaŋ ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa trukaa. loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he naagbai ni yaa nɔ ni oleee bɔ ni ooofee otsu naagba lɛ he nii bo diɛŋtsɛ

english: What kind of sample should I take to the agriculture station when my crops are dying?
ga: Mɛɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ esa akɛ mikɛya okwaayeli he lɛ beni miŋmɔshi nibii miigbo lɛ?

english: Bring a fresh, whole plant showing both healthy and sick parts, including leaves, stems, and roots with soil attached, so officers can accurately diagnose the issue.
ga: Okɛ tso hee ni eye emuu ni tsɔɔ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ hela fɛɛ, ni baai, shishifãi, kɛ shishifãi ni sũ ekpɛtɛ amɛhe lɛ fata he lɛ atsu nii. Bɔni afee ni nitsulɔi lɛ anyɛ ana naagba lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crop varieties survive heavy rainfall and waterlogged fields better than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu afua naa jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties have stronger, shallow root systems or bred-in tolerance that allows them to endure wet conditions, while standard varieties succumb quickly to root rot.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ yeɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ oya lɛ anɔ.

english: This usually means your soil is low on nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow, so when it is lacking, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ Tsei lɛ elaaje lɛ, amɛgbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make my next maize crop yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantains protect them from harsh heat and wind until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What is causing the small holes in my maize leaves and ragged edges on the young shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides in the center whorl of maize plants and feeds on soft young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni darako lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed, usually due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy. Lifting them on stakes keeps leaves off the wet ground, reduces disease, and helps the plant produce bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ awo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaaa baai lɛ agbo yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills the air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the cassava roots and allowing water-loving fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni amɛha ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ atutua ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients and water, which leads to smaller bunches. Removing extra suckers directs all energy into the main tree's fruit.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii Ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso titri lɛ yibii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weed growth.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Are there tiny living things in the soil that can make my crops sick just like diseases make humans sick?
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ jɛmɛ. Ani shikpɔŋ ni haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ hela lɛ mli yɛ tamɔ hela ni haa adesai yeɔ hela lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, just like germs cause cholera in humans, there are microscopic organisms like fungi, bacteria, and viruses in the soil and air that attack plants, causing them to rot, wilt, or die.
ga: Hɛɛ, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɛ kolera baa adesai anɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ ŋmei, muawai, kɛ muawai yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni tutuaa tsei. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbo, ebaagbi, loo ebaagbo.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops get dark spots and die even when I do not see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi?

english: Diseases are not always caused by visible insects. Tiny fungal spores or bacteria carried by wind or rain can settle on leaves, feeding on the plant and causing spots, blight, or leaf decay.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kooloi bibii ni anaa lɛ kɛ hela baa. Fungal loo bacteria spores bibii Mɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ kɛyaa lɛ baanyɛ akpɛtɛ baai ahe, amɛye tsei ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet conditions. The fungus spreads easily through water droplets and rapidly destroys wet cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni efɔ lɛ oya.

english: Is it good to soak my maize seeds in water for a long time before planting them?
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ awo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ani ehi dani adu?

english: Soaking seeds for a few hours can help them germinate faster, but leaving them in water for too long deprives them of oxygen, causing the seeds to rot and fail to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo lɛ ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Shi kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛnáaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛwaaa.

english: Why do my planted seeds decay in the ground instead of growing when the soil is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Seeds need both water and air to sprout. When soil stays flooded or overly wet, the seeds choke from lack of air and get attacked by water-loving soil fungi, causing them to rot before sprouting.
ga: Nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ ni hydrophilic soil fungi lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Can using dirty water from a polluted stream to water my vegetables make the crops unsafe to eat?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛwo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ?

english: Yes, dirty water contains harmful bacteria and germs that can stick to leaves and fruits, which can cause illnesses like cholera or stomach fever in people who harvest and eat those vegetables.
ga: Hɛɛ, muawai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ akpɛtɛ baai kɛ aduawai ahe yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha mɛi ni kpaa nakai aduawai lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ aná helai tamɔ kolera loo musu mli hela.

english: Do my crops suffer if I do not give them fertilizer, like a person who goes without food?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná he sɛɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli tamɔ mɔ ko ni niyenii eshɛɛɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Yes, plants need essential nutrients from the soil to stay healthy. Without sufficient soil nutrients or added fertilizer, crops become weak, stunted, and unable to yield good fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ, amɛbaagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plant leaves turn yellow and weak even when they receive plenty of sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ enine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are damaged by disease and cannot absorb food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo helai efite shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start to spoil and rot so quickly after I dig it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ oya beni mifo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots continue to breathe and react to air. Damage to the root skin allows micro-organisms and oxygen to enter, causing rapid internal rotting within two to three days.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ amɛmu ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔ. Nɔ ni fiteɔ shishifã lɛ hewolo lɛ haa nibii bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fitemɔ baa oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: What causes my stored maize to turn soft and moldy when kept in a damp room?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli?

english: Dampness creates a perfect environment for microscopic mold and fungi to grow on stored grains, breaking down the seeds and making them unsafe for human consumption.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni baakwɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. efiteɔ dumɔwui ni ehaaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai niyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, the plant starves and moves the limited nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth at the top. This causes the bottom leaves to turn yellow from the tip inward and dry up.
ga: Beni ŋmãa bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe koni eha ŋmãa heei ada yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbee mli kɛyaa mli ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very small tubers when planted under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo agbo shishi lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct, strong sunlight to make energy through its leaves and store it as starch in its roots. In deep shade, the plant uses all its energy stretching upwards to reach for light, leaving no extra energy to form big tubers.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia Yucca koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛgbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni ená la. ni efiteee hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛfee yitso agbo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes the pollen inside tomato blossoms to dry out and become sterile. Because the flowers are not pollinated, the plant naturally sheds them instead of wasting energy on unfertilized blooms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afɔko fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ,.

english: Why are the bottoms of my sweet peppers turning dark and rotten before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboi dani amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually due to irregular watering. When soil dries out completely and then gets soaked, the plant cannot transport calcium smoothly to the fruit tips.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni edɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and yield fewer peppers when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves shade each other from sunlight. This stress starves the plants and stops them from growing full branches and flowers.
ga: Beni pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekakwɛ eniji kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and greener than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, aggressive root systems designed to steal water and food faster than domesticated crops. When fertilizer is added, weeds absorb the nutrients first unless they are cleared out before feeding the crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ miiwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ, jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. ja ajie amɛ dani aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young maize plants get chewed up overnight even though I see no insects on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ shwie shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ? Ni minaaa kooloi bibii yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide deep inside the central funnel of the plant or in the soil during the hot day to avoid heat and birds, coming out only at night to feed on tender leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ kɛ okpoi lɛ ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ pɛ koni amɛbaye baai bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die in the afternoon heat even when the soil has plenty of moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or fungal root rot, which damages the plant's internal water channels. Even if the soil is wet, the damaged roots cannot pull water up to the leaves, causing the plant to collapse in hot sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni haa tsei amli nu gbɛi lɛ fiteɔ Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does covering my vegetable soil with dry grass or leaves help crops survive hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mulching with dry grass creates a protective blanket that shades the dirt from direct sunlight, keeps the root zone cool, and prevents soil water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ atade ni buɔ mɔ he ni buɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: Why do my yam vines produce much bigger tubers when I give them wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ bulbs ni da kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tso tso ko ha lɛ ni ekwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up into the open air and sunlight so they can catch maximum light without tangling or rotting on the ground, enabling the plant to produce more energy and store it in the underground tuber.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Enɛ baaha ená la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni ekɛ ehe akawo mli loo egboŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my seeds staying on top of the soil in my nursery bags instead of going inside easily when I try to push them in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ grow bag lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabote mli mlɛo beni mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mikɛ amɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: If the soil or sand mixture in your nursery bag is packed too tightly or has dried out into a hard crust, seeds cannot enter smoothly. You should moisten the soil beforehand and gently loosen the top layer so the seed can be set at the correct depth.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ loo ŋã ni akɛfutu yɛ grow bag lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ loo egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ klɛŋklɛŋ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋwɛi fã lɛ afee blɛoo koni dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ he ni sa.

english: Why is it necessary to poke holes in the bottom of my plastic nursery bags before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo bu yɛ plastic kotokui ashishi dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Drainage holes allow extra water to escape from the bag. Without these holes, water collects at the bottom and drowns the roots, causing seed rot or killing your young plants.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛji bu nɛɛ bɛ Nu lɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ nubu lɛ shishi ni eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akpɔtɔ loo eha tsei bibii lɛ agboi.

english: Why do experienced farmers mix clean sand with topsoil when preparing nursery bags for seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ ŋã ni mli tse futuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛsaa dumɔwui kotokui kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing sand with topsoil creates a loose texture that does not compact into hard blocks. This allows water to drain properly and makes it easy for delicate root sprouts to spread and absorb nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã futu sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋãi ni wa. Ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ jaa ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ mlɛo

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to place my seeds during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: A general guideline is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its width. Planting too deep prevents the seedling from reaching the surface, while planting too shallow causes the seed to dry out or get eaten by birds.
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ elɛɛmɔ lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I bought are good quality and will actually sprout before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani adu?

english: You can perform a simple float test by placing your seeds in a container of clean water. Seeds that sink to the bottom are generally healthy and full, while floating seeds are usually dry, damaged, or empty inside and will not germinate.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee buoyancy kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oookɛwo nu ni mli tse mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyiɔ obɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ egbi, efite, loo nɔ ko bɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Seeds need the right balance of water, warmth, and oxygen to break open. If the soil is completely dry, excessively wet, or planted too deeply, the seeds will either stay asleep or rot before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu, dɔlɛ, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa ni efɔ tsɔ loo adu mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ loo amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and turn yellow when left under direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have fragile stems and undeveloped roots that cannot manage severe heat. Placing temporary shade, like palm fronds, over them protects them from burning until they grow stronger roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni waaa kɛ shishifãi ni edako jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛ́ okɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo, tamɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ wo ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akashã lɛ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do my young crop stems fall over and break right at the ground level even when I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by damping-off disease, a fungal problem that attacks young stems when the soil stays too wet and hot. Reducing water slightly and ensuring good airflow around the plant helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tsei bibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ. Nu lɛ ni oooshɛ shi fioo ni okwɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abɔle Nitsumɔhe lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ohe.

english: What causes the lower leaves of my growing crops to turn yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is waterlogged. The plant moves available nutrients to its newer upper leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titri, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know the right time to move my young crops from nursery bags into the main farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔji akwɛmɔ kotokui lɛ amli kɛya ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for transplanting when they have grown 3 to 5 strong leaves and developed a firm root bundle, usually about 3 to 4 weeks after sprouting depending on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3 kɛyashi 5 ni amɛfee kui ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ

english: How do I know if my land is fertile enough to grow a good maize crop this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Dark, soft soil that crumbles easily and holds moisture usually shows good fertility. If weeds like wild sunflower grow tall and green on the land, it is a good sign that the soil has enough natural nutrients for your maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiteɔ oya ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jieɔ fɔmɔ kpakpa kpo kɛji jwɛi tamɔ koo mli hulutsoo tso lɛ dara ni efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji okadi kpakpa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the cleared bush on my farm land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning cleared bush destroys useful organic matter and beneficial insects in the soil. Allowing cleared grass and leaves to rot back into the dirt feeds the soil, keeps it moist, and makes it stronger for your crops.
ga: Brɔshi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aná hewalɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni oha onibii lɛ awa

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. This usually happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients from the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye abɛi tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up in the hot afternoon and open up again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons to save water from evaporating into the air. It is a natural protection mechanism plants use to survive intense sun until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu akaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant produce tall stems and bushy leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are too shaded, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in roots. Proper spacing and balanced nutrients force the plant to develop larger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ehiɛ hulutsoo tsɔ Yɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ baaha bulbs agboi aba.

english: Crowded crops fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting seeds too close results in thin, weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food. Proper staking leads to bigger tuber growth underground and prevents soil diseases from infecting the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Staking ni sa baawo shikpɔŋ shishi tuber babaoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ he hewalɛ. Ni tsi helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do young plantains need so much shade when I first put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo be babaoo beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have weak roots and dry out easily under harsh sunlight. Shade protects them from heat stress until their root systems grow strong enough to pull water from deep in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when plants suffer from inconsistent watering. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the bloom instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ naa nu ni ejaaa be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer on my crop land when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve properly so crop roots can drink it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots and damage your crops instead of helping them grow.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow before the crops are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for plant growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo eji akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi? Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, while legumes like beans and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil naturally. Planting them after maize helps replenish the land so your future crops yield better.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Abɛi ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni eha he lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ yibii kpakpai kɛha owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in bright sunlight and need protection. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that shade young cocoa, keeping them cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni abu he. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning your trees to let in sunlight and fresh air helps keep the pods dry and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight, which supplies energy to grow large tubers under the ground. Raising the vines off the dirt also protects the leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ jɛɛhe ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are there small worms eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a widespread pest in Ghana that feeds on the central growing leaves of maize. Spraying recommended insecticides or applying local remedies like sand and ash directly into the plant whorls early can stop them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛ eshwa Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ loo akɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai tamɔ ŋã kɛ sũ tsuɔ nii. Eboteɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ shishijee. lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete heavily for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Proper distance gives roots enough room to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If your seeds germinate and the soil dries out before regular rain starts, the fragile young seedlings will die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagboi.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my field reduce the amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, plant food, and light from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the nutrients in the soil go straight into growing your crops instead of useless grass.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, tsei aniyenii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ jwɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why can't I just save and plant the small yams from my previous harvest instead of buying new ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makpa ŋmeii kɛkɛ ni madu ŋmeii bibii ni jɛ ŋmeii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahe ehee?

english: Reusing yams from previous harvests often carries hidden pests and diseases built up in the soil, which leads to weaker crops and smaller yields in the next season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers always tell us to buy fresh seed yam every planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔhe ŋmeii heei daa be mli ni okwaayeli yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh seed yams are grown in clean, protected environments without diseases, ensuring your crops start strong and yield larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Aduɔ sweet potatoes ni ji dumɔwui heei yɛ he ko ni he tse, ni abuɔ he ni hela bɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does the quality of my seed material really affect how big my yams will grow?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ saa sweet potato lɛ dalɛ he?

english: Yes, clean and disease-free seed material allows the plant to use all its energy for growth, resulting in bigger, smoother, and healthier yams.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ahe nibii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa dalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni dara, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yams get smaller and less healthy every year if I keep using seeds from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Seeds gradually collect diseases and pest damage over time when kept on the farm, which weakens the crop's ability to produce good harvests over successive years.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baabua helai kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa fiofio yɛ be mli ni akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo yibii kpakpai yɛ wɔsɛɛ afii amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young plants look so healthy in the nursery but get diseased when I transfer them to the open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi hela ba amɛnɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ ko ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery areas are protected from insects, but open farmland contains naturally occurring pests that attack young crops and spread diseases to them.
ga: Abuɔ he ni akwɛɔ gbekɛbii yɛ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe. Shi ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli baa. ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How do small insects on my farm actually cause my crops to get sick?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela?

english: Insects act like carriers; when they feed on sick plants, they carry the germs and inject them into healthy crops while feeding on them.
ga: Kplukai feɔ amɛnii tamɔ vectors. Kɛ amɛye tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ Amɛhiɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ hu.

english: Why are insects and crop pests much worse out in the open field than in specialized seed production houses?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ehiii kwraa yɛ ŋmɔji amli fe dumɔwui pɔtɛɛi amli lɛ?

english: Specialized seed production facilities use barriers to keep insects out, whereas open farms naturally attract wild insects searching for food.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei ni he esa waa lɛ kɛ gbɛtsii nii tsuɔ nii koni amɛtsi kooloi akabote mli. Beni ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ gbalaa koo mli kooloi bibii ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ,

english: What is the main reason my neighbor's yams are growing much larger than mine this season?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo titri ni ha mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara fe minɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Using certified, clean seed material free of field pests gives crops a major advantage, allowing them to grow full-sized and healthy compared to crops planted with old seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni he tse ni yɔɔ odaseyeli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa waa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛdalɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui momoi duɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I protect my yam crops from getting infected with diseases right after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hela amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji midu?

english: Starting with clean, fresh planting material ensures your yams are healthy enough to withstand the natural pests present in the farm soil.
ga: Je shishi kɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ehee koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ o-sweet potato lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akpee adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: If I plant clean seeds in a field that already has insects, will I still get a good harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni he tse yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli lɛ, ani maná yibiiwoo kpakpa lolo?

english: Yes, starting with disease-free seed gives the crop a strong immune start, helping it grow big and healthy even if field pests are present later on.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni hela bɛ mli lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa. Ye obua lɛ ni etsɔ agbo ni ehiɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green leaf growth. When the plant does not get enough nitrogen from the soil, it steals it from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni etsɛ lɛ koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas will make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans have small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ jwɛi abɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under hot weather, traps moisture so you water less, prevents weeds from sprouting, and slowly rots into rich plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ekɛ nu ŋmɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged because saturated roots cannot get oxygen to breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rain drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛha mumɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: During the Harmattan, dry air and hot sun make water evaporate quickly from leaves. Cocoa trees shed leaves to conserve moisture and survive, but keeping shade trees on your farm helps protect cocoa leaves from drying out.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛhi shi. Shi hulutsoo ni akɛhaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a sturdy branched bamboo pole keeps it standing.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes leaves to light and keeps them off damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli, ni ehaaa sũ ni mli efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aya nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and balanced fertilizing encourage the flowers to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from young leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the plants early with neem oil or recommended sprays controls these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ abaanyɛ akudɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crop grow slowly and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early allows your crop roots to absorb all available water and plant food without sharing.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛja.

english: Why am I harvesting so few bags of cocoa this season compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpa kookoo kotokui fioo pɛ yɛ afi nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Low yields usually happen due to irregular rainfall, aging trees, nutrient-depleted soil, or diseases like Black Pod that ruin the beans before they mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ hewɔ lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa. tso shikpɔŋ momo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ ŋmeii dani amɛdaraa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dry and shrivel up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree sheds extra pods it cannot support due to drought, low nutrients, or early pest attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ okadi nɛɛ ji ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso ko fite ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ, niyenii ni faaa loo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ.

english: Why is my neighbor getting more cocoa bags from the same size farm as mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nine shɛɔ kookoo kotokui krokomɛi anɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ ko ni dalɛ tamɔ mi nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Higher yields come from regular pruning to let in light, removing diseased pods early, keeping weeds down, and applying proper soil nutrients at the right time.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ tsei ni afoɔ daa koni akɛha la lɛ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni okɛ sũ mli niyenii ni sa awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if dark spots on my cocoa pods mean the tree has a bad disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hela ni naa wa?

english: If dark spots spread quickly over the pod and turn it black, it is Black Pod disease. The fungus spreads fast through rain splashes if infected pods are left on the tree.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya yɛ pod lɛ mli fɛɛ ni etsɔ ediŋŋ. tsɔɔ akɛ eji black pod hela Fɛ̃i lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ mli kɛji akɛ pods ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ tee nɔ ehi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: If I harvest cocoa pods that look infected, can I still ferment and sell the beans inside?
ga: Kɛji obua kookoo ŋmeii ni tamɔ nɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa Ani abaanyɛ afee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Diseased pods usually contain flat, moldy, or rotten beans. Mixing bad beans with healthy ones ruins the quality of your whole harvest and lowers your selling price.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni mli ewo muji, loo ni efite yɛ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni ehiii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaafite onibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ, ni ebaaha jara ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What makes cocoa diseases spread so quickly from one part of my farm to another?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome kɛyaa fã kroko nɔ?

english: Fungal diseases spread through rain drops bouncing off infected pods, wind, uncleaned harvesting tools, or insects moving between trees.
ga: Agbɛɔ ŋmeii hela lɛ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa nibii ni he tseee lɛ anɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ amɛhe?

english: Flowers fall off when trees are stressed by dry spells, lack essential nutrients, or when microscopic insect pests attack the delicate blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao yɛ ŋmɔtɔ hewɔ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii waa tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves to save water in hot weather, but severe leaf loss can mean your farm lacks enough shade trees to protect the cocoa from direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Shi baai ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ tsei ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ abu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: How often should I harvest my ripe cocoa pods during the main season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: Harvest ripe pods every two to three weeks. Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes them to overripe, attract pests, or catch diseases.
ga: Kpaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere fe nine. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba

english: Why is it important to cut off old or sick branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tso niji ni egbɔ loo ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead wood where diseases hide, reduces shade overcrowding, and allows sunlight and air to flow through the tree to keep pods healthy.
ga: Tsoi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi yɛ he ni helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo be mli ni oha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees easily burn and die under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together so I can get more food from my small piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and space to grow strong and yield more harvest overall.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant cassava on the exact same plot every year, why do my tubers keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ miyitso lɛ miifee bibioo kɛmiifee bibioo lɛ?

english: Cassava draws a lot of nutrients out of the soil to grow its tubers. Planting it in the same place without resting the land or adding compost drains the soil, leaving fewer nutrients for subsequent crops.
ga: Kassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛkwɛ cassava ŋmeii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli nu atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ wɔsɛɛ yinɔi ni baaba lɛ amli lɛ faaa.

english: How do I know it is truly the right time to sow my seeds when the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Sowing right after the very first rain is risky because it might be followed by a long dry spell that kills young seeds. It is best to wait until the ground stays consistently moist for a few consecutive rainy days before planting.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui bibii lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani odu.

english: Is it better for my crop if I water it in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can soak up the water before the sun heat causes it to evaporate. Afternoon watering can waste water through heat evaporation and sometimes burn wet leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha etsɔ la. Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ afite nu lɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai ni efɔ lɛ ashã.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the plants from intense dry heat helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunshine, and soil food directly away from your pepper roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your pepper plants get all the resources they need to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua o-pepper tso lɛ ni ená nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Will pruning or cutting off some shoots from my cassava plant hurt its growth?
ga: Ani mi-cassava lɛ yitsei ni afolɔ loo afolɔ lɛ baafite edalɛ?

english: Pruning extra stems and lower shoots does not hurt the plant; instead, it helps the cassava focus its energy on building bigger roots underground rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ he kɛ ŋmeii ni baa shi lɛ efiteee tso lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ ngmlɛfia ɔ ngɔɔ e juɛmi kɛ ma si fɔfɔɛ nguahi nɛ a ma maa ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy so quickly inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize turns moldy when it is stored while still holding moisture inside the grain. Drying your harvested corn thoroughly under the sun until the kernels are completely dry and hard prevents mold and insects from destroying it.
ga: Abele baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto shi ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lolo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baagbi kwraa ni ewa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is their main food for growth. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives them the nutrients they need to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa mɔ daa lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not during heavy rainfall. Placing the fertilizer in a small hole a few centimeters away from the plant stem and covering it with soil prevents the rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ bu bibii amli Okɛ sɛntimitai fioo komɛi awo tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ koni nugbɔ akafɔ lɛ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of the same specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your crop with beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and keeps pests away.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni eye ebua ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii, tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight because it dries out their tender leaves. Leaving big trees or planting plantains beside them provides shade and traps moisture in the soil until the cocoa plants are mature enough to handle the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi ejaakɛ ehaa amɛbaai bibii lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ aná.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunshine to manufacture energy for the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil to prevent leaves from rotting and helps the plant produce larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni baai lɛ akafite ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them in flat, poorly drained soil for too long. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells in the soil. Watering your plants consistently at their bases during flowering helps the blossoms stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I allow weeds to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's food and light so they can produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. koni anyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating small hole patterns into the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which feed directly on the growing tips of young corn plants. Applying neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides into the central funnel of the plant early on kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ. Akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli mra. koni amɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. Spraying the plants with soapy water or appropriate organic treatments controls the insects so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ko ni sa shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the soil has too much water which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extremely high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking from swollen tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cocoa tree take up to three years before it starts producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ he afii etɛ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a deep root system and a strong main trunk to support heavy pods; modern hybrid cocoa starts producing in about 2 to 3 years, whereas older types take longer.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso titri ni mli wa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ feemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo lɛ heɔ be babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato roots rot whenever the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato roots rot because water settles in poor-draining soil, starving the roots of air and creating a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains all the nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ fɛɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava curling up and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curled cassava leaves with pale patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by small whitefly insects.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii bibii. Eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ

english: What is eating small round holes into my cabbage leaves during the night?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ gbɛkɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars, such as the Diamondback moth larvae, which hide during the heat of the day and feed on leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Diamondback moth larvae, ni teɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees dry up and break easily during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan dry winds remove moisture from broad plantain leaves faster than the roots can pull water from the dry soil, making the plant weak and brittle.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ

english: Why do I need to clear the grass around my young yam vines and give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Sweet potato tso bibioo ko kɛ tso ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves into direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers, and clearing weeds prevents wild grass from stealing water and nutrients.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo mla ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ aya nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ. Ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi koo mli jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shã ni efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct heat from the sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside young cocoa gives them the shelter and shade they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ baaha amɛná wɔɔhe kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when rain falls too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale yellow from the middle while the outer edges stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the roots helps the corn regain its green color and grow big cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee amɛbaai lɛ eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛfata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eyɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and applying organic fertilizer or balanced nutrients helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ja fataa he lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Why do I need to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛ amɛ fĩɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbers that need tall sticks so their leaves can reach the sunlight. The more sunlight the upper leaves get, the more food the plant makes to build large yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbaaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Babaoo ni obaanyɛ odu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, babaoo ni tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Will cutting off side branches from my tomato plant reduce the amount of tomatoes I harvest?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha tomato ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: No, removing small extra side branches actually improves your harvest because it prevents the plant from wasting food on unnecessary stem growth and redirects energy into producing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Dabi, tsei niji bibii ni oooŋɔ Nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Ejaakɛ etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite niyenii yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aya aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating ragged holes inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
