ga: Mɛni ji buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni yeɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These holes are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the corn plant. Spraying safe pesticides or neem tree leaf extract into the central funnel early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that feed on plant sap and spread diseases. Spraying the plants with soapy water or appropriate insecticides gets rid of these insects and stops leaf curling.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ akpa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does grass and weeds growing in my farm make my crops look weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and plant food from the soil that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure all soil nutrients go directly into feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why did the maize seeds I stored in my house fail to sprout when I planted them this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ shĩa lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to grow if they are stored in damp or warm places where insects or mold damage them. Storing fully dried seeds in airtight containers mixed with wood ash in a cool room keeps seeds alive for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be ni kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii kpataa amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi kwraa lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi kɛha dumɔ.

english: What part of the crop do I actually bury in the ground to start growing Irish potatoes?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã diɛŋtsɛ mifuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mabɔi Ireland ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: To grow Irish potatoes, you plant whole small tubers or pieces of tubers that have sprouting buds called 'eyes,' rather than planting tiny botanical seeds like tomato or pepper seeds.
ga: Bɔni afee ni okwɛ Irish ŋmɔtɔ Esa akɛ odu bulb bibii muu loo bulb ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘buds’, shi jeee dumɔwui bibii tamɔ tomato loo pepper dumɔwui.

english: Is it better to plant real seeds or small tuber pieces when growing root crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu anɔkwa dumɔwui loo bulb bibii kɛ́ oodu bulb tsei?

english: For most root and tuber crops like potatoes, planting small tuber pieces is better because true seeds are tiny, grow very slowly, and do not always produce tubers that are identical to the parent plant.
ga: Kɛha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmeii bibii ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ daraa, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, ni jeee be fɛɛ be amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ.

english: Do I plant Irish potatoes in big soil mounds the same way I plant my yams?
ga: Ani miduɔ Ireland ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ agbo ko mli tamɔ bɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, while yams need huge individual soil mounds to produce large roots, potatoes are usually planted closer together in lower ridges or rows so you can easily pull soil over their stems as they grow.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ wulu ko he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ efee shishifãi wuji moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, aduɔ atomoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii amli loo yɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii amli. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ okɛ sũ aha tsei lɛ ahe mlɛo beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Can I cut a potato tuber into smaller pieces before planting, or will that make it rot in the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bibii bibii? Ani abaanyɛ afee dani adu? Aloo ebaaha sũ lɛ akpɔ̃?

english: You can cut large tubers into pieces as long as each piece has at least one active sprout or 'eye', but you should let the cut surface dry for a day or two in the shade before planting so it does not rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo yitso agbo ko mli bibii bibii. Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ fã fɛɛ fã yɛ bud loo 'bud' kome ni tsuɔ nii. Shi esa akɛ oha he ni afo lɛ agbi gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani odu. koni ekagbo

english: What is earthing up, and why must I keep covering the base of my growing potato crop with soil?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ shishitoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya nɔ mikɛ sũ aha mi-atomo ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Earthing up means pulling loose soil around the base of the plant stem; this protects growing underground tubers from sunlight, which turns them green and bitter, and creates extra space for more tubers to form.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shishitoo tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ ni agbalaa kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaa gbɛ kroko fataa he kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How many months does it take from planting Irish potatoes until they are ready to harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani aduɔ Ireland ŋmeii dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Irish potatoes are a short-duration crop and typically take about 3 to 3 and a half months (around 90 to 110 days) from planting to reach full harvest maturity.
ga: Ireland ŋmɔshi nibii ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi etɛ kɛ fã (aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 110) kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops like yams take almost a year to yield while potatoes take only three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ko tamɔ sweet potato heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni potato heɔ nyɔji etɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Different crops have different maturity cycles based on their genetics; short-term crops like potatoes complete their entire lifecycle quickly, whereas long-duration crops like yams need many months to accumulate heavy food stores in their roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ atomo, gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ naa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ, he miihia nyɔji babaoo dani amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii naa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I know that underground tubers are ready for harvest if I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tubers lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ?

english: You can tell underground tubers are mature when the leaves and stems above ground naturally begin to turn yellow, dry up, and die down.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko edara beni eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: What happens if I harvest my tubers too early while the plant leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa bulb lɛ mra tsɔ be mli ni tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Harvesting too early results in smaller yields and soft, thin-skinned tubers that bruise easily during digging and spoil quickly in storage.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ haa yibii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa, ni efiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Can I leave mature tubers in the soil for a long time after the plant dies off?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmeii ni edara lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni tso lɛ egbo sɛɛ?

english: It is best to harvest tubers soon after the plant leaves die off, because leaving them in the wet soil too long makes them vulnerable to rotting, pest attacks, or sprouting again.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa bulbs lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni tso lɛ baai lɛ egboi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi, kooloi bibii aba amɛhe, loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to keep some seed in reserve instead of planting everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ dumɔwui ato he ko moŋ fe ni madu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Keeping a reserve of seeds ensures you have backup planting material if your initial planting fails due to poor rains or pests, saving you from total crop loss.
ga: Dumɔwui krokomɛi ni okɛtoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni onáa nibii krokomɛi ni okɛduɔ nii. Kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ lɛ yeee omanye yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, Ehereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni baafite lɛ mli.

english: How can I safely keep my stored maize grains so pests do not ruin my crop reserves before next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni ŋmeii akafite mi-reserve ŋmãa lɛ dani be ni baa lɛ aba?

english: Drying your maize thoroughly and storing it in airtight bags or clean silos keeps moisture and insects like weevils away, preserving your grain for seeds or future sale.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto vacuum bags loo silos ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ahe. Too ŋmaa lɛ he kɛha wɔsɛɛ dumɔwui loo jarayeli.

english: Do my young crop seedlings need the same type of fertilizer as mature plants that are producing cobs?
ga: Ani midumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsei ni eda ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Young plants need high nitrogen to grow strong roots and green leaves, while mature crops need phosphorus and potassium to produce healthy seeds and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo he miihia tsei bibii koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Should I give the same amount of water to tiny crop seedlings as I give to full-grown plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha tsei bibii lɛ nu babaoo tamɔ bɔ ni mikɛhaa tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and need light, frequent water so they do not drown, while full-grown plants have deep roots that need larger, deeper soakings.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni ehe hiaa nu ni waaa, ni afɔɔ feemɔ koni amɛkabote nu mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu babaoo ni mli kwɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually indicate that the young plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential food it needs early on to build green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso bibioo lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Koni afee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why do some extension officers encourage planting soybeans together with maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hei komɛi lɛ woɔ soybeans kɛ ŋmãa ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ?

english: Soybeans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize crop and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Soybeans lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why does maize grow very well on my neighbor's farm but performs poorly on my farm right next to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil properties like nutrient levels, depth, and water retention vary from plot to plot, meaning your field may require different nutrients or soil care than your neighbor's.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, emlibotemɔ kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ oyale lɛ mli niyenii loo shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ he hiamɔ nii yɛ srɔto fe okutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural trick plants use to reduce their leaf area exposed to the hot sun, preventing them from losing too much water.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji koni nu akafite fe nine.

english: Why do my soybean plants stop growing leaves and stem height once flowers start appearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ kpaɔ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ beni fɔfɔi jeɔ shishi ejieɔ lɛ?

english: When soybeans begin flowering, the plant shifts all its energy away from making leaves and stems into forming flowers and seed pods.
ga: Beni soybeans jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ Tsei tsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe ni amɛfeɔ lɛ mli amɛfeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui akutsei.

english: Why do weeds reduce the yield of my young crops much more than my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei bibii lɛ ayibii baa shi babaoo fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops are small and weak, so weeds easily steal their sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, whereas mature crops are tall enough to shade out competing weeds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo. Beni amɛdara lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛlɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ahe shade.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main food for leaf growth. It can also happen if heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the roots waterlogged and unable to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves most. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts helps put nitrogen back into the soil and stops crop-specific pests from living in your soil season after season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ waa lɛ afite. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Yeɔ ebuaa nitrogen ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni otsi tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkahi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in open land without large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni eda bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and hot dry winds. Plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the seedlings cool and keeping moisture in the air and soil while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant blossoms keep dropping off before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani etsɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel too much heat or drought stress. The plant lets go of its flowers to save energy and moisture so the main plant can survive until weather conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ babaoo he. Tso lɛ baajie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ hulutsoo he. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the roots fight for soil food and water, and the stalks stretch upward to steal sunlight from each other. Spacing gives each plant enough room to grow thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Ni tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout after sowing them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to awaken the embryo inside and soften their outer shell. If the soil stays completely dry after planting, the seeds remain asleep or rot beneath the ground before they can shoot up.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui koni ekɛte fɔmɔ kotoku ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shi ni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lolo yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ loo amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains stay on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air spaces in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long without draining, it smothers the roots, causing them to drown and rot in the mud.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni amɛgboi yɛ muji lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds growing around my cassava reduce the size of my yield?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni ebɔle mi-cassava lɛ he lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your cassava needs to build big tubers. When weeds take over, your crop starves and uses all its strength just to survive instead of making large roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa ŋmei koni ŋmei wuji lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishifãi wuji ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do worms hide and eat deep inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛboteɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like fall armyworms target the central leaves because they are soft, juicy, and easy to chew. The rolled leaves also shield the worms from rain, sun, and bird attacks.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ leafworms lɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli nu, ni amɛyeɔ oya. Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ hu buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ, hulu, kɛ okpoi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their green leaves exposed to the sun. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai eŋɔli ni hulu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo ni eha sũ lɛ he atse kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my maize plants instead of planting them as close together as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ato he ko ni sa moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves, resulting in thicker stems and larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaai lɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water doesn't evaporate quickly. It keeps the roots cool, conserves moisture during dry weeks, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akafee oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehiɔ nu mli yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. When a plant doesn't get enough nitrogen from the ground, it takes nutrients from its older, bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, showing you that the soil needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Maize continuously pulls the same nutrients out of the soil every year without putting anything back. Rotating maize with beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen to the soil and stops crop-specific pests from building up in the land.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa afi ni ekɛ nɔ ko fataaa he ekoŋŋ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii, tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni etsĩ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but produce small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ tuber bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava spends all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems above ground when there is too much nitrogen or excessive water. For the plant to transfer that energy underground into thick root tubers, it needs balanced nutrients and good soil drainage.
ga: Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo loo nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ajie nakai hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛya shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ anɔ lɛ, Ehe miihia niyenii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kpakpa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the deep center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the tender center of young maize plants where fresh leaves are forming. They feed inside the funnel because it hides them from the heat and predators, so treating the central funnel early is key to saving the crop.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni baai heei miije kpo yɛ lɛ anɔ. Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛi amli ejaakɛ ekɛ amɛ teeɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ mra. No hewɔ lɛ, eji nɔ titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants get yellow spots and dry up from the bottom moving upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease that lives in the soil and splashes onto the lower leaves when it rains. As damp weather continues, the fungus climbs up the plant, causing leaves to dry out and drop prematurely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni shwieɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kwɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their tiny flowers before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ pod?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or attacks by small sucking insects like mirids. Maintaining shade trees helps keep the air humid and protects delicate flowers from burning off.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nugbɔshiimɔ trukaa. loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni mli edɔ lɛ tutuamɔi. Kɛ́ okɛ otsei lɛ wo hulutsoo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ, ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into small cups during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves on hot afternoons to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the burning sun. This is the plant's natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating too fast until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agro-dealer sprout better than seeds I save from my own harvested crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi tsei ni mikpa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from dealers are specially produced, treated against diseases, and stored in ideal conditions to keep the embryo alive. Seeds saved from regular harvests may carry hidden diseases, be insect-damaged, or lose their vigor over time.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, atsuɔ he nii ni akɛtoɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli koni fɔmɔ kotokui lɛ ahi shi. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Afiteɔ kooloi bibii. loo hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants fold up at night when the evening sets in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ beni shɛɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold up at night to reduce water loss and protect themselves from the cool night air. This natural movement helps the plant conserve moisture and energy for daylight growth.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni baa gbɛkɛ lɛ he. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nyiɛmɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water. By dropping leaves, the plant stops losing water through evaporation, allowing its underground tubers to survive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaa. Shi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the maize regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop after I apply fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that take up nutrients faster than domestic crops. Clearing the weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get the nutrients instead of the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai yɛ jwɛi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl upwards when it gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji edɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism tomato plants use to reduce the surface area exposed to intense heat and sun, which helps them hold onto water during hot weather.
ga: Leaf curling ji gbɛ ko ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba he ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop extra young pods when they do not have enough water, nutrients, or light to support all of them. This natural self-thinning helps the tree save energy for the remaining pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii krokomɛi kɛji nu, niyenii, loo la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli he-kɛ-afɔleshaa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Without steady moisture and moderate warmth, the plant cannot complete pollination to form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo ni sa bɛ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ afee tsei lɛ pollen kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Why should I wait until after the first heavy rain before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ dani adu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Planting in dry soil can cause seeds to rot or get eaten by insects before they germinate. Waiting for heavy rain ensures the soil has enough moisture for the seeds to sprout quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo kooloi aye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting if I leave them in the ground too long after the vines dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni wain tsei lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Once yam vines dry up, the tuber stops growing and loses its defense against pests and diseases. Leaving tubers in damp soil makes them vulnerable to rot and soil insects.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛbuuu amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya.

english: How many years can a single cocoa tree keep producing pods before I need to replace it?
ga: Kakao tso kome baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii enyiɛ dani esa akɛ atsake lɛ?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree can live and yield pods for 30 years or even longer, provided you prune it regularly, manage pests, and protect it from diseases.
ga: Cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛyashi afii 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛji ofoɔ tsei lɛ ahe daa Pest management kɛ helai atsĩɔ naa

english: Why do older cocoa trees in our village produce fewer fruits compared to when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ akɛto shishijee lɛ he lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their roots take in fewer nutrients, their branches become overgrown, and they become more vulnerable to soil depletion and diseases like swollen shoot, which reduces fruit production.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Amɛniji lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine. ni amɛyɛ oshara akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu, ni baaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some crops die after just one season while tree crops like cocoa live for decades?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi gboiɔ yɛ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ kookoo hiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ?

english: Annual crops like maize put all their energy into making seeds quickly and then die, whereas tree crops build deep roots and strong wooden trunks that allow them to survive and fruit year after year.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa afi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ dumɔwui oya, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboiɔ. Shi tsei ahe tsei lɛ, amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why can't I grow cocoa in every region of Ghana, like in the dry areas around Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu kookoo yɛ Ghana kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa nɔ lɛ? Nakai eji yɛ hei ni nu bɛ ni bɔle Accra lɛ hu.

english: Cocoa trees require deep, rich soil, consistent high humidity, and regular rainfall typical of forest zones; drier coastal plains like Accra do not have the right rain or soil conditions for cocoa to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii babaoo he miihia koko tsei. Humidity ni fa babaoo be fɛɛ be Ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa, ni ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli. Accra ŋshɔnaa shikpɔŋ kplanaa ni mli egbi lɛ bɛ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni sa ni baaha kookoo aya hiɛ.

english: Is it possible for me to farm vegetables successfully in areas where traditional crops like cocoa refuse to grow?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafee omanyeyeli yɛ aduawai abɔɔ mli yɛ he ko ni blema nibii tamɔ kookoo kpooɔ akɛ ebaakwɛ?

english: Yes, crops like tomatoes, peppers, and leafy vegetables can grow in dry or poor soil areas, especially if you use irrigation or protected farming structures like greenhouses.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ aduawai ni baa yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo okwaayeli he nibii ni abuɔ he tamɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii miitsu nii.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it protect my crops differently than open field farming?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of plastic or glass that creates a controlled environment, protecting plants from heavy rainfall, intense sun, and destructive pests.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo glase fee ni haa shihilɛ ni akudɔ lɛ baa. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: If I spend money to construct a greenhouse structure on my land, how many years will it last?
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ shika lɛ ma greenhouse yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaaye?

english: A properly built greenhouse structure made with durable materials can last for 30 years or more, though the covering plastic may need replacement every few years.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ni akɛ nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ fee ni ama jogbaŋŋ lɛ baahi shi afii 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai, eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni atsake plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be moŋ. Afii enyɔ loo etɛ

english: Can I plant big tree crops like cocoa inside a greenhouse?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei wuji tamɔ kookoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: No, greenhouses are designed for small, high-value vegetables and fruits like tomatoes and cucumbers; tree crops like cocoa grow too tall and wide to fit inside standard structures.
ga: Dabi, afee greenhouses kɛha aduawai bibii ni jara wa waa kɛ aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ kukumba. Tsei tamɔ kookoo daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛlɛɛmɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbote tsɔnei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli.

english: How does soil stay fertile enough to feed tree crops for over 30 years without getting exhausted?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aaatsɔ nɔ afee fɛo bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei kɛ tsei nɔ ni fe afii 30 ni etɔɔɔ amɛ?

english: Forest trees naturally drop leaves that rot and decay, continually returning nutrients back into the soil, though adding compost or fertilizers over time helps maintain high yields.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni egboi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ.

english: How does harsh sunlight and heavy rain affect the long-term life of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ he?

english: Excessive heat causes plants to lose water quickly and dry out, while heavy rain can wash away topsoil and nutrients; using shade trees or protective shelters helps crops stay healthy longer.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei tsu nii akɛ hulutsoo loo wɔɔhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa onibii ni okwɛɔ nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate stems and shallow roots that cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them protects the young cocoa from burning until their roots are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cacao tso lɛ masɛi lɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a vital food for growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will give the plants the food they need to become dark green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ wuji.

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in three to four months, leaving the cassava with plenty of space and time to grow and mature over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ naa hegbɛ kɛ be babaoo ni ekɛdaa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ afi ni eshwɛ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is causing my tomatoes to get black, rotten spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ dani eshɛ po?

english: Dark rotten bottoms on tomatoes are usually caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the soil lacks calcium or when watering is irregular during the time fruits are forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato shikpɔŋ ni eyɛ su ni tsuɔ waa lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither even when rain falls and water stays around the plant stems for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni nu ebɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe gbii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: When standing water stays around stems for too long, the soil becomes waterlogged and drowns the roots, preventing them from breathing. This causes the roots to rot and the leaves above ground to dry up.
ga: Beni nu lɛ ebɔle tso lɛ he lolo lɛ etsɛ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nu ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ baawo nu mli, ni ebaaha amɛmli agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu agbi.

english: Why should I measure space between my maize plants instead of scattering many seeds closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ dumɔwui babaoo ashwã amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small harvests. Proper spacing lets each plant grow strong and produce maximum yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my farm than my actual planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and adapted to steal water and soil food very quickly. Clearing weeds early gives your cultivated crops a fair chance to grow without being starved.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe oya koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni odu lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni hɔmɔ yeee amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store food for the plant, but if left in dry soil past their maturity time, they lose water and turn into tough fiber, making them hard to cook and eat.
ga: Kasava shishifãi toɔ niyenii kɛhaa cassava tso lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyashi be ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ ho lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ fibrous. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo nii ni aye nii.

english: Why is it recommended that I pinch off some extra branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cutting or pinching off excess leaves and small side shoots helps the pepper plant direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier peppers rather than feeding unnecessary leaves.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni afolɔ loo aaafolɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei tso lɛ atsɔ ehewalɛ nɔ efee ŋmei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobote baai ni he ehiaaa mli lɛ

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to perform well only in their first planting generation. Saving seeds from that harvest will result in unpredictable, weaker plants with smaller yields in the second season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abaajie kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize crops produce much smaller ears during dry spells than during the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ toi bibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ?

english: Maize plants need a steady supply of water especially when flowering to build full, heavy grains. During dry spells, the plant enters stress mode and saves its energy, which results in smaller ears and incomplete grain formation.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa tsei daa, titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, koni amɛwo ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ ni tsii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ yaa stress mode mli ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni yeee emuu.

english: Why does my harvested cassava taste watery instead of starchy when I harvest it right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ ŋɔɔ tamɔ nu yɛ starchy najiaŋ kɛ́ mikpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain falls after a dry period, the cassava plant quickly drinks up water and pushes it into its roots. This water dilutes the concentrated starch in the tuber, making it feel soft and watery if harvested immediately.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ Kasava tso lɛ nuɔ nu oya ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu nɛɛ baaha starch ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ afee mlɛo. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ nu kɛji akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. When temperatures get very high, the plant rolls its leaves inward to reduce the amount of surface exposed to the scorching sun, helping it conserve water.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field before planting maize make the maize stalks greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea roots rot in the soil, they release natural nitrogen fertilizer that feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmei henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do young cassava roots rot under the soil when the field stays flooded for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like plants above ground. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava tubers, which causes root cells to die and allows soil fungi to quickly rot the crop underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi koni amɛmu, tamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi amli wala yibii lɛ gboiɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why do worms always attack the tender center leaves of my young maize right after the first light rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs on young green leaves right after the early rains begin. When caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hatch, they seek moisture and protection inside the tender central whorl of the plant where it is easy to eat.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛtaoɔ nu kɛ hebuu yɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli, he ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mlɛo lɛ.

english: High daytime temperatures can damage the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it sterile. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the useless flower to save energy.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ afite pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. kɛ render sterile Kɛ́ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers drop their leaves and slow down growth after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛdaraa blɛoo beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are dug up, their root connections are broken. The plant undergoes transplant shock and drops its outer leaves to cut down on water loss while it focuses energy on growing new roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsa plantain tsei lɛ, shishifãi lɛ ateŋ tsakpaa lɛ baafite. Akɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ashɛrɛɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ashwieɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ shishifãi heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: If I save seeds from my best-yielding hybrid maize harvest this year, why won't those seeds produce a good crop next year?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui komɛi ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn ni woɔ yibii kpakpa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli afi nɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ to lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants to give extra high yields in the first generation. The seeds produced by that crop lose that special balance of traits, leading to uneven and lower yields if replanted.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛwo yibii ni fa babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni tso lɛ woɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛsui lɛ ni ja. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee ekome, ni ebaa shi kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees off my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow under forest canopy shade. Their leaves burn under direct, intense sunlight because their young root systems cannot absorb enough soil moisture to offset the harsh heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ashishi. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ sũ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: If I grow my crops inside a greenhouse, will I get more harvest than if I use a net house?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli Ani maná yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔ ni akɛ trellis tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops grown in a greenhouse generally produce a higher yield than those in a net house because greenhouses provide better control over water, heat, and severe weather conditions.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ trellis ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsũi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nu, dɔlɛ, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops produce more fruit inside a protected greenhouse than out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji ni abuɔ he lɛ amli fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses protect plants from extreme heat, heavy rain, and destructive insects, allowing the crops to stress less and use more of their energy to produce healthy fruits.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ koolooi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ haomɔ babaoo ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is a greenhouse much more expensive to build than a net house?
ga: Ani tsũ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa kwraa fe tsũ ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ maa?

english: Yes, building a greenhouse usually costs about double the price of building a net house of the same size because of the heavier framing and full covering materials required.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, shika ni akɛmaɔ tsũ ni akɛ tsei fee ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ maa lɛ aaafee shii enyɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebiɔ tsɔne ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa nɔ.

english: Why would a farmer choose to build a net house if a greenhouse gives a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi halaa akɛ amɛbaama trellis tsũi kɛji akɛ greenhouses lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: A net house is a popular choice because it costs about half as much to build as a greenhouse while still giving good protection against pests and sensible crop yields.
ga: Trellis ŋmɔji ji nɔ ko ni ehe gbɛi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eheɔ aaafee shika ni akɛmaɔ ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fã. yɛ be mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahebuu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai haa lolo.

english: How do I decide whether to invest in a net house or a full greenhouse for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ mishika baawo net house loo greenhouse ni yeɔ emuu mli kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If you have limited capital, a net house offers a lower-cost way to protect crops from insects, but if you have a larger budget and want maximum yield per square meter, a greenhouse is better.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oyɛ shika fioo lɛ, Netting greenhouses haa gbɛ ni jara waaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe. Shi kɛji akɛ oyɛ shika babaoo ni osumɔɔ ni oná nɔ ni fe fɛɛ yɛ sqɛɛ mita kome mli hu? Greenhouse hi fe no.

english: How does a net house protect my vegetables from insect pests?
ga: Te ŋtayaa ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ baabu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A net house uses fine mesh screens that act as a physical barrier, keeping large destructive insects like moths and beetles away from your vegetables while letting air flow through.
ga: Netting greenhouses kɛ mesh screen kpakpa ko ni tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ kooloi wuji ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ o-vegetables lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii, yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli.

english: Will heavy rain break my delicate vegetable plants if they are inside a net house?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baafite mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛji amɛyɛ trellis shĩa mli?

english: The netting breaks heavy raindrops into fine mist, which prevents heavy rainfall from damaging delicate leaves and washing away young plants.
ga: Ŋshɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ feɔ afua kpakpa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ekɛ tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does growing crops inside a greenhouse protect them from flooding during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nu afua akafee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Greenhouses have solid roofing covers that completely block rain from hitting the crops directly, allowing you to control the exact amount of water your plants receive.
ga: Greenhouses lɛ yɛ ŋwɛitsu ni wa ni tsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ nu pɔtɛɛ ni otsei lɛ náa lɛ.

english: Do crops inside a net house still get enough sunlight and fresh air to grow well?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ trellis lɛ mli lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, net houses are designed to let plenty of sunlight and cool natural breeze pass through while keeping harmful pests outside.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee trellis greenhouses lɛ koni hulu la babaoo abote mli ni adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ atsɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ hu hiɔ kpo nɔ.

english: Can growing vegetables under a structure like a net house reduce my crop losses?
ga: Aduawai adumɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ Ani trellis greenhouse baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mifiteɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, protected structures reduce crop loss by lowering pest damage, preventing physical weather damage, and helping crops stay healthier throughout their lifespan.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni abuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baafite amɛ lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kpakpa yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen. The plant is moving its remaining nutrient energy from older leaves up to feed the new leaves and growing cob at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii mli hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni miida yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with large green leaves, but when I harvest, the tubers under the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted in extremely rich soil, the plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to build thick, healthy roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they lack sufficient soil moisture, if key nutrients like potassium are missing, or if there are not enough tiny insects in the shade to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ potassium ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpea or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-corn lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer for the maize plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. Lifting the vines off the damp ground exposes leaves to light and air, preventing leaf decay and encouraging larger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I wait until after a good rain to apply fertilizer instead of spreading it on dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Fertilizer granules must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink them in. Applying fertilizer on bone-dry soil causes it to sit uselessly or scorch the roots when the sun gets hot.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni he ehiaaa loo ebaaha amɛshã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and getting small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled, wrinkled leaves on tomato plants are usually a sign of a plant virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies, or a reaction to extreme heat where the plant curls to protect its moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. aloo hetoo ni akɛhaa kɛha dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni tsei shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and snapping near the stem before the fruit bunch fully grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by stem borer pests or fungal diseases in the soil that destroy the plant's internal water tubes, cutting off moisture and food from reaching the leaves.
ga: Kooloi awuiyelɔi, stem borers, loo fungal helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ayashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my vegetable crop leaves look droopy and dead in the hot afternoon sun, but look fresh again by the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi leebi lɛ, okuɔ osɛɛ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can pull it from dry soil, causing temporary wilting. Overnight, when temperatures drop, the roots catch up and refill the leaves with water.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kukuoo mli Gbi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baafata baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my hot pepper fruits sometimes very spicy, but other times during wet weather they taste mild?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili yibii lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ? Shi bei komɛi lɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ lɛ waaa.

english: Pepper plants naturally produce higher levels of the heat-causing chemical when they face dry, sunny conditions. When they receive plenty of water and shade, the fruits become milder.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ tsofai ni haa dɔlɛ babaoo baa kɛji akɛ amɛtee shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛná nu babaoo kɛ hulutsoo Yibii lɛ baafee blɛoo.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, the intense sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture, causing them to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the mid-day heat even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. They temporarily droop to conserve moisture and usually recover when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaatsi amɛhe be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What is eating the leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small holes full of dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai ni eshiɔ bu bibii yɛ tso lɛ he fɛɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) of the maize plant during the day, chewing tender leaves and leaving behind sawdust-like waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves getting dark brown lines and dying from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called Black Sigatoka. It attacks older leaves first, creating dark spots that dry out the leaf, which reduces the plant's energy and leads to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka. Etutuaa baai ni egbɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ ni haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni ehaa plantain tsei bibii baa.

english: Why do many of my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up before growing into full fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani eda ni etsɔ aduawai ni eyi obɔ.

english: This can happen due to cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot nourish, or due to Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during cool, rainy weather.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli yɛ cherelle lɛ ni egbo lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. aloo yɛ black pod hela hewɔ Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs resting or fertilizer before I plant my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni miŋmɔ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo awo mli ŋmɔshi nii dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If you notice that past crops grew slowly, had pale yellowish leaves, or yielded smaller roots than usual, the soil nutrients are exhausted and need replenishment through crop resting, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oyɔse akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ daa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo eyɛ shishifãi bibii fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei ni heɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Cutting weeds above the surface leaves their roots untouched under the ground. As soon as it rains, those live roots rapidly shoot up new leaves.
ga: Jwɛi ni afoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai heei oya.

english: When maize is crowded, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall with weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe yɛ tsɔi ni amɛkwɔ. Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or beans together with my cassava on the same plot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside cassava is beneficial because legumes capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ dumɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmei.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting in the storage barn before the rains even arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ po baa lɛ?

english: Yams have a natural internal rest period after harvest. Once that rest period ends during the dry season, the warm air triggers the tuber to start sprouting automatically, signaling it is time for planting.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha bulb lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aje shishi ekwɛ̃. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees away from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates a protective living canopy that gives young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why are black spots appearing on my cocoa pods during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are a sign of Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the moisture that helps the fungus spread.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii diji hela he okadi. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, nu shihilɛi amli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ekpaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growth stage will restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield for only one harvest cycle. If you replant seeds saved from a hybrid crop, the new plants will grow unevenly, become weak, and produce much smaller cobs than the original seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be kome mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli Tso hee lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee, egbɔjɔ, ni ebaawo dumɔwui ni baa shi kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and look distorted?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Curled and twisted cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and pulling up infected plants early keeps the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can carefully dig up one stand to check if the tubers are large and firm before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa shidaamɔhe kome ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from stress, usually caused by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp around the roots helps the plant retain its flowers and turn them into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ehaa efeɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and ground nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to produce large, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long hot spell before the main rains settle in. If you plant too early, the heat can scorch and kill the newly germinated seeds before the next rainfall arrives.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa sɛɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to grab water and soil nutrients faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds while they are still small prevents them from starving your crops of sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe for me to mix my weedkiller and insect spray together in one tank to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ baafutu tanki kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: No, mixing different agrochemicals together can reduce their effectiveness, burn your crop leaves, or create toxic chemical combinations that are dangerous to spray.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ agrochemicals srɔtoi futu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhewalɛ aba shi. Shãa otso lɛ baai lɛ loo ofee tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni yɔɔ oshara kɛha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so fast on my farm even after I spray them with chemical weedkiller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ.

english: Many chemical sprays only kill the green leaves above ground, leaving root systems intact or weed seeds dormant in the soil ready to sprout again after rainfall.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ baai eŋɔli pɛ. Shi shishifãi lɛ ahi shi loo jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when there is heavy rain for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Too much rain saturates the soil and washes away important nutrients like nitrogen, while also preventing roots from getting enough air to feed the plant properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when plants do not get enough water, which prevents successful pollination from occurring.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa pollination lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green bushes above ground but very tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely, cassava uses all its energy to grow leaves instead of storing energy in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting up and shrinking into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking leaf sap and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive wetness and shade allow fungal spores to spread Black Pod disease, which rots the pod tissue from the outside inward.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa pod fãji lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛboteɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing plantain trees provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my groundnut crop needs extra fertilizer or if the soil is already fine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-peanut tso lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hi momo?

english: Groundnut plants pull nitrogen directly from the air using small nodules on their roots, so if the leaves remain dark green without yellowing, extra nitrogen fertilizer is usually unnecessary.
ga: Peanut tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly when I store them inside a dark room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ?

english: Stored yams need cool, well-ventilated spaces with good airflow to keep moisture from building up on the skin and attracting rotting fungi.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ abua ehe naa yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: How long after my tree flowers should I expect to see fruits starting to grow?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ tso lɛ etse fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ akɛ mana aduawai ni baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Fruits usually begin to form right after the flowers are pollinated and drop their petals, though the time it takes for those fruits to fully mature can range from a few weeks to several months depending on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ be dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ moŋ, shi ebaanyɛ ehe kɛjɛ otsii fioo kɛyashi nyɔji babaoo yɛ bɔ ni aduɔ nii ahaa lɛ naa.

english: When should I expect my young tree crop to bear its very first fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ midumɔwui lɛ baawo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii?

english: Most perennial tree crops start bearing their very first small set of fruits between 3 years and 9 months to 4 years after being planted, provided they get adequate water and nutrients.
ga: Tsoi ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii bibii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi afii 4 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ amɛna nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: At what age will my tree crop start giving me plenty of fruits for a major harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ afii mitso lɛ baabɔi yibii babaoo womɔ kɛha kpamɔ agbo?

english: Tree crops usually reach full maturity and produce their heaviest, most abundant harvests from 6 or 7 years onward as the tree canopy fully expands.
