ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛfaa babaoo kɛjɛɔ afii 6 loo 7 kɛyaa beni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ egbɛ eshwa kwraa lɛ.

english: Is it normal for my young tree to yield only a small amount of fruit in its first bearing year?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii fioo pɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ mli?

english: Yes, it is completely normal. Young trees around 3 to 4 years old are still growing and focus energy on building strong trunks and roots, so heavy fruit production only happens later when they mature around 6 to 7 years.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. Tsei bibii ni eye aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ miida lolo ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ miitsu tsei akutsei kɛ shishifãi ni wa amamɔ he nii. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai ni fa babaoo lɛ baa yɛ sɛɛ mli pɛ, yɛ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 ni amɛdara lɛ mli.

english: How do high-yielding improved seeds differ from the traditional seeds I save from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa daa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Improved seeds are specially selected and bred to grow faster, resist common local pests and diseases, and produce much higher fruit yields per tree than traditional saved seeds.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Ni yibiiwoo ni jɛɔ tso kome mli baa lɛ fa kwraa fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: What basic steps can I take to make sure my new crop seeds become very productive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii manyɛ matsɔ nɔ makwɛ koni midumɔwui heei lɛ awo yibii waa?

english: To get high productivity, plant seeds with correct field spacing, maintain regular weeding, apply recommended fertilizers early, and ensure young plants get enough water during dry spells.
ga: koni ená yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ Dumɔ dumɔwui ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo mli mra. Ni kwɛmɔ ni tsei bibii lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I participate in agricultural extension projects that supply improved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni kɛ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ haa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension projects give you access to tested, high-quality seed varieties along with expert guidance on planting techniques that significantly boost your farm's harvest and income.
ga: Okwaafoi agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ haa onine shɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛfata ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ ŋaai ni akɛduɔ nii ni baanyɛ aha oŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo kɛ shika ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ waa lɛ he lɛ fata he.

english: Why are the flowers on my crop dropping off without developing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdarako ni amɛfeee aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop early when crops suffer from water stress during dry heat, lack proper soil nutrients, or experience poor pollination from insects.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo naagbai ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni ehiii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: What special care should I give my crops once they start flowering?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔii lɛ?

english: During flowering, ensure the soil stays moist, avoid spraying harsh chemicals that kill pollinating bees, and ensure the plants have enough nutrients like potassium to support fruit development.
ga: yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Kwɛmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Ni kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ potassium, ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to start harvesting my tree fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ be ni sa ji ni mabɔi mitsei lɛ akpamɔ?

english: Harvesting should begin when fruits reach full size, change to their mature color (such as yellow, red, or orange depending on the crop), and appear in large quantities across the farm.
ga: Esa akɛ aje ŋmaakpamɔ shishi beni aduawai lɛ eshɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɔɔ su ni ekwɛ̃ (tamɔ ŋmɔŋ, etsuru, loo ŋmɔŋ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ) ni ejieɔ ehe kpo babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when the sun is very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni hulu lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or trees above them to shield them from the sun and keep moisture in the soil while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to make food that grows the big tubers underground. Putting up stakes lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they could rot, helping them get full sun to build larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee niyenii beni amɛduɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ama shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdu sweet potatoes wuji.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and soft when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo?

english: Heavy rain and high moisture cause a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread fast. Water droplets splash the tiny fungal spores from the soil or infected stems onto the pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nu mli nui shwieɔ fungal spores bibii anɔ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ

english: Why are tiny holes and ragged edges suddenly appearing on the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These insects hide inside the inner leaves of the maize plant during the day and chew on the tender foliage, which slows down plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: During very hot hours, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull water up from the ground. The plant wilts to protect itself from losing more moisture, but usually recovers when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi babaoo lɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe waaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is hungry for soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, which makes leaves rich green. Rain provides water, but plants still need rich soil or compost to feed their growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu hia shikpɔŋ kpakpa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ dalɛ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots and leaves compete fiercely for soil food, water, and light. The plants will grow tall and thin above ground, but produce very small, thin roots under the soil.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ la. Tsei daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa baahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small stems growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Mɛi krɛdɛɛi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food away from the main mother plantain tree. Removing most of them lets the main plant put all its energy into growing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni fata he lɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ he ko ni kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do so many small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but many fall because small insects did not pollinate them or because the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to feed every pod. The tree naturally drops excess flowers so it can focus on a smaller number of healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fioo komɛi anɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots under the ground are mature enough for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves at the bottom of the plant turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the tubers swell up beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishi baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: What causes the cocoa pods on my tree to turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather. You can control it by clearing weeds, pruning excess leaves to let in sunlight and air, and spraying recommended fungicides.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign that your soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the tree is stressed by drought, insect damage, or diseases like Swollen Shoot virus.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ hɔmɔ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo helai, tamɔ bud swollen virus miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Is there a medicine that can cure my cocoa tree once it gets the swollen shoot disease?
ga: Ani tsofa ko yɛ ni baanyɛ atsa kookoo tsei kɛji amɛshishifãi efuu?

english: There is currently no chemical cure for Swollen Shoot virus once a tree is infected. The best action is to remove and destroy the infected tree so the disease does not spread to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛbaatsa Swollen Shoot hela lɛ kɛji tsei lɛ emɔ hela lɛ pɛ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ afee ji ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ. Enɛ ji koni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Where can I go to get reliable advice when a strange disease attacks my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ maná ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ kɛ́ hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ba? tutuamɔ miŋmɔshi nibii

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) extension office or contact agricultural research institutions like the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana (CRIG) for proven guidance.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) nitsumɔhe nine ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Aloo oya okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhe ko tamɔ Cocoa Nibii Amli Taomɔ Nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ Ghana (CRIG) lɛ ŋɔɔ koni ona ŋaawoo ni ana he odaseyeli.

english: How do I know if a farm chemical is safe and effective to use on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Always look for approved chemicals certified by regulatory bodies like the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) or recommended by extension officers, and strictly follow the dosage instructions on the label.
ga: Taomɔ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) lɛ etsɔɔ mli loo ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ atsu he nii. Ni onyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ tsofa ni yɔɔ wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do mirid bugs attack my cocoa trees and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo miitutua mi cacao tsei lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Mirid bugs suck the sap from young leaves and pods, especially in areas where sunlight directly hits canopy gaps. You can manage them by maintaining proper canopy shade and applying approved insecticides during peak seasons.
ga: Mirid kooloi lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ hei ni hulu la lɛ tswaa ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be ni sa ni oookwɛ nɔ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did the chemical spray I bought fail to kill the pests on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi ni mihe lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sprays often fail if the product is expired or fake, mixed with the wrong amount of water, applied at the wrong time of day, or if the pests have built up resistance to that specific chemical.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ tsofa lɛ be eho loo eji amale. Akɛ nu ni ejaaa efutu mli Kɛkɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa tsu nii loo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ etswa ehe shi ewo nakai tsofa pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: How often should I spray protective medicine on my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During the wet season when fungal diseases spread rapidly, extension officers usually recommend spraying every 2 to 4 weeks using approved protective treatments.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ helatsamɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ, akɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ atsĩɔ hela naa lɛ atsu nii kɛfɔ hela lɛ nɔ daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 4.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tso masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed and scorched under full direct sunlight. Shade trees protect young plants, retain soil moisture, and create a cooler climate for cocoa to thrive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni kookoo akwɛ̃.

english: How does protecting my crops from diseases help me secure money for my children's school fees?
ga: Mi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe buu kɛjɛ helai ahe Te ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi tɛŋŋ mawo mibii lɛ akasemɔ he nyɔmɔ?

english: Controlling crop diseases ensures you harvest a full yield of high-quality cocoa, which means more weight at the scale, higher farm income, and consistent profits to cover family expenses like education.
ga: Helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ haa onáa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ muji babaoo kɛha dalɛ. Okwaayeli mli shika ni fa kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa daa ni akɛbaatsu weku lɛ shika tamɔ nikasemɔ he nii.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, showing it needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia bo.

english: Why do my cocoa tree blossoms fall off without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by prolonged dry weather, lacks sufficient shade, or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges in the field to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ jɛmɛ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves curling tightly into tubes during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward to protect themselves from losing too much water during high heat, but if they stay curled, it often means small sucking pests like aphids are hiding underneath.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shi kɛji amɛbɔle amɛhe Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce lots of green foliage but empty shells underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium and phosphorus, nutrients that the plant specifically needs to form solid seeds inside the shell.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ calcium kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei pɔtɛɛ koni amɛfee dumɔwui ni wa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my planted seeds rot in the dirt after a heavy rainfall instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains soak soil with poor drainage, water fills all air spaces and starves seeds of oxygen, causing soil fungi to attack and rot the seed before it can sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ aba dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small and watery instead of thick and starch-filled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ starch lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is packed too hard for roots to expand, if the plant receives too much shade, or if you harvest before the plant has had enough time to store starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛji tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo kɛji okpa nii dani tsei lɛ ná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ starch ato.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark brown and rot before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants do not get a steady supply of water, which prevents them from moving calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ haaa calcium aya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is my plantain stalk falling over by itself even when there is no windstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi lɛ? He ni ahum bɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall over when underground pests like nematodes or stem borers eat into the roots and bulb base, destroying the anchor that keeps the heavy tree upright.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ye shishifãi lɛ kɛ bulb lɛ shishi. Gbalamɔ ŋshɔkei ni haa tsei ni tsii lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves develop brown spots and dry up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam leaves is typically caused by anthracnose, a fungal disease that spreads quickly across fields during rainy and humid weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ gbiɔ oya. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do some heads on my rice stalk turn completely white and stay empty of grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yitsei komɛi feɔ futafuta kwraa ni ŋmãa ŋmãa ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: White heads occur when stem borer insects burrow inside the rice stem and cut off the flow of nutrients up to the grain head while it is developing.
ga: Whiteheads baa beni stem borers lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ni amɛfoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa yitso lɛ mli lɛ mli beni edara lɛ.

english: I want to plant tree crops on my land in a dry area like Tamale, but how can young trees survive the long dry season here?
ga: Miisumɔ ni madu tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni nu bɛ tamɔ Tamal. Shi tso bibioo ko Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ biɛ lɛ mli?

english: Tree seedlings survive dry conditions if you plant them right at the start of the rainy season so their roots reach deep into the ground before the drought begins, and by covering the soil around their roots with dry leaves or grass to hold in moisture.
ga: Tsoi amli dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli kɛji odu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hɔmɔ lɛ aje shishi. kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize crops turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow well. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the stems early in the season will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei wo Stems lɛ he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without draining, causing fungi to attack the roots. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rain flow away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ joɔ foi. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why should I space my tomato plants far apart instead of planting them tightly together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ lɛ.

english: Giving plants space ensures each one gets enough sunlight, air, and nutrients from the dirt. Planting too close creates crowded, humid shade where plant diseases spread quickly and crops choke each other out.
ga: Kɛ́ oha otsei lɛ gbɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ baa. he ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Can I plant my grain crops directly under big trees, or will the shade ruin them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmaa yɛ tsei wuji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo shade lɛ baakpata nakai tsei lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Most grain crops like maize and millet need full sunlight all day to make good yield. Shading them under dense trees will make them grow tall and weak with very little grain to harvest.
ga: Ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, biɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmãa kpakpa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛnáa ŋmaa fioo ko pɛ ni amɛbaakpa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die right after I move them from the nursery bed into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings go into shock when their roots are disturbed and exposed to strong sun immediately. Moving your seedlings late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day and watering them right away helps them settle into the field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa kɛji akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ hao ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba amɛnɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ odumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmɔ mli shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu ewo nɔ lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ nu wo amɛmli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛma shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some seeds I buy from the market fail to grow when I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ waaa kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Grains sold in the market are meant for cooking and may be old, heat-damaged, or stored poorly. Certified seeds from recognized farm dealers are kept specifically for planting and tested to ensure they sprout.
ga: Akɛ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛhoo nii, ni ekolɛ egbɔ. hulutsoo efite loo akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ Akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli jarayelɔi ni ale amɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ toɔ pɔtɛɛ koni adu ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them during the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the ground is cool, allowing the plant roots to absorb the water before the hot sun can evaporate it away.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and adapted to steal water and food from the soil quickly. Clearing them early while they are small keeps them from stealing nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe oya koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkajuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why does my farmland produce less food every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa daa afi lɛ? Ni miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish. Alternating your main crop with legumes like beans or cowpeas returns vital food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do rice crops need so much standing water in the field to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa tsei yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice plants can survive flooded soil, but water is mainly used because standing water blocks sunlight from reaching the soil, which smothers weeds and prevents harmful pests from destroying the young crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi akɛ nu tsuɔ nii babaoo ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni egbe jwɛi lɛ ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young rice usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil or that the field is too dry for the roots to drink up the nutrients they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ anu niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How do improved rice seeds perform better than the old seeds I saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui momo ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Improved rice seeds are specially selected to grow faster, resist common local diseases, survive tough weather better, and produce more grains per plant than older saved seeds.
ga: Ahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. helai ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ Ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa mli jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ tso kome mli fe dumɔwui ni ato momo lɛ

english: Why does a banana plant naturally die after producing just one main bunch of fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana tsei gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni amɛwo ŋmei titri kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A single banana stem is designed by nature to flower and produce fruit only once in its life; after harvest, it dies so its root system can feed the young shoots growing beside it.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee banana ni yɔɔ tso kome lɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ ewala be mli. Kɛ́ akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, egboɔ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye abua ŋmeii bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Should I allow all the small shoots growing around my main banana plant to stay, or should I cut some off?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? ni miida yɛ Mi banana tso titri lɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Aloo esa akɛ afolɔ fãi komɛi amli?

english: You should remove most shoots and leave only one or two strong ones, because too many shoots will steal food and water from the main plant, resulting in very small fruits.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yibii lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my banana leaves get black spots and turn brown before the fruits are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by a fungal leaf disease that spreads during warm and rainy weather, which weakens the leaves and stops them from making food for the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaaa amɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting a coconut tree before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Traditional tall coconut trees usually take 6 to 10 years to start producing fruit, but improved dwarf coconut varieties can start bearing nuts in just 3 to 4 years with proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema ŋmei tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi dwarf coconut henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny immature coconuts dropping off my tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Egbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ agbo?

english: Young coconuts fall off when the tree does not get enough water or nutrients during hot periods, causing the plant to shed extra fruit to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Kokoobii bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji tso lɛ náaa nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Ha ŋmei tso lɛ awo yibii krokomɛi koni ekɛbu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Can I plant other crops like maize or cassava between my young coconut trees while I wait for them to grow?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting short crops between young coconut trees is a great practice because the coconut seedlings are spaced far apart and take years to create deep shade, giving lower crops plenty of sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ ni amɛheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛfeɔ hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ana hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural protection trick where the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to slow down water loss and keep from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa. Tsei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu lɛ akafo mli fioo ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ naa.

english: Plantain stems naturally fruit only once in their lifetime. After you harvest the bunch, that main stem dies off, but it transfers its energy to young underground shoots called suckers, which grow up to produce the next bunches.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli plantain tsei lɛ woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Beni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ogbe naa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baagbo. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa zugba sisi tso bibihi nɛ a tsɛɛ mɛ ke tso ɔ a mi. ni daa ni ekɛ nine ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa

english: Plantain plants have very soft, watery stems and broad leaves that lose moisture quickly in direct heat. During dry months, the plant sacrifice its outer leaves to conserve water in its core root so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ, kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛ́ akɛwo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli Tso lɛ kɛ esɛɛ baai lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ nu ato eshishifãi titrii lɛ amli koni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do strong winds easily push over my plantain trees when they carry heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mi tsei lɛ amli mlɛo beni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Unlike big trees, plantains have shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than deep into the underground soil. When a heavy fruit bunch grows on top, the plant becomes top-heavy and requires bamboo or wooden poles for support.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tsei wuji lɛ, plantain shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai akui ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ ji ŋwɛi-tsii ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfee ŋmei fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I get new plantain plants to plant if they do not produce seeds like maize or pepper?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui heei? Kɛji amɛwooo dumɔwui, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa

english: Plantains do not grow from seeds. You multiply them using 'suckers,' which are the small side shoots that sprout naturally from the base of a healthy parent plant underground.
ga: Plantains jɛɛɛ dumɔwui amli ekwɛ̃ɔ. Okɛ ‘ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ amɛ babaoo.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain shoots when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ mi teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Planting them about 3 meters (10 feet) apart gives their large leaves enough room to capture sunlight without crowding or shading each other out, while also allowing roots space to feed.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) lɛ, ehaa baai agboi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsiii amɛhe loo amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: How long will I wait from the day I plant a sucker until I harvest my first plantain bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛjɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyashi be mli ni mikpaa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Under good rains and soil care in Ghana, a plantain shoot usually takes between 11 to 15 months to grow, flower, and fully mature a bunch ready for market.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛdaraa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize on the same field with my young plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi plantains lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize, garden eggs, or cassava with young plantains during their first few months works well because the small plantain shoots leave plenty of open sunlight for other short-term food crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa ni akɛ plantains bibii duɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ plantain ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Ha hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa aha niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: If too many shoots grow at the same spot, they fight over soil food and water. Pruning away excess shoots so that only two or three strong ones remain ensures your main tree yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eshi tsei 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo tsei agbo ni tsii.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Plantains thrive in rich, dark soil that holds moisture well but allows extra water to drain away. If water collects and forms stagnant ponds on your field for days, the plantain roots will rot and die.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ shi ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni efee ŋshɔi ni ekã shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo. Plantain shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young plantain plants early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi plantain dumɔwui lɛ mra No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Young plantain suckers grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nourishment. Keeping the base clear gives the young plant the strength to build a thick stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha tso bibioo lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛfee tso bibioo ni mli tse.

english: Why do stray animals and pests prefer to eat my farm crops instead of the wild grass surrounding my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni elaaje kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Farm crops are bred to be tender, sweet, and full of water and nutrients, which makes them much easier to digest and more attractive to animals than tough, bitter wild grass.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ koni efee bɔdɔɔ, eŋɔɔɔ, ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaaye, ni kooloi sumɔɔ waa fe koo mli jwɛi ni wa ni mli edɔ.

english: What natural barrier crops can I plant around my farm borders to deter animals from destroying my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii manyɛ madu yɛ ehe? Okwaafoi husui koni kooloi akafite miŋmɔshi nibii

english: Planting rows of hot pepper, lemongrass, or thick thorny shrubs like bougainvillea around your farm boundary creates a natural barrier that animals dislike smelling, tasting, or walking through.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ, lemongrass, loo tsei bibii ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli tamɔ bougainvillea ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he. Okwaafoi akui lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni kooloi sumɔɔɔ ni amɛnuɔ he, amɛnuɔ he, loo amɛnyiɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water loss, while yellowing indicates that the plant is stressed from lack of water or needs nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground even when the stem and leaves above ground look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Underground root rot usually happens when the soil retains too much standing water, which cuts off oxygen to the roots and allows harmful soil fungi to attack the tubers without immediately showing on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni ejieee amɛhe kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces your crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in weak stems, smaller leaves, and a lower total yield than properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, baai bibii, kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni adu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like calcium during the flowering stage, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ, ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do major pest attacks like armyworms happen suddenly in some years but not every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo, tamɔ asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mɛi babaoo trukaa yɛ afii komɛi amli shi jeee daa afi lɛ?

english: Pest outbreaks occur when specific weather conditions—such as a dry spell followed by sudden rain—trigger rapid pest breeding while temporarily reducing the populations of birds and beneficial insects that normally eat them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi komɛi, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be, nyiɛ sɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa. Ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okpoi kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni daa amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ ayibɔ baa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How can I prepare my land to safely replant crops after a severe pest outbreak wiped out my previous harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe koni adu nii ekoŋŋ? Beni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni naa wa kpata mi tsutsu ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: You should clear and burn or bury infected plant debris, turn the soil to expose hidden pest larvae to the sun, and rotate to a completely different crop family that those specific pests cannot eat.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tso ni hela emɔ lɛ ni oshã loo ofu. Tsakemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe. ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo tsei awekui sɔrɔtoi kwraa ni nakai kooloi lɛ nyɛŋ aye lɛ amli.

english: Why is it harmful to plant the exact same crop on the same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and creates a permanent breeding ground for soil-borne diseases and pests that feed on that specific plant.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ daa.

english: How do shade trees benefit sensitive crops during the hottest months of the year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Shade trees reduce heat stress by lowering leaf temperature, blocking harsh direct sunlight, retaining moisture in the topsoil, and breaking the impact of heavy rains that wash away young plants.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ baa dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi kɛtsɔ baa lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni baa shi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okpãtã nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ hiɛ.

english: How do I know if the maize seeds I bought at the local market will grow well before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ?

english: You can do a simple water test or a germ test. Good, healthy seeds usually sink in water, while damaged or weak seeds float. Testing a small batch in a moist cloth for a few days shows you how many will sprout before you spend time planting your whole farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka nu okwɛ loo oka helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ okwɛ. Akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ woɔ nu mli be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni efite loo ni bɛ hewalɛ baafo nu lɛ mli. Kaai bibii Gbii fioo komɛi ni akɛ mama ni mli efɔ baawo mli lɛ baatsɔɔ bo bɔ ni mɛi babaoo baakwɛ̃ dani okɛ be adu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant in my nursery fail to sprout at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of air, moisture, and warmth to wake up. If the soil is too dry, too packed down, or watered too heavily, the seeds can either dry out or drown and rot before they ever break through the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui hia kɔɔyɔɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu babaoo Dumɔwui baanyɛ agbi loo amɛgboi ni amɛgboi dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with big leaves, but producing small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or leaf nutrients, they spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients ensure the energy goes down into making big tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei loo foliar niyenii babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa hewalɛ shwereɔ bulbs wuji.

english: I water my tomato plants every single day, so why are they turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mikɛ nu haa mitato tsei lɛ daa gbi. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ tomatoi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water smothers their roots so they cannot breathe or pick up food from the dirt. Just like drought, overwatering stresses the roots and causes leaves to turn yellow and droop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso ko nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi eshishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu loo amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu hɔmɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a defense reaction when tiny insects like thrips or mites are sucking the juice from the under-side of the leaves, or when the plant is stressed by extreme heat and lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ he kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites nu nu kɛjɛ baai lɛ ashishi. aloo be mli ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to treat my seed yams before putting them into the soil mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oha ŋmeii niyenii dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Treating seed yams with wood ash or fungicide acts like a protective shield. It prevents soil insects and rot-causing germs from attacking the yam piece while it is trying to sprout in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsu nii kɛtsa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua sweet potato fãi lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they act like crowded children fighting over one plate of food. They compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaafee ehe tamɔ gbekɛbii ni miitao niyenii kome. Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo faaa.

english: What is the best way to spread out and dry my harvested pepper so it does not spoil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akpa lɛ ashwãa ni agbiɔ koni ekafite?

english: Peppers should be spread out in a single, thin layer on clean mats or raised drying platforms in direct sunlight. If you pile them up thick, heat and moisture get trapped inside, causing mold and rot to destroy them.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ chili lɛ ashwã ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yɛ tsɔne ni he tse loo nɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛto he yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ Heat kɛ moisture lɛ emɔ emli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ amɛ.

english: How can I keep tiny insects from destroying my maize after I put it in the storehouse?
ga: Ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkagbee shi. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpata ŋmãa hiɛ beni akɛto nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive on wet grain. Make sure your maize is completely dry before storage, keep the storehouse cool and leak-free, and use approved grain protection dust or airtight bags to suffocate pests.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛto. Kɛto shĩa lɛ mli ni ejɔ ni nɔ ko akaho. Ni okɛ sũ loo vacuum kotoku ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛmu tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs food before I start planting my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani mabɔi miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dumɔ?

english: If your previous crops were stunted, had pale leaves, or produced very low yield, the soil is tired. Looking at leaf color and testing soil texture or taking samples to an extension officer will tell you what nutrients are missing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ egbɔjɔ, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ahe su ni oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo okɛ nɔkwɛmɔnii ko baaha extension nitsulɔi lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo nɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the Harmattan dry wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves to save water during drought periods. Planting shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia around your cocoa blocks hot, dry winds and keeps the soil moist longer, helping leaves stay green.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo glicidia ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Cocoa yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ ahiɔ shi eŋɔli.

english: Those are fall armyworms, which feed on the fresh inner leaves (the whorl) of young maize. Applying recommended pesticides, neem extract, or wood ash directly into the center of the plant early in the morning stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Amɛji fall armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai heei (rings) lɛ. tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii Neem Extract Loo, tso sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ tuber bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of root tubers. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers allows the plant to send nutrients down into expanding the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛba shi koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce smaller fruit bunches when I let all the young shoots grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) steal nutrients, light, and water from the main mother plant. Pruning extra suckers so that only one or two remain leaves enough energy for the main plant to produce large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tso lɛ) juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni afoɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni eko loo enyɔ pɛ ashwɛ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry winds, or irregular watering, which stops pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Enɛ haa pollin lɛ kpaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds heavy-eating crops like maize during the following season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking holds leaves high up in the sun while keeping them off damp ground where fungal diseases can easily rot them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite oya lɛ.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer burn and kill my crops when I put it right next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that suck water out of tender plant roots if placed too close. Applying fertilizer in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem prevents root burn.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli loo yɛ line ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ akashã.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out the topsoil and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting for steady, continuous rain ensures young roots stay wet and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni eyaa nɔ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying early with neem oil or appropriate insecticides deters these insects and keeps new leaves growing flat and healthy.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai heei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow and rot whenever my farm stays flooded with water for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nu baaho miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When land stays waterlogged, air gets trapped out of the soil, causing roots to suffocate, stop taking up nutrients, and eventually turn yellow or rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Ekpaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egboɔ.

english: Can I still grow crops on my swampy farm land without the plants dying from too much water?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lolo ni tsei lɛ gboii yɛ nu babaoo hewɔ?

english: Yes, you can farm on swampy land by digging drainage channels to lead excess water away, or by constructing raised mounds and ridges so crop roots stay above the standing water.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli yɛ jwɛi shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu tsɔji ni oootsi koni ojie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ gɔji kɛ ŋmeii ni afee koni tsei shishifãi ahi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Which crops grow best in low valley areas where water collects easily during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishigbɛ he ni nu buaa ehe naa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Valley bottoms that hold water are ideal for crops like swamp rice, sugarcane, and taro (cocoyam), as these crops love high moisture levels unlike cassava or cocoa.
ga: Jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ taro (kookoo), ejaakɛ nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ ŋmei loo kookoo lɛ, nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ sumɔɔ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ.

english: Why should I ask an agricultural officer to test my land before I buy seeds and start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni eka mishikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛ dani mahe dumɔwui ni mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Testing your land reveals what nutrients your soil is missing and whether it holds too much water or acid, saving you money from buying wrong fertilizers or planting crops that will fail.
ga: Kɛ́ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ lɛ, ebaana niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛji nu loo acid babaoo yɛ mli. Ehaa onáa shika kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni ooohe loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite lɛ akwɛmɔ mli.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is too wet for planting cassava?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ adu ŋmei?

english: Cassava roots rot easily in soggy soil. If water stays pooled on the surface for days after rain, or if a small test hole fills with underground water quickly, the land is too wet for cassava.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Kɛji nu tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ, Aloo kɛji kaa bu lɛ ji bibioo Akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu eyi mli obɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmei.

english: What makes the soil on one part of my plot good for crops while soil just a short distance away yields nothing?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ wooo yibii kwraa.

english: Soil properties like underground water levels, sand or clay content, and past land use vary across short distances; testing helps identify these hidden differences so you put the right crop on the right patch.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ŋwɛi ŋã loo shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ srɔtoi yɛ gbɛ kukuji amli. Kaa yeɔ ebuaa ni ayɔseɔ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my soil dry out and turn hard like concrete just a few days after heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Clay-heavy soil bakes hard under the sun when dry. Adding organic matter like decayed crop leaves or poultry manure softens the clay and helps the ground retain moisture without becoming hard.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii shãa waa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi beni egbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tsei ahe baai ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ais efeee.

english: How does water sitting on my farm lead to more leaf diseases on my vegetables?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha foliary helai babaoo aba mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ?

english: Excess water creates high humidity around plant leaves, which provides the perfect damp environment for fungal spores to spread, causing leaf spots and black rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa tsei lɛ ahe, ni no ji he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ. Ekɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa.

english: Where does all the fertilizer I apply go after a heavy downpour washes across my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ni egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yaa?

english: Heavy rain on waterlogged or sloping ground causes leaching and runoff, which washes fertilizer off the surface or pushes it too deep into the soil for crop roots to reach.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ haa nu hoɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsiɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither and collapse when I transplant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young transplants have fragile roots that cannot draw up water fast enough to survive strong sun heat; providing shade with fronds for the first week allows root systems to recover.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni adu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ wo baai lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps the plant recover and produce bigger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ toi wuji.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to plant vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai?

english: Healthy soil feels dark and crumbly, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and contains earthworms. If water sits on top of your land for days after heavy rain, the soil needs compost or organic matter to improve drainage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ duŋ ni egbɔjɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Ehe miihia ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ahi mli koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds the yam leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. When leaves get full sunlight, they produce more energy, which leads to bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Okɛ sweet potato baai lɛ awo ŋwɛi koni emɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face extreme stress, such as very high heat, dry soil, or sudden heavy rainfall. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. They also hide insect pests and diseases that can spread to your plants and reduce your total harvest yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ hu teeɔ ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rainfall leaves the soil flooded for a long time, the roots choke and fungal rot sets in, destroying the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baatsi ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baaye nɔ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them during the dry season?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shield that blocks the hot sun. It traps moisture in the soil longer so your crops do not dry out quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩii oya.

english: What makes my cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown during the Harmattan?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ Harmattan beaŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of leaves faster than the roots can drink from the dry ground. Planting shade trees around young cocoa helps break the harsh dry wind and retain air moisture.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ naa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I change the type of crop I plant on my field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Rotating crops prevents specific pests and diseases from building up in the soil year after year. It also stops one single nutrient from being completely depleted from your land.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi akabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kome pɛ akafite oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help protect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: A greenhouse is a frame covered with clear plastic or net that creates a safe house for crops. It protects sensitive plants like tomatoes from heavy downpours, intense direct sun, and damaging insect pests.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsɔne ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ shĩa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them provides living canopy protection and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning pale yellow near the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the key nutrient plants use to build green foliage, and when the soil is depleted, the plant pulls nutrients from older leaves to support new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot inside the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava root rot is caused by fungi that thrive when water collects and sits around the roots for too long during heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fitemɔ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he lɛ mli. shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow while providing a secondary crop harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa kɛfataa ŋmãa ni ji enyɔ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ he.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my pepper plants drop off before producing pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi, tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when the soil is ready for me to sow my maize seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until after two or three deep, reliable rains have thoroughly soaked the topsoil. Planting too early in dry ground causes seeds to dry out or germinate unevenly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close forces the stems to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough underground space to swell and form thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛbaafu ni efee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and produce small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiiwo yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts on a plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, while groundnuts naturally restore nitrogen to the earth. Rotating groundnuts into that field refreshes the soil quality naturally without over-relying on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa adebɔɔ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmeii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ tsɔ.

english: Why are some of the seeds I saved from last year's harvest not sprouting when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their power to sprout if they were stored in humid conditions, damaged by insect pests, or harvested from fruits that were not fully mature.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛshweremɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kplukai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite loo akpaa kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni ekwɛko jogbaŋŋ lolo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant timber trees on my farm if they take so many years to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ amɛheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛdaraa?

english: Planting timber trees acts like a savings account for your future or your children, while also helping to mark your land boundaries, protect your farm from heavy winds, and keep the soil cool and moist for other crops.
ga: Tsoi ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikatoohe kɛha bo loo obii lɛ awɔsɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ husui. Buu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do some farmers plant shade trees inside their cocoa farms instead of clearing all the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaajie tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa trees from the harsh sun, help the soil retain water during dry seasons, and drop leaves that rot and turn into natural manure for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen nutrients in the soil or need more water. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer early will feed the plants and turn them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo he miihia amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant maize on the same patch of land every season, why does my harvest get smaller each year?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same land every year drains the exact same food out of the soil. Rotating your maize with groundnuts or cowpeas puts good nutrients back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it better to use animal dung or bought chemical fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ kooloi ashishifã baatsu nii loo akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baahe ni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Animal dung improves your soil for many years by helping it hold water and stay healthy, while chemical fertilizer gives crops a quick boost. Using manure regularly builds good soil that lasts.
ga: Manure haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo afii babaoo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when there are weeds growing around them?
