ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo beni jwɛi ebɔle mihe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops. Keeping your farm clean lets your crops eat well and grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: When too many small shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight over the soil's food and water. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main stem grows big, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa bibii ni amɛbɔleɔ Plantain kome lɛ fa tsɔ. Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their roots crowd each other under the ground and fight for nutrients, resulting in many small, thin roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ bulb agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Black pod disease spreads when the air around your cocoa trees is too damp and shaded. Pruning extra branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and wind dry out the trees, stopping the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni amɛyɛ hulutsoo. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbi kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. tsei ni ekpa fitemɔ

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready to harvest from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni obaanyɛ ole be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I stop grasscutters and other rodents from eating my young cassava plants?
ga: Makpa jwɛifolɔi kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Animals like grasscutters love tender cassava stalks. You can protect your field by clearing the surrounding bush to destroy their hiding spots, setting traps along their trails, or planting barrier crops like chili peppers around the edge of your farm.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi sumɔɔ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oyale lɛ he kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. koni amɛfite amɛteemɔhe lɛ Okɛ tsɔnei awo gbɛ lɛ he. Aloo dumɔ nibii ni tsiɔ mɔ gbɛ, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and getting full of tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with small holes are often caused by pests like Fall Armyworms feeding on the plant. Early spraying with recommended organic extracts like neem oil or approved insecticides helps control them before they destroy the crop yield.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa, ni akɛ nɔ ko ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni ajie lɛ kpo mra, tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep birds from destroying my rice field when the grains start to mature?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni okpoi akafite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Birds attack rice when grains start filling out. You can deter them by installing reflective shiny tapes, setting up scarecrows, or organizing with neighboring farmers to plant at the same time so bird damage is spread out.
ga: Okpoi tutuaa ŋmãa kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ bɔi eyimɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. Too gbeyeishemɔ ko Aloo okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ afata he koni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli. amɛfee ekome koni amɛha okpoi lɛ agbɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ amɛshwã.

english: If I build a small house or storage shed on my farm, can I safely leave big shade trees standing right next to it?
ga: Kɛ mima shia bibioo loo ŋmɔ mli tsũ lɛ mashi tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mimasɛi. Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, you can keep mature trees near structures if you trim heavy branches that overhang the roof and ensure the roots do not damage the foundation. Leaving trees provides cooling shade and shields your building from strong windstorms.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei wuji ahi tsũi ahe. Kɛji ofolɔ tsei niji ni tsii ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ tsũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ Ni okwɛ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite shishitoo lɛ. Tsei ni oooha amɛha hulutsoo ni obu otsu lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do some trees on my farm start looking weak after I clear all the bushes around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When surrounding bush is suddenly cleared, exposed trees can suffer from sun shock and root disturbance. Adding mulch around the base of the tree and avoiding deep digging near its trunk helps it adapt to the open sunlight.
ga: Beni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ trukaa lɛ, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa mɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná tsei ni ajie amɛ kpo lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ he, ni ajie sũ ni afoɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to cut down all large wild trees on my land before planting crops, or should I leave some standing?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ mafolɔ koo mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ ashwie shi dani madu nii? Aloo esa akɛ mamɔ shi?

english: It is usually better to leave selected large trees standing. These trees provide essential shade for crops like cocoa, prevent soil erosion during heavy rains, and act as windbreaks to protect your farm from strong storms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tso ni eda ni ahala lɛ ni edamɔ shi. Tsei nɛɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, ni amɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ofee tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ahum ni naa wa he.

english: How can I help my crops grow stronger and stay green during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the ground cool and traps moisture in the dirt, helping your plants stay healthy and continue growing even when rain is scarce.
ga: Mulching around Kɛji okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) ha onibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in dark, wet conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air reach the trunk, along with removing infected pods immediately, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ewo duŋ, ni efɔ lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough for planting vegetables, or if it needs extra food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai akwɛmɔ loo ehe miihia ni akɛ niyenii krokomɛi afata he?

english: Good soil is usually dark, crumbly, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms. If your soil feels dry, hard, or pale, mixing in compost or well-rotted manure will add nutrients and make it healthy for planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su tsuɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, ewa, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he ni eha efee nɔ ni hi kɛha otso lɛ.

english: Why should I space my crops out instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he kroko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing gives every crop enough room to grow big leaves and produce maximum yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ baai wuji ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying even when there is sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate foliage and small root systems that easily scorch in direct sunlight; planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them from heat stress while they establish.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifã bibioo ko ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava directly alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ adu ŋmei tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Cassava grows aggressively and aggressively competes with cocoa seedlings for soil nutrients and water, so it is better to plant less competitive shade crops like plantain or banana.
ga: Cassava daa oya ni ekɛ cocoa dumɔwui yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni akaŋshii bɛ mli, tamɔ plantains loo banana.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal pathogen that thrives in high humidity and excessive shade, spreading quickly during wet conditions if dead or infected pods are not cleared.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ,.

english: Why do the leaves and stems on some of my cocoa trees start swelling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Swollen shoot disease is a viral infection spread by tiny insects called mealybugs; infected trees must be safely removed to prevent the virus from spreading throughout your farm.
ga: Bud swollen hela ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing out of the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those shoots, called chupons, suck water and nutrients away from the main trunk and branches, reducing the tree's ability to produce flowers and pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsei akutsei nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does pruning branches actually help my crop yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and airflow, which reduces humidity where diseases live while encouraging fresh flower formation.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi yɛ hei ni helai yɔɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni fɔfɔi heei baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods form during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees experience water stress from dry weather, they drop flowers to conserve water and survive until the rains return.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ, Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are typically a sign that the soil is low in essential nutrients like nitrogen, which can be fixed by applying manure or cocoa-specific fertilizers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni abaanyɛ asaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some cocoa varieties produce pods much earlier in the year than mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo henɔi komɛi miiwo ŋmɔtɔ mra kwraa fe mi nɔ lɛ yɛ afi nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties are bred specifically to mature early, flower sooner, and tolerate dry spells better than older, traditional cocoa varieties.
ga: Atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛshwere oya. Ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa fe blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ.

english: Why should I avoid picking cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ahe be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Green pods contain immature beans with low sugar and oil content, which prevents proper fermentation and results in poor-quality cocoa beans.
ga: Green pods lɛ mli ŋmeii ni edako ni sugar kɛ fɔ faaa yɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the ground has too much standing water, which stops the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure or decayed leaves to my farm make crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi loo baai ni egboi fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Animal manure and decayed leaves act as natural soil food that improves the ground's ability to hold water during hot dry spells and slowly releases nutrients to crop roots.
ga: Koolooi ashwiei kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ yaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting on raised dirt mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. The leaves use sunlight to produce the food needed to grow large tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small worms eating holes right in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender middle leaves of corn plants. They feed on the growing point of the plant and must be caught early to prevent damage to the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Amɛyeɔ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ, ni esa akɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra. Koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They require partial shade from larger trees or plantain plants to protect their leaves and keep the soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo dumɔwui adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light rain and wind even when they look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that carry heavy weight. Tiny pests in the soil can damage these roots, making the plant unstable and unable to hold itself up when bearing heavy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsii. kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata shishifãi nɛɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ehe kɛ́ ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures get too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wo la tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil and help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛye amɛbua ŋmãa lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my crops are very small rather than waiting until they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early prevents the young crop from becoming permanently stunted.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee mɛi ni shwieɔ shi daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and curling up before the stalks even produce ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ toi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is being attacked by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which drain nutrients from the plant before it can form ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli dani enyɛɔ ekwɛɔ toi lɛ miitutua lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly during the hot afternoon even when the soil feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden afternoon wilting in moist soil is often caused by soil-borne diseases like bacterial wilt, which block the plant's internal veins so water cannot reach the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ bacteria wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shwane mli ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ anaa. Koni nu akashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe

english: Why does cassava produce large tubers in some parts of my farm but small, woody roots in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ? Shi tsei shishifãi bibii yɛ hei krokomɛi?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil to expand its roots into thick tubers; hard or compacted soil restricts root growth, making them small and woody.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cassava koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Ha efee bibioo ni efee tso.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I plant on the same plot without leaving the land to rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mishiŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni miyajɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to rebuild them, while allowing soil pests to accumulate over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛma amɛ ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my stored maize seeds not sprouting when I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Stored seeds lose their ability to sprout if they were exposed to heat, dampness, or insect pests during storage, which damages the living embryo inside the grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ baafite fɔmɔ kotoku ni hiɛ kã ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my cowpeas so the rain does not ruin the flowers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsina ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni nugbɔ lɛ akafite fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Planting cowpeas towards the end of the main rainy season allows them to grow with residual soil moisture while ensuring they flower during dry periods so rain does not knock off the blossoms.
ga: Cowpeas ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ naagbee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha jwɛi lɛ agbi bɔni afee ni nugbɔ akahanɛ amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when I grow them directly under big mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛdu yɛ mango tso agbo ko shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants require direct, full sunlight to produce and hold onto flowers; heavy shade prevents them from making enough energy to grow fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɛ mli. Shade ni mli wa lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛdu aduawai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by strong sunlight; plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential temporary shade and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many blossoms but only a few turn into healthy pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ feɔ fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can support, but excessive flower drop happens when there are not enough insect pollinators around or when soil nutrients are low.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my yam tubers start to rot if I leave them in the soil past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Once a yam plant finishes its life cycle and dries up, leaving the tubers in wet ground exposes them to soil bacteria and fungi that feed on mature roots.
ga: Beni sweet potato tsei lɛ gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ shishifãi ni eda lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast during the dry season even when I water them by hand every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine shwieɔ nɔ daa leebi moŋ.

english: Light hand watering only wets the very top layer of soil, which quickly evaporates in hot weather. Crops need deep watering so moisture reaches deep into the soil where roots grow, helping them survive hot dry spells.
ga: Nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni baaho oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni mli kwɔ he miihia tsei koni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do crops like pepper and tomato rot during heavy rain while cassava keeps growing fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers have delicate root systems that suffocate and rot when soil stays flooded with water. Cassava has a strong, hardy root system that can tolerate wet conditions and store excess food underground.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baaha sũ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ebaagbo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baanyɛ adamɔ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ anaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when they lack consistent water. Heat causes stress, so the plant drops flowers to save its energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu bɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Dɔlɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I plant them right at the start of the rainy season instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa waa waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ lɛ?

english: The first rains trigger a release of nutrients like nitrogen that built up in dry soil, giving young seeds a natural energy boost. Early planting also lets roots spread before heavy downpours wash away soil.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen jeɔ kpo, ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ Dumɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu gbɛɔ eshwaa dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops stay small and produce tiny fruits when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed, leading to bigger stems and larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ agboi kɛ aduawai agboi baa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that maize lacks nitrogen, the main food it uses to build healthy green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil, so adding fertilizer or manure helps restore the plant's color and strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni akɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every time I plant the same crop on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly. Rotating crops like maize with beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and bigger than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so their roots absorb water and plant food faster than cultivated crops. Removing weeds early stops them from stealing sunlight and food away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra leaves and small side branches from my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ mi aduawai lɛ amli?

english: Trimming unnecessary leaves and branches redirects the plant's energy away from growing leaves and straight into growing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Baai kɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa he kroko kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. kɛmiiya aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get covered in mold if I bag them right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii haa ehe kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli beni mikpaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain hidden moisture inside them. Bagging wet grains traps this water, creating a moist environment where mold and insects multiply rapidly, so grains must be thoroughly sun-dried before storage.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee amɛmli. Nibii ni efɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ baamɔ nu nɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo yɔɔ mli oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto.

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and cannot tolerate direct, heavy sunlight. They need partial shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to shelter them and keep the soil humid while their root system develops.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛná he ko ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop lose almost all its leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ fite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant to protect the edible tubers storing energy underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ehiɔ shi ni ekɛbuɔ eshishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ ahe, ni nomɛi kɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or well-decomposed animal manure helps the leaves regain their deep green color and boosts stalk growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛbatsɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers dry up and drop off without bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when plants experience sudden water stress. Regular watering at the base and light mulching help keep the soil root zone cool and stabilize flower development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf distortion and keeps the plant growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut roots rot under the soil when heavy rains flood the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need oxygen from the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain causes long-term waterlogging, air is cut off, causing the roots to suffocate and rot in the soaked soil.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Abaafo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like an insulating blanket that slows down water evaporation, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from springing up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it risky for my farm yield if I plant maize on the exact same soil every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oshara yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo he kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients year after year and encourages maize-specific pests to stay in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ewo ŋmãa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the young shoots growing around the foot of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for food, light, and water. Removing excess suckers leaves the main stem strong enough to produce large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine (tsoji) kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very small fruits when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their foliage shades each other out and their roots fight for nutrients and water. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough light and nutrition to bear large fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed for the plant to produce large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ ashɛ amɛtso lɛ he. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni tsei afee ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Planting seeds too close together causes crowding, forcing crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin stems and poor yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Watering early in the morning allows the roots to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, preventing rapid evaporation and heat stress on the leaves.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Etsiɔ la ni hoɔ oya kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs fertilizer before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu tsei?

english: If your soil appears pale, turns hard easily, or produced crops with yellowing leaves and slow growth in previous seasons, it is low in essential nutrients and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ewaa oya loo ewoɔ tsei ni baai yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for maize afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What can I cover the ground with to keep my crops from drying out quickly in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dried grass, leaves, or crop leaves—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the soil and cools down root zones.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the middle leaves and stalks of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest common in Ghana that burrows into the growing center of maize plants and requires targeted pest management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ebiɔ ni akwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is a key sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that stunts growth and lowers crop yields.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ yɛ. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haaa dalɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight; they require shade from plantains or larger shade trees to protect their leaves from scorching during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji amli koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even during weeks when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow strong, acting as strong competitors even when water is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔ ni he wa yɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is usually a sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the younger leaves at the top to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant saves its energy by dropping blossoms instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sun so they can make more food for the plant, and it keeps the leaves off the damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases from ruining the leaves.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni amɛfee niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa from sunburn and heat stress until the plants are mature enough to handle direct light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, groundnuts release this nitrogen into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why do my crops look burnt and withered after I apply fertilizer right at the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer acts like salt; when placed directly against the stem, it pulls water out of the plant roots and burns them. Fertilizer should always be placed a small distance away from the plant stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni eshãa amɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni muji tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young corn plants during the day and eat through the soft growing leaves, leaving holes and waste behind.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ amli amɛyeɔ nii. Eshiɔ bu kɛ jwɛi yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the ground fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, fungal diseases easily infect and rot the cassava tubers beneath the surface.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, Fungal helai baanyɛ atswa cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why does the purple-flowered weed called Striga attach itself to my cereal crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ko ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ striga lɛ ekpɛtɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic plant that cannot make enough food on its own. It latches onto the roots of maize or sorghum to suck out water and nutrients, which leaves your crop stunted and pale.
ga: Striga ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi ahe koni ekɛjie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rains are no longer predictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Beni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Instead of planting after the very first rain, wait until the soil stays moist a few inches deep for two to three days in a row so seeds have enough steady water to germinate and survive.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ 2-3 inch gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to cut and harvest my mature crops quickly instead of leaving them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ ni mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ oya moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting promptly prevents crops from over-ripening, being destroyed by sudden weather changes, or being damaged by pests and diseases while still in the field.
ga: Nikpamɔ oya lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ fe nine. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ beni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why is timing so important as soon as my crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be he hiaa waa kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ pɛ?

english: Delaying harvest exposes mature crops to rain and field hazards; cutting them at the right time ensures you lock in their best quality before post-harvest handling.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ aná nugbɔ ni ebaafite ŋmɔji. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ be naa lɛ haa onine shɛɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ dani otsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: What is the proper way to dry my harvested crops after cutting them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ mikpamɔ lɛ beni afo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Proper drying involves spreading crops evenly on clean tarpaulins or raised drying mats in direct sunlight, ensuring they are kept completely clear of dirt and rain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he ji ni agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Okɛto tarp ni he tse loo tsɔne ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa muji kɛ nugbɔ bɛ tsei lɛ ahe kwraa.

english: Why is drying my produce properly just as important as growing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbimɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa tamɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbimɔ he hiaa lɛ lɛ? Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ?

english: Correct drying removes internal moisture, which stops rot and mold, preserves the crop's color and taste, and allows you to store or sell it for a good price.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kpaa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe su kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔmɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa okɛtoɔ loo ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara kpakpa.

english: Is it alright to leave my crops unattended outside while they are drying?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni kwɛɔ nɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: No, because sudden rain showers can hit the crops when you are not around, soaking them and ruining days of drying work.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni obɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ agbimɔ nitsumɔ lɛ gbii babaoo.

english: What happens if rain hits my crop while it is drying outside?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛmiigbi yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain hits a drying crop, moisture gets soaked back inside, creating perfect conditions for mold, rot, and discoloration that ruin the harvest.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ, Fɛ̃i baaku esɛɛ kɛba mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ su tsakemɔ ni yeɔ emuu ni fiteɔ yibiiwoo lɛ baa.

english: What happens if my crop gets wet from rain, dries in the sun, and then gets wet again?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli? Egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli Ni no sɛɛ lɛ eku esɛɛ eba ni efɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Repeated wetting and drying destroys the crop structure, causes deep internal rotting and fungal growth, and completely ruins its market value.
ga: Nibii ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ baafite bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ha lɛ Enɛ haa mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ baa. ni efite jarayeli jara lɛ kwraa.

english: How can I protect my produce from sudden rainfall during the drying process?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu minibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Spread your crops on a strong tarpaulin that can easily be folded up or covered with a plastic sheet as soon as rain clouds appear.
ga: Gbalamɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ tarp ni wa ni abaanyɛ abɔle he loo akɛ plastic aha nɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ atatui je kpo pɛ.

english: Why do my crops develop mold and spoil even after I dried them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: If the crops were repeatedly hit by rain during the drying phase, hidden moisture remains trapped inside, causing mold to grow later during storage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ tsei shii abɔ Yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baakã he ahi mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii baa sɛɛ mli beni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How does moisture damage the market price I get for my harvested produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo be fiteɔ jarayeli jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛha mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers reject or pay very little for crops damaged by water because dampness causes bad odors, dark spots, fungus, and poor flavor.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ loo amɛwoɔ nyɔmɔ fioo ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu efite lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo, ŋmɔlɔ diji, ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii baa.

english: How do I know which rice variety will grow best and yield well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa henɔi ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties are suited for different soil types and moisture levels. Varieties bred for local conditions in Ghana grow faster, resist common local pests, and produce strong grains that give higher yield and fetch better prices at the market.
ga: Omɔ henɔ fɛɛ henɔ sa kɛha shikpɔji kɛ hulutsoo be srɔtoi. Hei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ kɛha maŋ shihilɛi yɛ Ghana lɛ daa oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ekɛ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ baa jara nɔ.

english: Why do some rice crops ripen evenly while others have both green and brown grains at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi shwereɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ fɛɛ kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Uneven ripening happens when seeds are planted at different depths, when water is unevenly spread across the field, or if mixed seed varieties are planted together. Using certified, single-variety seeds and leveling your field ensures all plants mature at the exact same time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ mlijaa ejaaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he kome Dumɔwui komekomei ni awo he odaseyeli ni okɛaatsu nii ni okɛ ohegbɛ lɛ afee ekome lɛ baaha tsei lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: How do I tell the exact time my rice is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn golden-yellow while the lower stems remain slightly green. Harvesting at this stage prevents grains from shattering onto the ground or being eaten by birds.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 feɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔŋ fioo. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmaa lɛ naa koni ekagbala loo okpoi akaye lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to dry my harvested rice before sending it to a mill?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ dani akɛmaje ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ?

english: Yes, freshly harvested rice contains too much water, making the grains soft. If milled wet, the grains crush into flour and break easily; drying paddy evenly on clean mats until it is hard ensures whole, clean grains after milling.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Ehaa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli efɔ lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ baatsɔ ashikishaŋ ni ebaakumɔ oya. Agbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ebaawa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ mli tseɔ beni agbe lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested grain so that insects do not destroy it before I sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato? Bɔni afee ni kooloi akafite lɛ dani ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Insects thrive on moisture and air. Store your well-dried grain in airtight hermetic bags or clean containers raised off the ground on wooden pallets to keep pests and moisture out without needing harsh chemicals.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Okɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo vacuum kotokui amli loo tsɛnsii ni he tse ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa atsu nii.

english: Why does my rice come out broken into small pieces after it goes through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii bibii beni etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain breakage happens if the rice was dried too quickly under extreme heat, harvested too late, or if the milling machine's rollers are set too tight. Drying rice in partial shade and adjusting the mill settings protects grain wholeness.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fãa lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa gĩ oya tsɔ yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. akpa sɛɛ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ ebɔ he waa tsɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be fioo ko yɔɔ mli ni atsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmãa lɛ emuuyeli he.

english: Why do I find so many small stones and husks inside my rice after milling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa tɛi bibii kɛ ŋmeii? Mɛɛ shika yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli beni ashɛre lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Stones enter the crop when paddy is dried directly on bare soil, and excess husks remain if the mill's blower or sieve is dirty or broken. Drying grain on clean tarpaulins and ensuring the operator checks and cleans the mill machinery keeps the final product clean.
ga: Tɛi boteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã he ahi shi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo ŋmeii ni akɛfoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ mli ewo muji loo ekumɔ. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ kwɛɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni amɛtsumɔ he. koni naagbee nibii lɛ ahe atse

english: What causes rice grains to turn dark or discolored after harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa yibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Discoloration happens when wet, harvested rice is left piled in bags or heaps for too long before drying, causing heat build-up and fungal growth. Spreading rice out to dry immediately after cutting prevents grain spoiling and discoloration.
ga: Su tsakemɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmãa ni efɔ ni akpa lɛ yɛ kotokui loo ŋmãa ni ato mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani egbi. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa ni ŋmeii hu daa. Kɛ́ agbɛ ŋmãa lɛ ashwã ni egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ efiteɔ ni ehaaa ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or standing water that is too deep for young roots. Applying balanced fertilizer early and managing field water levels helps the plants produce green leaves that feed grain growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni ekã shi ni mli kwɔ tsɔ kɛha shishifãi bibii. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsuɔ nii mra Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni haa dumɔwui lɛ daa.

english: How does flooding my field help my rice crop grow better than weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu afua baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special roots that can take in air even when submerged in water, whereas most weed seeds drown and cannot grow underwater. Maintaining controlled water levels smothers weeds naturally and saves you labor.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ agbala kɔɔyɔɔ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli po. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nu shishi lɛ. Nu lɛ mlihilɛ ni akudɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaha okɛ nitsumɔ akatsu nii.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin roots that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or shade trees gives them the cooler temperature and leaf canopy they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ Adumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients needed to make the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep farming the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ mitsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground every season. If you do not put nutrients back using compost, manure, or fertilizer—or let the land rest—the soil gets tired and cannot feed new crops properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he ekoŋŋ—loo ohaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ—shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the middle of my maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-abele baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the central shoot of maize plants during the day. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract early on protects the crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ he ŋaawoo. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works very well. Maize grows tall quickly and is harvested in about three months, leaving space and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Shi he ko kɛ hulu la koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ akwɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to start before I put my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa koni madu dumɔwui?

english: Seeds need steady moisture in the soil to sprout and grow strong roots. Planting in dry soil after just one small rain can cause seeds to dry up and die underground before the true rain season starts.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aje shishi.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest before they spoil underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa dani amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. Leaving roots in the ground too long makes them hard, woody, or prone to rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi shishifãi lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. eji tso loo eyɛ mlɛo akɛ egboɔ

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil moist around the roots and giving partial shade during peak heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be fioo ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local climate and soil, so they absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Removing weeds early stops them from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation only. Saving and replanting those seeds results in mixed, weaker crops that produce much smaller cobs and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni abuɔ he ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tso ni efutu, ni egbɔjɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ, ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa lɛ baa.

english: How do I know which cocoa variety is best to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kookoo henɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties (like the Akokoabra) grow quickly and produce pods in about 2 to 3 years, while older traditional varieties take up to 5 years. Choosing the right variety depends on your local rainfall, soil type, and whether your farm gets high sun or heavy shade.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome (tamɔ Akokoabra) lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii enumɔ. Nɔ ni sa ni oooha lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ, kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ naa hulu loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it a good idea to plant different cocoa varieties together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooofee ekome kɛdu kookoo henɔi srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting different hybrid cocoa varieties together can improve natural pollination, resulting in more pods. It also protects your farm because if a disease attacks one variety, the other varieties may resist it and keep producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, cocoa hybrid henɔi ni akɛfee ekome ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pods babaoo. Ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ hu he. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ hela ko tutua kooloi srɔtoi lɛ eko lɛ, kooloi krokomɛi baanyɛ atsu nii ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: How many years does it take for a young cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso bibioo ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern high-yielding hybrid cocoa seedlings start flowering and bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting in the field, whereas older traditional cocoa types take between 4 to 6 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔii ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 6 dani ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if a new piece of land has good soil for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, rich in decaying leaves, and allows water to drain easily. If water sits on top of the ground forming deep mud for days after rain, the roots will rot and the cocoa will not perform well.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ baai ni egboi babaoo ni ehaa nu hoɔ oya. Kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efee sũ ni mli kwɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni kookoo lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I am preparing new land for cocoa, should I cut down all the big trees first?
ga: Kɛji akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo hee dumɔ Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: No, you should keep some large economic trees on the land. Cocoa trees thrive best when shaded from intense sun by large trees like Terminalia (Emire) or forest trees, which keep the soil cool and retain moisture during dry spells.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ shika helɛtemɔ tsei wuji ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cocoa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa mli kɛjɛɔ tsei ni eda tamɔ Terminalia (Emire) loo koo mli tsei amli, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa seedlings when expanding my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ miigbɛ mishwa?

english: Cocoa seedlings should ideally be planted 3 meters by 3 meters (about 10 feet apart). Proper spacing ensures the roots do not fight for food and light, while allowing enough room for air to flow between mature trees.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa dumɔwui lɛ mitai 3 x 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10 kɛjɛ amɛhe). Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akatswaa niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa hoɔ yɛ tsei wuji lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Yellowing leaves mean the plant is receiving too much direct heat and sun without enough shade or soil water to protect it.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ená dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baabu ehe.

english: What food crops can I plant alongside young cocoa trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii manyɛ makwɛ yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Planting plantain and cocoyam alongside young cocoa provides necessary shade and yields food for your household. Avoid planting cassava too close to cocoa because cassava roots suck up a lot of soil nutrients and choke cocoa roots.
ga: Plantains kɛ cocoa ni ooodu kɛfata cocoa bibii ahe lɛ baaha oná hulutsoo kɛ yibiiwoo ni he hiaa waa kɛha oshia lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots and branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tso ko ni ji ŋmeii kɛ eniji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or unwanted shoots (chupons) so the tree doesn't waste energy on useless leaves. It allows sunlight and air to reach the main trunk, helping the tree focus its strength on producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni ataooo (chupon) lɛ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: What can I do to help my cocoa trees produce more pods as they get older?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni maye mabua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo aba be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: To boost pod production, cocoa trees need regular weeding, timely pruning to control shade, protection from pests like capsid bugs, and balanced soil nutrients applied during the rainy season when the trees start flowering.
ga: Bɔni afee ni pod feemɔ aya hiɛ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ Cocoa tsei amli daa. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni akɛkudɔ hulutsoo Hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for healthy leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ ni mli wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and drop off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a self-defense trick to save water. By losing leaves, the plant reduces water loss and keeps its energy stored safely in the roots until rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ koni akɛbu nu he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhaa nu ni amɛlaajeɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my yam vines growing long leaves very fast, but the yams under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ baa kakadaji oya nɛkɛ? Shi yam ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure but not enough potassium, the plant spends all its strength growing leafy vines above ground instead of expanding the tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ bulbs eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like wooden trees, so their shallow roots struggle to hold heavy loads. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop helps carry the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua muji ni tsii. Tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etereɔ muji lɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the stems of my crops help them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ he fɛɛ he? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade cover that keeps soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaha nɔ

english: How can I tell if heavy rain is drowning my farm crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much water, their roots cannot breathe. You will see yellowing leaves, soft stems near the soil, and plants wilting even though the ground is completely wet.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Obaana kaadi ŋmɔŋ ko. Tso bibioo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ gboɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa po.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in water. Without steady moisture, the plant sheds flowers to protect itself.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu tsakemɔi trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛji hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he.

english: Why do the leaves on my garden eggs have small white powders underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: That white powder is a common fungal disease called powdery mildew. It thrives in warm, humid air and blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf, which slows down plant growth.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni etsĩ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in full sun. Fast-growing plantains provide big, broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants while they establish deep roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to the land without needing costly chemical fertilizers right away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehiaaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant my crops on raised mounds instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Planting on raised soil mounds prevents rainwater from sitting around the crop's base. The slope lets excess water run off easily, protecting the root system from waterlogging and rot during heavy rain.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ nu naa koni ekatara tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Ramp lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ fitemɔ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my crops if rainwater settles and stays around their roots for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ shwie shi ni ehi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: When water sits around crop roots, it cuts off oxygen supply to the soil. This causes root decay, turns leaves yellow, and can eventually kill the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ nu bɔle tso shishifãi ahe lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo.

english: How does a soil mound help direct water away from my plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: A mound elevates the plant above the ground level. Gravity forces the rainwater to flow down the sides of the mound and away from the root zone before it can collect.
ga: Gɔŋ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ nɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ afãi kɛyaa he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ dani ebua ehe naa.

english: Can I plant my plantain suckers on the same day that I dig them up from another farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gbi nɔŋŋ ni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kroko mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting freshly dug suckers on the same day is fine as long as you trim damaged roots and plant them into moist soil so they do not dry out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii heei ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ, kɛji akɛ ofo shishifãi ni efite lɛ ni okɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my freshly dug plantain suckers look weak right after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei ni mifo ehee lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Transplanted crops experience shock because their root roots are disturbed during uprooting. Once they establish new roots in the soil and take in water, they will bounce back and start growing.
