ga: Tsei ni adu lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ haoɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ amɛfee shishifãi heei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛmu nu lɛ Amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ni amɛbɔi dalɛ.

english: How long does a newly planted plantain sucker take before it starts showing new growth?
ga: Be enyiɛ plantain sucker ni adu ehee lɛ heɔ dani shweremɔ hee jeɔ shishi?

english: It usually takes a few weeks for the plantain sucker to settle its roots into the soil. After this establishment phase, you will see new green leaves shooting out from the center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani plantain suckers lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɛkɛ shishitoo be nɛɛ sɛɛ Obaana baai eŋɔli heei ni miijɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Can plantains still grow well if my farm land has a lot of rocks and stones?
ga: Ani plantains lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ tɛi babaoo?

english: Yes, plantains can grow in stony areas as long as you clear small spots, dig decent holes, and fill them with good topsoil or compost to give the early roots a strong start.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ lɛ, kɛji ojie he ko bibioo ko. Tsɔmɔmɔ bu ni sa. Ni okɛ ŋwɛi sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa afata he. Koni shishijee shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ

english: How do I prepare a small, rocky spot on my land so a plantain stem can survive?
ga: Masaa he bibioo ko. Nɛgbɛ tɛi yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi?

english: You need to dig out the loose rocks in that specific spot, make a wide planting hole, and mix rich soil or manure into the hole before placing the sucker inside.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa tɛi ni etse amɛhe lɛ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli. Feemɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛduɔ nii. Ni okɛ sũ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ afutu bu lɛ mli dani okɛ tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ nu lɛ awo mli.

english: What are the early signs I should look for to know my crop has successfully taken off?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni esa akɛ matao koni male kɛji ajie miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: The main sign that your crop has taken off is the appearance of fresh green leaf shoots in the center, showing the roots have begun drawing water and nutrients from the earth.
ga: Okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eba shi ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ebɔi nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jiemɔ.

english: Does planting on a small mound help if my soil is hard and difficult for roots to penetrate?
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ bibioo nɔ Ani ebaaye ebua kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni shishifãi lɛ amlibotemɔ wa?

english: Yes, building a mound creates a pocket of loose, aerated topsoil above the hard ground, making it much easier for young roots to spread and establish quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, gɔŋ ko maa haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛma shi oya.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Giving the crop nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant make food and regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛnáa su ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer is best applied 2 to 3 weeks after planting when young roots are ready to absorb nutrients, and always while the soil is moist to prevent the fertilizer from burning the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Beni shishifãi bibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akashã tsei lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, or a virus spread by insects. Treating for these tiny pests stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa Kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsamɔ Enɛɛmɛi baakpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant move calcium into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛwooo ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become tough and woody if I do not harvest them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tsei kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: After cassava reaches full maturity, the plant stops storing fresh starch in its roots and starts turning them into fibrous, woody tissue to support its growth, making the tubers hard to cook.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ eda kɛyashɛ ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmei hee ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni ebɔi lɛ tsakemɔ ni efeɔ tso mli ŋmei ni yeɔ ebuaa dalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ewa akɛ abaahoo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from lack of water, which causes the flower stems to weaken and fall before pollination takes place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani pollination baa.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, retains moisture so crops need less water, and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akaná nu babaoo ni amɛtsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye obɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables in the early morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs water deeply before heat evaporates it, giving plants enough moisture to survive the hot afternoon sun.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that filter strong sunlight and create a cool, moist environment for young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli aha kookoo bibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Keeping taller trees or planting plantains nearby creates shade and traps soil moisture, acting like a shield that keeps the young cocoa cool until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: Why does covering the bare ground around my pepper plants with dry grass keep them from drying out so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ koni amɛkagbi oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It protects the soil from direct heat, prevents water from evaporating into the air, and keeps the roots cool and moist during dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a corn plant are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for green leafy growth, so feeding the soil with poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔlii daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for my farm if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. Planting them alongside or after maize naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer for your corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu yɛ ŋmãa lɛ masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, will I harvest more cassava roots?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani makpa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They will grow tall and bushy above ground, but the tubers underground will stay very small and thin because there was not enough energy to share.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii waa ni amɛhe afee bibioo ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaajara.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around one main plantain trunk, they steal water and food from the mother plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, Plantain titri kome Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in sunlight to produce food for the tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and diseases while allowing the leaves to catch maximum light to build big yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai srɔtoi anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ aná la babaoo koni amɛfee ŋmeii agboi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival instead of spending it on fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ

english: Why does leaving tall weeds around my young crops cut my total harvest so drastically?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ haa mi yibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your young crops need to build strong roots. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Ragged holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the funnel of the plant. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem extracts into the funnel early helps destroy these pests before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green, healthy leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehiɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize draws the exact same nutrients out of the soil every season until the ground becomes exhausted. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under harsh sunlight and hot wind. Leaving tall trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living shade and keeps the air cool while cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni aaashi loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aaadu lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo aba ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines are climbers that need to lift their leaves up to catch direct sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to the sun and off the damp ground, helping the plant build larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he kɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Too many young shoots around one plantain stem steal water and food from the main mother plant. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main stem to focus its energy on producing large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo ni bɔleɔ plantain tso kome he lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ajwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔii wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing heart of the maize plant. Checking crops early and applying approved controls prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni adu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or pest stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby can help hold the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe haomɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔii akafite

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and rot in the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when standing water suffocates their roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Does leaving grass and weeds around my pepper plants really reduce how many peppers I harvest?
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi-pepper tso lɛ haa pepper ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Weeds act like extra plants stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your crops. Keeping the area around your pepper plants clear allows all nutrients to go straight into making bigger peppers.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei krɛdɛɛi ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why is it necessary to cut down my cocoa trees when they get sick instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsofa ko kɛkɛ?

english: Certain cocoa diseases, like the Swollen Shoot virus, live deep inside the sap of the tree where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the infected tree is the only proven way to stop the virus from spreading through the roots and killing the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi, tamɔ Swollen Shoot virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni egbe oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa farm if I leave just a few sick cocoa trees standing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi kookoo tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Diseases like Swollen Shoot spread quickly through tiny insects called mealybugs and natural root contact under the ground. Leaving even one sick tree allows the disease to continuously travel and destroy all surrounding healthy cocoa trees over time.
ga: Helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. kɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe ni etaa Tso kome po ni hela mɔ lɛ pɛ haa hela lɛ yaa nɔ efãa gbɛ ni efiteɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ

english: Will cutting down my old or diseased cocoa trees really help my land produce better cocoa in the future?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni egbɔ loo helai emɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafo lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ wɔsɛɛ?

english: Yes, removing sick or unproductive trees cleanses the land of persistent pests and diseases. Replanting with modern, high-yielding cocoa varieties gives your farm a fresh start to produce far more pods than the old trees ever could.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie ŋmeii kɛ helai ni ehi shi yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ehee ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo woɔ fe bɔ ni tsei momoi baanyɛ afee pɛŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in full open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Without temporary shade cover to shield their delicate leaves, they lose water too quickly, scorch, and eventually dry up.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni baabu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ, amɛshãa, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantains on the same farm with newly planted cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu kookoo ni adu ehee yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow tall very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants essential shade and moisture while they establish their roots during the first few years.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ beni amɛtoɔ shishifãi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do plantain suckers grow and leaf out so much faster than cocoa seedlings in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ baai oya fe kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains are fast-growing herbaceous plants with soft stems designed to store high amounts of water and energy, allowing them to shoot up rapidly compared to woody tree seedlings like cocoa, which spend early energy developing deep taproots.
ga: Plantains ji jwɛi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni afee koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ato. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ akɛto tso dumɔwui ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo he. Enɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shishijee fãi ni haa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do plantain plants help keep the soil moist for surrounding crops during dry periods?
ga: Te dumɔwui feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Plantain leaves block direct sunlight from hitting the ground, which slows down water evaporation from the dirt. Additionally, plantain stems hold large amounts of water that gradually release moisture into the surrounding soil.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ blɛoo. Kɛfata he lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ kɛ nu babaoo toɔ, ni fiofio lɛ, nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli

english: Will growing plantains next to my cocoa seedlings steal all the soil nutrients away from the cocoa?
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ baaju shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, because plantains and young cocoa feed at different soil depths and require complementary nutrients. As long as you space them correctly, plantains protect the cocoa without starving it.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ plantains bibii kɛ kookoo yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ srɔtoi anɔ, ni amɛbiɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Shii abɔ ni okɛ ohe aaawo mli bɔ ni sa. Plantain baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu kookoo he ni ekɛ hɔmɔ baaa.

english: How can I make an income from my farmland while waiting for my newly planted cocoa trees to mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi-kokoo tsei heei ni midu lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can harvest and sell food crops like plantains, cocoyams, and vegetables planted alongside the young cocoa. These quick-yielding crops provide regular household income during the early years before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa niyenii tamɔ plantain, cocoa, kɛ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa bibii ahe lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya nɛɛ ha shia lɛ ná shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Dani abaabɔi kookoo feemɔ

english: How long does a newly replanted cocoa seedling take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern improved cocoa varieties typically start producing their first pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, provided they are given good shade, water, and weed protection during their early growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ amɛná hulutsoo kpakpa, nu kɛ jwɛi ahebuu yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do my seedling nursery bags need small holes punched at the bottom before I fill them with soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui kotokui lɛ amli bu bibii lɛ? yɛ kotoku lɛ shishi dani akɛ sũ afata he.

english: Small holes at the bottom of nursery bags allow excess water to drain away. Without them, water settles at the bottom and rots the fragile roots of your young seedlings.
ga: Buu bibii ni yɔɔ grow bag lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. Kɛ amɛbɛ Nu lɛ baahi shishigbɛ ni ebaafite otsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni waaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and moisture while it gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛma shi lɛ.

english: Why do we plant cassava using stem cuttings instead of planting seeds from the flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmei yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ fɔfɔi amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings sprout much faster and grow into plants that are identical to the healthy mother plant, whereas growing cassava from seeds takes longer and produces unpredictable yields.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaada ni etsɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni tamɔ tso. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ heɔ be babaoo ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which the plant needs to feed its leaves; adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up short and crooked when I plant them in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛkpãtã kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand underground and need soft, loose earth or mounded soil to grow straight and long. Hard soil squeezes the growing tuber and prevents it from expanding properly.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋji anɔ koni amɛdara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ tsiɔ bulb ni miida lɛ naa ni ehaaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young crops when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa yɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ eji bibioo lolo?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from young crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong and resist diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients, causing the plant to save its energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by severe heat and dry spells that stress the leaf tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni kɛ haomɔ baa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ anɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves have small round holes all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ahe baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small holes in garden egg leaves are caused by tiny beetles or caterpillars chewing on them, which stops the leaves from making enough food for the plant.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa wɔji baai lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do small dark insects destroy my stored cowpea seeds after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miifite mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils lay tiny eggs on or in the cowpeas. When they hatch inside your storage bags, the young insects eat the inside of the beans, leaving behind empty shells.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ wɔji bibii. on or in cowpea Kɛ́ amɛfɔ lɛ, okɛwo onitoo kotoku lɛ mli. Kplukai bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmei lɛ mli, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmei lɛ mli fã ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I buy grafted mango seedlings instead of just planting seeds from the delicious mangoes I buy at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui ni jɛ mango ni ŋɔɔ mli kɛkɛ Ahe kɛjɛ jara nɔ?

english: Grafted seedlings guarantee you get the exact same delicious fruit quality as the parent tree and will bear fruit in just 3 to 4 years, whereas trees grown from seeds take 7 to 10 years and often produce sour or stringy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ haa onáa nɔmimaa akɛ obaawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni ebaawo yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ heɔ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii ni mli edɔ loo ni mli edɔ.

english: How can I make sure the mangoes I grow turn out sweet and tasty so people will want to buy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mango ni miduɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa bɔ ni mɛi baasumɔ ni amɛhe?

english: Fruit sweetness depends on choosing proven varieties like Keitt or Kent, ensuring the tree gets full sunlight, and providing enough potassium in the soil while the fruit is filling out.
ga: Bɔ ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ damɔ tsofa ko ni ana he odaseyeli, tamɔ Keitt loo Kent lɛ ni ahala lɛ nɔ, koni tso lɛ aná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Ni ha potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiwo amɛhe ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: What kind of soil do I need on my farm to successfully grow strong mango trees?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ he hiaa miŋmɔ lɛ koni manyɛ akwɛ mango tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Mango trees need deep, well-drained sandy-loam soil where their roots can spread easily, because sitting in waterlogged soil will cause their roots to rot and kill the tree.
ga: Mango tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko ta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi.

english: If my farm is in a drier area with long dry seasons, can I still grow good mangoes?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nu bɛ ni eyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ani manyɛ makwɛ mango kpakpai lolo?

english: Yes, mango trees actually thrive in warm, dry climates because they require a dry season of 2 to 3 months to stress the tree into flowering heavily and producing good fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, mango tsei shwereɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ egbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mango tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting a young mango tree before I can start harvesting fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du mango tso bibioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani enyɛ ekpa yibii?

english: If you plant a grafted mango seedling, you will start seeing your first small harvest in 3 to 4 years, and the tree will reach full production around 7 to 8 years.
ga: Kɛji odu mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ Obaaje shishi ona oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni tsei lɛ baashɛ yibiiwoo he yɛ aaafee afii 7 kɛyashi 8 mli.

english: Do I need to cut back the branches of my mango tree, or should I just leave it to grow naturally?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mango nine lɛ mli loo maha ekwɛ̃ yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and airflow, which prevents fungal diseases, keeps the tree at an easy height for harvesting, and encourages bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ loo afo lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni amɛkpamɔ waaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ feɔ agbo

english: Why does my mango tree produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop easily due to strong winds, insect pests, or sudden lack of water; applying mulch to keep soil moist and protecting trees from pests during bloom will help fruits stay on the tree.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaye abua ni yibii lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I keep watering my mature mango tree regularly throughout the dry season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi mango tso ni eda lɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: No, mature mango trees need a dry rest period to trigger flowering, so you should stop watering before the flowering season and only water lightly once the tiny fruits start forming.
ga: Dabi, mango tso ni eda lɛ he miihia be ni mli egbi dani efɔfɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okpa nu ni oooha lɛ dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ aba, ni okɛ nu awo mli fioo pɛ kɛji aduawai bibii je shishi amɛmiifee.

english: Why do my mangoes develop black spots and spoil on the inside before they even get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Black spots are usually caused by fruit flies or fungal diseases like anthracnose, which enter the fruit early and can be managed by hanging fruit fly traps and clearing fallen, rotten fruit from under the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii helai tamɔ anthracnose, ni boteɔ aduawai lɛ amli oya ni abaanyɛ atsu he nii kɛtsɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni ojie aduawai ni egbee shi ni egboi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick my mangoes so they stay fresh while being transported to distant markets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mango? Enɛ ji koni mango lɛ ahi shi ehee yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Harvest mangoes when the fruit shoulders around the stem swell up and the skin turns from dark dull green to a lighter green with a slight yellow tinge, showing the inside flesh has matured.
ga: Kpaa mango lɛ beni aduawai lɛ atsitsii ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ efuu. ni hewolo lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee eŋɔli ni mli tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ fioo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ loo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edɔ kwraa.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. When leaves curl and turn yellow, the plant cannot catch sunlight properly, which stops the cassava roots underground from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ baai lɛ shwie shi ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions during the rainy season. Removing infected pods early and clearing heavy weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If your previous crop leaves were pale yellow instead of dark green, or if the stalks grew thin and short, your soil is low on nutrients. Adding organic manure or fertilizer gives the new crop the food it needs to produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛji otsutsu tso lɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Aloo kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bafee ŋmɔŋ ni efee kuku Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a few get visited by tiny insects that pollinate them. Flowers also drop if the tree is stressed by dry weather or lacks nutrients to support growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kooloi bibii fioo komɛi yɛ ni baa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Fɔfɔi hu shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli loo ebɛ niyenii ni baaye abua fɔfɔi ni miida lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This makes all the plants thin and weak, resulting in smaller overall harvests than properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibii fɛɛ ni abaaná lɛ baafee bibioo fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree hurt my farm?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ baaná miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: No, pruning actually helps the tree. Removing dead or excess branches allows sunlight to reach all parts of the tree, reduces pest hiding spots, and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Tsɔɔmɔ hei ni kooloi awuiyelɔi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ shi ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii wuji

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out seeds before they can establish roots. Waiting until the rains are regular ensures young shoots get steady water to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kukuoo ko nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu ni hoɔ daa koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and bent instead of straight and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni etsii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become bent and small when the soil is too hard or full of rocks, making it difficult for the tuber to push downward. Making high, soft soil mounds gives the roots space to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaatsi sweet potato yitso lɛ shi. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ mli he lɛ mli alɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce less food even if I give the crops enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal fertilizer and soil food away from your main crops. They also block sunlight and hide crop pests, which weakens your plants even when they receive plenty of rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa ni ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ, ni baanyɛ aha otsei lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po.

english: Why should I buy newly released seed varieties from researchers instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni ajie lɛ kpo kɛjɛ niiamlitaolɔi adɛŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid or improved crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation, leading to smaller harvests. Newly released seeds from researchers are bred to produce higher yields, mature faster, and resist local pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome loo tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo. Akwɛ dumɔwui heei ni ajie kɛjɛ niiamlitaolɔi adɛŋ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛkwɛ̃ oya, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: What makes a newly released crop variety different from the traditional crops my family has grown for years?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei srɔtoi heei lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ blema tsei ni miweku lɛ edu afii babaoo lɛ ahe?

english: Newly released varieties are developed by agricultural scientists to solve specific farm problems. They are tested to withstand dry spells, resist common diseases, and produce more food on smaller pieces of land compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi fee tsofai sɔrɔtoi heei ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ koni amɛkɛtsu okwaayeli mli naagbai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe nii. Aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ehaa niyenii babaoo baa yɛ he ko bibioo kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: Can I multiply the new crop seeds I got from the agricultural officer and give them to my neighbor to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ dumɔwui heei ni minine shɛ nɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ashwã ni mikɛha akutsoŋbii koni amɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It depends on the type of crop. For open-pollinated crops like certain beans or traditional maize, you can save and share seeds if kept pure. However, for hybrid crops, saving seeds will lead to poor yield, so fresh seeds must be bought every season.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbeleɔ naa, tamɔ ŋmeii komɛi loo blema ŋmeii Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato ni okɛ amɛ aha kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi, kɛha tsei ni ji hybrid lɛ Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni ehiii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei daa be mli.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The plants stretch upward to reach the light instead of using their energy to build strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛhe la moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Extreme heat, insufficient water, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending resources on growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains or large forest trees provide vital shade and keep moisture in the soil, acting like protective covers while the young cocoa trees build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni yɔɔ kooi wuji amli lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa, ni amɛhaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I test if a new crop variety will grow well on my land before I plant my entire farm with it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji tso henɔ hee ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can set up a small trial plot on a piece of your land to observe the crop for one season. This allows you to see how the plant handles your soil type, rain patterns, and local pests without risking your main food or income.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee kaa he mfoniri bibioo ko. yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli be kome. Enɛ haa onaa bɔ ni tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa. Ni okɛ oniyenii loo shika ni onáa lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant needs from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and stops pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ akpa.

english: Yellowing and leaf curling are caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or red spider mites, which spread plant viruses. These pests multiply quickly in hot, dry weather when the cassava plant is already weak from lack of rain.
ga: Koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo red spider mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Be nɛɛ ji be ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot under the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when heavy rains cause water to collect around the roots without proper drainage, or when tiny worms called nematodes attack the tuber skin and let wet rot fungi inside.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo ni amɛshi ŋmeii ni egbo ni efɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is there a difference between the maize grown for human food and the maize grown for animal feed?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ kɛhaa gbɔmɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ kɛhaa kooloi aniyenii teŋ?

english: Yes, maize varieties for animal feed are often selected for high starch, protein, or oil content to help livestock grow fast, while maize for human food is selected for specific taste, texture, and flour quality needed for dishes like banku or kenkey.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, ahalaa ŋmãa henɔi ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ yɛ amɛmli ŋmãa, protein loo fɔ ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ koni eye ebua kooloi ni amɛdara oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ahalaa ŋmãa kɛha adesai aniyenii yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo pɔtɛɛ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha, kɛ ŋmãa ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii tamɔ banku loo kenkey lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is the difference between buying new seeds from an agro-dealer and saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui heei ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpaa lɛ mli ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Commercial seeds bought from stores are often specially bred hybrids designed to grow fast, resist local pests, and give high yields. Saved seeds from previous harvests lose these strong traits over time, leading to lower yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayeli dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety brought to our village will grow well in my farm soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛba wɔ akrowa lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Every crop variety has specific needs for soil type, temperature, and rainfall. Testing your soil and checking if the seed's required growing period matches your local rainy season helps ensure the crop will thrive on your farm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni ataoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ, latsaa, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he. Kaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛji be ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen. While rain gives plants water, nitrogen is what allows them to build green leaves and create energy to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ haa tsei nu moŋ Nitrogen ji nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni ehaa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa waa.

english: How does applying fertilizer actually help my crops produce bigger yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer works like food for the soil, supplying vital elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. These nutrients help the plant develop deep roots, strong stalks, and larger grains than the soil alone could support.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. Nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. tso ni mli wa Ni dumɔwui lɛ dara fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller grains when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves compete for the same limited water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow thick, healthy stalks.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa He ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do some farm chemicals burn my crops while killing weeds on another farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai komɛi shãa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli jwɛi lɛ?

english: Herbicides are designed for specific crop types and weed types. Using the wrong chemical, mixing it too strong, or applying it to a crop it wasn't designed for can damage your plants instead of protecting them.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ jwɛi. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsofai ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni akɛfutuɔ mli Aloo, kɛ akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeee aha lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbe otsei lɛ moŋ fe ni eeebu amɛhe.

english: Why do worms attack the tender center leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the soft, growing funnel of young maize because it provides tender food and protection. The warm, moist weather of the rainy season allows their eggs to hatch quickly and spread across fields.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ anɔ. Ejaakɛ ehaa niyenii ni mli jɔ kɛ hebuu. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested maize completely before taking it to the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi dani mikɛya ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Wet or damp maize creates a moist environment where destructive mold and dangerous toxins can quickly grow. Thoroughly drying your grain ensures it mills into safe, smooth flour and prevents spoiling during storage.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ loo edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ adara oya. Oŋmãa lɛ ni ooogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ashikiŋsha ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. ni otsi fitemɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ

english: Why do small insects like weevils attack my stored maize even after I have harvested it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ beni mikpa lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils are attracted to the moisture and soft centers of stored grain where they lay eggs and feed. Proper drying, using clean storage bags, or applying safe grain-preservation powders stops these insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli fɛ̃i kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii lɛ. Egbimɔ ni sa Kɛ kotoku ni mli tse ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ atsu nii Aloo okɛ powda ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii. Ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the middle in a V-shape usually means your maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the daytime temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry. When stressed by heat or lack of water, the plant sheds flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ edɔ loo nu efo mli lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants have very large leaves but tiny root tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth above ground instead of swelling its roots underground. Compacted soil can also choke tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e sisi ɔmɛ puɛɔ ngɛ zugba sisi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ atsĩ tuber dalɛ naa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are leguminous plants that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow better without competing for the same nutrients.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔŋŋ akaŋ.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn pale and drop off after a heavy rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ?

english: Too much water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing nutrients, causing leaves to turn pale yellow and drop off.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ekpaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: What causes ragged holes and small brownish droppings inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ mli

english: Ragged holes and caterpillar droppings inside the central shoot of young maize are key signs of Fall Armyworm. The worms hide deep in the funnel to eat the soft new leaves before they open up.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm he okadii ni he hiaa waa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii heei dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why are powdery white spots spreading across the leaves of my pumpkin plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powder egbɛ eshwa mi-pumpkin tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Powdery white spots are caused by a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives in warm, humid weather. It blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf, causing the affected leaves to wither and dry up.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ hela yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda baa. Amɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: If maize seeds are buried too deep, the young sprout uses up all its stored food energy just trying to reach the surface, resulting in weak plants or seeds that rot underground before emerging.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baatsu nii yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso loo dumɔwu lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani epuɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize yield far less crop than new hybrid seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni ahe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed from two distinct parent plants to produce maximum vigor in the first generation only. Saving and replanting seeds from that harvest causes those special high-yield traits to break down.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni abuɔ he ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nakai sui ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and need temporary shade trees or plantains to shield them until their roots grow deep enough to handle full heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbiɔ tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baaya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Rain spreads Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in heavy moisture. Pruning extra tree branches and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps the pods dry.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny flowers before they ever turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ pod?

english: Cocoa flowers drop due to intense heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination by tiny insects like midges that live in moist soil leaves.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ baai lɛ ahe shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni haaa amɛfee pollin lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to trim extra branches off my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing leaves and branches so the tree can send all its water and nutrients directly into growing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ enu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa tree stems to get swollen bumps and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifu ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Swollen stems are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, a serious disease spread by tiny insects called mealybugs that weakens the tree and requires cutting it out to protect nearby crops.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afolɔ amɛ koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does adding fertilizer help my mature cocoa farm produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Over many years, cocoa trees drain nutrients from the dirt. Fertilizer restores essential soil minerals so the tree has enough energy to produce continuous flowers and pods.
ga: Yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii aba be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know when an oil palm fruit cluster is ripe enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: An oil palm fruit bunch is ready for harvest when at least five to ten reddish-orange fruits break off naturally and fall to the ground beneath the tree.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kɛ hoo lɛ, tso yibii enumɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋma ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tswaa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do oil palm trees need so much space between them when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu mu tsei lɛ, gbɛ babaoo yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spread out wide leaves and compete heavily for sunlight and water. Spacing them well stops them from shading each other and leads to bigger fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi amɛhe naa ni amɛbaafee kuu wulu ko.

english: Why do farmers cut away the bottom yellow leaves of the oil palm tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ mu tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Removing dead or yellowing lower leaves cleans the tree canopy, allows more sunlight in, makes it easier to harvest fruit bunches, and stops pests from nesting.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egboi loo ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Ehaa hulu la babaoo kpɛɔ kɛboteɔ mli. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa aduawai akui ni etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee shĩai

english: Why do my farm crops grow so slowly during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of plant leaves and dry up the ground, forcing crops to slow down their growth to conserve water until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha amɛdalɛ aba shi koni amɛbu nu he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water quickly in direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains, planted beside them to block direct heat and keep moisture in the air until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ.

english: Why does trimming off branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight can reach the main trunk where cocoa pods grow. It also allows air to flow freely through the tree, reducing humidity that encourages diseases and directing the plant's energy into pod growth instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni kookoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo ni kɛ helai baa lɛ shi. Ni kudɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛya ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni oookɛ baai afata he.

english: Why are my older cocoa trees producing much smaller pods than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their roots and internal branches become less efficient at absorbing and moving nutrients from the soil. Over time, the soil also becomes depleted of key minerals unless organic matter or fertilizers are added to replenish it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Shishifãi kɛ emli niji lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛjie lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite shika tsuru ni he hiaa. Ja akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he koni akɛto najiaŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, cool conditions. When rain splatters soil or water drops from infected pods onto clean ones, the fungus spreads quickly, causing the pod to turn black and decay.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, sũ shwieɔ shi loo nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni he tse nɔ. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil usually means pests or fungal diseases are damaging the root system underground. When roots rot or get blocked, they can no longer transport water up to the stem and leaves, causing the plant to dry out from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ trukaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko miifite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo loo amɛtsi amɛhe lɛ Enyɛŋ ekɛ nu aya ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. Gbimɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods grow in twisted, strange shapes with hard bumps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee nɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ni efite lɛ? ni eyɛ bɔtin ni wa

english: Deformed pods are often caused by sap-sucking insects like mirids (capsids) feeding on tender young pods, or by viral infections like Swollen Shoot Disease, which disrupt the plant's normal growth patterns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni efite lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli tamɔ bud swollen disease, ni gbalaa bɔ ni tsei lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is missing essential nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. It can also happen if the roots are waterlogged and cannot breathe properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen ni haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔji Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is under stress from hot weather, drought, or lack of soil nutrients. It can also happen if there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baanyɛ afee pollination yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin instead of bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ shwiili mli ni efeɔ shwiili moŋ fe ni eeefee shwiili ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Plants grow tall and skinny when they are planted too close together or under heavy shade. They stretch upward as fast as possible to reach sunlight, sacrificing trunk and branch strength in the process.
ga: Tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo shishi. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji lɛ amli yɛ nifeemɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to survive in harsh conditions with very little care. They aggressively steal sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Young cocoa saplings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Shade trees like plantains act like umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by viruses they carry. As the leaf loses juice and becomes damaged, it curls inward to protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ amli Beni baai lɛ nu fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my green maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient for healthy leaf growth. When the plant does not get enough nitrogen from the soil, it pulls food from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my tomato plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It keeps moisture in the soil during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and prevents heavy rains from washing away rich soil.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantains produce small bunches when I plant the suckers very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are planted too close, their large leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for the same water and plant nutrients. Proper distance gives every plant enough space and light to make big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛ tso kome lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso agbo ko.

english: It is best to wait until the rain falls consistently for two or three good times so the soil becomes deep wet. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and quickly die if hot, dry days return.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛgboi kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to stretch high to catch full sunlight, which allows the leaves to make energy that feeds the growing yam underground. Raising the vines off the wet ground also prevents diseases from rotting the foliage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ashɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hewalɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava crops grow slow and weak if cassava is a tough plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmei tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji ŋmei lɛ ji tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Even though mature cassava is tough, young cassava needs full sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to build its energy. Weeds grow very fast and steal those essential resources before the young cassava roots can spread.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ daa waa moŋ, shi ŋmei bibioo lɛ he miihia hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nakai nibii ni he hiaa lɛ dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Too much water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots because they cannot breathe. Without air, root cells die and soil fungus easily invades the weak roots, causing them to rot underground.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ gboiɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or sudden dry conditions. If the plant feels it does not have enough steady water or moisture to raise the fruit, it drops the flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying recommended nitrogen fertilizers like NPK or well-rotted manure around the base will help restore their bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni mli tse lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry, causing stress to the plant. Watering consistently at the base of the plant during hot dry spells helps protect the blossoms so they can turn into fruit.
