ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishi nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: What is causing my pepper leaves to curl up and look small?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bibioo?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves, or by a virus spread by those pests. Spraying early with neem oil extract or appropriate insecticides helps control the insects and protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi bibii ni ebu shweremɔ heei ahe.

english: Why should I plant legumes like cowpea after harvesting cabbage from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii beni mikpa kaaba kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cabbage consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Planting cowpeas or beans afterwards puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots, restoring soil fertility for your next crop while breaking pest cycles.
ga: Kaabaji heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas loo beans ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to grow straight and large. Hard, compact soil or shallow mounds restrict the tuber from expanding freely, causing it to twist and stay small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee agbo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ gɔji ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe. ni haa etsɔ ehe ni etsɔɔ bibioo

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with young cocoa trees for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, while also hiding harmful pests. Clearing weeds gives your cocoa trees full access to plant food and space to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ teeɔ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa o-cacao tsei lɛ naa tsei niyenii kɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested so it does not spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can carefully dig up one stand to check if the roots are thick and firm before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa shidaamɔhe lɛ koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil stays cool and absorbs the moisture deeply before the hot afternoon sun can evaporate the water away or scorch wet leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eŋɔɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo eshã baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my watermelons splitting open right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa dani eshɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons split when they receive a sudden heavy amount of water after a dry period, making the inside grow faster than the skin can stretch. Giving the crop steady, regular water avoids these sudden growth bursts.
ga: Watermelon lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bote mli trukaa yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Enɛ haa watermelon lɛ daa yɛ emli oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ trukaa nɛɛ.

english: How can I select healthy plantain suckers to plant on my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Look for plantain suckers that have narrow, sword-like leaves, dark green stems, and solid white corms at the base that are free from brown spots, rot, or insect holes.
ga: Taomɔ plantain tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ klante. tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ rhizomes yɛŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo kooloi amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. Large shade trees protect young cocoa from extreme heat, keep the soil moist, and create the cool environment cocoa needs to grow healthy roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ofee shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ Cocoa biɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but produce small cassava roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi? Cassava shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Soft soil with balanced nutrients encourages root growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii mli nibii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small stems growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie ŋmeii ni ebɔle mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mli.

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and plant food from the main trunk. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, resulting in larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ejuɔ nu ni ekwɛ̃ɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain lɛ da ni etsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in the sun to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or that water is sitting around the roots for too long, preventing the plant from pulling up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning dry during the hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl when the plant is losing water faster than its roots can drink from the soil, or when tiny pests like whiteflies carry a virus to the leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ nu fite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any pepper fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like calcium in the soil during the flowering period.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year, why does my yield keep dropping?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season consumes the same soil nutrients repeatedly and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Ni aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be mli lɛ biɔ ni akɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii shii abɔ. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii atsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil absorbs the moisture before the heat of the day causes it to evaporate, preventing leaves from getting scorched.
ga: Nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: Why do other farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: What is 'galamsey' and why is everyone saying it is bad for my farmland?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Galamsey’ ni mɛni hewɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛɔ akɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Galamsey refers to illegal small-scale mining. It harms farmland because miners dig up and wash away the fertile topsoil, leaving behind rocky waste and dangerous chemicals like mercury that ruin the soil's ability to nourish crops.
ga: Galamsey tsɔɔ shika bibii ni ajieɔ yɛ mla naa lɛ. Eyeɔ okwaayeli shikpɔji lɛ awui ejaakɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shika tsuru mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Eshiɔ tɛi ni tamɔ muji kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ mercury, ni fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is healthy enough to plant new crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii heei?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, smells fresh like rain, and has visible earthworms. If your soil is hard, pale, or full of rocky sand from nearby land digging, it lacks the organic matter needed for crops to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee tamɔ nugbɔ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyi kɛ ŋã tɛi ni jɛ ŋã ni atsa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi lɛ faaa.

english: What should I do if miners start digging for gold on agricultural land near my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shika tsuru mli lɛ bɔi shika tsuru taomɔ yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should report the activity to local agricultural extension officers and community leaders immediately. Protecting your farm boundary is crucial because illegal mining destroys topsoil permanently and spreads toxic runoff to neighboring crops.
ga: Esa akɛ abɔ nitsumɔi ahe amaniɛ aha maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ akutso lɛ mli hiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe ni ooobu lɛ he miihia waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kwraa, ni egbɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni hoɔ lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the crops I planted turning yellow and dying even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni miduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Crops turn yellow and die when their roots are absorbing toxic chemicals or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. If the soil or ground water is polluted by nearby mining activities, plants cannot absorb the food they need.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ŋɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ shika tsuru nitsumɔi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ efite shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Why does muddy river water near my farm make my vegetable crops struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ haa mi-aduawai lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: River water contaminated with heavy mud and silt from galamsey chokes crop roots, preventing them from breathing. It can also deposit toxic heavy metals onto your farm, which slows plant growth and damages the leaves.
ga: Faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni tsii kɛ sũ ni jɛ galamsey mli lɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu. Dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ gbeyei hu baanyɛ abua ehe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa oya ni efiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees stay small and refuse to grow flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ ji bibioo ni ekpooɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, undisturbed soil with balanced nutrients and moisture. If the soil beneath them has been compacted or disturbed by nearby heavy earth-moving activities, the roots cannot spread enough to support flowering.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa lɛ he miihia koko tsei. Kɛfata niyenii ni ja kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ ehe nitsumɔi ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ gbaa enaa. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli bɔ ni sa koni amɛye amɛbua fɔfɔi.

english: Why are my maize crops giving me much smaller harvests this year than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ yibii lɛ faaa kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Shrinking harvests usually mean your soil has lost its nutrients due to erosion, land degradation, or continuous farming without replacing organic matter. Degraded land cannot support heavy feeders like maize without soil rehabilitation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni aba shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ miifite niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shwiemɔ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ loo okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeee Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Can land that was damaged by illegal mining ever be used to grow food crops again?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni shika tsuru tsaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ efite lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, but it requires land rehabilitation. The pits must be refilled, the soil leveled, toxic chemicals treated, and fresh topsoil and organic manure added before food crops can grow safely again.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, awo bu mli, afee shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei atsu nii. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei afata he dani niyenii tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ekoŋŋ.

english: Are there specific plants I can grow to help fix land that has been damaged?
ga: Ani tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu koni eye ebua ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: Yes, fast-growing cover crops like leguminous plants (such as mucuna or cowpeas) help rebuild topsoil, prevent erosion, and add vital nitrogen back into worn-out earth to prepare it for future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ ŋmeii (tamɔ mucilagina loo cowpea) yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ mli koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat root crops like cassava grown near a mining site?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmei ni adu yɛ hei ni atsaa shika tsuru yɛ lɛ?

english: It can be unsafe because root crops absorb chemicals directly from contaminated soil and water. If chemicals like mercury or cyanide are present in the ground near a mining site, they can collect inside the cassava roots and cause health issues.
ga: Ekolɛ ebɛ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji tsofai tamɔ mercury loo cyanide yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsaa shikatoohe lɛ. Nakai tsofai lɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛkɛ helai aba.

english: What is pruning, and why should I cut away some branches from my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni afoɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji komɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Pruning means carefully cutting away weak or unproductive branches so your crop doesn't waste water and nutrients on them, allowing the plant to send its energy to the healthy parts that produce your harvest.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ akafite nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ nakai tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ yaa hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa lɛ.

english: How do I identify which specific branches to cut off when my crop starts flowering?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse tsei niji pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: You wait for flowers to show on the crop first, then look closely for branches that carry no flowers at all. Those flowerless branches are the ones you cut away.
ga: Omɛɔ ni fɔfɔii aba tso lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, taomɔ tsei niji ni bɛ fɔfɔi kwraa. Nakai tsei niji ni fɔfɔii bɛ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni ofoɔ.

english: Why should I wait until flowers appear on my crops before I begin pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni fɔfɔii abaje kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Waiting for flowering lets the crop show you which branches are productive and which are useless, preventing you from accidentally cutting off branches that would have grown fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ omɛ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsɔɔ bo niji ni woɔ yibii kɛ nɔ ni he ehiaaa. Enɛ baatsi onaa koni okafo tsei niji ni baawo yibii lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: How can I safely prune non-flowering branches without destroying the flowers nearby?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ tsei niji ni bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee fɔfɔi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Work patiently and cut carefully around the flowers with a clean tool, taking care not to shake, crush, or accidentally trim the delicate flower buds.
ga: Okɛ tsuishitoo atsu nii ni ofolɔ he fɛɛ he. fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni he tse Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ oshara akakpokpo, okɛfolɔ, loo okɛfolɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What will happen to my harvest if flowers fall off or get damaged when I am working on my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji fɔfɔii shwie shi loo amɛfite beni miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Flowers are what turn into actual fruits or pods, so damaging or losing flowers directly reduces the total amount of food you can harvest at the end of the season.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni bafeɔ aduawai loo ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ loo amɛlaajeɔ lɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okpa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is the difference between the major and minor seasons for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli be kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: The major season brings main heavy rains and longer growing periods, while the minor season brings shorter rains, giving crops less time between harvest cycles.
ga: Be titri lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. Yɛ be mli ni be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ baanɛ fioo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa be fioo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ bei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why is heavy pruning risky for my crops when the time between the major and minor seasons is short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ waa lɛ ji oshara kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Akɛni be ni kã be titri lɛ kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ faaa hewɔ lɛ,.

english: When the period between seasons is short, crops do not have enough resting time to heal and grow back strong if you cut away too many branches all at once.
ga: Beni be ni kã bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ faaa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɛ hejɔɔmɔ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsa ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ofo tsei aniji babaoo shikome.

english: Should I do light pruning or heavy pruning on my crops during short resting periods?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be kuku mli?

english: You should do light pruning, carefully removing only the clear non-flowering branches so the plant stays strong and recovers fast before the next rains begin.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli fioo, ni fiofio lɛ ojie niji ni bɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe awa oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do some branches on my crop produce flowers while other branches remain completely empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi miifɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kã he amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Crops distribute their food and sunlight unevenly, meaning healthy and well-exposed branches will form flowers while shaded or weaker branches stay bare.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ hulu la yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajie amɛ kpo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo fɔfɔi. yɛ be mli ni niji ni yɔɔ shade loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: How does the length of time between seasons affect my farm maintenance schedule?
ga: Te be ni kã bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ saamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Short gaps between seasons require quick, careful maintenance right when flowers appear, so you finish farm work before the next rainy season begins.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ faaa. Ebiɔ ni akwɛ nɔ oya ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ogbeɔ oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ naa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Bottom leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow big. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to spread wood ash from my kitchen fire onto my farm soil before planting?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaashwã tso sũ ni jɛɔ ŋtayaai amli la mli lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu?

english: Yes, wood ash adds useful nutrients like potassium to the soil and helps sweeten sour (acidic) soil, making it easier for crops to feed. However, it should be used in small amounts so it does not dry out the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli sũ kɛ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ potassium fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ (acidic), ni ehaa tsei lɛ yeɔ nii mlɛo. Shi esa akɛ akɛtsu nii fioo fioo koni sũ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my young plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the soft plant skin and destroy delicate roots. It is best to place fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away from the stem so roots can safely reach for it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hiɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Ekɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. kɛha root hegbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by dry weather or when tiny pests like mirids feed on them. Spraying approved farm chemicals at the right season and keeping shade trees helps flowers turn into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui yeɔ amɛ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ahaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them in heavy rain. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ŋmei ni aaadu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What causes armyworms to suddenly appear and destroy my maize field overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii lɛ je kpo ni amɛfite mi-ŋma ŋmɔji lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Armyworms hatch quickly from eggs laid by moths and eat constantly in warm weather. Catching them early and applying the right pest control product while the caterpillars are still small stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Methworms lɛ fɔɔ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ nii be fɛɛ be yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Mɔ amɛ mra. Ni okɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo lɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many small shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main plantain tree for food and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot to yield a large harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ kɛhaa kpamɔ babaoo.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough land on my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal underground water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Planting crops too close together causes them to shade each other and fight for soil nutrients, leading to thin plants with small yield. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough light and food to grow strong.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshwere.

english: Pepper leaves curl during the hottest hours to protect themselves from losing water too fast. Watering your plants deeply early in the morning helps them handle the sun without getting stressed.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why are my plantain bunches producing very small fruits instead of big, heavy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa yɛ yibii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees need plenty of food and water when flowering to make big fruits; if the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium or gets too dry during flowering, the crop will produce smaller, lighter bunches.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu babaoo he miihia dumɔwui beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo egbi tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nibii ni adu lɛ baawo jwɛi bibii ni waaa.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and rot so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce a gas called ethylene as soon as they are cut, which speeds up ripening. When kept in hot, poorly ventilated sacks or direct sunlight, this gas builds up and causes the fruit to spoil rapidly.
ga: Plantains lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji afo amɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Gas nɛɛ buaa ehe naa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily when the fruit starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep wooden roots like major trees; their roots stay close to the surface, so as the fruit bunch gets heavy, the plant loses balance and needs wooden props for support.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei wuji. Eshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ, tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni esaaa ni ehe baahia ni akɛ tsei awo mli koni ekɛfi esɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain tree turning yellow and drying up from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛjɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant is short on nitrogen in the soil or that underground pests like nematodes are damaging the roots, preventing the plant from taking up water and food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes miifite shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do so many small plantain shoots grow around my main tree, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii lɛ Mɛi babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. mi tso titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mashi fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: A plantain tree produces shoots called suckers to reproduce, but if you leave too many, they will compete with the main tree for food and water, leaving you with smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛkɛfɔ bii. Shi kɛji oha etee shɔŋŋ tsɔ Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa onáa yibii bibii.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready when the sharp, flat edges on the sides of individual fruits turn round and smooth, and the dry flowers at the tips break off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my plantain plants take much longer to produce fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains rely heavily on steady water to build stem strength; during dry periods, the crop slows down its internal growth to conserve moisture and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Plantains kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni damɔ shi nɔ koni amɛma amɛtsitsi lɛ hewalɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha amɛmli dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he.

english: Why are my plantain fruits splitting open on the tree before they even turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ po lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting happens when a long dry period is suddenly followed by heavy rain; the inside of the plantain grows very fast with the sudden water, causing the skin to stretch and crack.
ga: Yibii amli gbalamɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ. Plantain lɛ mli lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ nu ba trukaa. Ehaa hewolo lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ.

english: Why does the main plantain stem die after I cut down the fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso titri lɛ gboɔ beni mifo aduawai akui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once in its life; once harvested, that stem naturally dies off so its stored nutrients can pass into the young suckers around it.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji akpa Tso lɛ tso lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Why do the roots of my plantain trees rot when rain water sits on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots need air in the soil to breathe; standing water drowns the roots by blocking oxygen, which allows harmful soil fungi to attack and decay the root system.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia plantain shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do different varieties of groundnuts exist if they all produce groundnuts in the end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ kɛji akɛ yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Different varieties are developed for specific traits—some mature faster during short rains, some resist local leaf diseases, and others produce larger nuts with higher oil content depending on market needs.
ga: Akɛ sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi feɔ srɔtoi. Henɔi komɛi shwereɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be kukuoo mli. Henɔi komɛi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa helai anɔ. ni ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Edamɔ jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ

english: How do I choose the best groundnut variety for my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You should choose based on your soil type, rainfall pattern, and common pests in your area. Short-duration varieties work best in drier zones, while long-duration varieties yield more in areas with extended rainfall.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ ni oyɔɔ lɛ naa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Be kukuoo mli henɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ bɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some groundnut varieties produce large seeds while others produce small ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ dumɔwui wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Seed size is determined by the genetics of that specific crop variety. Larger seeds often attract higher prices for eating, while smaller seeds are frequently grown for oil extraction or local seed stock.
ga: Tso henɔi lɛ amli wala yibii tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ. Dumɔwui wuji lɛ gbalaa jara ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛyeɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, aduɔ dumɔwui bibii koni akɛjie mu loo maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers drop down and push into the soil after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is unique to groundnuts: after pollination, the plant forms a stem called a peg that grows downward into the soil so the nut pod can safely form underground away from heat and pests.
ga: Sui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe ji: yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tsei feɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ he ko ni dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do groundnut plants spread out across the soil instead of growing tall like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are low-growing plants designed to cover the ground, which helps keep the soil moist, reduces weeds, and allows their flowers to easily reach the dirt to form pods.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei ni shwereɔ fioo ni afee koni akɛha shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ehaa jwɛi baa shi, ni ehaa efɔfɔi lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell when my groundnut pods are mature if they grow under the earth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanut pods lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You check by pulling up a few test plants; if the leaves turn yellow and the inside of the pods shows dark brown or black markings, the crop is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Okwɛɔ kɛtsɔ kaa tsei fioo komɛi ni oootsi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ediŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni eshɛ nikpamɔ.

english: Will planting groundnuts improve my soil for the next crop I plant?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, which enriches the soil naturally for the crop you plant in the next season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it beneficial to grow a mix of different crops on my farm instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Growing different crops reduces the risk of losing your entire harvest to pests or drought, keeps the soil healthy, and provides different food and income sources throughout the year.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ Ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baafite yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hɔmɔ hewɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi. ni amɛji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhei srɔtoi yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why does my neighbor's crop suffer from yellow leaf spots while my groundnut crop stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mi-peanut tso lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Your crop likely comes from a disease-resistant variety that can fight off rosette virus or leaf spot disease, whereas your neighbor may be growing a susceptible variety.
ga: Ekolɛ onibii lɛ jɛ tso ko ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ ni baanyɛ awuu ashi rose virus loo leaf spot hela lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ miidu tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do extension officers grow many different crop types side by side in demonstration plots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔji anɔ lɛ?

english: Demonstration plots allow extension officers to observe how different crop varieties react to the local soil and weather so they can recommend the best-performing seeds to farmers.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔji lɛ haa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ naa bɔ ni tsei srɔtoi lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ ajie dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ayi aha okwaafoi.

english: When crops are planted too close together without proper gaps, their roots compete heavily for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni he ko ni sa bɛ Tsei shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How much space should I leave between my cassava stems when planting them?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Leaving adequate spacing between cassava plants gives the roots enough room under the soil to swell and develop big tubers without choking nearby plants.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfu ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni amɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very leaves at first, but fail to produce fruit later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baa babaoo yɛ shishijee mli shi sɛɛ mli lɛ ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants can sprout well initially, but if they lack key nutrients like phosphorus during fruiting or suffer from extreme heat stress, their performance drops and flowers fall off before producing fruit.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo amɛnaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ hu? Ehewalɛ baa shi ni fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my young plantain suckers taking too long to establish after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants need proper soil preparation and moisture to build strong root systems before they can support heavy growth and fruiting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he saamɔ ni sa he miihia tsei bibii koni amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo.

english: What method can I use to prevent my cocoa pods from rotting during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi matsɔ nɔ matsɔ nɔ matsi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Pruning excess shade branches allows air and sunlight to dry the leaves and pods, preventing black pod disease from spreading and destroying your harvest.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Tsi black pod hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii.

english: How can I protect my cabbage leaves from being completely ruined by worms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cabbage baai lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii akafite amɛ?

english: Regular weed management and applying natural or recommended sprays early in the crop's lifecycle prevents pests from damaging the tender inner leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ jwɛi anɔ daa kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ wala be mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite tso lɛ mli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: How do I check if my yam plants are getting a disease before the crop gets ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ehiɛ hela dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtã?

english: Walk through your field regularly and inspect the leaves for curling, dark spots, or unusual yellowing, which are early signs of fungal infections or nutrient problems.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa ni okwɛ kɛji baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Ani ŋmeii diji loo ŋmɔŋ komɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ? Enɛ ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo niyenii mli naagba ko eba.

english: How can I tell if my crop soil has enough moisture for seeds to germinate well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pot sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds together without dripping water and crumbles easily when touched, it has ideal moisture for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ ata he. Eyɛ fɛ̃i ni sa kɛha shweremɔ.

english: Why are the old crop varieties my grandfather used not producing as well these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi momo ni minaa kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weather patterns and rainfall seasons are changing, so older crop varieties may struggle with drier weather, whereas improved seeds are bred to handle current climate conditions better.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miitsake. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ abɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose between an early-maturing crop variety and a long-duration one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra kɛ nɔ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Early-maturing varieties are best if the rainy season is short or unpredictable, while long-duration types work best when you have steady rainfall throughout the growing season.
ga: Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yɛ kuku loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, that nitrogen remains in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are many of my groundnut pods empty inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ efee efolo kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when there is not enough calcium in the soil while the pods are developing underground. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil before planting helps the nuts fill out completely.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rain water settles around them for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows water to run off easily and keeps the roots dry enough to avoid fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. Etsɛ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ agbiɔ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and stopping fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ekpaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that spread a virus while feeding on the leaves. Sprinkling neem leaf extract or soapy water on the underside of leaves helps control these whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo nu ni akɛ samla awo tso lɛ shishi koni eye ebua ni eye nɛkɛ ŋmeii yɛji nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves look healthy in the morning but wilt completely during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabeji baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa leebi shi amɛshwieɔ shi kwraa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can drink from hot, dry soil during midday. Placing dry grass or straw mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist throughout the day.
ga: Aduawai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ aaafee shwane fintiŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed all their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry weather or when there are no tiny midges present to pollinate them. Leaving some shade trees around cocoa farms keeps the air humid and creates a good environment for pollinators.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ. Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when bearing heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the stem with a strong bamboo or wooden prop pole helps hold the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛmiiwo aduawai akui wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my stored seed yams are ready to be planted in the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni ato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seed yams are ready to plant when small green buds or 'eyes' begin to sprout from the top end in your storage barn. Planting them before this natural dormancy breaks can cause the tubers to rot in dry soil.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛji ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi naagbee yɛ otsu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ dani adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha bulbs lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji efɔ fɔfɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when the soil moisture changes too suddenly from very dry to very wet, or during intense heat. Regular, consistent watering keeps the soil environment stable and prevents the plant from shedding its fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. aloo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni afeɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that create shade and preserve moisture in the soil, giving cocoa seedlings the protection they need during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans alongside my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a free natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried grass or plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter (mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, stops weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as it decays.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, improving airflow and leading to bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive severe heat. Once the rains return, the plant quickly uses energy stored in its roots to grow fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii oya ni ekɛbaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper blossoms drop off mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering during dry periods helps the flowers stay attached and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves of my garden egg plants getting small holes and fine web coverings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni ŋmeii ehà amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Small holes and webs indicate pests like spider mites or tiny beetles feeding on the leaves. Spraying the leaves with a mild neem seed oil mixture helps suppress these insects naturally.
ga: Bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Okɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni mli ejɔ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell before the continuous rainy season starts. Sowing early can cause seeds to sprout and then die quickly from a sudden lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my cassava start rotting just two or three days after I dig it out of the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react rapidly with oxygen, triggering chemical changes that rot the tuber fast. It is best to leave cassava in the ground until you are ready to use or process it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛ oxygen tsuɔ nii oya. Enɛ haa tsofai tsakemɔi ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii loo okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants regain a healthy green color and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná su ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to crowd each other and compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating crops, especially with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, restores soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, titri lɛ kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They require shade crops like plantain or shade trees planted alongside them to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, reducing soil-borne diseases and helping the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves and spreading viruses. Managing these pests early stops the curling and restores healthy crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much less food at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to produce a high yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Excess water sitting in the soil starves cassava roots of oxygen and encourages fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants suffer from heat stress, irregular watering, or pest attack. Providing consistent moisture at the base of the plant helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ Ni akɛ nu ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to put fertilizer on my farm right before heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ anɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the field before the plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is already moist or right before light rain ensures nutrients stay in the soil for the crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo fioo dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛdu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide the shade and cool moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto long wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking helps the leaves make more food, which leads to much larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji babaoo baa.

english: Why are holes suddenly appearing in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji jeɔ kpo trukaa ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is damage caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The moth lays eggs on maize leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they eat the leaves and hide inside the central shoot to feed on the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni fall armyworm pest, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ ewui yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ fiteɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Eyeɔ baai ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni eye tso lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips transmitting a virus. The feeding stresses the leaf tissue, causing it to curl upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ kɔɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ahe. ha ebɔle ehe

english: Heavy rains and high humidity create the cool, wet environment that Black Pod fungus needs to grow. Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil and old leaves directly onto the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni blackpod fungus lɛ he hiaa koni eda lɛ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ baai momoi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. The plant drops the flowers to save energy when conditions aren't right to raise fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi esaaa kɛha yibiiwoo.

english: Groundnuts naturally plant their own seeds underground. After the flower is pollinated above ground, the flower stem bends downward and burrows into the soft soil where the groundnut pod grows and ripens safely.
ga: Peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay green and survive even when there is no rain for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its top leaves during dry weather to stop water from escaping and uses the thick storage roots under the ground to store moisture, allowing it to survive severe drought.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu akajɛ mli. ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtoɔ nu Koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa shihilɛi amli.

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plant, they fight with it for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers directs all the plant's energy into producing one very large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ekɛ lɛ baawu koni ená niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ plantains akuu agbo kome ni tsii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, this extra nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy green growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ ni etsɔ V su lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground and acts as free, natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed, so they drop extra flowers to save energy. However, if they drop almost all flowers, it is usually a sign of water stress from dry weather or damage from tiny pests like mirids.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Shi, kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo gbee shi lɛ, Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu mli haomɔ jɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli loo nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ efite.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. Tiny insects like stem weevils or microscopic worms called nematodes often eat these roots, making the plant weak so heavy fruit loads or strong winds easily push it down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ stem weevils loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ ewaaa akɛ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil starves the roots of air and allows fungal water molds to grow rapidly. These fungi invade the cassava tubers under the wet soil and cause them to turn soft and rot.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ boteɔ ŋmei shishifãi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting shoots inside the storage barn before the rains even begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yams have an internal biological clock. After a few months of rest after harvest, warmth and moisture in the air signal to the yam that its resting period is over, causing it to use its stored food energy to grow new shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ wala mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko. Beni ejɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ leɔ akɛ ehejɔɔmɔ be lɛ eho. Enɛ haa akɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmeii heei.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies bite the leaf to suck sap, they spread the virus, which stunts the plant and stops it from fruiting properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji ŋmeii yɛji ŋmɔ baai koni amɛnu nu lɛ Amɛbaagbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaaa ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my crop protection chemicals in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ shwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon sun causes liquid spray to evaporate too quickly before the plant absorbs it, reducing its effectiveness. The intense heat combined with chemical droplets can also burn and damage your crop leaves.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bɔ ni nitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fataa he lɛ hu baanyɛ ashã ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it from the dirt. Drooping is the plant's clever way of turning its leaves away from the sun to save water, and they usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji ŋaa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛjieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la he koni amɛkɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade umbrella for the dirt. It keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and blocks weed seeds from receiving sunlight to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la koni amɛdara

english: Why is the spray medicine I use on my maize pests not killing them like it used to a few years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ egbeee amɛ tamɔ bɔ ni egbe afii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Pests can adapt over time when you use the exact same chemical repeatedly. The surviving insects pass this strength to their offspring, so switching to a different type of chemical prevents pests from building up resistance.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atsake amɛhe yɛ be ni sa mli. Koolooi ni hiɔ shi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ haa amɛbii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tsofa kroko nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni teɔ shi woɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my crops much faster during the warm rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures combined with rain create perfect breeding conditions for insects, causing their eggs to hatch rapidly into large populations that quickly feed on soft, new crop leaves.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi fɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛwuji lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ mɛi babaoo ni yeɔ tso hee lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ oya.

english: Can spraying too much chemical medicine on my field actually damage my crops instead of saving them?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeehere amɛyiwala?

english: Yes, using too much chemical can burn tender leaves, weaken plant roots, and kill helpful natural organisms in the soil that normally aid crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii. ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbeɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni bei pii lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is stressed, often caused by a lack of key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil or damage from small pests sucking the juice out of the leaves.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry weather stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to conserve water and energy rather than attempting to feed new growing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ashi amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Mohu ɔ, bɔ mɔde nɛ o ha tomato ehehi nɛ a ngɛ hɛ mi ɔ niye ní.

english: What happens to my crops if I put dry fertilizer in the soil when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. Placing fertilizer in dry soil keeps it concentrated in one spot, which can scorch and burn the roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ekome yɛ he kome. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni esha amɛ.

english: Why does rain water sit on top of my field and roll off instead of soaking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ taraa mishia lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ kɛyaa he kroko yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil that lacks organic matter acts like concrete. Adding natural compost loosens the soil so water can sink deep down to feed plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔnkrit. Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni nu lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weaker if I plant the same crop in the same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the ground and allows crop-specific diseases and pests to build up in the soil permanently.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haaa mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your seedlings by stealing soil water and fertilizer with their roots, while their tall leaves block the sunlight your young plants need to feed.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ odumɔwui lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ sũ mli nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛye nii lɛ naa.

english: Why do seeds saved from last season's harvest produce a weaker yield than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nyɔŋ ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Many modern seeds are bred specifically for one strong generation. Seeds collected from that harvest naturally lose those high-yield traits, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo pɔtɛɛ aha yinɔ nɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo babaoo sui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing flowers, but the flowers just fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off if tiny insects like midges are not present to pollinate them, or if the tree lacks enough nutrients and water to support the growth of the pods. Proper pruning and soil feeding help the tree retain its flowers.
