ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ, loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ. Kpojiemɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily when strong winds hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are too weak or planted too shallow in the ground. Planting seeds at the correct depth and piling soil around the base of the stems (hilling) gives the plants strong anchors against the wind.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa ni okɛ sũ ato tso lɛ shishi. (Gɔŋ lɛ nɔyaa) lɛ baaha tsei lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hewalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to make raised mounds or ridges before planting yam or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔwo gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ dani wɔdu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so that roots can easily expand into large tubers. The raised soil also prevents excess water from sitting around the roots and causing them to rot during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Shikpɔŋ ni awó nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts naturally grow their pods underground. After the flower on top is pollinated, the stem bends down and pushes into the soil so the nut can safely grow beneath the ground.
ga: Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This feeds the soil naturally and helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my crops yield much less food when I plant the exact same crop on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kwraa beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the ground every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I pinch off the little side shoots growing out of my tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato nine lɛ mli lɛ

english: Removing extra side shoots prevents the tomato plant from wasting its energy on unnecessary stems and leaves, directing all its strength into growing larger and healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi o-tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by heat stress when the plant tries to save water. Protecting plants from insects and keeping the soil moist helps keep leaves flat and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli beni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he lɛ. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Can I use the same chemical spray on my newly planted cocoa seedlings as I use on my older, mature cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii tamɔ bɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo tsei ni edara ni edara lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: No, young cocoa plants are very delicate and have tender stems and roots. Using strong chemicals meant for mature trees can burn the young plants and kill them, so seedlings need milder, specific treatments.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, ni amɛshishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni egbe amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui biɔ kwɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo babaoo.

english: How can I tell if a medicine or treatment I applied to my cocoa plants is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa loo tsamɔ ni mikɛ cacao tsuɔ nii lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will notice healthy signs such as new green shoots sprouting, leaves turning a rich dark green color, and a reduction in insect damage or yellow spots within a few weeks.
ga: Obaana hewalɛ kpakpa he okadii, tamɔ tsei heei ni eŋɔli. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What will happen to my young cocoa plants if I give them too much fertilizer or chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai babaoo ha amɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical or fertilizer can scorch the roots and leaves of young cocoa trees, causing them to dry up and die instead of growing faster.
ga: Tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I spray all parts of my farm with the same crop medicine at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tso kome lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi fɛɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Different areas of your farm may have plants at different growth stages. Young crops, flowering trees, and bearing trees require different care, so applying the same medicine everywhere can ruin sensitive young plants.
ga: Ekolɛ hei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Nibii bibii ni aduɔ, tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi, kɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Where is the best place for me to get quality cocoa seeds when starting a new farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ maná kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You should get certified seeds or pods from recognized agricultural officers or official research institutes, as seeds taken randomly from older farms may produce weak trees with low yield.
ga: Esa akɛ onine ashɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko loo niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhe ko ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Ejaakɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji momoi amli trukaa. Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need more special attention than the older trees already on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ fe cacao tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and thin stems, making them very vulnerable to hot sun, pests, and poor soil conditions, whereas older trees have established deep roots and thicker bark to protect themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛhewolo ni mli kwɔ ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe he.

english: How do I choose the healthiest young cocoa seedlings to plant on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select seedlings that have straight, thick stems, bright dark green leaves, no signs of insect bite marks or spots, and a strong root system.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni tsei lɛ ja, amɛtsii kɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Okadii loo ŋmeii komɛi bɛ ni ŋmeii emɔ lɛ. kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the young plant is stressed from lack of shade, poor soil nutrients, incorrect chemical use, or an attack by pests feeding on its roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ mli. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloi ni yeɔ eshishifãi lɛ atuatsemɔ.

english: When is the right time to start applying protective treatments to my newly planted cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje nibii ni akɛbuɔ kookoo ni adu ehee lɛ he lɛ shishi?

english: You should start protecting young cocoa once it is established in the soil and showing early signs of growth, but only using mild treatments designed for young plants when pests or diseases appear.
ga: Esa akɛ oje kookoo bibii ahebuu shishi beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli ni amɛjie amɛdalɛ he okadii lɛ akpo mra lɛ. Shi kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee aha tsei bibii lɛ pɛ atsu nii kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ba.

english: Why does cocoa respond better to crop medicines during certain seasons of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Plants absorb nutrients and medicines best during warm weather with steady rain; heavy rain can wash the treatment away before the plant uses it, while extreme heat can cause chemicals to burn the leaves.
ga: Tsei ŋmɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ tsofai jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsofa lɛ he dani tso lɛ kɛtsu nii. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsofai ashã baai lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is too much direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot handle strong, direct sun. Without shade plants like plantains to protect them, the sun causes them to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, causing them to wither.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or when the tree is stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or excessive heat, which forces the tree to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo be mli ni hɔmɔ miigba tsei anaa Niyenii nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Can I plant cassava inside my farm while my cocoa trees are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni kokoo tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: It is better to avoid cassava near young cocoa because cassava is a heavy feeder that competes aggressively for water and soil nutrients, and its large roots can disturb the weak roots of young cocoa trees.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie tapioka kɛjɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ji niyenii ni tsii ni kɛ ehe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ni shishifãi wuji baanyɛ agba kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my healthy green cocoa pods suddenly turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and humid conditions when rain splashes fungal spores onto the pods and air cannot circulate properly through dense branches.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ha fungal spores lɛ shwie ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the branches on some of my cocoa trees swelling up and leaf veins turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efuu ni baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: These are classic symptoms of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, a disease spread by tiny insects called mealybugs that infects the tree's vascular system and slows down its food movement.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ tso lɛ lá fãji lɛ anɔ ni ehaa niyenii lɛ yaa oya.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot branches growing from the stem of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called chupons, suck away valuable water and food nutrients from the main tree without producing good yield, reducing the overall pod production of your farm.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛkpaaa yibii kpakpai. Tsɔɔmɔ pod ni afeɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds stop growing under my cocoa trees once the branches grow big and join together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kpaɔ mi kokoo tso lɛ shishi be mli ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daraa ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa lɛ?

english: When cocoa branches join to form a thick canopy, they block sunlight from reaching the ground, and weeds cannot survive or grow without sunlight.
ga: Beni kookoo niji lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Ni jwɛi nyɛŋ ahi shi loo amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji hulu la bɛ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan wind affect the growth of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The Harmattan wind carries extremely dry air that strips moisture from leaves and soil, causing cocoa trees to drop their leaves early, shed flowers, and produce smaller pods.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa mli. ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Haa kookoo tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ oya, ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks nutrients for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn yellow instead of deep green, or if the trees grow very slowly and yield small pods year after year, it means the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Aloo, kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔŋ bibii afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick cocoa pods from my trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A cocoa pod is ripe and ready to harvest when its skin color changes completely, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to deep orange, indicating the sweet pulp and beans inside are mature.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛji amɛhewolo nɔ su etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there different types of maize seeds available, and how do I know which one to buy for my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Different maize varieties are bred for specific purposes, such as maturing fast during short rains, resisting dry spells, or producing larger cobs. Choosing the right one depends on how much rain your area gets and how quickly you need to harvest.
ga: Abele henɔi srɔtoi Akwɛɔ amɛ kɛha yiŋtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli, amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli, loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ bɔ ni okpaa nii oya lɛ nɔ ni ooohala nɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ.

english: Will all types of maize yield the same amount of grain if I apply the same fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmãa henɔi fɛɛ baawo dumɔwui babaoo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa henɔ kome wo mli?

english: No, each variety has a different built-in yield potential. Improved varieties are designed to turn soil nutrients into bigger cobs, whereas traditional seeds may produce less even with plenty of fertilizer.
ga: Dabi, srɔtofeemɔ yɔɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baanyɛ awo yibii aha. Afee ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛtsake niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. yɛ be mli ni blema dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii fioo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli po.

english: Can I save the seeds from my improved maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended because hybrid seeds lose their strength and uniformity after the first harvest. Planting saved seeds usually leads to lower yields and uneven plant growth in the second year.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni tsei lɛ hu daaa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can maize really mature in just three months, and how does it compare to normal maize?
ga: Ani ŋmãa baanyɛ adara diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nyɔji 3 pɛ mli ni te ekɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ yeɔ egbɔ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, short-duration varieties mature in about 90 days. They are ideal if the rainy season is short, though longer-maturing varieties often produce larger cobs if given enough rain throughout the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ shwereɔ yɛ aaafee gbii 90 mli, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛwoɔ lɛ kɛji amɛná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ moŋ.

english: What type of crop seed should I choose if the rain starts late in my region?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mahala kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: When rains are delayed, plant an early-maturing variety that matures in 3 months. This ensures the crop completes its growth cycle before the dry season sets in.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ Dumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra, ni shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbeɔ edalɛ be lɛ naa dani hɔmɔ be lɛ baa.

english: Are fast-maturing crops better at surviving drought than slow-maturing ones?
ga: Ani tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Fast-maturing crops 'escape' drought by completing their life cycle quickly before the soil dries up, whereas slow-growing crops need reliable rain for a longer period to produce grain.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ ‘joɔ’ hɔmɔ naa foi kɛtsɔ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ ni amɛgbeɔ naa oya dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni daa blɛoo lɛ he miihia nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛwo dumɔwui.

english: How many seeds of maize should I drop into one planting hole?
ga: Abele dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛwo dumɔ bu kome mli?

english: Planting 2 seeds per hole is usually ideal. If you put too many seeds together, the plants compete for soil nutrients and sunlight, resulting in thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui 2 ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo fata he lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: How can I test a new crop seed safely without risking my whole farm's harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka dumɔwui heei makwɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can plant a small test plot of about 10 to 20 plants alongside your regular crops. This lets you observe how the new variety behaves on your soil before spending money to plant it across your entire field.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni tsei aaafee 10 kɛyashi 20 yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ onibii ni oduɔ daa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa okwɛɔ bɔ ni tsei srɔtoi heei ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa dani ofiteɔ shika ni okɛduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant two different varieties of maize right next to each other in the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa henɔi enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: You can plant them side-by-side, but wind will mix their pollen, which affects the seed quality if you plan to save seeds. To see which variety performs best, keep them in distinct separate sections of your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ amɛhe. Shi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafutu pollen lɛ. Enɛ baaná dumɔwui lɛ ahe hewalɛ kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛto. Ani oosumɔ ni ona henɔi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ? Jajemɔ nakai srɔtoi lɛ amli awo fãi srɔtoi amli. srɔto yɛ onitsumɔ lɛ mli

english: How do I know if my newly sprouted maize is growing at the normal speed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ miida oya bɔ ni sa?

english: Healthy maize usually sprouts within 4 to 7 days and develops deep green leaves quickly. If growth looks delayed or leaves appear yellowish within the first few weeks, the plants may lack nutrients or be suffering from weed competition.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli ni ebaa oya. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni dalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tsei lɛ baanyɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ loo jwɛi akaŋshimɔ baanyɛ aná he amanehulu.

english: Why do my local mangoes spoil so much faster than the imported fruit juices sold in town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ mangoi lɛ fiteɔ oya fe nu ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fresh local fruits have high moisture content and natural sugars that attract bacteria and fungi after harvest, while processed imported fruit products contain additives and preservatives that prevent spoilage and extend shelf life.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli aduawai heei lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni adebɔɔ mli sugar ni gbalaa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii kɛbaa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nibii ni haaa amɛfite ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my harvested fruits fresh for a longer time without buying expensive machines?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha aduawai ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni miheee tsɔnei ni jara wa?

english: Harvesting your fruits during the cool early morning, keeping them under shade, and storing them in ventilated crates reduces field heat and slows down the natural ripening and rotting process.
ga: Yibii ni akpaa yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Ha ehi hulutsoo be mli. ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my harvested mangoes rot from the inside even when the skin looks clean on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Internal rotting is often caused by fruit flies laying tiny eggs under the skin while the fruit is still on the tree, or by fungal spores that grow inside as the fruit softens during ripening.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa. Hewolo lɛ shishi be mli ni aduawai lɛ kã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli beni aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I plant local fruit varieties or improved foreign seeds for my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu maŋ lɛ mli aduawai loo matsake maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Improved foreign varieties often yield more and meet commercial export standards, but local varieties are usually better suited to our soil, resist local pests better, and are preferred by local market buyers for fresh food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ tsoi srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛshɛɔ jarayeli nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ahe mlai ahe. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ sa wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli hei lɛ sumɔɔ niyenii hee.

english: Why do grafted fruit trees bear fruit much faster than trees I grow directly from seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso yibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe tsei ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grafting attaches a branch from a mature, fruit-bearing tree onto a young root system, which tricks the plant into skipping its young growth phase so it produces fruit within two to three years.
ga: Tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ niji ni jɛ tso ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli lɛ fĩɔ shishifã bibioo ko he. ni lakaa tso lɛ koni efo fã ni ji tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why are some of my mango trees producing large fleshy fruits while others produce small fibrous ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ loo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ yibii ni tsɔji bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Different varieties of mangoes naturally have different genetic traits, where some are bred to have thick meat for eating as solid food and others have stringy flesh best suited for juice extraction.
ga: Mango henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Akwɛɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛná loo ni mli edɔ ni ayeɔ akɛ niyenii ni wa. Ni ekomɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why do my fruit trees produce heavy yields this year but almost nothing the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi nɛɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, ani afeee nɔ ko kwraa?

english: This behavior is called alternate bearing, where the tree uses up all its stored energy and nutrients to produce a huge crop in one season, requiring the next season to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ tsakemɔ. He ni tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Esa akɛ amɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛtswa amɛhewalɛ amɛma shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my fruits taste watery instead of sweet and firm during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ tamɔ nu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops absorb excessive water right before harvest, the trees pump that extra moisture directly into the fruit, diluting its natural sugars and making the flesh soft.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo dani amɛkpaa lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli sugar lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa loo lɛ feɔ blɛoo

english: Can I turn my unsold fruits into processed products like dried snacks or juices to avoid wasting them?
ga: Mibaanyɛ matsɔ aduawai ni ahɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ afee nibii ni afee tamɔ niyenii ni egbi loo aduawai amli nu. Koni ekafite?

english: Yes, processing excess harvest into dried fruit slices or pasteurized juice preserves the crop, prevents post-harvest loss, and allows you to sell value-added products during the off-season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afee ŋmaa ni fa fe nine lɛ aduawai ni egbi loo nu ni akɛ pasteurized fee lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite. Tsi nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ naa. ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni jara wa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my sweet local fruits more than the commercial varieties on nearby farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mimaŋ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ fe srɔtoi ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Local fruit varieties often produce stronger natural odors and higher sugar levels as they ripen, which attracts pests like fruit flies more strongly than hybrid varieties bred with thicker skins.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli aduawai srɔtoi lɛ fɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa kɛ sugar ni fa babaoo kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii waa fe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛ amɛhe ewo mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are receiving too much direct sunlight or lacking nutrients like nitrogen. Young cocoa requires shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia trees to protect them while their roots establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛbɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen. Kookoo bibioo he miihia tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantain loo glicidia tsei. Koni abu amɛhe beni amɛshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my plantain tree falling over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over easily because they have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. Stacking soil around the base (mounding) and using strong wooden poles to prop up fruiting plants will keep them upright during heavy rains and winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ wo shishitoo lɛ he (pile) lɛ he, ni akɛ tsei ni wa tsu nii kɛfi aduawai tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody instead of growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if planted in hard, compacted soil where they cannot expand, or if planted too close together. Creating raised mounds or ridges softens the soil, giving the tubers room to swell and store food.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baakã he afee bibioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ ni nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwa lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛfuɔ ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to spread its leaves to catch maximum sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to prevent disease and helps the plant produce more energy to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the funnel (whorl) of maize plants. Early detection and applying recommended treatments or neem extracts into the center of the plants will protect the leaves and cobs.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ŋmeii (rings) amli. Nibii ni ana mra Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem mli nu lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer leaves (husks) turn completely brown and dry, and a small black spot appears at the base of a grain kernel when pulled from the cob, showing it has stopped growing.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ baai (chaff) lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi kɛji ajie kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ ekpa shweremɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, which is often caused by inconsistent watering or long dry periods while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and feeling hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Removing heavily infected plants and spraying with insecticidal soap helps control the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Is it better to apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is dry or after rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafata he kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer should always be applied when the soil is moist after rain. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the nutrients because plants need water to absorb fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu he miihia tsei koni amɛnyɛ amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas make my farmland better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This natural food stays behind to feed heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli ni amɛyɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ashiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ koni akɛye kooloi aniyenii tsei ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas provides shelter and traps moisture, helping young cocoa plants survive dry spells.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni ehiɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer, compost, or well-rotted animal manure can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing, usually a few weeks after planting and again before flowering. Applying fertilizer during heavy rain washes it away, while applying it to dry soil can burn the plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ kɛ ekoŋŋ dani fɔfɔii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafɔ ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem cuttings for planting on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select healthy stems from mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from pests or diseases. Cut stems that are firm and thick, ensuring each planting stick has at least 4 to 6 strong buds for proper sprouting.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai bɛ mli lɛ amli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni mli wa, ni mli tse. Kwɛmɔ ni tso fɛɛ tso ni aduɔ lɛ aná kɛ hoo lɛ ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting crops too close causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and airflow to grow strong and produce well.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly when I leave weeds in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your main crops. Keeping the field clean, especially during the first few weeks after planting, ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hia, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Gbɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse Titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat hole shapes into my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that damages young maize leaves and growing points. Catching them early and applying approved crop protection sprays, neem extract, or hand-picking them helps save your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmei baai bibii kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ, neem mli nu, loo nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face severe heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrition. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps flowers stay attached and form healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni falɛ faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Insects thrive on moisture in stored grains. Ensure your harvested maize is thoroughly dried in the sun until the grains are hard before bagging, and store them in clean areas using sealed bags or approved grain protection dusts.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani okɛwo kotoku mli. ni okɛto he ko ni he tse kɛtsɔ kotoku loo dumɔwui ahe nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed for green leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed the food away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaye abua mi?

english: Yes, groundnuts take natural nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps the land fertile without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa ni ŋmãa ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by severe heat and uneven watering that stresses the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be, ni haa tso lɛ haoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ aniji je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can easily be damaged by underground pests like stem borers or nematodes, making the heavy plant tip over when strong winds blow.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Enɛ haa tso ni tsii lɛ kuɔmɔɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo dani etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers, but losing too many flowers usually happens when the tree lacks water, loses shade, or is attacked by insect pests like mirids.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu. ŋmɔlɔ ni elaaje loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutuaa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested seed yam lie dormant for months before it begins to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ehi shi lɛ? Nyɔji enyiɛ dani ebaaje shishi ekwɛ̃?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural sleeping period called dormancy after harvest, which protects them from drying out until the weather conditions are right for new growth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekagbi kɛyashi shihilɛi baafee nɔ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ hee.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose all their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their leaves to conserve water when the soil gets dry, helping the stem survive the hot weather until the rains come back.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do crops like sorghum stay alive during dry spells while my maize dries up and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deeper roots and can temporarily pause its growth and roll its leaves to save moisture until rain returns, whereas maize needs steady water.
ga: Sorghum shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛbaa lɛ abɔle ehe koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa he hiaa nu daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil blocks air from reaching the cassava roots, causing water rot and fungi to quickly breakdown the tubers before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa muji kɛ ŋmeii baa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akpaa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and absorb water and soil food faster than young crop seeds, allowing them to germinate and spread very quickly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand direct, intense sunlight. They burn easily and need temporary shade crops like plantains to cover them and keep the soil moist while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛshãa oya ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why is my maize crop turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves are a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to build green leaves. Applying fertilizer or compost rich in nitrogen gives the crop the nutrients it needs to grow healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look twisted with light yellow patterns on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps stop the virus and ensures you get large cassava roots at harvest.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ Ashishi tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akaboteɔ mli ni ehaa onáa ŋmeii shishifãi wuji kɛji akpa.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers from my plantain tree instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie plantain tso ko mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain plant, they steal water and nutrients from each other. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the plant to focus its energy on producing bigger, heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: This black rot is caused by uneven watering, which prevents the plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil. Watering your tomato plants consistently keeps the fruit healthy and rot-free.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ black rot hela nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ nu haa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkafite.

english: Yam vines need to stretch out in the sunlight to produce food for the root tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, protecting them from diseases and helping the yams grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ashɛ hulu lɛ he koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help my soil for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize or vegetables on that same land afterward, they naturally grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ Amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need without sharing them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛja.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry soil. Spreading dry grass or leaves around the base of the plant as mulch keeps the soil cool and moist so the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa. Mulch kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it good to burn all the vegetation on my land before planting?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashã tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic material in the soil that feeds your crops. Clearing the land without burning or leaving dead leaves to rot keeps the soil naturally fertile and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni fiɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa lɛ loo ahaaa baai lɛ agbo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green leaves. It can also happen when the roots are soaked in too much water and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shishifãi lɛ bote nu babaoo mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why are the small pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is commonly caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet weather and in farms with too much shade and poor air flow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. kɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu eyaaa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest since the tubers stay hidden under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ejaakɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the main stem turns woody, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil drops too low in moisture, or when tiny pests damage the small stem holding the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ tsei bibii ni akɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii lɛ

english: How can I tell if my crops are weak because the soil is poor or because insects are attacking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Poor soil causes uniform yellowing, thin stems, and slow growth across the whole leaf, while insect damage leaves distinct holes, chewed edges, curled leaf tips, or sticky spots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ buji ni yɔɔ srɔtoi, ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ebɔle ehe, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines start drying up prematurely before the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miije shishi amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by leaf spot diseases like anthracnose or soil-borne pests like nematodes that damage the roots and block water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe helai tamɔ anthracnose loo shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes, ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu gbɛ koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops grow so thin and weak when I leave grass growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mishiɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots, leaving your plants underfed and shaded.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naaa niyenii kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the leaf sap, or by a virus transmitted by small whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: During peak heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can drink it up. Drooping is the plant's way of reducing leaf size to save water until the afternoon heat passes.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Defoliation ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebaa baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛto nu he kɛyashi shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaho.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when the fruit bundle starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny soil worms called nematodes or banana weevil pests destroy the root system, leaving the plant without a strong anchor in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo banana beetle ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni wa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow and die after heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When floodwater covers the soil for days, it prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing the plant to drown, turn yellow, and eventually die.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu afua lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground after a long period of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot because standing floodwater starves the roots of oxygen and creates a damp environment where underground fungi thrive, causing the roots to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ. ni efee shihilɛ ko ni mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant on land that regularly gets flooded during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like rice, cocoyam, and sugarcane tolerate high moisture and standing water much better than crops like maize, pepper, or cassava, which rot quickly when flooded.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, kookoo, kɛ ŋmãa nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ nu ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni damɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fe nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa. ni baafite oya kɛji nu afua

english: Why do my young seedlings stop growing after floodwater leaves mud all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ nu afua ko sɛɛ, ni amɛshi muji yɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Mud covers the leaves and blocks the sunlight that crops need to make their food. Without sunlight and air, the young plants cannot grow and may suffocate.
ga: Muji lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii lɛ naa. Kɛji hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ adara ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi.

english: Why do I notice more plant diseases on my field after floodwaters dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina akɛ tsei ahe helai etee hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔji amli beni nu afua lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Excess moisture and high humidity after flooding create ideal conditions for fungi and bacteria to multiply, while plants weakened by waterlogging are less able to fight off infections.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ nu afua lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwu amɛshi helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my farm from flooding if I don't have tractors or heavy machines to reshape the land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ nu afua he? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ traktɔ loo nibii ni tsii ni mikɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu?

english: You can manually dig simple drainage channels or ditches around your farm using basic tools like hoes and cutlasses to direct excess rainwater away from your crops and into nearby streams.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu homɔ gbɛ loo nubu ko yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Obaanyɛ otsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he bo diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ shishijee nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei nɔ ni okɛjie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ onibii amli kɛya faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does planting crops on high soil mounds help them survive heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛye nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ kunim?

english: Making high mounds raises the crop roots above the standing water level, allowing them to get oxygen and stay healthy even when floodwater gathers in the hollow spaces between the mounds.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ fe nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu afua lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ po mli lɛ.

english: Why does fast-moving floodwater carry away the good topsoil from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu afua ni hoɔ oya lɛ miiho shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Topsoil is light and easily washed away by heavy rain if there are no plant roots or physical barriers to hold it down. Once the topsoil is gone, the land loses most of its natural nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ waaa, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya. Kɛji tso shishifãi loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii komɛi bɛ ni baaha ehi shi yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ etee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ebɔɔ nii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Can planting trees or tall grasses along my farm boundary stop floodwaters from destroying my crops?
ga: Ani tsei loo jwɛi kakadaŋŋ adumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ akpa nu afua ni mifiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting deep-rooted grasses like vetiver or broad trees along the edges of your farm acts as a natural wall that slows down fast-moving water, traps fertile soil, and prevents crop destruction.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni mli kwɔlɔ ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni haa nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Emɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akpãtãmɔ naa

english: Why does the soil on my field become very hard and cracked after floodwater dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa beni nu afua ko egbi lɛ?

english: Floodwater washes away organic matter and packs fine soil particles tightly together. When the tropical sun dries the wet land, these tightly packed soil particles bake into a hard, dense crust.
ga: Nu afua mli nu lɛ hoɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni ehaa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ sũ mli nibii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe nɛɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ sũ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants turn yellow from the leaf tips when they lack nitrogen, which is the essential plant food needed to build strong, green leaves and healthy stalks.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ebaai lɛ anaa kɛji nitrogen bɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do extension agents recommend planting cowpea or groundnuts inside my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpea and groundnuts gather natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil and helps neighboring crops grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait until after my seeds sprout before applying fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds without roots cannot absorb fertilizer, so applying fertilizer before sprouting can wash it away with heavy rain or burn the delicate new root tissues as they emerge.
ga: Dumɔwui ni shishifãi bɛ amɛhe lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nɔ loo eshã shishifã hee ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ beni ejɛɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big canopy trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect tender leaves from scorching sunlight and to retain soil moisture while their root systems establish.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce food for the root tubers below ground; staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal decay and improving food production.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa ni ehaa niyenii afeemɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops when there seems to be plenty of soil for everything?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your crops and leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi fioo.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or viruses transmitted by these pests as they feed on leaf sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without setting any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry out tomato pollen, causing flowers to drop off as the plant conserves energy rather than developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ fe bɔ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil deprives roots of oxygen and creates excess moisture, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to multiply and rot the mature roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náa lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi ni eda lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds lose their strong characteristics after the first generation, so planting seeds saved from a hybrid harvest leads to weak plants and much lower yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaa nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi kwraa.

english: How do I know if my land is ready and good enough for planting maize before the rains start?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ lɛ baakpa?

english: Good soil for maize should be loose, well-drained, and cleared of big weeds. Preparing your land early allows the soil to trap the first rainwaters and gives your seeds a soft environment to sprout quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ojie jwɛi wuji Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ nu lɛ. ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: How does adding dried animal dung or compost to my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal dung and compost act as natural food for the soil. They improve the soil's ability to hold water during dry days and release nutrients slowly to your crops as they grow.
ga: Koolooi ashishi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni ojie niyenii mli hewalɛ kpo fiofio kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my last harvest or buy new certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Aloo obaahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: While saved seeds are free, certified seeds from registered dealers are tested to resist common diseases and produce much higher yields, giving your farm a stronger start.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he ehiaaa moŋ, shi akaa dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Ye obua oŋmɔ lɛ ni eje shishi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do agriculture officers advise us to measure specific distances between plants instead of just scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔsusu he ni tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui kɛkɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets its fair share of sunlight, water, and soil food. When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other and grow weak.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe baabɔ akaŋ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: How does planting at the very beginning of the rainy season help my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔ ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Planting with the early rains allows young crop roots to establish deep in the soil while it is warm and moist, giving them a strong head start before the dry spells or heavy weed invasion begin.
ga: Dumɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be loo jwɛi ni baa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why should I nurse tomato seeds in a small nursery bed first instead of planting them directly on the big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and delicate. Nursing them lets you protect young seedlings from hot sun and heavy rains, so you can pick only the strongest plants to transfer to your main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohala tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ni okɛya oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers plant maize and cassava together on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping allows you to maximize your land. The fast-growing maize is harvested early, leaving the field open for the cassava to expand later without competing for light and nutrients at the same time.
ga: Tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ohe woɔ mli babaoo. Akpaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ni ashiɔ koni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã sɛɛ mli ni ekɛ la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ akaŋ yɛ be kome mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is getting too much water around its roots. Correcting the soil nutrients early helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehe miihia ni asaa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ

english: Does clearing weeds when crops are very small really make a difference in my harvest?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ baa mikpamɔ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your young plants. Removing weeds early ensures all the goodness goes straight to your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa kpakpai fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize plants mostly inside the middle funnel of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the central leaf funnel because it is soft, cool, and provides fresh tender growth for them to eat. Checking the funnels early helps you spot and control them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo, amɛhe jɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ehee. Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mra Ehaa onaa nakai gbɛi lɛ ni okudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying my maize with chemicals before I can safely harvest it?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai eshwie ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa ŋmãa lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Every pesticide has a required waiting period called a pre-harvest interval. Harvesting too early leaves chemical residues on the maize, which can make consumers sick and cause your crop to fail market safety tests.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná hela ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaye jarayeli shweshweeshwefeemɔ he kaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Can using too many chemical sprays on my crops cause long-term health problems like cancer for people who eat them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, tamɔ kansa aba mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, when crops are over-sprayed, harmful chemical residues build up in the grains. Eating food with high pesticide residues over many years increases the risk of serious health conditions, including cancer.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashwie tsei anɔ fe nine Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Niyenii ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli lɛ ni oooye afii babaoo lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ obaaná helai ni mli wa waa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kansa fata he

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plant turn yellow and burn after I apply weedkiller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much weedkiller or spraying during the heat of the day causes chemical burn and stresses the plant, interfering with its normal growth and ability to make food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi babaoo tsu nii loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ashã tsei lɛ ni amɛhao. Etsiɔ dalɛ ni sa kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhoɔ niyenii lɛ naa.

english: How can I check if my harvested maize has hidden chemical residues before I take it to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ dani mikɛwo jara nɔ?

english: You can take a small sample of your grain to an agricultural laboratory for residue testing. The lab uses special chemical analysis to tell you if the grain is safe for human consumption.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko aya okwaayeli he ko koni oyakwɛ kɛji nɔ ko eshwɛ yɛ mli. Lab lɛ kɛ tsofai krɛdɛɛi amlipɛimɔ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsɔɔ bo kɛji ŋmaa lɛ hi kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: Why do commercial grain buyers ask for a lab paper or test certificate before buying my maize in bulk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa kɛha jarayeli lɛ biɔ ni aha amɛ laboratorio woji loo kaa he woji dani amɛheɔ mi ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: A laboratory test paper proves that your maize meets safety standards, showing that it is free from dangerous levels of chemical residues and fungal toxins that cannot be seen with the human eye.
ga: Laboratory kaa woji maa nɔ mi akɛ o-abele lɛ yeɔ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai lɛ anɔ. Atsɔɔ akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ kɛ mycotoxins ni gbɔmɔ hiŋmɛi enaaa lɛ bɛ mli.

english: What standard must my maize meet if I want to export it to buyers outside Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai esa akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ashɛ he kɛji miisumɔ ni mikɛmaje mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Exported maize must meet strict national and international safety limits. It must be thoroughly dried, free from live insects, and pass official lab checks showing very low pesticide and toxin levels.
ga: Esa akɛ abele ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ashɛ maŋ kɛ majimaji shweshweeshwefeemɔ he naatsii ni mli wa lɛ he. Esa akɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ. Ebɛ kooloi ni hiɛ ka ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ laboratori ko ni maŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ mli.

english: Why do international buyers reject some of our Ghanaian grains even when they look clean and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ wɔ Ghana dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse ni amɛgbi moŋ?

english: Grains may look clean on the outside but still fail safety standards due to invisible contaminants, such as high pesticide residues from field spraying or unseen fungal poisons like aflatoxins.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmaa baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi eshɛɛɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai lɛ ahe lolo yɛ muji ni anaaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni fa babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli. loo tsofai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni anaaa tamɔ aflatoxin.

english: Why does my stored maize develop dark mold even after I dried it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ migbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?
