english: Sun drying might dry the outer layer, but if the core of the kernel still holds moisture above 13%, fungi will continue to grow inside the storage bag, producing dangerous poisons.
ga: Hulu lɛ baanyɛ aha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ agbi. Shi kɛji akɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi fe 13% lɛ, ŋmeii baaya nɔ ada yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli. Ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara baa

english: Why do insect pests like armyworms attack my maize plants more heavily during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ waa fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather stresses the maize plant and weakens its natural defenses, making it easier for pests to feed on the leaves and reproduce quickly.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa abele tsei haoɔ ni ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hewalɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Does spraying heavy chemicals repeatedly every season damage the soil for my next crop?
ga: Tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ shi shii abɔ Ani be fɛɛ be fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, excessive chemical sprays accumulate in the topsoil and kill beneficial soil micro-organisms, which reduces natural soil fertility and can stunt future crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi, ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for green leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore the dark green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce long bushy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of food below. Planting in loose, well-drained soil and balancing soil nutrients helps the plant send energy down to build big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe niyenii ni yɔɔ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni edaa lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ woɔ shi ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally release this food into the soil, feeding nearby maize crops without requiring extra commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii nɛɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni jarayeli ŋmãa kroko he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni baai ni egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or straw acts like a shade blanket. It shields the soil from the hot sun, keeps water from evaporating too quickly during dry spells, and cools the plant roots so they can absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ mlɛo

english: Every extra shoot steals water, light, and soil nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main parent plant gets maximum energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tso lɛ yitso fɛɛ tso ni fata he lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate energy to build big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves into the sunlight and keeps them away from hot, damp soil where fungal diseases easily rot the plant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la he ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni edɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbo oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the air gets too hot, when soil moisture changes rapidly from dry to wet, or when bees aren't around to pollinate them. Regular watering and planting flowering herbs nearby to attract pollinators helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ koni amɛfee pollination, amɛha nu ni amɛdu fɔfɔi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. daa koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds pull water out of cocoa leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from dry soil. Keeping shade trees over cocoa plants and placing dry grass mulch around the roots holds in water and shields the crop from harsh winds.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ He Kwɛmɔ: Ha kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo ehe. shishifãi ni akɛtoɔ nu he ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaf, which can also spread plant viruses. Spraying the undersides of leaves with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã tsei amli hu Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Aloo neem fɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground. Rotating with root crops or beans gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ shishifãi loo ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛsaa ehe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even after I spent money buying fertilizer from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mikɛ shika lɛ he ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are lacking nitrogen, or heavy rain washed the fertilizer away before the roots could soak it up. Applying fertilizer in split doses and burying it lightly in the soil prevents this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ mlijaa mli ni afuɔ lɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to clear all weeds before putting fertilizer around my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani wɔkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmei lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the expensive nutrients from the fertilizer before your cassava roots can reach them, making your investment a waste.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ejuɔ niyenii ni jara wa waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛɔ he. Ha shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ afee yaka.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight like small balls and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny invisible pests like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the plant juice and spreading viruses. Treating the plants early with organic neem oil or recommended sprays stops these insects.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni anaaa tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei mra. Kɛ organic neem fɔ loo spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ. lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating the inner growing leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that target the tender center of young maize plants where it is moist and safe from sun. Checking your field early and putting neem powder or recommended control into the plant centers protects them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni mli edɔ ni hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ amli mra Ni akɛ neem powder loo nibii krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baafata tsei akwɛmɔhei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and wilt during the afternoon sun even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes tomatoes to lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. They usually recover by evening once the air cools down.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, elaajeɔ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my bean plants without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or a sudden lack of water during flowering causes severe stress, making the plant shed its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunshine; their tender leaves burn easily. Planting plantains alongside them provides essential shade and moisture until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Ebaai bibii lɛ baashã oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant maize and cowpeas together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as natural food that helps your maize grow bigger without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava focus all its energy on leaf growth instead of storing starch underground. Balanced nutrients encourage big root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa lɛ dalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ powda lɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa.

english: Why do small weevils appear inside my stored maize bags even when I tied the bag tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei bibioo lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ Mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid on the corn while it is still in the field. Drying your grain thoroughly under the sun before storing kills those hidden eggs and prevents them from hatching.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛwoɔ ŋmãa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Why do traders insist on packing harvested tomatoes in wooden boxes instead of sacks when transporting them long distances?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ amɛkɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ awo tsei adekai amli moŋ fe kotokui kɛ́ amɛkɛmiiya he ko ni jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have soft skins and crush easily under weight. Rigid wooden boxes absorb the pressure of stacking and protect the fruit inside from getting crushed when trucks bounce on rough roads.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔɔ oya kɛji etsii. Tso adekai ni wa lɛ jieɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ, ni ebuɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe koni amɛkakumɔ kɛji lɔle lɛ tswa yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my papayas and mangoes a few days after transport, even when the outer skin is not broken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mipapaya kɛ mango lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni mikɛmaje lɛ sɛɛ? Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ etseee po.

english: Those dark spots are internal bruises caused by fruit repeatedly bumping against hard surfaces or other fruit during transit. Even if the skin stays intact, the delicate flesh underneath breaks down from shaking.
ga: Nakai ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ji mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni aduawai lɛ tswaa nɔ ko ni wa loo aduawai krokomɛi shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ kɛbaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ni yeɔ emuu mli lolo moŋ. Shi loo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ mli fã kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my crops very close together so the farm is tightly packed, will I harvest more yield?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi lɛ Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, packing crops too tightly forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Squeezed plants become thin, weak, and produce much smaller yields than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli fe nine lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei ni ashɛreɔ lɛ yɛ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize and cassava plants keep falling over whenever strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants fall over (lodging) when their root systems are shallow or stems are weak. Mounding soil firmly around the base of the stem gives the roots a solid anchor to keep the plant stable during heavy winds.
ga: Tsei gbeeɔ shi (wɔɔ) kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he shiŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni ma shi shiŋŋ koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why should I harvest plantains while they are still hard and green if I am sending them to a distant market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa plantains be mli ni amɛmli wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ kɛji akɛ mikɛ amɛ baatsu nii yɛ jarayeli he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ?

english: Green plantains are firm and resistant to bruising during long, rough journeys. If you wait until they turn soft and yellow, the shaking of the vehicle will crush and spoil them before they reach buyers.
ga: Plantains eŋɔli lɛ wa ni enyɛŋ etswa yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni mli wa mli. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Tsɔne lɛ mli hosomɔ lɛ baakumɔ lɛ ni efite lɛ dani eshɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Is it safe to seal my harvested yams in an airtight container to keep them safe from pests?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mawo mi-sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite amɛ?

english: No, harvested roots and tubers are living plant tissue that need to breathe. Sealing them in airtight containers builds up heat and moisture, which causes rapid rotting and mold growth.
ga: Dabi, tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni akpa lɛ ji tso lɛ mli fãji ni hiɛ ka ni ehe hiaa ni amɛmu. Kɛ́ akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fiteɔ oya ni ŋmeii hu daa.

english: How do I know my harvested maize is dry enough to pack tightly into sacks for long storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛwo kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can test maize by pressing a grain with your fingernail or biting it. If it is hard and snaps cleanly without leaving a dent, it is dry enough; moisture trapped inside a packed bag will cause dangerous mold and spoilage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ onineshi ni ooonyɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni oooŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ewa ni ehiɛɔ hetsemɔ mli ni eshiii ŋmeii. Etsɔɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ oshara aba.

english: When transplanting young seedlings, why must I press the soil down firmly around the stem?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu dumɔwui bibii lɛ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pressing the soil removes large air pockets around the delicate roots, ensuring they stay in direct contact with soil moisture while holding the seedling upright and stable.
ga: Kɛ́ anyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui wuji ni bɔleɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young seedlings dry out and die so quickly when left exposed in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have thin stems and shallow root systems that cannot pull water fast enough to replace what hot sun and wind dry out. Providing temporary shade shields them until their root systems grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsoɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo baaye abua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves around my crops help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ebɔle he lɛ shwieɔ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) acts like a protective blanket that shields the ground from hot sun, preventing soil moisture from evaporating and keeping the crop roots cool.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why should I spend money buying fresh certified seeds instead of just planting leftover seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ du wuhi nɛ piɛ ngɛ nyagbe ní kpami be ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected and treated to give you a strong foundation, leading to higher germination rates, better resistance to local diseases, and uniform growth compared to old saved seeds.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni eha oná shishitoo ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ ni eshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni edaa pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe

english: How can I test if the crop seeds I stored from last season are still alive and good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: You can do a simple germination test by putting ten seeds in a moist cloth for a few days; if fewer than eight sprout, the seeds have lost their strength and will not give you a good yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji dumɔwui ni fa fe kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli ni amɛhaŋ bo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some imported seed varieties fail on my farm even when I give them the same care as my local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ yeɔ tamɔ mimaŋ tsei moŋ.

english: Imported crop varieties are often bred for different soil conditions and weather, so they require specific inputs and soil preparation to perform well compared to locally adapted crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ he miihia koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsake yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after putting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a precise balance of moisture and loose soil to wake up; if the soil is too dry, too compacted, or planted too deep, the seed struggles to push its first green shoot to the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui hia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛte shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi tsɔ loo adu lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my young seedlings look pale yellow and weak instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young plants usually mean they lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient that crops need at the early stage to build green leaves and feed themselves through sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ amɛmli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei yɛ shishijee mli koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛna niyenii amɛha amɛhe kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ.

english: Is it possible to kill my young crop shoots by giving them too much water?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ agbe mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni mikɛwoɔ amɛnɔ fe nine lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, overwatering fills all the small air spaces in the soil, which smothers the young roots, prevents them from breathing, and leads to root rot and weak plant growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni awoɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. tsiɔ mumɔ naa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many seeds as possible close together to get a bigger crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and a much lower total harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa baa.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery bed into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants experience transplant shock when moved suddenly to harsh sunlight; they need to be gradually exposed to full sun and handled carefully so their tender roots are not damaged.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ naa shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ amɛtsakemɔ mli kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli trukaa. Esa akɛ amɛfee fiofio Get full sun ni amɛtsu he nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkafite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds when my crops are still tiny green shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ayeɔ lɛ he hiaa waa lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lolo?

english: Tiny seedlings need maximum soil nutrients to build strong roots, and aggressive weeds will steal those nutrients and sunlight if you do not remove them early in the crop's life.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Ni jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ baaju nakai niyenii kɛ hulu la lɛ kɛji ojieee amɛ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi.

english: What is cutting down my young crop shoots right at the ground level during the night?
ga: Mɛni ji mi tsei bibii lɛ ni miifo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ?

english: Pests like cutworms hide in the soil during the day and feed on soft tender seedling stems at night; controlling soil pests at the planting stage protects your crops before they are destroyed.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛkɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe dani amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to measure and space out my cocoa trees in straight lines instead of planting them anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ni mikɛ amɛ ato amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Proper spacing and straight rows ensure that every tree gets equal sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier as the farm grows.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni falɛ kome. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Can I grow crops like cassava or maize on the same plot of land with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ?

english: Crops like plantain or cocoyam are good to plant with young cocoa because they provide helpful shade. However, cassava and maize steal too much water and nutrients from the soil, which can stunt young cocoa trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ kookoo bibii baadu tsei tamɔ plantain loo cocoa ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa juɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tso lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from my bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving some tall economic trees on your farm creates a canopy that protects the young seedlings from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shika tsei ni oooshi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does cutting off extra branches and suckers help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Removing unwanted branches and suckers prevents the tree from wasting food and energy on useless leaves. It opens up the tree to sunlight and airflow, encouraging more healthy flowers and pods to grow.
ga: Niji kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa trees to drop their flowers before the fruits even start growing?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi cacao tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ po je shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Flowers drop off when the tree lacks water or proper nutrients, or when insects attack them. Regular weeding, proper soil feeding, and shade management help the tree hold onto its flowers until pods form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni sa. aloo be mli ni kooloi tutuaa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa Kɛ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees bloom mostly during the rainy season and stop flowering during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni ekpaa fɔfɔi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need plenty of soil moisture to produce flowers and feed developing pods. During the dry season, trees save their water and energy just to survive the heat, so flowering naturally slows down.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ babaoo koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛha niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baakwɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, overly shady, and wet conditions. Keeping your farm well-pruned and clear of weeds lets in sunlight and breeze to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni jwɛi akafee nɔ ko. Ha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear the weeds around the base of my trees instead of letting the grass grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ mitso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni mahã jwɛi akwɛ̃?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop trees for soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water. Clearing a wide ring around each tree ensures the tree gets all the food and removes places where harmful pests hide.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu. Tso fɛɛ tso haa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ, ni ejieɔ hei ni kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Good soil for cocoa is dark, rich in decayed organic leaves, soft enough for roots to grow deep, and retains moisture without staying flooded or muddy after rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha kookoo lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ nii babaoo Eyɛ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ Ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni nu afua loo sũ akafee lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my cocoa pods are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when they mature, turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow. Harvesting them as soon as they change color prevents the beans inside from germinating or spoiling.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ tsake amɛhe lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ loo amɛkafite.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the essential food plants use to stay green and grow strong, so adding organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer like urea can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do weeds lower my harvest even if I put enough fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive and grow faster than crops, so they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying recommended organic or chemical sprays early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni ji organic loo chemical spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: This is often bacterial wilt, a soil disease where microscopic bacteria block the water pathways inside the stem. Infected plants cannot drink water, so removing sick plants and rotating crops helps protect the remaining field.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt kɛbaa Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni bacteria bibii ni anaaa lɛ tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread viral infections. Controlling these small pests early prevents the leaves from curling and stopping plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni ebaatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space helps it grow larger, produce bigger yields, and stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ oha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etsɔ agbo. amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa

english: Yam vines naturally climb to spread their leaves toward sunlight, which powers root growth. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing disease and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. ni tsirɛɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Flowers drop when the cocoa tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests, or when there are not enough tiny midges present to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao cacao tso lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Eshɛɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my groundnut plants bending down and pushing their flowers into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miikoto shi ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ miitsi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally form their pods underground. After flowers are pollinated above ground, the stems bend downward to push the developing seeds safely into the earth where the nuts grow.
ga: Peanuts feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi dumɔwui ni miida lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the earth before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Tubers rot when soil holds too much water for a long time, allowing rot-causing fungi to multiply. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Tubers fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ afa babaoo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if the rain stops unexpectedly right around harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: If rain stops suddenly during harvest, cocoa pods can dry out too quickly or mature unevenly. Keeping an eye on weather patterns helps you time your harvesting properly so you don't lose the quality and weight of your cocoa crop.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya tsɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona kpamɔ be ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, cacao lɛ mlihilɛ kɛ egbɔjɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why do my crops look weak or dull when the sky stays cloudy and dim for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ be mli ni ŋwɛi efee atatu ni edɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their food through photosynthesis. When the sky is dark or overcast for long periods, plants slow down their food production, making them appear dull, but they will recover once normal sunlight returns.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Beni ŋwɛi edɔ loo ewo atatu be kakadaŋŋ. Tsei baaha niyenii ni afeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Ehaa ofeɔ tamɔ mɔ ko ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ Shi ebaahi shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ daa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How does a long dry season affect the way cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During a severe dry season, cocoa trees drop their leaves to save water and may shed small young pods to survive. Providing good shade and mulching the soil helps hold moisture so the trees retain more pods.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie dumɔwui bibii. koni ehi shi Shade kpakpa ni akɛhaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa so I don't spoil the beans?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo? Bɔni afee ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akafite

english: Harvest cocoa when the pods turn fully yellow or orange, depending on the variety. Harvesting too early leads to flat, undeveloped beans, while leaving them too long causes the seeds inside to sprout or rot.
ga: Kpaa kookoo beni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Edamɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmãa. yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi.

english: Why do my harvested cocoa beans spoil so easily if I leave them on the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested cocoa pods left on damp ground absorb excess moisture and attract pests and fungi. Pods should be gathered, cracked, and fermented within a few days of harvesting to prevent rot and preserve bean quality.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni akpa ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ebaagbala kooloi kɛ ŋmeii. Esa akɛ abua ŋmeii lɛ anaa, akumɔ amɛ, ni afee amɛ ŋmeii yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ koni akafite ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do to protect my picked cocoa pods if heavy rain starts suddenly before I can break them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni mihala lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa dani amɛfo mli?

english: Stack picked pods on raised wooden platforms or cover them with tarps or palm fronds off the bare dirt. This keeps rainwater and soil dampness from seeping into the pods and ruining the beans inside.
ga: Okɛ pods ni ahala lɛ ato tso kpoku ko ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tarp loo ŋmei baa aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu akabote ŋmeii lɛ amli ni efite kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: What key things should I check before taking my tools and chemicals to spray my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ dani mikɛ nibii kɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Before spraying, clear thick weeds with a machete so the chemical reaches the target plant, check that your equipment does not leak, ensure you have protective clothes, and confirm that it is not about to rain.
ga: dani okɛ tsofa lɛ ashwie nɔ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ kɛ machete koni tsofa lɛ ashɛ tsei ni ataoɔ lɛ ahe. Kwɛmɔ akɛ otsɔne lɛ miiho nu. Kwɛmɔ ni oná atadei ni buɔ mɔ he. ni ema nɔ mi akɛ nugbɔ enɛŋ

english: Is it okay for me to spray chemicals on my farm on a very dry and hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso ni nu egbi lɛ mli?

english: It is best to avoid spraying in high heat because hot sun causes chemicals to evaporate too fast, reducing their effect and potentially burning the leaves. Spray early in the morning or late afternoon instead.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ hei ni la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ he ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Ha nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ aba shi ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baa lɛ ashã. Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli moŋ.

english: Why should I inspect my farm carefully before buying and using pest control chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani mahe tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Inspecting your farm first helps you identify the specific pest or disease present. This prevents you from wasting money on the wrong chemical and ensures you apply treatment only when necessary.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli. Enɛ baatsi onaa koni okafite oshika yɛ tsofai ni ejaaa ahe. ni eye ebua ni okwɛ akɛ okɛ tsofafeemɔ tsuɔ nii pɛ kɛ ehe miihia.

english: Should I cut down all the tall trees around my cocoa farm with my machete to give my crop full sun?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Okwaa ŋmɔ mli kookoo kɛ machete koni tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa?

english: No, cocoa trees actually benefit from partial shade provided by larger trees. Moderate shade protects cocoa leaves from harsh sun damage, retains soil moisture during dry periods, and keeps the farm cooler.
ga: Dabi, kookoo tsei náa hulutsoo fã ko ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ he sɛɛ. Shade ni mli tse buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli adɔ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose moisture quickly. Shade trees protect young cocoa from extreme heat and keep the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build healthy green leaves and grow tall. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help bring back the dark green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ hewalɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crop harvests keep getting smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Excess rain causes water to sit around the roots in flat ground, suffocating the tubers and causing fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shishifãi ahe yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ anɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut down the extra young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers but only a few of them turn into real cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmɔji diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of nutrients, or pest attacks. Ensuring the tree has enough moisture, shade, and protection from sap-sucking insects helps more flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ hao amɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa, hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe Enɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my tomatoes get soft black spots at the bottom before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ shishigbɛ dani edɔ kwraa?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and flowers when tiny green insects gather under the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho baai kɛ fɔfɔi beni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are aphids that suck the sap and vital nutrients out of the leaves, causing the plant to get weak and shed its leaves and flowers. Spraying the plants with soapy water or appropriate bio-pesticides removes the insects and saves the fruit.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ebaa kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ shwie tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Weeds have stronger, faster-growing roots than crops and will consume the fertilizer first if they are present. Clearing all weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get all the nutrients instead of the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji akɛ eyɛ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi fɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ baaná niyenii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jwɛi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow when there is no shade on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting delicate cocoa leaves from burning while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he beni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, wet conditions. Pruning overcrowded branches lets sunlight and air pass through the farm to dry the pods faster.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni eha pods lɛ agbi oya

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to stay green and grow thick cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to hide inside and eat the leaf whorls of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the center shoot of maize to feed on tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai bibii dani amɛje kpo.

english: Why do I get smaller corn cobs when I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stalks and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very tall, bushy leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or water, it puts all its energy into expanding its top green leaves instead of storing energy in the roots below.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli moŋ fe ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward sunlight so they can make food faster, while keeping them off damp ground where fungal diseases can easily infect them.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ koni amɛhoo oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha ehi he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: How does covering the dirt around my crop stems with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating in the hot sun, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve safely; putting dry fertilizer on bone-dry soil can scorch and burn the plant roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my pepper plant blossoms drop off without producing peppers during dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry conditions stress pepper plants, causing them to shed flowers to conserve water and stay alive until weather improves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa chili tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain floods the land, drowning the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds completely before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young cassava and will steal water, sunlight, and soil food from your crop. Clearing them early gives the cassava cuttings a chance to establish strong roots and grow large tubers without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛma shishifãi ni wa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops on raised soil mounds or on flat ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Mounds are best for heavy or low-lying soils that trap water, because they keep root crops like yam and cassava from rotting in soggy mud. Flat ground is better for light, dry soils to keep moisture from escaping too fast.
ga: Gɔji hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hiɛɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni amɛkafite yɛ muji ni mli efɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔji ni egbi ni nɔ ejɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the harsh midday sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get extremely high or when the soil gets too dry, which causes the plant stress. High heat also prevents proper pollination, so the flower dies and drops off instead of forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ pollination naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves to suck out the sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. This damage stops the leaves from making food, causing the plant to stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii. tsei ni egbɔjɔ

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cool, and overly shady conditions. Rain drops splash the fungal spores from the ground or infected leaves onto healthy pods, causing them to turn black and decay.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get tiny holes in them after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by tiny beetles called weevils that lay microscopic eggs on the seeds. When the eggs hatch into larvae, they eat their way out from inside the bean, leaving holes and ruining the grain.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu lɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii Eyeɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa buji baa ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: During intense sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the dirt. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to shrink its leaf area and save water, and it usually recovers once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛbaa baai lɛ amli ni ekɛbuɔ nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell before the real rainy season starts. If you plant too early, seeds will sprout but then scorch and die in the dry soil when the rain pauses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily burn under direct sun. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra shoot stems growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning them so that only one or two strong suckers remain allows the main plant to put all its energy into producing a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, loo suckers, kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Tso lɛ ni afolɔ koni eshi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni he wa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant build chlorophyll, turning the leaves green and boosting growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ klorofil. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize in the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the topsoil without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops—such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize—helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ekoŋŋ. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies, which can also spread plant viruses. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa tsei amli hu Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on tender leaves inside the maize funnel. Applying safe bio-pesticides or recommended treatments early in the morning into the funnel will kill the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo kooloi lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the damp ground toward sunlight. Exposure to sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which is directed downward to grow bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Hulu la ni baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni atsɔɔ shishi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering and using a balanced compost encourage the flowers to set into healthy tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves yellow and drop, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell that dries out the topsoil, which can scorch newly germinated seeds. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the soil stays consistently moist for your seeds to grow safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they are exposed to full sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ amɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct sun. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees nearby to filter the sunlight and keep the soil moist during their first two to three years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes to support my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni mikɛfi mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight exposure to produce large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch sunlight easily, improve airflow, and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ mlɛo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom leaves upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves stored nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without growing into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛdarako amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture, or a lack of bees and insects for pollination cause stress to the tomato plant. When stressed, the plant sheds its blossoms to conserve energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away most of the small suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɔleɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Extra suckers compete aggressively with the parent plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough strength to grow heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui babaoo baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when there is a heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil fills all air pockets with water, suffocating the tubers and causing rot-causing fungi to thrive underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ amli kɛ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Heavy rainfall washes away surface fertilizer before the roots can absorb it, carrying the nutrients into gutters and rivers, which wastes your money and harms nearby water sources.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii aya nu ŋshɔi kɛ faai amli Enɛ baafite shika ni ebaaye nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ awui.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the crop dies, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi. Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã sũ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight cups and stop growing leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiikpa baai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking sap from the tender leaves while simultaneously transmitting viruses into the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa, ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa tso lɛ mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients faster and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific crop to multiply in huge numbers season after season.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli niyenii komɛi afite oya. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ bei ni hoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Does the nutrient level in my soil affect the protein content and quality of my grain harvest?
ga: Ani niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa protein ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ bɔ ni miŋmaa kpamɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, crops need adequate soil nutrients like nitrogen during their growth stage to build proteins. Providing proper soil nutrition helps crops achieve high nutrient levels and produces healthier, more valuable grains.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen he miihia tsei yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ koni amɛfee protein. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii babaoo ni haa amɛnáa ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni jara wa waa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. When the crop cannot get enough nitrogen from the ground, it cannot feed its leaves, causing them to lose color and slow down growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enaaa nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ baai anɔ aha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛhe su sɛɛ foɔ, ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do people say planting leguminous crops like soybeans or cowpeas helps my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ soybeans loo cowpeas ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops have special root systems that pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This naturally enriches your farm's soil nutrition for the next crop cycle without extra chemical cost.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe nyɔmɔwoo fataaa he.

english: Why do my crops stop growing taller once they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Crops switch their energy focus as they mature. Once flowering begins, the plant stops using energy to grow taller and directs all its food and moisture into developing seeds, fruits, or pods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ he ni amɛhewalɛ lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Be ni esa akɛ aje fɔfɔi afeemɔ shishi Tsei kpaɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛdara ni amɛkudɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ koni amɛná dumɔwui, aduawai, loo ŋmeii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops dry out and turn brown right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: As crops reach full maturity, they naturally stop feeding their leaves and redirect all remaining nutrients and water straight into ripening the seed or grain yield.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛkpaa foliar niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛtsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa dumɔwui ni shwereɔ loo dumɔwui afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick leaves but producing very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the crop spends all its energy developing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited soil nutrients, sunlight, and groundwater, which causes them to grow thin, weak, and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds slow down the growth and yield of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo aba shi?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young crop shoots wither quickly when there is a short dry spell right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni be kukuoo ko yɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts have shallow roots that cannot reach deep groundwater yet. Without steady topsoil moisture during early growth stages, the shoots dry out and wilt quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ mra be mli ni edara lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to target the soft, young leaves of my crops first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Young leaves are tender and packed with fresh moisture and concentrated plant nutrients, making them the easiest and most nutritious meal for sucking insects.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee kɛ tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ kɛha kooloi ni nuɔ nu.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally prefer gentle shade; direct heat from full sunlight stresses the tree, causing flowers to drop off and reducing the overall pod yield.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo be ni mli jɔ. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa pod lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity that allows Black Pod disease to spread quickly; clearing weeds and pruning cocoa branches lets air flow through to dry the pods.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no haa blackpod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kookoo tsei lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of food from the earth, but leguminous crops like groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil, restoring fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look small during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during dry spells is often caused by tiny insects like cassava green mites that suck sap from the leaves when moisture levels are low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ cassava green mite lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers under the ground, while keeping leaves off wet soil prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs wuji ni baa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsi baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.
