english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during storms; removing extra side-suckers and supporting the stem with wooden props keeps them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔnei krokomɛi ni akɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ, ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ haa amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant cannot take up calcium from the soil, which usually occurs when watering is irregular or the ground dries out too much.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by intense heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer on my crop bed right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo midumɔ shii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the crop's root zone down the slopes or deep underground, which wastes your money and leaves the plants without food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli kɛyaa gɔji lɛ anɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baafite shika ni ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. This can happen if the soil is poor, or if heavy rains have washed the nutrients away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii. Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains away the specific nutrients maize needs, making the soil weak. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What advantage does covering the ground around my vegetables with dry grass give my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ hay mulch ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ kɛhaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under hot sunshine and traps water so you do not need to water as often.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, which is often caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf decay and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When the bunch grows heavy, strong winds can easily pull the roots out unless you prop the tree up with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji tso lɛ da lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya. Ja okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa miifi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if it is safe to plant my seeds after the first rainfall of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the very first rain is risky because the soil might still be hot and dry underneath. It is best to wait until there are two or three steady rains so the ground has deep moisture to keep seeds alive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi yɛ shishi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because roots need air to breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if my crops still have space to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi? Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko lolo ni amɛbaada?

english: Even if there is space, weed roots spread fast beneath the ground and secretly steal water and fertilizer away from your crops, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching your plants.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ he ko yɛ moŋ, shi jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ teemɔŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much direct sunshine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ?

english: Cocoa leaves burn easily under full sun, turning brown at the edges or fading to yellow. Young cocoa trees need shade trees or plantains nearby to filter the hot afternoon sunlight.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Baai lɛ ahe baatsɔ asarasu loo ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ koni amɛjie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛjɛ shwane mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the key food plants need to stay green and build strong stems, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps restore healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, leaving free nutrients that help your next crop of maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa o-maise ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and covered in a white powdery substance?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda yɛŋ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with white residue are typically caused by sap-sucking insects like cassava mealybugs or whiteflies. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or a neem-based organic pesticide helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ cassava mealy aphid loo whitefly lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ neem fee lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent and adding well-rotted manure or poultry litter helps plants absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot withstand direct sunlight, which burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving some taller trees or interplanting with plantains provides necessary shade and retains soil moisture while the cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baa shã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Plantains ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ baaha aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clean my field with weedicide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ etsumɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weedicides kill growing weeds, but millions of dormant weed seeds remain alive in the soil waiting for sunlight and rain. Covering the soil with a layer of dry leaves or straw—known as mulching—blocks sunlight and prevents weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni miida lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni miida. Shi jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ Dumɔwui akpekpei abɔ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiimɛ hulu kɛ nugbɔ. Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it better to raise pepper and tomato seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them directly in my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper kɛ tomato dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi fe ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Vegetable seeds are tiny and easily destroyed by heavy rain, strong heat, or insects in the open field. A nursery allows you to shade, water, and protect young seedlings until they develop strong stems and roots before transplanting.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui bibii ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. He ni akwɛɔ tsei yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ hulutsoo, nu, ni obuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani okɛwoɔ he kroko.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing my seeds after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui dumɔ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil is soaked deep enough—about the length of your hand—after two or three good rains. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a week-long dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa—aaafee onine lɛ kɛlɛ—yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ otsi kome.

english: Flowering plants drop blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or excess nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the roots moist with regular watering during hot spells helps flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ ahã shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my harvested yams rotting so fast when I store them inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during digging, stored in hot rooms without airflow, or placed directly on damp ground. Storing undamaged yams on raised wooden racks in a shaded, well-ventilated barn keeps them cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Aloo okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ atomɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ ato tso adekai ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa edɔ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to raise my seeds in a separate nursery bed instead of planting them directly next to mature crops in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ ngɛ tsehi nɛ a wa a he ngɛ ngmɔ ngua ɔ mi.

english: Young seedlings are delicate and need specialized attention just like human babies. Planting them near mature plants causes them to get shaded out and infected by pests or diseases already living on the older crops. A nursery provides a safe, controlled environment for young roots to become strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛbiɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ, tamɔ abifabii pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni hiɔ tsei ni edara lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. He ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni akudɔɔ koni shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava stems fail to sprout well when I plant them underneath big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big, established trees have massive root systems and dense leaf canopies that steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Young crops need their own dedicated space with direct access to sun and soil moisture to start growing successfully.
ga: Tsei wuji ni etsɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ ni juɔ nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Hulu La Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛje amɛdalɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I put too many maize seeds into one small planting hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo wo ŋmãa bu bibioo kome mli?

english: When too many seeds grow in the exact same spot, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Because of this competition, all the plants grow weak, tall, and thin, leading to tiny cobs or no harvest at all.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛhe waaa, amɛkwɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. aloo eshwɛ fioo ni kpamɔ ko kwraa bɛ

english: How do I know the correct space to leave between my pepper plants during planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni ka pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing depends on how wide the mature plant grows. Leaving enough space between plants allows air to flow freely, prevents diseases from spreading easily, and ensures every branch gets enough sunlight to bear fruit.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ damɔ bɔ ni tso ni eda lɛ baanyɛ adara babaoo eha lɛ nɔ. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Tsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ naa ni oye obua tso nine fɛɛ nine ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in direct, open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that dry out quickly under strong sun before their roots are mature enough to pull up enough water. Providing shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from burning until it grows older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings collapse and die right after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain drops can violently crush tender young stems and compact the soil around them, suffocating their roots. Protecting young seedlings with a grass mulch or temporary shelter helps break the force of the rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ tsei bibii lɛ waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo he ko ni akɛhiɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ abu tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni nugbɔshiimɔ hewalɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow and leaning toward one side of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiikwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Crops naturally bend toward sunlight to create their own energy. If trees or tall structures block light from one direction, plants will lean toward the sun, and lower leaves shaded from light will turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni amɛkɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsũi ni kwɔlɔ tsi la ni jɛɔ gbɛ kome nɔ lɛ naa Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger than the main crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to compete aggressively for water, light, and nutrients in local soil. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing essential food away from your growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings look weak and wilted right after I move them from the nursery to the big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi trukaa beni mishi he ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ agbo ko mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants disturbs their delicate feeder roots, causing temporary 'transplant shock' where they cannot absorb water efficiently. Transplanting in the cool late afternoon or on cloudy days helps them recover without losing too much moisture.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ gbalaa niyenii shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ ‘transplant shock’ baa be kukuoo mli yɛ he ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso loo gbi ni atatu ewo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ tsɔ.

english: How can I tell that my tomato seedlings are strong enough to be moved out of the nursery into the open field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready for transplanting when they have developed 4 to 6 true leaves and a thick, sturdy stem, usually around 3 to 4 weeks after germinating. At this stage, their root systems are strong enough to anchor in field soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛheɔ aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if capsid bugs are attacking my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ capsid kooloi miitutua mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Capsids feed on tender shoots and young cocoa pods, leaving dark, sunken spots and causing leaves to dry up and fall off, which makes the tree canopy look burned.
ga: Capsids yeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii. Eshiɔ okadi ni tsuɔ waa ni shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ ha tso lɛ yitso lɛ shã.

english: How often should I walk through my cocoa farm to check for insects on my trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni makwɛ kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: You should inspect your cocoa farm at least once every week or two so that you can spot pest infestations early before they spread to the rest of your trees.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. dani egbɛ eshwa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What time of day is best for me to search for pests on my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ matao ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Searching early in the morning or late in the afternoon is best because insects are active then, whereas during the hot midday sun they hide deep inside bark cracks or dense leaves.
ga: Nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kooloi bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii waa. Be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii loo tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I notice more pests on cocoa trees growing close to streams or damp areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ faai ahe loo hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Humid and moist environments near water sources create ideal breeding conditions for insects like capsids, while also keeping the cocoa shoots softer and more attractive for pests to feed on.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ fɔɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo akɛ niyenii kɛha kooloi bibii.

english: Which specific parts of the cocoa tree do harmful insects like to target the most?
ga: Mɛɛ kookoo tso lɛ fãi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua amɛ waa?

english: Pests prefer soft, growing parts of the tree—such as young green pods, soft leaves, and new stems—because they are easy to pierce and rich in sap.
ga: Gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛyaa tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni miida, tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli, baai bibii, kɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ, ejaakɛ amɛboteɔ mli oya ni amɛmli nu babaoo.

english: If I notice insects on only one cocoa tree, will they spread to neighboring trees?
ga: Kɛji mina tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ kookoo tso kome pɛ nɔ lɛ, Ani amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, insects can crawl or fly to neighboring trees, especially if the branches touch each other or if the insect population grows too large for one tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii baanyɛ akɔlɔ loo amɛfo kɛya tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ niji lɛ ta amɛhe. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii lɛ ayibɔ fa tsɔ kɛha tso kome.

english: Can I remove insects from my cocoa trees by hand, or must I always use spray treatments?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ minine ajie kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be?

english: Removing bugs by hand works well if you catch a few insects on just one or two trees, but widespread pests across many trees require proper chemical treatments to control fully.
ga: Nine ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ omɔ kooloi fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ tso kome loo enyɔ nɔ. Shi tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ biɔ tsofai ni sa koni anyɛ akudɔ amɛ kwraa.

english: Does pruning overlapping branches help stop pests from moving around my farm?
ga: Niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya he fɛɛ he. Miŋmɔ loo daabi?

english: Yes, trimming branches creates space between trees so crawling bugs cannot easily cross over, and it improves sunlight and airflow, which discourages many pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa gbɛ baa tsei lɛ ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afo mli mlɛo. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo nyɛɛɛ ahi jɛmɛ.

english: Why are the tips of my young cocoa shoots turning brown and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Shot tips turn brown when insects suck out the plant sap, cutting off water and food supply to the growing tips and causing them to die back.
ga: Tso lɛ yitsei lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ blɔfo be mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛya ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. ni oha amɛgboi

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is recovering after I clear off the pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miihe ajɔ amɛ beni mitsa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A recovering cocoa tree will begin sprouting fresh, healthy green leaves and shoots without any new dark scars or wilting within a few weeks.
ga: Kakao tso ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baabɔi baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni egboɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli bɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food, or that the ground has too much water drowning the roots. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ he miihia oŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long or when underground pests create wounds where fungus can enter. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and keeps the roots dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fee pilamɔi ni ŋmeii baanyɛ abote mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the hot sun. It stops water from evaporating quickly and prevents unwanted weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: What is eating small holes inside the leaves at the top of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the funnel of the plant. Spraying neem leaf water or recommended pesticides early in the morning when the insects are active will protect your corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmei lɛ he.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and drying up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches and clearing weeds around the farm lets sunlight and air in to keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the days are too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or if you use too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant produce leaves instead of fruits. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo tsu nii ni haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi.

english: Can I plant beans and maize together in the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good because beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This natural food helps the maize grow stronger while giving you two different crops from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli baa lɛ baa.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves in the sun to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to maximum sunlight and reducing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai lɛ eshwã hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Na hulu la babaoo ni oha baa helai aba shi

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and heavy trunks that can easily snap or pull out of the ground under the weight of heavy fruit or strong winds. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy wooden Y-stick supports the weight until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii ni baanyɛ akumɔ loo ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ yibii ni tsii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tsii lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ Y-shape ni wa to tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua shwiili lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do seeds saved from store-bought hybrid vegetables produce weaker crops than the parent plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni akɛfee tsofai ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe fɔlɔ tso lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different parent plants to produce a high yield only for one generation. Seeds saved from those harvested fruits lose those strong qualities, resulting in smaller or mixed crop yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai aduawai ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ baafite nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa loo efutuɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching brown and dropping off during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees to shelter them, the hot sun burns their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa amɛbaai lɛ ni egbiɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually show that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Feeding the soil with nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure restores the healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce only small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo pɛ lɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing upper stems and leaves instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight, which allows the plant to manufacture food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp soil, reducing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni hulu la aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa helai baa shi

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Severe stress prevents the flower from forming tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Haomɔ ni naa wa tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo tomato.

english: Multiple shoots coming from the same base compete with each other for water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong shoots allows the main stem to grow big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsobii babaoo ni jɛɔ shishitoo kome mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on leaf sap underneath. Controlling these pests helps new leaves grow smooth and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa baa heei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots containing natural bacteria that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, enriching it naturally for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli sɛɛnamɔ afata he kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water around the crop while it grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle ehe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Standing water controls weed growth naturally and maintains a steady root temperature, allowing lowland rice varieties to continuously draw the heavy moisture they need.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ kudɔɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli dɔlɛ yaa nɔ daa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gbalaa nu babaoo ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do the leaves on some of my cassava plants get green-and-yellow twisted patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf distortion is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava planting sticks prevents this sickness from taking over your field.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli tsakemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea gives the plant the energy it needs to stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops when I plant maize on the exact same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the ground every season. Planting it repeatedly exhausts the soil, whereas alternating your maize with beans or groundnuts returns natural nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu shii abɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa sũ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the tender cocoa from excessive heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebuɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: When crops are planted too tightly, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block light from one another. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow full and bear larger yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni baai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot beneath the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rainfall leaves standing water, the roots suffocate and rot, which is why forming raised mounds or ridges of soil helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ kwɔɔ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers but dropping them before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi no sɛɛ lɛ egbeeɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the soil is too dry, or if there are no insects around to carry pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ lɛ bɛ?

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during the middle of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in high heat to protect themselves from losing water too quickly to the air. If the leaves recover by evening, the plant is managing heat, but if they stay limp, the roots need water.
ga: Ha ni curl lɛ mli adɔ yɛ la ni mli wa nɔ koni nu lɛ akaje kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ he wa yɛ gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ miikpe. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ nyiɛ lolo lɛ, Roots hu he miihia nu.

english: Why do weeds cause my vegetable crops to stay small even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that drink up water and steal fertilizer before your main crops can reach it. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly start eating the centers of my young maize plants after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ trukaa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on fresh green growth right after early rains start. When caterpillars hatch, they head straight for the soft center leaves of the maize to feed, so checking leaves early helps catch them before major damage occurs.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ amɛwui. Beni ŋmei lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyaa baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ amɛ dani nɔ ko wulu abafite.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder after staying in the storehouse for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called weevils bore inside stored grain if it isn't completely dried before storage. Thoroughly sun-drying your corn until the kernels are hard stops these pests from multiplying in your stored yield.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ baabote ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa koni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akafee ŋmãa ni ato lɛ babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping them cool and moist until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛná nu kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to stay green and build strong stalks. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging them all up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers expand below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants have big holes eaten into the leaves near the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ bu agboi ni ayeɔ yɛ baai ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in the center leaves are a common sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender inner leaves. Catching them early and applying organic neem spray or recommended control treatments prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Buu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ he. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem spray loo nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller when I leave weeds growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow strong. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment available in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I cut off extra small branches from my adult cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? kɛfata kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: Pruning removes crowded branches so air and sunlight can circulate through the tree canopy. This keeps the tree dry, reduces fungal diseases like black pod, and directs energy into producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ejieɔ tsei niji ni mli ewo wu lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa tsei lɛ mli egbiɔ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa shi, ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I spread dry plant leaves on the soil around my crops during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and breaks down over time to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my tomato crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants can drink before the hot afternoon sun arrives, and wet leaves dry quickly during the day, which stops leaf fungal diseases from taking hold.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ anu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aba. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer when the soil is completely dry and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb them safely. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can scorch the crop's roots and waste the fertilizer until rain finally arrives.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha tsofa lɛ afite, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, nugbɔ anɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I mix different varieties of rice seeds together when planting in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi futuɔ he kɛji midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different rice varieties grow at different speeds and ripen at different times. Planting mixed seeds means some grains will be ripe while others are still green, leading to uneven harvests and lower prices from buyers.
ga: Omɔ henɔi srɔtoi daa oya oya, ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Dumɔwui ni efutu ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui komɛi baakwɛ̃ be mli ni ekrokomɛi baakwɛ̃. still green Enɛ haa nibii ni afee lɛ ejaaa kɛ jara ni baa shi kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ adɛŋ.

english: How does buying certified seeds from dealers help my crop grow better than using saved seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ dɛŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully selected and treated to grow uniformly, resist diseases, and give higher yields. Saved seeds often carry hidden diseases and produce weaker plants with unpredictable grain sizes.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara daa. Enyɛɔ helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo Bei pii lɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my rice plants produce flowers earlier than others in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ mra fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Uneven flowering usually happens when seeds of different varieties get mixed together or are planted at uneven depths. Using one pure variety of seed ensures all your plants mature together at the same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi futu mli loo adu yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Dumɔwu krɔŋŋ kome pɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha otsei lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my rice crops turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating from stagnant, trapped water. Applying the right fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu efo shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni ekã shi ni ekã shi lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes my crops fall over easily during heavy rains right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani kpamɔ baa lɛ mli?

english: Crops fall over when stems are weak, which can happen if plants are crowded too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer. Weak roots and heavy rain combine to knock top-heavy plants down.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he babaoo tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are weeds growing much faster and taller than my young rice seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya ni amɛmiikwɔ fe mi tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally aggressive and suck up water, light, and fertilizer faster than young crops. Clearing weeds early gives your rice plants enough space and food to grow strong and shade out new weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná he ko ni fa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa ni amɛha jwɛi heei lɛ aná hulutsoo.

english: How does flood water affect the way my rice crop develops?
ga: Te nu afua lɛ saa ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli shweremɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While rice needs moisture, being fully under water for too many days starves the plant of air, turning leaves brown and slowing growth. Controlled water levels help roots grow deep and produce heavy grains.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmãa moŋ Shi kɛ́ ehi nu shishi gbii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ asasu ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi. Nu ni akudɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa ni mli kwɔ ni dumɔwui ni tsii hu baa.

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when they are milled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Be ni afee kɔla?

english: Grains break easily if they are left in the field too long to over-dry in the hot sun or dried too fast after harvest. Harvesting at the right moisture level keeps the grains strong during milling.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. loo egbiɔ oya tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ Kpãmɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akpãa nii lɛ.

english: Why do millers pay less money when my harvested grain has different grain sizes mixed together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo be mli ni mikpamɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni dalɛi srɔtoi efutu mli lɛ?

english: Milling machines are set for specific grain sizes; mixed grains get crushed or left unhusked during processing. Buyers pay more for uniform grains because they mill cleanly and cook evenly.
ga: Ato tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko. Akɛ ŋmaa ni efutu lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ashiɔ lɛ ni atsuuu he nii yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha unifɔm ŋmaa. Ejaakɛ amɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhoɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What causes empty or light grain husks on my rice plants at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe su tsakeɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Empty husks happen when extreme heat, drought, or insect attacks strike the plant right while it is flowering, preventing the grain inside from filling up with starch.
ga: Bark ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo kooloi tutuamɔ ba tso lɛ nɔ beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii eyi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rainfall keeps changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ tsakeɔ daa afi hewɔ lɛ

english: Wait until the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains that soak into the ground before planting, rather than sowing immediately after the very first light rain, so your seeds have enough moisture to germinate and establish strong roots.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa dani okɛdu. Mohu ɔ, mo du ngɛ kekleekle hiɔmi nɛ ɔ nɛ ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu konɛ o wu ɔmɛ nɛ a ná nu nɛ sa konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a pee sisi nɛ mi wa.

english: What can I do to protect my crops if the rain stops for a long time right after I plant?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your young crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves (mulching). This acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and prevents the sun from drying out the soil roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Are there crop varieties I can plant that will give a good yield even if the rains are small this year?
ga: Ani tsei komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ makwɛ ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba yɛ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ afi nɛɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can ask for early-maturing or drought-tolerant seed varieties. These crops grow faster and complete their life cycle quickly using less water, helping you harvest successfully even in short rainy seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ obi dumɔwui srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛgbeɔ amɛshihilɛ naa oya kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli po.

english: Why do my seeds fail to come up after putting them inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are planted too deep for the shoot to reach the surface, if the ground is too hard and dry, or if insects and heavy rains wash them away before they can take root.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni egbi Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: Is it better to put many seeds in one hole or space them out across my farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui babaoo? Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo bu kome mli loo oja amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Spacing crops out gives every single plant its own space to draw food, water, and sunlight without fighting its neighbors, resulting in stronger stems and larger crop yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la baa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops start turning yellow during the middle of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that your crops are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil has become too dry for the roots to drink up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: What steps can I take to make sure my land produces more bags of crop this season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: You can increase your bags of harvest by preparing the land early, using quality certified seeds, applying the right fertilizer at the correct growth stages, and clearing weeds early so they do not steal plant food.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha okpamɔ kotoku lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosaa mra lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ amli. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni akaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli

english: How does adding fertilizer into the ground help my crops grow bigger and produce more?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer works like nutritious food for the soil. It supplies vital elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that make crops grow tall, stay healthy, and form bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ Hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni owo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji

english: How can I protect my harvested crops so they don't lose weight or spoil before weighing day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mikpamɔ lɛ he? Koni akafee shwiili loo efite dani asusu shwiili lɛ he

english: Thoroughly dry your harvested crops on clean tarpaulins until they are crisp before bagging them, and store the bags off the ground on wooden pallets in a dry, ventilated shed to prevent moisture build-up and mold.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmaa lɛ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛwo kotoku mli. Ni okɛ kotokui lɛ ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ tsũ ko ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my stored bags of grain weigh less after keeping them in the room for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains lose weight in storage because remaining moisture naturally evaporates over time, or because hidden pests like weevils are inside the bags eating away the inner parts of the grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Aloo ejaakɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ kotokui ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Why should I leave some big trees standing on my farm instead of cutting all of them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Keeping select trees on your farm acts like a protective parent for your crops. They break strong winds, protect young crops from scorching sun, and drop leaves that turn into natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Tsei ni ahala yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baatsu nii akɛ bulɔi ni buɔ onibii ahe. Amɛfiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni okɛ baai ni bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aba shi.

english: How do shade trees help my young crops survive the hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees act like big umbrellas over your farm. They reduce direct sunlight and extreme heat, keeping the air cooler underneath so young plants do not burn or lose too much water.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã loo amɛkaná nu babaoo.

english: Can planting trees around my farm protect my plantains from falling during storms?
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ ahum be mli?

english: Yes, planting strong trees along your farm boundary creates a windbreak. These trees slow down powerful storm winds before they can snap or uproot delicate crops like plantains and maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni wa ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ haa ahum ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani amɛfoɔ loo amɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ plantains kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some of my crops grow better when they are planted near certain native trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei komɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Certain trees help create a friendly environment underground and above. Their leaves add nutrients to the dirt, and their canopy creates gentle shade that keeps surrounding crops relaxed and moist.
ga: Tsei komɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli baa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ ŋwɛi fɛɛ. Amɛ baai lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni eshishifã lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni ehaa mɔ he jɔɔ

english: How do tree roots help protect my farm soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi buɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tree roots act like strong ropes underground that hold the soil tightly together. When heavy rain hits, the roots stop the rich topsoil from washing away into nearby rivers.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ kpãi ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni fiɔ sũ lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ koni ekaho kɛya faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out quickly after heavy rain while my neighbor's farm stays wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Soil that has shade from trees and a layer of organic material acts like a sponge. It absorbs heavy rainfall and holds onto the moisture for weeks, whereas bare soil dries out fast under direct sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsei yɔɔ nɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli otsii babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I store water in my farm soil so my crops do not suffer during dry weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã nu ahi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: You can trap rainwater in the ground by keeping trees on the farm and covering the soil with dry leaves or straw. This stops the sun from evaporating the water that soaked into the ground during heavy rains.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nugbɔ nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa hulu la lɛ akafee nu ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Does leaving dead leaves on my farm floor help hold rainwater in the ground?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, dry leaves form a protective blanket over the dirt. When a heavy rain falls, this blanket slows down the water, letting it soak deep into the soil and keeping it moist for up to a month.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, baai ni egbi lɛ feɔ muji ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa Nɛkɛ blanket nɛɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Ha ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni oha ehi shi kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome.

english: How do deep tree roots help keep moisture in the ground for other plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ashishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi?

english: Deep tree roots create channels underground that allow heavy rainwater to sink deep into the earth instead of running off. This deep water stays stored safely underground where crop roots can reach it.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi gbɛi ni haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeejo foi. Akɛ nu ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: How can a single heavy rain keep my crops watered for a long time without extra watering?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nugbɔ kome ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu be kakadaŋŋ ni nu kroko fataaa he?

english: If your farm soil is healthy and protected by tree shade, heavy rain soaks deep into the ground like an underground tank. The soil holds this water and slowly feeds your crops for up to a month.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo buɔ he lɛ, Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tanki. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii fiofio. kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many of their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers when they experience stress from sudden dry spells, insect pests, or fungal diseases. Keeping the soil moist during dry periods and managing pests early helps the flowers stay on the branch and develop into healthy fruit.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa kɛ mra be mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do grafted mango trees produce fruit so much faster than trees grown straight from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei ni akɛwo amɛhe lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A seed produces a young tree that must spend five to seven years growing before it reaches adulthood and flowers. Grafting attaches a branch from an already mature, fruit-bearing tree onto young roots, so the plant grows as an adult and bears fruit in just two to three years.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ tsei bibii ni heɔ afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Grafting kɛ tsei niji ni jɛ tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ fĩɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ daa ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which maize needs to build strong green leaves. Applying organic manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the maize is knee-high helps turn the leaves green and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ organic loo nitrogen fertilizer, tamɔ urea wo ŋmãa lɛ mli beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific nutrients in the dirt, so planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil and lets maize pests build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mikɛ ŋmei nine lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to turn its shoots around, resulting in weak plants and smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tsei ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsake ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and turn it into energy, which feeds the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛhe hulu la ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni awó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aba mli babaoo. ni amɛkwɛ hetsemɔ nɔ kɛjɛ baa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantains planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu kookoo tsei bibii ni dumɔwui awo amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with big leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist air they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by stress from extreme heat and dry soil. Shielding plants, keeping soil moist with dry grass mulch, and controlling whiteflies keeps leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ mli. tsei ahebuu Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi Kɛ whitefly nɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crop field so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni mikafite nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist right after a mild rain, but not during heavy downpours. Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away before roots can drink it, while dry soil can burn plant roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so quickly even when there is plenty of rain for all plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa nugbɔ kpakpa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, root space, and fertilizer nutrients directly from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main element plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding fertilizers like NPK or well-rotted poultry manure gives the soil the nutrients needed to make the crop green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which means they have tiny roots that pull natural fertilizer out of the air and put it back into the soil. This feeds the soil naturally and helps neighboring crops grow stronger without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi bibii. No gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by too much heat, lack of water, or attacks from sucking insects like capsids. Providing shade trees to lower temperatures and spraying safe pest treatments helps flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi, ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can easily rot or get eaten by tiny soil worms called nematodes. Supporting the main stems with wooden prop poles and planting clean, healthy suckers stops the roots from snapping and keeps the tree standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ afite loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ abote mli. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes, ni ayeɔ amɛ oya. Akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ sɛɛ Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ ni eha tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: What is eating holes in my maize leaves and leaving tiny black dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji diji bibii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which loves to hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended pesticides or organic neem leaf powder into the leaf center will kill the worms before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo organic neem baa powder ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wither and die within a few days even when there is water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: This rapid dying is caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living inside the soil that blocks water from moving up the plant's stem. Once a field has it, you should avoid planting tomatoes, peppers, or garden eggs in that same spot for a few seasons to starve the bacteria.
ga: Gbele ni baa oya nɛɛ jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji he lɛ yɛ Esa akɛ okpa tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ooodu yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ he kome lɛ bei fioo komɛi koni hɔmɔ aye helatsɛmɛi lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long or when rot fungi attack the root in waterlogged ground. Raising the soil into mounds or ridges lets extra rain drain away so roots stay dry and healthy until harvest time.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo koni shishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛhe awa kɛyashi kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can catch full sunlight, which creates the energy needed to grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread and boosts the final size of your yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbaji lɛ aje kpo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ, ni ebaaha o-sweet potato lɛ naagbee dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield only in their first planting. If you save and replant those harvested seeds, the second generation crop will grow unevenly and produce very small yields, so buying fresh certified seed each season yields much higher profit.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ekome ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo baaba.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop dark rotten spots on the bottom ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Dark spots on the bottom of peppers are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium because soil moisture fluctuates too much. Watering your vegetable field at regular intervals prevents the roots from drying out and stops the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ashishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni egbo lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsakeɔ fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akagbi, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ ashishi hu akafite.

english: How can I tell if the rice seeds produced here in Ghana will actually give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni ajieɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ?
