english: Locally produced Ghanaian rice seeds are specially bred and tested by agricultural researchers to thrive in our specific soil and weather conditions. They often give strong yields because they are naturally adapted to local heat and common regional pests.
ga: Ghana ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi etsɔ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ ni amɛka amɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ wɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ nɔ. Amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo ejaakɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy government-certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je nyagbe kpami be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to konɛ o du.

english: Certified seeds undergo strict quality checks to guarantee high germination rates and strong growth. Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to weaker plants, uneven field growth, and lower total yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa waa. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ. He ni jɛmɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ yeee egbɔ. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi

english: Are imported crop seeds always better for planting than seeds developed here in Ghana?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shweremɔ be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni afee yɛ Ghana biɛ lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Foreign seed varieties are often developed for cooler climates or different soils, whereas local Ghanaian seeds are tailored for our tropical rainfall and sunlight, making them more reliable without needing costly imported inputs.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui kɛhaa hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli ejɔ loo yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, Ghana dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔ tropical nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nibii ni jara wa aba maŋsɛɛ.

english: How do I confirm that a crop seed bag is genuine local certified seed and not a fake market re-package?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mama nɔ mi akɛ dumɔwui kotoku ko ji maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni awo he odase? Ni jeee amale nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Certified local seeds come in official sealed bags featuring certification tags from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) or seed regulatory bodies, showing lot numbers and germination test dates.
ga: Akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ kotokui ni amralo lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ amli. Eyɛ odaseyeli wolo ni jɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) loo dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ dɛŋ. Etsɔɔ lot yibɔ kɛ shweremɔ kaa gbi.

english: Why do local Ghanaian rice varieties handle short dry spells better than some foreign seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Ghana ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmãa he nii jogbaŋŋ fe maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui komɛi lɛ?

english: Local crop varieties have built-in genetic traits and root systems developed over time to endure hot African sun and unpredictable rains, allowing them to seek deep soil moisture when surface water dries up.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mli ni etee hiɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ edamɔ Afrika hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ naa. Enɛ haa amɛtaoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow a few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage around the roots. Adding appropriate fertilizer at the early vegetative stage and draining excess standing water helps the plants turn deep green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ehiii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ, ni ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do two different varieties of rice take different numbers of months to mature on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi enyɔ heɔ nyɔji srɔtoi dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for different growth cycles; short-duration varieties mature quickly in around 90 days for dry areas, while long-duration varieties take up to 150 days to maximize grain size in flooded fields.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha amɛdalɛ bei srɔtoi. Be kukuoo mli henɔi lɛ daa oya yɛ aaafee gbii 90 mli kɛha hei ni nu bɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 150 dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe fɛɛ he yɛ hei ni nu afua lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why does rice bought from the local market fail to sprout evenly when I sow it in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Grain sold in food markets is meant for eating, not planting. It is often old, improperly dried, or damaged by pests, whereas certified planting seed is harvested and treated specifically to preserve embryo viability.
ga: Akɛ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihei lɛ tsuɔ nii koni aye, shi jeee ni adu. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ. egbi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite yɛ be mli ni akpaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ akahi shi.

english: What causes my rice stalks to fall over easily right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani akpaa?

english: Stalks fall over (known as lodging) when plants are overcrowded, over-fertilized with nitrogen, or lack potassium. Correct plant spacing and balanced fertilizer strengthen the stem so it can support heavy grain heads.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi (ni atsɛɔ lɛ lodging) kɛ́ tso lɛ mli ewo wu tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo potassium ni faaa Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ.

english: Will planting locally certified rice seeds affect the milling quality and price of my grain?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaná mi ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ kɛ ejara nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, certified local seed varieties produce uniform grain sizes that break less during milling, resulting in higher-quality whole grains that fetch a better price in local consumer markets.
ga: Hɛɛ, akutsoŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ omɔ wui ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe ni fiteɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops take around six months to mature while others take a shorter time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Different crops have distinct growth cycles based on their genetics; six-month crops use that time to develop deep roots and store enough energy to produce larger tubers or bigger harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Nyɔji enumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nakai be lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa toɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji loo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce new shoots from the soil every few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa nyɔji fioo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants naturally reproduce by sending up side shoots called suckers every few months, ensuring the plant continues producing fruit stems even after the main stem is cut.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ daa nyɔji fioo lɛ nɔ, ni enɛ haa tso lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni afo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ po sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature, such as leaves turning yellow, stalks drying up, or fruit reaching a stable color and size, indicating they have stopped growing.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni baagbi, loo aduawai ni eshwɛɔ ni amɛhiɛ su kɛ amɛdalɛ daa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa shweremɔ.

english: Is it better to plant large seed yams or small seed yams on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii ni dumɔwui wuji yɔɔ mli loo ŋmeii ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Large seed yams sprout faster and give strong early growth, but small seed yams are cheaper, easier to find, and will still produce full-sized yams if given good soil and proper nutrients.
ga: Atomɔ dumɔwui wuji kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhaa dalɛ oya. Shi yam dumɔwui bibii lɛ jara waaa. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaana Amɛbaawo ŋmeii ni fa babaoo lolo kɛji akɛ aha amɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni sa.

english: Should I choose big plantain suckers or small ones when establishing a new field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahala plantain tsei wuji loo bibii kɛ́ mifee shikpɔŋ hee?

english: Big plantain suckers establish faster and produce fruit sooner, while smaller suckers are easier to transport and find, and will still grow into healthy producing trees with proper care.
ga: Plantains wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe nitsumɔ kɛ enamɔ waaa. Ni ebaaya nɔ eda ni etsɔ tso ni woɔ yibii kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cassava cuttings grow into thick, healthy stems while others stay thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Stem thickness depends on the quality of the cutting used; cuttings taken from the mature middle section of a healthy stem carry more stored energy to grow thick stems and large tubers.
ga: Bɔ ni tso lɛ tso lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ damɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ ŋmɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Niji ni afo kɛjɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ teŋgbɛ ni eda lɛ toɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛwo tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Where can I get reliable seeds and planting materials when I want to expand my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui kɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ? Be ni miisumɔ ni magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: You can get quality, disease-free planting materials through local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) offices, government seed stations, and registered agricultural nurseries.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui ahe nibii ni hi, ni hela bɛ mli kɛjɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) nɔyeli dumɔwui atoohe lɛ. kɛ okwaayeli he ŋmɔji ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from agricultural officers instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛtsu nii lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Certified seeds from agricultural institutions are specially bred and treated to resist common pests and diseases, giving uniform field growth and higher yields than old saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni Agricultural Institute lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui momo ni ato lɛ.

english: Is it difficult to find small planting suckers or seedlings during the main planting season?
ga: Ani ewa akɛ aaana tsei bibii loo dumɔwui yɛ be titri ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli?

english: Small planting materials like seedlings and suckers are widely available and easy to get because government centers and specialized nurseries continuously propagate them for farmers.
ga: Nibii bibii ni akɛduɔ nii tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii Amɛyɛ he fɛɛ he ni amɛhemɔ waaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ajaa nɔyeli hei kɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei krɛdɛɛi lɛ ahaa okwaafoi lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my young transplanted seedlings wilt and die soon after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings experience transplant shock from sudden heat and root damage; planting them during cool morning or evening hours and watering them immediately helps them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui naa amanehulu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ trukaa kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli, ni okɛ nu wo amɛmli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why can't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season like I used to do with local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ fee lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing two specific plant parents to get high yields. If you replant seeds saved from a hybrid harvest, the second generation loses that special vigor, resulting in uneven growth and much lower yields.
ga: Akɛ tso fɔlɔi enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ du ekoŋŋ lɛ, Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: What makes these new hybrid seeds produce so much more food than the traditional seeds my parents used?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ ni mifɔlɔi kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds combine the best traits of two different parent crops—such as stronger roots and bigger fruits—giving the plant extra energy to grow faster and produce a larger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ kɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome, tamɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji. Ehaa tsei hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do all the plants from hybrid seeds grow to the exact same height and mature on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei fɛɛ ni jɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ he kome ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are genetically uniform, meaning every seed carries the exact same growth instructions. This makes the crop grow evenly and ripen at the same time, making harvesting much easier.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ekome yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ bɔ ni edaa lɛ he lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ be kome too mli. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: If I switch to planting hybrid seeds, do I need to buy more fertilizer than I usually use for my farm?
ga: Kɛji mitsake kɛdu dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni mahe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe nɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, because hybrid crops grow faster and yield much more produce, they consume more soil nutrients. To get the high yields promised by hybrid seeds, you must feed them with adequate fertilizer and water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ ana shiwoo ni ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa aha amɛ niyenii.

english: Are these new crop varieties completely immune to farm pests and diseases?
ga: Ani nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei nɛɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kwraa?

english: No seed is immune to everything. While hybrids are often bred to resist specific common diseases, you still need to monitor your fields regularly and protect them from insects and weeds.
ga: Dumɔwu ko bɛ ni baanyɛ adamɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ moŋ, shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii kɛ jwɛi ahe.

english: Why do hybrid seed packages recommend specific planting distances between rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Precise spacing ensures each plant gets the exact amount of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients it needs to produce maximum yield without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo yibii babaoo ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why do some of these new hybrid varieties handle short dry spells better than our old traditional crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei komɛi ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ hɔmɔ be kukuoo he nii jogbaŋŋ fe wɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid seeds are often selected by crop scientists to develop deeper root systems or use leaf water more efficiently, helping them stay green during brief periods without rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi halaa ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Aloo okɛ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli be kukuoo ko ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety being sold in the market will actually grow well in my local soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni mihɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Different varieties are suited for different regions. You can ask local agricultural extension officers, who test new seeds in your district to see which ones match your soil type and rainfall patterns.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi lɛ sa kɛha kpokpai srɔtoi. Obaanyɛ obi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kaa dumɔwui heei ekwɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ koni ena nɔ ni kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ henɔ kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why are hybrid seeds so much more expensive to buy at the agro-shop compared to local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ jara wa waa ni abaanyɛ ahe yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Producing hybrid seeds requires specialized breeding techniques, hand-pollination, and strict quality testing by seed companies every year, which increases the cost of production.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ afeemɔ biɔ fɔmɔ he ŋaai pɔtɛɛ. nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ he kaa ni mli wa daa afi. Enɛ haa nibii ni afee lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Will buying expensive new seeds every season actually bring me more money in the end?
ga: Ani dumɔwui heei ni jara wa ni miheɔ daa afi lɛ baaha maná shika babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Although buying new hybrid seeds every planting season is an extra cost, the significantly larger harvest they produce usually earns you far more income than the cost of the seeds.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahemɔ daa be lɛ yɛ shika kroko moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha oná shika babaoo fe dumɔwui lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo.

english: Why can't I plant yams at any time of the year I want in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu sweet potatoes afi muu lɛ fɛɛ bɔ ni miisumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yams depend heavily on natural rainy and dry cycles. Planting them out of their natural season means the seed tubers will either dry out in baked soil or rot in waterlogged land before they can sprout and mature properly.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be nɔ waa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ baagbi yɛ sũ ni ashã mli loo amɛbaagbo yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli dani amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam plants turning brown and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn yellow and brown near the end of the season, it is usually a natural process called maturity. The plant is transferring its remaining energy into the tuber underground and preparing for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni be lɛ naagbee lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ shweremɔ. Tso lɛ miitsɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ kɛmiiya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ni esaa amɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots inside the barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living storage organs with a natural internal clock. Once their natural resting period ends, they use their stored food energy and moisture to sprout, signaling it is time for the next planting cycle.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Kɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my yams are ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potatoes lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the vines stop growing, wither, and turn dry. You can also dig gently near the mound to check if the head of the tuber has hardened.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji wain tsei lɛ kpa dalɛ, amɛgbi, ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ hu atsu nii blɛoo. Ebɛŋkɛ gɔŋ lɛ koni ekwɛ kɛji tuber lɛ yitso lɛ ewa.

english: Why do some of my yam varieties mature faster than others planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato henɔi lɛ ekomɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Different yam varieties have unique genetic growth cycles. For example, early-maturing types like Pona ready within 6 to 9 months, while late-maturing varieties require up to 12 months to fully develop.
ga: Sweet potato henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwereɔ mra tamɔ Pona lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ nyɔji 12 dani amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: What happens if I harvest my yams too early before the leaves dry up?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmeii mra tsɔ, dani baai lɛ agbi?

english: Early-harvested yams have thin, delicate skin and high water content, which makes them spoil quickly, bruise easily, and rot faster in your storage barn.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpaa mra lɛ yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya, amɛgboiɔ oya, ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ otsu lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my ripe yams if heavy rains stay longer than expected before I harvest?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potatoes ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ dani akpa?

english: Excess rainwater staying in the mounds when yams are already mature can cause the underground tubers to absorb too much water, rot in the soil, or sprout prematurely.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni eshwɛɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli beni sweet potato lɛ egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tuber lɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo. ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya

english: When is the best time for me to start clearing land and preparing mounds for yam planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi gɔŋ ko ni akɛbaadu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ kɛ he saamɔ?

english: Land preparation and mound building are best done late in the dry season (around November to January) so the loose soil is ready to receive seed setts right before the early rains begin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kɛ gɔji amamɔ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. (aaafee November kɛyashi January), no hewɔ lɛ, sũ lɛ efee klalo kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same farm plot right after harvesting my yams?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, but because both yams and cassava pull heavy nutrients from deep in the soil, it is best to add animal manure or plant legumes like cowpeas first to restore soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmeii loo ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmei baafata he klɛŋklɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I choose which part of the harvested yam to save as seeds for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala mi-sweet potato ŋmaa lɛ fãi ni mikɛto akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: The head portion (the top part attached to the vine) or small, clean, healthy whole tubers make the best seed setts because they sprout fastest and produce strong young plants.
ga: Bulbs ni eye emuu, ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ (ŋwɛi fã ni akɛkpɛtɛ wain tso lɛ he) loo bulbs bibii haa dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What are the main benefits of growing pawpaw (bɔfrɛ) on my farm besides eating the fruit?
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi titri yɛ papaya (bɔfrɛ) ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Mɛni ji nɔ kroko hu kɛfata aduawai ni ayeɔ lɛ he?

english: Pawpaw is a fast-growing crop that provides quick income, generates shade for soil moisture retention, and its leaves and seeds can even be used to prepare natural farm remedies to ward off insects.
ga: Pawpaw ji tso ko ni daa oya ni haa anáa shika oya. Ha hulutsoo koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Abaanyɛ akɛ ebaai kɛ edumɔwui hu asaa adebɔɔ mli tsofai yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: How long does a pawpaw tree usually take to start giving fruit after I plant the seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani pawpaw tso ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni midu dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees grow very fast and typically begin flowering and producing mature fruits within six to nine months if they receive enough sunlight and adequate water.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ daa oya waa ni bei pii lɛ, amɛbaabɔi fɔmɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii ni egbɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi nɛɛhu mli kɛji amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can plants like pawpaw help me fight off pests that feed on my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei tamɔ Paw Paw lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awuu?

english: Certain crop parts like pawpaw leaves contain natural bitter compounds that pests dislike; crushing these leaves in water creates an organic spray that repels leaf-eating insects.
ga: Nibii komɛi ni aduɔ, tamɔ pawpaw baai lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni mli edɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ akumɔ baai nɛɛ awo nu mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ baa.

english: Why do tiny insects gather on my young plants, and how do they harm crop growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ amɛyeɔ tsei adalɛ awui?

english: Insects like aphids gather on soft green leaves to suck out vital plant sap, which weakens the plant and stunts fruit production unless they are controlled early.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa yibiiwoo. ja akudɔ lɛ mra

english: Why do my harvested fruits spoil so quickly if I leave them out in the sun after cutting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni mifolɔ amɛgbe naa lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight and heat speed up fruit ripening and rot after harvest; keeping harvested produce in a cool, shaded place slows down spoilage significantly.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ okpamɔ lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha efitemɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo waa.

english: How can I store my harvested fruits so they stay good for several weeks before selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-fruit ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ehi shi otsii babaoo dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Harvesting crops just as they begin to mature—rather than fully ripe—and placing them in a well-ventilated, dry, and cool store keeps them fresh for a longer period.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ lɛ—shi jeee ni amɛshwere kwraa lɛ—ni akɛwo shwapo ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What should I do with cut-down stems and leaves when I am tired of clearing my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni afolɔ beni mihe ejɔ mi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Instead of burning cut plant stems, gathering them and spreading them on the ground creates mulch that keeps the soil cool and slowly decays into rich organic fertilizer.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni afo lɛ Amɛbuaa naa ni akɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ fiofio. Efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why is it important to remove dead or rotten plant parts from near my living crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei ni egboi loo ni egboi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaving dead or decaying plant waste next to healthy crops creates a breeding ground for diseases and pests that can easily spread to your healthy plants.
ga: Tso mli jwɛi ni egboi loo ni efite ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ Ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to harvest my crops to prevent damaging them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni nɔ ko akafite?

english: Harvesting early in the morning when the weather is cool ensures the crops retain their moisture and prevents heat-induced stress and bruising.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How does leaving cut plant materials on top of the soil protect my crops in dry weather?
ga: Te tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around crop roots with cut leaves and stalks acts as a protective blanket, stopping water from evaporating from the soil during hot afternoons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ ni akɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni afo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on my land before planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries them up. Fast-growing plantain trees act like umbrellas, providing necessary shade and moisture for the cocoa trees during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my maize crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil, resulting in weak plants and small cobs. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning light yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil has run out of Nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure will give the soil back the nutrients your crops need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from a dealer instead of just planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, i du dumɔwuhi nɛ a he yi kɛ je ye nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off diseases, resist dry weather, and produce more food. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over time, resulting in lower yields and higher chances of disease.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkɛ helai awuu. Te shi owo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni oha niyenii babaoo aba Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni helai hu baanyɛ aba.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats young maize leaves and damages the growing tip. Catching them early and applying the recommended spray or neem water helps protect your crop from destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem spray loo nu shwie nɔ taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected planting stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension officials lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Trimming extra tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm to stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know the right time to put my seeds in the ground when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the ground has received two or three heavy rains and the soil stays wet beneath the surface. Planting too early after a light rain can cause seeds to dry up and die if the sun returns for a few days.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba gbii fioo krokomɛi.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will steal all the water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your plants. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a strong start before the weeds can choke them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la fɛɛ ni jɛɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim or cut off some of the side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ?

english: Trimming extra side branches stops the tomato plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. Instead, the plant directs its energy into producing bigger, healthier fruits that ripen faster.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baatsi o-tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, tsehi kɛ a he wami ɔ woɔ yiblii nguanguahi nɛ a ngɛ he wami nɛ a yeɔ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the tall trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni majie tsei kakadaji lɛ Fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from burning under harsh sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Leaving some tall trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ajieɔ tsei kakadaji loo aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi Cacao tso lɛ baaha ŋwɛitsu ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashi ebaada ni enyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves and strong stalks. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help restore the soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them for long periods because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the roots easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli oya.

english: What is making holes in my young maize leaves and leaving small dark dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu ni amɛshi muji bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ? yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing shoot of maize plants. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf funnel helps kill the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Supporting the plants with wooden props or bamboo poles, and keeping soil pests like root nematodes under control, prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ haa efeɔ tsii. Akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ tsei asɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo akajie lɛ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nitrogen, while leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Rotating maize with beans naturally restores soil fertility without requiring expensive chemical fertilizers every time.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli be fɛɛ be.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough space on the field for everything to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji akɛ he ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. If weeds are left unchecked, they steal the essential food your crops need, leading to weak plants and lower yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and squishy before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering or mulching helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread plant viruses while feeding on sap. Spraying early with neem oil extract or recommended insect treatments helps manage these pests and keep leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa be mli ni enuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy, steady rains have thoroughly soaked the soil rather than planting after the very first light rain. This ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to germinate without drying up during short dry spells.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se konɛ zugba a nɛ e hyɛ bɔ nɛ sa konɛ duwu ɔmɛ nɛ a puɛ nɛ a be gbie ngɛ hiɔmi be kuku ɔ mi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and getting small holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with holes are usually a sign that pests like the Fall Armyworm are feeding on your maize or that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen needed for healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ buji ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, miiye o-corn lɛ. Aloo nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny whitefly insects that spread a plant virus, or by severe heat stress and inconsistent watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which enriches the land and helps your maize grow bigger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni edaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do weeds harm my cassava crop if they are growing a few feet away from the main stems?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ tso lɛ shishitoo titri lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo ko pɛ?

english: Weeds have underground roots that stretch far to steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients away from your cassava, leaving the crop weak and causing the tubers to remain small.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as very dry soil, extremely hot weather, or attacks by tiny insect pests like thrips that damage the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rain creates stagnant water in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal water-molds to breed and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ fɔɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under strong, direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees act as living umbrellas that provide essential shade and cool moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ŋwɛitsu, ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy winds before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially if tiny soil worms called nematodes have eaten the roots, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop prevents them from blowing over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ. Ale lɛ akɛ nematodes ni yeɔ shishifãi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fi tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams start shrinking and growing shoots inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni ŋmeii miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that use up their stored water and nutrients to grow new shoots when they are stored in warm, humid places for too long.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii heei kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my maize seeds after the early rain starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Soil is ready for planting when you can scoop up a handful and squeeze it into a soft ball that holds its shape without dripping water, showing that there is enough moisture for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni obaanyɛ ojie nine kome ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hiɛɔ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or adding well-decomposed animal manure helps the crop regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea, loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every time I plant maize on the same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving it time to replenish. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore essential nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which have special root nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade from plantains or taller trees to trap soil moisture and protect them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ plantains loo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛbu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need maximum exposure to sunlight so their leaves can create food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes increases sunlight capture, prevents leaf diseases from damp soil, and allows the tubers underground to grow much larger.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shwereɔ babaoo. Tsi tso helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli baa lɛ naa. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially during strong winds or if soil pests have damaged the roots. Supporting the stems with sturdy wooden Y-props prevents the heavy weight from uprooting the tree.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni eye ebua aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo kɛji sũ mli kooloi fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Akɛ nibii ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tsei ni wa fee lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi nibii ni tsii ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaku tso lɛ shi.

english: How do weeds growing next to my crops actually reduce my final harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi Te fee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ ba shi?

english: Weeds act like hidden thieves in your farm, aggressively absorbing the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the food it needs to grow healthy and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ shwieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by those insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and broad so the plant can produce healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli atse bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent through regular watering or mulching helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava root rot occurs when heavy rains waterlog the soil, drowning the roots and allowing fungal diseases to thrive in the excessive moisture. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa kɛji ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the food it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm land produce smaller yields every year when I plant maize on the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do plants like cowpeas and groundnuts help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te tsei tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes have small bumps on their roots containing friendly bacteria that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Muawai ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood flat soil, the roots drown and rot; planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into pepper fruits when it gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to the plant, making it drop its flowers to save energy and water. Providing shade or watering during hot dry periods helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough light and food to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees and plant them in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ ni midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from the heat until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted yam setts take a long time to sprout while others sprout quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yam setts cut from the head of the tuber sprout faster because that part naturally contains more growth buds. Setts cut from the middle or tail take longer because they need extra time to develop new sprouts.
ga: Afoɔ sweet potato kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã ni daa oya lɛ mli ejaakɛ nakai fã lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ loo sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo ejaakɛ eheɔ be kroko dani dumɔwui heei baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the sap from the plant and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with soapy water or neem oil stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops full access to nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves become healthy and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds your maize, helping it grow bigger without relying only on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-corn lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua lɛ ni eda ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp and rainy weather. Removing affected pods immediately and pruning extra branches lets sunlight in to dry out the trees and stop the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la lɛ aha tso lɛ agbi ni ekpa hela lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing pale green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies that feed on the leaves. The best solution is to plant improved, disease-resistant cassava stems provided by extension officers.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ akɛ mɛi ni hiɛɔ lɛ Tsabaa ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni adu ŋmei tsei ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ efee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why are small ragged holes suddenly appearing in the middle of my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibioo ko je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abele baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying neem seed liquid or recommended control powders early in the morning kills the caterpillars before they ruin the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Neem dumɔwui amli nu loo powda ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛbaatsu nii leebi lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or lack of water. Giving the plants steady watering and mulching the base keeps the soil cool so the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu haa tsei lɛ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebatsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my yam vines yield bigger tubers when I support them with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei kakadaji fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, exposing them to more light and keeping them safe from rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa la babaoo boteɔ mli ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why are my ripe tomato fruits getting dark, rotten spots right at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egbo yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist throughout the dry periods stops the spots from forming.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and dry up quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are very wide and lose moisture fast under direct sun. Spreading dried leaves or grass around the base of the plant retains soil moisture and protects the roots from harsh heat.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli lɛɛ waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my main crops immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry period that can scorch delicate seedlings. Waiting until the rainy season fully sets in ensures the young plants have enough moisture to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil produce lower crop yields now than it did when my elders farmed it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ be mli ni mi onukpai lɛ ŋmɔɔ yɛ nɔ nakai afii fɛɛ ni eho lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops or adding organic matter returns essential nutrients to keep the land fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the crops you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die if I clear all the tall trees from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Tall shade trees or plantains act as natural shields, preserving soil moisture and cooling the environment for young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shĩa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa he ko ni mli ejɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly like straws during afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating out of the plant during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to preserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with no ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛbɛ toi beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to produce good ears.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo toi kpakpai.

english: This is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by small insects called whiteflies, which stops the plant from growing healthy tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ haaa tso lɛ akwɛ bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot inside my barn before I can take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akɛbaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when stored in warm, unventilated spaces or when damaged during harvest, allowing fungi and bacteria to enter through cuts.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. aloo kɛ́ efite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ baanyɛ abote pilamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Weeds have strong roots that aggressively absorb water and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can reach them, starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or are suffering from waterlogged roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps them regain their healthy green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛmiipiŋ yɛ shishifãi ni nu ewo mli lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: When heavy rains waterlog the soil, oxygen cannot reach the cassava roots. This lack of air causes soil bacteria and fungi to multiply rapidly, leading to tuber rot before you can harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ayi faa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when afternoon temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress stops proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ shwane mli loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ haomɔ haa pollination ni sa lɛ kpaa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do I know if a crop needs direct sunlight or full shade to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu la loo hulutsoo he miihia miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops like maize, cassava, and tomatoes need full direct sunlight all day to make food and produce heavy yields, while crops like young cocoa or leafy greens prefer partial shade to prevent their leaves from burning.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo bibii loo baai eŋɔli he miihia shade ko koni baa lɛ akashã.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects, which distorts the plant's leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel on the stem before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani eda lɛ?

english: This can be caused by 'cherelle wilt,' where the tree naturally discards pods it cannot support, or by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during wet, humid weather.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha enɛ aba ji ‘cherelle wilt’ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛŋ aye abua lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ black pod hela mli Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it better to plant sweet potatoes on soil mounds rather than on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ hi fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so root tubers can expand easily underground, while also improving drainage so excess rainwater drains away instead of rotting the developing roots.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli moŋ fe ni eeefite shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan weather affect the way my crops take up water?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ Harmattan lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harmattan winds dry out soil moisture quickly and draw water out of plant leaves faster through transpiration. Crops need extra watering or soil mulching during this time to prevent wilting.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa sũ mli nu lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ biɔ ni aha amɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli koni amɛkagboi.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that quickly steal fertilizer nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops, effectively starving your plants before they can use the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ hɔmɔ aye tso lɛ dani enyɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, this stored nitrogen naturally fertilizes the soil for crops planted after them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do people say I should plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa, keeping them cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha kookoo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important food it needs to stay healthy. Heavy rains can also wash this food out of the soil away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni esa akɛ aná koni aná hewalɛ kpakpa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ahoo niyenii nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ akabɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the leaves look very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlɛ waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves instead of feeding the tubers underground. Heavy, hard soil can also prevent roots from expanding.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei agboi kɛ baai. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni wa hu baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How can I tell if worms are destroying my maize farm before the crop is ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miifite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite?

english: Check the center leaves of the young maize plants for ragged holes and small dark droppings. Catching pests like fall armyworms early makes them much easier to control with simple sprays.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli kɛji bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ mli. Ni ooomɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms mra lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baakudɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I burn all the weeds and bushes before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the beneficial insect life in the ground and burns away natural plant material that keeps the soil moist and fertile. Clearing without fire helps the soil retain nutrients.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. ni ashã adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni la bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Should I plant my maize seeds as soon as the very first rain falls in the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ mli pɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until rains become regular over two weeks. The very first rain is often followed by hot dry sun that can heat up the soil and kill young seeds before they get strong roots.
