ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba yɛ otsii enyɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hulu ni mli edɔ, ni egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbe dumɔwui bibii dani amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my high-yielding maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred for one great harvest. If you save and replant those seeds, the second crop loses its strength, producing smaller yields and uneven growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ wuji. Kɛji okɛto ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ Dumɔwu henɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even if I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds drink water and eat soil nutrients faster than your crops can. When you apply fertilizer on a leafy farm, you end up feeding the weeds, which suffocates your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Kɛji okɛ baai wo ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ Ehe baahia ni oha jwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in strong afternoon sun to stop water from evaporating out of the plant. It is the crop's natural way of protecting itself from drying out when the ground lacks moisture.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. yɛ shwane mli koni nu akajɛ tsei lɛ amli Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekagbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cocoa beans turn moldy while I am drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi beni migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans turn moldy if they are piled too thick or left unturned on the drying mat. Spreading them in a thin layer and turning them often allows air and sun to dry them evenly.
ga: Cocoa yibii lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe tsɔ loo ashi amɛ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛkɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ otsake lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when exposed to full sunlight during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaf surfaces and shallow root systems that cannot retain enough water under direct heat. They require shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees to shield them from high heat while their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Spacing cassava stems about one meter apart gives each plant enough space for its roots to expand into large tubers and ensures leaves get adequate sunlight without competing with neighboring plants for nutrients.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mita kome, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee bulbs agboi. ni ehaa baai lɛ náa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, too little water, or too much water around their roots. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu fioo tsɔ he. aloo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted food crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni aduɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally hardier than cultivated farm crops and have seeds that can sit in the soil for years waiting for moisture. Because their roots spread rapidly to steal available water and nutrients, early weeding is necessary to protect your crop.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ni dumɔwui komɛi yɛ ni baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɛ ŋmɔtɔ afii babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehe miihia ni abu onibii ahe.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal infection that spreads in wet, cool conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and reduces fungal growth.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are holes appearing on the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes on cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or insects feeding on the soft greenery. Inspecting under the leaves regularly and applying biological or recommended pest treatments protects the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa kɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: These base shoots, called chupons, waste the tree's food and water. Removing them allows the cocoa tree to direct all its nutrients toward producing healthy cocoa pods on the main branches.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ baafite tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ kookoo yibii lɛ, ehaa kookoo tso lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil if heavy rain collects on my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need well-drained soil to breathe and grow. Standing water starves the tuber of oxygen and creates damp conditions where rot bacteria thrive, which is why planting on mounds or ridges is recommended.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛmu ni amɛdara. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oxygen ni yɔɔ oxygen lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu amɛ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ.

english: How can I tell that a bunch of plantains on my farm is full and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyi obɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fingers lose their sharp, angular edges and become plump and rounded, and the small flower parts at the tips of the fruits dry up completely.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji inchi fɛɛ inchi ŋta ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. kɛ fɔfɔii bibii lɛ ahe fãi Yibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baagbi kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects the young seedlings from heat stress and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantain yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Maize seeds carry only a limited amount of stored food to push their initial shoot to the surface. If buried too deep, the young shoot exhausts its energy before reaching sunlight and dies underground; planting seeds about 2 to 3 centimeters deep gives optimal results.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui yɛ niyenii fioo ko ni ato ni baatsi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, oblahii kɛ oblayei lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ haa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni midu lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the leaf tips usually mean the maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores healthy green foliage and improves yields.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ yitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, so planting it repeatedly in the same field drains the soil's vitality and encourages crop-specific pests. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and restores its fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots or suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain plant for water, sunlight, and food from the soil. Removing excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main plant to produce bigger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to manufacture food that expands the tubers underground. Staking holds the vine up into the light and keeps leaves off hot, moist soil where fungal diseases spread easily.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa wain tso lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Protecting plants with insecticidal soaps, neem oil, or appropriate pesticides controls these pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi, neem fɔ, loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ bu tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before setting any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when temperatures become extremely hot, during sudden dry spells, or when attacked by insect pests like thrips. Maintaining regular watering and providing shelter during heat waves helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ wɔɔhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my mature cassava tubers rot in the soil when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water from heavy rains starves cassava roots of air, causing soil bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the tubers. Harvesting mature cassava before waterlogging occurs prevents crop loss.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa muawai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ. Kasava ni egbɔ ni akpaa dani nu afua baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the stems of my vegetable crops help them grow better in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi awo he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating under strong sunlight. Over time, the grass rots and enriches the soil with organic matter.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, jwɛi baafite ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo baayi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and twist, and how does that stop the roots from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ekpa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. When leaves twist and turn yellow, the plant cannot gather enough sunlight to make food, leaving the underground tubers small and undeveloped.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmei yɛŋ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ tso tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ abua hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdarako.

english: How does crop sickness move from my neighbor's farm into my own cassava field?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases move mainly through wind, flying insects like whiteflies, contaminated tools, or infected planting stems shared among farmers. Insects feeding on a sick plant in a nearby field can easily fly over and infect your healthy crops.
ga: Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ fiji tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ, kɛ nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ titri. loo dumɔwui ahe tsei ni hela emɔ ni aja yɛ okwaafoi ateŋ Kplukai ni yeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ afo kɛho oya ni amɛwo otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli hela.

english: What should I do immediately if I see a few cassava plants in my field showing signs of disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ ŋmei tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔɔ hela he okadii?

english: Uproot the infected plants completely, carry them away from your farm, and burn or bury them. Leaving sick plants in the field allows pests to feed on them and spread the sickness to your remaining healthy crops.
ga: Jiemɔ tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni no sɛɛ lɛ ashãa loo afuɔ Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela amɛshwãa oŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if the cassava stems I want to plant are healthy and free from disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei tso ni otaoɔ odu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli?

english: Select stems only from mother plants that have bright green, unwrinkled leaves and strong stems free of spots or dieback. It is best to source certified disease-resistant stems from agricultural extension offices.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni jɛ nyɛ tso lɛ mli ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmɔlɔ bɛ mli, kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ bɛ mli. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ana tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ema nɔ mi.

english: What makes new cassava varieties better at fighting off disease compared to our traditional varieties?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei henɔi heei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwuɔ helai jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto wɔ blema ŋmei henɔi lɛ ahe?

english: Improved cassava varieties are specifically bred by agricultural scientists to naturally resist common viruses like mosaic disease, allowing them to yield healthy tubers even when disease is present in the area.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi efɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ mosaic hela lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni enɛ haa amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji hela lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ po.

english: Why do my cassava plants sometimes grow tall with big leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants get damaged by disease early on, the plant puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients and clean stems help ensure good tuber development.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni helai efite tsei mra. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ akwɛmɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ tsei ni he tse lɛ haa ŋmeii kpakpai yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does cassava manage to survive long dry seasons better than crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep underground roots and can naturally drop its leaves during severe dry spells to conserve water. As soon as the rains return, it sprouts new leaves and resumes growing.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ebaanyɛ ejie ebaa lɛ kɛjɛ ehe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the price of cassava go up so high in the market when a disease hits our community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei jara yaa hiɛ waa yɛ jara nɔ kɛ́ hela ko ba wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When disease reduces harvests across many farms, less cassava reaches the market. Because cassava is a daily food staple that people rely on, high buyer demand for the small supply drives prices up rapidly.
ga: Beni hela haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo amli lɛ, ŋmãa fioo pɛ yɔɔ jara nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei ji daa gbi niyenii ni gbɔmɛi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ faaa lɛ haa nibii ajara yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Can planting cassava together with other crops like maize or beans help protect my farm from disease?
ga: Cassava ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baadu Ani ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: Yes, mixing crops creates physical barriers that slow down the movement of insect pests and plant diseases across your field, while also providing alternative harvests if one crop performs poorly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai lɛ yaa oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a single crop disease seem to destroy farms across our entire village all at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tso hela kome kpataa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ ahiɛ yɛ wɔ akrowai lɛ amli yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: This happens when neighboring farmers share stem cuttings from the same infected source or when pests carry the disease easily between adjacent fields, causing widespread crop loss across the whole community.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ jaa niji ni jɛ hela kome mli lɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ helai baa shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ mlɛo Enɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii fite babaoo yɛ akutso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How is growing vegetables inside a greenhouse different from growing them in my open field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ he?

english: In a greenhouse, crops mature faster—often within 4 to 6 months—because they are protected from harsh weather, strong heat, and common insect pests, whereas open fields leave crops fully exposed to rain, heat, and seasonal diseases.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya—bei pii lɛ yɛ nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 6 mli—ejaakɛ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, dɔlɛ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and curl up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl and yellow when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or when tiny insects like whiteflies spread a plant virus. Giving the plants steady water and shade helps reduce this stress.
ga: Tomatoi baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eba nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ shi.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes drastically from dry to very wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa kɛjɛ he ni egbi kɛtee he ni edɔ waa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my garden eggs taste bitter when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Garden egg fruits turn bitter if they are picked too late after over-ripening or if the plant suffered from severe water shortages while the fruit was developing on the stem.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmei yibii lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ beni eshɛ fe nine sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ naaa nu waa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is a major food crops need to grow green and strong. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deeper into the soil away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that shield young cocoa trees from direct sun and preserve moisture in the ground until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my sweet potato plant grow lots of green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes sweet potatoes to put all their energy into growing top leaves and vines instead of developing thick, heavy underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ zugba sisi sisi nɛ mi wa nɛ e mi wa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest cassava so it does not spoil underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping. Leaving cassava roots in the soil for too long turns them tough, woody, and watery.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ tso kɛ nu.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody so quickly after forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ mlɛo oya ni amɛfeɔ tso beni afee amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Okra pods grow very fast and must be harvested within 3 to 5 days after the flower opens. If left longer on the stem, the pods develop tough fibers that make them hard to cook and eat.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni haa ewaa akɛ abaahoo ni aye.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas in my field after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the soil, while legumes like cowpeas naturally fix nitrogen back into the dirt and break the cycle of pests that target maize.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nitrogen lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji ŋmãa lɛ oti lɛ mli.

english: What is the main difference between MD2 and Sugarloaf pineapples?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ Pineapple MD2 kɛ Sugarloaf teŋ?

english: MD2 pineapples are uniform, golden-yellow, and have a longer shelf life, making them preferred for commercial processing and export. Sugarloaf pineapples are conical, sweeter, softer, and stay green even when ripe, making them ideal for immediate local fresh consumption.
ga: Pineapple MD2 lɛ yɛ su kome. Eji shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa ehe gbɛi waa kɛha jarayeli nitsumɔ kɛ maŋsɛɛ nitsumɔ. Sugarloaf pineapple lɛ tamɔ cone, eyɛ ŋɔɔ, eyɛ blɛoo, ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli kɛji ekwɛ̃ po. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii hee ni ayeɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do juice processing companies prefer buying MD2 pineapples over other varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ aduawai amli nu lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe MD2 pineapple fe srɔtoi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Juice manufacturers prefer MD2 because it has a consistent balance of high sugar and acid, yields a lot of juice, and maintains a rich yellow color that makes processed drinks look appealing to buyers.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ juice lɛ sumɔɔ MD2 ejaakɛ eyɛ sugar kɛ acid ni fa babaoo, ni ekɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee po. Ehaa aduawai amli nu babaoo ni ehiɛɔ su ni mli kwɔ ni haa nibii ni anuɔ ni afee lɛ fɛfɛo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pineapples not sweet even after I harvest them and wait for them to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ ŋɔɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni akpa ni mimɛɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ po lɛ?

english: Pineapples do not get any sweeter after they are cut from the plant. Unlike bananas, pineapples get all their sugars from the plant's leaves while growing, so if harvested too early, they remain sour.
ga: Pineapple lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ́ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ banana lɛ, pineapple naa e-sugar lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli beni edara lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, Pineapple yɛ ŋmɔlɔ lolo.

english: What causes my pineapples to develop small, weak fruits instead of large ones?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pineapple lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ yibii wuji najiaŋ?

english: Small fruits usually happen when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium and nitrogen, or when plants are crowded too close together and forced to compete for sunlight and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen. Aloo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo tsɔ ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ.

english: Why do pineapples on the same farm flower at different times instead of all together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe be kome mli lɛ?

english: Pineapples naturally flower based on individual plant size and subtle changes in weather or temperature stress. Farmers often apply safe flower-inducing treatments so all plants produce fruit at the same time for easier harvesting.
ga: Pineapple baawo fɔfɔi yɛ e diɛŋtsɛ ehe yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ tsakemɔi fioo ni baa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo hulutsoo be mli haomɔ mli lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ gbɛi ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii ahe hewalɛ shweshweeshwe tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɛɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli koni ŋmaakpamɔ afee mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves of my pineapple plants turning red and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple baai lɛ miitsɔ etsuru kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Reddish or yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is under stress, usually from drought, nutrient deficiency in the soil, or mealybug insects attacking the roots.
ga: Baai tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. ni bei pii lɛ ejɛɔ hɔmɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mealybug kooloi ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ amli baa.

english: Is it better to start a new pineapple farm using suckers or the tops cut from the fruit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooobɔi pineapple ŋmɔ hee kɛtsɔ suckers nɔ loo kɛtsɔ yibii lɛ anɔ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ?

english: Suckers are better because they are larger and already partially developed, so they mature and produce fruit several months faster than the tops (crowns) of the fruit.
ga: Sucker lɛ hi fe no ejaakɛ eda ni etsɔ fã ko. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii nyɔji komɛi mra fe yibii lɛ yiteŋ (akɔɔble) lɛ.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted pineapple shoot to produce a ready fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Depending on the planting material and variety, pineapples generally take between 12 to 18 months from planting to harvest in warm tropical climates like Ghana.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ. Enɛ damɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ kɛ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell that a pineapple is fully ready to be harvested for selling?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ abaanyɛ akpa pineapple ni esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Look for the base of the fruit turning yellow, the skin's eyes flattening out, and a sweet pineapple aroma coming from the base of the plant.
ga: Taomɔ ni aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ afee ŋmɔŋ, ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ, ni ji ŋmeii ni jɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pineapples develop soft, burnt patches on one side while still growing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ shãa blɛoo yɛ efã kome be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is sunburn caused by direct intense heat from the sun hitting exposed fruit. Farmers usually bent or cover leaning pineapples with dry grass or leaves to shade them during hot afternoons.
ga: Enɛ ji hulutsoo ni hulutsoo ni naa wa ni tswaa aduawai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe lɛ anɔ loo amɛhaa amɛ koni amɛha amɛná hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture for the young cocoa trees to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess leaves allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and reduce fungus growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong, or that waterlogging is stopping the roots from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Aloo nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛha niyenii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or peanuts on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and peanuts put natural nitrogen back into the soil, restoring fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni okɛ babaoo aba ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy enough to support good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, smells rich like fresh earth, holds moisture without becoming muddy, crumbles easily in your hands, and contains living earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ muji Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the tubers without draining, it drowns the roots and causes rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil experiences extreme dry spells, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly even after I apply water to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ po lɛ?

english: Soil loses water quickly when left bare under direct sunlight. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the ground cool and traps moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching ni akɛbaa ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply liquid fertilizer or pesticides to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: The best times are early morning or late evening when the weather is cool. High heat during midday can burn plant leaves or cause sprays to evaporate before doing their job.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai loo eha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ la dani ebɔi nitsumɔ.

english: These are pests hatched from eggs laid by adult butterflies. They feed on soft green leaves to grow, and they can be controlled by handpicking, using light traps, or applying safe farm sprays.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ awui amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛdara. ni abaanyɛ akudɔ kɛtsɔ nine ni ahalaa nɔ Kɛtsɔ tsɔnei ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni akɛtsuɔ nii Aloo akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or they are getting too much or too little water. When crops lack key soil nutrients, they cannot make green food for themselves and their leaves turn pale.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. loo nu babaoo loo fioo ni anáa Beni tsei bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii ni ji ŋmɔji amɛha amɛhe. ni ebaai lɛ hu tsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I space my cassava plants far apart instead of crowding them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ fe bɔ ni amɛbaafee ekome lɛ?

english: Giving cassava plants enough space lets their underground roots expand into big tubers without competing with neighboring plants for soil food, sunlight, and moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ aha ŋmei tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ abɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ.

english: Why do tiny worms keep eating the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing heart of young maize plants. Detecting them early and applying recommended natural or chemical controls stops them before they destroy the crop's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ atsuii anɔ. Ni ooona amɛ mra ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Tsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite hei ni onibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up their flower pollen. When the plant feels overheated, it drops its flowers to conserve energy and water until cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, feeding the maize without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Abaanyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce hundreds of small flowers, but only a few turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii ohai abɔ, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can feed. If insects do not pollinate the flowers, or if the tree lacks enough water and fertilizer, it naturally drops the extra flowers so it can concentrate its power on growing a few good pods.
ga: Kookoo tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii shwieee fɔfɔi anɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa lɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi kpakpai fioo komɛi ni ebaakwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my pepper plants make the peppers grow so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi Pepper Tso lɛ Haa Pepper Feɔ Bibii Waa?

english: Weeds act like stolen roots on your field—they aggressively soak up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your pepper plants, leaving your crop starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ shishifãi ni aju yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛkɛ yiwalɛ shwieɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-pepper tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni oduɔ nii lɛ, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: How does adding manure or compost change the way my yam tubers grow under the dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Organic matter like manure softens hard soil, allows roots to penetrate deeper, retains rainwater longer, and supplies slow-release food that lets yam tubers swell into large, clean tubers.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Too nugbɔ nu lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo blɛoo ni yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he tse.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot or catch insects when I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo ŋmeii yeɔ amɛhe kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains rot if they are stored before drying completely under the sun. Moisture encourages mold and attracts grain beetles, while thoroughly dried grain sealed in airtight bags keeps pests out.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto dani amɛgbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Fɛ̃i woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ ni egbalaa ŋmaa ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaboteɔ mli.

english: Why do my vegetables wilt so quickly during the minor rainy season compared to the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season brings shorter rains and longer sun exposure, which evaporates soil water quickly. Crops wilt because their roots cannot drink fast enough to replace water lost from their leaves.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa shi fioo lɛ baatsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo kɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ la oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wilt so quickly between January and February in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ oya yɛ January kɛ February teŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Between January and February, Ghana experiences the dry Harmattan season, where low humidity, dry winds, and a lack of rainfall rapidly strip moisture from both the soil and plant leaves.
ga: Yɛ January kɛ February teŋ lɛ, Ghana kɛ Harmattan be ni mli egbi kpeɔ. Fɛ̃i ni baa shi, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, kɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ gbalaa fɛ̃i kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ amli oya.

english: How can I protect my farm and crops from bushfires during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ koo mli la he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can clear a clean strip of bare land about 3 to 5 meters wide around your farm's boundary, known as a firebelt, which stops wild grass fires from jumping onto your cropland.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi he ko ni mli tse ni mli tse ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee mitai 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ he. Ale lɛ hu akɛ la hebuu. Enɛ haa koo mli jwɛi la lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to plant my seeds to make sure they get enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui koni nugbɔ anɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: The best time to plant is right after the main rainy season sets in (typically around March or April in southern Ghana), ensuring the soil has soaked up enough steady moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ. (Be pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ March loo April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ.) Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What can I cover my soil with to stop water from drying out when it stops raining?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mawo mli koni ekagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: You can place dry grass, crop leaves, or cocoa husks around the base of your plants—a practice called mulching—which shades the ground and holds moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, tso baai, loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ abɔle tso lɛ shishi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve into a form plant roots can take up; without water, concentrated chemical fertilizer remains around the roots and can burn or kill the plant.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ bɔ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo egbe tsei lɛ.

english: Can I still grow vegetables on my farm during dry months if I do not have a river nearby?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai lolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli? Kɛji faa ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ

english: Yes, by using simple water-saving methods like hand-watering early in the morning before the sun gets hot, or setting up small drip buckets to deliver water directly to the plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛbaatsu nii koni akɛbu nu he, tamɔ nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ leebi dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo nu tsɛnsi bibioo ko ni shwieɔ shi ni atoɔ Koni akɛ nu aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up under intense sun as a natural protective response to reduce their surface area and lower the amount of water escaping into the hot air.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛba nu ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi.

english: Why do my crops drop their lower yellow leaves when there is a short drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ baai ŋmɔŋ ni baa shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo ko ba lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, plants deliberately drop older, lower leaves to save their remaining water and nutrients for the younger, growing parts of the plant.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ eshwieɔ baai ni egbɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ koni ekɛto nu kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛha tso lɛ fãi bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Should I clear dry weeds from my land before the first rains start?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni egbi kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi?

english: Yes, clearing dry weeds before planting prevents them from stealing early rain and nutrients from your crops, while also removing dry material that could easily catch fire.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni agbiɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jiemɔ nibii ni egbi ni baanyɛ atswa la oya lɛ.

english: How do cover crops like cowpeas help keep my land healthy during dry spells?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cover crops spread across the soil, providing shade that keeps the ground cool, prevents soil erosion from dry winds, and enriches the soil with nitrogen for future crops.
ga: Ha tsei ni gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when rainwater sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When water stands on your farm, it blocks air from reaching the crop roots. Just like people need air to breathe, plant roots need air in the soil to survive, so standing water suffocates the roots and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu ba oŋmɔ lɛ mli Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛmu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does digging small water channels or gutters around my farm help my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ bibioo ko ni aaafo Aloo te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni nubui ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Gutters carry excess water away from your field so it does not drown your crop roots. Removing excess water keeps the soil moist but healthy, allowing roots to breathe and absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Gutters shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ shi ehi jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are there specific crops I can plant in wet parts of my farm where water always collects?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu yaa nɔ ebua ehe naa yɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like rice, cocoyam, and sugarcane love wet soil and thrive in waterlogged areas, whereas crops like cassava or maize will rot if left in standing water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ omɔ, kookoo, kɛ shɛ̃ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Baafite kɛji ashi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: How does leaving grass or cover crops in my farm help with soaking up extra ground water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: Grass and cover crops have many fine roots that act like a sponge in the soil. They drink up extra groundwater and prevent heavy rains from washing away your topsoil and crop fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi kpakpai babaoo ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo ni amɛtsiɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ anaa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Will growing cover crops in my farm dry out the soil and leave no water for my main crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekɛ nu haaa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Cover crops actually shade the ground and prevent sunlight from baking the earth. This reduces evaporation, keeping the soil moist longer for your main crops, especially during short dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli

english: How can dry grass spread around my crops protect them from heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he?

english: Spreading dry grass around your crops creates a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch shields the soil from direct sun, keeping the root area cool and holding moisture in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛaawo Oŋmɔshinii lɛ ahe lɛ baafee nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Mulch buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear thick weeds and choked drains near my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Clearing thick weeds and blocked channels prevents stagnant water and stops harmful pests and diseases from hiding near your crops, giving your plants a clean and safe environment to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni atsĩ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ akafee nɔ ko, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshara akahi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Ha otsei lɛ shihilɛ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in tough conditions, so they quickly take advantage of rainwater and nutrients in the soil. If you do not clear them early, they will steal food and sunlight from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli, no hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ oya. Kɛji ojieee amɛ oya lɛ, Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops droop or curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural trick to save water. By curling its leaves, the crop reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to stop moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni ekɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: How do crop roots know how to find water under the ground during a dry spell?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Plant roots naturally grow towards moisture in the soil. As the top layer of soil dries out, the roots stretch deeper into the earth where water is still stored.
ga: Tse shishifãi daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ mli egbi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them, the intense sun scorches their tender leaves, causing them to turn yellow, dry out, and die.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, dumɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo koni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is my maize crop producing flowers and tassels when the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Ani tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Maize plants flower early when they experience stress from poor soil nutrients or a lack of water. The crop rushes to reproduce early to survive, even though it hasn't grown tall enough to support large corn cobs.
ga: Abɛi tsei fɔɔ mra kɛji akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafɔ oya bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekwɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji anɔ moŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy with plenty of green leaves, but when I dig it up the tubers are very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi kɛ́ atsa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli etse waa?

english: When there is too much nitrogen in the soil, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food to expand the roots underground.
ga: Beni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato koni ekɛgbala eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between rains or watering days.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni ashwieɔ gbii lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers onto the ground instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiku efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from sudden heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips that damage the blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ trukaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground and train them up on wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mitsɔseɔ lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the hot ground into the sunlight, helping the plant make more food for bigger tubers while keeping soil diseases from damaging the foliage.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ ajie kɛjɛ he ni edɔ lɛ kɛya hulu lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu naa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: If I want to start experimenting with growing soybean on a small plot, how will I know if my soil is good for it?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni obɔi soybeans ni oookwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ he kaa. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You can tell the soil is good if the seeds sprout evenly within a week and the roots develop small, healthy pink nodules inside, which show the plant is fixing its own natural fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. Ni shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ pinki. ni mli wa yɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiwo ehe fɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the bunches on my plantain trees getting smaller when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui niji ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ bibii beni mishiɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil food. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one strong replacement so the main tree can bear large bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii loo ni eda fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ shwɛɔ bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ jwɛi agbo ko.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves look completely wilted in the afternoon heat but look strong and fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni oná hejɔɔmɔ leebi?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it from the soil, causing the plant to temporarily drop to save water before recovering overnight.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu nu he dani amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Why did my cowpea crop produce so many heavy green leaves during the rainy season but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni tsuɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Too much rain encourages cowpeas to focus on growing vines and leaves. The plant needs a mild dry period to trigger flowering and pod production.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa wain tsei kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Tsei hia be ni mli egbi fioo koni ekanya fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas next to them creates shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the base helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies feeding underneath the leaves. These pests drink the plant's sap and spread viruses, which distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers heat stress, experiences uneven watering, or lacks pollination. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and providing afternoon shade can help the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni tsei lɛ toɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he amɛhaa lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shwane mli hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: On very hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. This temporary wilting is the plant's natural defense to conserve moisture, and the leaves usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will they fight for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: Cowpeas and maize work well together because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better. This natural partnership feeds both crops without them competing for nutrients.
ga: Tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsakpaa nɛɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ niyenii ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows pests and diseases targeting that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like beans or peanuts refreshes the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaku hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it in. When put on dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer cannot be absorbed, can burn the plant roots, or can evaporate into the air.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji wo mli lɛ, enyɛŋ eŋɔ, tso shishifãi lɛ ashã, loo etsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvest of hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first generation. If you plant seeds harvested from hybrid crops, the second-generation plants will produce smaller yields, uneven growth, and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ Tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baawo yibii fioo. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole stem?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem begins to crack and swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This happens when the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize prioritizes new growth, so it pulls stored nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi sumɔɔ dalɛ hee. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under full sunlight. They need living shade, like plantains or shade trees, to protect them and keep the surrounding air humid until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka, tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ aaawa.

english: Why is it important to measure exact distances between my crops instead of just planting seeds closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ a du dumɔwuhi nɛ a bɛŋkɛ a he kɛkɛ.

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When crops are planted too close together, they grow tall and weak, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out very small and rot inside the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, well-drained soil to expand properly. If soil holds too much water, air cannot reach the roots, causing the tubers to choke and rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer can cause plants to drop their blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my fertilizer into the soil at once when I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young plants can only absorb tiny amounts of nutrients. Applying all the fertilizer at once wastes money because heavy rains will wash it away before the crop matures enough to feed on it.
ga: Tsei bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ. Shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ ji shika fitemɔ ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Yam leaves use sunlight to manufacture food for the plant. Staking spreads the leaves out so they catch maximum sunlight, which sends food downward to swell the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni ená hulu la babaoo. ni tsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni eha yitso lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable crops curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant sap, which causes the leaf tissue to distort as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When planted together, this nitrogen naturally feeds the soil, giving the maize free nutrition to grow tall.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ he kome Nitrogen nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Na niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ ŋmãa mli koni okwɛ.

english: How do I know my maize is completely dry and ready to harvest so it does not rot after picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, egbooo?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and a tiny black layer forms at the bottom tip of each kernel where it joins the cob, showing the grain has stopped taking in water.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ŋmei diŋŋ bibioo ko baahi Ebaa yɛ ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishigbɛ naagbee he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekpa nu mumɔ.

english: Why are my rice seeds taking so long to sprout after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture, warmth, and air to wake up. Sometimes seeds take a bit of time to absorb water and push out their roots, so even if you do not see green leaves above the ground immediately, they are growing beneath the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ, latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi. Bei komɛi lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be fioo dani amɛmɔɔ nu lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji onaaa baai eŋɔli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my planted seeds have rotted and died or are just slow to come up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni midu lɛ egbo ni amɛgboi loo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya?

english: You can gently dig up a seed or two in one spot to check. If the seed is firm and swelling or showing a tiny white shoot, it is alive and growing; if it is soft, mushy, or smells bad, it has rotted and died.
ga: Obaanyɛ Okɛ dumɔwu kome loo enyɔ atsu nii fiofio yɛ he kome koni opɛi mli. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛfuu loo amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ. Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni eedara kɛji eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Egboɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do local rice seeds behave differently from the new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Local seed varieties have adapted to survive harsh local conditions over many years, so they might take longer to germinate or grow taller to outsmart weeds, whereas new store-bought seeds are bred to grow quickly and uniformly.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛda babaoo dani amɛye jwɛi lɛ anɔ kunim. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why does rice grow so well in flooded or very wet soil where other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo nɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ tsei krokomɛi gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow air tubes inside their stems that send air down to their roots under water, allowing them to breathe and survive in wet conditions where other crops would drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Ehaa emuɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi baagboi yɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they use up all their stored food energy trying to push through the heavy dirt and can suffocate or rot before reaching sunlight at the surface.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baafite amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ efo loo egbo dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings look weak or drooping shortly after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ loo amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When young plants are first put into the field, their roots get disturbed and cannot pull up water right away, causing temporary transplant shock until the roots settle into the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baafite ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hosoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Does soaking my rice seeds in water before planting help them grow faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui wo nu mli dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya?

english: Yes, soaking seeds softens their hard outer shells and signals them to start growing, which speeds up germination once you plant them in the moist soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing above ground for a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kwɛ̃mɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After making their first leaves, plants often pause top growth to direct energy into building a strong, deep root network underground to anchor themselves and absorb nutrients.
ga: Beni afee klɛŋklɛŋ kaadi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ tsei kpaɔ ŋwɛi dalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni amɛkɛma amɛhe shi ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How deep should I cover my rice seeds when planting in the farm?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Rice seeds should only be covered lightly with about one to two centimeters of soil so that the small shoots can easily push through to reach air and sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni feɔ sɛntimita 1-2 pɛ aha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ fioo. koni akɛfee ŋmeii bibii Ebaanyɛ ebote kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli mlɛo.

english: Why do heavy rains sometimes cause my newly planted seeds to disappear from where I put them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Strong rainwater can wash away loose topsoil and carry light seeds down into deep soil cracks or sweep them away completely, making it look like the seeds vanished.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etsilɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui bibii aya. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli loo shwiemɔ mli kwraa. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlaaje.

english: Why are my cocoa trees giving fewer pods now than they did ten years ago on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe bɔ ni amɛwo afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Just like people get weak when they work without eating, soil loses its strength after growing crops for many years. Every harvest takes food out of the ground, so if you do not feed the soil with nutrients, the land gets tired and your harvest drops.
ga: Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ gbɔmɛi ni gbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ amɛtsu nii ni amɛyeee nii lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he waaa yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ. Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ be kɛ niyenii baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni okpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my soil is getting exhausted and needs help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ miije shishi efo ni yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia mi?
