english: You can tell your soil is weak if plant leaves start turning pale or yellow, crops grow slower than usual, or your harvest gets smaller every year even when there is enough rain.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Aloo ani okpamɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: What happens if I keep farming my land without ever putting fertilizer or manure into it?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji mitee nɔ matsu okwaayeli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he?

english: If you keep taking crops from the land without putting nutrients back, the soil becomes completely empty of food. Over time, your crop yields will continue to fall until the land can barely support healthy trees.
ga: Kɛji okpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kwraa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaya nɔ aba shi. Kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Is animal manure better for fixing tired land than chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani kooloi aŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ fe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Both are helpful, but animal manure improves the earth itself by helping it hold water like a sponge for a long time. Chemical fertilizer gives quick food to the crops, but manure builds up the long-term health of tired soil.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii baaha shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do old trees stop bearing fruit properly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kpa yibiiwoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As crop trees grow older, they need richer soil to stay healthy, but old farmland often runs out of essential plant food. Rain gives water, but without nutrients in the dirt, the tree cannot make new flowers or heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni jara wa he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ bɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo fɔfɔi heei loo ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: If I add fertilizer to my farm, will I see more pods on my trees immediately?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ Ani mana ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer takes a little time to work because the roots must drink it up first to rebuild the tree's strength. Usually, you will see greener leaves first, and then more flowers and bigger fruit in the next harvest cycle.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ heɔ be fioo pɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii ejaakɛ esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ewo tso hee lɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, obaana baai eŋɔli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ aduawai wuji baaba yɛ kpamɔɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does cutting off extra unwanted branches help my cocoa tree produce bigger pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When a tree has too many useless branches, it wastes its food trying to keep all those leaves alive. Pruning removes the extra branches so all the soil nutrients go directly into growing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji ni he ehiaaa babaoo tsɔ Ebaafite niyenii ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha nakai baai lɛ ahi shi lɛ. Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni miida waa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can I leave fallen cocoa leaves and dry weed cuttings on the farm ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi kookoo baai ni egbee shi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, leaving clean leaves on the ground forms a natural cover that rots down into good soil food. It also acts like a blanket that keeps the dirt cool and stops the sun from drying out the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ashi baai ni he tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ niyenii kpakpa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu hu koni ekɛha muji akafee fɛ̃i ni ekɛtsi hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to leave large shade trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young crops from strong direct sunlight that bakes the ground and drains nutrients. Their deep roots also hold the dirt together so heavy rains do not wash away the rich top layer of your soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ muji feɔ ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does soil seem to lose its strength faster on fields that get heavy sunshine all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ mli gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Direct hot sun bakes the bare ground and burns away organic material that feeds the crops. When soil stays exposed to harsh sun without shade or leaf cover, its moisture dries up fast and its nutrients break down.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ, ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ shɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni hulutsoo loo baai bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do grasscutters only nibble small parts of my crops and move to another spot instead of eating one whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔ lɛ ŋmɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã bibioo ko pɛ lɛ? Ni ajie lɛ kɛya he kroko moŋ fe ni oooye tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Grasscutters naturally forage by moving around to sample different plants for nutrients and to stay alert for predators. This scattered feeding habit means they take quick, small bites across different plants rather than staying in one place.
ga: Jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi naa niyenii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Koni abua tsei srɔtoi ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa Koni ana niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ Nɛkɛ niyenii ni mli eja su nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ tsei srɔtoi. oya kɛ kuku Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohi he kome

english: Why do I see scattered bite marks across different sections of my farm instead of damage in just one area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmɔlɔ he okadii ni egbɛ eshwã hei srɔtoi lɛ? ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mana nɔ ni efite yɛ he kome

english: Pests like grasscutters move continuously between bushes and farm plots to test food freshness and avoid human presence, leaving light, widespread damage across several spots.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔji lɛ nyiɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmɔji kɛ okwaayeli ŋmɔji ateŋ koni amɛka niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amɛkwɛ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ adesai ahe. Ekɛ la baa ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa he ko ni da yɛ hei babaoo.

english: Why do wild animals like grasscutters travel between different bushes instead of staying in one field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa jwɛi srɔtoi ateŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Wild animals move between multiple bushes to search for a variety of tender plants and to hide from danger, which keeps them constantly on the move across different farm boundaries.
ga: Koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ jwɛi srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ. Koni ana tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ oshara he Enɛ haa amɛyaa nɔ amɛfoɔ ŋmɔ husui srɔtoi amli.

english: How can I tell if the bite damage on my crop stalks is caused by a grasscutter?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni ha mitso lɛ tsei lɛ fite lɛ?

english: Grasscutters leave clean, sharp, angled cuts on the lower stems of plants, often leaving small bits of chewed crop scattered around without eating the entire plant to the ground.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ shĩɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛshiɔ tsei bibii ni amɛyeɔ. Egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he ni eyeee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kwraa.

english: How does partial chewing by grasscutters affect the overall growth of my crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ fã ko ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When an animal chews small parts of a crop, the plant suffers from stress and must spend extra energy repairing stem tissues, which can delay its growth and overall yield.
ga: Kɛ́ kooloi ye tso ko fãi bibii lɛ, tso lɛ naa haomɔ ni ebiɔ hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛsaa fãji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dalɛ kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Will my crops survive if an animal just bites the stem a little bit and moves away?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi kɛji kooloo ko ŋmɔ tso lɛ shishi fioo pɛ ni ejie lɛ?

english: Crops usually survive light chewing, but the open bite wounds make the plant vulnerable to fungal infections and secondary pests if the stem is severely damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ hiɔ shi kɛji akɛ eye ŋmɔlɔ fioo, shi ŋmɔlɔ ni etswa lɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji enyɔ lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ eshishifã lɛ fite waa.

english: Why do my crops take longer to produce fruit when animals keep taking small bites from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? Akɛni kooloi ŋmɔɔ amɛ nibii bibii hewɔ lɛ?

english: Every time a plant loses part of its leaves or stem to an animal, it pauses fruit development to focus its energy on growing new tissues to heal itself.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni tso ko baa loo eshishifãi lɛ ekomɛi baafite kɛha kooloi. Tso lɛ kpaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ ama fãji heei ni edaa lɛ anɔ koni etsa ehe.

english: Why do grasscutters prefer biting the bottom part of my crop stalks instead of the top leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛfo tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: The base of crop stalks is often softer, sweeter, and holds more moisture and sugars, making it the most attractive part for chewing animals like grasscutters.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sugar babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ni kooloi ni yeɔ jwɛi, tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ waa.

english: How can I protect my crops when pests keep moving from bush to bush into my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai jɛɔ jwɛi amli kɛyaa jwɛi krokomɛi amli kɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing wide buffer zones around your farm edges reduces bush cover, making moving animals like grasscutters feel exposed and less likely to cross into your fields.
ga: Buffer he ko ni da ni ajieɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa koolooi ni tsiɔ amɛhe, tamɔ jwɛi shwielɔi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe egbele ni amɛfoŋ kɛbote oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do grasscutters attack my farm crops more during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: When wild bush vegetation dries up or gets cleared, grasscutters move more actively into crop fields searching for soft, green plant tissues that are easy to chew.
ga: Beni koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ egbi loo ajie amɛ. Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ baafã kɛya ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ amli babaoo. Koni ana tso mli fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ waaa

english: Young cocoa leaves turn yellow under intense direct heat because the plant loses water faster than its roots can pull it from the ground. Planting shade crops like plantains near cocoa helps block extreme sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ amɛwo la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or rain early in its growth, it spends all its energy growing leafy stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo nugbɔ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baa tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like green tubes during the dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli yɛ shwane ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a self-defense mechanism to hide their surface area from the sun, which stops the plant from losing vital moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ato hulu lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafite nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when temperatures become too hot or when water supply is irregular, which damages the flower's pollen and prevents fertilization.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. ni fiteɔ pollen ni etsĩɔ fɔmɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why does my yam vine need a tall wooden stake to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need stakes to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. Maximum sunlight on the leaves helps the plant manufacture energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishitoo mla ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kɛyaa hulu la nɔ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling downwards and looking crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Downward leaf curl on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids feeding on the undersides of leaves, or viruses passed on by those pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and look weak when water stays on the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ be mli ni nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water sits on the soil for too long, it pushes out air, preventing plant roots from breathing oxygen and absorbing essential nutrients from the earth.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkamu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of lower leaves in a V-pattern indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, showing that the plant needs manure or fertilizer to grow properly.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anaa yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei he miihia tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my vegetable plants flowering when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miifɔ lɛ? Ani eji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Vegetables flower early when they feel stressed by drought or poor soil. The plant panics and produces flowers early so it can make seeds before it dies.
ga: Aduawai fɔɔ oya kɛji hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hao amɛ. Tso lɛ sheɔ gbeyei ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi mra bɔni afee ni enyɛ eyadumɔ mli dani egbo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into ribbons when there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their veins during high winds to allow air to pass through without snapping the main stem or uprooting the whole plant.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ekuuu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ loo ejieee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant quickly grows new leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my young maize leaves so fast after the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms fiteɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ trukaa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs that hatch quickly when warm rains arrive. The young caterpillars feed greedily at the same time on fresh maize leaves before you notice them.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɛ. Kplukai bibii kɛ hiɛjoomɔ miiye ŋmãa baai heei yɛ be kome too mli dani oyɔse.

english: You should wait until the ground gets two or three good rains that soak deep into the dirt. Planting after just one light shower can cause your seeds to sprout and then die if the ground dries up.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ kpakpa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ shii enyɔ loo etɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Dumɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduuu ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or when the soil gets too dry or waterlogged, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil, working like a free natural fertilizer for crops planted afterwards.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei ni adu sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when the branches get too bushy and crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ be mli ni eniji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛhe eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are too thick, sunlight cannot reach the trunk where flowers grow, and damp air stays trapped inside, which encourages diseases like black pod to spread.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ tsei ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ baatsi mli. Enɛ woɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the day to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant hold onto its water until the weather cools down.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie hidden in the dirt ready to sprout immediately when cleared ground gets sunlight, while crop seeds take more time to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji he ni ajie lɛ lɛ ná hulu la pɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do early-maturing maize seeds give smaller yields than the traditional late-maturing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe blema dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early-maturing maize grows and produces grain in a shorter time to avoid drought, but because it spends less total time gathering sunlight and nutrients, its ears stay smaller.
ga: Abele ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaawo dumɔwui yɛ be kukuoo mli koni hɔmɔ akafee. Shi akɛni ŋmãa heɔ be babaoo ni ekɛbuaa hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa hewɔ lɛ, toi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is short on nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or well-decayed animal manure will restore their healthy green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛfee baai ni wa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop field is hungry for fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Crops show hunger through slow growth, thin stems, or pale leaves instead of rich green ones. Applying fertilizer a few weeks after planting gives crops the nutrients they need right when they enter their fastest growth phase.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ hɔmɔ kpo kɛtsɔ dalɛ ni yaa blɛoo, tsei bibii, loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ beni eboteɔ eshishijee dalɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop early when the weather is too dry or when shade is lacking. Maintaining shade trees on your farm keeps the air humid and protects the tiny insects needed to pollinate the cocoa flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo hulutsoo be bɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ, ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe. ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo fɔfɔii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ

english: What causes small holes and ragged edges in the center leaf funnels of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing tip of the corn. Spraying neem leaf water or recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning catches them before they ruin the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaamɔ amɛ dani tso lɛ afite.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hottest part of the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting in wet soil usually points to root disease or bacterial wilt blocking water movement inside the stem. Rotating tomatoes with non-related crops like maize or cassava helps clean the soil of these hidden diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ shishifã hela loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Tsɔɔmɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsuɔ ​​shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects around them and cannot drain away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow off so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my crop soil dry out so fast just two days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sũ ni mikɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water quickly to hot sun and tropical winds. Covering the ground between crop rows with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket to trap water in the soil for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hewɔ. Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli koni ekɛha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be babaoo.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest yield much less grain this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many commercial hybrid seeds lose their vigor and high yields after the first generation. Buying certified fresh seed each planting season guarantees strong plants that resist disease and yield heavy harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii sɔrɔtoi babaoo lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ aná nɔmimaa.

english: Does letting wild weeds grow around my young cassava really reduce my yield?
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he Ani mi-cassava tsei lɛ baaha mi-cassava tsei lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like thief plants, stealing water, sunlight, and nutrients directly from young cassava roots. Clearing weeds during the first three months gives your cassava full access to soil food so it can build large tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha o-yucca lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee yitsei wuji.

english: Why do I see so many insects attacking my crops right after I prune them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikpa amɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you prune your crops, the fresh cuts and new growth attract pests. You need to spray appropriate pesticides right after pruning to protect the exposed, vulnerable plants from pest damage.
ga: Beni ofoɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nibii heei ni afolɔ mli kɛ nibii heei ni eda lɛ baagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ogbe ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni abu tsei ni egbɔjɔ kɛ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Should I feed my crops fertilizer right after I finish cutting back old branches?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahã ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo tsei niji momo lɛ?

english: Yes, after pruning, crops need extra nourishment to recover and build strong new shoots. Spraying liquid fertilizer onto the plants immediately after pruning gives them the fast nutrients they need to grow back healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, niyenii krokomɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛha amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii shwie tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ oya koni enyɛ eda ekoŋŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it risky to leave my farm unsprayed after I finish trimming the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ tsofa shwieee nɔ beni mifo tsei lɛ agbe naa lɛ?

english: Trimming creates open wounds on the plants that emit scents insects love. If you do not spray pest control right after trimming, pests will quickly invade and feed on the fragile leaves and stems.
ga: Tso lɛ nɔ ni afoɔ lɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbeleɔ naa lɛ baa tso lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni kooloi bibii sumɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieee nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ofo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ baatutua oya ni amɛyeɔ baai kɛ tsei ni waaa lɛ.

english: What sequence of care should I follow right after I finish pruning my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Immediately after pruning, you should first spray your crops to prevent pests from invading the fresh cuts, and then apply liquid fertilizer to nourish the plant for fast recovery.
ga: Beni ofo tso lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote tsei niji heei lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afata he koni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe wa oya.

english: Why do my crops get weak and diseased if I only prune them without taking further action?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛji mifolɔ amɛ ni mifeee nɔ ko dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning puts stress on the plant and leaves cut open stems. Without immediate spraying against pests and applying fertilizer water to feed them, pests will attack the weakened crops and stunt their growth.
ga: Tso lɛ he tsei ni afoɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni je kpo lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ni amɛbaahã amɛdalɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ niyenii.

english: It is best to apply liquid fertilizer early in the morning. Cool morning temperatures allow the plant to absorb the nutrients before the hot midday sun dries the water up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli leebi. He ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ leebi lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ haa nu lɛ gĩɔ.

english: I noticed my fertilizer water doesn't seem to work well when I spray it in the afternoon. Why is that?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-liquid fertilizer lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ afɔ nɔ shwane mli. Mɛni he je nɛ e ba jã a?

english: Afternoon heat causes liquid fertilizer to evaporate quickly before the plant leaves can absorb it. Applying or checking your liquid fertilizer early in the morning ensures the plant gets the full benefit.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani tsei ahe baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli loo akwɛ mli leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How does spraying fertilizer dissolved in water help my crops recover?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer water is absorbed quickly through leaves and fresh stems, giving plants instant access to moisture and nutrients needed to heal open cuts and push out new growth.
ga: Akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma nu lɛ tsɔɔ baai heei kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ oya. Ehaa tsei lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛtsa pilamɔi ni agbele lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ hee aba.

english: Do cut branches and fresh leaf buds really attract bugs to my farm?
ga: Ani tsei niji ni afolɔ kɛ baai heei lɛ gbalaa kooloi kɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, fresh cuts release sap and scents that attract harmful insects. This is why spraying pest control right after pruning is a crucial step to protect your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, loo ŋmɔŋ jieɔ mliki kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ ofo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni he hiaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do experienced extension officers advise me to check my liquid fertilizer application early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akwɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli leebi lɛ?

english: Early morning is when plant pores are open to take in food and liquid without the risk of sun scorch or evaporation. Checking early helps ensure your fertilizer water is absorbed properly.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji be mli ni tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni hulutsoo loo la ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ oshara mli. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni o-fertilizer nu lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and harsh winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that keeps the air humid and protects the leaves from burning until the trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii ewo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a clear sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for crop roots to absorb it. If applied to dry soil under a hot sun, the concentrated chemicals can burn and kill the plant roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Black pod is caused by a water mold that thrives in damp, shady conditions. When rains are heavy and bushes around the trees are overgrown, moisture gets trapped, allowing the disease to spread rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni jwɛi ni ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ, nugbɔ baamɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. As they feed, they weaken the leaf tissue and can spread viruses that cause the leaves to distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Amɛhaa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the plants experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough resources to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso lɛ haa anáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii koni akɛfee cob agbo ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging them all up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ amɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the stem base begins to crack from the swelling tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko edara kɛ́ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ yitso ni efuu lɛ mli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or cowpeas between rows of my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil for neighboring crops while also covering the ground to stop weeds from growing.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shwiemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating into the air, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant big trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally thrives under forest canopies. Shade trees protect sensitive cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, lower temperature stress, and retain soil moisture needed for strong growth.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa lɛ ahi shi.

english: Should I plant shade trees across my entire farm or just in some sections?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli loo efã ko kɛkɛ?

english: Shade trees need to be distributed evenly across the entire farm so that all cocoa plants receive equal protection from the sun and soil moisture remains consistent throughout the land.
ga: Ehe miihia ni aja tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu kookoo tsei fɛɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛ hulu la he. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Won't big shade trees steal water and nutrients away from my cocoa plants?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ejuŋ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: Recommended shade trees have deep root systems that collect water and nutrients from far underground, leaving topsoil nutrients for cocoa. Their fallen leaves also rot and enrich the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei ni ajieɔ yi akɛ amɛfee shade lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni buaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ kookoo Baai ni egbee shi lɛ hu fiteɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do shade trees help my cocoa during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Shade trees block direct sunlight and hot winds from reaching the soil, which slows down water evaporation and keeps the ground cool and moist even when rain is scarce.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How far apart should I space the shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafee tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees should be spaced widely apart—typically around 12 to 15 meters—so they form a loose overhead canopy that filters sunlight without completely blocking light or crowding cocoa plants.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ahi amɛhe shɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee mitai 12 kɛyashi 15 koni akɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ mlɛo. yɛ yiteŋ koni ekɛjie hulu la lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee nɔ ko fe nine loo ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee kookoo tsei lɛ.

english: Do young cocoa plants need more shade than older cocoa trees?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo babaoo fe kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Yes, young cocoa seedlings need heavier shade to survive the heat as their leaves burn easily, whereas mature cocoa trees need lighter, filtered sunlight to flower properly and produce pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulu la ni mli tse, ni ajieɔ lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: What happens if my cocoa farm has too much shade from trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ tsei babaoo ebɔle mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Excessive shade creates a cold, wet environment that promotes fungal diseases like black pod disease and reduces the amount of flowers and pods your cocoa trees produce.
ga: Shade babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela baa, ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni cacao tso lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune the shade trees as my cocoa grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi shade tsei lɛ amli be mli ni mi kokoo lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes heavy overhead branches to let sufficient light and air circulate through the farm, keeping fungal diseases away and allowing cocoa branches space to bloom.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo niji lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi

english: Can I plant any type of tree on my farm to shade my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tso srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha kookoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: No, some trees host cocoa pests or compete aggressively for water. It is best to select approved leguminous or permanent hardwood trees that fix nitrogen in the soil and support healthy cocoa.
ga: Dabi, tsei komɛi ji kookoo ŋmeii loo amɛyeɔ amɛhe akaŋ yɛ nu he. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala klover loo tso ni wa ni hiɔ shi daa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ saa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will planting shade trees reduce the total number of cocoa pods I harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni miduɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: When spaced correctly, shade trees actually increase long-term yield by protecting cocoa trees from heat burnout, allowing them to stay healthy and productive for many extra years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ sa Shade tsei lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii afii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves. It can also happen when too much water drowns the roots, keeping them from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii

english: Flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or improper fertilizer. To save its own life, the plant drops the flowers instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaaa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon but stand straight again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the ground, causing temporary wilting. Overnight, the plant catches up on drinking water and recovers its structure.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ gbɛkɛ kome mli lɛ, tso lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni anuɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe baawo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small, ragged holes appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni etse amɛhe lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kaabaji lɛ ahe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes are caused by farm pests like caterpillars or beetles chewing on the leaves. When leaf leaves are eaten, the crop loses its ability to capture sunlight and grow a big cabbage head.
ga: Buji ni etse lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai loo ŋmeii baa. Kɛ́ aye baai lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ dɔŋŋ, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ kaabe yitsei wuji.

english: When I am planting cassava stem cuttings, how do I tell which end goes up into the sky?
ga: Be ni akɛduɔ ŋmei niji Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole naagbee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised bumps on the stem where old leaves grew. The tiny leaf buds on those bumps must point upward toward the sky so the new green shoots can easily grow straight out.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmei bibioo lɛ. Yɛ tsei momo ni yɔɔ baai ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ. mlɛo

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to heat and burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller trees or plantains act as natural shade umbrellas that keep the young cocoa plants cool while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ loo plantain tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli jɔɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to be high up in the sunlight to produce enough energy to swell the big tuber underground. Keeping leaves off the wet ground also prevents rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ahi hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs wuji lɛ aya nɔ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai ahe helai anaa.

english: The small extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food away from the main stem. Trimming them off leaves enough food for the main stem to produce a single heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Kpãa amɛ sɛɛ koni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi tso titri lɛ ni ekɛbaawo plantains babaoo.

english: Why is it a bad idea to spread fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu lɛ ashwã dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away down the farm slope before root systems have time to absorb it. Fertilizer works best when applied to soil that is already moist after rain or during light drizzles.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds actually steal food from my crops and reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that drink up the water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. They also grow tall and block sunlight, leaving your crops weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛnuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaakwɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ hu ni amɛ naa hɔnɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibioo.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my vegetables instead of picking them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa aduawai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makpa amɛ mra tsɔ?

english: Crops show clear maturity signs like changing color, reaching a full firm size, or showing specific skin sheen. Picking too early reduces total crop weight and flavor, while picking at full maturity ensures your harvest gets maximum quality and weight.
ga: Tsei lɛ jieɔ dalɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ su tsakemɔ kɛ shifimɔ kpo. aloo ejieɔ hewolo ni kpɛɔ titri kpo Kɛ́ oookpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ amli tsiimɔ kɛ eŋɔli lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ baaye abua ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ onibii lɛ ashɛ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ muji ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do market buyers sometimes ask me to harvest my fruits while they are still green instead of fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ biɔ mi akɛ makpa aduawai lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo moŋ fe ni amɛkpamɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Buyers prefer crops like green tomatoes or peppers when they need to transport them over long distances to city markets. Green produce is firmer, resists bruising during transport, and ripens gradually on the journey.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato eŋɔli loo ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ gbɛ kakadaŋŋ miiya maŋtiase jarayeli hei lɛ, nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Eŋmɛɔ etsui shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛ lɛ majeɔ lɛ, ni ekwɛɔ fiofio yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I delay my harvest by a week or two?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ shwie ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving mature vegetables on the plant too long causes them to turn tough, woody, or rot. It also signals to the plant to stop producing new flowers, which reduces your total produce for the season.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi aduawai ni edara lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ais. Ani eji tso loo egbo? Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hu akɛ ekpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni obaafee yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it better for me to harvest my crops in the cool morning rather than during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli fe shwane lɛ?

english: Vegetables harvested in the cool morning hold internal moisture and are firm. Picking them in the afternoon heat leaves field heat inside the produce, causing them to wilt, soften, and spoil quickly before reaching the market.
ga: Aduawai ni akpaa yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Nibii ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛfiteɔ dani amɛshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Is it safe for my plants if I harvest ripe fruits from them every single week?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mitsei lɛ kɛji mikpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ amɛmli daa otsi?

english: Yes, for continuous-bearing crops like peppers, okra, and garden eggs, regular weekly harvesting encourages the plant to form new flowers and fruits continuously instead of putting its energy into aging seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii, okra kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ, otsi fɛɛ otsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei. be fɛɛ be Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔ lɛ,.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during hot afternoons even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the soil. Wilting is a natural defense to lower leaf exposure to the sun, and healthy plants usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he baajɔ amɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some fruits on the same branch ripen quickly while others stay green for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni yɔɔ tso nine kome nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fruits receive different amounts of direct sunlight, airflow, and plant nutrients depending on their position. Fruits on the outer or lower stems mature faster because they capture more sunlight and energy.
ga: Yibii lɛ naa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli yɛ yibɔi srɔtoi amli Edamɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ Yibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ kponɔ loo shishi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ejaakɛ emɔɔ hulu la kɛ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why are small green fruits falling off my plants before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso yibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ dani amɛshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit drop usually happens when plants face stress from irregular watering, poor soil nutrients, or excessive heat. The plant sheds extra fruits it cannot support so it can keep the rest of the plant alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo la ni mli edɔ fe nine Tso lɛ baawo yibii krokomɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ato tso lɛ fãi ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: What determines how many boxes of crops I can get from my field during the very first harvest?
ga: Mɛni tsɔɔ adekai enyiɛ ni maná kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Initial yield depends on your plant spacing, soil fertility, and early water supply. The first harvest is usually smaller because only the earliest flowers have set fruit, but yield increases as more branches mature.
ga: Shishijee yibiiwoo damɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo ejaakɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ pɛ woɔ yibii. Shi yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my farm in batches at different times instead of planting all my seeds on one day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔ lɛ mli kui yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ?

english: Staggering your planting dates allows your crops to mature in waves. This gives you a continuous weekly harvest over several months so you can sell fresh produce steadily rather than swamping the market all at once.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ ŋshɔkei amli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa otsi kpamɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oya nɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii heei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ jara lɛ nɔ obɔ shikome lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight. Planting them under temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava protects their delicate leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo yucca shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden sticks to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Koni okwɔ be mli ni aduɔ nii?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. The sunlight helps the plant make food, which is then stored underground to form big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ yam ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know which side of a cassava stem to plant into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ni esa akɛ odu o-cassava tso lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the raised leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down confuses the growth direction, delaying shoots and lowering root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ kɛ basabasafeemɔ baa yɛ gbɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I scrape off the outer roots and dark skin of plantain suckers before putting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-plantain tsei lɛ asɛɛ shishifãi kɛ amɛhewolo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Paring or peeling plantain suckers removes hidden pests like root nematodes and stem borer eggs, preventing you from introducing diseases into your clean farm field.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni ajieɔ loo ajieɔ amɛhe lɛ jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ hela akaba oŋmɔ lɛ he ni he tse lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant many seeds very close to each other in one hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes overcrowding, where plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. he ni tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle tip downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips that spread along the center indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and produce healthy, full cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating in hot weather, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer onto completely dry soil during a warm week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer applied to dry soil can scorch crop roots because it needs water to dissolve safely. Without soil moisture, plants cannot absorb the nutrients anyway.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ejaakɛ amɛbiɔ nu koni amɛshwie shi shweshweeshwe. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small green caterpillars keep eating the leaves inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the tender young leaves inside the center whorl of maize. Spotting them early allows for effective treatment before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha anyɛ atsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Why are some of my freshly planted cassava stems drying up and dying in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso ni midu ehee lɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly planted cassava stems need sufficient soil moisture and healthy buds to grow. Stems dry up and die if they are cut from old, diseased plants, planted upside down, or planted during a hot dry spell without enough soil moisture.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei tsei ni adu ehee lɛ aná shikpɔŋ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Tsoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ afo amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli, adu amɛ ŋwɛi, loo adu amɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: If some of my young crops die after planting, should I plant new ones in those same spots?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboi yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ hu? Ani esa akɛ madu tso hee yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, replanting or filling gaps is good practice to maximize your field space, but you must first fix whatever killed the original plant—such as soil pests or poor watering—so the new crop does not die as well.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni ooodu ekoŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni ooowo mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa ni baaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, esa akɛ osaa nɔ ni kɛ shishijee tso lɛ gbele baa lɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi loo nu ni ehiii. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ hu akagboi tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: How often should I go to check on my newly planted crops during the first few weeks?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli?

english: You should check your field at least two to three times a week early on. Regular monitoring helps you catch early signs of pest attacks, wilting, or weeds before your young crops die.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oyale lɛ mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli dani be lɛ ashɛ. Nibii amlipɛimɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ebatutua bo, amɛgboi loo jwɛi dani otsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and you can carefully dig around one root to check if it has grown fat enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ eko he nii koni ona kɛji amɛhe ejɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem is healthy enough to cut and plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afo ni adu?

english: Choose strong, thick stems from mature, healthy plants that show no holes from pests or signs of disease. The stem should have clear, undamaged buds along its length.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni wa, ni mli tse kɛjɛ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii loo helai okadii bɛ mli lɛ amli. Esa akɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ aná ŋmeii ni mli tse ni efiteee yɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ mli.

english: Can I leave my cassava roots in the soil after they mature, or will they spoil?
ga: Kɛ́ egbɔ lɛ, ani abaanyɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Aloo ebaagbo?

english: Cassava can safely stay in the ground for a few extra months, acting as natural storage. However, if left for too long, the roots will become hard, woody, and lose their starch content.
ga: Cassava baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji fioo krokomɛi, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohe. Shi, kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, amɛfeɔ tsei, ni amɛmli starch lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why does cassava grow well in one part of my farm but die or grow poorly in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi egboɔ loo edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kroko?

english: Soil quality changes across a single farm. Areas where water collects and creates muddy soil cause cassava roots to rot and die, while well-drained soil allows roots to breathe and expand.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Hei ni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa.

english: Why do my crops wilt and die even when there is enough rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi lɛ? Higbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Crops can wilt during rain if soil pests or microscopic worms (nematodes) are damaging the roots underground, preventing the plant from taking up water and food from the soil.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ agbo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji akɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. (Nematodes) lɛ miifite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Should I keep using traditional farming methods from my family or seek help from extension officers?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mikɛ kusum nifeemɔi ni kɔɔ weku okwaayeli he lɛ atsu nii loo matao yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Traditional methods provide useful local knowledge, but combining them with agricultural extension advice helps you handle new crop diseases, changing weather patterns, and modern planting techniques to get bigger yields.
ga: Kusum gbɛi haa maŋ lɛ mli nilee ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kɛ akɛ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ he ŋaawoi fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okwɛ tsei ahe helai heei anɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔ gbɛ̀i koni aná yibii babaoo.

english: Why does cocoa grow well in the southern region but struggle in drier areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Anaigbɛ lɛ? Shi yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ, naagbai yɛ?

english: Cocoa requires consistent rainfall, high humidity, and moist soil to thrive. Southern regions naturally provide these rainy conditions, whereas drier areas lack the constant moisture cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Cocoa taoɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, fɛ̃i babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni ekwɛ̃. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hei ni egbi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ni he hiaa cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why might a crop fail on one part of my land but grow well just by the roadside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miiyeee yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Soil depth, moisture levels, and sunlight can change within just a few meters on the same farm. Roadside areas often collect extra water runoff or have looser soil, making them better suited for certain crops.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ Humidity level Kɛ hulu la baanyɛ atsake yɛ mitai fioo komɛi pɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Bei pii lɛ, gbɛjegbɛi ahe hei lɛ yɛ nu krɛdɛɛ ko ni hoɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei komɛi.

english: How can I tell if my land has no prospect for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hegbɛ ni akɛduɔ kookoo?

english: If your soil is extremely dry, rocky, shallow, or has been heavily damaged by aggressive crops, cocoa seedlings will fail to establish roots and will wither easily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa, eyɛ tɛi, ekɔɔɔ he eko, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei efite lɛ waa. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ afee shishifãi ni amɛbaagboi oya.

english: Can growing certain cash crops ruin my soil for future farming?
ga: Ani shika ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, heavy-feeding cash crops can drain the soil of essential nutrients and moisture, leaving the land depleted and difficult for sensitive crops like cocoa to grow afterward.
ga: Hɛɛ, shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni ayeɔ niyenii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: How do I choose a cash crop that won't spoil my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteee mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You should pick crops suited to your specific soil type and rainfall, and practice crop rotation or intercropping to prevent any single crop from stripping all nutrients from the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ atsu nii koni ŋmɔshi nibii kome akajie niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What should I do if a previous crop has already ruined my land?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu tsutsu lɛ efite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You can restore depleted soil by allowing the land to lie fallow, adding compost or organic manure, and planting cover crops like legumes that naturally rebuild soil nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni oooshi lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. kɛ tsei ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does cocoa need to be planted in areas with a lot of water?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu kookoo yɛ hei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa needs naturally moist, well-drained soil to support its roots, but it should not be left in standing swamp water which can cause root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia kokoo koni enyɛ eye ebua eshishifãi lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ashiɔ yɛ ŋmei nu mli, ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How does taking a cutting from a plant help me grow new crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso ko mli ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ tsei heei?

english: Taking a cutting means using a stem or branch from a strong plant to grow a new root system, allowing you to create new crops without waiting for seeds to grow.
ga: Ni aaafolɔ tso lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aaaŋɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ko shishifã loo nine koni akɛfee shishifã hee. Ehaa onyɛɔ obɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni omɛɛɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I uproot a struggling crop and replant it elsewhere to save it?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie ŋmɔshi nibii ni miigbɔjɔ lɛ ni madu yɛ he kroko koni mikɛhere lɛ yiwala?

english: If a plant is young, uprooting it carefully and using it as a cutting or transplanting it to a location with better soil and water can help it recover.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo Kɛ́ ojie amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmeii loo okɛ amɛ aya he ko ni shikpɔŋ kɛ nu hi jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do some crops wither even after I uproot and replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwieɔ shi ni miduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Transplanting causes root shock, and if the new location lacks proper shade, water, or soil fertility, the plant will fail to recover and die.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kɛji akɛ he hee lɛ bɛ hulutsoo, nu, loo shikpɔŋ ni baa shi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsake ni ebaagbo.

english: If I cut down a large tree on my farm, will it completely die or can it grow back?
ga: Kɛ mifo tso agbo ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani tso lɛ baagbo loo ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: Some tree species do not die when cut down. Instead, their deep root systems remain alive in the soil and produce fresh new sprouts from the stump, allowing the tree to grow back naturally.
ga: Tsei komɛi gbooo kɛ́ afolɔ amɛ. Shi amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ha tsei akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe

english: What happens to old trees on my farm if I cut them back near the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo amɛ ekoŋŋ kɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cutting back old trees can rejuvenate them. It triggers dormant buds on the stump to push out strong, healthy new shoots, bringing fresh life to an aging plant.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tsei momo ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekanyaa ŋmeii ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, tsimɔ tsei heei ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa tsei ni egbɔ lɛ náa wala hee

english: Why do some plants produce fresh shoots after being chopped, while others just rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi shwieɔ ŋmeii heei beni afolɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Different plant species have different survival methods. Hardier trees store food energy in their roots, allowing them to push out new growth after being cut, while weaker plants lack these reserves and die.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso yɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ beni afo amɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: Should I dig out old tree stumps completely, or is it better to leave them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei akutsei momo lɛ fɛɛ mli loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cut stumps in the ground saves heavy labor and soil disturbance. If the tree species sprouts easily, the stump can quickly produce new wood, foliage, or shade without needing to plant new seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa nitsumɔ ni tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ haomɔ baa. Kɛji tso lɛ daa mlɛo lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baakwɛ̃ tso hee, baai, loo ŋmɔlɔ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu dumɔwui heei.

english: How can I encourage an overgrown tree on my farm to produce fresh green leaves again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Pruning or cutting back heavy, mature branches removes old growth and signals the tree to direct its energy into producing fast-growing, healthy new sprouts.
ga: Niji ni tsii ni eda lɛ ni afolɔ, loo ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ dalɛ momo lɛ ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee dumɔwui heei ni daa oya, ni he wa.

english: Is it possible for a cut tree to give me new shade without me planting new seedlings?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ tso ni afo lɛ baaha maná hulutsoo hee ni ehe ehiaaa ni madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, through natural regeneration, a cut stump can quickly grow multiple tall stems that mature into fresh branches, providing shade much faster than a newly planted seedling would.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ nɔ Tso ni afo lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ tsei kakadaji babaoo ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei niji heei. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why do older, traditional tree varieties seem to regrow so easily when cut back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni maŋ tsei ni edara lɛ daa ekoŋŋ oya kɛji afo amɛ lɛ?

english: Older local varieties usually have massive, mature root systems established deep in the soil, giving them abundant nutrient reserves to shoot back up vigorously after being cut.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni eda ni ta shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii babaoo ni haa amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ kɛ hewalɛ beni afo amɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is the main advantage of cutting a tree at its base instead of uprooting it?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tso ni afoɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ moŋ fe ni aaafo lɛ he?

english: Cutting at the base preserves the soil structure and leaves the existing root system intact, which allows new shoots to grow back rapidly using the existing roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ momo lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii heei daa oya kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ momo lɛ anɔ.

english: Will new sprouts coming from an old stump grow faster than a young seedling?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni jɛ tsei akui momo amli lɛ baadara oya fe tsei heei?

english: Yes, sprouts from a cut stump grow much faster because they feed off the large, pre-existing root network, whereas a seedling has to build its roots from scratch.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei bibii ni jɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ amli lɛ daa oya ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ shishifãi ni da momo lɛ amli niyenii. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ dumɔwui afee shishifãi kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: How can I tell if a tree on my land will sprout back up after I prune it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ mifo amɛ?

english: Most broadleaf hardwood trees and local shade trees in Ghana naturally sprout from cut trunks, whereas palm trees and conifers generally cannot regrow if their growing tip is cut off.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli wa kɛ umbrella tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei kɛ pine tsei nyɛŋ adara kɛji afo amɛnaa ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the old seeds saved by community elders sometimes grow better than the new ones from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui momo ni akutsoŋ onukpai kɛtoɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui heei ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Elder-saved seeds, often called local or heirloom seeds, have adapted to your local weather, rains, and soil over many years. While market seeds might produce more under perfect conditions, local seeds are usually tougher against local droughts and pests.
