ga: Dumɔwui ni onukpai lɛ to Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ maŋbii loo gboshinii dumɔwui. Ekɛ ehe ewo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ mli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni yeɔ emuu shishi moŋ, shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ fɔɔ hɔmɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the agriculture office instead of saving seeds from my own farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni obaabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from the agriculture office are specially bred to resist diseases and give higher yields. Seeds saved from your own farm naturally weaken over multiple seasons and can carry hidden crop diseases into the next planting.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ helai anaa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ bei ni hoɔ lɛ amli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aya dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why does a crop variety that grows very well in another region fail to produce food in my district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ wooo niyenii yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different districts have different soil types, rainfall patterns, and temperatures. A crop variety bred for a cool, rainy area will struggle to survive or bear fruit in a hotter, drier district with different soil.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa, kɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ha. Tsei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ amɛ kɛha hei ni mli ejɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi loo amɛwo yibii yɛ hei ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants make the soil better for my next crop like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. When the beans are harvested, this nitrogen stays in the ground, acting like natural fertilizer for crops planted next.
ga: Beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nitrogen nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested beans so small insects do not destroy them in the storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato koni kooloi bibii akafite amɛ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils love stored beans because they are dry and nutritious. You can protect them by using airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) or mixing clean, dry wood ash with the beans before sealing them tightly in containers.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛkpa ŋmeii ejaakɛ amɛgbi ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo tso mli sũ ni egbi ni he tse ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ baafutu mli dani okɛ amɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans and cassava together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting beans and cassava together uses land efficiently. Fast-growing beans cover the soil early to stop weeds and feed the ground, while the slow-growing cassava takes its time to branch out and form heavy roots.
ga: Beans kɛ cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ he ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Beans ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra. Bɔni afee ni akpa jwɛi ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ heɔ be dani ejɛɔ niji amli ni efeɔ shishifãi ni tsii.

english: Can I plant a piece of a cassava stem directly in the ground to grow a new crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni makwɛ tsei heei?

english: Yes, cassava does not grow from seeds; it grows directly from stem cuttings. When you cut a healthy, mature stem into pieces and plant them at an angle in moist soil, nodes on the stem grow roots and new shoots naturally.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei jɛɛɛ dumɔwui amli ekwɛɛɛ. Edaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ofo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara lɛ mli lɛ, No sɛɛ lɛ, odu yɛ koŋ ko nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nodes ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baakwɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Plants need direct sunlight to produce their own food. When shaded by big trees, crops stretch upward searching for light, making them grow tall, thin, and weak instead of producing thick foliage and strong fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ baai ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. When soil lacks this essential food, the plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left from its older bottom leaves to feed the young leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when soil becomes extremely dry, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Stress forces the plant to shed flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ lɛ Haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my tomatoes start rotting on the plant after I spray them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ beni mikɛ tsofa eshwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Spraying during hot daytime hours or using the wrong dosage can burn the fruit skin, creating wounds where fungal rot enters. Spraying early in the morning when plants are dry helps prevent moisture-loving rot from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo akɛ nɔ ni esaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ ashã. Enɛ haa pilamɔi baa he ni ŋmeii baanyɛ abote mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi be mli ni tsei lɛ egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying pest medicine before I can harvest my crops to sell?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ eshwie shi lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa onibii ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Every chemical has a safe waiting period called a Pre-Harvest Interval, usually printed on the bottle. Harvesting too soon leaves chemical residues on crops that make them spoil faster and can be unsafe for consumers.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛmɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ baa. Bei pii lɛ, akalaa enɛ yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni ehiii kɛha mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ.

english: Will chemical weedkiller damage my crops if a small amount gets on the main stems?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baafite miŋmɔshinii lɛ kɛji akɛ fioo ko yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ?

english: Non-selective herbicides will harm or kill any green plant tissue they touch, including crop stems. Using a protective spray shield on your nozzle ensures the spray only hits the weeds and keeps your crop safe.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ yeɔ tsei eŋɔli ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ awui loo amɛfiteɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni fata he ji tso lɛ shishifã. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsu nii yɛ nozzle lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofa lɛ tswaa jwɛi pɛ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up while still attached to the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air flow to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants and leaving behind small dirt-like powder?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tamɔ muji?

english: That is damage from Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the plant's central funnel. Applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning stops them before they ruin the young crop.
ga: No ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baawo ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi. Ekpaa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha lɛ mra moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass or mulch keeps the roots cool and holds water in the soil longer.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow before the cobs are grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Applying fertilizer like Urea at the right stage gives plants the energy needed to stay green and produce full cobs.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli, ni haa niyenii haa ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does my cassava have very large leaves on top but thin, weak tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji waa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Shi ani yitso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava put all its energy into growing top leaves instead of root tubers. Potassium-rich nutrients are needed instead to push energy underground so roots grow big and heavy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ baa lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ potassium he miihia koni akɛtsi hewalɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛtsii.

english: Is it better to apply all my fertilizer at planting time or spread it out over the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ awo mli yɛ dumɔ be mli loo madu yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer in split doses is much better because young roots cannot absorb all nutrients at once. Feeding the crop at key growth stages ensures constant nourishment without wasting fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli yɛ fãi amli lɛ hi kwraa ejaakɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ amɛdalɛ fãi titrii amli lɛ haa niyenii yaa nɔ ni amɛfiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested yam tubers from rotting in storage before taking them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sweet potato ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani mikɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Yams rot when they get bruised during harvest or are kept in hot, unventilated spaces. Storing undamaged yams on raised, shady bamboo racks allows cool air to circulate and prevents rot from setting in.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko to ŋmei adeka ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because full direct sunlight overheats their delicate leaves and quickly dries out the soil. Leaving large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from harsh heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛbaai bibii lɛ adɔ fe nine. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that produce tubers based on how much sunlight their leaves catch. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight, prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil, and leads to larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni feɔ bulbs ni damɔ hulu la ni baai lɛ náa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major nutrient maize uses to stay green and build energy. The plant pulls remaining nitrogen from its lower leaves to feed the upper growing parts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ehiɛ eŋɔli su lɛ mli ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Tso lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi fãi ni miida lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete against each other for soil nutrients, water, and light. They spend all their energy stretching upward to reach light instead of building strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli wa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la mli. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ tsei akutsei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in flat soil for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that cause the tubers to rot. Planting on raised mounds helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɛ tuber rot baa lɛ he hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass keep them green in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts as a protective blanket called mulch. It shades the soil from direct heat, reduces water evaporation, and keeps the soil cool and moist for the plant roots.
ga: Mulching ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni ale lɛ akɛ mulch. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot weather, strong winds, or inconsistent watering. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to save energy for survival rather than fruit production.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my groundnut plants push stalks into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi eshishifã lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their seeds underground. Once the flower above ground is pollinated, the plant extends a growth stem called a peg downwards into the dirt, where the groundnut pod actually grows and matures.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pegs lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bean pods lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaadara.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small plantain suckers to grow around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa dumɔwui bibii kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for water and soil food between the mother plant and young shoots. Cutting back extra suckers leaves energy for just one or two shoots, resulting in much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛdara babaoo lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa plantain tso ni da kwraa baa.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck sap from under the leaves, or by viruses carried by those insects, which distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa saplings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack sufficient water, shade, or pollinators like midges. Maintaining moderate shade and keeping the farm moist during dry spells helps flowers stay on the tree and develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu, hulutsoo loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ midge bɛ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why do my mango trees start flowering during the hot dry season when there is no rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mango trees use dry weather as a natural signal to produce flowers. Their long roots reach deep underground water sources, allowing them to bloom and set fruit even when the soil on top looks dry.
ga: Mango tsei kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli okadi ni haa amɛfɔ̃ɔ. Eshishifãi kakadaji lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi po.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects around them without proper drainage, encouraging fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch direct sunlight with their leaves. Sunlit leaves produce energy that feeds the plant, resulting in larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants finish growing, that nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the plant. Using neem leaf extracts or recommended insecticides controls these pests and stops leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem tso mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ekpa baa lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by 'blossom end rot,' which happens when the plant does not receive steady moisture to absorb calcium from the soil. Watering your crops regularly prevents this issue.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋwɛi diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa ji ‘Blossom tip rot’ ni baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni oooha otsei lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my garden egg plants dropping flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Garden eggs drop flowers when temperatures are too high or when there are not enough insects to move pollen between flowers. Keeping the soil moist and planting flowering weeds nearby attracts bees to pollinate your crop.
ga: Ajieɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛba koni amɛbawo onibii amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars suddenly eating up my whole maize field so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ye mi-ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ oya trukaa lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that multiplies quickly. They hide deep inside the leaves and feed aggressively day and night, so inspecting leaves early and applying approved pest treatments at dawn or dusk helps save your maize.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ nii waa shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra. Ni kɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, ebaahere o-abele lɛ yiwala.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crop leaves more heavily during early morning and late afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ waa yɛ leebi maŋkpa kɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Most crop pests avoid the burning heat of the mid-day sun to stay cool. They come out during the cooler hours to feed on your plant leaves, which is why checking or spraying your field early in the morning yields the best results.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛná kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛbaye otsei lɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo okɛ tsofa shwie nɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa lɛ.

english: When is the exact time my crops need fertilizer so they don't starve?
ga: Mɛɛ be mi tsei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ?

english: Crops need fertilizer most when they are growing rapidly and when they start forming flowers or fruit. Feeding them right after early weeding when the soil is moist gives them the nutrients required to produce strong stems and high yields.
ga: Tsei he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii fe fɛɛ be mli ni amɛmiida oya kɛ be mli ni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ loo amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ oha amɛ niyenii beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if I am giving my tomato plants too much food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiha niyenii fe nine?

english: If you give tomatoes too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow very thick, tall green leaves but produces very few flowers and fruit. Balancing fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium encourages fruiting instead of just leaf growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo ha o-tomato lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi ebaawo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium to o-fertilizer lɛ he lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ.

english: Why does my soil dry out and turn hard so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ewaa oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil left exposed under the strong heat loses water through direct evaporation. Adding compost, animal manure, or dry leaves (mulch) around the base of your crops holds moisture in the ground longer like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi lɛ baafite nu yɛ la ni hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔji, loo baai ni egbi (Mulch) fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my young cassava even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-babi cassava lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive wild roots that suck up water, light, and soil food much faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds early in the first three months gives your cassava enough space and sunlight to grow big enough to shade out future weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ náa he ko kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny ears when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɔɔ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other like hungry livestock for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Planting maize with proper spacing ensures every single stalk gets enough food to develop full, heavy corn ears.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaawuu tamɔ tsinai ni hulu la he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha abele toi ni tsii kwraa aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow and wilted leaves mean your crop is stressed, usually caused by heat, drought, root pests, or lack of nitrogen in the soil. Protecting the root area with mulch and providing water early in the day helps stress recovery.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, shishifãi amli kooloi, loo nitrogen ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi mra lɛ abuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ haomɔ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have small, soft roots that cannot draw enough water to balance what their leaves lose under direct hot sun. Planting them under fast-growing shade plants protects them until their roots grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai ni elaaje yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ afee ekome. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers under the ground are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When yam tubers finish storing energy underground, the leafy vines above the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up. This drying indicates the crop has stopped feeding and the tuber is ready to be dug up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni amɛto yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa lɛ, Above-ground vine tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa niyenii yeli ni ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are early signs of sickness or starvation. It usually means the crop lacks essential soil food like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji hela loo hɔmɔ he okadi mra. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: If I see just one sick plant in my field, why is it important to pull it out right away?
ga: Kɛji mina tso kome pɛ ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mitsi mihe kɛjɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crop diseases act like infectious sicknesses. Removing one infected plant early stops insects, wind, or rain from spreading the sickness to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Tsei ahe helai tsuɔ nii tamɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo nugbɔ akagbɛ hela kɛya hei krokomɛi. ni ji oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tight during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense behavior. The plant curls its leaves to shield itself from the scorching sun and save water so it does not dry up and die.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji subaŋ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛbu nu he. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ.

english: Should I wait to see bugs on my crop before taking action, or should I protect them early?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mana kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ dani mafee nɔ ko? Aloo esa akɛ wɔtsi enaa kɛjɛ shishijee?

english: It is much safer to protect crops early. Acting at the very first small sign prevents diseases from taking root, making it cheaper and easier to secure your harvest.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa akɛ ooobu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe mra. Okadii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akatswa shishifãi. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ jara waaa ni efeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot so fast during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and damp air give the black pod disease the perfect chance to grow. The fungus travels quickly through water drops on the stems and pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ haa black pod hela lɛ hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛdaraa. Fuŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do some farmers mix chemical powder with seeds before putting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsofai fɔji futuɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli dani amɛduɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Treating seeds acts like a medicine that protects the seed underground. It stops tiny soil bugs and diseases from attacking the seed before it can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔ tamɔ tsofa ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ baatutuaa dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do improved seed varieties perform better against plant sickness than seeds I save from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ahe helai atsimɔ mli fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred using crop science to fight off local plant diseases and endure dry weather, giving you stronger plants and higher yields.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilee etsu nii kɛkwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi helai ni baa tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ ni akɛdamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa. Ha tsei lɛ awa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my cassava rot in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When the soil stays full of standing water for too long, the roots choke, allowing rot diseases to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa ŋmeii tutuaa.

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress makes them stretch upward for light instead of putting energy into developing fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhe la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛwo yibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has become too weak to support healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Weak soil shows itself when crops grow slowly, stems remain thin, and leaves turn pale early. These signs mean the soil food has run out and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ jieɔ ehe kpo kɛ́ tsei dara blɛoo. Tso lɛ yibii lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni baai lɛ miiho oya. Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize shows it is ready when the leaves turn brown and dry, the husks turn straw-colored, and the kernels become hard with a black spot forming at the base of each grain.
ga: Akɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Ehewolo lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ jwɛi su. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni ŋmeii diji feɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Why do some fast-growing crops like cowpeas mature in three months while tree crops take years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni eheɔ afii babaoo dani tso ko kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are annual food crops designed to complete their life cycle quickly during short rainy seasons, while tree crops like cocoa or oil palm spend years growing strong trunks and deep root systems before producing fruits.
ga: Cowpea ji niyenii ni aduɔ daa afi ni afee koni egbe ewala shihilɛ naa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow and curling leaves on tomato plants are usually caused by heat stress, lack of water, or viruses spread by small sucking insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo, nu ni faaa, loo helai ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil gets too dry, temperatures become extremely high, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa waa. Aloo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ aduawai ni shwereɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do armyworms prefer to attack my maize plants when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target young maize because the tender leaves in the central funnel (whorl) are easy for caterpillars to eat and provide rich nourishment.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ kwɛɔ abifao ŋmãa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta (ring) lɛ mli lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaaye nii, ni amɛhaa amɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin plants with small tubers instead of big, heavy yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ náa yitsei bibii yɛ yibii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Beans and groundnuts gather nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil through their roots, naturally feeding the maize and improving soil fertility.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and look pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, leaving the crop starved of food and unable to make green chlorophyll.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee klorofil eŋɔli.

english: How does fertilizer make my yam crop produce bigger tubers underground?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii haa mi sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food like potassium and nitrogen that helps the yam plant produce green leaves to capture sunlight, which builds large, starch-filled tubers below the ground.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen jɛɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai eŋɔli ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii agboi ni eyi obɔ kɛ starch baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why will my harvested maize rot or grow mold if I store it right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikpa lɛ beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain trapped moisture; if you store them immediately without sun-drying, mold and fungi grow quickly in the warm, moist environment.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpɛtɛ amɛhe. Kɛ okɛto amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛwooo hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Mold kɛ mildew daa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to measure and leave specific spaces between my crops instead of just planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni mafee amɛ gbɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight underground for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing gives each plant enough personal space to grow big leaves, strong stems, and healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa wuji lɛ baa. tso ni mli wa kɛ aduawai ni hi kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ

english: Why do I need to keep my young cocoa seedlings under a shaded nursery before moving them out into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ toɔ hulutsoo shishi dani mikɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sun and harsh winds. The nursery shade protects them while they build strong stems and roots, preparing them for the open farm.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fiteɔ amɛ oya. He ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ hulutsoo buɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ tsei kɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ. Koni asaa amɛ kɛha ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with huge, broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the damp shade young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does growing groundnuts on my land help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a special ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the groundnuts are harvested, that extra nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛha o-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and rot when water stays around their stem for too long after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu hiɔ tsei lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need to breathe air in the soil just like humans need air. When soil stays flooded, water fills up all the air pockets, suffocating the roots and causing root rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lolo lɛ Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How do I know if the leaves on my cassava are turning yellow because of poor soil or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: Yellow leaves from poor soil usually affect the bottom, older leaves first as the plant moves nutrients to new leaves. Disease yellowing often forms strange spots, twisted shapes, or patches across both young and old leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ nɔ lɛ saa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ahe klɛŋklɛŋ be mli ni tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa baai heei amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baa ŋmɔŋ hela kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baa. shape ni etsake Aloo fãi komɛi yɛ. Yɛ baai bibii kɛ onukpai fɛɛ amli

english: Why do some of my crops grow very tall and skinny with few leaves when planted under large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni amɛhe feɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Plants need light to make food. When shaded by big trees, a crop stretches frantically upward to reach the sunlight, using up all its energy on height instead of growing thick stems or heavy fruits.
ga: La he miihia tsei koni amɛfee niyenii. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛyashɛɔ he ni hiŋmɛi baanyɛ ana koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, du tso yiblii nɛ mi wa aloo tso yiblii nɛ tsii.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my pepper plants while the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Pepper tsei be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Young pepper plants have short roots. Fast-growing weeds quickly steal the shallow groundwater and soil nutrients, effectively starving your pepper plants before they can establish.
ga: Chili tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye o-pepper tsei lɛ dani amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my cassava stems at the start of the rains instead of during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stems need consistent soil moisture to sprout roots and fresh buds. Planting in the dry season causes the wood stem to dry out and die before it gets a chance to grow.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ ni ŋmeii lɛ afee ehee. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why should I cut off dead or excess branches from my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming dead or extra branches prevents diseases from spreading and stops the tree from wasting food energy on useless stems. This directs all energy toward producing bigger flowers and fruit.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ eshwa, ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai wuji aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and dry up when there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy of shade that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching sun and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of green leaves, but end up with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ebatsɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or if plants are shaded, the cassava puts most of its energy into growing stem and leaf tissue above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ amli fãji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden sticks to yield good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei aniji anɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground using stakes exposes maximum leaf surface to sunlight. Sunlight allows the plant to manufacture the food energy needed to fill out and enlarge the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso ko wo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ nibii ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a sign of insect pests like whiteflies, thrips, or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or transmitting a plant virus that distorts normal leaf formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ. loo egbɛɔ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ afeemɔ ni sa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the stem during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus. Excess shade, high humidity, and rain droplets splashing soil onto lower pods help spread the fungus quickly across the pod surfaces.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu mli baa Hulu la ni fa babaoo, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do I find ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark drops inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing tip of the maize stalk during the day and leaves behind its waste inside the whorl.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oshi jwɛi yɛ kooyigbɛ

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and sunken before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato fruit cannot pull enough calcium from the soil during rapid growth, usually triggered by irregular watering or sudden dry spells.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni baa beni tomato yibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips down the middle, even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant pulls stored nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed newer leaves, causing the older ones to pale.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ baai wuji lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei lɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in neat rows rather than scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo mli moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding, while making weeding, fertilizer application, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the dry topsoil without deep soaking. If hot sun returns for several days after, the shallow moisture evaporates completely and roasts the germinating seeds before roots can go down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ pɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba gbii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Ebaatsɔ la kwraa ni ebaashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with tiny beneficial organisms in the ground to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil like free natural fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛmɔ nitrogen ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during wet, shady weather. Clearing weeds, trimming shade branches to let light in, and removing infected pods helps keep the air dry around the tree and stops the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. weeding Niji ni afolɔ koni la atsɔ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ebaaye ebua kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Tso lɛ gĩɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this virus from destroying your yield.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛshɛ amɛbaa lɛ he koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Koni hela akatswa tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crop plants as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal water, sunlight, and plant food away from your crops, leaving your young plants weak, thin, and unable to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe feɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is my heavy plantain tree falling over before the fruit bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akutsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, so a heavy bunch of fruit can easily pull the entire stem down, especially in strong wind. Supporting the stem with a sturdy wooden fork holds the weight until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai ni tsii baanyɛ agbala tso lɛ shishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi mlɛo. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa. Kɛ akɛ tso ni mli wa tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛfi muji lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops droop or roll up during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po?

english: Rolling or drooping leaves is a crop's natural way of saving water. By exposing less leaf surface to the direct sun, the plant stops moisture from evaporating too quickly, and leaves usually bounce back when evening cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Tso lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya tsɔ lɛ naa. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji amɛhe jɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without forming fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress the tomato plant, causing flowers to dry out and drop off before pollination can happen. Mulching the soil and regular morning watering help keep the roots cool and save the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out small and hard like wood when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe wa tamɔ tso kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become small and woody if they are planted in hard, compact soil, left in the ground too long past maturity, or grown in poor soil without enough nutrients to expand the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. Shi amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara tsɔ. aloo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy packaged improved maize seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo kotoku mli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Packaged improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller ears and weaker plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ awo adeka mli lɛ woɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa toi bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides a cool canopy that protects fragile cocoa leaves from burning during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites. Spraying early with neem oil or soapy water controls these pests before they stunt your crop's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo samla nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Abaanyɛ akudɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ dani amɛtsi ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall bushy leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into top leafy growth rather than root formation. Roots require balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, to swell into large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishifãi lɛ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. titri lɛ potassium ni ekɛbaatsɔ yitso agbo

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when nutrients are low. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extremely hot periods helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to catch more sunlight to make food, while keeping them away from damp soil diseases, ultimately resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhooɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has become tired and lost its natural nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli ejɔ ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu efo mli?

english: Tired soil becomes hard, loses its rich dark color, and fails to hold water well. Crops planted in tired soil remain stunted, have pale leaves, and yield far less fruit than in previous seasons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni wa. ehiɛ su ni tsuɔ waa ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo, amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe be ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are easily weakened by microscopic soil worms called nematodes. Treating the soil and propping up heavy trees with wooden poles prevents them from blowing down in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oookwɛ ni okɛ tsei ni tsii awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa amɛ.

english: Why do my tiny vegetable seeds rot in the soil when I plant them directly in the open field during early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii dumɔwui Ani minɔ lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small seeds are delicate and can drown or wash away in heavy rain. Starting them in a sheltered nursery bed gives them time to develop strong root systems before you transplant them into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nu mli loo eho amɛ kɛya. Kɛ́ oje amɛ shishi yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatso ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛ be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa dani okɛ amɛ aya saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are mature enough to be cut for planting material?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ mli kɛfee dumɔ nii?

english: Cassava stems are mature enough for planting when the plant is around 8 to 12 months old, and the main stem has turned woody and brown, showing strong buds along the stem.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ daraa kɛha dumɔ beni tsei lɛ eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyɛ fɔfɔii ni mli wa yɛ tso lɛ he fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I cut my plantain bunch off the tree while the fingers are still thin and flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ plantains fã ko kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni miniji lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Cutting plantain bunches too early prevents the fruits from filling out completely, resulting in smaller, lighter plantains that fetch lower prices in the market.
ga: Kɛ́ afo plantain lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ amɛdalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jara ni baa shi fe jara nɔ lɛ

english: Why are some of my maize stalks growing tall with big cobs while others nearby stay short and produce tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida ni amɛtoi lɛ dara lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ bei pii lɛ amɛfeɔ kukuji ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Maize grows unevenly when soil nutrients or moisture are not evenly spread across the farm, or when seeds are planted too close together, forcing shorter plants to compete for sunlight.
ga: Abɛi daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji akɛ ajaaa sũ mli niyenii loo ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. aloo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ kukuji lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow into small or misshapen sizes instead of long, thick yams?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛhe esaaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yams become small or misshapen when the soil mound is too hard or shallow, preventing the tuber from expanding freely, or when the soil lacks sufficient nutrients.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eshɛɛɛ tsɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ eshwa ehe. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Yellow and curled cassava leaves are typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and by using infected planting cuttings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛtsɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods can even start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ebaabɔi shweremɔ po.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers during severe heat or drought to save water, or as a result of insect damage from pests like mirids (capsids).
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ loo nu egbiɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. aloo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ amli baa.

english: Does the size and thickness of the cassava cutting I plant affect how big my tubers will grow?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ emli ŋmɔlɔ saa bɔ ni mi-tubers lɛ baadara aha lɛ he?

english: Yes, thick stem cuttings from mature plants store more energy, allowing the young plant to grow stronger roots and produce larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii náa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to the size of my crops if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which leads to weak stems and small fruit sizes.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ena niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni no haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ aduawai bibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look light green or yellow instead of deep dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ moŋ fe eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pale green or yellow leaves are a sign that the crop is short on nitrogen, an important food element that helps plants build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to trim off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach all parts of the tree, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod and directs energy into forming larger pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ feɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand intense direct sunlight. They require temporary shade plants, such as plantains, to shield their delicate leaves while their root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off the dead lower branches of my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ niji ni egboi lɛ?

english: Removing dead leaves allows more sunlight and airflow around the tree stem, prevents pests from hiding, and makes harvesting fruit bunches much easier.
ga: Baai ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo bɔleɔ tso lɛ he, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ akatee amɛhe. Ni ehaa aduawai akutsei lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very thin and woody even after waiting a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tso yɛ be mli ni mimɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell into large tubers if planted too close together or in poor, nutrient-depleted soil lacking potassium and phosphorus.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwereŋ ni amɛtsɔ bulbs wuji kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli ni potassium kɛ phosphorus bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ niji afata he koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Staking yam vines spreads the leaves out to catch more sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to swell the tuber underground.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ baagbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã koni hulu la babaoo aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like waste inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baa mli ni ŋmãa yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing whorl of young maize plants.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my lowland rice seedlings turning yellowish-bronze in flooded fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ miitsɔ akɔɔble ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Stagnant, poorly drained water can cause iron buildup in the soil, which damages root health and turns the leaves bronze.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha dade abua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ akɔɔble su.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often resulting from irregular or uneven watering.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping all their flowers without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that encourages leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni haa baai yeɔ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ hao amɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting groundnuts on the same land where maize grew last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu ŋmei yɛ afi ni ho lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring fertility for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Plantains have shallow roots. Allowing too many sucker shoots to grow around one plant weakens its root hold in the soil.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Tso kome pɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha eshishifãi lɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves high off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to grow bigger underground tubers, while also preventing fungal diseases from soil contact.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Beans and cowpeas trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or during dry spells because extreme heat or lack of water prevents the flower from successfully pollinating.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the plant stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, ni obaanyɛ ona kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil, effectively starving your plants during their critical early growing phase.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a viral infection spread by flies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize foliage so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite mi-abele baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the central funnel of maize plants where birds cannot reach them, eating constantly during cool hours and multiplying rapidly.
ga: Fall worms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli he ni okpoi nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Amɛyeɔ niyenii be fɛɛ be yɛ gbɛkɛ mli ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb water before the sun causes heavy evaporation, and keeps leaves dry at night to reduce plant diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ haa hulutsoo ni naa wa baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ gbɛkɛ koni tsei ahe helai aba shi

english: Can I grow vegetables like peppers and tomatoes inside old flour sacks or plastic containers behind my house?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato yɛ ashikishaŋ kotoku momo mli loo plastic tsinsii ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, growing vegetables in sacks or containers works very well. It allows you to control the soil quality, save water, and move your plants away from excessive sun or flooding, making it ideal for small spaces or backyard farming.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui loo tsɛnsii amli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, okɛ nu toɔ, ni ojieɔ otsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni fa fe nine loo nu afua he. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei bibii loo sɛɛgbɛ okwaayeli.

english: Why do my tomato plants die when I leave them sitting in flooded water inside containers after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ gboi beni mishi amɛ ni amɛtara nu ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu yɛ tsɛnsi mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air just like they need water. When water stays trapped in a container, it drowns the roots and causes them to rot, so you must always poke drainage holes at the bottom of containers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu tsɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni eha amɛgboi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be.

english: How does drip irrigation help my crops survive during hot, dry spells?
