ga: Te nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ be ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Drip irrigation drops water directly at the root of each plant slowly and steadily. This prevents water from evaporating in the heat and ensures the plant stays hydrated using very little water.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu shwieɔ tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ blɛoo ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtsɔ nu fioo pɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly into cups during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops the plant from losing too much moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with dark green leaves but fail to produce flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: This usually happens when plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer. Nitrogen builds strong leaves and stems, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to produce flowers and healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nitrogen lɛ feɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When crops lack nitrogen in the soil, they move the remaining nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to feed the young growing top leaves, causing the bottom ones to yellow and die.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is ready for harvest in a few months for quick food and income, while cassava grows slowly underneath and is harvested later, giving you continuous food security from one plot.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli kɛha niyenii kɛ shika oya. Beni ŋmei daa fiofio yɛ shishi ni akpaa sɛɛ mli lɛ. Niyenii ni yaa nɔ ni akɛhaa bo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mikɛ he ko akafite?

english: When planted too close, crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes them grow weak and thin, producing smaller yields than properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe tsei ni aduɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither and die immediately after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by damaged roots and sudden exposure to strong sunlight. Moving seedlings late in the afternoon and watering them right away helps them survive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ni efite kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa trukaa. Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui lɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds now that the rainy season is so hard to predict?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Ejaakɛ ewa akɛ aaatsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Instead of relying on fixed calendar dates, wait until the ground receives a thorough soaking rain that wet the soil deep enough so seeds have reliable moisture to germinate.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ gbii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ kalanda lɛ nɔ lɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ anɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ waa bɔ ni sa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is pollination, and why do my crops need it to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mitsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pollination is how plants reproduce. It happens when pollen moves from one flower to another—usually carried by wind or insects like bees. Without pollination, flowers dry up and fall off without ever turning into fruits or seeds.
ga: Pollination ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii. Ebaa kɛji pollen ŋmeii lɛ je fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ enɛ yaa kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Why do bees and other insects flock to the flowers on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Insects visit flowers to feed on sweet nectar. As they move around, tiny grains of pollen stick to their bodies and get transferred between flowers, which fertilizes the plant so it can form healthy fruits.
ga: Kplukai yasaraa fɔfɔi koni amɛye nu ni mli tse. Beni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛbɔleɔ pollen ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe lɛ Ekpɛtɛɔ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ ahe ni etsɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops sometimes drop their flowers before any fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, extreme heat, or poor soil nutrients, or when insects fail to pollinate the flowers in time.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Can wind alone help my crops make fruit, or do I always need insects?
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ pɛ yeɔ ebuaa midumɔ nii lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii. Aloo ŋmeii he miihia mi be fɛɛ be?

english: It depends on the crop. Crops like maize rely on the wind to blow pollen from the tassels to the silks, while crops like cocoa, peppers, and cucumbers rely heavily on insects to carry pollen.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ejie pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛya siliki lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kukumba kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi anɔ waa koni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does the same crop yield very well in one area but struggle in a neighboring district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ he kome shi enaa amanehulu yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Even nearby areas can have different soil types, water retention, shade, and micro-climates. Crops thrive best where the soil nutrients, rainfall, and sunlight match their specific growth needs.
ga: Ekolɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po yɛ sũ henɔi srɔtoi. Nu ni ahiɔ mli, shade kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo baanyɛ aba mli. Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ hulu la kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ hiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why do my plants near the dusty roadside grow slower than those inside the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ he ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ daa blɛoo fe ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ?

english: Dust coating the leaves acts like a blanket, blocking sunlight. Plants need sunlight on their leaves to make food, so dusty leaves mean the plant starves and grows slowly.
ga: Mulu ni hà baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Tsei taoɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Baai ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni ebaada blɛoo.

english: Why do some of my crops only produce flowers during specific months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi pɛ amli lɛ?

english: Many crops react to seasonal changes in rainfall, temperature, or daylight length. These environmental triggers signal to the plant that it is the right time to flower and reproduce.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ be tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, dɔlɛ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ he nii. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ mli nibii nɛɛ haa tsei leɔ akɛ be ni sa ji ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Why do some of my crops produce small, deformed fruits while others grow big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miiwo yibii bibii ni ehiii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Deformed or small fruits often result from incomplete pollination, where only part of the flower received pollen, or from a lack of sufficient water and nutrients while the fruit was developing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibii ni efite loo bibii lɛ jɛɔ pollination ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ mli baa. he ni fɔfɔi lɛ fã ko pɛ nine shɛɔ pollen nɔ loo kɛjɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ mli.

english: Why does my produce spoil so quickly when I travel long distances to sell it in other towns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mifã gbɛ kakadaŋŋ koni miyahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested produce continues to breathe and generate heat. When packed tightly in bags or crates during hot transport, heat builds up fast, causing fruits and vegetables to soften and rot.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Kɛ akɛwo kotokui loo adekai amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛfaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa oya, ni ehaa aduawai kɛ aduawai feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How does harvesting my crops too early affect their quality by the time I reach the market?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ baaná amɛnɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛshɛ jara nɔ?

english: If harvested before full maturity, fruits haven't stored enough sugars and moisture from the main plant. They will shrivel, fail to ripen evenly, and taste poor to buyers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa dani eda lɛ Yibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ sugar kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. amɛbaagbi Ahooo amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is a major food for plants, or that the soil is waterlogged and choking the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage will help them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo okɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak plants that produce much smaller harvests than plants given proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmaa bibii kwraa fe tsei ni aha amɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees keep shedding their flowers before forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ dani ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, prolonged dry spells, or sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids). Maintaining partial shade trees and protecting the cocoa from pests allows the flowers to turn into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids). Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he hulutsoo be fioo ko, ni abu kookoo he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap and transmitting viruses. Controlling these pests early using neem oil or recommended sprays keeps the foliage flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when heavy rains leave stagnant water around the roots, creating conditions for soil fungi to attack. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my mature plantain plants fall over easily when strong winds hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer grubs often weaken them underground. Mounding fresh soil around the base of the plant and supporting heavy fruiting stems with wooden props helps prevent them from falling.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ hee ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ Akɛ tsei ahe nibii fiɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eshishifãi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei akagbee shi.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots in the barn long before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams break their natural resting phase when exposed to heat and moisture in storage, signaling to the tuber that it is time to sprout. Storing yams in a well-ventilated, shaded, and cool barn slows down this sprouting process.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i mli yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli, ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why are the small tomatoes falling off my plants before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato bibii miiho kɛmiijɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed young fruits when soil moisture fluctuates wildly—such as heavy rain after a hot dry period—or during extreme heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching helps the plant hold onto its fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake waa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be ko ni mli edɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. aloo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ Sũ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii.

english: Weed seeds live deep in the soil for years and germinate rapidly as soon as clearing exposes them to sunlight. Covering cleared soil with dead grass or leaves (mulch) blocks light from reaching the soil surface and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ hulu la shɛ amɛhe pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi baawo mli. (Mulch) baatsi la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaatsi jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right week to plant my seeds now that the rainfall patterns are changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male otsi ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui amrɔ nɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔi etsake lɛ?

english: Instead of planting on fixed calendar dates, wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply for two or three consecutive days. Planting in moist soil ensures seeds germinate quickly and build strong roots to withstand short dry breaks.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa koni amɛdamɔ be kukuoo mli nugbɔshiimɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for plant growth, or they are getting too much water in the soil. Adding proper fertilizer or rich compost can help turn them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ loo nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by very small pests like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the plant juices, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Clearing surrounding weeds and applying appropriate organic or chemical sprays can control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the edges of my crop leaves turn brown and burnt after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer behaves like strong salt; if it touches the plant directly or if the soil is too dry during application, it draws moisture out of the leaves and roots, causing burn marks.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋoo ni mli edɔ. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ tsei kpe tɛ̃ɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ shwiemɔ teŋ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shishifãi amli, ni ekɛ shãa baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they face stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks like mirids. The tree saves its energy to survive instead of using it to grow fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli haomɔ mli. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɛi tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔi. Tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Plantain trees fall over when microscopic worms in the soil, called nematodes, destroy the root system under the ground. Without strong roots to anchor it, the heavy plant cannot support itself against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kpata shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni fiɔ esɛɛ Tsei ni tsii po nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long without draining away, it chokes the roots and encourages mold and fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ ŋmɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up the soil without giving it enough lasting moisture. Seeds need steady wetness for several days in a row to sprout; otherwise, the hot dry ground burns the seed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa. Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli ejɔ daa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. They waste energy growing tall to reach light instead of using energy to grow big fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, amɛyeɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛdara bɔni afee ni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai wuji lɛ

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often because the ground keeps switching between being too dry and too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunshine on their leaves to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and helps them catch maximum light.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo baa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers need pollination before they can produce pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ awo mli dani amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers must have pollen transferred from one part to another to make seeds and fruit. Without proper pollination, the flowers cannot form pods and will simply dry up and fall off the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ fɔfɔii aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ he kome kɛya he kroko koni amɛfee dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pods. ni ebaagbi ni ebaagbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my trees without ever turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off mainly because they were not pollinated by insects or human hands in time. When a flower goes unfertilized, the tree sheds it to conserve energy and nutrients.
ga: Nɔ titri ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ji akɛ, kooloi loo adesai kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ fɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: What is the best time of day for flowers on my trees to be pollinated?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mitsei lɛ amli?

english: Early morning is the best time because flowers usually open at night or early dawn and are freshest in the cool morning hours, making pollen transfer most successful.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ fɔfɔi fɔɔ fɔmɔ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa. Ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fe fɛɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa pollination yeɔ omanye fe fɛɛ.

english: What is hand pollination, and why are extension workers encouraging me to do it?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi hewalɛ koni mafee enɛ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination means using a small brush or tool to move pollen between flowers yourself instead of waiting for natural insects. It guarantees that a higher percentage of flowers successfully turn into pods, greatly increasing your harvest.
ga: Nine nɔ pollination tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko tsuɔ nii. koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaamɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii lɛ Ayɛ nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi ni fa fe oha mlijaa 100 lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Ehaa nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why should I hire trained young people to assist with hand pollination on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛye amɛbua kɛ nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hand pollination requires good eyesight, patience, and quick hands to work with tiny flower parts. Young people trained in the technique can cover many trees quickly, ensuring maximum pod development.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ biɔ hiŋmɛi kpakpa, tsuishitoo kɛ oyaiyeli ni akɛtsuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi bibii ahe nii. Oblahii kɛ oblayei ni atsɔse amɛ yɛ ŋaa nɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei babaoo ahe oya. Enɛ haa pod lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo.

english: Is paying for extra labor to hand-pollinate my trees actually worth the investment?
ga: Ani nitsumɔ kroko ni awoɔ koni akɛ niji awo mi tsei lɛ amli lɛ sa shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, because hand pollination can increase your harvest by 50 percent or more on the same plot of land. The income from the extra pods you harvest easily covers the cost of hiring labor.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oha mlijaa 50 loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ pods krokomɛi ni okpaa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu onitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ he nii oya.

english: How can I produce much more yield without spending money to buy more land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo yibii babaoo ni mikɛ shika heee shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: You can get more yields from small land by making sure every existing tree produces at its full capacity using techniques like hand pollination, proper pruning, and good soil nutrition.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná shika babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ kɛtsɔ nɔmimaa ni ooona akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋaai tamɔ nine-pollination nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ

english: Can a single cocoa tree really produce more pods than it naturally does right now?
ga: Ani cacao tso kome baanyɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, standard trees usually produce far below their limit because insects miss many flowers. Assisting the trees with hand pollination ensures almost every healthy flower turns into a harvestable pod.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa fe amɛhusui lɛ ejaakɛ kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa tsei kɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni wa lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: What happens to my crop harvest if there are not enough wild insects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ koo mli kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When insect numbers are low, fewer flowers get visited, which leads to a poor harvest. Doing manual pollination helps protect your yield even when natural insects are scarce.
ga: Beni kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi ni abaayasara lɛ baafee fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii. Self-pollination yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛji akɛ ewa akɛ aaana adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii po.

english: How long after a flower is pollinated can I expect to harvest the mature pod?
ga: Be enyiɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ yɛ pollination sɛɛ?

english: Once a flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about 5 to 6 months for the tiny pod to grow, ripen, and become ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani fɔfɔi bibii lɛ daraa, amɛshwereɔ, ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up, even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: When leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow. The plant moves whatever green food it has left to its top new leaves, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Tso lɛ baajie niyenii eŋɔli ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Shi shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of big green leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: This happens when the soil has too much leafy food (like nitrogen) and not enough root food (like potassium). The plant spends all its energy building a big bush on top instead of sending that energy down to fatten the cassava roots.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ baai amli niyenii babaoo (tamɔ nitrogen) ni shishifãi amli niyenii (tamɔ potassium) faaa. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa jwɛi agbo ko yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a tsuɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ kasava sisi ɔ nɛ hi.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize in neat rows instead of scattering the seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in rows leaves clear pathways so crops do not fight each other for sunlight and soil food. It also makes it much faster and easier for one person to walk through, remove weeds, and apply fertilizer without stepping on the plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etswaaa akaŋ. Ehaa efeɔ oya ni efeɔ mlɛo hu kɛhaa mɔ kome akɛ ebaatsɔ mli, ekɛ jwɛi awo mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni ekɛ enaji efɔɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the earth on my farm turn hard like dry clay so quickly whenever the sun comes out for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ waɔ oya tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi be fɛɛ be ni hulu lɛ baaje kpo gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses its water fast when the sun hits it directly. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulch) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and stops the sun from baking the dirt hard.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya kɛ́ hulu lɛ tswa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe Mulch (mulch) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa hulu lɛ haaa muji lɛ mli awa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from the farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like babies; their leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool canopy of shade that protects them until their bark and leaves become strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tso bibioo tamɔ abifao. Baai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni ajieɔ tsei kakadaji loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ebaaha hulutsoo aba. No yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally built to survive harsh soil conditions and steal water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them while they are still tiny prevents them from drinking up the plant food meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkanu tsei niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off to the ground without turning into any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or sudden changes in water levels. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save its own life rather than using energy to grow fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu lɛ mli tsakemɔi trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ ko lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do my tomato plants need to be tied to wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tomato tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaaha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting tomato plants off the ground keeps their leaves and fruits away from damp soil bugs and fungal rot. It also allows air to blow through the plant so it stays dry and healthy.
ga: Tomato tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Koni tso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my stored yams start growing sprouts and getting soft after keeping them in the barn for just a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni efee blɛoo beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli be kukuoo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that wake up and try to grow new plants when they feel heat and light. Storing them off the ground in a well-ventilated, shady barn keeps them cool and asleep so they stay firm longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji bulbs ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ tsei heei kɛji amɛnu dɔlɛ kɛ la he. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛwɔ. Enɛ baaha amɛnu he akɛ amɛhiɛ kã shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my plantain shoots produce big bunches while others right next to them stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi feɔ kui wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: A main plantain tree shares its food with all the young shoots growing around its base. If you do not cut away the extra shoots (suckers) to leave just one or two strong ones, the mother plant gets exhausted and produces small bunches.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jaa niyenii. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ (ŋmeii) lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashwɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he baajɔ ni ebaagbala mli ewo kui bibii amli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean tiny insects called whiteflies are spreading Cassava Mosaic Disease. Planting healthy, disease-resistant stem cuttings helps protect your field from this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ miigbɛ yucca mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwã. Niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ he.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day. Checking inside the plant leaves early allows you to spot and destroy them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei ahe baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ onaa amɛ ni okpãtãa amɛhiɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without producing big corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants have to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper distance allows it to grow a thick stalk and large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get dry and hard so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ewaa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic material like decayed leaves or manure, which normally acts like a sponge to hold water. Adding a layer of dry grasses or leaves on top of the soil helps trap moisture for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, while groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating these crops keeps the soil fertile for future plantings without relying only on expensive fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yaa nɔ eshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Dani abaadu aduawai?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden dry hot weather or uneven watering. Watering the roots consistently helps the plant retain its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong growth only in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in smaller, weaker plants and much lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yams rot quickly if they were cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are stored in a hot place without fresh air flow. Storing uninjured tubers on raised slatted racks in a cool, shaded barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni pilaaa lɛ to shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ ni akɛ tsei ewula nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for years waiting for sunlight and rain to hit them. When you clear bare ground, you give those seeds sunlight to sprout; covering the soil with crops or mulch blocks the light and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ hulu kɛ nugbɔ ni anɛ amɛ. Kɛji ojie he ni agbele lɛ Obaahã nakai dumɔwui lɛ hulu la ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow big leaves, so adding organic manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help fix this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa baai wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick stems, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of roots below. Cassava needs balanced nutrients, especially potassium, to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi. Niyenii ni ja he miihia cassava. titri lɛ potassium ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the soil dries out completely. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, so keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ he haomɔ baanyɛ atsĩ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Cocoa pods show they are mature by changing color. Green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods change to an orange-yellow color. Harvesting right when the color changes ensures the seeds inside ferment properly for good quality beans.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara kɛtsɔ amɛhe su ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni su lɛ tsake lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into a cup shape and stopping green growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miiho amɛhe amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni amɛmiikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies that feed on the soft underside of young leaves. It can also be the plant's response to severe heat, so inspecting under leaves and providing adequate water helps control it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ebaanyɛ efee bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli hu. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing in the young leaves of my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's central leaves. Catching them early by inspecting the growing center of the plant allows you to apply recommended treatments before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miitao niyenii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ mlipɛimɔ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava too close to my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ?

english: Cassava develops wide roots and big leaves that quickly shade out nearby crops and steal water and nutrients. Giving both plants proper spacing prevents them from competing, allowing your maize to get full sunlight to make large cobs.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye amɛhe akaŋ. Okɛ o-abele lɛ awo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my plantain crop take so long to produce fruit when I leave all the shoot stems growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mishiɔ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When too many plantain suckers grow around one parent plant, they all fight for the same water, light, and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to leave only two or three healthy shoots gives the main plant enough energy to fruit faster.
ga: Beni plantain tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛ kome tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni eshi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii oya.

english: Why are my groundnut seeds taking so long to sprout after planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds need loose, warm, and moist soil to germinate easily. If planted too deep or in dry, compacted soil, the tender shoots cannot push through the surface, while overly wet soil can cause the seeds to rot before sprouting.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli edɔ, ni efɔ koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji akɛ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the vines and leaves of my yam plants drying up and turning brown near the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ beni be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam leaves turning brown and drying at the end of the growing season is a natural process showing that the plant has finished its lifecycle. The plant transfers all remaining energy into the tuber underground, signaling that your yams are mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ naagbee lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ewala shihilɛ naa. Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Aloo akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them in heavy soil without draining, or when underground pests bite the roots and let water-loving fungal diseases inside.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ŋmɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshi hydrophilic fungal helai yɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by too much heat, dry weather, or when tiny pests like mirids bite the delicate flowers before they can form fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine hao amɛ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves, so staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into full sunlight where they can get maximum energy to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni fata staking he ji ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Biɛ ji he ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkɛfee yitsei wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the wind blows hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep in the ground, so when heavy bunches of fruit grow at the top, strong winds can easily push the heavy top over unless supported with wooden forks.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ beni aduawai babaoo teɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi ni tsii lɛ nɔ oya. ja tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and twisting tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a virus from plant to plant, or by extreme hot and dry weather causing the plant to curl its leaves to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ mli Ha tsei atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture free nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and helps the neighboring maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do weeds come back so quickly after clearing, while my planted crops take long to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ be mli ni midumɔi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Wild weeds have tough, deep roots and seeds already waiting in the soil that can survive harsh weather, allowing them to steal water and sun before your domestic crop seeds settle in.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni miimɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛju nu kɛ hulu la dani shia dumɔwui lɛ atswa shishifãi.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for me to plant my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until rain has soaked deep into the ground at least two or three times so the soil holds enough steady moisture to feed the seed until it shoots roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaawo shishifãi.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the main funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ agbɛi titrii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which are caterpillars that hatch from tiny eggs laid by moths directly inside the hidden tender leaves of young maize plants where it is safe for them to feed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni amɛtee ni amɛye nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient they need to grow strong and green. Adding animal manure, compost, or the right fertilizer early in the growing season provides this nourishment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa koni gbɔmɔtso lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔshi nii. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii nɛɛ aha.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans put natural food back into the soil that heavy-feeding crops like maize take away. Rotating them keeps your land fertile so you harvest better crops without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ mli. Rotation haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is very strong and can burn the tender stem and roots if touched directly. Placing it a few inches away in a small ring lets the plant's roots reach out and safely soak up the nutrients.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ shishifãi kɛji ekɛ ehe kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli He ni kɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping larger shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from severe heat until they are strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kookoo tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛfee wuji loo dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ he kome Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ ahe waa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off before growing into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or sap-sucking insects. Giving them regular water and keeping insects away helps the plant retain flowers so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ na tso lɛ he amanehulu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi adɛŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no haa efeɔ tomato.

english: The very first rainfall often heats up dry soil without providing enough steady moisture for seeds to fully grow. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the ground stays damp enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa dumɔwui lɛ daa. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots under the ground are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the plant is 9 to 12 months old, its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ daa kɛji tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12. Eshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit buried in the dirt waiting for light and rain. When you clear the land, you expose those seeds to sunlight, causing them to sprout fast. Planting your crops quickly or covering the ground helps block weed growth.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛmiimɛ la kɛ nugbɔ. Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, hulu la baashɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya Dumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them handle hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the harsh sun, keeps rainwater from evaporating too fast, and keeps root zones cool.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that loves hiding in the funnel of young maize plants. Checking your farm weekly and spraying organic neem oil or recommended control solutions into the funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi ni okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ afɔ hoppers lɛ anɔ. Kpa nakai ŋmɔji lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Should I burn the weeds and dry grass on my farm before planting, or leave them on the land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Burning might seem fast, but leaving cleared weeds to rot naturally creates organic manure, protects soil moisture, and prevents the sun from baking your land hard.
ga: Ekolɛ ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni shãa oya. Shi kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni otsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise against burning land before planting when many elders used to do it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akashã shikpɔŋ dani adu nii lɛ? Beni onukpai babaoo feɔ lɛ?

english: Soils today are much more exhausted than in the past. Fire kills beneficial earthworms and destroys topsoil nutrients, making it harder for crops to yield well without expensive fertilizers.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ. La gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa bɛ mli.

english: What can I do with the heavy bush I cut down if I do not burn it?
ga: Mɛni mafee kɛ jwɛi ni tsii ni mifoɔ lɛ kɛji mishãaa amɛ?

english: You can pile the cut bush in neat lines between crop rows or around farm edges. Over time, it breaks down into natural compost that enriches your soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ato tsei lɛ ateŋ loo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: I am a new farmer clearing land for the first time; is clearing without fire better for my crop roots?
ga: Okwaafonyo hee ji mi ni miikpa shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Ani ŋmɔ ni la bɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, clearing without fire leaves the soil soft and rich in organic material, which allows young crop roots to spread deep easily and absorb water during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni la bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ahi mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shɔŋŋ oya ni amɛmɔɔ nu yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry out faster during hot spells when I burn all the trash off my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, beni mishãa jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning leaves the bare soil exposed directly to the harsh sun, causing water to evaporate quickly. Unburnt plant materials act as a shade blanket that retains moisture in the ground.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya Tsei ni ashãko lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How does leaving plant residues on my farm stop heavy rain from destroying my soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Plant residues cushion the force of falling rain, preventing the water from washing away the rich topsoil and leaving behind hard, unproductive ground.
ga: Nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. ni amɛshi hei ni wa ni wooo yibii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Will leaving unburnt weeds on my farm make the soil too hard for seed germination?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ashãko lɛ ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃?

english: No, unburnt weeds decay and attract soil insects like earthworms that burrow through the earth, making the soil loose, soft, and easy for new seedlings to break through.
ga: Dabi, jwɛi ni ashãaa lɛ fiteɔ ni egbalaa sũ mli kooloi bibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ bu lɛ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efeɔ blɛoo ni ewaaa akɛ dumɔwui heei baanyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Farming without burning is very hard work; how can I manage land clearing without exhausting myself?
ga: Okwaayeli ni shãaa lɛ ji nitsumɔ ni wa waa. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ajie shikpɔŋ ni nijiaŋ ejeee wui?

english: You can clear your land in smaller sections bit by bit, or use cover crops that naturally suppress weeds so you don't have to clear heavy bush every season.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fãi bibii amli yɛ be kome mli loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbeɔ jwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ atsu nii. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni ojie jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ kɛjɛ mli daa be.

english: As a beginner, is it better to focus on one small farm or try to plant across multiple plots of land?
ga: Kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ agbala jwɛŋmɔ kɛya ŋmɔji bibii anɔ. he kome pɛ Aloo kaa ni odu yɛ shikpɔji babaoo nɔ, ani no baafee nɔ ni hi?

english: It is best to start with one small plot that you can manage well, weed properly, and feed natural compost to before taking on larger or multiple farm lands.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko aje shishi. Nɔ pɛ ni obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni aha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu ŋmɔji wuji loo ŋmɔji babaoo.

english: How can I cut down on the labor needed to clear my farm every farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛjie miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa okwaayeli be lɛ nɔ?

english: Practicing zero-burning and leaving plant cover keeps the soil shaded, which stops new weed seeds from receiving sunlight and growing back quickly.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ zero burn ni oshi tsei akɛ mulch koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa jwɛi dumɔwui heei lɛ akashɛ hulu la he ni amɛdara oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the corn regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin without making big cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɛɛ ŋmeii wuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close, the plants spend all their energy fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow thick stems and develop large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwuu amɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ekɛtee mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: Those caterpillars are commonly fall armyworms, which feed on tender young leaves. Identifying them early allows you to use neem oil sprays or targeted treatments to protect the plant before it loses its growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbeeɔ asraafoi ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii, bibii amli. Amɛyoomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu tso lɛ he dani eshishifãi ni miida lɛ afite.

english: Why is it important for me to heap soil into high mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo sũ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ dani madu ŋmeii?

english: High mounds create loose, soft soil that allows the yam tuber to expand easily beneath the ground while preventing standing water from soaking and rotting the yam.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift and support my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the growing tuber, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akashɛ ohe.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small when I leave tall weeds growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa beni mishiɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and fertilizer away from your yam vines. Clearing the weeds ensures all available nutrients go directly into growing a larger tuber.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ o-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but after pollination, the plant pushes a special stem into the soil so the pods can safely form and mature underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ tso krɛdɛɛ ko kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve the soil for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer that feeds the crop planted in that field next season.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: You can check by lifting just two or three plants in different parts of the farm; if the inside of the pods has turned a dark brownish color and the leaves begin to yellow, the crop is mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni ooowó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔtɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do the broad leaves of my plantain trees split into strips during heavy winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ fãi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their veins to let strong winds pass through easily without tearing down the entire leaf or snapping the main stem of the tree.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ahe fãji lɛ amli bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ nɔ oya ni egbalaŋ baai lɛ loo efoŋ tso lɛ shishitoo titri lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves and grow green. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the ground too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni amɛkwɛ̃ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui bibii fioo pɛ?

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen in the soil, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of flowering. Cowpeas fix their own nitrogen naturally, so adding heavy fertilizers reduces pod production.
ga: Kɛji cowpea tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ahe tsei amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas saa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha pod ni ajieɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Blackened cocoa pods are caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in damp, heavy shade with high humidity. Pruning overgrown shade trees lets air and sunlight in to dry out the farm and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni edɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be, hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that transmit viruses. When these pests feed on young shoots, the plant leaves wrinkle up and growth becomes stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye tsei bibii lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: Why do my stored dried maize cobs get full of tiny holes and powdery dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Those holes and dust are caused by grain weevils and borers that eat into the dry seeds. If maize is not dried completely before storage or stored in airtight containers, insect eggs hatch and destroy the harvest.
ga: Nakai bu kɛ sũ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baafɔ ni ebaafite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do tomato flowers keep falling off my plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from very dry to soaked. Severe weather stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ashi efɔfɔi lɛ koni ebu ehe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil during long rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When wet ground stays flooded for many days, oxygen gets trapped out, allowing rotting fungi to attack the soft roots underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ jɛmɛ edɔ lɛ, nu afua baa gbii babaoo. Oxygen lɛ efo mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing kernels and empty gaps on the cob during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni bɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs plenty of water right when it produces silks and pollen. If drought strikes during this stage, the silks dry out before pollen can fertilize them, leaving empty spots on the cob.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa beni ekɛ siliki kɛ pollen baa lɛ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Siliki lɛ gĩɔ dani pollen lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ fɔmɔ kotoku. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ko baa yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: How come my plantain trees easily fall over when strong rain winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the top surface of the ground. When heavy rain softens the soil, weak or shallow root networks lose their grip and get pulled out easily by wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ amɛhe, ni kɔɔyɔɔ gbalaa amɛ oya.

english: Why do my yam plants produce very small tubers when I plant them on flat ground without soil mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gɔŋ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand easily as they grow deep underground. Planting on raised soil mounds breaks up hard ground so the tubers can swell larger without meeting hard dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo beni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ adara ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli wa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for the roots to expand into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore green leaf color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpea or beans help make my soil better for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When the crop season ends, this leftover nitrogen enriches the soil naturally for demanding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni dumɔ be lɛ baa naagbee Nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, prevents weeds from growing, and breaks down into natural plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, maximizing sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Extra suckers steal water and soil nutrients away from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantains babaoo ni tsii waa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather is too hot or when the plant doesn't get consistent water. Regular watering keeps the stems strong enough to hold onto flowers until they turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi waɔ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ emɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Afternoon heat causes water to evaporate into the air before plant roots can drink it. Morning watering lets plants absorb moisture deeply and stay hydrated through the heat of the day.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my maize plants during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which thrive in warm conditions and prefer feeding on tender center leaves of young maize. Checking your crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides prevents major yield loss.
