ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa bibii ni ji ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut down my cocoa tree if only a few leaves look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ cacao tso ko kɛji akɛ baai fioo komɛi pɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot travel through the tree's internal sap and root network. Cutting down an infected tree completely is the only reliable way to stop the virus from spreading through the soil or insects to your surrounding healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ shikpɔŋ loo kooloi bibii anɔ kɛya kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I spray chemical medicine to cure a cocoa tree that has swollen stems?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ anɔ?

english: Currently, there is no chemical spray that can cure viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot once a tree is infected. The only effective treatment is removing the affected tree and planting improved, disease-resistant cocoa varieties.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni baanyɛ atsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa, tamɔ kookoo ni fũuɔ kɛji tsei amli hela lɛ bɛ. Tsofafeemɔ pɛ ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ji ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni adu kookoo henɔi ni asaa amɛhe, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How do crop diseases spread from one cocoa farm to another nearby farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli?

english: Tiny insects like mealybugs carry the virus on their bodies from infected trees to healthy ones. Wind, shared farming tools, and physical contact between overlapping tree branches can also spread diseases across farms.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ mealybugs hiɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ, okwaayeli nibii ni ajaa. Ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ nifeemɔ ni ka tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbala helai ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How long will it take for my farm to yield pods again if I clear sick trees and replant?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe ni miŋmɔ lɛ baawo pods ekoŋŋ kɛji mijie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni midu eheei?

english: With modern hybrid cocoa varieties, replanted trees can begin flowering and bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years, provided they receive adequate shade, water, and weed management during their early growth.
ga: kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi Tsei ni adu ehee lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná hulutsoo, nu kɛ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Is it safe to plant fresh cocoa seedlings directly on land where sick trees were just cut down?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Before replanting, you must remove all infected roots and stumps from the ground, allow the field to rest, or plant temporary shade crops like plantains to ensure the virus and pests have died out completely.
ga: dani ooodu ekoŋŋ Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi kɛ tsei akutsei fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha he ko ahi shi. Aloo dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ agbe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kwraa.

english: What are the early signs that my cocoa tree is getting infected by a disease?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ emɔ hela?

english: Look out for red or yellow band patterns along the leaf veins, swollen branches or roots, abnormally shaped pods, and premature yellowing of leaves. Noticing these early helps you take quick action.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe. Niji loo shishifãi ni efuu Pods ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli kɛ kaadii ni tsuɔ nii oya Nibii nɛɛ akadimɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ofee nɔ ko oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa from harsh heat while preserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Are new cocoa seedlings from extension officers stronger than the old trees planted by my parents?
ga: Ani kookoo dumɔwui heei ni jɛ extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ mli wa fe kookoo tsei momo ni ofɔlɔi du lɛ?

english: Yes, newly developed hybrid cocoa varieties are specifically bred to mature faster, produce higher yields, and tolerate common diseases better than older, traditional tree varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse kookoo henɔi heei ni afee lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya. Haa yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ fe blema tsei srɔtoi ni etsɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa trees recover quickly after a bad season while others die off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ahe waaa oya yɛ be ni ehiii mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Trees with deep, healthy root systems, good shade cover, and nutrient-rich soil can withstand stress and disease better. Weaker trees in poor soil succumb quickly to pests and dry weather.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Ayɛ shade kpakpa ni akɛhaa nɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɔ eshiɔ nɔnyɛɛ kɛ helai babaoo. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ baagboi oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ adɛŋ.

english: What should I do with the wood and branches from diseased cocoa trees after cutting them down?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee beni afo kokoo tsei kɛ amɛniji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Diseased branches and stems should be gathered and burned or dried completely away from your healthy trees so that pests like mealybugs living on the wood do not crawl back to healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ abua tsei niji kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa ni ashã loo agbi kwraa kɛjɛ otso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɔ tsei anɔ lɛ akaku amɛsɛɛ amɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they are exposed to direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sun and lose moisture faster than their small roots can absorb it. Planting quick-growing shade crops like plantain next to them provides a cool umbrella that keeps the air moist and shields the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ aŋɔ awo mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shade ni mli ejɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves folding up and turning brown during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ efolɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmatta be ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally fold their large leaves during dry wind conditions to reduce water loss through evaporation. When leaf edges turn brown, the plant is conserving its remaining moisture in its central stem and underground corm to survive until the rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai wuji lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tso lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ etsitsi teŋgbɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli koni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and build leaves. Rainwater often washes nitrogen deep past root levels, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi yɛ eŋɔli ni amɛwo baai. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the legume plants are harvested and their roots decompose, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural plant food for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Nakai nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmãa, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow bushy leaves everywhere while the tubers underneath stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai akui yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ be mli ni anaigbɛ bulb lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil tricks sweet potato plants into spending all their energy growing stems and leafy vines instead of storing energy underground. Reducing nitrogen and ensuring the soil has enough potassium encourages the plant to swell its roots into larger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ lakaa sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai kɛ wain tsei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ potassium ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers onto the ground without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulch and providing light shade helps the plant retain its blossoms long enough for bees or wind to pollinate them into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akɛ muji kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ afee aduawai lɛ amli fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my growing tomatoes get dark, sunken spots on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miida lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni ebote shishi lɛ?

english: Dark spots on tomato bottoms, known as blossom-end rot, happen when plants cannot absorb enough calcium due to dry spells or irregular watering. Maintaining consistent soil moisture helps the roots continuously draw calcium from the soil into developing fruit tissues.
ga: Hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛya nɔ amɛwo aduawai amli fãji.

english: Yam tubers encounter hard, compacted soil or rocks beneath the surface that their soft growing tips cannot push through. Building deep, loose soil mounds or ridges gives the tubers room to expand smoothly downward without obstruction.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ kpeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa yitso he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting if I leave them in the ground after heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills up all air spaces underground, suffocating mature cassava roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply rapidly. Harvesting mature cassava right at the onset of heavy rains prevents root loss and preserves tuber quality.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni eda kwraa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya. Kasava ni eda ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tuber lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops immediately after the August rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ August nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil for long periods and are adapted to sprout rapidly at the first sign of moisture to steal sunlight and nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your main crops do not get starved of water and light.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ mli koni amɛju hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ náaa nu kɛ la.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: You should wait until the rain wets the soil deep enough—about the length of your hand—for a few days in a row. Planting after just one light drizzle is risky because the dry soil underneath will quickly dry out your seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ aahu kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ—aaafee onine kɛlɛ—gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi oya.

english: What will happen to my seeds if I plant them in dry soil and the rain delays for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni mikɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo otsii enyɔ?

english: Seeds need water to awaken and grow. If they stay in hot, dry soil too long, ants and birds might eat them, or heat can spoil them inside the earth, meaning you will have to buy new seeds and plant again.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. Kɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Ants kɛ okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ. Aloo latsaa lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I clear and plow my land before the rains begin or wait until after the first rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu nii yɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi loo mamɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to clear and plow your land just before the main rains start. This opens up the soil so that when the first rain falls, the ground easily drinks the water and becomes soft for planting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni otsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ. Egbeleɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni anuɔ oya ni efee blɛoo kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural defense mechanism. When it is too hot and water is low, the plant rolls its leaves tightly to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun so it loses less moisture.
ga: Baai ni etsiɔ amɛhe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni no haa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like humans do. When water covers your field for too long, the roots drown because they cannot breathe, which stops them from taking up plant food and causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nu ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Enɛ haaa amɛye tsei aniyenii, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Can sudden heavy rain right after planting destroy my farm?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ?

english: Yes, very heavy downpours can wash away light seeds, bury small seeds too deeply under heavy mud, or wash away the fertile topsoil that young crops need to sprout.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo ŋmaa bibii lɛ, ni efu dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Eshɛɔ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi tsɔ loo ejie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for rain before applying chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛmɛ nugbɔ dani akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is like dry food that needs water to dissolve. If you apply it on dry soil, the plant cannot drink it, and the sun or heat can burn the roots or waste the expensive fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii ni egbi ni he hiaa nu koni etsɔ mli. Kɛji okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu. Ni hulu la loo dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ loo afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: If the rain in my area is becoming unpredictable, what type of crop seeds should I buy from the agro-shop?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mahe yɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli?

english: You should ask the agro-dealer for 'early-maturing' or 'drought-tolerant' seed varieties. These crops grow quickly and yield well even if the rainy season ends earlier than expected.
ga: Esa akɛ obi okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ‘shwereɔ oya’ loo ‘ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa’ lɛ ahe sane. Tsei nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ po.

english: How can I keep my soil moist so my crops do not suffer when the rain stops for a week?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii akapiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, a practice called mulching. This blanket shields the dirt from the scorching sun, keeping moisture trapped near the crop roots longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ atade nɛɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ muji kɛ muji ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild and tough, so their roots absorb rainwater and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing the water your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbeyei ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: If I take over a piece of land that has been left unused for a long time, how do I know if the soil is still good for planting?
ga: Kɛji miŋɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi lolo kɛha dumɔ nii?

english: Unused land often regains nutrients naturally through fallowing, but weeds and soil compaction can be an issue. You can check soil health by looking at soil color, moisture retention, and testing the soil texture before planting fast-growing crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ mli. Shi jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afee naagba. Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ha kɛtsɔ ehiɛ su ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kaa dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their first two years.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: My crop yield keeps decreasing every season; how can I bring nutrients back to my worn-out soil?
ga: Mi nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo mishikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore exhausted soil by adding organic compost, poultry manure, or planting nitrogen-fixing leguminous cover crops like cowpeas or mucuna, which naturally nourish the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kooloi aŋmɔji, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ cowpeas loo mucilage ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or poor drainage causing waterlogging around the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How long should I leave my farm land to rest before planting on it again?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani madu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Leaving farmland to rest or fallow for 2 to 3 years allows natural wild vegetation to decay and replenish vital organic matter and nutrients back into the topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ koni ejɔɔ ehe loo ehi shi afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ baaha koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ akumɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How can I protect my vegetable crops from insects without spending money on expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can practice crop rotation, plant strong-smelling herbs like marigolds nearby to repel insects, or prepare a natural spray made from boiled neem tree leaves and water.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ akase nii. Dumɔ tsofai ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa tamɔ marigolds yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo koni okɛshwie kooloi bibii, loo saa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛ neem baai kɛ nu ni ahoo fee lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot dry weather is a plant's natural defense to reduce water loss. Covering the soil around the roots with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps trap moisture and lower heat stress.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: What is the best way to clean and store my knapsack sprayer so it does not spoil between farming seasons?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsumɔ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ he ni akɛtoɔ? Bɔni afee ni ekafite yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli.

english: Rinse the tank thoroughly with clean water after every use, pump water through the hose to clear chemical residues, and dry it completely before storing it under shade away from direct sunlight.
ga: Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tanki lɛ he jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be. Pɔmpɔ nu kɛtsɔ hose nɔ koni ojie tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ. ni otsumɔ he kwraa dani okɛto hulutsoo be mli. Kaaha hulu la lɛ miishɛ onɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it better to plant only maize on my farm or mix it with cowpeas on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmãa pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo okɛ tsina ŋmãa afutu mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Planting maize together with cowpeas is beneficial because cowpeas fix nitrogen into the soil to help feed the maize, while growing two crops reduces your risk if one fails.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ tsina ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aha niyenii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafee nɔ ni ehiii lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from strong sun and heat; without tall shade trees or companion crops like plantains, the harsh sunlight burns them.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo nanemɛi tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã nakai tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava on mounds loosens the soil so the roots can easily expand into large tubers, while allowing excess rainwater to drain away so the roots do not rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee bulbs agboi oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer to grow green leaves, or heavy rains have flooded the soil and starved the roots of air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ akwɛ̃. Aloo nugbɔ miinɛ waa, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni haaa kɔɔyɔɔ aná shishifãi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or damage from microscopic insects like thrips feeding on the blossom buds.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ efite amɛ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during extreme heat to shrink their surface area, which helps the plant reduce water loss until the air cools down.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni eha ŋwɛi he lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How can I prevent wandering cattle from destroying my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsinai ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can plant live fences made of thick, thorny bushes like acacia or jatropha around your field boundaries to naturally block cattle while marking your land.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ gbogbo ni hiɛ ka ni akɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ akasia loo jatropha fee lɛ abɔle ŋmɔ husui lɛ ahe koni ekɛtsi tsinai anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni okadiɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Yam vines climb to lift their leaves higher into the sunlight, which helps the plant capture energy and send it underground to form large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for nearby crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously in the same field drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover, while allowing crop pests to build up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa.

english: Why do my stored grains spoil quickly when I put them in bags right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain internal moisture; if they are not thoroughly sun-dried before storage, mold and insects will multiply rapidly in the trapped dampness.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Mold kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on tomato plants often mean the plant is stressed by a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen, improper watering, or early damage from sap-sucking insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni esaaa ni akɛhaa lɛ hewɔ. loo mra be mli ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot, when soil moisture swings between too dry and too wet, or when there are not enough insects or wind to pollinate them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ teŋ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing thin and woody instead of big and full of starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin and woody when the soil is hard and tightly packed, or when the soil lacks potassium, which the plant relies on to swell its roots with energy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ awo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: If your crop leaves looked light green or yellow in the last harvest, grew very slowly, or produced thin stalks, the soil has lost key nutrients and needs manure, compost, or fertilizer to restore its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli, amɛdara blɛoo waa, loo amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii titrii lɛ elaaje ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: It is best to plant maize after two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the soil, ensuring the topsoil stays moist long enough for seeds to sprout without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii 2-3 ni yaa nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi waa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mifo jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds naturally lie hidden in the ground for long periods and react instantly to moisture and sunlight, whereas crop seeds take more time to build strong root systems before growing rapidly above ground.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsuɔ ​​he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo kɛ hulu la yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ be dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa shishi dani amɛdaraa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the leaves of my pepper plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome

english: Night-active pests such as beetles, caterpillars, or snails come out in the cool evening to chew tender leaves, which can be managed by checking fields at dusk or applying organic neem sprays.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kooloi tamɔ ladybugs, caterpillars loo ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni amɛbaye baai bibii. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli kwɛmɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli. Aloo okɛ neem spray ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why is it harmful to pour water directly over the leaves of my vegetables instead of at the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni oooshwie shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Wetting leaves directly keeps them wet for long periods, creating an ideal damp environment for fungal diseases and leaf rot to spread, whereas watering the soil base feeds the roots safely.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi baai lɛ ni efɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa saplings turn brown and burn when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight and need temporary shade from fast-growing companion crops like plantains to protect their tender leaves until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do some of the seeds I saved from last year fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm, humid places lose their internal energy over time, so only seeds dried well and kept in cool, sealed containers remain strong enough to germinate properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni mli edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ baafite amɛmli hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsinsii ni mli ejɔ ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ pɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants to cover them, sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ Hulu la lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna nu.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food, which is stored in the tuber underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the wet soil, preventing leave rot and maximizing sunlight exposure for bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ bulb wuji lɛ ahe babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. When nitrogen is low, the plant starves and pulls remaining food from older leaves at the bottom to feed new green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni ebaagbala niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eha gbɛ aha baai eŋɔli heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, prolonged dry soil, or too much chemical nitrogen. The plant drops its blossoms to save water and energy so the main plant can stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ. aloo tsofa ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: What happens to my maize seeds underground if the rains stop for two weeks right after I sow them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If the seeds haven't germinated yet, they will lie dormant in the dry dirt until water returns. However, if they have just started sprouting, dry soil for two weeks will kill the fragile new root, requiring you to replant.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛko lolo lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã shi kɛkɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyashi nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Shi, kɛji akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛŋ Shikpɔŋ ni hiɔ shi ni egbiɔ otsii enyɔ lɛ baagbe shishifãi heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. ni haa okɛ ohe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and split during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbalaɔ yɛ harmattan ni agbiɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are large and lose water quickly. During the dry, windy harmattan, the leaves split naturally to stop dry winds from tearing the whole stalk, and outer leaves turn yellow as the plant conserves water inside its main stem.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ akagbala tso lɛ shishi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm result in much smaller cassava roots when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients directly out of the ground before your crop can get them. When cassava has to compete with weeds, it gets less food, resulting in thin, small roots instead of large, heavy ones.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Beni esa akɛ ŋmei kɛ jwɛi abɔ akaŋ lɛ Enine shɛ niyenii fioo nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or by a virus transmitted by insects. As insects suck out plant juices, the leaves distort, curl up, and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo virus ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛji kooloi bibii miinu tsei nu lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove extra young shoot stems growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Every young shoot sucks food and water away from the main trunk. By cutting back extra shoots and leaving only one strong sucker, you ensure all soil nutrients go into producing one large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibioo fɛɛ tso bibii shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ŋmeii kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ. Obaanyɛ oná nɔmimaa akɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha plantains ŋmɔji wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: How do I know my cassava crop is fully mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the leaves at the bottom naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a mostly bare stem, and the soil right around the base of the main stem begins to crack upward from growing tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ edaa kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Enɛ ha tsɔne lɛ mli fã ko nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni adu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly on the hilly parts of my land compared to the flat areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni gɔji yɔɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: When heavy rain falls, it washes away the fertile topsoil and fertilizer from the slopes down into the flat areas. To fix this, you can make ridges across the slope (contour farming) to catch the water and soil so your crops on the hills can grow just as well.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa Ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛha naagba nɛɛ naa tsabaa Obaanyɛ ofee ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ. (contour farming) koni akɛto nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he Koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ hu anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does water collect in the low areas of my farm after rain, and why is it rotting my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miifite lɛ?

english: Low-lying ground acts like a bowl that holds standing water. Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, so when they stay soaked for days, they suffocate and rot. Low wet areas are better suited for water-loving crops like rice.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɛnsii ni nu ni damɔ shi yɔɔ mli. Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛwo nu mli gbii babaoo lɛ, ebaagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbo. He ni nu yɔɔ shishi lɛ hi kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How do I know which crops will grow best on the different parts of my farmland?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ? mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Look at how your land naturally drains and gets sunlight. High, dry areas suit deep-rooted crops like cashew or cocoa; gentle slopes suit maize and vegetables if protected from erosion; and damp, flat bottomlands suit crops like rice or sugarcane.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ lɛ. He ni nɔ kwɔ ni egbi lɛ hi kɛha tsei ni shishifãi mli kwɔ tamɔ cashew nuts loo cocoa. Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa kɛ aduawai kɛji akɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why are my young maize plants bending sideways instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee afã moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean toward sunlight to feed themselves. If big trees or tall bushes are casting shade on one side of your field, your maize will bend sideways to catch as much light as possible.
ga: Tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe. Kɛji tsei wuji loo tsei bibii kakadaji ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome he lɛ, Abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa fã kome koni enyɛ emɔ la ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable plants turn light yellow when I grow them under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their food and maintain their rich green color. Heavy shade from big trees starves the vegetables of light, causing their leaves to turn yellow and their stems to become weak.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛha amɛhe su eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi. Tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo ni mli wa lɛ haaa aduawai lɛ aná la. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ ahe gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up the pollen inside the flowers, preventing pollination. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant drops it to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every single plant gets enough space, sunlight, and nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also makes it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do I need to make big heaps of soil before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large underground and need soft, loose soil to expand easily. Building high mounds gives the tubers room to grow big while keeping them safe from rotting in waterlogged ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa efite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why was my harvest very big in the first year after clearing the bush, but got smaller in the second and third years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ da waa nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mijie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi eba shi yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ kɛ etɛ lɛ mli?

english: Bush clearing leaves behind years of rich, built-up soil nutrients. Planting the same crop every year drains those specific nutrients faster than the soil can replace them, which lowers your yield over time.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ afii amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsake amɛ. Enɛ baaha nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: As someone starting farming for the first time, how can I choose a crop that won't fail easily on my land?
ga: Ákɛ mɔ ko ni je okwaayeli shishi klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ, mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ efooo mlɛo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Start by observing what nearby farmers grow successfully and check your soil type. Hardy, fast-growing crops like cassava, maize, or cowpeas are ideal for beginners because they tolerate tough conditions and have steady local demand.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ nɔ ni okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ edu yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ. ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli, ni eyɛ nibii ni maŋ lɛ biɔ waa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas and beans are special crops that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores nutrients to your farmland for the next season.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand easily into large roots. Mounds also protect the tubers from rot by allowing excess rainwater to drain away quickly instead of gathering around the root.
ga: Sweet potato tubers he miihia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃ mlɛo. Gɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ehaa ehoɔ oya moŋ fe ni eeebua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods develop black spots and turn completely rotten while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egbo kwraa kɛ́ amɛyɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp conditions. Pruning shade trees and excess cocoa branches allows sunlight and air flow to dry out the farm and prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a plant virus they carry. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray or soapy water helps protect new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are caterpillars eating large holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye bu agboi ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on cabbage leaves, which hatch into hungry caterpillars that feed on the crop. Hand-picking them off early or spraying safe natural controls like neem seed extract keeps them from destroying the leaves.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabe baai anɔ. ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Mra be mli ni akɛ niji ŋmɔɔ loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni kudɔɔ nibii tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwiemɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep drying up and falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of consistent water. Providing regular watering and light shade during the hottest parts of the day helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily weaken under heavy fruit bunches or if damaged by soil pests like root nematodes. Supporting mature stems with strong wooden stakes prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ agbɔjɔ oya yɛ aduawai akui ni tsii shishi loo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi nematodes lɛ fite lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso ni eda lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa egbee shi.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing them early ensures your young plants get all the energy they need to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni odumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the main leaves start to turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant cracks due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa yɛ bulb ni mli elɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK, or adding well-rotted animal manure, will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that plant needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How does covering my garden soil with dry leaves help my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi wo abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It traps moisture in the ground so you water less often, keeps the soil cool under hot sun, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your vegetables.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ o-vegetables lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off because of high temperatures, lack of consistent watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting during cooler months helps the blossoms set into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni adu yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaawo yibii kɛ fɔfɔii ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants stunted and curled up with short bushy branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ niji kukuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, stunted pepper plants are usually attacked by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites that spread viral diseases. Spraying the plants early with organic neem leaf extract or an approved insecticidal soap keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ tutuaa pepper tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ organic neem baa mli nu loo samla ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear all over my okra leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ yɛ okra baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which thrives when plants are crowded and air cannot circulate well. Spacing your okra plants properly during planting and removing infected leaves stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɛkɛ powda yɛŋ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Okɛ okra tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni oduɔ lɛ ni ojie baai fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe or diseased pods quickly stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ eshwa oya kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, indicated by the lower leaves yellowing and falling off. You can test harvest one plant by carefully digging around the base to check if the roots are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oyɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome ni okpaa lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋtayaa ni ooofee jogbaŋŋ kɛbɔle he lɛ nɔ. shishi koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam rot happens when water gathers around the roots due to heavy soil or poor drainage. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, preventing fungal rots from destroying the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni fungal rot akafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops on raised soil mounds or flat ground during heavy rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Planting on raised mounds or ridges during rainy seasons lifts crop roots above waterlogged soil. This prevents root rot and improves soil aeration, which is essential for root crops like cassava and yams as well as vegetables.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ aya hiɛ. Enɛ he miihia kɛha shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to high heat and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living cover to shield the young trees and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaye abua ni akɛ tsei bibii ato. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which the crop needs to grow green and healthy. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy foliage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every year and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ aba afi fɛɛ afi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut and plant for my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from the middle portion of the cassava plant with clear, undamaged buds. Avoid using the soft green top parts or the overly dry, woody bases.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni mli wa ni edara kɛjɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni efiteee lɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shishi ni egbi tsɔ lɛ he.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the plants are actively growing and the soil is moist, usually two to three weeks after sprouting. Applying it on dry soil can burn the crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso shishifãi.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli fãa?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the leaf center during the early stages of crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ jeɔ shishi edara lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips, which feed on the leaves and can also pass viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baai ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai hu aha tsei

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli loo afɔɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifɔ lɛ.

english: How can I stop the soil around my crops from drying out too fast during the hot season?
ga: Mibaatsi muji ni ebɔle he lɛ naa Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmɔshi nibii akagbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with a layer of dry grass, leaves, or straw acts as mulch. This shields the soil from the hot sun, slowing down water evaporation.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi, baai, loo jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni etsu nii akɛ mulch. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to grow strong tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so leaves catch more light while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha baai lɛ aná la babaoo kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large broad leaves that provide shade, keep the soil moist, and protect the young cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant beans or groundnuts alongside our maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ wɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen naturally from the air and store it in their roots. When grown near maize, they feed the soil and help the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofa babaoo awo ŋmãa mli.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight underground for nutrients, water, and space. Giving them proper distance allows each plant to form larger, thicker tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before they can produce any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ mawo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from heat, irregular watering, or insect damage. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during very hot weather prevents the flowers from dropping.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Watering early in the morning lets the roots absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate quickly from the warm soil before the roots can take it up.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots and lower branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mikoo tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛ shishigbɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner part of the tree, which prevents diseases and directs the plant's food energy into making larger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa ni ekwɛɔ tso lɛ niyenii hewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are damaged by heat or insects during storage, or if they are planted too deep in dry soil. Using fresh, healthy seeds and planting them at shallow depths helps them germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji dɔlɛ loo kooloi fite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive tough conditions. They drink up water and feed on soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing weeds early is necessary for crop growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni jwɛi ni akuɔ mra lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the lower stem turns woody. Digging up one plant to check root thickness confirms if the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ tsake efee tso Tso kome ni akuɔ koni ana bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa ha lɛ maa nɔ mi kɛji tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: If I clear a fresh plot of bush on my farm, how long should I wait before planting my seeds?
ga: Kɛji mijie ŋmɔ hee ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: After clearing land, it is best to wait about one to two weeks so the cleared weeds can dry up and decompose or be managed, which prevents them from re-growing quickly and choking your new seeds.
ga: Beni ajie he lɛ sɛɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ dani jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbi ni egbo loo atsu he nii. Enɛ haaa amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei oya ni amɛmiimɔ odumɔwui heei lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for my soil if I leave cleared bushes to rot on the farm or burn them?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji miha tsei bibii ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mishã amɛ?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation to rot on the farm acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, holds moisture during hot days, and gradually enriches the soil with natural fertilizer as it decays.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Hiɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni fiofio lɛ ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger and stronger when I remove weeds and extra shoots from the middle of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ mijie jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing out weeds and extra shoots from between your plants removes competition for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, allowing your main crop to get all the energy it needs to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ kɛyaa. Ehaa tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe awa.

english: Will weeds really hurt my crops if I leave them growing together in the same plot?
ga: Ani jwɛi lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii awui diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, weeds act like crop thieves; they rapidly steal water, light, and soil food away from your plants, causing your crops to become thin, weak, and produce small yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii julɔi. Amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are some of my plant stems growing thin and weak while others grow strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ ekomɛi yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu he wa lɛ?

english: Thin and weak stems usually mean the plant is not getting enough sunlight or lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, whereas balanced fertilizer or manure helps build strong, thick stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ sũ lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua ni etswa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli tse.

english: How deep into the soil should I plant my seeds after clearing the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Seeds should generally be planted at a depth equal to two or three times their size; planting too deep prevents the sprout from reaching the surface, while planting too shallow causes them to dry out or get eaten by birds.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: Planting early in the rainy season allows young roots to establish deeply while water is plentiful, giving the plants strength to withstand short dry spells later in the growth cycle.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ be kukuoo ni nuɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting a disease before the whole farm gets affected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emɔ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ emɔ?

english: Look out for early signs like spots on the leaves, yellowing, curled leaves, or wilting when the soil is wet, as these signs indicate disease before it spreads across your entire field.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ hela dani egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: What should I do immediately if I see yellow spots spreading on the leaves of a few crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwã ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: You should carefully remove and dispose of the infected leaves or plants away from the farm immediately so that insects or wind do not carry the sickness to your healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie baai loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi kooloi loo kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekɛ hela aba onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops look sickly and yellow even though it is raining heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away key nutrients from the soil or cause waterlogging around the roots, which smothers the plant's roots and prevents them from taking in food, making the crop look sick.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eha nu abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni ehaaa eye niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ.

english: Maize seeds need moist soil and warm conditions to wake up and germinate. If the soil is too dry or planted too deep, the seeds will delay sprouting or rot in the ground before coming up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ he miihia Abele dumɔwui koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo adu lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛje kpo.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees around my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant roots are soaked in too much standing water, which prevents them from taking up soil nutrients like nitrogen. Improving soil drainage usually restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli tsɔ. Enɛ tsĩɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ehiɛ feɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes my tomato plant leaves curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by intense heat stress, lack of water, or tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit plant diseases. Protecting plants from harsh heat and controlling insects prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ baa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛ kooloi ni akudɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my crop field is getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miihe nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: When crops receive too much water, their leaves turn pale or yellow, growth stops, and stems become soft because waterlogged soil starves the root system of oxygen.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. dalɛ kpaa Ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when soil moisture drops too low during hot days, or when there are not enough insects like bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi tsɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back faster than my main crops after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients from poor soil very quickly. Clearing them early prevents them from crowding out your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo onibii amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my yam seed tubers too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui akui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting yams too close forces the underground roots to compete with each other for water and food, resulting in very small yam tubers at harvest time.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fruits plump up, lose their sharp edges, and become smooth and rounded, even while the skin remains green.
