ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ etee, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo moŋ

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot weather, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why are my new high-yield seeds failing when I treat them the same way as my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii beni mikɛ amɛ yeɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mikɛ mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: High-yield varieties are bred to produce much more harvest, but they require different care—such as precise plant spacing, proper fertilizer timing, and controlled watering—than traditional seeds. Using old practices on new seeds often leads to poor yields or crop failure.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛbiɔ kwɛmɔ srɔtoi, tamɔ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ. Be ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ fe blema dumɔwui Bei pii lɛ, nifeemɔi momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ dumɔwui heei haa yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my new hybrid crops wilt so easily during short dry spells compared to my local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli kɛ akɛto mimaŋ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Local seed varieties have adapted over generations to survive tough conditions by growing slowly, whereas hybrid crops channel their energy into fast growth and high production. Because of this, high-yield crops need consistent soil moisture management, such as mulching, to handle dry spells.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ etsake amɛhe yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ daa, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli, koni akɛtsu hulutsoo be lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my high-yield crop leaves turn yellow faster than local varieties when I don't use fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya fe maŋbii tsei lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ?

english: High-yield crops grow faster and produce larger fruits, which means they consume soil nutrients much more rapidly than traditional crops. Without adequate fertilizer to replenish the soil, high-yield crops quickly show signs of nutrient starvation, such as yellowing leaves.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei nɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii oya fe tsutsu tsei lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ bɛ Tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he okadii oya, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I just copy the farming practices used by my neighbors in the village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikaseɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni mi akrowa lɛ mli akutsoŋbii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Every farm has different soil quality, moisture levels, and pest pressures. Copying a neighbor without understanding why they use specific methods—especially if they are using outdated techniques—can cause you to apply the wrong inputs or mismanage your crops.
ga: Okwaafoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa. Humidity level kɛ pressure ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi amli Kɛ́ okɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ fee ekome ni onuuu nɔ hewɔ ni amɛkɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko tsuɔ nii lɛ shishi—titri lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ ŋaai ni etsɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ—ebaanyɛ eha okɛ nibii ni ejaaa awo mli loo okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops suffering even after I followed the traditional advice of an experienced local farmer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa amanehulu eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ akusum ŋaawoo tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Older farming advice is usually tailored to traditional seed varieties and past soil conditions. Modern crop varieties have specific technical needs that standard traditional practices cannot meet, so following old methods for new seeds can harm your output.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kusum mli okwaayeli he ŋaawoi lɛ toɔ shishijee dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ kɛ yinɔsane mli shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ he. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ yɛ ŋaa taomɔ nii krɛdɛɛi ni blema nifeemɔi nyɛŋ atsu he nii. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛi momo ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ dumɔwui heei ahe nii lɛ baanyɛ aye onibii ni obaawo lɛ awui.

english: Why can't I rely on the exact planting months that my father used in Ghana years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ nyɔji pɔtɛɛ ni mitsɛ kɛdu nii yɛ Ghana nakai afii fɛɛ ni eho lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weather and rain patterns in Ghana have shifted over time, and modern seed varieties have different growth cycles than older crops. Sticking strictly to old planting calendars can cause your crops to suffer from unexpected droughts or heavy rains at critical growth stages.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ yɛ srɔto fe tsei ni etsɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui adumɔ kalanda momo lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do new high-yielding seed varieties need different spacing between plants than my old seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe mi momo lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties often develop larger root systems and broad canopy leaves to take in maximum sunlight and nutrients. Planting them using old spacing rules can cause overcrowding, leading to competition for light and nutrients that lowers overall yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ feɔ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo. Mlai momo ni kɔɔ gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he lɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha mɛi ayi obɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa kɛha la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni no haa yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does adding too much fertilizer make my high-yield crops fall over before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa mitsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ shwieɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Excess fertilizer, especially nitrogen, causes plants to grow tall and weak stems too rapidly without building structural strength. When rain or wind hits, these top-heavy plants fall over (lodge) and the harvest gets spoiled.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine, titri lɛ nitrogen Ebaaha tso lɛ adara ni eshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ oya tsɔ ni ewajeee shishitoo lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswa Tsei ni tsii baagbee (shĩa) lɛ nɔ ni amɛha nibii ni adu lɛ agbo.

english: Why does my neighbor get a huge harvest from high-yielding seeds while mine fails even though we planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli shi minɔ lɛ eshɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: High-yield seeds depend heavily on proper field management conditions. If your neighbor adjusted their soil preparation, weed control, and nutrient timing to match the crop's specific needs while you used general practices, their harvest will be significantly better.
ga: Dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔ shihilɛ ni sa nɔ waa. Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ tsake shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ be ni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ woɔ mli lɛ mli koni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba mli yɛ be mli ni okɛ nifeemɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ. Amɛkpamɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kwraa fe no.

english: Why do improved cocoa seedlings require different shade levels compared to traditional cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo srɔtoi kɛ akɛto blema kookoo tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Modern high-yield cocoa varieties are bred to mature faster and tolerate more sunlight once established, but they still need temporary shade when young. Using old shade management methods on modern varieties can either starve the crop of light or burn young trees.
ga: Atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwere oya, ni kɛ́ amɛto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ, amɛŋmɛɔ hulu la he gbɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni ená be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be mli ni eji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Kɛ akɛ blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛye la loo amɛshã tsei bibii.

english: Heavy rain washes away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen and fills soil spaces with water, preventing roots from breathing and taking up food. Applying fertilizer after heavy rains helps restore these lost nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ekɛ nu woɔ sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaye nii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɛkɛ niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem can burn the plant's delicate outer skin and roots. Fertilizer should be applied in a ring a few inches away from the base where feeding roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi yɛ he ni shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do many small flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only flowers pollinated by tiny insects called midges will turn into pods. Unpollinated flowers naturally drop off, which is normal for the tree.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi pɛ yɔɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ tsɔɔ pod pɛ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main stem for water and nutrients. Keeping only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to grow a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ tso lɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the stalks to grow thin, weak, and produce small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. loo cob ko bɛ kwraa

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that grows the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering during fruit development. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Weeds are wild local plants that have adapted over generations to survive tough soil conditions and dry weather, whereas cultivated crops require extra care, proper spacing, and nutrients to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ daa jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know if the seeds I bought are good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: You can do a simple float test in water—seeds that sink are usually healthy and full of life, while seeds that float are often dry, damaged, or empty inside.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni oyɔɔ nu mli lɛ okwɛ mlɛo. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni wala eyi mli obɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ egbi, efite, loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Is it okay to keep using seeds saved from my last harvest, or should I buy new planting materials?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aya nɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii? Aloo esa akɛ mahe nibii heei ni akɛduɔ nii?

english: Using saved seeds from hybrid crops often produces weaker plants and lower yields over time. Getting fresh, certified seeds ensures stronger crops and better harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui heei ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ ni anáa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa kɛ ŋmaa kpakpa aba.

english: How can I take care of my farm tools so they stay in good condition throughout the planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi okwaayeli nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Clean off all soil after use, dry them completely to prevent rust, and wipe the metal parts with a little oil before storing them in a dry place.
ga: Tsumɔ sũ fɛɛ he kɛji okɛtsu nii sɛɛ. Tsumɔ ni egbi kwraa koni ŋmei akafee. Ni okɛ mu fioo atsumɔ dade fãi lɛ ahe dani okɛto he ko ni egbi.

english: How often should I water my crop nursery during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-nursery lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young seedlings in a nursery need watering early in the morning and late in the afternoon to keep the soil moist without scorching the leaves under the hot sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nu leebi kɛ shwane koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ ashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Is it better to pour water directly on the crop leaves or at the base near the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Always water at the base near the roots. Wetting the leaves unnecessarily encourages fungal diseases and wastes water through evaporation.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, nu awo shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ. Baai lɛ ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ ni efiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear and prepare my land early before the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e he hia nɛ a kpata zugba a nɔ nɛ a dla lɛ mla a? Ehe miihia dani nugbɔ ni naa wa anɛ.

english: Clearing early gives cleared plants time to dry and rot into rich manure, and ensures your field is ready to trap the very first rainwater for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa tsei ni ajie amɛ lɛ naa be ni amɛgbi ni amɛgboi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni oye obua ni okwɛ akɛ oŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo koni amɛmɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When crops are overcrowded, they fight each other for light, food, and water, which results in thin stalks and small, empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, niyenii, kɛ nu, ni no haa amɛnáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my young plants wither even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Young seedlings often suffer from heat stress under direct harsh sunlight. Providing light shade using palm fronds protects them until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei baai tsu nii ni okɛwo amɛhe shade lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn yellow when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ ji gbekɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy, or a sign that the soil is too waterlogged and choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ miibolɔ kɛmiitao nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Aloo eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if insects are starting to damage my crops before the leaves are completely eaten?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miibɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afitemɔ dani aye baai lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Look closely for tiny pinholes in leaves, sticky liquid on stems, curling leaf edges, or drooping young shoots during your morning farm walks.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ, nu ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ, baai lɛ ashishi ni ebɔle ehe, loo ŋmeii bibii ni egbee shi yɛ be mli ni onyiɛɔ ŋmɔ mli leebi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure early in the season keeps leaves green so the plant can produce large, heavy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo toi wuji ni tsii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which can draw nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave behind enriched soil that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: What is making the leaves of my young corn look ragged and full of holes overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-baby corn baai lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni bu eyi mli obɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central whorl. Catching them early and applying safe bio-pesticides or neem leaf solution directly into the whorl stops them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ awo ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Curled and twisted leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the underside of the leaves. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or insecticidal soap allows fresh, healthy leaves to grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ he okadi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—their tender leaves burn easily in full direct sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains provides a protective umbrella that keeps the soil moist and shields the seedlings from severe heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. releasing tall trees Shade loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains waterlog the ground without proper drainage, the roots drown and begin to rot, so planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewoɔ nu ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering, which prevents proper pollination. Providing light shade and maintaining consistent moisture in the soil during hot spells helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Ni akɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse haa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: How does putting dried grass around my vegetable plants help them during dry weather?
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi-vegetable tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It reduces soil water evaporation from the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni hulu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in the sunlight to produce the food required to grow big tubers underground. Staking elevates the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, leading to larger yams at harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji kɛ́ akpa.

english: Why are my harvested rice grains discolored instead of clean and uniform?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ su tsakeɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni he tse ni efee ekome lɛ?

english: Discolored rice grains are often caused by rain damage or fungal growth when paddy is left wet after harvest. Drying your harvested grains thoroughly on clean tarpaulins right after harvesting keeps the grains clean and prevents discoloration.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni efiteɔ loo ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni etsake amɛhe lɛ baa kɛ́ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Gbimɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe atse ni amɛkatsake amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no taller shade plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and scorch easily. Planting crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living shade umbrella that reduces heat stress and holds soil moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips in maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the plants restore green growth and produce full corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rain stays on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills up oxygen pockets in the ground, suffocating root systems. Without oxygen, harmful fungi and bacteria thrive in the wet soil and easily invade and rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Fungi kɛ bacteria ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. ni eboteɔ ŋmei shishifãi amli oya ni efiteɔ

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and leaves enough room to grow big and productive.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua eshishifãi lɛ ni eshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller corn yields when I plant maize on the exact same farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural nitrogen to the soil and stops pest buildup.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the central funnels of my young maize plants and eating the foliage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are fall armyworms, a common pest that targets young corn leaves. Checking fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the funnel protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves and grass on the bare ground around my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ mabɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry foliage creates mulch, which shields the soil from hot sun rays to keep it cool and moist. Mulch also prevents weed seeds from sprouting and slowly breaks down to add organic nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Mulch hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa fiofio. Efiteɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of plant nutrients like phosphorus. Maintaining steady watering routines during flowering helps the plant hold onto its blooms and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo tso mli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's hybrid maize harvest grow into weaker plants than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high performance only in their first generation. The seeds collected from that harvest lose those superior genetic traits, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields if replanted.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ fɔmɔ nii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa ni kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant energy to make food, which is then sent down into the soil to grow large, heavy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛmaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmeii lɛ agboi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying a few weeks after I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Otsii enyɔ komɛi asɛɛ beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young seedlings often die from transplant shock, harsh sunlight, or lack of water. Planting them at the very start of the rainy season and giving them shade from plantain trees helps their delicate roots establish safely in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ he shoofeemɔ, hulu la ni fa babaoo, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli, ni aha amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantains mli lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: If some of my crop seedlings die on the farm, can I plant new ones in those exact same spots?
ga: Kɛji mi tso dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ madu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, this practice is called 'supplying' or replanting. You should completely remove the dead seedling and check the soil for pests or rot before placing a fresh, healthy seedling into the same hole early in the rainy season.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ‘nihemɔ’ loo dumɔ ekoŋŋ. Esa akɛ ojie dumɔwui ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ. Ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mli. Dani oookɛ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ awo bu kome mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: How can I tell the right time to start planting my seeds when the rainy season begins in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist for at least three consecutive days. Planting after just one isolated rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither when the hot sun returns.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be ni kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How do I know if my land itself is bad or if my crop seeds were just low quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo midumɔwui lɛ ehiii?

english: If plants across your entire field grow yellow and weak despite good rainfall, the soil is likely lacking nutrients or too acidic. If only a few plants fail while others nearby grow strong, the problem is usually poor seed quality or improper planting depth.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo eyɛ acid tsɔ. Kɛji tsei fioo komɛi pɛ fite yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fite. Nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ daa waa Bei pii lɛ naagbai jɛɔ dumɔwui ni ehiii loo dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ ni esaaa lɛ mli.

english: I want to expand my farm to clear new acres of land, but how do I know if the new soil is good for crops?
ga: Miisumɔ ni magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mafo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Look at the natural wild plants growing on the new land. Dark, moist topsoil rich with earthworms and deep organic matter indicates good soil that can support healthy crop growth just like your existing field.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni edɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara kɛ agbɛnɛ hu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Should I burn the bush on my new farm plot before planting, or leave the cleared grass on the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ dani madu loo mashi jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it kills beneficial soil insects and burns off organic nutrients. Leaving cleared weeds to rot on the soil acts as mulch, keeping the ground cool, trapping moisture, and feeding your crops naturally over time.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Mohu ɔ, e gbeɔ zugba a mi koolohi nɛ a he hia lɛ, nɛ e shãa níhi nɛ ngɛ mi ɔ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow even when there is enough rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani nugbɔ enɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the ground is waterlogged from poor drainage. When soil stays flooded, roots drown and cannot absorb nutrients even if plenty of water is present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ po.

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each crop to grow strong leaves and large fruits, resulting in a higher total harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ baai ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the roots of my crops rotting underground while the stems still look green on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Root rot is caused by soil fungi that thrive in overly wet land with bad water drainage. The roots decay hidden underground first, and by the time you see the top leaves wilt, the fungal damage has been happening for weeks.
ga: Sũ mli ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi fitemɔ baa. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaahi shikpɔŋ shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Ni kɛ́ ona akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ miihoso No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ emɔ otsii komɛi nɛ.

english: Why do my cashew trees grow so slowly in their first year compared to fast crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei ni daa oya tamɔ yucca lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their entire first year building deep underground taproots so they can survive long dry seasons later in life. Fast crops like cassava put immediate energy into top growth and tubers within a single season.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi amli lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ fɛɛ maa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã ko ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei haa hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛha dalɛ babaoo kɛ ŋmei yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do animals and insects attack my crops more when they are young seedlings than when they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo beni amɛji dumɔwui fe be mli ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are soft, tender, and easy for pests to chew and digest. As crops grow older, their stems become hard and fibrous, making them less attractive to many early-stage pests.
ga: Nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii baanyɛ aye ni amɛye. Kɛ tso lɛ eda Amɛshishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛyɛ tsɔi, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔɔ amɛ yɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: How long after planting do I need to keep protecting my young seedlings from farm pests?
ga: Yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ maya nɔ mabu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: The first 10 to 14 days after germination are the most critical. Once seedlings develop strong roots and tough leaves, they are better able to survive minor pest damage.
ga: Abuɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ akɛ eji gbii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni wa Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ hu yɛ nibii bibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my seeds sometimes disappear from the soil before they even sprout into plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ midumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ po ni amɛfeɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Pests like rodents, birds, and ants dig up planted seeds underground because the seeds are rich in nutrients. Covering seeds properly with soil or using temporary seed treatments helps stop them from being eaten.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ejaakɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ha dumɔwui lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ loo okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛtsaa dumɔwui ahe be kukuoo ko tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akaye dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do some pests show up on my farm early in the season while others appear much later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi je kpo yɛ sɛɛ mli babaoo lɛ?

english: Different pests prefer different stages of crop growth. Some insects feed on soft germinating seeds, while others wait for flowers or mature fruits to appear later in the season.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi biɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi. Kplukai komɛi yeɔ dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi mɛɔ fɔfɔii loo aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ koni amɛje kpo yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ.

english: Will chemical sprays that kill insects also stop larger bush animals from eating my young plants?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ baatsi koo mli kooloi wuji anaa koni amɛkaye mi tsei bibii lɛ?

english: No, insect sprays only work on small bugs like caterpillars and beetles. Larger farm animals like grasscutters or rats require physical protection like fencing, wire netting, or specific animal repellents.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii pɛ anɔ. Kooloi wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli, tamɔ jwɛifolɔi loo ŋmeii Gbɔmɔtsoŋ hebuu tamɔ gbogboi, waya ŋtayaai loo nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi lɛ ahe miihia.

english: How many days should I keep temporary guards or nettings over my young crop beds?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ maná be kukuoo mli bulɔi loo ŋshɔŋlooi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: You should leave protective guards on for about 10 days until the seedlings grow tall and strong enough to withstand the local pests without dying.
ga: Esa akɛ owo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why is it important to clear bush and weeds around the edge of my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa dani adu lɛ?

english: Weeds and overgrown bushes give pests like rats and grasscutters a safe place to hide and breed before attacking your young crops. A clean farm perimeter keeps them further away.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ŋmɔji. Ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli ni ofɔ bii dani amɛtutua oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ. Okwaa husu ni mli tse haa amɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my nursery plants look weak and get damaged easily in their first week after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-nursery tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanting creates shock because the plant's roots are disturbed. During the first 7 to 10 days, the plant works on roots instead of leaves, making it temporarily weak and vulnerable to pests.
ga: Tso lɛ ni aaawo lɛ ji nɔ ko ni haa mɔ naa kpɛɔ ehe ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haoɔ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii 7 kɛyashi 10 lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ baatsu eshishifãi lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ebaai lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: What causes my fresh maize seedlings to snap and fall over at ground level overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-abele dumɔwui heei lɛ fã ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by cutworms or small rodents that chew through tender stems near the soil surface at night. Keeping the soil clean around the stem helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aka naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Can bad weather make my young crops more vulnerable to pests and diseases?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ afee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baanyɛ atswa mi?

english: Yes. Severe heat, excessive rain, or dry spells weaken seedlings, reducing their natural ability to recover if pests nibble on their leaves or roots during the early days.
ga: Hɛɛ. Dɔlɛ babaoo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo. aloo fɛ̃i be lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Dumɔwui lɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe lɛ baa shi kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ŋmɔ baai loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and sensitive roots that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them protects them from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that bakes the ground. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die before the regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the leaves to a healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts on the same land where I plant my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is very good for the soil. Groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps the land fertile.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: This issue is usually caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil moisture steady and adding wood ash or agricultural lime helps plants form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ tso sũ loo lime fataa he lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat the young leaves in the middle of my corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. They hide inside the central shoot to feed on tender growth, but spraying early with organic or recommended control treatments stops them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Shi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni akudɔ ni akɛwo mli mra lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛnaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months. Leaving them underground too long during heavy rains exposes them to excess water and soil fungi that cause the tubers to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa nu kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and produce poor harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground and exposes them to sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Propping up the main stem with strong wooden poles prevents wind from blowing the plants down before harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ dani akpa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow. Adding well-rotted animal manure or NPK fertilizer gives them the nutrients required to stay green and produce big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ha amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná toi wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my young crop plants look weak and small even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe ehiaaa lɛ? Kɛji miha amɛ nu po.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil before your crop roots can get them. Clearing weeds early in the plant's life allows your crop to get all the nourishment it needs.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping some large trees or planting plantains beside them creates shade that keeps the soil cool and protects the young plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo baa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Providing regular watering at the base of the plant keeps the flowers cool and healthy so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nu ni afɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water or when tiny organisms attack the roots. Planting on top of raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo kɛ́ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Leaf curl happens when tiny insects like thrips or aphids suck the juices from young leaves and spread plant sicknesses. Spraying your plants with neem oil mixture repels these insects so new leaves grow normally.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids nu nu kɛjɛ baai bibii amli ni amɛgbɛ tso helai amɛshwã. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa

english: Why do my cowpea pods end up with tiny holes and worms inside them before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mli dani akpaa.

english: Insects lay eggs on cowpea flowers and young pods, and when the eggs hatch, caterpillars bore into the pods to eat the seeds. Spraying natural neem seed extract during flowering keeps these insects away.
ga: Kplukai woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsina fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem dumɔwui ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and when a heavy bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy. Propping the stems with sturdy wooden poles supports the plant so it stays upright until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni beni kuu lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa ma tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make food that builds big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, preventing leaves from rotting and helping tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ, ni ekwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my rainfed rice grow poorly whenever the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi nugbɔshiimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaa gbii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have shallow roots that need consistent moisture to absorb nutrients from the soil. Building low earth bunds (small ridges) around your field holds rainwater on the land longer, protecting the rice during dry gaps.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni biɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni enyɛ ejie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ooofee ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ (ŋmeii bibii) ni bɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Buu ŋmãa he yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their young roots can absorb it. Planting shade crops like plantain or banana next to them shields them from the hot sun while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Adumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can fit more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting trees too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak trees. Overcrowding also traps moisture, which makes it very easy for diseases to spread from tree to tree.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ hela lɛ baajɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support. Flowers often drop because tiny insects called midges have not pollinated them, or because the tree lacks sufficient water and nutrients to feed developing pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi bibii ahewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ eshɛko pollin lolo. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Cocoa pods change color as they mature. Pods that start green will turn bright yellow when ripe, while pods that start red or purple will turn orange-yellow, indicating the beans inside are fully formed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ etsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ orange-yellow. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ebɔi feemɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their leaves and produce fewer pods when the dry Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind removes moisture from both the soil and the plant leaves. Cocoa trees shed leaves and drop small pods as a self-defense mechanism to conserve water and survive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni akɛto nu he ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree if that leaves less wood on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ kɛji akɛ ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tsei fioo?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and fresh air to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity inside the tree canopy, helping prevent fungal rot and encouraging healthy pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, hela emɔmɔ amɛ, loo ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ. Koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsiɔ fungal rot naa ni ehaa pod lɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which thrives in high humidity and wet conditions. Rain splashes the fungal spores from the soil onto the low-hanging pods, causing them to turn black and decay rapidly.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Nugbɔ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ diŋ oya ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning pale yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium. When nutrients are depleted, the leaves cannot produce energy, requiring fertilizer or organic compost to restore soil health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ eho lɛ Baai lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my mature cocoa farm to harvest extra food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni eda lɛ teŋ koni maná niyenii krokomɛi?

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava among mature cocoa trees because cassava roots consume large amounts of water and nutrients, directly competing with your cocoa trees and damaging cocoa roots when harvested.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi kɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo tsuɔ nii. Enɛ kɛ cacao tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ ni efiteɔ cacao shishifãi lɛ kɛ́ akpa.

english: Why does a cocoa tree take several years before it starts bearing fruit compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tsei jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that must build a strong trunk, expansive root network, and dense branch canopy before it has enough stored energy to support pod production, which can then continue for over 30 years.
ga: Kookoo ji tso ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ewo tsei ni wa. Shishifãi babaoo kɛ niji babaoo dani hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ koni eye ebua pods ni baanyɛ aya nɔ fe afii 30 lɛ afeemɔ aba

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and need temporary shade trees like plantains to shield them from sun scorch while their root system and canopy mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ atsu hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he nii. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize stalks turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of bottom leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency, as the corn plant shifts available nutrients from older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋmãa heei ni dara yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water staying in the soil cuts off oxygen to cassava roots, creating waterlogged conditions that encourage fungal root rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi ni woɔ ŋmeii shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a viral infection spread by these insects feeding on the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms dropping off the plant before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, extreme drying of soil, or a lack of essential nutrients like potassium needed to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing small bunches when many small shoots are growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ lɛ Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he?

english: Extra sucker shoots take away nutrients and water from the main mother plant, so removing unwanted suckers leaves more energy for larger fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni ataooo lɛ baagbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha aduawai ni dara lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my yam plants grow smaller tubers if I let the vines crawl on the ground instead of using stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs bibii kɛji mishi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into maximum sunlight and increases airflow, enabling the plant to produce more energy through photosynthesis to store in the underground tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ koni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ shishi tsei amli.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often heats up dry soil without leaving enough lasting moisture, causing seeds to dry out and die before steady rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eshiuuu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I clear and weed it regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli ni mijieɔ jwɛi lɛ daa moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes essential nutrients from topsoil, meaning the soil needs rest, organic manure, or rotation with crops like legumes to recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia hejɔɔmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ koni ekɛsaa ehe ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle growing leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is characteristic damage from the Fall Armyworm, an insect pest that burrows into the central leaf funnel of young maize to feed on tender shoots.
ga: Enɛ ji bɔ ni Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli koni eye ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning yellow and scorched under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. They require shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees above them to shield their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil moist until their roots develop fully.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to remove some of the shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete for water and nutrients in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the plant produces large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe single trunk Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni tso lɛ awo yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata tso lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and decays, it releases this natural nutrient into the soil, acting as free fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛgboi Ejieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when water sits on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Excess standing water chokes the roots, preventing oxygen from reaching them and allowing fungal diseases to quickly cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmeii helai fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam leaves to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible for making food. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha amɛhoomɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. Extreme heat dries out the flower pollen, preventing the fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsei ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and look weak when the soil surface forms a hard crust after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A hard soil crust prevents rain from soaking down to the roots and blocks fresh air from reaching underground. Loosening the soil surface allows roots to breathe and absorb water properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekaná shishifãi lɛ amli, ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛmuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings look weak and wilted right after I transplant them into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Transplant shock happens when a seedling's roots are disturbed while moving to new soil. Providing temporary shade and adequate water helps the crop relax, adapt, and settle into its new spot without dying.
ga: Transplant shock baa kɛji akɛ dumɔwu ko shishifãi lɛ fite beni aduɔ lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛhiɔ he hee ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young crops like cocoa cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting shade crops like plantains provides living cover that protects the young cocoa leaves until the tree is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii tamɔ kookoo nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ kɛji amɛji bibii. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the maize to grow tall and thin with small or empty cobs instead of strong, healthy yields.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii nɛ mi wa nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign of stress, usually caused by a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, pest attacks, or getting either too much or too little water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds around my crops on a regular basis?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji daa?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal light, water, and plant food from your crops. Clearing them gives your crops the space and food they need to grow without disturbance.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi ni juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden poles to climb up on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally seek height to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Climbing a pole allows the leaves to catch light easily, which helps the plant manufacture food and produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ he ko ni kwɔ koni amɛbaji lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa la oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack pepper to live permanently in that soil. Changing crops allows the soil to reset and heal.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi nakai sũ lɛ mli daa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsaa ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Flower drop occurs when the plant is stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or bad weather. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do the roots of my tomato plants start to rot after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on your farm without draining away, it drowns the roots by blocking air. Without air in the soil, crop roots suffocate and begin to decay.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ.

english: Will trimming off some extra branches from my tomato plants make them produce bigger fruits?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha mi-tomato lɛ awo yibii wuji?

english: Yes, cutting off weak side branches allows the plant to focus its nutrients and water on developing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii kɛ nu nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do some vegetable farmers build net structures or cages over their crops instead of growing them under open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni feɔ aduawai abɔɔi lɛ maa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ŋtayaai loo ŋtayaai ŋtayaai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Net structures or greenhouses protect tender crops like tomatoes and sweet peppers from heavy rains, scorching sun, and harmful insects. This controlled environment allows plants to grow faster, suffer fewer diseases, and yield more produce on a small piece of land.
ga: Trellis loo greenhouse buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ tomato kɛ bell peppers ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. Helatsɛmɛi ni helai fioo pɛ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ babaoo yɛ he bibioo ko

english: What is intensive farming, and how can it help me harvest more from my small farm?
ga: Mɛni ji okwaayeli ni mli wa? Ni ebaaye ebua mi ni makpa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Intensive farming means using precise modern techniques—such as drip irrigation, proper plant spacing, and controlled feeding—to get maximum yield from a small area. It helps you produce high crop quantities without needing vast acres of land.
ga: Okwaayeli ni mli wa tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai pɔtɛɛ tamɔ nu ni hoɔ nu shwieɔ shi tsuɔ nii. Tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ he bibioo ko mli Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii babaoo ni okɛ hei wuji tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted directly under open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a protective canopy that reduces heat and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmei ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming any peppers during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni efeee pepper yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?
