english: Excessive rainfall and wet weather can wash pollen away from the blossoms or keep pollinators like bees away. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers instead of turning them into fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo atsĩ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do tomato plant roots rot and cause the plant to die after rain sits in my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni egbeɔ tomato tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe. When water pools around the base without proper soil drainage, the roots drown, rot, and lose their ability to take up food and water for the plant.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa kɛbɔle he Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, amɛbaagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu amɛha tso lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore leaf color and crop health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the corn ears are small and poorly filled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmãa toi lɛ daraaa ni ehiii kwraa?

english: This happens when the soil has plenty of nitrogen for leaf growth but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which are necessary for forming strong stalks and fully developed grains.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia kɛha tsei ashishifãi ni wa kɛ dumɔwui ni eda kwraa lɛ afeemɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and root space. This results in thin, weak plants that yield smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and stunt the growth of the crop during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that thrive in hot, dry weather. These pests transmit viruses that disrupt normal plant growth and reduce tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites lɛ kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ kɛ helai ni gbalaa tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ mli lɛ baa, ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like beans and groundnuts have natural bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn in harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish their roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ woɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying NPK or Urea fertilizer around the base of the plants gives them the nutrients needed to stay green and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea fataa he kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ tso lɛ shishi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Underground tuber rot happens when water sits around the cassava roots for too long, causing soil fungi to attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Tuber rot baa kɛji nu hi shi yɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds when they start producing bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and a heavy fruit bunch makes the tree top-heavy. Supporting the stem with a sturdy wooden or bamboo prop tied just below the bunch helps anchor the plant until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. ni aduawai akui ni tsii haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants shed flowers when they suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. Watering your crop regularly at the soil level early in the morning keeps the soil cool and helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Aduawai tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot soil, spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, and prevents fungal diseases from spreading on wet ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Gbalamɔ mli koni onine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ. Ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Ragged holes inside the central whorl of young maize are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide or organic neem seed extract into the plant funnel early in the morning kills the pests.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem dumɔwui ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually fix fresh nitrogen back into the dirt. Rotating your crops keeps the soil fertile and breaks the lifecycle of pests living in the soil.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii saa nitrogen hee lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii, ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ sũ mli lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die suddenly during the day even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is typically caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, which damages the plant's water pipes from underground. Removing infected plants immediately and avoiding waterlogging prevents the disease from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ a-nu paipii lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya, ni ajie nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does letting weeds grow on my farm cause my crops to produce very small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your main crops for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks of planting allows your crop to consume all available nutrients without competition, resulting in bigger yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa from heat, keep the soil cool and moist, and create a sheltered climate that allows the seedlings to establish roots and survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni efee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which maize relies on to build healthy green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea early in the growth stage helps restore the leaves to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ ni ŋmãa afee baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ shishijee be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the right part of a cassava stem to plant so that it sprouts well?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni adu koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Choose the middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem that is about 20 to 30 centimeters long with at least 4 to 6 visible eye nodes. Avoid soft top stems because they dry out easily, and avoid the woody base which sprouts slowly.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni eda ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Amɛkɛlɛ aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30, ni kɛ hoo lɛ, amɛyɛ ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni anaa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei bibii ahe ejaakɛ amɛgbiɔ oya. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ base tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need full sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers below. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground to catch the sun and prevents fungal rot from soil moisture.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛfee niyenii aha bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni emɔ hulu la ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Tomato flowers often drop due to heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist at root level and protecting plants from severe afternoon heat helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is eating small holes deep inside the center whorl of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on tender young leaves tucked inside the plant funnel. Inspecting crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides directly into the center funnel helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni akɛwo tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akpaa amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into tight knots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids that carry leaf-curl viruses. Spraying plants with neem oil or insecticidal soap reduces pest populations and prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni hiɛ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ayibɔ aba shi, ni ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu naa.

english: Why is it risky to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific soil nutrients and lets maize-loving pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnut restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni oha kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for starting a new plantain farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker henɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha plantain ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base—are best. They are stronger, establish roots faster, and produce bigger, healthier plantain bunches than broad-leafed maiden suckers.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishi ni mli tse lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛhe wa fe no. Bɔɔ shishifãi oya ni ofee plantain panicles ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid watering my vegetable garden during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu ni mikɛhaa yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot sun causes moisture to evaporate quickly before roots can absorb it, and water droplets on leaves can trap heat and scorch foliage. Watering early in the morning gives roots time to drink deeply before the heat sets in.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dɔlɛ ni eha baai lɛ ashã. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛnuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ dani latsaa lɛ baaje shishi.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my rice seeds for a new farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛha ŋmãa shweremɔ be hee lɛ?

english: Rice needs plenty of water to grow well, so it is best to plant right at the start of the main rainy season in your area or when your land can hold enough water, ensuring the young shoots do not dry out.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia omɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shishijee mli. aloo be mli ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: When my bag of rice seeds arrives from the market, how should I store it before planting day?
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa kotokui lɛ ba kɛjɛ jara nɔ Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛto dani dumɔ gbi lɛ aba?

english: Store your seed bags off the ground on wooden pallets in a cool, dry, well-ventilated room to prevent moisture, mold, and insects from damaging the seeds before you plant them.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui kotokui lɛ ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi akafite dumɔwui lɛ dani adu.

english: Why is it necessary to level my farmland properly before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsake he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Leveling the field ensures that water spreads evenly across the farm, preventing some rice plants from drowning in deep water while others dry out on higher ground.
ga: Kɛ́ afee he lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi anaa koni amɛkabote nu ni mli kwɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ

english: Should I scatter my rice seeds randomly over the field or plant them in straight lines?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Planting in neat rows gives each crop enough space to get sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, while also making it much easier for you to weed and care for the crop.
ga: Dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo hu akɛ obaajie jwɛi ni okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some farmers start rice seeds in a nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi jeɔ amɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei dani amɛduɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: A nursery protects young, fragile seedlings from pests, birds, and harsh weather until they are strong enough to survive and compete with weeds in the main field.
ga: Nursery lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, okpoi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ ahe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ abɔ akaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my young rice crop needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Healthy growing rice leaves are deep green; if the leaves start turning pale or yellow, it usually means the crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and needs fertilizer.
ga: Omɔ baai ni edara jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds steal strength from my crops, and when is the best time to remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiju hewalɛ kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crop. You should clear them within the first two to four weeks after planting before they crowd out the young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Esa akɛ ojie amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ be mli ni odu lɛ sɛɛ. Dani ebaayi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii

english: Does my rice field need to stay flooded with water until the day I harvest?
ga: Ani nu baaho yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛyashi nikpamɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: No, rice needs water while growing, but you should drain the water out of the field about two weeks before harvest so the grains can dry properly and the ground becomes easy to walk on.
ga: Dabi, nu he miihia ŋmãa be mli ni edaa lɛ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ nu afɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli aaafee otsii enyɔ dani okpa ŋmaa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmaa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ nyiɛmɔ afee mlɛo.

english: Why is it harmful to plant rice on the same spot on my farm year after year without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop diseases to build up; alternating with crops like cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai aba Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to get brown spots and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa?

english: Brown spots are often caused by fungal diseases or sap-sucking insects; keeping proper space between plants and avoiding over-fertilizing helps keep the leaves healthy and disease-free.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa nɔ, ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni helai akafee amɛ.

english: How can I safely test a new crop chemical on my farm before spraying my whole field of maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka tsofa hee ko ni akɛwoɔ tso mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe dani mafɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Always apply the chemical to a small sample of 3 to 5 plants first and observe them for 48 hours. If the leaves do not turn brown, scorch, or wilt, the chemical is safe to use at that dosage on your entire field.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsofa lɛ awo nɔkwɛmɔnii bibii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli klɛŋklɛŋ ni okwɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ etsɔko ŋmɔtɔ, amɛshãaa, loo amɛgbooo lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ nakai falɛ lɛ mli yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray crop medicine on my crops to avoid damaging them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsei ahe tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikafite amɛ?

english: Spray early in the morning or late in the cool afternoon. Midday heat causes chemicals to evaporate too fast or burn tender leaves when combined with direct sunlight.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo ehaa baai bibii lɛ shãa kɛ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fata he.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when they are in direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need partial shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantains during their first two years to trap moisture and protect their leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaf tips on bottom leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer. The maize plant is robbing nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to send food to the newer leaves growing on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei miitswa nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ koni amɛkɛ niyenii aya baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with leafy tops, but the roots under the ground stay thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen or excess shade, they put all their energy into making leafy tops above ground instead of storing food starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii mli starch baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers heat stress or inconsistent watering. If the plant feels it does not have enough water to support fruit, it sheds flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii lɛ bɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them as they open up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ porous kɛ́ amɛtswa lɛ?

english: Small ragged holes in maize leaves are a key sign of early Fall Armyworm feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying approved bio-pesticides into the funnel early stops the damage.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ fall armyworms ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ fall armyworms lɛ miiye nii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra yɛ gbɛi amli. lɛ baakpa nɔ ni efite lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt in the middle of the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is caused by fungal or bacterial root rot that blocks the plant's internal water pipes. The roots are damaged, so they cannot pump soil water up to the leaves during hot weather.
ga: Fungal loo bacteria shishifãi ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Shishifãi lɛ efite no hewɔ lɛ anyɛɛɛ ajie shikpɔŋ nu kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close together, won't I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. Spacing crops properly reduces competition, resulting in bigger, healthier fruits and higher total yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha akaŋshii aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ daraa. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okɛ nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ babaoo aba

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and greener on my plot than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots that absorb water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the nutrients meant for them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, harsh heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them creates a living umbrella that keeps the air cool and preserves soil moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rains wash them away, the plant cannot produce green pigment, which slows down its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei kɛyaa. Tsei nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of pushing them straight into the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle gives the stem optimal contact with damp soil while leaving enough buds above ground. This encourages strong roots to spread out horizontally beneath the surface, resulting in larger cassava tubers.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ agboi.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil and helps the maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa abele lɛ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes in the middle whorl of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest. Moths lay eggs inside the central funnel of young maize plants, and when the caterpillars hatch, they feed on the soft growing leaves before the plant can fully develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Eyeɔ baai bibii dani tso lɛ daa kwraa.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate food for tuber growth under the ground. Lifting the vines off the damp soil onto tall stakes prevents leaf diseases caused by soil moisture and allows the leaves to catch more sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtee tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ tsei ahe helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts as a protective shield. It stops the sun from quickly drying out the soil water, keeps the ground cool, and prevents unwanted weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my seeds often fail to sprout if I plant them immediately after the first short rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kuku lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often only moistens the top surface of baked dry soil. If you plant right away and a dry spell follows, the seeds will sprout, run out of deeper ground moisture, and wither under the hot sun before the main rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ashã lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni hɔmɔ ba lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ ni egboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to produce very small fruits and roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii kɛ shishifãi bibii kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for survival. They steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need, causing your plants to become starved and weak, leaving them with little energy to make big tubers or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee bulb agbo loo aduawai.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and rot inside bags even after I have collected it from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miifite ni miifite yɛ kotoku lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ?

english: Freshly harvested grains still hold moisture inside them. If you bag them immediately without drying them completely under the sun, trapped moisture creates warm damp conditions where mold grows and storage insects quickly multiply.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ kotokui lɛ wo kotokui lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ baafa oya.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth, or that heavy rains have flooded the root zone and prevented the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava plant producing tall leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai ni kɛlɛ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants receive excessive shade, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: High temperatures and lack of water cause heat stress in tomatoes, making the plant drop its blossoms to save water rather than spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ baa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus transmitted by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crop needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller crop yields every year even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground each time they grow. If you plant the same crop repeatedly without adding manure, compost, fertilizer, or rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaadara. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ, Ni okɛ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, loo okɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite.

english: Pruning extra side stems helps the plant direct its water and energy toward growing larger, healthier fruits instead of wasting resources on useless foliage.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start to rot quickly after digging them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised or cut during harvesting, or if they are stored in warm, damp places without good airflow where fungi and bacteria thrive.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when there is not enough in the ground, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to keep the top growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni eha ŋmei lɛ aya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my yam vines grow smaller tubers when I let them trail on the ground instead of using tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs bibii beni mihaa amɛnyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the root. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they get maximum sunlight and stay safe from wet rot, giving the plant energy to make larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ. ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: How does growing cowpeas in my field help prepare the land for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have small bumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the earth as free natural food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ bɔɔt bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, strong sunlight. Shade trees protect fragile young cocoa plants from harsh heat and wind, keeping the air moist around them until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when rain falls heavily for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves soil waterlogged, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing fungal rot to settle into the swollen tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ ni eboteɔ yitso ni efuu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming fruits during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato flowers become stressed and pollen dries up. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers to save energy instead of forming tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni haoɔ ni pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee tomato.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl tightly together and stop the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding on the undersides of leaves. As they drink the plant's juices, they cause leaf distortion and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot rapidly during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold that multiplies in cool, dark, and damp conditions. Rain splashes spores from the soil onto the low pods, where moisture allows the disease to spread quickly.
ga: Nu mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ fɛ̃i nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why does my main plantain stem produce a small bunch when I leave many small shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ mli fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii bibii Amɛ babaoo ebɔleɔ he. Mi plantain titri lɛ

english: The small shoots, called suckers, share the root system with the main plantain trunk. Leaving too many suckers forces the main plant to share food and water, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Ebaajara shishifãi lɛ kɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishifã lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehe bahia ni tso titri lɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are my green oranges falling off the tree before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tangerines lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshɛɔ dalɛ he lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit if they suffer from water shortages, or if fruit flies pierce the skin to lay eggs inside. The plant sheds compromised fruit early to conserve its resources.
ga: Orange tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna nu ni faaa. Aloo kɛji akɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii tsɔ hewolo lɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ mli. Tso lɛ jieɔ aduawai ni efite lɛ mra. koni akɛbu nibii ahe

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn brown and lose their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and dry air because their roots are not deep enough yet. Shade plants like plantains protect them from sunburn and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to build green leaves. Applying fertilizer or compost helps the plants turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the middle leaves inside my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths. They crawl into the central rolled leaves because it is soft and sheltered, eating the young leaves before they open up.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ shwieɔ. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ baai ni shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyɛ he ko ni amɛyɔɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Cassava tubers store water and starch. When the soil stays very wet during heavy rains or when roots stay in the ground too long after maturity, natural fungi in the soil cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli loo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara kwraa sɛɛ. Fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to create energy that goes down into the ground to build large tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground gives them more light and protects them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni baa shi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bulbs agboi. Kɛ́ owó wein tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha wein tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaatsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start producing big bunches of fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi aduawai wuji womɔ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface of the soil rather than a deep taproot. When a heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil unless you support the trunk with strong wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu agbo ko dara yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo Ja okɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the water in the soil changes suddenly from dry to wet. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop it to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo beni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ahe koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from young leaves. The damaged leaves grow unevenly, causing them to twist and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Baai ni efite lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto dry soil when there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops can only drink fertilizer when it is dissolved in soil water. Putting dry fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots or sit unused on top of the ground until heat spoils it or heavy water washes it away.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛkafee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ muji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water and soil food, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room, light, and nutrients to produce bigger fruits and grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii kɛ ŋmaa wuji.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly onto my crops in the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and hot for plants because of high ammonia levels, which can burn plant roots. It is best to dry or compost it first so it breaks down safely and releases rich organic nutrients into the soil.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa kɛha tsei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ammonia ni fa babaoo yɛ mli. ni baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbi loo ooofee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Koni efolɔ mli shweshweeshwe ni ejie niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a crop input is organic?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji organic?

english: An organic input is made from natural living materials like plants, animal droppings, or natural minerals without chemical additives. It feeds both the crop and the soil safely without leaving harsh chemical chemical residues.
ga: Akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ tsei, kooloi ashwiei, loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ feɔ Organic saji. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ niyenii shweshweeshwe ni eshiii tsofai ni mli wa ni eshwɛɛɛ.

english: How do natural or organic liquid mixtures help my crops grow better?
ga: Te adebɔɔ mli nibii loo nibii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni ji nu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Liquid organic mixtures feed the soil microbes and provide easily digestible nutrients to crop roots. This helps plants grow stronger leaves, build resistance to weather stress, and produce better yields without damaging the soil over time.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli ni ji nu lɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ niyenii ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa baai ni mli wa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔi nyɛɔ eshiɔ ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen or is standing in too much water. Giving the plant nitrogen-rich organic nutrients helps it produce food again and turn dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and well-nourished gives the plant strength to hold flowers until they become fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing big bushy leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough balanced nutrients, the plant spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of sending starch down to build thick roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni niyenii ni sa ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu starch kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Is it better to water my crops in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning before the sun gets strong. Afternoon heat causes water to evaporate rapidly into the air before the roots can drink it.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa, dani hulu lɛ atswa waa. Gbi gbɛkɛ latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, plants become thirsty and weak, making them easier targets for insects seeking moisture from green leaves. Keeping crops healthy helps them resist insect damage.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaye kumai ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi ni he hiaa nu ni jɛɔ baai eŋɔli amli lɛ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and poor yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to jump up fast and steal water and nutrients from the soil before your crops can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni sa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjo foi oya ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is strong enough to grow good crops before I spend money planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani mafite shika kɛdu amɛ?

english: You can judge soil strength by looking at how quickly local weeds and wild plants grow on it. Rich, fertile soil produces thick, dark green growth rapidly, which shows that your crops will also have the nutrients they need to grow well.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ha lɛ kɛtsɔ bɔ ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ koo mli tsei lɛ daa oya lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni baa nii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu baaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can looking at how fast wild grass grows on my land tell me if my maize will yield well?
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ani ebaanyɛ ekɛɛ mi kɛji mi-ŋma lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, fast-growing and thick wild vegetation is a clear sign of healthy soil with good water retention and natural nutrients, meaning crops like maize planted on that land are likely to yield heavily.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, koo mli tsei ni daa oya ni amɛhe eyi obɔ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he okadi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Eyɛ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do crops grow very slowly on some parts of my farm while other parts produce tall, healthy plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miida blɛoo waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni fãi krokomɛi woɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Soil strength varies across the same piece of land due to differences in topsoil depth, organic matter, and water drainage. The weaker areas need added compost or manure to bring them up to the same strength as the productive areas.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ naa. Enɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mlibotemɔ srɔtoi, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. He ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni amɛhe awa tamɔ hei ni woɔ yibii lɛ.

english: What signs should I look for on my bush land to know it is ready for farming after resting?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao yɛ tsei bibii ahe koni male akɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Land is fully restored and ready for farming when wild bushes and trees have grown back thick and dark green, showing that the soil has recovered its natural nutrients and strength during the resting period.
ga: Atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ kwraa ni efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii beni koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ená niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ehiɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields after I farm on it for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ etsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every season. Farming continuously without adding organic manure or letting the land rest exhausts the soil's strength, causing plant growth and crop yields to drop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo ashiɔ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Ehaa tsei adalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know the right time to dig and clear my land before the farming season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafo mli dani okwaayeli be lɛ aje shishi?

english: The best time to till your land is right after the first light rains when the soil is moist and workable. Observing how easily wild plants break ground around this time also signals that the land is soft enough for crop roots to spread.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ji beni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii Kɛ́ okadi bɔ ni koo mli tsei fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ oya yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, no hu ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Does digging my farm soil deeply every season help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mifoɔ shɔŋŋ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Tilling softens hard soil so roots can grow, but digging too deeply or too frequently breaks down the soil structure and dries out the fertile top layer. You should only till deep enough to create a soft bed for seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atswaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛ́ atsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ akumɔ ni eha ŋwɛi fã ni baa nii lɛ agbi. Esa akɛ odu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni efee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛha dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I test if my farm ground is too wet or too dry to start tilling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo egbi tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: Pick up a handful of soil and squeeze it into a ball. If it crumbles easily when gently touched, it is ready to till; if it sticks together like wet clay or is too hard to break, wait for better moisture conditions.
ga: Mɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ko ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ ata he fioo lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaatsu he nii. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo ewa tsɔ Mɛɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ.

english: If I burn all the cleared weeds and trees on my land, will it make the soil stronger for my crops?
ga: Kɛji mishã jwɛi kɛ tsei fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ani ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Burning cleared bush gives a temporary boost of ash nutrients, but it destroys the natural organic matter and helpful soil organisms that give the land long-term strength, causing the soil to dry out faster.
ga: Brɔshi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ baaha ashwishwɛ mli niyenii mli nibii lɛ aya hiɛ be kukuoo ko. Shi efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout even when I plant them immediately after clearing hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Seeds need moist, well-aerated soil to germinate. If the ground is cleared and tilled when it is too dry or compact, the seeds cannot absorb moisture or push roots down into the hard earth.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsu he nii beni egbi loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu loo amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and scorch easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the seedlings and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds face when I stick cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Mɛɛ gbɛ ŋmei niji lɛ baakwɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes delayed growth, weak stems, and significantly fewer tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha dalɛ asɛɛ afo, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulbs fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen-based fertilizer or compost helps the crop regain its color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená ehiɛ su ekoŋŋ ni eda waa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots and leaves the nutrients stuck in the soil where crops cannot drink them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akã shikpɔŋ ni tsei nyɛŋ anu nu kɛjɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose maximum leaves to sunlight, which generates the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Vines left on the ground are more prone to leaf diseases and produce smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso ko nɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ aha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Wein tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ foliar helai babaoo ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato bibii.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain plant for soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce larger, heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu, kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why are weeds making my crops produce smaller yields even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow full produce.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or overwatering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with proper watering or mulching during hot periods helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa fe nine Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my garden eggs and tomato fruits developing dark, rotten spots on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egboi yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of fruits are usually blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the plant. Irregular watering makes it hard for plants to absorb calcium, so keeping watering steady prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee ŋmeii. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa amɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nitrogen, while legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally fix nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots. Rotating them helps restore fertility for the next crop without needing extra chemicals.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the bottom up even though it is raining well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Rain gives water, but crops also need nutrients like nitrogen to stay green and build big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi niyenii tamɔ nitrogen hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer on my crops as soon as I put the seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Seeds without roots cannot absorb fertilizer yet, and strong chemical fertilizers placed too close can burn and destroy the seed before it sprouts. It is best to wait until roots develop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni shishifãi bɛ amɛhe lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui dani amɛkwɛ̃. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests build up in that spot. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: What is eating small holes into the center of my young maize plants and leaving waste behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni mishiɔ jwɛi yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the growing leaf whorl of maize and needs early treatment with approved insecticides or neem extract to protect the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ baai lɛ amli. ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ mra. kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and look wrinkled instead of spreading out flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Wrinkled or curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves. Spraying soaps or insecticides early prevents them from spreading crop diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahelai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, will I get more harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani ŋmaa babaoo baaba?

english: No, planting too close forces plants to fight for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small tubers. Proper spacing allows each plant to grow thick, heavy roots.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain stems?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ani ajie mi plantain shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many suckers starves the main plant. Keeping only the main mother stem, one medium follower stem, and one small sucker gives you much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ pɛ ni ooobua naa Tso lɛ yitso kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome baaha oná plantain ni da kwraa.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, reduces weeds, and turns into soil food as it rots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle mihe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Big shade trees protect cocoa leaves from burning and keep the soil moist during hot periods.
ga: Kokoo tsei, titri lɛ bibii lɛ, nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets extremely hot or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. Regular watering and root shade help keep flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build healthy green leaves. Heavy rains can also wash away these nutrients or leave the roots waterlogged, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ afee nu. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees lose water quickly through their leaves during dry spells like the Harmattan. Without enough moisture in the soil or shade trees to block hot winds, the tree drops its leaves to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ harmattan. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei lɛ ewo amɛhe shade kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my cassava plants when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly at first and cannot compete with weeds for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures the young cassava gets all the food it needs to build large roots later on.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei bibioo lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi wuji sɛɛ mli.

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are too shallow or if stem borer insects have weakened the stalk. Planting seeds at the correct depth and mounding soil around the base of the stems gives them stronger support.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli, ni ehaa tso lɛ mli gbɔjɔɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa kɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ. Tso lɛ shishi baaye abua ni eha dumɔwui lɛ awa.

english: How can I tell when my yams are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up at the end of the rainy season. This shows the plant has stopped growing and stored all its energy in the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excess leaves instead of pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when they get too much water while flowering. High nitrogen encourages leaf growth rather than flower and pod development.
ga: Cowpea woɔ baai ni fa fe nine yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa baa lɛ daa fe fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave all the shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Beni ashɛrɛɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main trunk lɛ he lɛ ashwieɔ?

english: Plantain suckers share the main stem's root system. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the mother plant for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller, lighter fruit bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses, or by stress from severe heat and drought. The curling reduces the leaf surface area, slowing down fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ mli. Curling haa baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ baa shi. Ha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: Why do small holes appear on my pepper leaves, and what is causing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi pepper baai lɛ anɔ Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛbaa?

english: Small holes on pepper leaves are usually caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars feeding on the green leaves. These pests chew the leaves mostly during the cool hours of the night or early morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars ni yeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai babaoo yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ mli.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, cool, and overly shady conditions. Rain drops splash the fungus onto the pods, causing them to decay if infected pods are not removed promptly.
