ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees protect them from sunburn, keep the soil cool, and hold moisture so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ama shishifãi ni wa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is hungry and lacks nitrogen. Feeding the soil with compost, manure, or the right fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni nitrogen bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha o-ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa koni etsɔ ŋmɔji ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Too much trapped water smothers the roots, causing underground rot, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni emɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early make my crops grow bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii wuji?

english: Weeds act like uninvited guests that steal food, water, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing them early ensures your plants get all the nutrients they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni afɔ̃ko amɛ nine, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ofɔ amɛhe mra lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are insects eating holes in my tomato leaves after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ bu yɛ mi tomato baa lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Warm rain combined with humidity creates ideal conditions for insect eggs to hatch and multiply quickly. Checking your crops regularly and using protection early keeps pests from destroying your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo fata he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi awɔlɔi ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite otsei lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil stay rich?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa?

english: Cowpeas and other beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally feed the soil and help neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra side shoots growing at the base of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo sɛɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra stems waste the plant's energy growing extra leaves instead of fruit. Trimming those extra shoots directs all the plant's food into making larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai krokomɛi ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye nii kwraa, ni ebaaha tomato agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do crops grown from certified seeds often do better than seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist common local diseases and harsh weather. Saved seeds from previous harvests often lose their strength and produce weaker plants over time.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it bad to plant pepper on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant loves and allows pests and soil diseases that target peppers to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown alongside them to shield them from excessive heat and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. When the plant grows heavy bunches of fruit, it becomes top-heavy, making it easy for rainwater-soaked soil to release the roots during heavy winds unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ aduawai akui ni tsii Ebaaná nɔ ni tsii fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ja akɛ tso nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that make food in their leaves using sunlight. Raising the leaves off the ground on sticks allows them to catch maximum sunlight and stay away from hot, damp soil, which encourages bigger tubers to grow underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and crop strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. The neighboring maize plants absorb this extra plant food to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ mli koni amɛdara waa.

english: How can I tell if the ground has enough water to plant my maize after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Grab a handful of topsoil from your farm and squeeze it tightly into a ball. If the ball stays together easily without dripping water, but crumbles when you touch it lightly, the soil has the right moisture to germinate seeds without rotting them.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa. Kɛji bɔɔlu lɛ kpɛtɛ he mlɛo ni nu shwieee Shi efoɔ kɛji eta he fioo pɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ ni egbooo.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat out the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing tender leaves hidden inside the central whorl of the maize plant. Catching them early with recommended biopesticides or ash mixtures prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni miida ni akɛtee ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus disrupts the movement of food inside the plant, causing twisted leaves and stopping the plant from producing quality fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Virus lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ gbɛfaa naa, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ awo yibii kpakpai.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save energy and survive when conditions are too harsh.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbuɔ hewalɛ he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy clay soils stay completely waterlogged for long periods, the roots choke from a lack of oxygen, allowing waterborne rot bacteria to break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli tse lɛ hiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: I have a small piece of empty land right behind my house. What simple food crops can I grow there to feed my family?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ, ni niyenii dumɔ waaa. Mɛɛ nɔ manyɛ makwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ koni makwɛ miweku lɛ?

english: Vegetables like peppers, garden eggs, tomatoes, and leafy greens (like kontomire) grow very well in small backyard spaces and produce yield continuously for household meals without requiring a big farm.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, tomato, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai (tamɔ contomir) kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ sɛɛgbɛ hei bibii ni amɛhaa shia niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa ni ehe ehiaaa ni afee ŋmɔ agbo.

english: Can I grow food crops right next to my house without damaging the building foundation?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ mishia lɛ masɛi ni mifiteee tsu lɛ shishitoo lɛ?

english: Yes, shallow-rooted crops like pepper, okra, garden eggs, and leafy greens are completely safe to grow near houses because their roots do not grow deep or thick enough to harm building foundations.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ ŋmeii, okra, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ shia lɛ masɛi shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛmli etseee bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite tsumaa shishitoo lɛ.

english: The ground in my backyard is very hard and dry. How do I prepare it so seeds can grow?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ wa waa ni egbi. Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mihe koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Clear the area, loosen the hard soil using a hoe to a depth of about a hand's length, and mix in decomposed dried grass or livestock dung to soften the earth so young roots can breathe and spread.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni miihe ashɛ nine kome nɔ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kooloi aŋmei ni egbo lɛ afutu mli koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ muɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa.

english: Is it okay to plant different crops together in a small backyard space, or will they choke each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ shia bibioo ko mli? Aloo tsei lɛ baatsi amɛhe?

english: Planting complementary crops together—such as cassava with beans, or maize with pepper—is actually good because crops like beans add natural nutrients into the soil that help feed the neighboring plants.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ehi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Chemical fertilizer is too expensive for me right now. How can I feed my crops without spending cash?
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa waa kɛha mi bianɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii?

english: You can make your own rich organic fertilizer called compost by gathering dry leaves, vegetable food scraps, ash, and manure, piling them up to rot with water, and applying the dark soil mixture around your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee bo diɛŋtsɛ o-nibii ni jara wa, ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ compost kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi ni ooobua naa lɛ nɔ. Akɛ tsei amli nibii ni efite, sũ kɛ ŋmeii toɔ he koni nu lɛ agbo. Ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ abɔle onibii ahe.

english: Times are difficult and I need food quickly. Which food crops mature the fastest after planting?
ga: Bei lɛ mli wa ni niyenii he miihia mi oya. Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya fe fɛɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Leafy green vegetables can be harvested in as little as 3 to 4 weeks, while crops like okra, beans, and sweet potatoes give food within 2 to 3 months of planting.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ okra, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii haa niyenii yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ.

english: How can I keep my small home garden alive during the dry season when water is scarce?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akwɛ shia abɔɔ bibioo ko nɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nu faaa lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your plant stems with dry grass or leaves (mulching) to trap moisture in the soil, and re-use household wash water (greywater without harsh detergents) to water the crop bases directly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai (mulch) aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni emɔ sũ lɛ mli nu. ni okɛ nu ni akɛfɔɔ he yɛ shia lɛ mli (nu ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli ni tsofai ni mli wa bɛ mli) atsu nii ni okɛfɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce many flowers during the season, but very few turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ? Shi mɛi fioo pɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Mango trees often lose flowers due to strong winds, dry weather stress, or tiny pests like thrips that feed on flowers before pollination happens; keeping the tree watered and protected from pests helps fruits set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ ni mango tsei lɛ fɔfɔi fiteɔ lɛ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛfeɔ pollination lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni abu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ ni etswaa shi.

english: Why do small mango fruits fall off the tree long before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees drop young fruit when they don't have enough water or soil nutrients to nourish all of them, or when fruit flies attack the young fruit; the tree naturally sheds extra fruit it cannot support.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii beni amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛye amɛbua lɛ. aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua aduawai bibii Tso lɛ baawo aduawai krokomɛi ni adebɔɔ naa nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my mango tree turn black and sticky when it is in season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa kɛ́ amɛshɛ be mli lɛ?

english: This black sticky coating is called sooty mold, caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mealybugs that secrete sweet liquid on the leaves; spraying the leaves with soapy water or mild neem oil helps clear it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ diŋ ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ akɛ sooty mold. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs ni jieɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee faŋŋ.

english: What is causing the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite?

english: That rot is black pod disease, a fungal infection caused by high humidity and heavy rains. It spreads quickly through rain splashes if infected pods are left on the tree or if approved protective fungicides are not applied.
ga: Black pod rot ji hela ko ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Is there a specific medicine or spray that can protect my cocoa trees from black pod disease?
ga: Ani tsofa ko loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ni baanyɛ abu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ black pod hela he yɛ?

english: Yes, using copper-based fungicides approved by the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) during the wet season protects your pods from fungal infection and stops the disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛ akɔɔble fee ni Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, ebaabu o-pods lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe helai ahe, ni ebaaha helai akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What should I do with cocoa pods that have already turned black so the disease does not spread?
ga: Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni helai akagbɛ ashwã kɛ́ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ diŋ?

english: Pluck all diseased pods off the trees immediately and bury them far away from the farm or burn them. Leaving infected pods on the trees allows rain to splash the fungus onto healthy pods.
ga: Jiemɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofu amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he loo oshã amɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aba ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does black pod disease get much worse on my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ mli wa waa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes black pod thrives in cool, damp conditions. Raindrops hit infected soil or pods and splash fungal spores onto healthy fruits, spreading the disease rapidly across your farm.
ga: Fung ni haa ŋmeii diji baa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. ni okɛ fungal spores lɛ afɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ hela oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does trimming excess branches from my cocoa trees help prevent black pod disease?
ga: Te niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod hela naa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to reach the pods. This dries out moisture on the leaves and pods quickly after rain, making it difficult for the black pod fungus to survive.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa black pod fungus lɛ akɛ eeehi shi.

english: How do I know if a farm chemical I bought is officially safe and approved for my cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛfaŋ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ mikɛ mi-kookoo lɛ atsu nii?

english: Always look for approval seals from the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) on the package, or consult your local extension officer. Official bodies like the Quality Control Division test chemicals to ensure they treat diseases without damaging your crops or cocoa beans.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo bi mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli tamɔ nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ Kaa tsofai lɛ okwɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsa helai ni amɛyeee onibii loo kookoo yibii lɛ awui.

english: What happens if I use an unverified or fake chemical on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo amalei tsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Unapproved chemicals can burn your cocoa trees, fail to cure the disease, and leave dangerous chemical residues in your harvested beans, causing buyers to reject your entire harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã cacao tsei. nyɛɛɛ atsa helai ni eshiɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kɔfi yibii ni akpa lɛ amli. Ha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akpoo onibii fɛɛ.

english: Can I use water from my farm well to mix spraying chemicals for my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu kpakpa ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afutu tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, well water can be used as long as it is clean and free of mud or dirt, which can weaken the chemical. However, always store and mix chemicals far away from the well head so you do not contaminate your drinking water supply.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ nubu mli nu atsu nii, kɛji akɛ ehe tse ni muji loo muji bɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ agbɔjɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ato be fɛɛ be ni akɛfutu mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ nubu lɛ yitso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Bɔni afee ni okafite nu ni onuɔ lɛ.

english: What support does the Ghana Cocoa Board provide when I have disease problems on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ Ghana Cocoa Board lɛ kɛhaa kɛ́ miyɛ hela ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: COCOBOD provides farmers with extension officers for practical advice, supplies approved inputs and fungicides, and conducts scientific research to test new methods and chemicals for controlling cocoa diseases.
ga: COCOBOD kɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔi haa okwaafoi koni amɛwo amɛ ŋaa ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii. Na nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii. ni amɛfee jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔi koni amɛkɛka gbɛi heei kɛ tsofai amɛkwɛ. yɛ kookoo hela lɛ nɔyeli mli

english: Why does the Quality Control Division test cocoa beans before they are exported?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ kaa kookoo yibii lɛ amɛkwɛɔ dani amɛkɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: They test cocoa to ensure the beans are well-dried, free from mold, and clear of harmful chemical residues. This protects consumer health and maintains Ghana's international reputation for high-quality cocoa.
ga: Amɛkaa kookoo lɛ amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi lo. Ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsofa ko bɛ mli ni eshwɛɛɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɛi ni yeɔ nii lɛ ahewalɛ he ni ebuɔ Ghana majimaji ateŋ gbɛi kpakpa ni eyɔɔ yɛ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in direct sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing companion plants like plantain to cover them and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata amɛhe ni daa oya tamɔ plantains koni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning dark brown and rotting before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in damp, cold, and excessively shaded farm conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches to allow sunlight in, and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. weeding Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ koni hulu la abote mli. Ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs nutrients for my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Tired soil often produces maize plants with pale yellow leaves, thin stalks, and small or incomplete cobs. These signs show that essential nutrients like nitrogen have been exhausted from the soil, requiring fertilizer or organic manure to restore productivity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmeii bibii, kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni yeee emuu. Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ miiho kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ wala mli atsu nii koni akɛsaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does laying dry leaves around my crop stems help them survive the heat?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ latsaa lɛ nɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It traps moisture in the ground, shields plant roots from hot sun rays, and slowly decomposes to add nutrients back to your soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize is effective because maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and expands after the maize is cleared, allowing you to maximize space and harvest two crops from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants must fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them correctly gives each plant enough room to develop strong roots and produce healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa aba ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop when the plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of specific nutrients like potassium. Consistent watering and ensuring balanced soil nutrients help the flowers stay on the plant and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko tamɔ potassium bɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my tree crops when they are growing so big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ aniji komɛi beni amɛdara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or extra branches so the plant doesn't waste energy feeding leaves it doesn't need. It allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner branches, encouraging the crop to focus its strength on producing more flowers and fruits.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛ baai ni ataooo lɛ haa lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Wo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai babaoo ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a sudden dry spell. If seeds sprout right after the first rain, the young roots may dry out and die in the hot soil before the regular rainy season fully begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sa lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital resources away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade because direct sunlight overheats their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping some shade trees or planting temporary shade crops protects them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛbaai bibii lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are there tiny caterpillars chewing holes through my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft center of maize leaves. Checking your farm early allows you to use appropriate controls before the caterpillars destroy the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni okɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa atsu nii dani ŋmeii lɛ akpata tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ hiɛ.

english: Excess water sitting in heavy soil starves the roots of air and allows fungal rot to spread. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the roots quickly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist during flowering helps the plant keep its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cowpeas and other beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root systems. When the plants decompose, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to nourish the crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need to reach up to sunlight to produce energy for expanding the heavy tubers underground, and keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ baai helai anaa.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Managing these insects early stops the virus from spreading to the rest of your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, lowers soil temperature under the sun, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ nɔ aba shi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Is it safe to plant cassava and maize together in the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, because maize grows rapidly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the slow-growing cassava behind to use the remaining space and mature on its own schedule.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi yucca ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni ekɛ he ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii ni eda yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛjianɔtoo naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help your crop recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing bunch. You should prop up the stem with a strong, forked wooden stick as soon as the fruit bunch appears to protect it from falling in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni tsii lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afi tso lɛ shishi kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je kpo pɛ koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the farm during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or lack of water. Watering your plants regularly around the base and spreading dry grass as mulch will keep the soil cool and help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Okɛ nu awo tsei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ amli. Base daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha nɔ kɛtsɔ mulch nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛma shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat. Controlling whiteflies early with neem oil sprays and keeping the plants well-watered stops the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Mra Whitefly Control Kɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ bɔ ni sa koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do tiny worms chew holes into my cowpea pods just as they start to fill up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛye bu yɛ mi tsina ŋmeii lɛ amli beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛyiɔ lɛ?

english: These worms are pod borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid inside the flowers by moths. Spraying organic or approved pest controls during the flowering stage prevents these insects from laying eggs on your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji pod borers ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant my rice in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting rice in straight rows gives each plant enough space, sunlight, and air to produce more stalks. It also makes weeding and applying fertilizer much easier without damaging your growing plants.
ga: Omɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why must I erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the food that grows big tubers under the soil. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and prevents fungal diseases that spread on damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their flowers before turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛtsɔmɔɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off easily if the air is too dry, if the soil lacks moisture, or if insects attack them. Maintaining shade trees on your farm helps trap humidity and keep the air cool enough for pods to form.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. aloo kooloi bibii yɛ ni tutuaa Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large leaves but refusing to form tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi efeŋ yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form heads when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, irregular watering, or excessive heat. Using balanced fertilizer and maintaining steady soil moisture encourages the inner leaves to fold tightly into a head.
ga: Kaabaji efeŋ yitsei kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nine shɛɔ dɔlɛ babaoo nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaawo mligbɛ baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfolɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ kɛya yitso lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I plant them in a cleared field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct overhead sun. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, preserving moisture and protecting the young trees until they grow strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná la ni fa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize crops turning yellow instead of staying rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food crop plants use to make green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores green color and helps the plant grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji lɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni amɛdara.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting to insert into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small raised buds or leaf eyes along the stalk. The stem must be planted with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow directly up; planting them upside down weakens the plant and reduces harvest.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo baai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he. Esa akɛ adu tsei lɛ ahe ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high to capture sunlight for energy. Keeping the leaves off the bare ground also prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the leaves and allows maximum food production for bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni emɔ hulu la kɛha hewalɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni fiteɔ baa lɛ anaa, ni ehaa niyenii babaoo baa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward into tight cups and stopping fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper bushes are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves. Sucking out the plant's juices distorts leaf growth and starves the plant, preventing pepper pods from swelling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ mɔ ko nu nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, efiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ. Koni pepper pods lɛ akafu

english: Why should I cut off some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajieɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow around one mother plant creates competition for soil water, food, and light. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong replacements, ensuring the main plant yields large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu, niyenii kɛ la he, ni ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa ni baaye najiaŋ lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them after a heavy-feeding crop like maize naturally restores lost plant food back into the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aku tso mli niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off to the ground without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant faces extreme stress, usually caused by long hot dry spells or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay on the vine and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto my soil during a hot, dry weather spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only absorb fertilizer nutrients when those nutrients are dissolved in soil water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots and waste expensive fertilizer, as it sits unusable until rain falls.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli niyenii kɛji akɛ nakai niyenii lɛ shwie nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. Ejaakɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow well in flooded soil while my maize rots and dies under the same condition?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishi ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have specialized internal airways in their stems that carry oxygen down to their submerged roots. Maize lacks these internal air pathways, causing its roots to suffocate and rot when standing in deep water for too long.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi pɛ ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛdamɔ nu ni mli kwɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants do not like strong direct sunlight because their young roots cannot pull up water fast enough to replace what the sun bakes away. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye nɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ najiaŋ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ashishifãi ni buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shwereɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop even produces corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmãa dani tso lɛ po woɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting at the tips, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa shishigbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves above ground, but only tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or overly rich manure without balanced plant nutrients, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni tsei amli niyenii ni sa lɛ bɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato ŋmei yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa ŋmei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight over water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves block sunlight from each other. This causes the stalks to grow thin and weak, resulting in small corn cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii baa loo ŋmãa ko bɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers on the ground instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat or water stress. If the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu mli haomɔ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slow even when I rain water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and act like food thieves—they take up nitrogen, phosphorus, and moisture from the soil much faster than your crops can. Even with water, your crops will grow slowly because the weeds are stealing their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ enii tamɔ niyenii julɔ. Amɛheɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛ nu po yɔɔ mli lɛ, onibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio ejaakɛ jwɛi miiju amɛ niyenii.

english: Why does putting dry grass on the soil around my tomato plants help them survive heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-tomato tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Dry grass acts like an umbrella over the soil, stopping the strong sun from evaporating water out of the ground. It keeps the soil cool and moist so the plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates very damp and cool air, which allows tiny fungal spores to grow quickly. Raindrops splash these fungi from infected leaves or soil directly onto the cocoa pods, turning them black.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni mli ejɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ daraa. shwereɔ oya Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ amɛ ediŋŋ

english: Why does my land yield less harvest if I plant maize on the same patch of soil every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on the exact same plant food year after year, which empties those nutrients from the soil. Planting the same crop repeatedly also allows soil pests and diseases that eat maize to build up in that spot.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ tso niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi. Enɛ baaha nakai niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: How do crops like cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have natural nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into rich plant food in the soil. When the crop dies, that natural food stays in the ground for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ mli efeɔ tsei aniyenii ni baa nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Beni ŋmɔshi nibii gboi lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do people plant plantains on the same farm next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi duɔ plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu lɛ naa lɛ,.

english: Yam is a climbing vine. Staking the vine on sticks lifts the leaves toward the sunlight, allowing the plant to capture light and make food to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Atomɔ ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooodu yɛ tso nine nɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa la ni efeɔ niyenii bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afuu.

english: What should I do when small pests start making noise and destroying my crop leaves in the farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii fee dedei ni wa ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai?

english: You should inspect the undersides of the leaves to identify the pest type, clear surrounding weeds where pests hide, and apply neem leaf spray or an approved organic pesticide to protect the crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni ona tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ henɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. He ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli Ni okɛ neem baa mli spray loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How can I stop insects and nocturnal animals from coming to eat my vegetables at night?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mi aduawai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi-vegetables lɛ gbɛkɛ?

english: Keeping the edges of your farm cleared of thick bush reduces hiding spots, and setting up physical barriers like fencing or reflective farm ribbons helps keep night pests away.
ga: Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ he tse kɛjɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hei ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii tamɔ gbogboi loo tsɔnei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni aaafee lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akabote mli gbɛkɛ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering during dry weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogging around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure and improving water drainage will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he ni aha nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is suitable for planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained sandy-loam soil. Heavy clay soils hold too much water and block the roots from expanding into large cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei agboi.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when the plant lacks adequate nutrients during its flowering stage.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ

english: Weeds are native wild plants adapted to absorb nutrients and water faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and light from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: When is the best time to plant my seeds after the major rainy season begins in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ eje shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to plant right after the first steady rains begin so the seeds can soak up enough soil moisture to germinate and build strong roots before dry spells occur.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ je shishi lɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ sũ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani hulutsoo be aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key food that helps plants stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains have soaked the ground for too long, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so the plant roots can actually drink it in. If you put fertilizer on dry soil under a hot sun, it can burn the plant roots and get wasted.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ baashã ni amɛbaafite.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there seems to be enough soil for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛ fɛɛ yɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbours; they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, your crops become weak and yield much less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani miduɔ yucca lɛ yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, it matters very much. You must look at the small buds on the stem and make sure they point upward toward the sky; if you plant the stem upside down, the plant will waste energy trying to correct itself and produce very small tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa, okwɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni okwɛ akɛ amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ejaje ehe lɛ ni ekɛ bulbs bibii waa baa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate like human babies and burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have huge leaves that create living shade to protect the cocoa trees during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa tamɔ adesai abifabii, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is the best one for me to dig up and plant on my new land?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ?

english: Choose 'maidenhead' or spear suckers, which are shoots with thick bases and narrow, blade-like leaves. Avoid suckers that already have broad, flat leaves because their roots are weaker and they take longer to settle after transplanting.
ga: Halamɔ ‘obalayoo yitso’ loo akpɔlɔ tso, ni ji tso ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli tse kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmei. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ momo lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛmaa shi yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot during the afternoon, or when the plant does not get enough water continuously. Keeping the soil covered with dry grass mulching helps keep the roots cool and saves the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ shwane mli. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafiteɔ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on tall stakes gets them into the sunlight and keeps the leaves off damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ wein tsei lɛ anɔ, ni ehaaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant juices. Spraying neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap helps clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efɔ he.

english: Is it bad if I water my vegetable garden in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is very strong?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering in the midday heat wastes water because the hot air turns it to vapor before roots absorb it, and water droplets left on leaves can focus sunlight like glass and scorch the leaves.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya sɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa efeɔ lasu dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala hulu la lɛ tamɔ glase ni eha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong stems and leafy growth. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hia tsei kɛha amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ baai adalɛ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I put fertilizer in the soil at the same time I plant my crop seeds, or wait until after they grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ loo mamɛ kɛyashi amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until about two weeks after seeds sprout before applying main fertilizers like urea or NPK. Young seedlings cannot absorb heavy fertilizer yet, and applying it too early risks burning the delicate young roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ aaafee otsi enyɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK awo mli. Tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii lolo. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii oya tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baashã.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes through the center of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni aye bu bibioo ko Yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on maize leaves. You can control them early by applying recommended insecticides or neem leaf extracts directly into the leaf whorls as soon as you spot tiny holes.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji ana buji bibii pɛ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and get white and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread between plants by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-free stems from certified agricultural sources prevents this virus from ruining your field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni helai bɛ mli ni jɛ okwaayeli hei ni awo he hewalɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akabote he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent with mulching helps roots steadily transport calcium to the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulching tsuɔ nii daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ daa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct harsh sunlight burns their soft leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving large trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment for seedlings to survive their first two years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently. Staking keeps leaves dry and clean, which prevents fungal rot and helps the plant send more energy down to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhe tseɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afite, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look wilted during hot afternoons even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from excessive heat, but it naturally recovers as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. Shi ebaatsa ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoots to cut and plant on a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ mlifomɔ kɛdumɔ?

english: Look for 'maiden suckers', which are shoots with narrow, sword-like leaves rather than wide leaves. These suckers have stronger underground corms and produce healthier, faster-growing plantain trees.
ga: Taomɔ ‘bamboo shoots’, ni ji tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ klante yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Nɛkɛ suckers nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi rhizomes ni mli wa ni amɛwoɔ plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daa oya.

english: How does clearing weeds from around my crops actually help them grow bigger fruit?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Removing weeds regularly leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops, helping them grow stronger and yield larger produce.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa onibii lɛ. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my rice farm need so much water compared to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in very wet soil because their roots are adapted to pull oxygen even when submerged. Standing water also acts as a natural barrier that prevents weeds from growing and competing with the rice for food.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛji amɛyɔɔ nu shishi po. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akaŋ akaŋ kɛha niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crop turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks essential nutrients in the soil, especially nitrogen, or when the roots are receiving too much water. Feeding the soil with compost or manure gives the leaves their healthy green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ náa nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants enough space allows them to grow thick stems and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tsei lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop so much during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and grow slowly at first, while weeds grow very fast. If weeds are not cleared early, they steal the light, water, and soil nutrients your young crops need to survive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaada blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa lɛ. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my soil dry out and crack so quickly when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly to the sun's heat through evaporation. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and traps moisture where the roots can reach it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hei ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why does my land yield less food when I plant rice in the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts restores nutrients and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crop drop off without producing any food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo niyenii ko lɛ?

english: Crop flowers often fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil properly watered helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ fɔfɔii, ni no baaha ewo yibii.

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm more aggressively right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The warm rain causes crops and nearby bushes to sprout fresh, tender leaf growth, which attracts insects to feed, lay eggs, and multiply rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai bibii. ni gbalaa kooloi bibii koni amɛtao niyenii, amɛwo wɔji, ni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Rice is ready to harvest when the crop turns golden yellow and most of the grain heads hang downward. Waiting too long causes the grains to dry out completely and shatter onto the ground during cutting.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmaa yitsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwie shi lɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ agbi kwraa ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ yɛ be mli ni afoɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain spoil and catch mold when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Grain spoils in storage when it still contains hidden moisture inside the seeds at harvest. Drying the harvested grains thoroughly under the sun until they are hard prevents mold and insects from ruining your harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ lolo ni akɛtee dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ akpa. Kɛ́ ogbala odumɔwui ni okpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaawa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn under direct sunlight. Retaining shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa provides a cooler shelter and holds soil moisture, helping the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eye ebua kookoo ni ehi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow along the middle vein while the rest of the farm is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main stem or leaf center is a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen. Applying poultry manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the roots gives the maize the nutrient it needs to stay green and build large ears.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ loo ebaa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii yɛ Shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: If I cut off the top leafy branches of my cassava plant early, will the roots underground stop growing bigger?
ga: Kɛji mifo niji ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli lɛ mra lɛ, Ani shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baakpa shweremɔ?

english: Yes, cassava roots swell by feeding on food created by the green leaves above ground. If you remove the leaves too early, the plant loses its main way of making food, causing the underground tubers to stay thin and woody.
