ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fee lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ojie baai lɛ oya tsɔ Tsei lɛ baafite gbɛ titri ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots and applying straw mulch helps maintain stable temperatures so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing green shoots in the barn even when I have not planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ be mli ni miduuu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that naturally wake up and sprout when air temperatures rise and the air becomes humid, signalling the start of the rain. Keeping your storage barn well-ventilated, shaded, and cool delays this natural sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ tee hiɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. ni ji nugbɔshiimɔ he okadi Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, hulutsoo, kɛ fɛ̃i baaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize make the maize stalks grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the ground through their root nodules. The surrounding maize roots absorb this natural food from the soil, growing thicker and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi shishifãi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting twisted like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled, twisted pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. Spraying neem seed extract early helps keep these insects off the leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni etse ehe lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem dumɔwu mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akagbee shi kɛjɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree give smaller bunches when I allow all the shoots coming from the base to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain akui lɛ daraaa lɛ? Akɛni miha ŋmeii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ekome kɛdaraa hewɔ lɛ.

english: Multiple suckers growing from the base steal water, food, and sunlight away from the main fruiting stem. Removing extra shoots and keeping only one or two healthy suckers allows the parent plant to concentrate its energy on growing a large bunch.
ga: Suckers babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ yibiiwoo tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ahiɛ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso agbo ko ni ebaakwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my upland rice heads stay empty and light even though the plants grew tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni amɛkpɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Rice requires continuous soil moisture during its flowering stage to form grain inside the husk. If a dry spell hits right when flowers open, the plant cannot move nutrients upward, leaving empty, chaffy grain heads.
ga: Omɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli koni enyɛ efee dumɔwui yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii ba be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ pɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ayitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do weeds cause my young vegetable crops to grow tall, thin, and weak instead of short and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When weeds crowd around young crops, they block sunlight. The young crop stretches rapidly toward the sky to reach light, spending all its energy growing tall and thin instead of building thick stems and strong branches.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ Amɛbaatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Hewalɛ fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛdara ni egbɔjɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ niji nɛ he wa.

english: Why are the maize seeds I bought from the certified dealer doing so much better than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ hi kwraa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred, tested, and treated to be free from hidden diseases. Seeds saved from previous harvests often carry over unseen fungi or bacteria and tend to produce weaker plants over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ, akaa amɛ akwɛɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ akafee amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ni anaaa amɛ. ni esumɔɔ ni eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if the pepper seeds I bought are contaminated with disease before I put them in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela yɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛdu?

english: Many seed contamination issues are invisible to the naked eye because fungi or bacteria live inside or on the seed coat. Buying certified seeds from reputable agricultural officers and using recommended seed treatments before planting are the best ways to protect your crop.
ga: Naagbai babaoo ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli mujiwoo mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni hiŋmɛii enaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi hiɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli loo yɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yɔɔ gbɛi kpakpa lɛ dɛŋ ni ooohe ni okɛ dumɔwui ahe tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii dani odu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu onibii ahe.

english: Why are my cassava cuttings rotting in the ground even though they came from healthy-looking stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ejɛɔ?

english: Cassava cuttings can get contaminated after being cut if they are stored in damp, dirty areas or cut with unclean tools before planting. The germs infect the open ends of the stem, causing them to rot once planted.
ga: Cassava tsei ni afo lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni muji yɔɔ mli beni afo lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni muji yɔɔ. aloo akɛ nibii ni he tseee afo dani adu Helatsɛ lɛ tsɛŋeɔ tsei lɛ anaagbee ni agbele lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu lɛ, ebaagbo.

english: Is it bad to store my seed yam tubers in a dark, damp room before the planting season starts?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baato tsu ko ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ mli dani ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Yes, damp and unventilated storage encourages mold, rot, and early sprouting. Storing yam tubers in clean, dry, and well-ventilated sheds prevents disease contamination before you put them in the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitoohe ni efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei, fitemɔ kɛ kwɛ̃mɔ mra he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ to he ko ni mli tse, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa dani adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why did my cocoa seedlings start dying shortly after I transported them from the nursery to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings can get damaged or exposed to dirty conditions and heat during transport. Stresses or dirty handling environments weaken the young plants, allowing diseases to quickly infect them before they take root.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afite loo amɛyaje shihilɛi ni mli ewo muji kɛ dɔlɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. Haomɔ loo shihilɛ ni mli ewo muji ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ha helai srɔtoi Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya dani ewoɔ shishifãi.

english: Can disease spread across my farm if I get plantain suckers from my neighbor's farm?
ga: Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji minine shɛ plantain ŋmeii anɔ kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, plantain suckers can carry hidden pests like nematodes or viral diseases from the source farm. Even if the sucker looks clean, planting infected material brings the disease directly into your clean soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain suckers baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ nematodes loo helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ ni amɛjɛ mli lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ suction cup lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse moŋ Shi nibii ni hela emɔ lɛ ni adu lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya shikpɔŋ ni he tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can using the same cutlass across my whole farm spread sickness from one plant to another?
ga: Ani dagger kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ?

english: Yes, cutlasses and pruning tools carry infected sap from sick plants to healthy ones. Cleaning your tools with soapy water or disinfectant after trimming sick plants prevents you from spreading disease around your farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dadei kɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ woɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai tsu nii kɛtsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings fall over and rot right at the soil level shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛyashɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is called 'damping-off,' which happens when soil or trays used for nursery beds contain fungal spores that attack tender stems. Using clean, treated soil for nurseries prevents this early contamination.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ loo tray ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni asaa he lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii kɛha ŋmɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite muji yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when people say I should treat my seeds before planting, and how does it help?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ dumɔwui anɔ dani adu lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua?

english: Treating seeds means coating them with safe protective fungicides or insecticides before planting. This creates a protective shield that kills any germs on the seed surface and prevents soil insects from attacking it.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ awo amɛhe dani adu. Enɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ hiɛ lɛ baa, ni ehaa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tutuaa lɛ.

english: How do germs get into my crop when the plant is still very young?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Germs can enter young crops through contaminated planting materials, dirty water, infected nursery soil, or unwashed hands and tools used during transplanting.
ga: Helai baanyɛ abote ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli kɛtsɔ dumɔ nii ni mli ewo muji, nu ni mli ewo muji, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ mli lɛ nɔ. loo niji kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ ni afɔɔɔ he.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ shade kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi.

english: Dried grass acts as mulch, keeping the soil moist, preventing weeds from taking over, and protecting crop roots from getting scorched by the hot sun.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ. ni ebu tsei shishifãi ahe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to build up. Swapping maize with cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with natural nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii komɛi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Cassava roots rot easily if water sits around them. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away, giving the roots loose soil to grow large and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Gbalamɔ shishifãi lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbo ni efee shiŋŋ.

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil food without fighting its neighbor.
ga: Aaafee sɛntimitai 75 ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ kɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 40 ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or the soil is too wet. Giving the plants nitrogen fertilizer early helps them stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa tsei mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Applying recommended neem oil or pest control into the center of the plant early stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the flowers stay on and grow into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I cut off some of the lower branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra shoots and lower leaves forces the plant to send its food and energy into growing bigger tomato fruits rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ aya tomatoi wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds sprout and the rain stops, the tender seedlings will dry up and die. Waiting for steady rains ensures your crops survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha onibii ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow before the crop is even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. It can also happen when there is too much water drowning the roots in heavy clay soil or when dry weather stops the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni tsii mli loo kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the days get extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat dries out the flower pollen, so the plant sheds the flower because it cannot produce a seed.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ bɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui lɛ hewɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites that hide under the leaves and suck the plant juices. They can also pass a leaf-curl virus to the crop while feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ leaf curl hela lɛ hu aha ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: The very first rain often triggers seeds to sprout, but it is usually followed by a dry hot stretch before the main rainy season fully establishes. If the soil dries out completely right after sprouting, your young seedlings will burn and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Otsei bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do I need to clear away some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: If too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and soil food. Cutting away the extra shoots allows the main tree to get full energy and produce a very large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, single main trunk Amɛbaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii hu. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ebaawo ŋmeii babaoo, babaoo, ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing tuber under the ground. If the vines lie flat on the hot soil, they get scorched, catch rot diseases easily, and yield very small yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛji wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Amɛbaashã. Efiteɔ oya. ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa

english: Why do older farmers cover the soil around their crop roots with dried grass and dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni egboi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and suppresses weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni ekpaa jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ naa

english: Can putting too much chemical fertilizer on my crops actually end up killing them?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, putting too much chemical fertilizer creates a salty environment around the roots. Instead of the roots drinking water, the fertilizer pulls water out of the plant, causing the crop to wither and look burned.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ anu nu lɛ, Fertilizer baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbeɔ la he guɔ.

english: What causes the cocoa pods on my farm to turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. When rain drops bounce off infested soil onto low pods, or when high humidity stays trapped in thick shade, the fungus grows and rots the cocoa pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ nɔ eshwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo, ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ hulutsoo be mli Fɛ̃i lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni eha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest since they grow under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a long stem with foliage only at the top, and the soil near the stem base begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ, tso lɛ yitso kakadaŋŋ kɛ baai lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Can I grow cocoa successfully in other regions of Ghana outside the Western North Region?
ga: Minyɛ midu kookoo yɛ omanyeyeli mli yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ. ni yɔɔ Ghana ni yɔɔ Kooyi-Anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa grows well in several other regions of Ghana such as Ashanti, Eastern, Central, Ahafo, and Western South, as long as the soil is fertile and there is adequate rainfall and shade.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ. Ghana hei babaoo tamɔ Ashanti, Bokagbɛ, Teŋgbɛ, Ahafo kɛ Anaigbɛ Anaigbɛ kpokpai. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if the strange marks on my cocoa leaves mean my farm has a serious disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo baai anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hela ni naa wa?

english: Diseases often cause leaves to turn yellow, develop dark spots, or cause branches to swell and die back. Having an extension officer inspect your farm is the best way to identify the exact disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Hei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo loo ehaa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛgboiɔ Ni oooha extension nitsulɔ ko akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aleɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the young shoots on my crop turning brown and drying up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely strong sunlight and high heat can scorch tender new shoots if the plants do not have enough shade trees or soil moisture to protect them.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashã ŋmeii heei kɛji tso lɛ bɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu ehe.

english: What steps should I take if an extension officer discovers a disease on my cocoa farm?
ga: Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ na hela yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ amɛfee?

english: You should follow the officer's guidance, which often involves cutting out infected branches or trees to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy parts of your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ nitsulɔi lɛ agbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji tsei niji loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Can a plant disease from my neighbor's farm spread to my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani helai ni jɛɔ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, many crop diseases spread easily between neighboring farms through wind, rain, insects, or shared pruning tools that carry the disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, loo nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni hiɛ hela lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ.

english: If I cut off diseased branches from my cocoa tree, will it shoot fresh healthy leaves again?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo tso nine ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ, Ani ebaakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, if the disease has not infected the entire plant, pruning away bad branches allows the tree to direct its energy into growing healthy new shoots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji hela lɛ eshɛɛɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Niji ni ehiii ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why would an officer advise me to cut down an entire cocoa tree instead of just treating it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafo cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ fe ni matsa lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain devastating viral diseases infect the whole plant system, meaning the tree cannot be cured and must be completely removed to protect nearby healthy trees.
ga: Virus helai komɛi ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ gbɛ eshwa tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ anyɛŋ atsa tso lɛ kwraa. ni esa akɛ ajie fɛɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does harsh sunlight affect the growth and behavior of my young cocoa trees?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛjeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Direct harsh sun without shade stresses young trees, causing shoot burning, leaf drop, and stunted growth because young cocoa plants require moderate shade to thrive.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa, ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii haoɔ. Enɛ haa shãa, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshwere.

english: Why is it necessary for an extension officer to visit my farm in person to check my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ayasara miŋmɔ lɛ koni amɛbakwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: An in-person farm visit allows the officer to examine the leaves, soil, and field conditions directly, which is crucial for making an accurate diagnosis of pests or diseases.
ga: Gbɔmɔtsoŋ saramɔi ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ tsei ahe tsei, shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ he hiaa koni ana tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce weak new shoots even when I weed the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weak shoots can be caused by underlying soil nutrient deficiencies, hidden root diseases, or severe weather stress, which weeding alone cannot fix.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ aba. Shishifã hela ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn the bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã tsei bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys beneficial living organisms in the ground, burns away valuable organic matter, and makes the soil dry out much faster under the sun.
ga: Taakɛ shãa lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu. Shãa nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya kwraa yɛ hulu la shishi.

english: Why do I need to rotate my crops instead of planting maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and soil diseases to build up, whereas rotating crops keeps the soil healthy and disrupts pest lifecycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi komɛi aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why should I mound the soil around my yam seeds instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua muji naa kɛbɔle he lɛ? Sweet potato dumɔwui moŋ fe ni ooodu amɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Mounding creates soft, loose soil that makes it easy for the yam tuber to expand deep underground while also preventing water from gathering around the roots and rotting the crop.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or that too much water is choking the roots; applying a nitrogen fertilizer or improving drainage will help the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo eyɛ nu babaoo ni miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Young cassava plants have weak root systems and must compete directly with weeds for sunlight, water, and nutrients; removing weeds early allows the crop to establish strong roots and build bigger tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool, shaded conditions; pruning extra tree branches lets air and sunlight in to dry out the pods and prevent the fungus.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are sick with a disease or just drying up from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ loo amɛgbi kɛkɛ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli?

english: Heat causes leaves to curl upwards without changing color much, whereas diseases usually cause spots, yellowing, rotting on the fruits, or sudden wilting even when the soil is wet.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe su tsakeee kwraa. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ haa aduawai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. loo egbi trukaa, kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning brown and drying up from the edges even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: This is often caused by leaf diseases like Sigatoka or tiny worms in the soil eating the roots, which prevents the plant from drinking water properly even when the ground is damp.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, foli helai tamɔ Sigatoka loo ŋmeii bibii kɛ enɛ baa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Enɛ haaa tsei anu nu jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly on a tarp before putting it into bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tarp nɔ dani mikɛwoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storing damp maize traps moisture, which encourages dangerous mold growth and attracts crop-destroying insects like weevils during storage.
ga: Abele ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not have strong leaves yet and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or leguminous trees to keep the air humid and protect the leaves while the tree is growing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lolo, ni kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo legumes amli. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi ni ebu baai lɛ ahe be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Yellowing in the middle of maize leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the key soil nutrient that helps leaves stay green and make food for the plant to grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa niyenii kɛha tsei lɛ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: When rain sits on the field for too long without draining, it blocks air from getting into the soil. Without air, the cassava roots suffocate and soil fungi quickly cause them to decay.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. The maize puts all its energy into growing tall to catch light instead of making big cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Abɛi kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛdaraa koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences water stress, which prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and return it into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ, heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ leebi?

english: These holes are caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day and come out to eat the young leaves at night or early morning.
ga: Nɛkɛ buji nɛɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ amli. ni amɛjeɔ kpo amɛbayeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa

english: Yam plants produce tubers based on how much sunlight their leaves catch. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground towards the sun and protects them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii yɛ hulu la ni baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ falɛ naa. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni etsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal the water and fertilizer from the soil faster than your crops can absorb them, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni ogbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during windy storms when they are bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli beni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. When rain softens the ground, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the mud.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Je kpo kɛjɛ muji lɛ mli mlɛo

english: It is usually better to wait until the rains become regular. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which can dry up the soil and kill young seeds before they can properly grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii dani amɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which way to put my cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni akɛ ŋmei tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ mli kɛ́ adu?

english: Look closely at the tiny buds where leaves used to grow on the stem stick. Make sure these buds are pointing upward toward the sky so the fresh green shoots can easily grow up into the light.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ehiɔ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpaakpa. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam plants to tall wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing disease and helping the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do older farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of their crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ amɛhe lɛ? Amɛtso lɛ shishitoo lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, stops water from drying out quickly under the hot sun, and prevents unwanted weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ naa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green leaves. Heavy rains can also wash this food out of reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant finishes growing, that extra food stays in the dirt, making the soil richer for the next crop you plant there.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Nakai niyenii ni fa lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli kɛ powda bibii ni tamɔ muji ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the center of the young plant during the daytime and feeds on the tender new leaves before they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni oye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are sucking juices from the undersides of the leaves, or passing a virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies he okadi. Nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa tsei

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers dropping off before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed, usually because the weather is too hot or the soil is going from very dry to very wet suddenly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ he ni egbi waa kɛyaa he ni edɔ waa.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me make more profit from my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi koni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers provide expert advice on correct farming techniques, timely pest management, and crop care to ensure your farm yields more harvest and brings in higher profits.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ okwaayeli ŋaai ni ja he. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɛ be naa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo.

english: How does increasing my crop yield help both my household and Ghana as a whole?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishia lɛ kɛ Ghana fɛɛ?

english: Producing more crops increases your personal income at market while contributing to food security and national trade, which strengthens Ghana's economy.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooofee lɛ baaha bo diɛŋtsɛ oshika ni onáa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa maŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ jarayeli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ Ghana shika helɛtemɔ.

english: Why do my crop plants produce flowers before they start growing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Flowers are the plant's natural reproductive stage where pollination happens; once a flower is pollinated, it develops into the fruit, grain, or pod you harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji tsei adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ be ni pollination baa mli. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wo mli lɛ Etsɔɔ aduawai, dumɔwui, loo ŋmeii ni okpaa.

english: Why are bees and other insects important when my crops are blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe hiaa be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ?

english: Insects carry pollen from flower to flower, which fertilizes the blossoms so they can grow into healthy fruits and seed pods.
ga: Kplukai kɛ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Akɛ fɔfɔi woɔ amɛmli bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui akutsei.

english: What causes the flowers on my crops to drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Flowers can fall off due to extreme heat, insufficient water, heavy chemical spraying, or a lack of natural pollinating insects.
ga: Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni tsii loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ ni bɛ

english: How can I tell if my crop plants are healthy and thriving?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshwereɔ?

english: Thriving crops show rich leaf color, steady growth, strong stems, and healthy flowering without unexpected leaf loss or withered blossoms.
ga: Tsei ni shwereɔ lɛ baajie baai lɛ ahe su ni yɔɔ fɛo kpo. stable growth strong trunk kɛ fɔfɔi ni yeɔ emuu ni baai lɛ sɛɛ efooo loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi trukaa.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical pesticides on my crops while they are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Spraying during flowering can kill beneficial insects that pollinate your crops and cause delicate blossoms to drop off, reducing your final yield.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ni eha fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji naagbee nibii ni anáa lɛ nɔbaa.

english: When is the best growth stage to spray my crops to control pests safely?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shweshweeshwe koni akɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ?

english: It is best to spray before the plants start blooming or after the flowering stage has finished, so you protect insects and fragile blossoms.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ abɔi fɔmɔ loo yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ sɛɛ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii kɛ fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ ahe

english: Can applying chemical sprays at the wrong time damage my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, spraying harsh chemicals during blooming or under hot sun can burn tender plant leaves and destroy flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi loo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbe fɔfɔii lɛ dani aduawai aba.

english: What should I do to protect my crop flowers so I get the biggest harvest possible?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Leave the flowers undisturbed by avoiding pesticide sprays during blooming, maintaining good soil moisture, and letting pollinators work safely.
ga: Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ni nɔ ko akagbala amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa. ni amɛha ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu amɛnitsumɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to drain and replace standing water around my crops every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo nu ni damɔ shi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli ni matsake lɛ daa otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Standing water loses its oxygen over time and can breed fungi or bacteria that cause roots to rot. Refreshing the water keeps the root system healthy, oxygenated, and disease-free.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ fungi loo bacteria ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba. Nu lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ. nine shɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nɔ ni hela bɛ ehe

english: Why should I harvest or remove my crops as soon as they get very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa loo mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji eda pɛ?

english: Leaving overgrown crops in the bed takes away water and nutrients from smaller plants. Removing big crops when ready gives smaller ones room to grow while preventing the mature ones from going bad.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu kɛ niyenii ni haa tsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji kɛji amɛfee klalo lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei ni eda lɛ afitemɔ naa.

english: What should I do if some seedlings in my water bed grow much faster than the others?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi nu lɛ mli lɛ daraa oya kwraa fe ekrokomɛi?

english: You can gently pick out the bigger seedlings and plant them out in the field early. This creates space and allows the slower-growing seedlings to get enough sunlight and water to catch up.
ga: Obaanyɛ Ohala dumɔwui wuji fiofio ni odu amɛ mra yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa gbɛ baa ni eha dumɔwui ni daraa blɛoo lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does leaving dirty or old water in my vegetable bed affect my plants?
ga: Te nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu momo ni ashiɔ yɛ aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Old water collects dirt, waste, and harmful microbes that block plant roots from taking in food. Replacing old water prevents root suffocation and keeps your plants growing strong.
ga: Nu momo buaa muji, jwɛi, kɛ nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tsiɔ tso shishifãi anaa koni amɛkabote tso lɛ niyenii mli lɛ anaa. Nu momo ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akatsi amɛhe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I allow my crops to get too crowded as they grow?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ tsɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots compete for food. Thinning them out ensures every plant gets what it needs.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ afee amɛ mlɛo lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Can keeping the same water in my vegetable garden for too long bring pests?
ga: Ani nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛtoɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba?

english: Yes, stagnant water attracts harmful pests like insects and mosquitoes, and creates a humid environment where fungal diseases spread easily among young plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei bibii lɛ amli oya.

english: If I am growing vegetables directly in water, do I need to add fresh nutrients every time I change the water?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni odu aduawai yɛ nu mli tɛ̃ɛ Ani esa akɛ mikɛ niyenii heei afata he be fɛɛ be ni matsake nu lɛ?

english: Yes, because growing plants quickly absorb the nutrients dissolved in water. When you empty old water and put in fresh water, you must add fresh plant nutrients so they don't starve.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli lɛ oya. Beni okɛ nu momo lɛ shwieɔ shi ni okɛ nu kpakpa fataa he lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tso mli niyenii heei afata he koni hɔmɔ akaye bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe.

english: How do I know if my crop roots are drowning from too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu mli tsɔ?

english: If your plant leaves start turning yellow, feeling soft, or wilting even when the ground is wet, the roots are likely drowning from lack of air in soggy soil or standing water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ, enu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo, loo egbo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ. Shishifãi hu sumɔɔ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni ekã shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Is it okay to leave fully grown vegetables in the ground if I am not ready to sell them?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ashi aduawai ni edara yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛji mifeee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the bed for too long can make them tough, bitter, or prone to rot and pest attacks. It is usually best to pick them when mature and store them properly.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ebaanyɛ efite kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ akpa amɛ kɛji amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to control when water enters and leaves my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ be mli ni nu boteɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ?

english: Controlling water flow helps you give plants water when they are thirsty, and drain the field when roots need air or when it is time for the crops to dry and ripen before harvest.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ haa onyɛɔ ohaa tsei nu kɛ́ kumai miiye amɛ. ni okɛ nu afɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shishifãi lɛ he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ. aloo be mli ni be eshɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni ekwɛ̃ dani akpa.

english: During hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can draw it up. This temporary wilting is the plant's natural defense to reduce heat surface area, and it usually bounces back in the cooler evening once the sun sets.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛha e-thermal surface he ni ebaa shi lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a response to attack by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus transmitted by them. These pests suck the plant's sap, causing the young leaves to distort and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji hetoo ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ tutuaa amɛ lɛ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni jɛɔ amɛmli Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ kpo.

english: What causes my cassava plants to grow big leaves and tall stems but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava tso lɛ baa agboi kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from excessive manure or fertilizer— cassava puts most of its energy into growing leafy branches above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eniji kɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to manufacture energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which maximizes leaf light exposure and prevents fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa la ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak stems that fall easily and cobs that are small or unfilled.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ tsei bibii loo ni bɛ dumɔwui baa.

english: Why do weeds make my maize leaves turn light green or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-abɛi lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal nitrogen and soil moisture directly from the roots of your maize. Without sufficient nitrogen, the maize plant cannot produce the green pigment needed to feed itself properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nitrogen kɛ sũ mli nu ni jɛɔ o-corn shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Abɛi tsei hu nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii ni he hiaa koni amɛye amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why did my crops burn and turn brown after I put chemical fertilizer directly next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ewo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Applying it directly against the stem draws water out of the plant tissues like a sponge, causing chemical burns and damaging the roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa tsofai shãa ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant it on land where I previously harvested cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa tsina ŋmãa yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are leguminous crops that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this leftover nitrogen to grow strong and dark green.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmãa ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa tree leaves turn brown and drop during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle the dry harmattan winds and direct heat. Without shade trees to cover them, the low humidity strips water from the leaves faster than the root system can replace it.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ harmattana kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo aba lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsake.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have a deep central taproot; they have shallow feeder roots that spread near the topsoil. When heavy fruit bunches form at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy and can easily uproot during stormy weather.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ko ni tsii ba yɛ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ ji ŋwɛi ni tsii ni abaanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli oya yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when I don't give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a crop's way of showing hunger, usually for nitrogen, which plants use to make green leaves and build their structure.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ hɔmɔ kpo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nitrogen. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛmaa amɛshishitoo lɛ

english: Can I use the same NPK fertilizer for my cassava that I use for my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii?

english: Cassava grows heavy tubers underground and needs more potassium, whereas maize grows leaves and stalks quickly, needing more nitrogen early in its growth.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe miihia potassium babaoo. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, ebaa kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ oya. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: If fertilizer is good for crops, why do my plants dry up and burn when I give them too much?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ?

english: Too much fertilizer acts like salt in the soil, drawing water out of the crop's roots instead of feeding them, which causes the leaves to dry out and die.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. ni haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of big leaves but very few fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai wuji waa shi ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Giving crops too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing tall leaves instead of flowering and producing fruit or grain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ fɔfɔi ni ewo aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ,.

english: Why do crops planted in different parts of my town grow differently even if I feed them the same fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ tsei yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ? Yɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ haa amɛ niyenii moŋ.

english: Soil type and water holding change from location to location, meaning some soils hold onto fertilizer well while others let rain wash it away before plants can drink it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ baatsake yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔji komɛi hiɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi haa nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ dani tsei nuɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops get stunted and weak when the farm soil becomes hard and packed down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, packed soil prevents plant roots from getting air and spreading out easily, making it difficult for the crop to drink water and reach nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Enɛ haa ewaa aha tsei akɛ amɛa nu nu ni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do crops planted near riverbanks grow greener than those on high, dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ faai ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji fe nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland soil near water keeps moisture longer and collects natural nutrients washed down from higher areas, giving plants a constant supply of food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ naa. Ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu daa.

english: Why do my maize crops need extra plant food when the weeds around them grow fine without any help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ he hiaa tsei niyenii krokomɛi lɛ? Beni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Daa jogbaŋŋ ni yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Weeds are wild and naturally tough, but farm crops like maize have been bred to produce heavy food for humans, which requires far more nutrients than wild grass needs.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli, shi akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa koni ekɛ niyenii ni tsii aha adesai. ni biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo fe koo mli jwɛi

english: Why do some crops like beans make the soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii, haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free plant food behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster after a rainstorm than when I water them by hand from a well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe beni mikɛ minine shwieɔ amɛnɔ nu kɛjɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater picks up natural nitrogen gas from the air as it falls, giving crops an instant nutrient boost that regular well water does not provide.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni nu ni yɔɔ nubu mli lɛ haaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted about one meter apart. This space ensures the roots have plenty of room underground to expand into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ he nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa he babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei he hiaa tsei kakadaji koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which catches more sunlight, improves air movement, and prevents leaf rots.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni nine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni ebɔleɔ ehe jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass over my garden beds help my crops during hot periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mibɔɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around your crops acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, lowers soil temperature under the sun, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ aba shi yɛ hulu la shishi ni otsi jwɛi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ anaa.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the ground is moist. Applying fertilizer during the high heat of midday can burn the plant leaves and roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. ni ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baa kɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli?

english: This is typical damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Treating the central funnels of the maize plants early with recommended neem extracts or safe pesticides helps stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ fe fɛɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛ lɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ naji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium properly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant gets too much water or nitrogen. Regular, balanced watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu loo nitrogen babaoo Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa, ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have stronger, aggressive root systems that suck up rainwater and soil food faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the food and water they need to grow strong.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni feɔ basabasa. ni baaŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can the seeds I put in the ground actually carry diseases directly into my new crop?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, many crop diseases live inside or on the surface of seeds. If you plant infected seeds, the disease activates as soon as the seed sprouts, attacking the young plant from the very beginning.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo hiɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli loo amɛhiɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Hela lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsei bibii ni atutuaa kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ nɔ.

english: What does it actually mean when a seed is called 'certified'?
ga: Atsɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ akɛ "dumɔwui". Mɛni ji ‘akɛ hegbɛ’ tsɔɔ?

english: Certified seeds are inspect-tested seeds produced under strict government supervision to ensure they are pure, free from seed-borne diseases, and guaranteed to sprout strongly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni etsɔ kaai ni akɛkwɛɔ mli lɛ amli, ni afee yɛ nɔyeli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi. koni akwɛ akɛ ehe tse Helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ bɛ mli ni aná nɔmimaa akɛ ebaada waa.

english: What is the danger of buying cheap maize grain from the open market to use as seed on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji osharai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jara waaa ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ jara ni agbele naa lɛ mli koni akɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Market grain is meant for eating, not planting. It is often uncertified, carries hidden diseases, and comes from mixed plant varieties that will give you low yields and uneven growth.
ga: Jarayeli ŋmãa ji niyenii, shi jeee ŋmãa ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni ejɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni efutu ni woɔ yibii fioo kɛ dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ amli.

english: Why do some seeds from certified dealers have a bright red or pink coating on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: That colored coating is a special chemical treatment that protects the seed from soil fungi, diseases, and insects while it is buried underground before sprouting.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ ji tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli ŋmeii, helai, kɛ kooloi ahe be mli ni afuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If my neighbor's maize field had yellow leaves and disease last season, is it safe to plant seeds from his harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hela yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ, Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooodu dumɔwui kɛjɛ ekpamɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, it is very risky. Diseases from sick plants usually pass into their seeds, so planting those seeds will transfer the sickness directly into your field.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ oshara waa. Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot underground instead of coming up, even after good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds often rot in the soil because they are damaged, uncertified, or infected with seed-borne fungi that eat the seed before it gets a chance to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛfite. ebɛ odaseyeli loo eyɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni dumɔwui ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛbaa dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: If I plant seeds that look normal but are uncertified, will my harvest really be that bad?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni sa shi bɛ he odaseyeli hu? Ani mikpamɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii nakai lɛɛlɛŋ?

english: Even if uncertified seeds look healthy, they often carry invisible diseases or poor genetics, leading to smaller cobs, weak stalks, and a much smaller harvest overall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ po, Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ helai ni anaaa loo amɛfɔmɔ nii ni ehiii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa baa.

english: Why do my crops grow unevenly with some plants tall and others stunted when I reuse seeds from my past harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ekomɛi daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ekomɛi hu shwereɔ beni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Reused or saved seeds lose their genetic strength over generations, causing plants to sprout at different times, fight each other for nutrients, and grow unevenly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ loo akɛtoɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Ha tsei akwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli Atswa amɛhe akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ

english: Is spending money on certified seeds really worth it compared to planting seeds I saved for free?
ga: Ani shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni mikwɛɔ ni mikɛtoɔ yaka lɛ he?

english: Yes, certified seeds produce much higher crop yields and resist local diseases better, which brings you far more profit at harvest than the initial cost of the seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kwraa, ni helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa onáa sɛɛnamɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli ni fa kwraa fe shishijee nyɔmɔwoo ni akɛhe dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do some certified maize varieties handle dry spells better than the local seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ni awo he odase lɛ tsuɔ ŋmãa he nii jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred by agricultural scientists to resist specific conditions like drought or pests, whereas local saved seeds lack these improved protective traits.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi ekwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ hɔmɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ hebuu sui ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: When young maize leaves turn yellow from the leaf tips downward, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and fast growth, and heavy rains can wash it out of the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people say it is good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them restores natural fertility to your soil for the next crop without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain tree, they steal water, food, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures your main plant grows big and produces heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, Dumɔwu kome pɛ baaju nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otso titri lɛ ni etsɔ agbo ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to swell the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do my crops produce thin stems and small harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ko beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other underground for water and soil nutrients, and above ground for air and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow strong.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni eshwere.

english: Why do I see small holes in my corn leaves and moist dirt inside the center of the young plant?
