ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli

english: This is a sign of the Fall Armyworm pest, which hides in the central funnel of young maize plants to eat tender leaves before they unfold. Detecting it early allows you to clean out the funnels or apply appropriate controls before the plant is ruined.
ga: Enɛ ji fall armyworm pest lɛ he okadi, ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsumɔ gbɛi lɛ amli loo okɛ nibii ni sa tsuɔ nii dani akpataa tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants falling off without producing any peppers or tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pepper loo tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, drought, or too much water. When a plant gets uncomfortable, it drops its flowers to save energy instead of spending it on growing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu babaoo ha tso lɛ hao. Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ebɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni eeefite yɛ aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ he.

english: Why should I cover the dry ground around my vegetable plants with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha hei ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahe lɛ? Aduawai ni baai egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground—also called mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the hot sun from evaporating moisture out of the soil. It keeps the ground cool, saves water, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ehaaa nu ahi shi, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and droop in the hot afternoon, even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko kwraa po.

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to protect themselves from losing too much water through their pores. Once the sun goes down and temperature drops, the leaves usually flatten back out.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni tsɔɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How can I tell beneath the ground that my cassava is mature and ready to dig up without spoiling it?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ ni efiteee?

english: Cassava plants show they are ready when their bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward due to the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Yucca tso tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Chemical fertilizer is too expensive for me this season; what local materials can I put in my soil to feed my crops?
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa waa kɛha mi yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Mɛɛ maŋ nibii manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii?

english: You can use decomposed poultry manure, compost made from food scraps and dried leaves, or animal waste. These natural fertilizers feed the soil slowly, improve its ability to hold water, and keep your crops healthy without buying expensive bags of fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifã ni nyɛɔ efiteɔ lɛ atsu nii. Kompost ni akɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛ baai ni egboi feɔ. loo kooloi aŋmei Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii fiofio. Ha nyɛmɔ ni oyɔɔ ni okɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ aya hiɛ Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: If I can only afford a single bag of fertilizer, at what point in my crops' growth should I apply it?
ga: Kɛji manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku kome pɛ Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Crops need nutrients most when they are young to grow strong roots, and right before they flower or produce grain. Applying small amounts near the base of the plant during these two critical stages gives you the best yield for your money.
ga: Niyenii babaoo he miihia tsei beni amɛdarako koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. kɛ dani fɔfɔi loo dumɔwui baa Kɛ́ okɛ fioo ko wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nibii enyɔ ni he hiaa nɛɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha oná shika ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei kɛfataa ŋmei he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This naturally feeds the soil and helps the nearby maize grow bigger without needing as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni baajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ babaoo awo mli.

english: The rains do not fall like they used to; what crops can I grow that do not easily dry up and die?
ga: Nugbɔ enɛɛɛ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ. Mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ adu ni amɛgbiii oya?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas are naturally tough. They have deep roots or small leaves that help them retain water and survive long stretches of dry weather better than crops like maize.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tsina ŋmãa ji nibii ni wa waa kɛjɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli. Amɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai bibii. No yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does my crop soil dry out so quickly after it rains, and how can I keep the earth moist for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: When sunlight hits bare ground directly, it bakes the soil and evaporates the rainwater. Leaving crop residues or spreading dried grass around your plants (mulching) acts as a protective shield that keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baashã ni nugbɔ nu lɛ baaho. Nibii ni adu lɛ amli nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How can digging small pits or trenches on my farmland protect my crops during dry periods?
ga: Bu bibioo loo ŋshɔ ni afoɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pits (like Zai pits) and shallow trenches collect rainwater that usually runs off the surface. They trap water and organic matter right around the plant roots, giving crops a hidden reservoir to draw from when the rain stops.
ga: bu (tamɔ Zai bu) kɛ ŋmeii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ Ebuaa nugbɔ nu ni bei pii lɛ ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amɛbɔleɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu kɛjɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key food crop plants use to stay green and grow. It means the soil nutrients are exhausted or heavy rains washed them away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etã loo nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efo amɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily during hot, dry spells than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they become stressed and weak, making it harder for them to fight off damage. Pests notice this weakness and multiply faster in warm, dry conditions.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Amɛbaafee mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛhe baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaawu amɛshi nibii ni efite lɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɔseɔ bɔjɔmɔ nɛɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds saved from my last harvest produce less food than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over generations and can pass down hidden diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, handle harsh weather better, and yield more food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔi amli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ aba. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli ni ewoɔ babaoo

english: Will burning the bushes and dry grass on my farm before planting harm my crops later in the season?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mishãa dani miduɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes. While burning clears the land fast, it kills beneficial soil insects and destroys organic matter that holds moisture. Over time, burning makes the soil hard and dry, leaving your crops helpless during dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ. Taakɛ shãa haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya lɛ, Shi egbeɔ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbiɔ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ko yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that dry out quickly under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural canopy that blocks harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa naa lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight tubes during the sunny dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water. By curling its leaves, the pepper plant hides its breathing pores from the sun and heat to preserve moisture until the temperature cools down.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni nu babaoo akafite. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛmumɔ bu lɛ ato hulu kɛ dɔlɛ he koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their health and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves and animal manure on my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Organic matter like dry leaves and manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It retains rain water for a long time during dry spells and slowly breaks down into natural food that feeds crop roots continuously.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ daa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that traps nitrogen food from the air and stores it in the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to exhausted soil without spending extra money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abɛi sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ ni efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni afite shika yɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition results in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs, leading to a smaller total harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii waa baa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to dig mounds of earth before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards underground and need soft, loose earth to expand fully. Mounding loosens the soil so tubers can grow big and long, while also preventing excess rainwater from pooling and rotting the roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaawo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulbs lɛ adara ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekafee ekome ni efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Flowers drop off when the crop is stressed by extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or a shortage of helpful insects like bees to transfer pollen inside the flower so fruit can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni baajie pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and fibrous even though the plant leaves look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen food early on, it spends all its energy growing leafy branches above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy, starchy root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha cassava nitrogen babaoo mra lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni tsii ni yɔɔ starch.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller fruits even if there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, fertilizer, and light away from your crops. When weeds share the field, your crops get half the food they need, resulting in small and weak harvests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ jaa ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fã. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I buy packaged seed varieties from suppliers instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛwo kotoku mli kɛjɛ nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Packaged seeds from recognized suppliers are bred to give high yields and resist common local diseases, whereas saved seeds often produce weaker plants and smaller harvests over time.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni awo mli kɛjɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii haa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ewo kotoku mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does applying fertilizer actually help my crops grow and perform better in the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer works like food for crops, providing essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that help build strong root systems, green leaves, and bigger fruits.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ aduawai wuji baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying healthy and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the crop lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is either too waterlogged or too dry for roots to feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ loo egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable crop leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon heat but stand up straight again in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from dry soil, so they wilt temporarily to protect themselves until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi.

english: If I plant many seeds close together to get more plants on my land, why do I end up with small and light harvests?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo kɛ fioo nɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every single crop weak, stunted, and unable to produce full fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii ni fa.

english: Why are some of the seeds I planted failing to come out of the soil as young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ejeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil lacks sufficient moisture, if they were planted too deep for sunlight and air to reach them, or if soil insects ate them before they could grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tsɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he, Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye amɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from heavy heat, lack of water, or missing soil nutrients, causing the crop to drop its blossoms to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii agbee shi koni amɛhi shi

english: Why do crops grow faster and stronger in dark topsoil compared to hard red soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ duŋ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa he lɛ?

english: Dark topsoil contains decomposed organic leaves and manure that retain moisture and feed plants, while hard red soil often lacks organic food and makes it tough for roots to stretch.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ ji baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei niyenii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa lɛ bɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do caterpillars and insects attack the young soft leaves of my crops first before touching older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ dani amɛtaa tsei ni edara lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young tender leaves are soft, full of water, and rich in easy-to-digest plant nutrients, making them the favorite food choice for leaf-eating pests.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. nu eyi mli obɔ ni tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ mli Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii ni mɛi ni yeɔ baai lɛ sumɔɔ waa.

english: How can I tell when my grain crops are fully mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ edara ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Grains are ready for harvest when the stalks and leaves naturally dry out and turn brown, and the grains themselves become hard enough that you cannot easily mark them with your fingernail.
ga: Akɛ ŋmaa efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa akɛ onyɛŋ okɛ oniji akadi amɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow before the cobs grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the corn plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early helps the plant stay green and make big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I see tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest common in West Africa that eats the central growing point of maize. Spraying the leaves early with recommended pesticides or neem extract stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Afrika Anaigbɛ ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ afɔse mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava under the ground is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base starts to crack. You can carefully dig up one stem to check if the roots are thick enough before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso lɛ shishi koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. When the leaves get plenty of sun, the plant produces more food to feed and grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie niyenii babaoo ni amɛbaaye ni amɛkwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Should I let all the small plantain suckers keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha plantain tsei bibii akwɛ̃ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he?

english: No, you should cut away extra suckers and leave only two or three strong ones of different heights. If too many suckers grow together, they fight for water and nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛlɛɛmɔ yɔɔ srɔto lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells. Watering your plants regularly around the base helps keep the soil moisture steady so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishitoo ni yɔɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap underneath the leaves. Applying insecticidal soap or neem oil gets rid of the pests so new leaves grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ. Baai heei lɛ yɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is wet, usually a few weeks after seeds sprout and again when crops start flowering. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my farm right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping in dry soil for months and sprout immediately when they get water. Clearing these young weeds early prevents them from stealing water and plant food from your newly planted seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ amli.

english: My land has been giving me smaller cassava yields every year, does this mean my soil is tired?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo daa afi. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, growing the same crop continuously removes essential nutrients without giving the ground time to recover. Adding animal manure, compost, or rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps feed the land back to health.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmeii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and prevents them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my fertilizer seem to work on one side of my farm but fails on another side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-fertilizer lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi etsuuu nii yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Different parts of your land can have different soil properties. If one area is too sour or acidic, it locks up nutrients so the roots cannot swallow them, even if you apply fertilizer.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hei srɔtoi baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ sui srɔtoi. Kɛji he kome mli edɔ loo eyɛ acid tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ami amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ fɔmɔ wo mli po

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the afternoon sun even when the soil feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. Drooping is their natural way of saving water, and they usually bounce back when temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Leaf curling and pale yellow patches are signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to produce extra leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do the roots of my yam tubers rot when water sits on my field after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the field for days, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. beni nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade and a humid environment because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Keeping large shade trees protects young seedlings from intense heat and conserves soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsei ni eda lɛ ni oooha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Wait until the rainfall wets the soil deeply enough to stay moist for a few days. Planting after just one light shower is risky because the seeds may sprout and then wither if the rains pause.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni ehi shi gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow, thin, and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal the resources your plants need to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe Jwɛi nɛɛ juɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees keep dying when I plant them in a open, fully cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni mɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh heat. Without shade trees providing cover, direct sunlight dries out the soil and stresses the cocoa plants, causing them to die before they can grow to maturity.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo aba lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ gboɔ dani edaa.

english: Do cocoa trees really need other bigger trees growing around them, or can I grow cocoa alone?
ga: Ani tso agbo kroko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ he miihia kookoo tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo manyɛ makwɛ kookoo kɛkɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need bigger shade trees around them to survive long-term. Planting cocoa alone without any cover shortens their lifespan, preventing them from living long enough to reach full productivity.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ tsei wuji ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Cocoa pɛ ni aduɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baaha ewala be lɛ afee kuku. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛjie amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kpo.

english: What happens to cocoa plants if they receive direct sunlight all day long?
ga: Mɛni baa cacao tsei anɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Direct all-day sunlight burns cocoa leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. This constant environmental stress prevents cocoa trees from maturing and significantly shortens their life.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baashã kookoo baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ ni yaa nɔ daa nɛɛ haaa kookoo tsei adara, ni ehaa amɛwala be lɛ feɔ kuku kwraa.

english: Will planting shade trees on my farm help my cocoa trees live longer?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni madu lɛ baaye abua ni kookoo tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, shade trees create a cooler environment and protect cocoa plants from intense sun exposure, allowing them to reach maturity and stay productive for many years.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni edara ni ewoɔ yibii afii babaoo.

english: Is it better for my cocoa if I cut down every single tree on my land before planting?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha mikoo lɛ kɛji mifo tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani midu?

english: No, cutting down every tree leaves your cocoa vulnerable to sun damage. Keeping desirable forest trees provides the necessary shade canopy that cocoa seedlings need to survive.
ga: Dabi, tsei fɛɛ tsei ni ooofo lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ o-cocoa lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ni aaaha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers leave certain big forest trees standing when clearing land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shiɔ tsei wuji komɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛ́ amɛmiitsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Farmers leave specific trees because those trees provide desirable shade and wind protection, ensuring that newly planted cocoa seedlings survive into adult, fruit-bearing trees.
ga: Okwaafoi shiiɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu. Enɛ ji koni kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Can cocoa trees produce pods if there is no tree canopy or shade above them?
ga: Ani kookoo tso baanyɛ awo ŋmeii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Without shade or tree canopy, cocoa trees struggle to reach full maturity. Most unshaded cocoa plants suffer heat damage and die before they can produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hulutsoo bɛ tsei ahe Cacao tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ dalɛ he. Kookoo tsei ni bɛ shade lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ dɔlɛ mli ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa seedlings wilting and dying even when I water them during sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone cannot shield young cocoa from intense solar radiation. Cocoa needs direct physical shade from higher tree canopies to reduce leaf temperature and avoid lethal heat stress.
ga: Nu pɛ nyɛŋ abu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Cocoa biɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ashishi. Koni akɛba baa lɛ mli dɔlɛ shi ni ajie dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa.

english: How do shade trees help protect the health of my cocoa crop?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahewalɛ he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees act as protective umbrellas that filter sunlight, lower air temperatures, and hold moisture in the soil, creating the ideal ecosystem for cocoa plants to grow strong and mature.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa shi ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli Bɔɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ edɔ.

english: Does any type of tree work as a shade tree for my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ akɛfee hulutsoo kɛha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Not all trees are suitable; you need desirable trees that provide good canopy cover without competing with the cocoa for ground nutrients or spreading diseases.
ga: Tsei komɛi esaaa. Osumɔɔ tso ni ŋɔɔ ni hiɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hi ni ekɛ kookoo etswaaa akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain causes water to sit in the soil, preventing roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally enrich the soil with nitrogen, which feeds the maize and reduces the need for expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛbaahã nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii

english: Why do my vegetables survive better when I cover the bare soil around them with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps soil cool and traps moisture so it doesn't evaporate under the hot sun. It also blocks weed seeds from receiving light and growing.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui hu naa la ni amɛdaraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why must I use wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tso he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the damp soil also prevents fungal diseases and heat damage, allowing the plant to concentrate its energy on growing large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu lɛ aje kpo koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii anaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I trim off extra shoots from my tomato plants when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ amli be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Trimming extra side shoots forces the tomato plant to send its water and nutrients directly into producing larger, healthier fruits rather than spending energy growing excessive stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tomato tso lɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of stored energy to start growing. If they are planted too deep, they run out of energy before the shoot can break through the heavy soil into the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato koni amɛje dalɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ Hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe inside the soil. When soil remains waterlogged for too long after heavy rains, harmful water-loving fungi multiply and attack the roots, causing them to turn soft and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Fungi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ fa babaoo ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any fruits show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot weather, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are there small holes and brown dust inside the center leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the soft center of young maize plants to feed during the heat of the day, leaving behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛyana niyenii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei kpakpa yɛ esɛɛ.

english: If I soak my crop seeds in water to sprout faster, why shouldn't I seal them tightly in a plastic container for days?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛwoɔ plastic tsinsii ko mli jogbaŋŋ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Seeds are living things that need to breathe even while soaking. Sealing them tightly in water without air starves them of oxygen, causing them to rot and die instead of sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni esa akɛ amɛmu kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli po. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye amɛ ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it recommended to leave air inside tied bags when pre-germinating rice seeds in moist bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ ashi kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ tai kotoku lɛ mli beni aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ kotoku ni mli ewo fɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need both moisture and air to wake up and grow. Leaving trapped air in the sealed wet bag ensures the seeds get enough oxygen to sprout strong roots without decaying inside the wet environment.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ awoɔ kotoku ni mli ewo fɔ ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo yɛ he ko ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to stir or refresh the water when I soak my vegetable seeds before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mafolɔ nu lɛ mli loo mafee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ aduawai dumɔwui wo nu mli dani mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Stirring or refreshing the soaking water adds fresh oxygen back into the water, preventing the seeds from running out of air while they drink the water needed to germinate.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ni aaaha efee basaa loo eha ehe ajɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hee ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa nu lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ be mli ni amɛnuɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die after heavy rain floods my farm, even though plants need water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia tsei moŋ

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess floodwater completely fills up the air spaces in the soil for days, it suffocates the roots because they cannot get oxygen under water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu lɛ ho lɛ, nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli gbii babaoo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ nu shishi.

english: Do crop roots really need air even when the soil is completely wet?
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa po?

english: Yes, roots need to take in oxygen to process plant food and energy. Even in wet soil or water, roots rely on trapped oxygen pockets; without air, the roots drown and stop taking up nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu tso niyenii kɛ hewalɛ he nii. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ loo nu mli po lɛ, shishifãi hu kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ni amɛbaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do swamp rice plants manage to survive in standing water while my maize plants drown?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa tso ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ ahi shi yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa tso lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Swamp rice plants have natural hollow tubes inside their leaves and stems that carry oxygen from the air down into their underwater roots, while maize roots lack this feature and suffocate in flooded soil.
ga: Marsh rice tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ ni amɛfoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When transporting moist crop seedlings in tied plastic bags to my farmlands, why must I leave air inside the bags?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tso dumɔwui ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ plastic kotokui ni akɛfi mli lɛ miiya he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings trapped in wet bags will rapidly use up the air around them. Leaving plenty of trapped air inside the bag keeps the seedlings breathing and prevents them from spoiling in the heat.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotokui ni mli efɔ mli lɛ yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ashi kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo ni amɔmɔ lɛ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ muɔ, ni ehaaa amɛfite yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my young nursery seedlings drop over and die when I overwater the nursery bed every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo midumɔwui akwɛmɔhei lɛ anɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Constantly soaked nursery soil drives out all the air, suffocating young roots and creating a breeding ground for destructive fungi that kill weak, air-starved stems.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ shwie shi be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaajie kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii ni gbeɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Can I keep my cassava stem cuttings fully submerged in a closed bucket of water for a week before planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo nu baagi ni atsĩ naa mli otsi kome dani madu?

english: No, submerging cuttings in closed water for that long removes all air supply from the stems, which rots the growing buds that are supposed to sprout into new branches.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo nu ni agbe naa mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni miida ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ niji heei lɛ agbo.

english: Why do seeds rot quickly if I put them into closed plastic sacks while they are still wet after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ mikɛwo plastic kotoku ko ni aŋã mli be mli ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wet seeds in closed bags use up oxygen quickly while building up damp heat, which cuts off air to the seeds and encourages mold to grow rapidly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni efɔ ni yɔɔ kotoku ni aŋã mli lɛ yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni mli efɔ baa. Enɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa dumɔwui lɛ amli ni ewoɔ ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and holding moisture in the soil while the cocoa is getting established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stems grow thin and fall over easily when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and nutrients. They stretch upwards as fast as they can to reach the light, which makes their stems long, weak, and easy to break in strong wind.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛhe mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni efoɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the young plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves the soil too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso bibioo lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wrinkled during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant retain water and prevent drying out when the ground is dry.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli, ni ehaaa amɛgbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with broad green leaves but producing tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava uses all its energy to grow tall branches and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ kɛ akɛto potassium he. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting fast when kept in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto tsũi ni aŋã mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are alive and continuously breathe. If kept in a warm room without air movement, moisture builds up on their skin, creating an ideal environment for rot fungi to grow.
ga: Yams ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiimu. Kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ adalɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when there is an irregular supply of water. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to drop unpollinated flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ bɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants produce plenty of flowers but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: If insects like bees cannot reach your farm to pollinate the flowers, the blossoms will drop off without forming okra pods.
ga: Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollination lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee okra pods.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops every year even when I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same plot every season drains the specific nutrients that plant needs. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted unless you rotate crops or add nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fata he.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant maize seeds from the grains I bought at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ?

english: Market grain often comes from hybrid seeds. If you plant the seeds saved from a hybrid crop, the second generation usually grows unevenly and yields much less than the original parent seed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ hybrid plantings mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young tomato plants burning and turning brown during the dry afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young vegetables have delicate leaves that get scorched by intense, direct sunlight. Using protective shade nets lowers the surrounding temperature and filters harsh light so seedlings can grow without heat stress.
ga: Aduawai bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Kɛ akɛ shade netting tsu nii lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baa shi, ni ejieɔ la ni naa wa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ adara ni hulutsoo be akafee amɛ nɔ ko.

english: Should I keep shade trees above my cocoa plants permanently or reduce them as the cocoa gets older?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahã shade tso lɛ ahi kookoo lɛ nɔ daa loo mafo mli be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need heavy shade from trees or plantains to survive their early years, but mature cocoa trees produce better yields when shade is reduced to allow more sunlight for pod development.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo waa kɛjɛ tsei loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo be lɛ shi koni ekɛ hulu la babaoo aha pod lɛ shweremɔ.

english: How can I keep small insects from destroying my cabbage without spending money on chemical sprays every week?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-cabbage lɛ ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ he daa otsi?

english: Covering your vegetable beds with fine insect netting creates a physical barrier that keeps pests like moths and beetles out while still letting air, rain, and sunlight reach the crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ kooloi bibii ha o-vegetable ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akabote mli. yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ hulu la shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lolo lɛ.

english: If I cover my vegetables with protective net material, won't it trap heat and suffocate my crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋtayaa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ha aduawai lɛ ahe Ani ebaamɔ dɔlɛ ni eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: Agricultural insect nets are designed with tiny breathable mesh holes that allow hot air to escape and fresh breeze to pass through, keeping the environment inside cool.
ga: Akɛ ŋtayaai bibii fee okwaayeli mli kooloi ahe ŋtayaai. Mumɔ Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ha shihilɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will installing net covers over my nursery beds help during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Ani ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛwoɔ gbekɛbii askul saatso nɔ lɛ baaye abua yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, fine net covers break heavy falling raindrops into a soft mist, preventing torrential rain from damaging delicate seedlings or washing away topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋshɔŋloo kpakpa baagbala nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni etsɔ afua ni mli jɔ. Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ loo ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops planted on top of high hills dry out much faster than those at the bottom of the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: High elevated areas experience stronger winds and direct sun, which speeds up water evaporation from both the soil and plant leaves, while water naturally drains downward.
ga: He ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ mli oya. yɛ be mli ni nu lɛ baaho yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I successfully grow vegetables on elevated, windy land without the wind breaking my plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa yɛ ni mifiteee tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, growing crops on windy hills is possible by placing windbreak nets or planting shelter rows of trees around your farm to reduce strong gusts that snap plant stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa yɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔnei ni akɛaama shi loo tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is proper airflow so important between my crop rows when they are growing bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ he hiaa waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida yɛ kui amli lɛ?

english: Good air movement dries excess moisture on plant leaves, preventing fungal diseases like mold and blights from spreading in humid weather.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. Tsi fungal helai tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my crops are dying because of insect pests or because of a disease in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ?

english: Pest damage usually leaves visible holes, webs, or insect droppings on leaves, whereas soil diseases cause whole plants to suddenly wilt or turn yellow even when leaves look clean.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa buji, ŋmeii, loo kooloi amli ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ trukaa loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse po.

english: Why do my pepper seeds die shortly after sprouting when I sow them directly into the open ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ beni mikɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Directly sown seeds face heat, heavy rain, and soil insects before they are strong enough to resist. Raising them in a protected, shaded nursery first ensures high seedling survival.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ sũ mli kooloi kpeɔ dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo. Amɛtsɔsemɔ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow long and straight in soft, loose soil, but turn out small and bent in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse nɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ nyafii nɛ e ngɛ zu nɛ wa ɔ mi.

english: Yam tubers expand by pushing deep down into the dirt. Soft, loose soil allows the tuber to grow smoothly downward without obstruction, whereas hard clay soil blocks root movement, forcing the tuber to become stunted, short, or bent.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse lɛ haa bulb lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ sũ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ agbɛfaa naa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kuku loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do groundnuts yield better in sandy, light soil compared to heavy, sticky soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni tsii he?

english: After groundnut flowers drop, the plant sends down sharp stems called 'pegs' into the earth to form nuts under the ground. Light, sandy soil makes it easy for these pegs to push into the dirt and form nuts, while heavy clay soil resists them.
ga: Beni ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ haa ewaa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baatsi amɛhe kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ sũi ni tsii teɔ shi woɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers fall over so easily during heavy winds when I plant them in shallow, gravelly ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves and heavy trunks that easily catch the wind. In shallow or gravelly soil, the roots cannot dig deep enough to anchor the plant securely, making them easy to blow over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ oya. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ afo kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooofo kɛya

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stay small when I plant it in waterlogged soil near the river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibioo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ yɛ faa ko masɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize roots need air pockets in the soil to breathe. In waterlogged land, water fills up all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and preventing them from feeding the plant, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and stunts growth.
ga: Abele shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why does swamp rice grow so well in lowlands flooded with water while my other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Swamp rice has special internal air tubes in its stems that carry oxygen from the air down to its underwater roots. Most other crops lack these special tubes and will suffocate and rot if submerged in standing water.
ga: Swamp rice yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ eshishifã lɛ mli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ. ni ebaagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ awo lɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry up and drop their leaves when planted on a steep, rocky hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gĩɔ ni baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tɛsaa ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Steep, rocky hills lose rain water very fast through runoff and have thin soil that dries out quickly. Pepper plants have shallow roots that cannot find enough moisture on dry slopes, causing them to drop leaves to save water.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ nugbɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni sũ ko hu yɛ ni gbiɔ oya. Pepper tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hei ni egbi. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni amɛshɛrɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwie koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do young cocoa trees struggle and scorch when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally grow under tall forest canopy trees. Direct, intense sunlight burns their delicate leaves and bakes the surrounding soil, so they need shade trees to act as natural covers during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eshã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants get leaf spots and drop their flowers when I plant them under big, shady trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ baa nɔ tsɔi ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Shade trees block the sunlight needed for tomatoes to make energy, and they trap damp air around the plants. Wet leaves under deep shade create a ideal environment for fungal diseases to multiply and destroy flowers.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa tomato koni ekɛfee hewalɛ lɛ naa. Ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ amɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Baai ni efɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛfite fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge, leafy stems but tiny tubers when planted in extremely rich black soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nii babaoo nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often found in very rich, unused soil—the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and tall stems above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, anaa enɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cowpeas produce plenty of seeds in moderate rains, but rot away during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii woɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi fitemɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas are naturally adapted to dry and warm conditions. Heavy rainfall floods the flowers, prevents pods from drying out properly, and causes fungal rots to destroy the seeds before harvest.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi Etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani akpaa.

english: First rains can be deceptive; planting immediately after the very first shower can cause seeds to dry up if the rain pauses for weeks. Wait until the soil stays consistently moist for a few days and regular rains have truly settled in before putting seeds in the ground.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa diɛŋtsɛ. dani adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds before the rainy season actually begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Planting in dry soil before steady rains come exposes seeds to heat and soil pests like ants or birds that eat them before they can sprout. Without continuous moisture, seeds will either rot, get eaten, or dry out.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ yaa nɔ enɛɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii loo okpoi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni yaa nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi, abaaye amɛ, loo amɛbaagbi.

english: Why does planting in the same month every year not yield good results like it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni aduɔ nii yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli daa afi lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Weather patterns are shifting over time, meaning the rains may start earlier or later than in previous years. Relying strictly on a fixed calendar month rather than observing current rainfall and soil moisture can cause you to plant too early or too late.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ baanyɛ aje shishi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe afii ni eho lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kalanda nyɔŋ ni mli wa tsu nii moŋ fe ni oookwɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amrɔ nɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha odu nii mra loo okɛtsu nii sɛɛ tsɔ.

english: How can I check if the seeds given to me are healthy before I plant them on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni akɛha mi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can do a simple float test in a bucket of water—seeds that sink are usually full and healthy, while seeds that float are often light, damaged, or empty inside. You can also plant ten test seeds in a container to see how many sprout before planting your whole field.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee buoyancy kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nu baagi mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni nyiɛɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe waaa, amɛfite, loo amɛmli nɔ ko bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ kaa dumɔwui 10 hu awo tsɛnsi mli koni ona bɔ ni amɛyi fa ha dani okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ adu.

english: Is it better to keep saving seeds from my old harvest or get fresh ones every year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ ato loo mikɛ dumɔwui heei ato daa afi?

english: While saving seeds saves money, using certified fresh seeds often produces much stronger crops because saved seeds can lose their vigor and disease resistance over time, leading to lower yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa shika baa shi moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to grow after planting, and what should I do about the empty spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to grow due to poor moisture, pests eating them, or being buried too deep. When you notice empty spots, perform 'supplying' or replanting right away with fresh seeds so all your plants mature around the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ. loo afu lɛ mli tsɔ Kɛ́ ona he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ, ‘kɛ dumɔwui heei awo mli’ loo okɛdu ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: If a crop dies shortly after sprouting, is it safe to plant a new seed in the exact same spot?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, you can replant in the same spot, but first check why the original plant died. If it was killed by soil insects or fungal rot, treat the soil spot or clear surrounding weeds so the new seedling does not suffer the same fate.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ha wɔkwɛ nɔ ni kɛ shishijee tso lɛ gbele ba. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii gbe lɛ lɛ, Tsa sũ lɛ mli he ni eyɔɔ lɛ loo jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei akaná nakai shihilɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: What causes young crop sprouts to wither and die right after coming out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young sprouts usually wither because of intense sun heat coupled with dry soil, or from a fungal issue caused by overly wet soil. Protecting young sprouts with light shade or ensuring good soil drainage helps them survive their early days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ mli. aloo kɛjɛ fungal naagbai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine kɛbaa lɛ mli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ he kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do some plants on my farm grow much faster than others even though I planted them all on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe ekrokomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil nutrition and water level vary across different spots on a farm. Crops that land in areas with richer soil, better manure content, or better water retention will naturally grow faster than those in poorer soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ehi akɛ ooona ŋmɔshi nibii. loo nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni hiɔ shi Ebaada oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ.

english: How does a seed know when it is time to wake up and start growing underground?
ga: Te dumɔwui feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Seeds stay dormant until they absorb enough water and feel warmth from the soil. Once water penetrates the seed's outer coat, it signals the tiny plant inside to wake up, sprout roots downward for food, and push shoots upward toward the light.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he amɛwɔ kɛyashi amɛ nu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ nu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ nu bote dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli lɛ, Ebaatsu okadi kɛya tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. Mɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ teɔ shi. Ekwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi koni ekɛ niyenii aha. ni otsi tso lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya kane lɛ he

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground feels slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo po.

english: Yam vines droop in intense heat because the leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. Placing dry grass mulch around the base of the mound keeps the root zone cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli ejaakɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulch ni egbi ni bɔle gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellowing maize leaves are a clear sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. Applying manure or balanced nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ daraa waa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow tall and bushy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen or gets excess water early on, cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth rather than root storage. Trimming excess leafy branches encourages the plant to channel nutrients down into expanding the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo nu babaoo mra lɛ, Cassava kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekpa shishifãi. Niji ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How does planting cover crops like velvet beans improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ velvet beans ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cover crops absorb nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Their thick leaf blanket also suppresses weeds and stops heavy rains from washing away valuable topsoil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Blanket ni mli tse hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.
