english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that drain sap and spread viruses. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying neem leaf extract early helps manage these pests.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ mliki lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Gbalamɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to develop black, rotten spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes indicate blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. This usually occurs when water supply to the plant is irregular during hot dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ naagbee efite, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa nitsumɔhe lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off without forming any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flower dropping in cowpeas is commonly caused by tiny insect pests called thrips feeding on the buds, or by extreme heat stress. Protecting the plants with safe bio-pesticides just before flowering prevents this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Tsei ahe kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When corn plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmãa tsei lɛ anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody if I wait too long to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: Okra pods harden as the seeds inside mature for reproduction. Harvesting the pods while they are small and tender signals the plant to keep producing new flowers and soft pods continuously.
ga: Okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli waɔ kɛ́ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ koni amɛfɔ. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baaya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Where can I get high-quality seeds to plant on my farm instead of buying food from the market?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ niyenii ni mahe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: You can obtain certified seeds from approved agricultural dealers, extension officers, or local seed producers. Using certified seeds ensures your crops grow healthy, resist diseases, and yield more harvest compared to using seeds saved from market produce.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ. Nɔyaa he nitsulɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔ ni akpɛlɛ enɔ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa onibii lɛ daraa waa, amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛto jara nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: Can I reuse the seeds from my harvest for next season, or do I need to buy new ones?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: For standard open-pollinated crops, you can save and reuse seeds if stored properly in a cool, dry place. However, if you plant hybrid crops, reusing their seeds will result in weaker plants and lower yields, so you should buy fresh hybrid seeds every season.
ga: Kɛha tsei ni agbele naa lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato ni okɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kɛji akɛ odu tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa be.

english: Is it possible to get high crop yields directly in our local soil, or do good harvests only come from other regions?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ana ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ wɔmaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ŋmaa kpakpai jɛɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ pɛ?

english: You can get great yields right on your farm if you match the right crop variety to your soil type and provide adequate water, weed control, and nutrients. Local soil and climate conditions in Ghana are well-suited for high production when properly managed.
ga: Obaaná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji okɛ tso henɔi ni sa lɛ to oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ni oha lɛ nu. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nibii babaoo ni afeɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops produce a low harvest even when I plant at the same time as my neighbors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi wooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ mikutsoŋbii lɛ duɔ amɛ moŋ?

english: Low yields often happen due to poor soil nutrients, planting too closely together, using uncertified seeds, or unaddressed pests and diseases. Improving soil fertility with manure or fertilizer and maintaining correct plant spacing will significantly boost your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa yɛ sũ mli niyenii ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Kɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli atsu nii. aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi yɛ ni atsuuu he nii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ, ni okɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ to he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How can we process our raw crops locally in the community instead of selling them raw at low prices?
ga: Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔtsu wɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wɔkwɛɛɛ lɛ ahe nii yɛ wɔ akutsei lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔɔhɔ̃ɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ?

english: Local processing involves cleaning, drying, milling, or packaging your harvest using simple community processing equipment. Turning raw crops like cassava into gari or maize into flour preserves them longer and allows you to sell them for higher profits.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli nitsumɔ biɔ ni okɛ akutsoŋ nitsumɔ he nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii kɛsaa, ogbimɔ, okɛ onibii lɛ atsu nii loo okɛwo kotoku mli. Kɛ́ otsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ ofee gari loo ŋmãa ofee ashikishaŋ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ ni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: What basic machines do we need in our community to process harvested crops into food we can store?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee tsɔnei he hiaa wɔ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli koni wɔkɛtsu nibii ni akpa lɛ ahe nii ni wɔfee niyenii ni wɔbaanyɛ wɔkɛto?

english: Simple machines like mechanical threshers, cassava graters, solar dryers, and corn mills help process raw crops quickly. Using these machines reduces spoilage and turns raw harvests into shelf-stable food like flour, dried chips, or oil.
ga: Mshinii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa Cassava grater solar dryer kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa tsɔne Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ ŋmãa ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ he nii oya. Kɛ akɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ ashikiŋsha, ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi loo fɔ.

english: Will processing my crops right after harvest prevent them from spoiling before they reach the market?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baatsi enaa koni ekafite dani eyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yes, processing crops soon after harvest removes excess moisture and stops rot, mold, and insect infestation. Dried or milled food items last for months, giving you time to transport and sell them without rushing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsuɔ he nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ekpaa fitemɔ, ŋmei kɛ koolooi ni baa lɛ. Niyenii ni egbi loo ni afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo. Enɛ haa onáa be ni okɛfãa kɛyaa he kroko ni okɛ oyaiyeli tsuuu nii.

english: How do I safely transport my harvested crops from the farm to the community processing center without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ aya kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya akutso lɛ mli nibii ahe nitsumɔhe lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ nɔ ko akafite?

english: Use clean, ventilated sacks or sturdy wooden crates to transport your crops, and avoid stacking them too high on vehicles. Keeping produce shaded during transport prevents bruising, heat buildup, and rapid decay.
ga: Kɛ kotokui ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli loo tso adekai ni wa atsu nii ni okɛya onibii amli. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi tsɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni adu lɛ wo shĩa mli yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite. hulutsoo ni buaa ehe naa kɛ fitemɔ ni yaa oya

english: How do we ensure that the crops we process with local machines are safe and clean for our families to eat?
ga: Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔkwɛ koni nibii ni wɔtsuɔ he nii yɛ he ni wɔyɔɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehe tse ni wɔwekui lɛ baanyɛ aye?

english: Keep all processing equipment, storage containers, and processing areas clean and dry before use. Washing raw crops thoroughly and drying them properly prevents mold and harmful bacteria from contaminating the food your family consumes.
ga: Ha nibii fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii, nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli, kɛ hei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ ahe atse ni amɛgbi dani okɛtsu nii. Nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni ooofɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni ogbi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafite niyenii ni oweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some crops spoil quickly after harvesting while others can last for months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsei komɛi ato nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops with high water content, like fresh cassava and vegetables, rot quickly because moisture allows bacteria and fungi to grow. Dry crops like mature maize and beans have naturally low moisture, allowing them to stay fresh longer if kept in a dry, pest-free store.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei kɛ aduawai ŋmɔŋ Amɛgboɔ oya ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ. Tsei ni egbi, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni eda lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto shwapo ko ni mli egbi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective shield that lowers the temperature and keeps moisture in the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: If I plant cassava and cocoa together on the same land, will the cassava harm my cocoa?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani ŋmei baaye mi kokoo lɛ awui?

english: Cassava does not harm young cocoa if spaced properly; in fact, its tall leaves provide good temporary shade. However, you must harvest the cassava carefully so digging up the heavy tubers does not damage the young cocoa roots.
ga: Cassava yeee kookoo bibii lɛ awui kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ to he ko ni sa. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, baai kakadaji lɛ haa hulutsoo kpakpa yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okpa ŋmei jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ bulb ni tsii lɛ atsu nii lɛ, efiteee kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: Can I grow crops again on farmland that was dug up for illegal gold mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni ajie shika tsuru yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil and often leaves harmful chemicals and stones behind. Crops cannot grow well on damaged land unless the pit is refilled, heavy organic compost is added, and the soil is restored over several years.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, eshiɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tɛi. Nibii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ ja awo bu lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii afata he. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ afii babaoo mli.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer crops after I farm on it continuously for five years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni midu nɔ be fɛɛ be afii enumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every harvest takes natural plant nutrients out of the earth. If you do not replenish the soil with manure, compost, or fertilizer, or let the land rest, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed new plants.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. loo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei heei nyɛŋ aye abua.

english: Why does it take so many years for cocoa trees to start producing pods after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛji adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Permanent tree crops spend their first few years building deep root systems and strong trunks. They must establish this sturdy foundation before they have enough saved energy to grow and support heavy fruit pods.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Esa akɛ amɛma shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ nɛɛ dani amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaadara ni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do officers ask me to prune and cut healthy-looking branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ bi mi akɛ mifolɔ niji ni yɔɔ fɛo ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mijie lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can flow through the tree canopy. This prevents diseases from hiding in dark, damp leaf areas and directs the plant's energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni edara fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekatee ehe yɛ hei ni baa ni yɔɔ duŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot as soon as the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa pɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high humidity, which encourages the Black Pod fungal disease to spread quickly through water drops splashing from leaf to leaf. Clearing weeds and harvesting infected pods early helps stop the spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ woɔ blackpod fungus hela lɛ hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya kɛtsɔ nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ akpamɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning red and the branches swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ miitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni eniji lɛ miifu lɛ?

english: This swelling is caused by Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus attacks the tree's internal pipes that carry water and nutrients, causing swollen stems and discolored leaves.
ga: Kokoo Swollen Shoot hela lɛ kɛ fuumɔ nɛɛ baa, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ mli paipii, ni nu kɛ niyenii yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fũuɔ kɛ baai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with tough root systems built to grab water and nutrients immediately after rain. Crops take longer to establish, which is why early weeding is needed to keep weeds from choking young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni ama koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ ji koni jwɛi akagbala ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do plantain leaves curl up and droop when rain does not fall for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a natural defense mechanism. By reducing the surface area of the leaves exposed to direct sun, the plant slow downs water loss through evaporation while waiting for the next rain.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical weedicides on my land before planting new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ kookoo tsei heei?

english: Chemical weedicides can leave harmful residues in the dirt that weaken delicate young cocoa roots, while also killing beneficial soil organisms that help your crops grow naturally.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ashi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa onibii ni okwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: What is the best way to clear weeds from my farm without hurting the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Clearing weeds manually or with mechanical slashers keeps the topsoil intact and leaves behind cut vegetation that rots into rich, natural organic fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Kɛ akɛ niji loo taper shwie jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei ni afolɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens to my young cocoa trees if I let weeds grow freely around them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe?

english: Weeds steal vital water, nutrients, and sunlight away from young cocoa plants, making the trees grow weak and creating habitats for destructive crop pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli. egbɔjɔ tso lɛ ni efee shihilɛhe kɛha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii.

english: How can mechanical tools help me when setting up a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mato ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Mechanical tools speed up heavy tasks like digging holes and clearing land, saving you intense manual labor while making sure seeds are planted at uniform depths for better growth.
ga: Tsɔne nitsumɔ dadei yeɔ ebuaa nitsumɔi ni tsii tamɔ bu tsamɔ kɛ muji jiemɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ gbɔmɔ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he kome koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do motorized farm tools require special fuel that is hard to find?
ga: Ani okwaayeli he nibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ biɔ fuɛl krɛdɛɛ ko ni enaa wa?

english: Most small motorized farm tools run on regular petrol that you can easily buy from the nearest filling station in your local town.
ga: Okwaayeli he nibii bibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo kɛ pɛtrol tsuɔ nii daa, ni obaanyɛ ohe yɛ pɛtrol shĩa ni bɛŋkɛ bo fe fɛɛ yɛ omaŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need to be pruned regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, overgrown, or non-bearing branches so the tree can direct all its energy and nutrients into growing large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni eda fe nine, loo ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ afee kookoo tsei agboi ni mli wa.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if I let the tree canopy get too thick and bushy?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ ni efee ŋmɔshi nii?

english: A thick canopy blocks sunlight and traps moisture inside the tree, creating damp conditions where fungal diseases like black pod thrive and destroy your crop.
ga: Kpoji ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. cause humidity Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ onibii.

english: How does cutting off high branches make harvesting cocoa easier for me?
ga: niji ni kɛlɛ ni afoɔ lɛ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eha kookoo ni akpaa lɛ afee mlɛo aha mi?

english: Keeping cocoa trees trimmed to a manageable height allows sunlight to reach lower branches where pods grow, making inspection, spraying, and pod harvesting much safer and quicker.
ga: Kɛ́ afo cacao tso lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ko ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ, ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni eyaa oya.

english: Does using harsh chemical sprays lower the long-term yield of my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Frequent chemical use weakens long-term soil fertility and damages root systems, causing cocoa trees to age prematurely and yield fewer pods in later years.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aba shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli, ni ebaafite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ daa mra, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow better when air can pass freely through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Mɛɛ be kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya?

english: Good airflow dries wet leaves quickly after rainstorms, preventing deadly plant diseases from spreading across your farm.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ahe helai ni naa wa gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the hot sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Be ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ ehe?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the soil moist until their stems become strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi tso lɛ shishi lɛ baawa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food crops need to build strong leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves naturally fall off, and you can dig carefully around one stem to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miidara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso lɛ fã kome he koni ona kɛji tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi koni mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight away from the hot soil. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which goes down to make larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛha amɛhe tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the plants suffer from water stress or extreme heat. Giving the plants consistent water at the roots helps the flowers stay attached and grow into full tomato fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ye nu he haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ shishifãi amli nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it good practice to plant beans or cowpeas alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and provides extra nutrients for your main crops without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa niyenii krokomɛi fataa otsei titrii lɛ ahe ni okɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: These holes are usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the funnel of the maize leaves during the daytime and chew through the tender leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miifee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the valuable water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food in the soil for themselves.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant my crops too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over soil space and nutrients while their leaves block each other's light. Spacing them out allows every plant to get enough resources to produce a heavy yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe la lɛ naa Spacing haa anáa nitsumɔhei fɛɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee nibii babaoo.

english: Why should I cover the base of my crops with dry grass or leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry foliage, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the dirt too quickly. It keeps the soil cool and moist for a longer time so your crops do not dry out.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekagbi muji lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, onibii lɛ egbiŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Nitrogen is the main food that helps plants produce green leaves and grow strong; without enough of it, the plant starves and draws nutrients away from older leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji eshɛɛɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni ebaagbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a virus spread by pests. This damages the leaves so they cannot feed the plant properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ aahu akɛ anyɛɛɛ aha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi to break down and rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do some crop seeds sprout quickly while others take weeks or fail completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ otsii babaoo loo amɛkwɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture, soil warmth, and air to sprout. Old seeds, seeds buried too deep, or seeds planted in dry soil cannot wake up properly.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa. shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni ekwɛ̃, dumɔwui momo, loo dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ Aloo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ateshi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants lose their flowers before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Excessive heat damages the flower's pollen, so the plant sheds the flower instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ yibii moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of flowering. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so extra fertilizer leads to many leaves but few beans.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baa lɛ dalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii ni amɛbaawo lɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai babaoo aba shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods dry up and turn black while still tiny on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods if they do not have enough water, shade, or nutrients to feed all of them to full maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Cacao tsei lɛ baajie amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara kɛyashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger yams when I stake them with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ sweet potatoi wuji kɛ mikɛ tso tswa lɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the vines up off the ground, giving leaves full light and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa wain tso lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa la ni yeɔ emuu. ni etsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why does my main plantain tree take so long to fruit if I leave all the young suckers around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain titri lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: All suckers attached to the same base share water and soil nutrients. Leaving too many suckers forces the main plant to share its food, delaying fruit production.
ga: Suckers fɛɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishitoo kome he lɛ jaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ aha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop plants after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems designed to quickly grab water and plant food before crops can. Crop plants take longer to establish and need protection until they grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Afee amɛ koni amɛgbala nu ni amɛkwɛ niyenii oya dani tsei akwɛ̃. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani etswaa shi ni ehe hiaa ni abu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Without enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant cannot produce green chlorophyll to make food, which slows down growth and reduces your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or from a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests helps the leaves stay flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots underground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or uncomposted manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing stem and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and push themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally mature underground. After pollination, the flower stem stretches down and buries itself into the loose soil so the pod can safely grow beneath the earth.
ga: Peanuts shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ pollination sɛɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛfuɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines high up on poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fɔ̃ɔ tsei anɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the plant using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and air, which directs energy down into growing larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyaa yitso ni da lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is under heat stress, lacks sufficient soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft before the fruit even gets ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It often happens when soil moisture fluctuates, such as going from very dry soil to heavy rain.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nɔ.

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow and can be easily destroyed by tiny soil pests like nematodes or root borers. Without strong roots, the plant cannot support the heavy weight of the bunch during strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powder inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ powder lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ amɛteŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the central growing shoot (the whorl) and eat the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ (whorls) lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why does my land produce less food when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow strong, or that heavy rainfall has flooded the roots and prevented them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛmuɔ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits stay very small even though the bushes look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni da ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When pepper plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and thick foliage instead of feeding the growing peppers.
ga: Kɛji pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse. Mohu ɔ, ha nihi nɛ a ngɛ wae ɔ niye ní.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow well even when I do not add chemical fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ wooo mli moŋ?

english: Cowpeas and other bean crops have special living organisms on their roots that trap natural nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food for the plant and soil.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Adebɔɔ krɛdɛɛi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Emɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and fall off when the Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds bring very dry air that pulls moisture out of plant leaves faster than roots can draw water from the ground, so the tree drops leaves to save water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. So trees drop their leaves to save water.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the air is too dry, or when the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs.

english: Why do my yam vines turn brown and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: When yam tubers reach full maturity underground, the vine naturally stops taking in water and dies off, signaling to the farmer that the crop is ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, wain tso lɛ baakpa nu ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni egbo. Ehaa okwaafoi lɛ feɔ okadi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees act like living umbrellas to provide shade and hold soil moisture during the first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka koni amɛha hulutsoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small or missing ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings horizontally instead of at a slant, how does it affect the yield?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni oootsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Te ebaaná nibii ni anáa lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings horizontally produces many shallow roots near the surface that are easy to harvest, whereas slanting them grows fewer but deeper roots that survive dry seasons better.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Mɛi babaoo bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni ekpamɔ waaa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi fioo shi amɛmli kwɔ ni yeɔ wala yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my clay field for days without sinking into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu hiɔ mi shikpɔŋ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ fee lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clay soil consists of extremely small particles packed tightly together, leaving very tiny air spaces for water to pass through compared to loose, sandy soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ji nibii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku bibioo ko eshwɛ. Ha nu atsɔ mli. Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ he

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct harsh sunlight dries out their leaves and burns them before their root system is strong enough to pull up enough water from the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbi ni ebaashã baai lɛ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 1 meter apart so that each plant has enough room for its roots to expand into big tubers without competing with neighbor plants for food and water.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ

english: How do I know if the ground has enough rain water for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: You can dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil; if it forms a firm ball without crumbling or leaking water, the soil moisture is right for seeds to sprout.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nine. Kɛji efee nɔ ko ni wa ni nu efoŋ loo ehooo. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or a shortage of essential nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist after a rain so the plant roots can easily drink in the food without getting burned by dry chemical salts.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii lɛ mli mlɛo ni tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ashãaa amɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji bibii ni tamɔ muji nɔ Mɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant and eats the tender leaves from the inside out.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants develop black spots and turn yellow after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splashes soil containing fungal spores onto the lower leaves, causing a disease called leaf blight that spreads upward if the lower leaves touch wet soil.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kɛ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf blight baa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛi kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpe.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows soil pests that target maize to build up in large numbers.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the sunlight, water, and plant nutrients in the soil before your main crop can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani otsei titrii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer puts that nourishment back into the soil so the plant can grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli koni eha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave old crop stalks to rot on my field instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei momoi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: When dead plants rot on the field, they naturally return nutrients back into the soil for your next crops to feed on. Leaving them also covers the soil like a blanket, keeping it moist and cool during hot days.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa onáa nu ni ehaa ohe jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava roots when I farm the same crop on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shishifãi bibii yɛ be mli ni miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava on the same spot every season continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt without giving the land time to rest. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts restores those missing nutrients naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they feel too much heat stress or lack water in the ground. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving its energy to survive when conditions around it are too hard.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Plantain plants have very shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than going deep into the earth. When rain softens the ground, strong winds can easily pull those shallow roots right out of the wet dirt.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Mɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo mlɛo.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the ground has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by disease-causing germs in the soil that block the tiny water pipes inside the plant stem. Even though water is around the roots, the plant cannot drink it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii bibii anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. tso ko shishi Eyɛ mli akɛ nu lɛ ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu.

english: How does weeding early help my crops produce more harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nourishment in your field goes directly to feeding your crops so they can yield more.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. koni amɛha amɛwo yibii babaoo

english: Why do my cassava roots start to turn soft and rot underground if I don't harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the dirt chokes cassava roots by cutting off their air supply. Waterlogged soil creates perfect conditions for rot fungi to eat the roots before you can dig them up.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni boteɔ mli lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ aye shishifãi lɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantains planted next to them during their first years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaf shade that shelters young cocoa until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do seeds need wet soil immediately after planting to start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he hiaa dumɔwui beni adu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Water wakes up a sleeping seed by softening its hard outer shell and starting the chemical reactions inside that push the first root down and the first leaf up.
ga: Nu teɔ dumɔwui ni ewɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Ni ejeɔ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni tsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifã lɛ kɛyaa shi kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ baa lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to shield their soft leaves from sunburn and keep the moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni akɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my maize, and how can I save the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Those holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender inner leaves. You can protect your maize by inspecting the plants early and applying neem leaf extract or recommended extension insecticides directly into the center leaf whorl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu o-abele lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ amli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower stem leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when the soil gets too dry, when the weather gets extremely hot, or when the soil lacks balanced nutrients. Regular morning watering and adding compost around the base will help the plant keep its flowers and set fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa leebi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔle he. Konu lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight, measured rows instead of scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every single plant gets its fair share of sunlight, air, and soil food without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni daa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crops grow slowly, look weak, and their leaves turn pale green or yellow even when there is plenty of rain. Adding manure, compost, or crop-specific fertilizer restores the soil's strength.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ daaa blɛoo, etamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ, ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ babaoo po. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tso pɔtɛɛ ko fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine that needs to climb tall stakes so its leaves can reach full sunlight to feed the plant. Keeping the foliage off the wet ground also protects the leaves from rot and fungal diseases, leading to larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ koni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it harmful for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and starves out maize pests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa abele mli kooloi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that aggressively pull water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your vegetables. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow big and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ nii, ni amɛgbalaa nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-vegetables lɛ ahe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize seeds so insects do not eat them before the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-abele dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akaye amɛ dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Sun-dry your harvested seeds until they are completely hard and dry, then store them in airtight containers or clean bags mixed with approved grain-protectant dust or dried neem leaves in a cool, dry room.
ga: Gbimɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni mli tse ni akɛ sũ ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem baai ni egbi efutu mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving your crops proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow strong stems and produce a healthy yield.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do young cocoa trees dry up and die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun and lose moisture faster than their small roots can absorb it from the ground. Planting plantains or shade trees beside cocoa provides living shelter that protects the young crops until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa enáa he ko ni buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen or has too much standing water around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or manure helps the leaves turn dark green and boosts crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil remains waterlogged for long periods, creating wet conditions where fungal diseases thrive. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and roll inward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water during high heat and intense sunshine. Mulching the soil around the plant roots and watering early in the morning keeps the soil cool and reduces heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my maize plants?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji nɔ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in the center whorl of maize leaves are typical signs of Fall Armyworm attack. Checking crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the center of the plants kills the caterpillars before severe damage occurs.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaai amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ lɛ yi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants with tough root systems adapted to absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing soil nutrients and suffocating your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha otsei titrii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from wet to dry. Providing steady, regular watering at the base of the plant helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi daa, ni afeɔ lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil has lost its nutrients and turned weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Weak or tired soil causes crops to grow slowly, show pale green leaves, and yield smaller harvests even with good rain. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or adding compost restores natural nutrients and strength back to the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo egbɔjɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo. Eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse. ni ewoɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and spoil inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested maize spoils in storage if the grains still hold moisture when bagged. Damp grains create ideal conditions for mold and insects to breed, so drying grains thoroughly under the sun until they are hard prevents decay during storage.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ toɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni amɛshwereɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi amɛhe wa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛfite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to dry my cocoa beans after harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi kookoo yibii lɛ beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans reduces their moisture content so they do not grow mold during storage or transport, which protects the cocoa's flavor and overall market quality.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baaa beni akɛtoɔ loo akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Enɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ jarayeli mli nibii fɛɛ ahe.

english: How many days does it usually take to dry harvested cocoa beans in the sun?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii enyiɛ eheɔ dani agbiɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Under clear weather conditions with strong sunshine, cocoa beans typically take about 7 days to dry completely on raised bamboo mats.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli tse ni hulu tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 7 dani amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa beans are fully dried and ready to sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Fully dried cocoa beans will crackle when you gently squeeze a handful, have a dark reddish-brown color, and break cleanly without feeling soft or damp inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni egbi kwraa lɛ tswaa kɛji okɛ nine kome mimɔ mli blɛoo, ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ. ni efoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni enuuu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ emli.

english: Drying cocoa on the ground exposes the beans to dirt, insects, and damp soil moisture. Using raised mats allows clean air to circulate underneath for faster, cleaner drying.
ga: Kookoo ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa muji, kooloi bibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ baa kookoo yibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni awo nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse tsɔɔ shishi koni egbi oya, ni ehe tse.

english: Why do I need to turn my cocoa beans regularly while they are drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa be mli ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Stirring or turning the beans several times a day ensures that all sides receive equal sun heat, preventing uneven drying and stopping mold from starting on the bottom layers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi loo otsake amɛ shii abɔ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ, ehaa fãi lɛ fɛɛ naa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ekpaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Can I dry my cocoa beans in the shade, or do they need full sunlight?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi kookoo ŋmeii yɛ shĩa mli? aloo esa akɛ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ aná

english: Direct sunlight is essential because the sun's heat quickly evaporates moisture. Drying cocoa in the shade takes too long and usually causes the beans to spoil or turn moldy.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he miihia ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya. Cocoa ni agbiɔ yɛ shia lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa kookoo yibii lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa beans if rain falls on them while they are drying outside?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miigbi yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater gets soaked back into the beans, lengthening the total drying period and greatly increasing the chances of mold developing inside the cocoa.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ eboteɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa be fɛɛ ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. ni ehaa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baajɛ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why does my drying time change from one week to the next during the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni mikɛgbiɔ nii lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ otsi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Drying time changes depending on daily weather conditions like sunshine intensity, humidity, and rainfall; cloudier or humid days slow down moisture loss from the crops.
ga: Be ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ daa gbi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ hulu la ni naa wa, hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ. Gbii ni atatu loo fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fiofio.

english: Why do cocoa beans need to be fermented before I dry them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation stops the seed from germinating and develops the essential chocolate flavor and aroma inside the bean before the drying process locks it in.
ga: Nɔ ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ haaa amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛnáa tsokolate ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ amli lɛ dani gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛ.

english: What happens if I leave my cocoa beans drying in the sun for too many days?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Over-drying makes the cocoa beans very fragile and brittle, causing them to shatter into small pieces during handling, which lowers their market value.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi tsɔ lɛ, ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ cocoa yibii lɛ miiwo mli lɛ, egbɛɔ etsɔɔ bibii bibii. Enɛ baaha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do people put chemical powders on harvested corn before storing it, and is it safe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ tsofa powda woɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ nɔ dani amɛkɛtoɔ lɛ? Ni ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Storage powders are chemicals applied to dried corn to kill or repel insect pests like grain weevils. When used correctly according to instructions, it protects your stored harvest for months, but the corn must be washed thoroughly or left for a specific safety waiting period before humans or animals eat it.
ga: Storage powder ji tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni akɛgbe loo ashwie ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii, kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi tsɔɔ lɛ. Ebaabu nibii ni ato lɛ ahe nyɔji babaoo. Shi esa akɛ ahoo ŋmãa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ loo ashi lɛ yɛ he ko koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe dani adesai loo kooloi aye.

english: How do I know if my maize is dry enough to store without it spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni efiteee?

english: Your maize is dry enough when the kernels feel glass-hard and crack cleanly when you bite them, rather than denting. Properly dried maize stops mold from growing and producing dangerous toxins that can make people and animals sick.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ mli wa tamɔ glase ni efoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekumɔ dumɔwui lɛ Abele ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ aha gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi hela aba lɛ baa.

english: How can I protect my stored corn from insects without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can protect stored corn naturally by making sure it is completely dry, mixing it with clean wood ash or dried neem leaf powder, and storing it tightly sealed in airtight containers or specialized triple-layer storage bags.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ nɔmimaa ni ooona akɛ egbi kwraa lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo neem baa powda ni egbi afutu mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛ nibii toɔ mli ni akɛ fãi etɛ ebɔ he lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to feed my chickens corn that has been treated with storage chemicals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: No, you should never feed chickens corn that has chemical storage powder or seed treatments on it unless it has been thoroughly washed or passed its safety waiting period. These chemicals can poison poultry or leave toxic chemical residues in their eggs and meat.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo tsofai ni akɛtsaa dumɔwui ahe lɛ haa lɛ niyenii. ja afɔ he jogbaŋŋ loo be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaamɛ lɛ eho Tsofai nɛɛ baanyɛ afee kooloi ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo amɛshi tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ kooloi kɛ loo mli.

english: Why do my chickens always try to eat my young corn crops, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikooloi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ amɛye mi-baby corn lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Chickens naturally love corn because both the fresh green shoots and the sweet grains give them energy. You can protect your young farm plots by fencing the area or putting temporary wire mesh over the seedbeds until the maize stalks grow tall and strong.
ga: Kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kooloi sumɔɔ ŋmãa ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ haa amɛ hewalɛ. Obaanyɛ obu shikpɔŋ bibioo ko he. Obaanyɛ obu o-abele lɛ he kɛtsɔ gbogbo ni ooofee loo waya ni akɛbaawo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ nɔ kɛyashi abele lɛ tsei lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are some of the corn seeds sold in agricultural shops colored red or pink?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa komɛi yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ tsuɔ loo pinki lɛ?

english: The bright color is a warning dye applied by seed companies to show that the seed has been treated with protective drugs like fungicides and insecticides. This chemical layer protects the seed from rotting in the soil or being eaten by bugs before it sprouts.
ga: Su ni mli tse lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ tsofa ni dumɔwui anitsumɔhei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ etsu dumɔwui ahe nii. Tsofa nɛɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi akaye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I just plant the regular corn I bought from the market for food, or do I need special seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ daa kɛha niyenii? Aloo dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi he miihia mi?

english: While grain bought from the food market will grow, buying certified planting seeds yields much better results because certified seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases, handle heat, and produce larger corn ears.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmaa ni aheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ miiya hiɛ moŋ Shi tso dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ hemɔ baaha oná yibii kpakpai babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, atsɔse dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Ehiɔ dɔlɛ naa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji

english: Why is it necessary to dry my corn thoroughly in the sun right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji akpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Sun-drying removes the excess water inside fresh corn kernels. Lower moisture prevents destructive molds and fungi from taking over, ensures the corn doesn't rot, and allows buyers in the market to offer you a better price.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli. Fɛ̃i ni baa shi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa akafite. ni oye obua mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ni amɛha bo jara ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: What causes corn ears to turn black or moldy while they are still growing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Mold on standing corn usually happens when rain water gets trapped inside the cob husk or when insects bore holes into the ear. Planting on time and using maize varieties with tight husks helps shield the corn from water and pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ tsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tswa bu yɛ toi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ be naa ni akɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni mli wa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmãa lɛ he kɛjɛ nu kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted chicken manure around the base of the plant will help it recover its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aku esɛɛ aba eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli.
