english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is short of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is getting too much or too little water. Nitrogen gives leaves their strong green color and helps the plant produce food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii.

english: If I notice diseased or spotted leaves on my cassava, should I pluck them off?
ga: Kɛji ona baai ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ni mashɛrɛ ashwie?

english: Yes, removing sick leaves helps stop leaf diseases from spreading to healthy parts of the plant and nearby crops, allowing the plant to direct its energy into healthy leaf and root growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa baai helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ. Ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: What can I do to strengthen the leaves of my leafy vegetables when they look pale and weak?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mawo mi tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ beni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Applying organic compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer supplies the plants with the key food they need to build thick, dark green leaves that resist harsh weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii titrii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sunshine even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon sun causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant naturally wilts to reduce water loss and usually bounces back when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baagboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Plantain trees grow broad leaves quickly, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do crops on one side of my farm grow tall and bushy while the crops on the other side stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ mli lɛ feɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Soil richness changes across a field. Areas with fertile soil and good water storage produce strong growth, while spots with washed-away nutrients or hard gravel stunt plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hei ni shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɔɔ kɛ nu kpakpa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha shweremɔ ni mli wa aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii loo tsei ni eda lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ tɛi ni wa.

english: Does trimming old bottom leaves from my okra plants help them produce more fruit?
ga: Ani mi gumbo tsei lɛ ahe baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, cutting away yellowing or shaded lower leaves prevents the plant from wasting energy on weak leaves, allowing more nutrients to go directly into flower and pod production.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ shade lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can heavy rains wash away the good strength in the soil and weaken my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsumɔ hewalɛ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni eha midumɔ nii lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, continuous heavy rain washes essential soil nutrients deep below the reach of roots. Adding mulch or compost helps protect topsoil so crops retain their foliage strength.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Mulch loo compost baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni otsei lɛ ahi amɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plant is weak because of insects or because the soil is poor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ kooloi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: Insect damage shows up as holes, chewed leaves, or sticky spots, while poor soil causes overall pale yellowing and small leaves across the entire plant without visible feeding marks.
ga: Nibii ni kooloi fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo tamɔ bu. baai ni ashɛre loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fɛɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai bibii. Yɛ tso lɛ he fɛɛ ni niyenii he okadi ko bɛ ni anaa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger on my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to compete aggressively for water, space, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the full benefit of soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye akaŋ kɛha nu, he ko, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Gbalamɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa trees when I want them to grow big and give me more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji lɛ? Be mli ni oosumɔ ni efee agbo ni ehiɛ pods babaoo.

english: Pruning removes overgrown, dead, or unproductive branches so the tree does not waste energy. It allows sunlight and air to reach the tree, helping the cocoa thrive and produce better pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni edara fe nine, ni egboi, loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. koni tsei akafite hewalɛ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ni edaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: My cocoa farm has become very bushy and overgrown. Will cutting the trees back kill them?
ga: Mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse waa ni efee amaŋfɔ. Ani tsei lɛ ni abaafolɔ sɛɛ lɛ baagbe amɛ?

english: No, cutting back overgrown cocoa trees does not kill them. In fact, removing wild branches helps the tree redirect its energy into growing healthy new shoots and bearing more fruit.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ egbeee amɛ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, tsei niji ni ajieɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa amɛhewalɛ lɛ yaa ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa yield drop when the branches on my farm become too thick and dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ tsei niji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: When trees are too crowded, they block sunlight and trap moisture, which creates diseases like black pod. Cutting everything back opens up the farm so sunlight can boost pod production.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Etsĩɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afoɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbele koni hulu la lɛ aha ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: If I prune my cocoa trees, will it help them survive better during the dry season?
ga: Kɛ́ mifolɔ kookoo tso lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua kookoo tso lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pruning reduces the number of extra leaves that draw water out of the tree, allowing the cocoa tree to keep moisture and thrive even when rainfall is low.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa baai ni fa fe nine ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni edaa yɛ bei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ po mli.

english: What happens if I leave the cut branches and fallen leaves lying around under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi tsei niji ni afolɔ kɛ baai ni egbee shi yɛ kookoo tso shishi?

english: Leaving debris on the farm creates a hiding place for pests and diseases. Clearing away the cut branches keeps the farm clean so the trees can grow in a healthy environment.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi nibii ni efite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baahiɛ amɛhe. Niji ni afo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛ ni hi mli.

english: Is it better to use a petrol-powered pruning machine instead of my traditional cutlass?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛ pɛtrol tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ baatsu nii moŋ fe tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ?

english: Using a motorized pruner with a little petrol makes it much easier and faster to cut through thick, overgrown branches cleanly without damaging the cocoa tree.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛ pɛtrol fioo fata he lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni eyaa oya akɛ aaafo tsei niji ni mli tse ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni efiteee kookoo tso lɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell us to clear away debris after trimming our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie sũ ni efite lɛ kɛji wɔfo kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing debris allows sunlight to reach the soil and prevents fungal spores from breeding in rotting leaves, which keeps your farm healthy.
ga: Nibii ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ baai ni miifite lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm if the trees are already growing in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo kookoo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji tsei lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo lɛ?

english: Over time, cocoa trees pull all the natural food out of the soil to make pods. Fertilizer restores those missing nutrients so the trees stay strong and keep producing harvests.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Cacao tso lɛ gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ. Fertilizer yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii daa

english: How do I know how many bags of fertilizer I should put on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kotokui enyiɛ?

english: Fertilizer is allocated based on farm size and tree needs; applying a standard amount, such as three bags per recommended area, gives the crop enough food without burning the roots.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahiamɔ nii anaa. Akɛ yibɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, tamɔ kotokui etɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛshãaa amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees before or after I prune the overgrown branches?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli tsofa dani mafolɔ niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ loo beni mafolɔ mli sɛɛ?

english: You should prune first and remove debris before applying fertilizer. Otherwise, the fertilizer will feed useless overgrown branches instead of helping the tree produce cocoa pods.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ahe klɛŋklɛŋ ni ojie jwɛi ni efite lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha tso niji ni he ehiaaa ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ niyenii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii aba.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough to plant maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil feels dark, crumbles easily, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms. If your soil is hard, pale, or dry, it lacks organic matter, which means you should add compost or manure before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ, efoɔ oya, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo egbi lɛ, no lɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he dani okɛdu.

english: Cassava plants grow tall with small tubers when the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly. The plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding its underground roots.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ daa kɛ bulb bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ amɛbaai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Planting maize too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and tiny ears rather than a larger harvest.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii baa yɛ yibii babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing needed shade and keeping the soil moist for young cocoa.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha shade bɔ ni osumɔɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen or that water is sitting in the field for too long. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving water drainage helps restore healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eta ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or a lack of soil moisture. Covering the soil with mulch and watering regularly helps keep the roots cool and prevents flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my cowpea plants right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-cowpea tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to absorb rain and soil nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your young cowpea plants do not get choked out or shaded.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni okwɛ koni o-cowpea tsei bibii lɛ akafee hulutsoo loo hulutsoo.

english: What is causing small, round holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? yɛ mi kaabaji baa lɛ nɔ

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars feeding on the plant. Removing them by hand early in the morning or using approved bio-pesticides stops them from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Okɛ onine ashwie leebi loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: Too much water causes tomato leaves to turn yellow, curl downward, and feel soft or wilted even though the soil is wet. Overwatering drowns the roots, preventing them from taking in oxygen.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha tomato baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ, amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe efee bɔdɔɔ loo amɛhe ejɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ naa

english: Why are my harvested yams rotting so quickly in my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly in storage if they were bruised during harvest, stored while damp, or kept in warm, stagnant air. Storing yams off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya yɛ nitoohe kɛji akɛ egbo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ha ehi shi be mli ni edɔ. Aloo okɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ dioo. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes lɛ to shikpɔŋ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin without producing big ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni toi wuji bɛ amɛhe lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough food and light to grow strong and produce large yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda waa ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and turn yellow even when I cannot see any big pests on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji komɛi moŋ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like whiteflies and mites hide underneath the leaves where you cannot easily see them. They suck the sap from the leaves and spread diseases, which causes the leaves to curl up and lose their green color.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies kɛ mites kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi yɛ he ni onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ mlɛo. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwãa, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛ su eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my young cassava plants stop growing well when weeds cover the ground around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crop roots can reach them. Clearing weeds gives your young plants direct access to everything they need to grow strong root tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa otsei bibii lɛ naa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is my farmland producing smaller yam harvests now than it did five years ago when I first started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ŋmɛnɛ fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ beni mije shishi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every year drains the soil of its natural food. Rotating your crops or adding organic matter like compost helps put essential nutrients back into the soil for future harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake loo okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong sunlight and burn easily. Planting them alongside temporary shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh heat until they are mature enough to handle full direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why don't my maize seeds sprout when I push them deep into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: If a seed is buried too deep, it wastes all its stored energy trying to push through the thick layer of soil before it ever reaches sunlight. Planting seeds at a shallow depth allows them to sprout quickly and reach the air.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛnáa kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plant leaves lose water faster than the roots can take it up from the ground. Drooping is a natural way for the plant to conserve moisture, and it will usually recover when the afternoon heat passes.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Foji ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ ho pɛ.

english: Why does my garden egg plant have plenty of green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ?

english: When a plant puts all its energy into growing thick branches and leaves, it leaves little energy for making fruit. Trimming excess branches encourages the plant to direct its strength into forming flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu tsei niji kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ahe nii lɛ, Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ekɛbaawo yibii. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni etsɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why did the stems of my crops turn brown and burn after I put fertilizer right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmasɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against plant stems concentrate strong mineral salts that burn the soft tissue and roots. Fertilizer should be applied a short distance away in a ring around the plant so the roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa mineral salts ni shãa fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ebɔle he lɛ mli. Tso lɛ kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo pɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make the maize look greener and healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil as natural plant food. Neighboring crops like maize feed on this extra nitrogen, making their leaves deep green and vigorous.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Nibii ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I spend time walking around and inspecting my cocoa farm even after I have finished weeding and fertilizing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛnyiɛ jɛmɛ lɛ? ni okwɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli Beni migbe jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo mli lɛ naa po.

english: Walking through your farm regularly allows you to catch early signs of pest attacks, black pod disease, or nutrient deficiencies before they spread and lower your harvest.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ ni ofeɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, black pod hela loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mra dani egbɛ eshwa ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: What specific things should I look for on the ground under my cocoa trees to know if the soil is healthy?
ga: Mɛni pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ matao yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli koni mana kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for dark, moist soil covered by decaying leaves and the presence of earthworms, which show that the soil is rich in organic matter and holding water well for your trees.
ga: Taomɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ ni baai ni egboi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ehà nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ, ni ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: Does keeping my farm clear of weeds really help my cocoa trees yield more fruit?
ga: Ani kɛ́ miha miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing them ensures your cocoa trees get full access to food and moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa o-cacao tsei lɛ náa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: How can visiting another farmer's field help me improve my own crop yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi aŋmɔji ni miyasaraa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Observing other farms helps you see how different shade levels, planting distances, or pruning practices work in your area so you can adopt good methods on your own land.
ga: Okwaafoi krokomɛi akwɛmɔ Ebaaye abua bo ni ona bɔ ni hulutsoo be srɔtoi, dumɔwui ashishijee, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛi kpakpai atsu nii yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can diseases from my neighbor's cocoa farm easily spread onto my own trees?
ga: Ani hela ko ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi diɛŋtsɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ mlɛo?

english: Yes, pests like mirids and fungal diseases like Black Pod travel through wind, rain spray, and shared farm tools, so watching neighboring farms helps you prepare early defenses.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids kɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pod lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni osaa ohe mra.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer before I clear the weeds from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie shi dani mafolɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cocoa trees and will steal most of the expensive fertilizer nutrients first, making the weeds thicker and choking your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei. ni ebaaju niyenii mli nibii ni jara wa lɛ ateŋ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ Ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are responding well to the fertilizer I applied?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miitsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: You will notice new flush leaves changing to a healthy deep green, increased flowering along the trunk, and steady development of young pods (cherelles).
ga: Obaana baai tsuji heei ni miitsɔ eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii (cherelles) ni yaa nɔ amɛyaa hiɛ lɛ

english: Can I plant other food crops underneath my established cocoa trees without harming them?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii krokomɛi. Ani abaanyɛ adu yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi ni eyeee amɛ awui?

english: Mature cocoa trees create heavy shade that prevents most food crops from getting sun, and heavy feeders will compete with cocoa roots for moisture and soil nutrients.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ hulutsoo be ni buɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ babaoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Ni niyenii ni tsii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sun when water is low. They need temporary shade, like plantain leaves, to keep cool and retain moisture.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantain baai, koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛhiɛ fɛ̃i mli.

english: Flowers drop when trees are stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of tiny pollinating insects (midges) that live in damp leaf litter on the farm floor.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Loo kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollination (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni hiɔ baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my crops are fully ready for harvest so I don't pick them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋɔɔɔ mra tsɔ.

english: Crops show clear physical signs when they mature, such as leaves changing color from green to yellow or brown, stalks drying up, or fruits reaching a specific firmness and size. Harvesting early reduces both your overall yield weight and crop quality.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi ni gbɛ́ɔ, loo aduawai ni feɔ shiŋŋ kɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko. mra be mli nikpamɔ Ebaaye ebua ni eha nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ agbɔjɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe nibii fɛɛ aba shi.

english: My neighbor has started harvesting their farm, so should I start harvesting mine at the same time?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ eje amɛŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ shishi. Ani esa akɛ mabɔi mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ be kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Not necessarily. Your harvest time depends on the exact date you planted, the seed variety you used, and your local soil conditions. Always judge maturity based on your own crop's appearance rather than what neighboring farmers are doing.
ga: Halamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Okpamɔ be lɛ damɔ gbi ni okɛbaadu lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ dumɔwui okɛtsuɔ nii? kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, akojoɔ bɔ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ akojoɔ shweremɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: What should I do immediately after picking my crops to keep them from spoiling in the field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mikpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni ekafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Move harvested crops out of direct sunlight into a cool, well-ventilated shaded area as quickly as possible. Handle them gently to prevent bruises and cuts, which allow mold and rot to enter.
ga: Tsimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli kɛya he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ, ni okɛtsu nii blɛoo koni akatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ abote mli.

english: How can I guide new farm laborers so they don't damage my crops while working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔ hee kpo? Koni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite be mli ni mitsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Demonstrate the proper tools and harvesting techniques to new laborers directly in the field. Working alongside them at the beginning helps them learn correct handling methods and prevents accidental crop destruction.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmaakpamɔ nibii kɛ ŋaai ni sa lɛ otsɔɔ nitsulɔi heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ amɛfee ekome kɛtsu nii kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkaseɔ bɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpata yɛ oshara mli lɛ anaa.

english: Is it good practice to divide my farmland into smaller sections to manage the work better?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ majara miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awo fãi bibii amli? Koni okwɛ nitsumɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, dividing your farm into smaller plots allows you to monitor crop development more closely, schedule weeding and harvesting in stages, and make labor management much easier.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni oooja oŋmɔ lɛ mli awo shikpɔji bibii amli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli jogbaŋŋ. Too jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Ni ehaa nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the crops on one side of my land growing much faster than those on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Uneven crop growth across a single field is usually caused by differences in soil fertility, variations in ground moisture, or shade cast by nearby tall trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo hulutsoo ni tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei kakadaji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during the growing stage usually indicate that the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil has either too much water logging or too little moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: No, crowded plants must compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper plant spacing gives each crop enough room to grow strong stalks and larger yields.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even when there is plenty of rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal fertilizer, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops, causing your crops to stay small and weak despite good rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni hulu la lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I plant two different types of crops together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Combining compatible crops, such as planting legumes alongside maize, can improve soil fertility and make better use of your farmland space.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee ni akɛaafee ekome, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi. Ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni ekɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant cocoa trees today, how long will they continue to yield fruits for my children to inherit?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo tso ŋmɛnɛ Be enyiɛ amɛbaaya nɔ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ amɛha amɛbii kɛ amɛnabii?

english: Cocoa trees can live and produce good yields for 30 to 40 years or more if well pruned, weeded, and protected from diseases, allowing your farm to support your family across generations.
ga: Cocoa tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli, ni atsĩ helai anaa. Ye obua oŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ oweku lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli.

english: Why does my farmland produce less food every year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil during every harvest. If you do not put nutrients back using compost, animal manure, or proper fertilizers, the soil gets exhausted and yields drop over time.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ be mli. Kɛji okɛtsuuu nii lɛ, okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafite ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is suffering from root damage caused by excess standing water. Water alone is not enough; crops need balanced nutrients to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ efite shishifãi. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Niyenii ni ja he miihia tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crop leaves more during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa mitsei lɛ baai lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, crops get stressed from water loss, which weakens their natural defense against pests. Warm temperatures also cause sap-sucking insects to reproduce much faster.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi. He ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ fɔɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with very small tubers when I plant them under big tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to make food through its leaves and store energy in its roots. Under heavy shade, the plant wastes energy stretching upward for light instead of growing thick roots.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create living umbrellas, giving young cocoa shade and moist air while it establishes roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. Ha kookoo shade ni mli tse kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ be mli ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Wait until the soil gets steady rain for at least one to two weeks so the deep ground stays wet. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and die if a dry week follows.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hoo lɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ. koni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahi shi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji otsii babaoo ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings sharply from very wet to very dry. Extremely high heat prevents proper pollination inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni efɔ waa kɛyaa nɔ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why should I trim or prune extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the branches so air and sunlight can reach the center of the tree. This dries out wet leaves quickly to prevent fungal diseases like black pod while helping the tree focus energy on pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni efɔ lɛ gĩɔ oya koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ hu ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ maa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose their vigor and disease resistance over time. Certified seeds are specially bred to fight local diseases, resist dry weather, and produce larger, uniform harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛ kɛ helai ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni da ni yaa nɔ daa

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the tender central leaf funnels of young maize. Treating your farm early with recommended pest controls or neem extract protects the leaves so the plant can grow strong ears of corn.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread viruses. Spraying to manage these small insects keeps the foliage healthy and allows normal fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛtsu nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ahe nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves when water is scarce to save moisture and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing standard roots.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ nu faaa bɔni afee ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shishifãi ni sa.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my maize crop when the soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nii momo lɛ?

english: Even dark soil can run out of key nutrients like nitrogen that heavy-feeding crops like maize need. Fertilizer restores these hidden nutrients so the plants can grow large, full cobs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ po bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, ni niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa he hiaa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ baa ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots. This acts like a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants struggle against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them enough space allows every stalk to grow thick and produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does leaving dry grass around my yam mounds help my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato he lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, holds water in the ground longer, and stops weeds from growing around your yams.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off some branches from our tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfo tomato niji lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Removing extra leaves and side branches (pruning) forces the plant to send its energy and water straight into making bigger, healthier fruits instead of growing extra leaves.
ga: Baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ Tso lɛ tsemɔ (pruning) haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu koni ekɛfee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai krokomɛi

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred to resist local diseases, tolerate dry spells, and yield more harvest, whereas seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses, or by extreme heat and drought. Controlling these insects and keeping the soil moist helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small green droppings inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day and eat the leaves, so early treatment is needed to save the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ mra koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or if too much nitrogen fertilizer was used. Regular watering and partial shade during very hot weather prevent flower drop.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can I spray chemical pesticides on my mango trees while they are flowering, or will it harm the fruits?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Aloo ebaaye yibii lɛ awui?

english: It is best to avoid spraying strong chemical pesticides during the flowering stage because chemicals can kill beneficial insects like bees that are needed to pollinate the flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ wuobii, ni he hiaa koni akɛ fɔfɔi ni tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ awo mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of the small green mangoes drop off the branch on their own, leaving only one or two behind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi komɛi po jɛ tsei niji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ anɔ amɛgbee shi. Hetooi 1-2 pɛ eshwɛ?

english: Fruit trees naturally shed excess young fruit when a branch is overloaded so that the remaining single fruits get enough food and water to grow big and healthy.
ga: Yibii tsei jieɔ yibii bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛniji fa tsɔ. Enɛ ji koni tso yibii kome ni eshwɛ lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ehe wa.

english: What kind of crops or plants can I grow around my farm boundary to keep thieves and farm animals out?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei loo tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Husu awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni julɔi kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi akabote mli.

english: Planting dense, thorny hedge plants like bougainvillea, sharp cacti, or closely spaced pineapples along your farm border creates a natural living barrier that deters unwanted visitors and stray animals.
ga: Hedge tsei ni ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ adumɔ, tamɔ bougainvillea kɛ cacti ni yɔɔ ŋmeii. Aloo ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he. Ekɛ gbɛtsii nii ko baa adebɔɔ mli wala nɔ ni tsiɔ saralɔi ni ataooo amɛ kɛ kooloi ni elaaje lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my mango tree take several years before it starts giving me a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mango tsei jeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afeemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Perennial fruit trees spend their early years building deep roots and strong trunks to support heavy crops later, so the full financial reward takes time to develop.
ga: Yibii tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii yɛ sɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shika he nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ heɔ be dani ebaa.

english: If I do not want to use chemical fertilizers on my orchard, how else can I feed my soil?
ga: Kɛji osumɔɔɔ ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso yibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ otso lɛ mli. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii?

english: You can feed the soil using well-rotted animal manure, compost, and dry leaves as mulch, which break down slowly over time and release rich nutrients without damaging the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi aŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni baafite fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo kpo ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How can I stop fruit flies from damaging my ripe mangoes without spraying chemicals directly on the fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi aduawai amli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ naa ni mikɛ tsofai shwieee aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: You can hang simple bait traps made from plastic bottles with sweet liquids or liquid protein inside the tree canopy to attract and trap fruit flies naturally.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni yɔɔ mlɛo awo mli. Akɛ plastic kɔɔpoo ko ni nu ni ŋɔɔ loo protein nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ feɔ, ni akɛwoɔ tso ko shishi koni ekɛgbala aduawai amli ŋmeii ni emɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to cut away some of the thick inner branches of my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli niji ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Pruning inner branches allows sunlight and air to reach deep inside the tree canopy, which prevents fungal diseases and helps all parts of the tree produce healthy fruit.
ga: Mligbɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I scrape away all the dry leaves and weeds under my tree until the dirt is bare?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ kɛyashi sũ baaha amɛhe kwraa?

english: No, keeping a layer of dried leaves or mulch on the soil under the tree shades the root area, keeps the ground moist during the hot dry season, and prevents topsoil from washing away in heavy rains.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why is my fruit tree producing a lot of flowers but failing to form actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ebɛ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Trees may drop flowers without forming fruit if the soil lacks key nutrients, if weather conditions are too dry, or if excessive chemical spraying has driven away natural pollinators.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Is there a way to manage my fruit trees so that they produce fruit when market prices are higher?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo yibii kɛ́ jara nɔ jara tee hiɛ?

english: By using proper pruning techniques, controlled watering during dry periods, and correct seasonal organic feeding, you can encourage earlier flowering and harvest during peak price periods.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsuɔ nii Nu ni anáa lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni atsake niyenii ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ yɛ be lɛ naa. Obaanyɛ owo fɔfɔii ni baa mra kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ he hewalɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their tender leaves burn easily in direct, intense sunlight. Keeping tall trees or planting plantains nearby acts like a natural umbrella that protects the cocoa and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ahiɔ shi loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and fold during the hot afternoon sun but look normal in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli, shi amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa yɛ leebi lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves fold during the hottest part of the day to reduce water loss from evaporation. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to stay hydrated during high heat.
ga: Akɛ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ dɔlɛ bei amli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong stems. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Ehe miihia ni niyenii titrii ni aduɔ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ su kpakpa baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves, but the tubers underground are very small when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa kɛ́ mikpa amɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water, cassava puts most of its energy into growing big leaves and branches on top instead of expanding its roots and tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei niji wuji yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ a sisi kɛ a tsɔwi ɔmɛ kɛ yaa zugba sisi.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like potassium, which the plant needs to hold onto its developing fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium, ni ehe hiaa ni tsei kɛkpɛtɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curling yellow leaves on tomatoes are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases, or by heat stress and insufficient soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ adu mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Allowing them to crawl on the wet ground causes fungal diseases and yields smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛkpã shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Seeds planted too deep burn through all their stored food reserves trying to push through the heavy dirt before reaching sunlight. Planting at shallow depths allows sprouts to emerge easily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baashã kɛtsɔ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do cowpeas make the soil better for my maize crop when I plant them next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, meaning their roots work with helpful soil organisms to pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, providing natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for food in the soil and sunlight above ground. They grow aggressively and steal nutrients that your crops need to mature properly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow well at first but then stop growing big even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli shi sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Crops consume essential nutrients from the soil as they grow. If the soil runs out of these nutrients, the plants stall in growth; adding compost, animal manure, or the right fertilizer restores the food supply in the soil so the crops can reach their full potential.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ Tso lɛ baakpa dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the ground and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating your maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the growing leaves of maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended neem extracts or safe sprays directly into the leaf whorls can stop them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ akɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves or spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with proper sprays prevents the leaves from twisting and preserves your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, abaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baahi shi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or bananas alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains loo banana yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, offering the shade and cool moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes overcrowding, forcing the plants to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stalks and produce large, fully filled ears of maize.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ kɛteke nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei wuɔ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baawo ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji yɔɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by dry soil or irregular watering while the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need to lift their leaves upward toward the sun. Exposing the leaves to sunlight allows the plant to make energy, which it sends underground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo hulu la mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ. Abaatsu lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni eyadu yam tsei wuji.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my field cause my crops to produce far less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the nourishment in the field goes straight to your crops so they can produce a heavy yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Koni enyɛ ekɛ nibii babaoo aba

english: Why do my maize crops perform poorly if I plant them even a few weeks late after the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ wulu lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Early planting allows crops to take advantage of the initial surge of nitrogen released in the soil by the first rains. Late-planted crops miss this nutrient peak and often face higher pest pressure and warmer, drier conditions later in their growth.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ nɛɛ. ni bei pii lɛ amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nɔnyɛɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kpeɔ. kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi kɛha sɛɛ mli dalɛ.

english: Why are the rain patterns changing so much in Ghana, and how does it affect when I should plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ etsake waa yɛ Ghana lɛ? Ni te enɛ baaná be ni esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Changing weather trends mean traditional planting months are no longer reliable. Shifting temperatures and rainfall mean farmers need to wait for sufficient soil moisture rather than relying strictly on fixed calendar dates.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miiha nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ miitsake. Anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ dɔŋŋ He ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ tsakeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okwaafoi lɛ amɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kalanda gbii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ.

english: When air temperatures rise, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it. Leaves curl up to reduce their surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant conserve water.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he.

english: How does hot soil affect the seeds I plant in my field?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When heat makes the topsoil excessively hot, seeds can get scorched or enter a dormant state, leading to poor germination and weak seedlings that struggle to grow.
ga: Kɛji latsaa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo amɛbote shihilɛ ni mli wa mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara lɛ hu baa.

english: Why do I see more pest insects on my farm during hot and dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Higher temperatures shorten the life cycle of many crop pests, allowing them to hatch and reproduce much faster than they do in cooler conditions.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo wala be lɛ feɔ kuku. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ mli.

english: Why should I leave some big trees on my farm instead of clearing every single tree before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tso fɛɛ tso dani madu?

english: Shade trees keep the surrounding air and soil temperatures cooler, protecting delicate crops from scorching heat and keeping moisture in the ground for longer periods.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the ground around my crop roots with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a shield that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and preventing moisture from evaporating into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming any pods during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees experience high temperatures and water stress, they automatically drop their flowers to save energy and water so the main tree can stay alive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ nu mli haomɔ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ ehe koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crops look pale and yellow even when the farm gets enough rainwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant cannot access vital nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, which can happen if high soil temperatures or heavy downpours wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsi niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to my cassava plants when the dry season lasts longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells to stop losing water, resting until temperature and rainfall return to normal before growing fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akpa. Hejɔɔmɔ kɛyashi hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ dani odu baai heei.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough water for me to safely start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: You can test your soil by squeezing a handful of dirt into a ball. If it holds its shape easily without dripping excess water or crumbling into dry powder, the soil has the right moisture for seeds to sprout.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka sũ okwɛ kɛtsɔ sũ fioo ko ni ooomimɔ bɔɔlu mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli mlɛo ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi loo efoŋ ni efee powda ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nu ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my farm give me less food every year when I keep planting cassava on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli niyenii faaa daa afi lɛ? Be ni midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until it becomes tired and empty. Changing your crops or planting legumes like groundnuts helps rest and rebuild the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ehiɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni etswaa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin, weak, and tall when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛkwɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. They stretch tall trying to reach the light, which makes them weak. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. ni haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings look like they are dying right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings disturbs their delicate roots, causing them temporary shock. Transplanting late in the afternoon when the sun is cool and watering them immediately helps young crops recover faster.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baagbala amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shoofeemɔ baa Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ edɔ ni awoɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhe waa oya.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that they are getting too much or too little water. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer brings back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and look lifeless in the hot afternoon sun, but stand up again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Shi teɔ shi ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes plants to lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can drink from the soil. They drop to protect themselves from the heat and recover overnight as the air cools down.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaa shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant feels too much stress from dry soil, extreme heat, or lack of plant food. Keeping the soil moist and adding organic matter helps the plant hold its flowers to form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tso niyenii ni bɛ lɛ miihao lɛ waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller harvest even when plenty of rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, quickly drinking up the rain and stealing the soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early leaves all the water and food for your crops to grow large.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Oya ni okɛ nugbɔ lɛ atsu nii ni oju niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaafee nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni baaha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do insects eating holes in my crop leaves cause the plant to produce less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo lɛ?

english: Leaves act as the plant's food factory using sunlight. When insects destroy the leaves, the plant cannot make enough food to feed itself or produce big fruits and tubers.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Beni kooloi bibii fiteɔ baai Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ amɛhe loo amɛwo aduawai wuji kɛ ŋmeii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when the crops are actively growing and the soil is slightly moist, usually a few weeks after planting and weeding. Applying it right before heavy rain washes it away, while applying it to dry soil can burn root tips.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ be mli ni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ ni ajie jwɛi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo ohe dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaafɔ he. Yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or shade-giving foliage, the strong sun scorches the tender leaves and dries out the moisture the plant needs to grow.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi.

english: Dropping leaves is the cocoa tree's natural defense mechanism to conserve water during dry weather. By shedding leaves, the tree reduces water loss through evaporation so it can keep its stem and roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbuɔ nu he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many tiny flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo nɛkɛ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to shed extra flowers so it does not overload itself with more pods than it can feed. However, excessive flower drop can also happen if the tree is stressed by lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baawo fɔfɔi babaoo. Afeɔ enɛ koni cacao tso lɛ akawo ŋmeii babaoo ni ayeɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready for harvesting just by looking at the pod color?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa kɛtsɔ ehiɛ su kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods change color when they mature. Pods that start out green will turn bright yellow when fully ripe, while pods that start out red or purple will turn an orange or deep yellow shade.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ etsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ orange loo yellow ni mli edɔ.

english: How many years can I expect one cocoa tree to keep bearing good fruit after I plant it?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ kookoo tso kome baaya nɔ afee nɔ ni hi?
