english: A healthy cocoa tree typically starts bearing fruit within 3 to 5 years after planting and can continue producing good pod yields for 25 to 30 years or more if it is well-fertilized, pruned, and protected from disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii kpakpai afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛji akɛ awo mli lɛ, afolɔ mli ni abu he kɛjɛ helai ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot so fast on the tree during the continuous rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall and high humidity create the perfect conditions for a fungal disease called black pod to spread. The fungus thrives in wet, cool air and easily spreads from pod to pod through splashing raindrops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Mold shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ mli. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the roots underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil or excessive water early on, it puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to expand the tuberous roots.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishijee mli Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala tuber shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: What happens to the cocoa tree when I cut off the extra shoots and suckers growing on the main stem?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted shoots and suckers redirects the tree's water and nutrients away from useless leaves and straight into pod production, while also opening up the canopy for better sunlight and airflow.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe kɛyaa pod feemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli.

english: Why does a plantain stem die off after producing only one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Each individual plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and produce fruit only once. After the bunch matures, the main stem dies so that the food and energy can transfer to the young suckers growing around its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii shikome pɛ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa sɛɛ lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ gboɔ bɔni afee ni niyenii kɛ hewalɛ aya ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does maize produce tassels at the very top of the stalk before the corn cob forms lower down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: The tassel at the top of the maize plant produces pollen. When the wind blows, this pollen falls onto the sticky silks lower down on the stalk, which fertilizes the plant to form the individual kernels on the corn cob.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ abele tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ jieɔ pollen. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa lɛ, nɛkɛ pollen nɛɛ baagbee siliki ni mli tse ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nii kɛyashi dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi baaje kpo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or are getting too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving farm drainage helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo amɛná nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves when the dry weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi egbi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry conditions to save water and survive the heat. Once the rains return, the plant will grow fresh leaves and continue growing tubers underground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a plant virus. Spraying with appropriate organic remedies like neem oil or recommended pesticides helps control the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites loo tsei amli helai ni baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed many flowers because they cannot support pods from every bloom, but heavy loss can happen due to lack of insect pollinators, dry weather, or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi. Shi laajemɔi ni tsii baanyɛ aba yɛ pollinators ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why are my tomatoes getting dark rotten spots on the bottom while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ yɔɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of leafy green stems but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ baai shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas grow leaves instead of flowers, or tiny insects called thrips might be eating the flower buds before they can turn into pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea lɛ baa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ baanyɛ aye fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli, ni ehaa amɛhe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete for light, water, and soil food, resulting in thin weak stems and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Rice falls over, or lodges, when stems are weak due to over-fertilizing with nitrogen, planting too densely, or strong winds pushing heavy seed heads. Balanced fertilizing prevents this.
ga: Omɔ gbeeɔ shi loo efoɔ kɛji eshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ yɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hewɔ. adu babaoo tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei anɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli ni ja lɛ tsiɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help my vegetables survive better in hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure like a sponge, helping sandy or hard soils hold onto water longer so plant roots can stay hydrated during dry days.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni wa yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains grown alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop produce smaller yields every season when I keep planting it on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa be mli ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize rapidly consumes nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those specific nutrients; rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores soil strength naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air through special bacteria in their root nodules and deposit it into the soil, providing free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ helatsɛmɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do I need to clear the soil and build high mounds before I plant my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafee gɔŋ dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers require loose, soft soil to expand smoothly. Deep, raised mounds prevent the growing tubers from hitting hard earth, which causes them to become stunted or deformed.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ bulb ni miida lɛ naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ shoo loo amɛhe feɔ shoo.

english: Why does my cassava crop survive and stay green during the long dry season when other crops fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hi shi ni ehi shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli beni tsei krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ?

english: Cassava drops some leaves to conserve water and extends deep roots far below the surface to reach hidden underground moisture, making it highly drought-resistant.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe koni enyɛ ená ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ehaa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ waa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, sunlight, and water. Removing extra shoots focuses the plant's energy into producing larger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu. Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa yibii wuji ni tsii ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the tender growing center (whorl) of young maize to feed before the cobs form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida blɛoo lɛ amli koni amɛye dani ŋmeii lɛ afee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow and rot during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess humidity and persistent rainwater create ideal conditions for fungal diseases to thrive. Raindrops bouncing off wet soil also splash fungal spores onto lower stems and leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Pepper blossoms drop off mainly due to extreme weather heat or sudden water stress, which prevents successful pollination. Keeping the soil regularly moist helps protect the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo nu mli haomɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ. ni nyɛŋ atsĩ pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it a bad idea to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ji susumɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer away from the crop's base before roots can absorb it, wasting your investment and washing nutrients into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I clear my farm land without burning the dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai lɛ?

english: Burning dry plant matter destroys valuable nutrients in the soil and kills beneficial earthworms. Leaving grass to decompose naturally adds rich organic matter back into the earth, helping soil hold moisture.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to plant cassava or yam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Healthy soil feels soft, moist, and crumbly in your hand rather than hard like concrete, and it is free of deep rocks so root tubers can grow large easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ oniji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni wa tamɔ kɔnkrit ni tɛi ni mli kwɔ bɛ No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ daa oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, getting too much water, or suffering from root damage that stops it from absorbing plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo ni anáa loo shishifãi lɛ ni fiteɔ ni haaa tso lɛ aná tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: Plants lose moisture faster through their leaves during peak heat than roots can take up. If they recover by evening, it is just a heat defense, but adding straw mulch around the base helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii. Kɛji ohe wa bo gbɛkɛ lɛ Eji dɔlɛ hebuu kɛkɛ. Shi kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ha shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Flowers drop off when the air gets too hot, when plants don't receive enough water, or when there is a lack of plant nutrients like potassium in the soil.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni tsei amli niyenii tamɔ potassium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small harvests and allowing plant diseases to spread quickly from leaf to leaf.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa akpaa nii fioo ni ehaa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and food faster than crop plants, which is why clearing them early gives your main crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Small holes are caused by tiny caterpillars or insects eating the leaves. Checking under the leaves early and using recommended organic or chemical sprays protects the crop.
ga: Buji bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I prevent insects from eating my harvested maize while stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in dampness, so maize must be thoroughly dried in the sun until hard before storing it in clean, airtight sacks or treated storage bins.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛwo kotokui ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo ŋmãa ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ amli.

english: What is the main difference between using animal manure and buying chemical fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titri ni yɔɔ kooloi aŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni aheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Animal manure improves long-term soil structure and holds moisture well over time, whereas chemical fertilizer gives crops a fast, immediate food boost but does not fix poor soil.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii oya yɛ be ni sa mli. Shi enyɛŋ esaa sũ ni ehiii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food found in healthy soil. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot produce the green pigment needed to make food from sunlight, causing its growth to slow down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee tsofai ni haa hulu la kpɛɔ niyenii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays soaked with water for too long due to poor drainage. Excess standing water suffocates the roots by cutting off air, allowing rot-causing fungi and bacteria in the soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off without forming pods if the trees are stressed by heat and dry weather, or if insects like mirids attack them. Pods also fail to form if tiny pollinating insects called midges are not present in the farm to transfer pollen between flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo kɛji kooloi tamɔ atatui ba ni amɛbatutua tsei lɛ. Pods hu nyɛŋ afee kɛji pollinators bibii bɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni ekɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When maize grows alongside or after these crops, it uses that stored food to produce bigger yields.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmãa kwɛ̃ yɛ tsei nɛɛ ahe loo amɛsɛɛ Ekɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with thick green leaves but showing very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ?

english: This happens when the plant receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh animal manure, but lacks phosphorus and potassium. High nitrogen forces the tomato plant to spend all its energy growing stems and leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo nɔ. Shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. When leaves receive full sunlight, they create energy that travels down the vine to feed and enlarge the tuber growing underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ekɛ hewalɛ ni nyiɛɔ wain tso lɛ shishi lɛ baa koni ekɛye bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wilted during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a pepper plant's self-defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the strong sun, preventing excessive water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni pepper tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ naa kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds actually damage my crop harvest if there is enough open space on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji akɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that aggressively steal water, fertilizer nutrients, and root space underground from your crops. Above ground, their bushy leaves shade your crops and block sunlight essential for plant growth.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ nu. fertilizer nutrients ni ejieɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni tsei lɛ ada lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant crops directly on land that was previously cleared and dug up for small-scale mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajie nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛha shika bibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Land dug up for mining loses its fertile topsoil and becomes hard and packed down. Before crops can grow well, the ground must be loosened, refilled with clean topsoil, and enriched with organic compost to restore soil nutrients and structure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsa koni akɛtsa shika tsuru lɛ fiteɔ eshikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ, ni ebafeɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbɔjɔɔ. Dani tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ. Okɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni he tse afata he. ni akɛ organic compost awo mli koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three heavy, soaking rains that penetrate deep into the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower. Deeply moist soil ensures seeds germinate quickly and roots do not dry out if rainfall pauses for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ni shishifãi lɛ egbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii 2-3.

english: Yellowing maize leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil stays too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why does my cassava produce thin roots with mostly tall stems when I plant it under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni kɛlɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to produce the energy required for plump, heavy tubers. When grown under heavy shade, the plant uses all its energy stretching upwards toward the light instead of building fat roots underground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia cassava koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ aba. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa la he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during wet, humid weather. Pruning extra tree branches to let in light and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading across the farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he koni eha la aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any tomatoes during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water. High temperatures can also damage pollen so the flower fails to form a fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu baanyɛ afite pollen ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on to produce good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ koni ená bulbs kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunshine on as many leaves as possible to create food for the growing tuber. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing ground fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I put four or five maize seeds into one single planting hole?
ga: Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo ŋmãa bu kome pɛ mli?

english: No, putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to compete with each other for water, light, and soil food. This results in thin, weak stalks with tiny cobs. Planting one or two seeds per hole yields larger cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe abɔi nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei agbo aba.

english: Why did the stems of my pepper plants burn and die after I put fertilizer right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmasɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly against a stem burns the tender outer skin and roots of the plant. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring a few inches away from the stem so roots can safely soak it up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Ekɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do the leaves of my cabbage plants look like small net full of tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋshɔŋlooi bibii lɛ? Eyi kɛ bu bibii?

english: Tiny caterpillars like the Diamondback Moth larva feed on cabbage leaves from underneath, eating holes straight through. Checking leaves early and using safe pest controls stops them before they destroy the head.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ kaabaji baai kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ. ni eyeɔ bu ni ja. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akpa dani ekpãtã bulb lɛ hiɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong performance only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest will produce uneven plants with much lower yields and smaller cobs in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha nitsumɔ ni mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves turn yellowish and dry up. You can test by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pods shows dark brown markings when scraped, the crop is mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni ashɛreɔ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edara kwraa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well during the dry season even if I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine shwieɔ amɛnɔ nu moŋ?

english: Hand watering often only wets the surface of the soil. Crops need deep, consistent moisture through proper irrigation so their roots can go deep and absorb nutrients continuously during dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nine ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. Tsei biɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli ni amɛya nɔ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Can giving my crops too much irrigation water during hot days damage them?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, over-watering blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to rot and leaves to turn yellow. It is best to irrigate early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cooler.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Esa akɛ awo nu lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do crops grow much faster when planted near an irrigation scheme compared to relying on rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ nu shwiemɔ nitsumɔi lɛ kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Irrigation schemes deliver a steady supply of water without the stress of unpredictable dry periods, allowing plants to continuously make food and absorb nutrients every single day.
ga: Nu shwiemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoi haa nu jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ daa ni hulutsoo bei ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ ahe haomɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai daa gbi.

english: Why do my banana plants produce small bunches even though the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi banana tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ

english: Banana plants require high amounts of water and soil nutrients, especially potassium, to form large bunches. Without continuous moisture and regular feeding, the plant spends its energy on leaf growth instead of big fruit.
ga: Banana tsei he miihia nu kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ potassium koni ená ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Ebɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ daa Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe aduawai wuji.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing bananas on a commercial scale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha jarayeli ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Bananas grow best in deep, fertile soil that drains well without waterlogging. They also need full sunlight, protection from strong winds, and a constant, reliable water source all year long.
ga: Banana kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ nɔ. Hulu ni mli kwɔ hu he miihia amɛ. Hebuu kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he kɛ nu jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ daa, ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What makes crops grown for foreign export different from the ones we sell in our local Ghanaian markets?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni aduɔ koni akɛyaa majimaji ateŋ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ tsei ni wɔhɔ̃ɔ yɛ wɔ maŋ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ he?

english: Export crops must meet strict international standards for exact size, appearance, low chemical residues, and zero pest damage, requiring very precise farming practices and careful handling.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ashɛ majimaji mlai ni mli wa kɛha dalɛ he. Hefɛo Tsofai ni eshwɛ ni faaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ bɛ mli Enɛ biɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi pɔtɛɛ kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do foreign export buyers reject fruits that have tiny insect spots or minor bruises?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ aheɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ aduawai ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Aloo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo ko?

english: Small spots or bruises accelerate rot during long international transport. Export buyers require defect-free fruit so that the produce stays fresh for weeks until it reaches consumers overseas.
ga: Hei bibii loo fãji haa fitemɔ yaa oya yɛ majimaji ateŋ lɛlɛ ni akɛyaa be kakadaŋŋ mli. Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ aduawai ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi ehee otsii babaoo kɛyashi ebaashɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ aŋɔɔ.

english: Why do large commercial farms get higher yields per acre than small family farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe weku ŋmɔji bibii lɛ?

english: Large commercial farms usually combine structured irrigation systems, uniform high-quality seeds, and regular soil feeding, ensuring every single crop receives optimum conditions across the entire land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ woɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii daa Enɛ ji koni akwɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ana shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to clear a very large piece of land for one crop or keep my farming area small?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ koni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome loo maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bibioo?

english: Large plots allow you to harvest in large quantities needed by major buyers, but they require reliable irrigation systems and steady financial investment to maintain high crop health across the whole field.
ga: Shikpɔji wuji haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii babaoo ni jarayelɔi wuji biɔ lɛ. Shi amɛmiitao nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli waa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does having a constant water supply affect when my crops will be ready for harvest?
ga: Te nu ni mikɛhaa daa lɛ baaná mihe nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: When crops receive uninterrupted water, they grow without drought delays, reaching harvest maturity faster, more predictably, and with higher overall quality.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nu be fɛɛ be lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni hɔmɔ baaa. Ehaa eshɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ he oya. Anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ mli babaoo ni eyɛ su kpakpa ni nɔ kwɔ

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves stay green and strong. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores nutrients to the soil so the maize can grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Planting them after maize acts as a natural fertilizer that restores soil richness for the next planting season.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain or cassava beside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantain loo cassava yɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily burn or die in direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and shady until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgboi yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four maize seeds in one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ dumɔ bu kome pɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing them out allows each stalk to build strong stems and produce larger, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ baaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afee tso ni mli wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes for the vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the foliage off the wet ground away from leaves rot and pests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ, kɛjɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I lay dry grass and leaves around the stems of my crops during the dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai abɔle he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) traps moisture in the dirt so the hot sun does not dry out the plant roots quickly, while also preventing weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: What is the best time during the day for me to water my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the weather is cool, allowing crop roots to absorb water before the hot sun evaporates it from the soil surface.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny green droppings inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing point of young crops. Catching and treating them early prevents them from destroying the crop before harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii ni miida lɛ. Mra mli ni aaamɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop a dark black spot at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when plants lack calcium or get uneven amounts of water while the young fruit is forming.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ bɛ calcium loo enine shɛɔ nu nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai bibii miifee lɛ.

english: Cassava plants show they are ready when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base begins to swell and crack open from large tubers underneath.
ga: Yucca tso tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ ŋmei agbo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving large trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby acts like a living umbrella, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni oooshi loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Koni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last harvest produce smaller cobs than the original seed packet I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high performance in their first generation. When you save and replant seeds from that harvest, the plants lose that special vigor, resulting in smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baafite hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ko. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow taller and greener when I plant cowpeas alongside them in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants take nitrogen gas from the air and naturally deposit it into the soil through their roots. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so it feeds on the extra nutrients provided by the cowpeas.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa nine shɛɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛi anɔ kɛjɛɔ tsina ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots become woody and tough to cook if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso ni ewa akɛ abaahoo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for food, but as the plant gets older, that soft starch turns into hard plant fiber. Harvesting cassava at its recommended age keeps the roots soft and starchy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ akɛ niyenii. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ, Starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔi ni wa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds sprout back so much faster than my crops right after I clear and burn a fresh piece of bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie jwɛi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ni mishã amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant underground waiting for sunlight. Clearing and burning the ground exposes those buried seeds directly to sun and rain, allowing them to germinate much faster than crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni ewɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi ni miimɛ hulu la Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛ la ni ashãa lɛ haa dumɔwui ni afu lɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baa tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and drop leaves when I put fertilizer right next to their main stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that suck water out of plant roots and stems if placed too close. Applying fertilizer in a small circle a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to absorb it safely without burning.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers underground if I do not give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mihaaa lɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make energy for building big tubers. When vines trail on the ground, leaves get shaded and produce less food for the growing root.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafee bulbs agboi. Beni wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaaa niyenii fioo pɛ amɛhaa shishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce small bunches when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plantains are crowded together, their roots struggle against each other for soil nutrients and water, while their large leaves block sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to make large bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ efee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ kui wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of tiny holes with small green droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the hidden central leaves of young maize plants and eat the tender new growth before the leaves unfurl.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii heei ni eda dani baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruits during very hot and dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ waa ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry out the pollen in tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When heat stress is too high, the plant drops its flowers to preserve moisture for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji dɔlɛ he haomɔ fa tsɔ Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: How do I safely mix my farm chemicals with water before spraying my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai afutu nu shweshweeshwe dani mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ?

english: Always mix chemicals outdoors using clean water, and add the chemical to the water rather than water to the chemical to prevent dangerous splashes. Always wear protective gloves and a face mask during mixing to avoid skin contact and breathing in fumes.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli tse afutu tsofai yɛ kpo nɔ. Ni okɛ tsofai awo nu lɛ mli yɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ tsofai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ koni ekɛtsi shwiemɔ ni yɔɔ oshara naa. Wo glɔvs ni buɔ mɔ he kɛ hiɛ he mask be fɛɛ be beni okɛfutuɔ nii lɛ koni akashɛ hewolo nɔ ni akamu lasu.

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemicals on my crops during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Spraying during intense afternoon heat causes the chemical liquid to evaporate into the air before the plant can absorb it, and the strong sun mixed with chemicals can easily burn and scorch crop leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni hulu la ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni eshã tsei ahe baai oya.

english: How long do I need to wait to harvest my vegetables after applying pest control chemicals?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa aduawai beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ?

english: Every chemical has a required waiting period—usually 7 to 14 days—known as the Pre-Harvest Interval. Harvesting too soon leaves toxic chemical residues on the crops that can make consumers sick.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ be ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ekɛbaamɛ (bei pii lɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14), ni ale lɛ hu akɛ be ni tsɔɔ ŋmaakpamɔ hiɛ. Nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ haa tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ.

english: Will my farm chemicals still work properly if I store them out in the open under the hot sun?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji mikɛ amɛ to kpo nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: No, direct sunlight and high heat break down the active ingredients in agrochemicals, making them weak or completely useless against weeds and farm pests.
ga: Dabi, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ agrochemicals lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ ahe waaa loo amɛhe ehiaaa kwraa yɛ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean either too much fertilizer was applied near the roots—burning them—or the soil is too dry for the plant roots to draw up nutrients, or there is a specific nitrogen deficiency in the soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ekɛ shãa eba. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ. loo shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen bɛ mli titri

english: Young cocoa leaves lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it during dry weather. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects cocoa plants from direct sun and wind, keeping the surrounding air moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do my crop roots struggle to grow deep into the ground when the soil gets very hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Compacted soil acts like a solid wall that prevents tender root tips from pushing downward, while also trapping out oxygen and water that roots need to extend deep into the earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni wa ni haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni he hiaa shishifãi koni amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is the main difference between chemical spray for weeds and chemical spray for insects?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Herbicides are designed to kill unwanted weeds and wild grass, whereas insecticides target leaf-eating bugs and pests. Applying an herbicide thinking it kills insects will destroy your main crop.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ataooo kɛ koo mli jwɛi. yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsu nii ni osusu akɛ egbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ, ebaafite onibii titrii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a leaf attack by armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai lɛ miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Look for small ragged holes in the central young leaves of the crop and moist, sawdust-like droppings inside the funnel of the plant where young caterpillars hide and feed.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli he ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does continuous heavy rain cause black spots and rot to spread on my vegetable leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa mi-aduawai lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ diji ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall combined with warm moisture creates ideal conditions for fungal spores to bloom and spread across wet leaves, causing rot and spot diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni fungal spores lɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ helai baa.

english: Why do agricultural officers need to inspect my farm when my crops look healthy to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni miyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Diseases often infect plants internally long before visible symptoms like spots or yellowing show on the leaves. Early inspections by experts catch hidden pests or mild infections before they ruin your whole harvest or spread to neighboring farms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani ejieɔ okadii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ kpo. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Nileelɔi baana tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo helai ni waaa kwraa. Dani amɛbaafite onibii fɛɛ loo amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli.

english: How does a crop disease move from one farmer's field to another so quickly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli?

english: Crop diseases are caused by microscopic organisms that travel easily through the air on wind currents, splash across fields during rainstorms, or spread via shared farm tools and infected planting seeds.
ga: Nibii bibii ni baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ tsei helai baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Aloo egbɛ eshwa kɛtsɔ okwaayeli nibii ni ajaa kɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy seed yams from a research center instead of just re-planting tubers from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmeii kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ he ko moŋ fe ni makwɛ ŋmeii heei ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seed tubers saved from previous harvests often carry hidden diseases from the soil. Seeds produced by research centers are scientifically bred to be disease-free, yield bigger tubers, and tolerate harsh weather better.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ayitsei ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ yɛ helai ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ jeŋ nilee ekwɛ dumɔwui ni niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ feɔ lɛ nɔ koni hela akafee nɔ ko. Ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ

english: How do newly developed crop varieties give higher yields than the traditional seeds my family has used for years?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei srɔtoi ni afee ehee lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni miweku lɛ kɛtsu nii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Scientists develop new varieties by selecting plants with superior traits, making them grow stronger roots, resist local pests naturally, and turn water and soil nutrients into edible food much faster than older varieties.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi feɔ tsei srɔtoi heei kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ sui kpakpai ni amɛhalaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waa. Eyɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni etsakeɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii lɛ ewoɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ mli oya kwraa fe tsutsu srɔtoi lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines always try to climb up poles or nearby trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ be fɛɛ be ni ekwɔ tso loo tso ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need direct sunlight to make the food that makes their underground tubers swell. Climbing holds the leaves up high toward the sun while keeping them off the damp ground where rot and soil pests can attack them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okwɔ lɛ, mɔmɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu lɛ he, ni oha amɛkashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams sprout at different times even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams go through a natural resting period called dormancy. Depending on which part of the tuber the seed piece came from and how much moisture it gets, some seeds wake up and sprout faster than others.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli. Dumɔwui komɛi teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi. Enɛ damɔ he ni dumɔwu lɛ jɛ kɛ bɔ ni enine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Early yellowing usually means the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, receiving too little water, or suffering from root damage caused by underground pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni baa mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tsei lɛ yɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen he, ni nu fioo pɛ amɛnáa. aloo shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ náa enɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant them close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to grow weak and small instead of strong and full.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ ni efeɔ bibioo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start getting soft and rotting while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rot is caused by bacteria or fungi entering small cuts made during harvest. Warm, damp air in dark barns helps these germs grow quickly and break down the tuber.
ga: Muawai loo ŋmeii ni baa mli ni amɛfoɔ mli bibii bibii kɛ fitemɔ baa. yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ haa helai nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season creates warm, moist conditions that cause insect eggs in the soil to hatch while providing plenty of soft, new plant shoots for the pests to eat.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ awuji fɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kooloi bibii lɛ yeɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade with their large leaves, protecting the young cocoa seedlings and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ baai wuji. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Which direction should I point the buds on a cassava stem when planting it in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Always plant cassava stems with the buds or leaf scars pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downward first, wasting energy and causing lower crop yields.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii loo baai okadii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baabi ni ŋmeii lɛ ada kɛya shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden stakes and guide my yam vines onto them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni majie tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that produce tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves high off the damp soil into the sunlight, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant direct energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Tsi baa helai anaa ni oha tso lɛ atsɔ hewalɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya ŋmeii wuji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted chicken manure restores the green color and fuels plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ ada.

english: Maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season, leaving the land weak, while crop-specific pests multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kpokpaa lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the field or deep into the soil past the crop roots before the plant can drink it. Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but heavy rain is not actively falling.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛho tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ anu. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ ni naa wa enɛɛɛ.

english: Why are weeds on my farm making my crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots. Clearing weeds early ensures all the food and water in the soil goes straight into growing your crop instead of unwanted grass.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa nibii ni odu lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ najiaŋ

english: What is eating small holes inside the leaves of my young maize stems, and why is it destroying the crop so fast?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai amli Ni mɛni hewɔ efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya nɛkɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows deep into the central growing shoot of maize where rain cannot reach it. Treating the whorl early with targeted pest controls stops them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni nugbɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Wie coverage from early on Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, otsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni otsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate from pepper leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground, so the plant wilts to protect itself. Mulching the soil with dry grass helps hold root moisture and reduces heat stress.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni ebu ehe lɛ, tsei gboɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when heat becomes too extreme, when water supply is irregular, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Keeping soil moisture steady and avoiding extreme field temperatures helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the tops are big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ da ni eyɛ baai?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium bɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ starch baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, leading to soil exhaustion and lower harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be. Bei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni nikpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting in the hot sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Daytime wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease blocks the plant's internal water tubes, stopping water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Kaaha nu lɛ shɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their leaves suddenly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed leaves when stressed by fungal diseases, sudden heavy waterlogging, or severe pest attacks like mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ miigba amɛnaa. nu ni hoɔ trukaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if there are not enough tiny pollinating insects (midges) in the farm, or if the tree is stressed by extreme dry weather and excessive sunlight.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ pollinators bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the wet ground to prevent rotting and helps them catch more sunlight, which drives the plant to produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkafite, ni ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ tsirɛɔ tsei koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up tightly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a natural defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves, the plantain plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to direct sun to save water inside its stem.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ haa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the crop seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to survive harsh conditions. They sprout quickly and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer before your crops can establish root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni afɔ amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rain season starts late?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wait until the rain falls consistently for a few days so moisture reaches deep into the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do imported hybrid seeds often perform poorly on my land compared to our local seed varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto wɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Foreign seed varieties are usually bred for specific weather conditions and soils from their country of origin. Local varieties are naturally adapted to Ghana's heat, rainfall patterns, and common local pests, allowing them to withstand harsh conditions more reliably.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛi kɛ shikpɔji ni jɛ amɛmaŋ ni amɛjɛ mli lɛ mli. Kuu lɛ mli henɔi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa Ghana maŋ lɛ mli latsaa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to test a new farming technique on a small piece of my land before using it on my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ maka okwaayeli he ŋaai heei makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? minɔ lɛ dani mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Testing on a small plot allows you to observe how the crop behaves in your specific soil and microclimate without risking your full harvest. It gives you room to make mistakes and adjust practices gradually with low financial risk.
ga: Kaa ni ooofee yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni onibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli. Ehaa onáa hegbɛ ni otɔ̃ɔ ni okɛtsu nii blɛoo. Customize practices with low financial risk

english: Young cocoa trees are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sun. Shade trees or companion crops like plantains act as natural shields, preserving soil moisture and cooling the surrounding air so the young cocoa can establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ. So that young cocoa can form roots.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling their leaves, plants reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun and slow down the rate of water loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Rolling the leaves reduces the plant's exposure to sunlight and slows the rate of water loss.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged soil. Nitrogen is essential for green growth, and supplying it early helps the plant manufacture food efficiently.
ga: Yellow leaves on young corn are a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged soil. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. and early procurement Helps food production plants operate more efficiently

english: How does leaving cleared weeds to decay on top of my soil help my future crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni mishiɔ koni amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miwɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Decaying plant material forms organic mulch, which acts like a sponge to keep moisture in the soil, lowers soil temperature, and slowly releases nutrients back into the earth as it breaks down.
ga: Tso lɛ mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shi ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ fiofio kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin without large tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ bulb agbo kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight for space, sunlight, and nutrients. Thinning the plants gives each cassava stalk enough room to develop strong, thick underground roots.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ bibioo lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Excess shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Pruning away weaker shoots ensures the mother plant retains enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ toɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking gets leaves off the hot ground, increases air circulation, and protects the vine from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni edɔ lɛ. ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ wain tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil surrounding the base of the stem begins to swell and crack due to tuber expansion.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food it needs to grow green leaves, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
