ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water during high heat, though persistent curling can also be caused by tiny insect pests like thrips or mites.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites hu baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ lɛ aba moŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect visits to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa Aloo kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbaye amɛbua ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the stems fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in thin, weak plants and tiny underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas on land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they extract nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots, naturally restoring the soil food that maize exhausted.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for starting a rubber tree plantation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha rɔbɔt tso shishijee?

english: Rubber trees require deep, loose soil that drains water easily because their roots grow deep and will rot if water stays trapped around them for long periods.
ga: Rɔba tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛbaafite kɛji nu ŋmɛ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers trim or prune the shade tree branches above their cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ loo amɛfoɔ hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛkookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming shade trees lets in just enough light and airflow to keep humidity down, which prevents fungal problems like black pod disease while still shielding young cocoa from excessive direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ afolɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa atsɔ mli koni hulutsoo aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe lolo kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully developed under the soil and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves start yellowing and shedding, and when you open a pulled pod, the inside wall has turned dark brown with full, firm seeds.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni kɛ́ ogbele pod lɛ mli lɛ, ojieɔ mligbɛ gbogbo lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why does a weed like Striga keep growing directly attached to my sorghum roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tamɔ Striga lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-sorghum shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed whose seeds wake up when sorghum roots grow near them, causing the weed to physically attach to the crop roots and steal its food and water.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni edumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ dara. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while maize dies if water collects around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli shi ŋmãa gboɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems that send oxygen down to their flooded roots, whereas maize roots drown and rot because they cannot get oxygen under standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifã lɛ mli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni amɛbaagboi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or upper-canopy trees to shield their leaves from heat and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Bɔni afee ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires significant nitrogen to grow strong and green, so applying compost, manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the crop's growth fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii mra. yɛ tsei adalɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What is eating small holes into the central leaves of my young maize and leaving powdery droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ko yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli ni eshiɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides deep inside the growing shoot of the plant. Applying approved pest control directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening stops the destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ tsei ashishifãi ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ awo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akpa.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut and plant to ensure my crop grows well?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo ni madu koni mitso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ?

english: Always use the mature, hard middle portion of a healthy cassava stem rather than the soft top or woody base. Cut pieces with 4 to 7 growth buds (eyes) and plant them with the buds pointing upward so strong roots and shoots can emerge.
ga: Kɛ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa, ni wa lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo tso shishitoo lɛ baatsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ fãi ni ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 7 ni miida (ŋmɔji) yɔɔ mli lɛ ni odu amɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the right plantain sucker to plant so that I get big plantain bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain sucker ni sa kɛha dumɔ koni maná plantain ŋmɔji wuji?

english: Select 'sword suckers,' which have a wide root base and narrow, spear-like leaves. Avoid 'water suckers' with broad, flat leaves, as they are weak and produce small bunches or take much longer to fruit.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante tu’ ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse, ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers but all the flowers drop off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from water stress or extreme heat. Watering your plants consistently at the base and placing mulch around the stems keeps the soil cool and helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miikpe tso lɛ. Ha tso lɛ nu yɛ eshishigbɛ daa ni okɛ sũ awo ehe. ŋmeii koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying organic neem leaf extract or targeted insecticides controls these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akɛtaoɔ kooloi amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baa heei adalɛ naa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden during the hot afternoon or in the early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants absorb moisture before the sun gets hot. Watering in the afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate before roots can take it up and can stress hot foliage.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu babaoo shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei ahe tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to expand their tubers underground. Mounding softens the earth so roots grow downward without resistance and prevents waterlogging that causes tubers to rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. ni etsi nu ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the dirt. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts traps nitrogen from the air and restores natural fertility to the soil for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni ooodu lɛ baamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow well. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves to survive, leaving the lower leaves to turn yellow and die. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni ehi shi. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. They have tiny bumps on their roots that work with helpful soil microbes to capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade cover that stops the hot sun from drying out the water in the soil. It keeps the roots cool, retains soil moisture longer, and eventually rots into beneficial organic matter.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ shade ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive rainfall early on, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in its roots. For big tubers, the plant needs balanced nutrients, particularly potassium, and well-aerated soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo mra. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛha tsei ni yitsei wuji lɛ Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni sa. titri lɛ potassium kɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: If you leave too many shoots (suckers) growing around the main plantain tree, they all compete for the same water, light, and nutrients in the soil. Removing extra suckers so that only two or three remain ensures the main plant has enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji oshi suckers (tsoji) babaoo yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, Nakai tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with sticks instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ niji aha mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the direct sunlight so they can make food efficiently for the growing tuber underground. It also keeps the foliage dry and off the damp ground, which prevents fungal rot diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni mɔɔ shi aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni fungal rot helai akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny beneficial insects called midges to pollinate them before they can form pods. Severe dry spells, high heat, or heavy chemical sprays that kill these midges cause unpollinated flowers to dry up and drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni ekɛ amɛ afee pollination dani amɛfee pods. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni naa wa gbeɔ mɛi nɛɛ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛmli lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, which usually occurs when soil moisture goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant move calcium into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Curling and wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaf surfaces. These pests can also spread plant viruses that cause leaf distortion and stunt crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ baai ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ hu ashwã.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize during the hot hours of the day, chewing through the tender leaves before they unfold and leaving behind their droppings.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni amɛyeɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Exposed tender leaves burn and roots dry out quickly unless fast-growing shade plants, like plantains, are grown nearby to provide shade and moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ashãa baai bibii ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ja adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni eha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil to catch maximum light while protecting the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni ená la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center of maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and leafy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ ahi eŋɔli kɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant harvest is done, that stored plant food remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ajieɔ Nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ beni akpaa tso lɛ. Tso niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to put fertilizer directly onto seeds when I am planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Raw fertilizer generates salts and heat that can scorch delicate new seeds. It is safer to put fertilizer a short distance away from the seed or apply it after the seedling has sprouted.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo loo beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the dirt when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil squeezes out air and creates damp conditions where harmful fungi grow, causing underground cassava tubers to decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baagboi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or weak plant food. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy to survive the hard conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsei niyenii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up tightly and feeling thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes usually happens when tiny insects like whiteflies spread a virus to the plant, or when the plant tries to protect itself from excessive heat and water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛtee tso lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Overcrowded plants must fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Instead of a larger harvest, crowded crops grow thin and produce very small cobs.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaakpa babaoo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ daa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when I water my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight out of the ground before your crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa plants can establish strong roots during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up while the top is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a signal that the maize plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top green leaves to keep growing, showing that the soil needs fertilizer or organic compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, the roots drown from a lack of air and fungal rot develops rapidly in the wet ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ekã shi. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ni ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and turn tight like balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ bɔɔlu lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the underside of new leaves, or by intense heat stress. Protecting the plants from pests and keeping soil moist helps leaves expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely during flowering. Without steady water and warm (not scorching) weather, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔɔ (ni shãaa) bɛ lɛ, tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy wind and rain when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli beni aduawai lɛ miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip deep into the ground. When the bunch grows heavy and rain softens the soil, strong wind easily pulls the shallow root system out of the earth unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni kuu lɛ bafee agbo waa ni nugbɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ sũ lɛ mli ja okɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in full sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and protecting them from soil diseases, which helps produce bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ yitso ni da.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans work with friendly natural bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni emɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso ko gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I allow weeds to grow right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal fertilizer nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. When weeds grow close, your crops starve because they are sharing limited resources with the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ miiye amɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miija nibii fioo komɛi.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away fertilizer from the surface soil into drainage ditches before the plant roots can drink it in. Fertilizer works best when applied to slightly moist soil during light rains so it can sink slowly into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nu homɔ ŋmeii amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Anyɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli fiofio

english: Why do my crops grow very thin with small yields if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ waa ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need space to breathe and feed. When you plant them too close together, their roots fight each other underground for the same food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another.
ga: He ko he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii amu ni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni ebaai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot of land where I just harvested peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and share the same diseases and pests. Planting them back-to-back keeps those pests alive in the soil, allowing them to attack the new crop much faster.
ga: Tomato kɛ pepper yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kome. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nakai ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei oya kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under direct heat. Plantains grow fast with big leaves, providing shade and trapping soil moisture to protect the young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni akɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shãa amɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines on wooden poles instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves onto stakes helps them catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers. Keeping leaves off the wet soil also protects the plant from leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ baai helai ahe.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and grow leaves. The plant moves whatever food it has left to its newest upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ nɔ ni amɛha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed, usually because the soil is too dry, the weather is extremely hot, or the plant does not have enough nutrients to support the heavy fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa enɛ baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ waa, loo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai ni tsii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain stays trapped in the soil without draining away, it smothers the roots, causing waterlogging and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ekpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni efooo. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt, keeping the hot sun from baking the ground and slowing down the evaporation of water, so the soil stays cool and moist longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Ragged holes inside the leaves are a classic sign of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central part of the plant during the day and feed on the soft inner leaves at night.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ni ale waa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my actual crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitsei diɛŋtsɛ lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to your local soil. They steal water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops, which is why clearing them early is critical for crop survival.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kwraa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie nibii amli mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees and plantain plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei wuji kɛ plantains fɛɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains next to them provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kookoo tso ni daa oya ni ooodu yɛ emasɛi Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, which also prevents foliage diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai hu anaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize crop turning yellow before the corn yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant leaves need to stay green and healthy. The plant is pulling stored food from older leaves to keep young leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni niyenii titri tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Tsei miigbala niyenii ni ato kɛmiijɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai bibii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava harvests when I plant it on the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmei fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time to rest or replenish, causing soil fatigue and reduced yields.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Under heat stress, the plant drops blossoms to save energy and water for survival rather than fruit production.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest give me smaller yields than the original seed packet I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui akui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum performance in their first generation. Saved seeds lose those parent qualities, leading to uneven growth and smaller ears in the second season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔlɔ tso lɛ nibii. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ bibioo yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, tiny tubers when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs bibii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight underground for limited water, space, and soil nutrients, leaving little energy for individual tubers to swell.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu, he ko ni yɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ koni tuber fɛɛ tuber alɛɛ mli.

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that drink water and steal fertilizer nutrients much faster than your crops can, effectively starving your plants of the food you added.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli oya fe otsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niyenii ni okɛfata he lɛ he hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly like old paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ wolo momo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which feed on leaf sap and infect the plant with viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu ni ekɛ helai ni haa baa lɛ dalɛ fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot underground instead of sprouting roots during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air pockets in wet soil, suffocating the cassava stem cuttings and encouraging soil fungal rots before the plant can form roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui amli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei niji lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgboi dani tsei lɛ aná shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting young cocoa seedlings during their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know which direction to plant a cassava stem in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo?

english: Look closely at the small buds on the cassava stem. Plant the stem so the buds are pointing upwards toward the sky, because planting them upside down makes it hard for shoots to grow and reduces your yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei bibii lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛbɛŋkɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he Dumɔ ŋmei lɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers from my plantain plant instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie plantain tso ko mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow makes them fight for food and water. Leaving only one main plant, one medium follower, and one small shoot gives you much bigger and heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ehaa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Shi tso titri kome pɛ. Follower kome ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kɛ tso bibioo kome baaha oná plantain ni da ni tsii kwraa.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in wet, cool, and dense shade. Pruning your cocoa trees to let in sun and air helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo, ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kookoo tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What is eating small holes inside the middle of my young maize plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides inside the growing center of the maize plant and eats the leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my plantain stems keep growing back in clusters even after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ kui amli beni mifo amɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow from an underground bulb called a corm. If you cut the top without removing or treating the underground corm, the roots will keep pushing up new baby shoots to survive.
ga: Plantains jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ tubers lɛ amli. Kɛji ofolɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ojieee loo otsuuu ŋmei lɛ he lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baatsi ŋmeii heei kɛje kpo koni amɛhi shi.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it means your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. This usually happens when the soil lacks nutrients or after heavy rains wash away your fertilizer.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele tsei lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bɛ mli loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ elaaje lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sheds flowers to save energy when conditions are tough.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsei lɛ miihao. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi amli wa.

english: Why do some weeds grow back so fast right after I cut them with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi daa oya beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many stubborn weeds have underground tubers or runner roots that store food. Just cutting the leaves leaves the roots alive, allowing them to quickly push out fresh new leaves.
ga: Jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni ji enyɔ ni kɛ niyenii toɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná wala. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛreɔ baai heei oya.

english: Why should I leave dry grass around the base of my crops instead of clearing and burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ he moŋ fe ni mafo mli ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving dry grass acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly during hot days, and slowly breaks down to feed the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi lɛ ni egbi lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni efite fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide vital shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa trees' early growth stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ kookoo tso dalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces plants to compete with each other for sunlight, root space, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weaker stems and smaller crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shishifãi ahe, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient found in manure or fertilizer that helps plants make energy and build strong, green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow bushy leaves but yield very few fruits after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baa bibii babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using fertilizers with too much nitrogen encourages the tomato plant to spend energy growing leaves and stems rather than developing flowers and setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ tomato tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: What causes black spots to appear on my pepper fruits before they are ready for market?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ anɔ dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ?

english: Black spots are often caused by fungal infections that spread through high humidity and rainwater splashing soil onto the plant, which can be reduced by spreading mulch on the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Abaanyɛ aba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is Striga weed so difficult to get rid of once it invades my cereal crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ abaajie Striga jwɛi lɛ kɛji etutua miŋmaa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches directly to the roots of crops like maize and sorghum to steal their food, and its tiny seeds can remain dormant in the soil for over ten years.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju eniyenii. kɛ dumɔwui bibii E-baanyɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma

english: How do I know if cassava stem cuttings are good quality before I plant them in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava ni mifo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Good cassava cuttings come from healthy, mature plants, have clear raised buds along the stem, and release a thick white sap when freshly cut.
ga: Cassava ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ amli. Fɔfɔi ni mli tse yɛ tso lɛ he fɛɛ. Ni mliki yɛŋ ni mli edɔ baahi kɛji akɛ afo ehee.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize lose their high-yielding genetics in the second generation, resulting in uneven crop growth and much lower harvests compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ laajeɔ wala yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my groundnut plants start dropping their leaves when rain falls constantly for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves plant roots of air, preventing groundnut roots from absorbing nutrients and causing the leaves to yellow and drop early.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines above ground naturally dry up and turn yellow, signaling that the plant has finished storing all its food energy in the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that create shade and keep the soil moist, giving young cocoa trees the safe environment they need to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing them properly allows each plant enough room to grow big leaves and full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Baai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaakwɛ baai wuji kɛ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the crop the strength to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps rain water flow away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔɔɔ Dumɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juice from under the leaves. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves open and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes into the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the plant leaves during the heat of the day, so treating the crop early in the morning or late evening targets them effectively.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ tsɔɔ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch maximum sunlight. When the leaves catch sunlight, the plant makes food that goes into the ground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafee niyenii ni abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Plantain roots lie shallow near the top of the soil while carrying heavy fruit stalks. Supporting the trunk with a sturdy branched stick or bamboo pole prevents wind from pulling the root out.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɛɔ aduawai ahe tsei ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei niji loo ŋmei tsei ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekajie shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently damp and cool helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ trukaa, nu bɛ, loo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does leaving weeds in my field stop my crops from yielding well?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mijieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your field, stealing water, fertilizer, and light away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all soil nutrients go directly to growing your crop.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oyale mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa odumɔi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ, ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it beneficial for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt. This acts as a natural soil food that helps neighboring heavy-feeding crops grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a plant virus they spread while feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings fall over and die right at the base of the stem in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni Mine gboi yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by dampness fungi in wet soil attacking weak stems. Overwatering nursery beds or overcrowding seeds creates humid conditions where these soil germs kill young shoots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni tutuaa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli loo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ baa. Nɛkɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli nɛɛ baagbe ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms even when they are not dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? Ni tso lɛ egbiko?

english: Plantains often fall because microscopic root worms or stem borer insects destroy their shallow roots underground, leaving the heavy plant without an anchor against windy weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. amɛteŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ ni amɛbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but the flowers fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely high, when the soil dries out completely during flowering, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Ehaa tsei woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their tiny young pods before they grow into mature cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miijie ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ? Bulk dani eda ni etsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eda kwraa?

english: Young cocoa pods drop off naturally (called cherelle wilt) when the tree does not have enough water, sunlight, or soil nutrients to feed all the pods at the same time.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe (ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt) kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu, hulu la, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water stays trapped around the roots in heavy clay soil after continuous rains, suffocating the roots and allowing rot fungi to attack.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be sɛɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: How do I know from looking at the plant that my yams are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji okwɛ tso lɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam plants signal maturity when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and completely dry up, showing that food storage in the underground tuber is complete.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ eshɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and stronger if I plant them at the very first major rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early planting allows crop roots to consume the 'nitrogen flush,' which is a natural surge of rich plant food released by warm dry soil immediately after the first heavy rains hit it.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ashishifãi ni amɛyeɔ ‘nitrogen flush’, ni ji tso niyenii ni fa babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying weedkiller on my crops when there is morning mist on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ahe be mli ni leebi afua yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Morning mist leaves extra water drops on plant leaves. When you spray weedkiller on wet leaves, the chemical gets diluted or runs off onto the ground before the weed can absorb it, wasting your expensive spray.
ga: Leebi afua lɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie baai ni efɔ nɔ lɛ Tsofai lɛ baatsɔ nu mli loo ebaaho kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa o-spray ni jara wa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How long after spraying my farm chemicals do I need to wait before rain ruins the work?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai shwie ŋmɔ ko nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aná nitsumɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Most crop chemicals need about two to four hours of clear, dry weather after spraying to soak properly into the leaves. If heavy rain falls sooner than that, it washes the chemical away and you may need to spray again.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse ni egbi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ koni ebote baai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ oya fe nakai lɛ, tsofai lɛ baaho ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni ashwie nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does spraying weeds early in the morning work better than spraying in the afternoon?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shwane?

english: Early morning is often best because winds are calm and temperatures are cool, which prevents the chemical from drifting away or evaporating into the air before it reaches the weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, leebi maŋkpa ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ dioo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa tsofai lɛ agbɛ ashwã loo amɛkatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛyashɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: How does morning fog affecting moisture in the air help or harm my growing crops?
ga: Te leebi afua lɛ saa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ eyeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ awui?

english: Gentle morning moisture helps keep young crops hydrated during dry periods, but prolonged foggy conditions leave leaves wet for too long, which can cause fungal diseases like black pod or leaf blights to spread.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ blɛoo leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Shi afua shihilɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni etsɔ diŋ loo baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba.

english: Why do weather conditions like wind and rain coming from neighboring regions affect when I should plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni jɛɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ saa be ni esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rain clouds and seasonal winds usually travel across large areas from neighboring regions. Understanding these movement patterns helps you time your planting so your seeds get enough moisture right after sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ atatui kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ be mli lɛ fãa kɛyaa hei wuji kɛjɛɔ kpokpai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ onu nɛkɛ nyiɛmɔi nɛɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ be awo odumɔ be lɛ mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to sprout and grow much faster than my crops right after an evening rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely hardy and lie waiting in the topsoil; a sudden evening rain gives them the moisture boost they need to germinate instantly and compete with your crops for sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa gbɛkɛ lɛ ha amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kroko ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni okɛ otsei lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun even if the air was cool and humid in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ waa leebi moŋ.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. The plant droops temporarily to protect itself from drying out, and it will recover as the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni ebaahe ewa lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ

english: Why is it important to clear tall weeds around my young crops before the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu midumɔwui lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Clearing weeds early ensures that when the rain arrives, your crops get all the rainwater and soil nutrients for themselves instead of sharing them with fast-growing weeds that can choke young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Mohu ɔ, jaa kɛ ha jwɛi nɛ waa oya nɛ ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ tsei bibihi nɛ a gbo ɔ.

english: Is it good practice to apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, a heavy downpour can wash your fertilizer straight off the farm or deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it. It is better to apply fertilizer when light rain is expected so it dissolves gently into the soil.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ o-fertilizer lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli blɛoo.

english: Why do yellow spots appear on my crop leaves after several days of damp weather and light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ miije kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ gbii babaoo ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow spots are usually signs of leaf fungus, which thrives when leaves stay wet and cold for days. Good spacing between crops lets air flow through and dry the leaves faster to prevent these spots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela he okadi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Amɛ daa kɛji baai lɛ edɔ ni edɔ gbii babaoo. He ni jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya koni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. They require shade from companion plants like plantain to shield their leaves from burning and to retain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even if it rained earlier in the week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ otsi lɛ shishijee mli moŋ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water vapor faster than roots can draw moisture from the ground. The plant temporarily droops its leaves to reduce surface area exposed to the sun and preserve its remaining water.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu lasu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni ekɛbu nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why is burning the bush on my farmland before planting bad for my soil in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: While burning clears land quickly, the fire destroys organic matter, beneficial insects, and soil microbes that keep the earth fertile. Over time, it leaves the soil hard, dry, and unable to hold moisture.
ga: Beni shãa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ Shi la kpataaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ. ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa je lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Be ni be hoɔ lɛ, enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear old crop stems and weeds out of my field before starting a new planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei akutsei momoi kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Old plant leftovers often harbor hidden crop diseases, fungal spores, and insect eggs from the previous season. Clearing them prevents these pests from spreading directly to your new seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei momo ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɛɔ tsei ahe helai. Fungal spores kɛ insect eggs kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã odumɔwui heei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers under the soil stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen or too much shade, the plant uses all its energy to build stems and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the storage roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ, moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛba shi koni amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni ato lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops need manure or fertilizer just by looking at their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Plants show hunger through leaf colors. If lower leaves turn pale yellow, the plant usually lacks nitrogen. If the leaves turn purple or reddish, the plant is missing phosphorus.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe su nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ purple loo etsuru Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together is beneficial. Cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, which feeds the maize plants, while maize provides shade and natural support.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aba sɛɛnamɔ. Cowpeas shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they were buried too deep for the shoot to reach air, if the soil dried out completely after planting, or if soil insects ate the seeds before they sprouted.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the maize crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to compete aggressively for sun, water, and nutrients. Because they grow faster than crop seeds, early weeding is necessary so your main crops aren't starved of resources.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ he miihia koni onibii titri lɛ akafee nɔ ni he hiaa bo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the leaves or extra stems from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning extra leaves and non-fruiting stems allows air to flow through the plant to prevent fungal diseases, while directing the plant's food and water straight into growing bigger tomatoes.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting plantains alongside cocoa provides fast-growing shade to protect the delicate leaves from burning and helps keep the soil moist during the cocoa plant's first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni daa oya koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots to spread and ensures it gets enough nourishment to grow larger ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekwɛ koni ená niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa tsei wuji.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is a key food crops need to grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps bring back the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make the soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the dirt. When the plant finishes growing, it leaves that natural food behind in the soil for the next crop to use.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Eshiɔ nakai adebɔɔ niyenii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Why does spreading dried leaves or grass around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minibii ni miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the dirt around crops with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and breaks down into natural food for the plant.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai gboi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni efite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei

english: These worms are likely fall armyworms, a destructive pest that loves to eat the tender leaves inside young maize. Treating your crop early with neem water or recommended pest controls keeps them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni sumɔɔ ni eye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi kɛ neem nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava shed all its leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells as a survival trick to save water and keep its roots alive underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Taakɛ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaawoo ni akɛbaabu nu he ni akɛha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, poor watering, or lack of nutrients. Ensuring regular watering and keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ nu awo tso lɛ shishi daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha tso lɛ shishi koni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why don't seeds saved from my last harvest produce as well as certified seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ jeee ekome lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are hybrid varieties specifically bred to give a high yield only in their first planting. Saving seeds from that harvest leads to weaker offspring, so buying fresh certified seed each season yields much better results.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa seshi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa yibii kpakpai babaoo baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes helps the plant produce larger tubers under the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full sunlight and harsh dry winds. They require temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava grown nearby to shield their leaves and maintain soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers have reached full maturity for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cassava tubers typically reach maturity between 9 and 12 months when the lower leaves begin to yellow and drop off naturally, indicating that the plant is storing maximum starch in its underground roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei kɛ ŋmeii babaoo toɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the central vein of lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency, which limits the maize plant's ability to build green foliage and produce strong ears.
