ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee baai eŋɔli kɛ toi ni mli wa.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are my young oil palm trees producing small bunches with empty palm nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ mli?

english: Underdeveloped palm bunches usually result from poor pollination or shortages of key nutrients like potassium, as well as water stress during the flower development stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tsei akui ni edako jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni ehiii loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni bɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ nu mli haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra shoot suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow causes them to compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, leading to smaller bunches and weaker stems.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ aniji lɛ feɔ bibii ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, which damage the leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwa tsei amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas in my field improve the growth of my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Cowpeas have root nodules containing beneficial bacteria that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food for tuber growth, while keeping them off damp soil to reduce fungal diseases.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ tso mli koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛfee niyenii aha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii helai aba shi.

english: Why do some of my harvested maize cobs have missing kernels at the top tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels at the tip occur when dry weather or high temperatures prevent the silk threads at the top of the cob from getting successfully pollinated during flowering.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo hulutsoo ni naa wa tsiɔ siliki ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ naa koni ekaye omanye yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out so quickly just a few days after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil loses moisture quickly when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure, or when it is left bare under direct sunlight. Covering the soil with organic mulch traps moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ Mulching kɛ organic mulch baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans restores nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves, but very small tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf vegetation above ground rather than swelling its root tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifã lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect activity for pollination. Stable moisture and proper airflow around the plant help flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be Loo kooloi bibii nyɛŋ afee pollination. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni bɔleɔ Tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my young maize plants and chew them up?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the growing central leaf whorl of young corn. Detecting them early allows you to apply recommended biological or botanical treatments before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ baa teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛnamɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsei ahe tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus they transmit. These insects feed on young leaves, draining the plant's food and stunting its development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living canopy shades, protecting the tender cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo ni mli tse lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do officers advise planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally feeding the maize while covering the soil surface to suppress weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look pale and thin even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for essential soil nutrients, space, and sunlight. Even with enough rain, the weeds steal the fertilizer and food that your crops need to stay healthy and green.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ hu juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still small rather than waiting until they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young crops are at their weakest stage and suffer the most from competition. Clearing weeds early ensures the crop gets all the nutrients during its most critical growth phase, resulting in a much higher yield later.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ ni akaŋshii náa amɛnɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the plants regain their green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji He ni esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. This temporary drooping is the plant's natural way of saving moisture, and the leaves will stand back up in the cooler evening as long as the soil remains moist.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ. Ni baai lɛ baadamɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Ensuring consistent watering and planting shade trees nearby to block harsh afternoon heat can help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na bei ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli daa ni odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ. Hebuu kɛjɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava stem cuttings have small leaf buds or 'eyes' above each leaf scar along the stem. Always plant the cutting with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight up without wasting energy.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ baai bibii loo ‘tsei’ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ fã fɛɛ fã ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ. ni hewalɛ fiteee

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field with no tall crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high winds, which dry out their leaves quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh weather until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he waa. ni haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni akɛfataa cocoa bibii ahe lɛ baabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Does lifting yam vines onto wooden stakes really make the yams underground grow bigger?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha sweet potato ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines onto stakes spreads out the leaves so they can catch more sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to manufacture food, which is then sent down into the soil to feed and expand the yam tuber.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. The nearby maize uses this extra nitrogen as natural food, helping it grow better without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Weeds are wild, native plants that have adapted to local soils over many years, allowing their seeds to sprout and soak up water much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing light, water, and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the growing top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center whorl of the maize plant to feed on young leaves. Applying approved biopesticides or neem leaf extracts into the center of the plant early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvested maize yield less grain than the original packaged seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo fe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishijee ŋmãa ni mihe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are hybrid varieties specifically bred to produce a high yield for only one season. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special genetic traits, resulting in smaller, less uniform plants in the next generation.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai fɔmɔ sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ baa yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture, giving the young cocoa trees the protection they need to grow strong during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ buɔ amɛhe koni amɛdara waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential food for plants to stay green and grow; when it runs out, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has left from the older bottom leaves to the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ efo lɛ, tsei jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ amli.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut to get the best yields when planting?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo koni ená yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ adu?

english: It is best to use the hard, mature middle portion of the cassava stem. The green top parts dry out too quickly, and the very bottom part near the roots is often too woody and sprouts slowly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ baatsu nii. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ fã ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei tsɔ ni edaa blɛoo.

english: What is eating holes into the deep center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni miiye bu ko yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel (the whorl) of the maize plant during the day and eat the soft young leaves, leaving sawdust-like droppings behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter (mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Flowers drop off pepper plants mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like boron and calcium. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ pepper tsei amli lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ boron kɛ calcium ni bɛ Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Yam plants need their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy. Raising the leaves off the ground on stakes allows maximum sunlight exposure and prevents leaves from rotting due to wet ground contact.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ ni amɛkpeɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Should I plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three consistent rains before planting. The first rain often clears the heat, but the soil remains dry underneath; planting too early can cause seeds to dry up and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ dani odu. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa shi. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo yɛ eshishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants wrinkling and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat and uneven watering. Keeping insects away helps protect the plants from this virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji hela ko ni haa tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛbaa. Kplukai ahebuu baaye abua ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Why do tiny beetles damage my harvested maize when I store it in bags inside my home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli yɛ shia lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects are weevils, which lay eggs inside the maize grains while they are drying or in storage. If the maize is not dried thoroughly to a very low moisture level before storage, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat the inside of the grains.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni agbiɔ loo akɛtoɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa kɛyashɛɛɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi waa dani akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii.

english: Yellowing leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are getting too much direct sunlight or lacking nitrogen in the soil. Providing shade crops like plantains protects them while their root systems develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water during hot periods. It is a natural survival trick, though prolonged curling means the soil needs moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ teemɔŋ sane ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ taoɔ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Flower drop in tomatoes happens when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady watering and balanced nutrients helps the plant hold its flowers to set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. aloo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo yɛ Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste very bitter when I harvest them after a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ mikpa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally produces higher levels of bitter defense compounds when stressed by prolonged drought. Harvesting after good rain or planting sweet cassava varieties helps reduce this bitterness.
ga: Cassava feɔ anti-bitter compounds ni fa babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli. Kɛ́ akpa nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ loo adu ŋmei srɔtoi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves turning yellow even though I water the farm every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering chokes plant roots by filling all the air spaces in the soil with water, preventing the roots from breathing. Yellow leaves can be a sign of drowned roots just as much as dried-out roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli fe nine lɛ gbeɔ amɛshishifãi kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ nɔ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi ni ebote shishi lɛ he okadi tamɔ bɔ ni amɛji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ shishifãi ni egbi

english: Why are there white powdery spots covering the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda ni ha ŋmeii tso lɛ baai ahe yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This white powder is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which spreads easily when plants are crowded together in humid conditions. Proper plant spacing improves airflow and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɛkɛ powda yɛŋ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning purple at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young corn indicate a phosphorus deficiency in the soil. Phosphorus is essential for early root and leaf growth, and applying a phosphorus-rich fertilizer resolves the purple coloring.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Fosfɔs he hiaa waa kɛha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu purple naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin instead of becoming strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ jwɛi najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, plants stretch unnaturally tall to compete for sunlight above their neighbors. Proper spacing allows plants to catch light on all sides and grow thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa koni amɛkɛ hulu la atswa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ ahe akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ la nɔ kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he, ni eyɛ tso lɛ shishi ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant beans alongside my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmãa ni ji kooloi aniyenii titri lɛ afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural nitrogen feeds the neighboring maize plant and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during digging or stored in a hot, airtight space. Storing whole, undamaged tubers in a cool, well-ventilated, elevated structure prevents fungal rot from starting.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa amɛ loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni bɛ muji lɛ ato he ko ni nɔ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Is it better to nurse palm seeds at home before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ shia dani aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli koni ayakwɛ amɛ?

english: Nursing seeds in a protected area at home allows you to give tender seedlings daily care, shade, and water. This ensures only strong, healthy plants are selected for transplanting into the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he yɛ shia lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ blɛoo, ohaa amɛ hulutsoo ni ohaa amɛ nu daa gbi. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahalaa tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ koni akɛwo ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli.

english: What time of the year is best for me to plant young tree seedlings in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu dumɔwui bibii yɛ Ghana?

english: It is best to plant young tree crops at the start of the main rainy season, usually around April or May. This allows the fresh roots to settle and grow deep while water is naturally abundant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu tsei bibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April loo May mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi heei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my oil palm seedlings when planting them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ abɔ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing oil palms about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern gives each tree enough space to spread its branches, access soil nutrients, and receive sunlight without crowding out neighboring trees.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mitai 9 yɛ koŋ etɛ mli, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eniji lɛ eshwa. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni anáa kɛ hulu la ni anáa ni atsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my young oil palm trees take a few years before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ heɔ afii fioo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Young oil palm trees focus their early energy on establishing strong root systems and thick trunks. It usually takes 3 to 4 years of growth before the tree is mature enough to bear heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ amamɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young palm trees turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-palm tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is missing important soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that the soil is too waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my palm trees dry up and turn brown over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: As palm trees grow new fronds from the top center, the older lower leaves naturally mature, dry out, and die so the plant can direct its energy toward new growth and fruit production.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei tso ko kwɛ baai heei kɛjɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ Baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ kɛya dalɛ hee kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Oil palms grow best in deep, loose, well-drained soil that holds moisture without staying flooded. They also prefer areas that get plenty of direct sunlight and regular rainfall.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ Amɛsumɔɔ hei ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ hu.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my newly planted palm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first two years while the palm trees are still small, you can grow food crops between the rows to maximize your land use, as long as you keep them a short distance away from the palm stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ koni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo. Shii abɔ ni okɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo lɛ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my young tree crops?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: You should clear weeds in a circle around the base of young trees every 1 to 2 months to prevent weeds from stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your developing crop.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi awo kooyigbɛ kɛbɔle he. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei bibii daa nyɔji 1 kɛyashi 2 koni jwɛi akaju nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off old dry leaves from my palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei ahe baai momo ni egbi lɛ?

english: Pruning dead leaves cleans up the tree, improves airflow, reduces places for pests to hide, and makes it much easier to inspect and harvest fruit bunches.
ga: Baai ni egboi lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni etsumɔ tso lɛ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Ha hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ayahi lɛ aba shi. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaakwɛ aduawai akui lɛ amli ni akpa amɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge, tall leafy stems but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or get too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing leaves to fight for sunlight instead of storing food down in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baa lɛ koni ekɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha niyenii ahi oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha hulutsoo bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant move calcium into the developing fruit.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil. They act as natural fertilizer builders, helping your maize grow stronger while enriching the ground.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa yɛ be mli ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and stake my yam vines high off the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo he ko ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to feed the growing tuber below. Lifting vines off the wet ground also keeps them from catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Too many extra shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain stem for food, sunlight, and water. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main stem to produce a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine (tso lɛ) kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds during the first few weeks after my crops sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikpa nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, plant food, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a strong start before the weeds can steal their nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, tsei aniyenii kɛ hulu la. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ aju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn soft and get ruined by insects so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa hela baa oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stored before it is completely dry retains moisture inside the grains. Moisture encourages mold to grow and creates ideal conditions for grain-boring insects to multiply and destroy your harvest.
ga: Abele ni akɛtoɔ dani egbiɔ kwraa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi. Fɛ̃i woɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha dumɔwui ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off to the ground without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off mainly when they are not pollinated by tiny beneficial insects, or when the cocoa tree is stressed by drought, bad weather, or insect pests.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe. Aloo be mli ni hɔmɔ miigba kookoo tsei anaa lɛ. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui

english: What is pollination in cocoa, and how does it actually happen on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ? Ni te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ebaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pollination happens when very tiny insects, called midges, carry yellow dust (pollen) from one cocoa flower to another so the flower can grow into a cocoa pod.
ga: Pollination baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ. Okɛ sũ ni ji ŋmɔŋ (pollen) kɛjɛ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the main trunk instead of just on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni ewoɔ eniji lɛ anɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers on the trunk and thick branches so that tiny pollinating insects can easily reach them, and so the trunk can support heavy pods later.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei akutsei kɛ tsei aniji ni mli tse nɔ koni amɛha kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ aná he ko amɛhi. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaaná Ni tsɔne lɛ baanyɛ aye abua pods ni tsii sɛɛ mli.

english: How long after my cocoa trees start showing flowers should I expect to see tiny pods growing?
ga: Be enyiɛ eho kɛjɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ bɔi fɔfɔi? Kulɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mana pod bibioo ko. eda loo edaaa

english: Once flowers open and get pollinated, you should start seeing small, green cocoa pods forming within a few weeks to a month.
ga: Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfee pollin lɛ Esa akɛ oje shishi ona kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Foji yɛ otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome mli.

english: How can I bring more of the tiny insects that help pollinate cocoa flowers to my farm?
ga: Mikɛ kooloi bibii komɛi baaba. Te amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛwoɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: You can leave rotting banana stumps and moist leaf litter under your trees, which creates a cool, damp home where pollinating midges can breed.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshɛrɛ banana tsei ni egboi kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ ashwie. Obaanyɛ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shia ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afɔ́ bii yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Will spraying chemicals while my cocoa trees are full of flowers affect my future harvest?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi eyi amɛmli lolo lɛ baaná wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, spraying harsh insecticides during flowering can kill the friendly midges that pollinate your crop, causing flowers to drop without making pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni he wa ni okɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni ji naanyobɔɔ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Does having too many shade trees on my farm prevent my cocoa trees from flowering?
ga: Ani tsei babaoo ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi kookoo tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi?

english: Heavy shade reduces sunlight, making the tree spend its energy growing big leaves instead of producing the flowers needed for cocoa pods.
ga: Shade ni mli tse lɛ baaha hulu la lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai agboi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do some of my very small cocoa pods turn black and dry up shortly after the flowers fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi pɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree naturally sheds excess young pods it cannot feed, or it can be caused by diseases like black pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherel wilt’, ni baa beni tso ko shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ helai tamɔ black pods ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa trees produce more flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne kroko ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo?

english: Pruning lets air and light reach the trunk, which encourages the tree to form healthy flower spots and lowers humidity that causes flower diseases.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efee fɔfɔii ni mli wa. ni eha hulutsoo ni kɛ hela baa fɔfɔi amli lɛ aba shi

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is taking too long to start flowering during the main season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiye be babaoo tsɔ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛbe titri lɛ mli?

english: If your trees show no flowers while neighboring farms are blooming after the rains start, your trees may lack nutrients in the soil or be suffering from pest damage.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ wooo fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ fɔfɔi yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ.

english: How far away from the trunk of my cocoa tree should I clear the weeds?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi kɛya he ko tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing a circle about three to four feet away from the main trunk protects the surface roots, prevents weed competition for soil nutrients, and keeps pests from easily crawling up the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie kooloo lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo tso lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my cocoa trees right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa amɛ.

english: Clearing weeds post-harvest removes hiding spots for pests like capsids and fungal spores, allowing your trees to recover quickly and prepare healthy leaves and flowers for the next season.
ga: Nikpamɔ sɛɛ jwɛi jieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal spores. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa oya. ni osaa baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Is it good to leave the cleared weeds on the ground near my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving cleared weeds on the ground acts as mulch. As they decompose, they keep the soil moist during dry periods and return natural nutrients back into the earth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni amɛgboi lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli nibii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How does clearing the ground under my cocoa trees prevent black pod disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ojie he ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ koni black pod hela akabote mli?

english: Black pod disease thrives in damp, dark environments. Clearing weeds around the base improves sunlight exposure and airflow, drying out excess moisture that allows the fungus to spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo mli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does the main cocoa harvest season in Ghana take place around October and November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kpamɔ be titri ni afeɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ baa yɛ October kɛyashi November aaafee lɛ?

english: October and November follow the major rainy season. The combination of rainfall followed by sun causes the cocoa pods to fully mature, sweeten, and turn ripe for harvesting.
ga: October kɛ November nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni hulutsoo nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kwraa, amɛfeɔ ŋɔɔ ni amɛshwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why should I clear the brush under my cocoa trees before harvest starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ dani ŋmaakpamɔ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing the farm floor before harvesting makes it safer to walk, prevents snakes and wild animals from hiding in the bush, and ensures you do not miss any ripe or fallen pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa ŋmaa lɛ, ebaaha efee shweshweeshwe akɛ ooonyiɛ nɔ. Tsi onufui kɛ koo mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ jwɛi lɛ amli. Ni ekwɛɔ koni okɛ pods ni ekwɛ̃ loo ni egbee shi lɛ eko akakpa ohe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn from green or red to yellow or orange when ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ nɔ beni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: The color change signals that the beans inside have finished growing, developed their natural sugars, and are ready to be harvested for proper fermentation.
ga: Su tsakemɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbe naa. Eyɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar babaoo ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa

english: Why do some of the small cocoa pods on my tree dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Ani mitsei lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaafee ediŋŋ dani amɛdara?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. The tree intentionally sheds extra young pods it cannot feed when it faces stress from sunlight, lack of water, or limited soil nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛjieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ awo amɛmli kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kpe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers after the heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The change from wet weather to drier sunlight acts as a natural signal to the cocoa tree that it is time to flower and start producing new pods.
ga: Tsakemɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛyaa hulu ni mli egbi. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ kɛha cacao tso lɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi heei feemɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantains when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ bɔ ni plantains lɛ fee beni midu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves, providing the necessary shade and humidity young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does maize manage to grow in drier places like Burkina Faso where there is less rain?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɔ fioo yɛ lɛ?

english: Certain maize varieties are bred to tolerate heat and mature very quickly, allowing them to make full use of short rainy periods and still produce grain in dry climates.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli ni amɛdara oya waa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli. ni ewoɔ yibii lolo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ amli

english: Why does maize seem to grow so exceptionally well in middle-belt areas like Techiman?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ titri yɛ middle belt hei tamɔ Techiman lɛ?

english: Areas in transitional climate zones have fertile soil and two distinct rainy seasons, providing the ideal combination of steady sunlight, good moisture, and nutrient-rich earth that maize needs.
ga: He ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ. ni haa hulu la ni tsoɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa ŋmãa yɔɔ mli babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before the cobs are fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the plant is starving for nitrogen or water, which causes it to draw nutrients away from older leaves to try to keep the growing cob alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ ŋmei ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but fail to produce any cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miida shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When plants are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen without enough water or sunlight, they use all their energy growing leaves and stalks instead of flowering and producing ears.
ga: Beni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aha amɛ nitrogen babaoo ni nu loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ amɛbai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ toi baa lɛ

english: Why are the grains on my harvested corn small and light instead of full and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eyi obɔ ni etsii lɛ?

english: Light grains happen if the crop suffers from dry spells or lacks nutrients during the flowering and grain-filling stage, causing the plant to produce incomplete kernels.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni eyiɔ obɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ wooo wui jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting my maize right at the first rain yield a better crop than waiting a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fe otsii fioo komɛi ni aaamɛ lɛ?

english: The first rains release a sudden burst of natural nitrogen trapped in the dry soil, giving early-planted seeds a rapid boost in root and shoot development.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni emɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ trukaa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni adu oya lɛ shwereɔ shishifãi kɛ tsei oya.

english: If you planted hybrid maize seeds, saving and re-planting them will yield weaker plants and fewer cobs; purchasing fresh certified seeds each season ensures high yields.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ Hebuu kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ŋmãa bibii lɛ hu baafee bibioo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa yibii babaoo baa.

english: How can I prevent wind from blowing down my maize plants before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatswa ŋmãa tsei lɛ dani akpa ŋmãa?

english: Planting seeds at the proper depth, spacing rows correctly, and mounding soil around the base of the stalks gives roots a strong anchor in the ground to withstand high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa Gbɛ ni ja ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ ŋta lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋta ni mli wa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: How can harvested corn stay good long enough to be transported to big regional markets without spoiling?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni akɛya kpokpaa nɔ jarayeli hei wuji ni efiteee?

english: Maize stays fresh for long trips when it is dried down to a very low moisture level before bagging, which prevents mold from growing and keeps the grains firm.
ga: Abɛi hiɔ shi ehee kɛha gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ kɛji akɛ egbi kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ baa shi waa dani akɛwo kotoku mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ adara, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do insects attack and destroy my stored corn so quickly after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ mi-ŋma ni mikɛto lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils and beetles thrive in warm, damp environments, so if corn is stored while still slightly wet or in humid spaces, insects reproduce rapidly and eat the grains.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ fioo lolo loo yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ oya ni eyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I safely apply pest spray on my farm without damaging my health or crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mifiteee mihewalɛ loo miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Always wear protective boots, gloves, and a face cover, and spray in the direction of the wind during the early morning. This ensures chemical fumes do not blow onto your skin or burn leaves under harsh sunshine.
ga: Woɔ atadei, glɔvs kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be. ni okɛshwie he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa Enɛ haa tsofa lasu lɛ shwieɔ ohewolo nɔ loo eshãaa baai yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: What should I do when I notice yellow, twisted leaves spreading across my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Twisted yellow leaves usually indicate cassava mosaic disease. You must pull out and burn the affected plants immediately to prevent insects from spreading the virus to healthy plants nearby.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni etsilɛ lɛ tsɔɔ cassava mosaic hela. Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oshã amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight lines instead of scattering seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every seed has enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow large. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier without stepping on crop stems.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ agbo. Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni atsɔ tsei ashishifãi anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and rot on the soil before the fruits can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally weak and cannot support heavy fruit. Tying the plants to wooden stakes keeps the tomatoes off the damp ground where soil insects and mold cause rot.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha tomatoi lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tomatoi lɛ agbo.

english: Do not plant after the very first rain because the soil beneath is still dry and hot. Wait until the farm receives two or three heavy rains so seeds have enough moisture to germinate safely.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I keep the soil moist for my crops during hot dry spells in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Cover the soil around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or leaves (mulching). This layer shields the ground from harsh sunlight, keeping moisture trapped in the soil longer.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi loo baai (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I grow maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and attracts permanent pests. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be, ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are my maize cobs coming out very small even though I clear the land carefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bibii waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Clearing land removes weeds, but maize needs heavy nutrients like nitrogen to make big cobs. Adding compost manure or fertilizer early in growth gives plants the food required to produce plump cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he ni jwɛi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie jwɛi lɛ. Shi niyenii mli nibii ni tsii, tamɔ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ efee ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Weeds naturally adapt to steal light, water, and soil food very quickly. Removing weeds within the first three weeks of planting gives your young crop the upper hand to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛju la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa otsei bibii lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ ni ji shishifãi ni wa ni amɛbaafee.

english: What is the best way to store harvested maize so tiny insects do not destroy the grains?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ toɔ? Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii akafite dumɔwui

english: Sun-dry your harvested maize until the grains are very hard, then store them in airtight bags or clean silos treated with safe grain protectants to keep webworms and beetles out.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo silo ni mli tse ni nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni webworms kɛ ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture to protect the young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field with my young cocoa trees, or will it ruin them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ? Aloo ebaakpata kookoo tso lɛ hiɛ?

english: You can plant cassava alongside cocoa, but you must keep proper spacing. Cassava roots feed aggressively on water and nutrients in the upper soil, so if planted too close, cassava will compete with and stunt the growth of your cocoa seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmei yɛ kookoo masɛi. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ bɔ ni sa. Cassava shishifãi yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ adu Cassava yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ cocoa dumɔwui lɛ baabɔ akaŋ ni ebaatsi amɛdalɛ naa.

english: If I have a small piece of land, how should I divide the space between cocoa, plantains, and root crops?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko lɛ Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aja gbɛ yɛ kookoo, plantains kɛ tubers ateŋ?

english: Prioritize your main crop by spacing cocoa trees about 3 meters apart. Place plantain suckers in between the cocoa rows for early shade, and plant cassava or vegetables only along the field boundaries so they do not compete with the cocoa.
ga: Ha onibii titrii lɛ afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛtsɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai etɛ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ koni eha hulutsoo aba mra. ni amɛdu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe pɛ. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ kookoo akaye akaŋ

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly out of the thick stem and main trunk instead of the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tso wulu lɛ mli moŋ fe niji lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the main trunk and heavy branches so that when the heavy cocoa pods develop, the thick wood can support their weight without snapping off.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kookoo ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ ba Tso lɛ mli lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ekwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli.

english: Why do new small plantain shoots start growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii heei miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui titri lɛ shishitoo

english: A plantain tree produces fruit only once and then dies. The small shoots at the base, called suckers, are the plant's natural way of reproducing so you can transplant them to grow new plantain crops.
ga: Plantain woɔ yibii shikome pɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ egboɔ. Atsɛɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ akɛ suckers. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ tsei ashwaa. No sɛɛ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ awo he kroko koni dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do older cocoa trees seem to survive fine without plantain shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo dumɔwui ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, their leaves branch out to create a thick overhead canopy of their own. This canopy shields the soil and lower tree trunk, reducing the need for temporary shade plants like plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa yɛ eyitso nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛitsu nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ he. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ dumɔwui ahe hiamɔ baa shi.

english: Lower leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up as the plantain focuses its energy on growing new leaves and forming fruit. However, widespread yellowing on younger leaves can be a sign of poor soil nutrients like potassium or fungal infection.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni plantains lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baa heei ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, baai bibii muu lɛ fɛɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, tamɔ potassium loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the main leaves turn yellow and drop, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open due to the swelling tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai titrii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ ŋmei ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do we plant cassava by cutting its stem instead of using seeds from its flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔduɔ ŋmei kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni wɔfoɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Growing cassava from stem cuttings is much faster and guarantees that the new plant will yield the same quality and quantity of tubers as the parent plant, whereas seeds take longer and produce unpredictable results.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yaa oya kwraa ni ehaa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ tso hee lɛ baawo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ.

english: How will using manure from farm animals benefit my cocoa and food crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua mi-kookoo kɛ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure and slowly releases essential nutrients into the ground. It helps the soil hold onto water during dry periods and feeds beneficial organisms that keep your crops healthy.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni ehaa nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know when my vegetables are fully mature and ready to be harvested before they spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-aduawai lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa dani amɛfite?

english: Crops like peppers and tomatoes give clear physical signals, such as changes in color, skin firmness, and size. Harvesting them right when they reach full maturity ensures they stay fresh longer during handling and transport to the market.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato Haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ su tsakemɔi Hewolo nɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ Nikpamɔ ni sa beni amɛdaraa lɛ baaha amɛhi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I leave them on the plants past their normal harvest date?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛho be ni sa akɛ akpa lɛ he?

english: When crops stay on the plant too long, they over-ripen, lose their firmness and sugar content, and become soft. Over-ripe fruits also attract insects and rot much faster, reducing your usable harvest.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafee nɔ ni edɔ fe nine. Amɛhe wa kɛ sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo. Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ oya kwraa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, obaakpa nii fioo.

english: Does the time of day I harvest my crops affect how long they will stay fresh?
ga: Ani be ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ saa be abɔ ni ebaahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, harvesting during the hot sun traps field heat inside the crop, causing it to lose water quickly and rot faster. Harvesting early in the morning when temperatures are cool helps crops retain moisture and stay fresh longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, kpamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baamɔmɔ dɔlɛ awo tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ oya. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops spoil within a few days while others can sit for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi baanyɛ ahi shi otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Different crops breathe and lose moisture at different rates after being cut. Soft produce like peppers or leafy greens break down rapidly, whereas hard root crops like yams or cassava have thick outer skins that naturally slow down moisture loss and rot.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi muɔ ni amɛfiteɔ nu yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ be mli ni afolɔ amɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ fiteɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni shishifãi ni wa tamɔ sweet potatoes loo cassava Eyɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli wa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I leave my harvested vegetables stacked in the shade for a few extra days while waiting for buyers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ ni ato yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo krokomɛi kɛfata he be mli ni mimɛɔ mɔ ko ni baahe lɛ?

english: Harvested produce continues to age even after being picked. Holding vegetables for extra days in ambient temperatures causes them to lose weight, soften, and lose market quality, even if kept in the shade.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ baaya nɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni akpa amɛ po sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai to gbii babaoo yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛhe feɔ mlɛo, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni jara waaa. Kɛji akɛ akɛto hulutsoo be mli po.

english: Why do my tomatoes bruise and rot so quickly when packed in large sacks or deep crates?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui wuji loo adekai ni mli kwɔ amli lɛ?

english: Delicate fruits carry water weight that easily crushes the bottom layers when packed too deeply. The physical pressure ruptures the plant tissues inside the fruit, causing rapid bruising and fungal rot.
ga: Yibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ woɔ nu ni tsiimɔ, ni kɛ́ akɛwo mli tsɔ lɛ, efoɔ shishigbɛ fã lɛ oya. Gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ haa tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ fãa. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe oya ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: Why do all my crops ripen at the exact same time, making it hard to manage and sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Ani ehaa ewaa akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Crops planted on the same day develop at the same speed under identical weather. To prevent everything from coming in all at once, you can plant your fields in staggered batches every one to two weeks so they mature in smaller, manageable waves.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kome mli. Bɔni afee ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akafee ekome Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔji yɛ kui amli daa otsi 1-2 koni eha dalɛ aya nɔ yɛ ŋshɔkei bibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii amli.

english: Why do my crops fetch very low prices at the market even when the harvest quality is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jara baa shi waa yɛ jara nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crop prices depend on supply and buyer demand in the market. When many farmers harvest and sell the exact same crop at the same time, or when regular buyers are away, the market becomes flooded, causing prices to fall regardless of quality.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe jara damɔ nibii ni ataoɔ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ anɔ. Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ mɛi ni heɔ nii daa lɛ bɛ lɛ, jara lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu, ni no haa nibii lɛ ajara baa shi ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni nibii lɛ hi ha.

english: Why do high yields on a small crop patch sometimes fail to make me a good profit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, yibii babaoo ni anáa yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli lɛ haaa sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa aba lɛ?

english: Small crop quantities cost more per unit to transport and manage relative to their total sales value. If buyer demand is low or transport costs are high, harvesting a small batch may cost more in labor and travel than the crop brings in revenue.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ aheɔ shika babaoo kɛha fã kome kɛha tsɔne ni akɛyaa kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ jara ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ he. Kɛji akɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ nii lɛ faaa loo gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ fa Nikpamɔ yɛ kui bibii amli Ekolɛ nitsumɔ kɛ gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo baafee babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shika baa lɛ nikpamɔ.

english: Does planting a larger area of a single crop change how efficiently I can farm it?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni da lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni okwaayeli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ?

english: Planting larger, uniform blocks allows you to spend less time and resources per plant on activities like weeding, spraying, and harvesting. Larger volumes also attract commercial buyers who prefer buying in bulk over visiting multiple small plots.
ga: Blɔkii wuji ni yɔɔ ekome lɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa okɛ be kɛ nibii fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tso kome nɔ yɛ nifeemɔi tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nɔ. Nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ hu ŋɔɔ jarayeli he jarayelɔi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhe babaoo moŋ fe ni amɛaayasara shikpɔji bibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce fruit at two different times in a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ?

english: Mango trees have two distinct harvesting periods each year: the first harvest occurs during the rainy season in June and July, while the second harvest occurs later during the dry season.
ga: Mango tsei yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ daa afi. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ June kɛ July mli. yɛ be mli ni kpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: When is the major rainy season harvest for mangoes in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be akpaa mango yɛ Ghana yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: The main rainy season harvest for mangoes takes place in June and July, requiring farmers to collect their fruits during the wet months.
ga: Nugbɔ be mli mango kpamɔ titri lɛ baa yɛ June kɛ July mli. Esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ abua aduawai lɛ anaa yɛ nugbɔ nyɔji lɛ amli.

english: Should I pick my mangoes in June and July even if it is raining heavily?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akpa mango yɛ June-July mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po?

english: Yes, the first harvest season naturally coincides with the rainy season in June and July, so harvesting during rainy weather is normal for this crop cycle.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji June kɛ July lɛ kpãa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ nɛɛ mli.

english: What is the main difference between my first and second mango harvests of the year?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ afi lɛ mli mango klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: The first harvest happens in the rainy season (June and July), while the second harvest happens during the dry season, which allows the mature fruit to remain hanging on the tree longer.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nikpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli (June kɛ July), yɛ be mli ni nikpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Enɛ haa aduawai ni edara lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my mangoes stay hanging on the tree longer during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: The second harvest falls in the dry season, which naturally allows the ripe fruit to stay attached and hang safely on the branch for an extended period without spoiling quickly.
ga: Nikpamɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Taakɛ eji lɛ, aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baakpɛtɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ he ni ebaakpɛtɛ he shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee oya.

english: How does dry weather affect how long mature mangoes can stay on the tree?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa be abɔ ni mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Dry season conditions give mature mangoes strong retention on the branch, enabling them to hang on the tree for a long time until you are ready to pick them.
ga: Hɔmɔ be lɛ haa mango ni eda lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji ahe jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ okɛ amɛ baato.

english: Can I leave my mango fruits on the tree for a while during the dry season harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi mango yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be fioo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni egbi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, during the second harvest season in the dry weather, mangoes can comfortably remain on the tree for a long duration before harvesting.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ kpamɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ, Mango baanyɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hejɔlɛ mli dani akpa.

english: When during the year can I expect to make the highest profit from my mango farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be manyɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ mi mango tso yibii lɛ amli yɛ afi lɛ mli?

english: You will make the most profit when your farm hits its peak season, as that is the period of highest crop output where the real money is made.
ga: Obaaná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛ́ oŋmɔ lɛ mli bii lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ ji akɛ, eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ nɔyaa ni fe fɛɛ ni haa anáa shika diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why is the peak season so important for my mango sales?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ he hiaa yɛ mi mango jarayeli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Peak season represents the time of highest fruit yield and market demand, allowing you to harvest in large quantities and maximize your income.
ga: Be ni aduawai lɛ fa babaoo lɛ damɔ shi kɛha be ni aduawai lɛ fa babaoo kɛ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii babaoo ni onáa shika babaoo.

english: Does harvesting mangoes during the dry season offer any advantage for selling?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ mango ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, because dry season fruits can hang on the tree longer, you have more flexibility in timing your harvest to match buyer demand.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ hulutsoo be mli aduawai baanyɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo mli koni okɛtsu mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii ahe nii.

english: Why do I need to buy new certified rice seeds every season instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: Improved rice seeds are bred to give high yields and resist diseases. Reusing seeds saved from a harvest causes the crop to lose these special qualities over time, leading to lower yields, uneven growth, and weaker plants in the next season.
