ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too closely together, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each rice plant gets enough room to grow thick stems and full grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ tsei niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout out of the dirt at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the ground is too dry, or if soil insects eat them before they sprout. Planting good quality seeds at the correct depth helps them come up evenly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why does rice grow much better in flooded fields compared to dry land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in lots of water, and flooded soil smothers most weeds and land insects that would otherwise attack the crop roots, giving the rice a safe environment to feed and grow.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu babaoo mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ atutua tsei shishifãi lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe haa ŋmãa koni eye nii ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged without proper air flow. Applying the right fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii kpakpai. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni mli wa, ni tsuɔ waa.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my crop after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are already adapted to your soil, so they absorb rain and plant food immediately. Clearing them early stops them from stealing food away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ kɛtee oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ lɛ ni amɛduɔ niyenii. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice before the grains spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa dani ŋmãa lɛ afite?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when most of the grain heads turn golden-yellow and the grains feel hard when you press them. Waiting too long makes the stalks dry out and drop grains onto the ground, leading to waste.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ amɛmimɔ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbi ni ŋmaa lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ, ni no baaha jwɛi aba.

english: Why do my harvested rice grains break into tiny pieces when I thresh them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Beni atswaa ŋmãa?

english: Grains break easily if they are threshed when they are completely bone-dry or if you hit them too hard against rough or hard surfaces. Using smooth tarpaulins and beating gently keeps the grains whole.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ atsɔ mli beni fãji lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ. aloo kɛji otswa lɛ waa tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ loo nɔ ni wa nɔ Okɛ tarp ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tswaa blɛoo atsu nii koni akɛbu ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why is it better to use modern harvesting containers instead of old sharp metal tools or baskets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmaakpamɔ tsɛnsii baatsu nii moŋ fe dade nibii loo tsɛnsii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ momo lɛ?

english: Old, rusty, or sharp metal equipment can easily injure your hands and cut into the harvested crop. Damaged crops rot faster, and modern plastic or cloth containers prevent injuries while keeping the produce clean.
ga: Dade nibii ni egbɔ, ni efite, loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ baanyɛ apila niji oya ni amɛfolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ amli. Tsei ni efite lɛ baafite oya. Ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ plastic loo mama ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akapila yɛ be mli ni ehaa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tseɔ.

english: What is the best way to store my dried grain so insects do not destroy it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ toɔ koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Storing clean, well-dried grain in airtight hermetic bags or sealed plastic drums stops air and bugs from getting inside. Without air, insects cannot survive, keeping your stored grain safe for months without harmful chemicals.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni egbi lɛ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo plastic tsɛnsii ni atsĩ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi akabote mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Kooloi nyɛŋ ahi shi. Ehaa odumɔwui ni okɛto lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli.

english: Why do some weedkillers I buy at the market work on my neighbor's farm but fail to clear the weeds on my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ etsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Different weeds require specific types of chemicals. Some weedkillers target only broad-leaf weeds while others target grasses. If you buy a chemical that does not match the exact type of weed on your land, or if you apply it at the wrong crop growth stage, it will not work effectively.
ga: Jwɛi srɔtoi biɔ tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ pɛ ahe nii. yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ jwɛi nɔ. Kɛji ohe tsofai ni kɛ jwɛi henɔi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpãaa gbee loo okɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ be ni ejaaa mli Etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I know if the crop medicine I am buying from the market is genuine and safe for my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ahe tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ehi kɛha miniyenii tsei lɛ?

english: Always buy agrochemicals from registered dealers approved by the Ministry of Food and Agriculture. Check that the container has an intact seal, an official approval label, clear instructions, and an unexpired date so you do not waste money on fake or spoiled medicine.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ agrochemicals kɛjɛ mɛi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ ni Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛkadiɔ lɛ. Eyɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni gbi lɛ ehoko lolo. Bɔni afee ni okafite oshika yɛ tsofai ni ji amalei loo tsofai ni efite lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe to double the amount of pest medicine I spray if the insects on my crops refuse to die?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni fa fe mi lɛ shii enyɔ nɔ kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ kpoo akɛ amɛbaagboi?

english: No, using too much chemical can burn your crop leaves, damage the soil, and make the insects resistant over time. Pests often survive because the spray was applied at the wrong time of day, during rain, or without the proper protective coverage.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai, efite shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni eha kooloi bibii anyɛ atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ shi ejaakɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, loo ni abuuu he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers plant rows of tall grass or trees like a belt around the edges of their land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ jwɛi kakadaji loo tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Planting rows of trees or dense grass creates a barrier called a shelterbelt. This belt breaks strong winds that could blow down crops and slows down heavy rainwater so it does not wash away your topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ loo jwɛi ni mli edɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa baa. Bɛlt lɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ atswa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛya ni eha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafee mlɛo lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: Why does my farm soil get washed away into the gutter whenever heavy rain falls on my sloped land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa nubui lɛ amli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mishikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater flows quickly downhill on bare, sloped land, carrying fertile soil with it. Creating soil ridges or planting crops across the slope acts like small dams to trap water and keep the soil in place.
ga: Nugbɔ nu hoɔ oya kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ni aaawo Ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni ama loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ faa bibioo ko. Koni akɛ nu ato ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year when I plant maize in the same spot over and over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like cowpeas or groundnuts helps rest the soil and refill its natural nutrients.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees on your farm creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture until the young cocoa plants grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Balanced soil care ensures the plant shifts its energy downward to form big, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ, Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe eshishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ja ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei jieɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow even after I put fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle mihe lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow if the soil is waterlogged, preventing roots from breathing, or if fertilizer is placed too close to the stem and burns the roots. Fertilizer must be placed a short distance from the plant in moist soil to work properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shãa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam vines as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ko ama mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. Providing stakes helps the leaves capture maximum sunlight to make food, which directly results in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Enɛ saa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops turn yellow and die when I plant them in reddish clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ tsuru mli lɛ?

english: Reddish clay soil traps water and hardens easily, which starves plant roots of air and nutrients like nitrogen. Adding compost or animal manure softens red soil, improves drainage, and gives crops the nutrients they need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tsuru lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli ni ewaa oya. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ tsuru lɛ afee blɛoo. ehaa nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does digging small drainage gutters across my farm help my crops grow better during heavy rains?
ga: Nu shwiemɔ tsɔne bibioo ko ni afoɔ Te Across Farm lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Gutters carry excess rainwater away from your crop roots. Standing water suffocates roots, causes them to rot, and washes away good topsoil nutrients that plants need to grow.
ga: Gutters tsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ, ni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ hoɔ.

english: Will my crops produce more food if I cut down all the big trees on my farm to let in full sunlight?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo aba kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ koni maná hulu la ni fa?

english: It depends on the crop. Sun-loving crops like maize and cassava need full sunlight, but crops like young cocoa need tree canopy shade to protect them from burning heat and drying out.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa he miihia hulu ni fa babaoo. Shi tsei tamɔ kookoo bibii lɛ he miihia tso lɛ shishi koni dɔlɛ akashã ni ekagbi.

english: What kind of crops can I safely grow on the land right near the edge of a river or stream?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei srɔtoi manyɛ makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa loo faa bibioo ko nɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Land near water stays wet and works best for moisture-loving crops like rice, sugarcane, cocoyam, and vegetables. Crops like cassava or maize will suffer root rot if planted in soil that stays swampy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ nɔ edɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kookoo, kɛ aduawai. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baafite amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my plants growing tall and thin without giving fruits when planted under thick tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ adu yɛ tsei niji ni mli ewo wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: When tree canopy shade is too thick, plants spend all their energy stretching upward to search for light instead of developing strong stems, flowers, and fruits. Pruning tree branches lets light reach your crops so they can yield properly.
ga: Kɛji ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛgbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi ni etao la. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa, fɔfɔihi, kɛ yiblii. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa la shɛɔ onibii ahe koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear rubbish and weeds from water pathways before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ nu gbɛi anɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Blocked pathways force water to flood into crop fields instead of flowing safely away. Clearing them keeps water moving, prevents flooding, and removes breeding grounds for farm pests.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbe naa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeho kɛya shweshweeshwe. Nu ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nu. Nu afua hebuu kɛ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ajiemɔ

english: Why does water dry up so fast on the higher parts of my land while staying muddy at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ he ni miyɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shi etsɔɔ muji yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Gravity pulls rainwater down from higher slopes into low areas, where soil tends to be tighter and holds water longer. Understanding this helps you plant drought-tolerant crops on high ground and wet-loving crops at the bottom.
ga: Nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa nugbɔ nu kɛjɛɔ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ onu enɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okwɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ, ni okwɛ tsei ni sumɔɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves get brown spots and rot after rain water sits on them for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nu eshɛ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Excess moisture trapped under shade or stagnant water creates warm, wet conditions that foster fungal diseases. Good drainage and proper air flow help dry leaves and soil quickly to protect plants from rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni amɔmɔ yɛ shade mli loo nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔɔ, ni efɔ lɛ baa. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbiɔ oya koni tso lɛ akafite.

english: Is it better to pour water directly at the root base of my crops or wet the whole plant from above?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ loo oookɛ nu afɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi?

english: Pouring water at the root base gets moisture straight to where the plant drinks while keeping the leaves dry. Wetting leaves unnecessarily can cause fungal diseases and wastes water through evaporation.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ yaa tso lɛ he ni enuɔ nu lɛ yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ egbi lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ nu ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo mli baa lɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land will hold too much water before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu babaoo mli dani adu ŋmãa?

english: Look at the soil color and texture after a rainstorm. If the soil stays muddy like paste, turns waterlogged easily, or is near a low water's edge, it will hold too much water for maize roots, which prefer well-draining soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ efee muji tamɔ shikpɔŋ Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ. loo ebɛŋkɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ naa Ebaahiɛ nu babaoo mli tsɔ kɛha ŋmãa shishifãi, ni sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak even when I don't see any insects or sickness on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi loo hela ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops can suffer from environmental stress like heat, drought, or poor soil just as easily as they suffer from diseases. While sickness can often be sprayed, stress weakens the plant from the inside and requires improving soil and watering conditions to fix.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana amanehulu kɛjɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli. Taakɛ bɔ ni helai yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ abaanyɛ ashɛrɛ helai ashwie shi moŋ, Shi nɔnyɛɛ haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli. Ni ehe miihia ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ aya hiɛ koni akɛsaa enɛ.

english: What is the difference between a crop disease and crop stress?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ahe hela kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe haomɔ teŋ?

english: Crop disease is an infection caused by germs or pests that can usually be treated with remedies. Crop stress comes from harsh growing conditions like excessive heat, lack of water, or bad soil, which makes the plant refuse to grow properly.
ga: Tsei ahe helai ji helai ni helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛbaa ni bei pii lɛ akɛ tsofai tsaa. Tsei ahe haomɔ jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli tamɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kpooɔ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves keep drying up even after I spray them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ egbi lolo beni mikɛ tsofa eshwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays only cure diseases and pests. If your plant is suffering from environmental stress like scorching sun or dry soil, medicine will not help and can sometimes cause even more stress to the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui pɛ. Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miikpe shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ, Tsofai eyeee ebuaaa ni bei komɛi lɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ babaoo po aba tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I force my crops to yield faster by giving them a lot of fertilizer all at once?
ga: Ani manyɛ manyɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwo yibii oya kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛaaha amɛ shikome lɛ nɔ?

english: No, forcing crops with excess fertilizer causes intense chemical stress that burns their roots. Plants need a balanced and peaceful environment to produce well, and overloading them will only harm the harvest.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii fe nine lɛ kɛ tsofafeemɔ mli haomɔ ni naa wa ni shãa amɛshishifãi lɛ baa. Shihilɛ ni ja ni toiŋjɔlɛ yɔɔ mli he miihia tsei koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Ni kɛ́ akɛwo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaana ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo pɛ.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences severe heat or water stress, it panics and drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival. Creating shade or watering regularly reduces this stress so the plant can hold its flowers.
ga: Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ ni naa wa Ebaafee gbeyei ni ekɛ fɔfɔii baashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. Kɛ́ afee hulutsoo loo nu aha lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha haomɔ aba shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to focus on preventing farm problems or treating them when they appear?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama naagbai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsĩmɔ nɔ loo bɔ ni ooofee atsa amɛ kɛ́ amɛba lɛ nɔ?

english: Preventing stress by keeping the soil healthy and well-watered gives crops a peaceful condition to grow strong naturally. It is much harder to recover a crop once stress and sickness have already set in.
ga: Kɛ́ atsĩ haomɔ naa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu ahi nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná shihilɛ ni toiŋjɔlɛ yɔɔ mli, ni amɛbaakwɛ adebɔɔ mli, ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ewa waa akɛ aaaná ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛji haomɔ kɛ hela eba.

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural reaction to heat stress. The crop rolls its leaves to hide from the harsh sun and trap moisture so it does not dry out completely.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛtee hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: How does providing shade help my young crops during the hot season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Shade reduces heat stress on young plants by lowering the soil temperature and preserving water. This protects delicate young roots from burning under intense sunlight.
ga: Shade haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ ni baa shi kɛ nu ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baabu shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã amɛ.

english: How does planting my crops too close together affect their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: Overcrowding creates competition stress. When plants are too close, they struggle against each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, leaving all of them weak and underproductive.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii he haomɔ baa. Kɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm make my main crops struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds cause nutrient and water stress by stealing food and moisture directly from your crops' roots. Clearing weeds gives your crops the peaceful environment they need to feed properly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he haomɔ baa kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ toiŋjɔlɛ ni he hiaa koni aha amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantains grow fast and have large, broad leaves that provide vital shade to shield young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, keeping the soil moist while giving you early food and income.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni abu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika baa oya.

english: Spacing plantains about 3 meters apart ensures that their broad leaves have enough room to spread and capture sunlight without overcrowding each other or shading out other nearby crops.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mitai 3, ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsiii ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anaa loo amɛtsĩii amɛnaa. bɛŋkɛ

english: Removing extra shoots—called suckers—prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from the main stem, ensuring the main plant grows strong and yields a much larger bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, ehaaa amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain plant turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during hot spells mean the plant is stressed from lack of water; applying dry grass or leaves around the base as mulch helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ miihao tso lɛ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ebɔle he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shishitoo lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough nutrients to grow healthy plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Plantains thrive in dark, soft soil rich in decayed leaf matter that drains water easily, so water does not sit around the roots and rot them.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni baai ni fiteɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nu kɛ ehe kpaaa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa amɛgboi.

english: Which plantain sucker is the best kind for me to plant to get strong growth?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sa akɛ madu koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad stem base, because they root stronger and produce healthier fruit bunches than 'water suckers' with broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud,’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ewoɔ shishifãi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ‘nu mli ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my plantain tree falling over easily before the fruit bunch is even big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall over when underground pests weaken the roots or when the fruit gets heavy; planting suckers deep in the ground and staking heavy plants prevents this.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ aduawai lɛ tsii. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni akɛ tsei lɛ wo ŋmeii amli waa lɛ, ebaatsi enɛ naa.

english: How long does a plantain plant take from the day I plant it to when I can harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ plantain heɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi ni miduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ gbi ni manyɛ makpa lɛ?

english: A plantain plant typically takes between 12 and 15 months to produce a full bunch ready for harvesting, depending on rainfall and soil fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ dumɔwui lɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ akpa. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell that a bunch of plantains is ready for me to harvest for market?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ odumɔwui lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akɛya jara nɔ?

english: Plantains are ready to cut when the fruit fills out and becomes plump and rounded, losing its sharp ridges, even while the skin is still green.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni elaajeɔ lɛ nɔ Eyɛ mli akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo moŋ

english: How should I store my harvested plantains so they do not spoil before the buyer collects them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-plantains ni akpa lɛ ato koni amɛkafite dani mɔ ni heɔ lɛ lɛ aŋɔ amɛ?

english: Keep harvested plantain bunches standing upright in a cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight, and avoid stacking heavy items on top of them to prevent bruising and premature ripening.
ga: Kɛ plantain tsei ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. He ni hulu la lɛ akashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni tsii ni okɛaawo nɔ lɛ he Okɛwo nɔ koni akafite ni akahoo nii oya.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull food from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds your maize crop and helps keep your soil rich for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-ŋmã lɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas planted nearby to cover them with giant leaves, keeping the temperature cool and the soil moist until the trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ aha amɛhe. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Does it matter which way I push cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Nɔ ni he hiaa ji bɔ ni mafee matsi ŋmei tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Yes, you must make sure the tiny growth buds on the stem point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the plant wastes its energy trying to turn its shoots upward, leading to weak growth and much smaller tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ Yɛ tso ko ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ Kɛji odu tsei ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaves and fast growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help feed the crop and keep it healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ aye nii ni eha amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have a special ability to pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it back into the ground through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize growing next to it without buying extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by excessive heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil moist by spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots helps regulate the soil temperature so the plant can hold onto its flowers and make fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ooogbɛ ashwã he lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: When tomatoes get too much water, their lower leaves turn pale yellow and look droopy even though the soil is wet, because wet soil suffocates the roots. If they lack water, the foliage wilts during the day and feels dry and crunchy.
ga: Kɛji tomato ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbo, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni enuɔ he akɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yams grow deep underground and need soft, loose dirt to expand easily. High mounds lift the topsoil and make it loose, giving the young tubers room to stretch long and grow thick without fighting hard dirt.
ga: Atomɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa bulb bibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition results in thin, weak stems and very small harvests compared to plants given proper space to spread out.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto tsei ni aha amɛ he ko ni sa koni amɛshwere lɛ ahe.

english: Why are holes appearing in my cabbage leaves even though I do not see any insects during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi komɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Many crop pests, like armyworms and caterpillars, hide under leaves or inside the dirt during the hot daylight hours to stay cool. They come out at night to eat the leaves, so inspecting the undersides of leaves early in the morning helps you spot them.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ahe ji ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Okɛ ohe awo baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai gbɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona amɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally suited to survive harsh weather and poor soil, so they quickly drink up water and steal food meant for your crops. Removing weeds while your crop seedlings are still young keeps them from being choked out.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkatsi amɛhe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top ones are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for plant growth. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni miida lolo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow plenty of big green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ewoɔ pea ŋmɔtɔi fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally grab their own nitrogen from the air, so if the soil already has too much rich fertilizer, the plant gets confused and spends all its energy growing leaves instead of making flowers and bean pods.
ga: Cowpeas sumɔɔ ni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ futuɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like giant trees; they rely on shallow surface roots. When the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top and the soil gets soaked and soft, strong winds easily pull those shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei wuji. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Beni aduawai akui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewoɔ nu, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Mɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo mlɛo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves wilt in direct sunlight to conserve water and protect themselves from scorching. Because cocoa naturally grows best under partial shade, planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby keeps the air cooler and moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kookoo daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be fioo yɔɔ lɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Cocoa pods rot and turn black due to black pod disease, which is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods and trimming extra tree branches helps air circulate and keeps the pods dry.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. ni ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa Ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and looking twisted and yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Twisted and curled leaves on cassava are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making leaves properly, which reduces the size of the cassava roots beneath the ground.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee baai jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat gets too intense or when the soil dries out completely. Extreme temperatures prevent the flower from pollinating itself, so keeping the soil consistently moist helps the tree turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔii feɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their leaves suddenly even when they look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their leaves when they experience water shock—such as going from completely dry soil to getting flooded with heavy water all at once. Keeping your watering light and regular prevents the plant from getting stressed.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji amɛbote nu mli, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ kɛyaa nu afua mli shikome. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa kɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akafee mɔ ni haoɔ.

english: Groundnuts have a natural behavior where, after the flower is pollinated above ground, the stem grows downwards to push the seed into the dirt. The groundnut pod actually grows and ripens safety hidden under the soil.
ga: Peanuts feɔ amɛnii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean ŋmɔtɔi lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out short and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the soil, but if the ground is hard, stony, or clayey, the growing tip cannot push through easily. Preparing deep, soft mounds or ridges gives the yam room to expand freely into smooth, long tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo eji shikpɔŋ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni atsɔ mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ asaa gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli alɛɛ ehe ni etsɔ ŋshɔŋlooi kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or are sitting in waterlogged soil, which stops their roots from taking up food from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛshishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow very tall but only produce small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants that grow tall with tiny cobs often received too much nitrogen early on, or they were planted too close together and had to compete with each other for sunlight and soil food.
ga: Abɛi ni daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Bei pii lɛ, amɛnáa nitrogen babaoo mra. Aloo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni ehe bahiaa ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he kwraa kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn completely dry and brown, and the kernels inside become hard with a tiny black layer forming at the base of each kernel.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa ni nɔ ko bibioo ko ni yɔɔ diŋ yɔɔ mli. Amɛfeɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How does applying fertilizer to my crop actually help my maize yield more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ewo niyenii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the soil, supplying essential elements like nitrogen and phosphorus that help maize build strong stems, broad green leaves, and larger cobs filled with kernels.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii. Ehaa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa tsei ahe tsei ni wa ni baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei wuji ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ

english: Why should I use improved government-supported maize seeds instead of keeping seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake ni nɔyeli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii? Mohu ɔ, i he dumɔwui nɛ ngɛ ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ yi wami.

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, survive drought better, and give higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over time and produce weaker harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does receiving subsidized farming inputs help me improve my crop production?
ga: Te okwaayeli mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ shika mli lɛ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Subsidized inputs lower your cost for quality seeds and fertilizers, allowing you to feed and protect your crops properly without spending more money than your farm can return.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha oshika ni okɛbaahe dumɔwui ni hi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi. Ehaa onyɛɔ oyeɔ onibii jogbaŋŋ ni obuɔ he ni ofiteee shika fe nɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛha bo ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize plants fall over if their brace roots are shallow or weak, which happens when seeds are planted too close to the surface or when pests damage the stem near the ground.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji amɛshishifãi ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛhe waaa. Enɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: These caterpillars are usually Fall Armyworms, a pest common in Ghana that hides inside the central funnel of young maize plants to eat tender leaves before cobs can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Why do some of my harvested maize cobs have empty patches with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty patches happen when the cob's silks do not get enough pollen during flowering, often caused by extreme heat, severe drought, or lack of rain during the flowering stage.
ga: Hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji cob silk lɛ enine shɛɛɛ pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: How do birds affect my crops, and should I try to keep them away from my farm?
ga: Te okpoi náa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ? Ni ani esa akɛ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni matsi amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Birds can eat your sown seeds and ripe produce, leading to harvest loss. Additionally, bird droppings can spread unwanted weed seeds and fungal spores across your fields, so using scarecrows or nets to protect vulnerable crops is recommended.
ga: Okpoi baanyɛ aye dumɔwui ni oduɔ kɛ yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni laajeɔ. Okpoi afɔfɔi hu baanyɛ agbɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni ataooo kɛ ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsu nii kɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can birds or insects carry crop diseases from my neighbor's field to my crops?
ga: Ani okpoi loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ ajie tsei ahe helai kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, birds and insects can carry disease-causing fungi, bacteria, and infected plant sap on their feet and beaks. When they land on your healthy crops after feeding on sick plants nearby, they can easily transfer those diseases to your farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmeii, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ tso mli nu ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ awo amɛnaji kɛ amɛnaabu nɔ. Kɛ amɛba shi yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛye tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ sɛɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ nakai helai lɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do birds and wild animals target my crops more when the farm is getting close to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ koo mli kooloi kwɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ waa beni ŋmɔ lɛ ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: As crops mature, they accumulate starches and natural sugars that release strong scents. Birds and pests naturally recognize these scents, which signal that the crop is soft, sweet, and rich in energy to eat.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, amɛbua adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ sugar ni jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ anaa. Okpoi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ leɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ kɛha niyeli.

english: What is the best way to prevent birds from picking up maize seeds right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ okpoi anaa koni amɛkajie ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting your seeds at the correct depth and covering them properly with soil keeps them out of sight. You can also cover seedbeds with a light mulch of dry grass until the seeds sprout and anchor into the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa ni akɛ sũ ha nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa. Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi bibioo hu aha dumɔwui lɛ ashishi. kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he

english: Why do strange weeds and plants keep sprouting on my farm even after I cleared the land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mifo jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Birds, animals, and wind carry wild seeds from surrounding bush areas and drop them in your soil, often through bird droppings. These seeds lie hidden in the dirt until rain comes, causing unexpected plants to grow alongside your main crops.
ga: Okpoi, kooloi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ koo mli dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Ha wɔŋmɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɛtsɔ okpoi afɔfɔi anɔ Dumɔwui nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Ha tsei ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe.

english: Why am I restricted from planting permanent tree crops like cocoa on land I am renting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsĩ minaa koni mikadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mihaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Under customary land practice in Ghana, planting long-term tree crops like cocoa establishes a long-term claim on the land. Landowners usually allow tenant farmers to grow short-term food crops like maize or vegetables to avoid disputes over land ownership.
ga: Yɛ kusum shikpɔŋ nɔ nifeemɔi ashishi yɛ Ghana Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli tamɔ kookoo ji be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni akɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi ŋmɛɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ koni amɛdu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. Enɛ ji koni akafee shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ahe béi.

english: Who is held responsible if birds or animals from my farm cause damage to someone else's crops?
ga: Namɔ baakwɛ nɔ kɛji okpoi loo kooloi ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fite mɔ kroko ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: As a farmer, you are responsible for managing your farm activities and livestock to prevent harm to nearby fields. If your animals or farming practices cause loss or damage to a neighboring property, local rules require you to settle the issue with the landowner.
ga: akɛ okwaafonyo Ogbɛnaa nii ji ni okwɛ oŋmɔ kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ nitsumɔi anɔ koni akafite ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ. Kɛji okooloi loo okwaayeli nifeemɔi lɛ kɛ nibii ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ laaje loo efite Kuu lɛ mli mlai biɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ atsu sane lɛ he nii.

english: Are bird droppings good manure for my crops, or will they harm my plants?
ga: Ani okpoi afɔfɔi ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaaye mitsei lɛ awui?

english: Bird droppings are high in nitrogen and make great natural fertilizer, but fresh droppings are very strong and can burn plant roots. Drying or composting bird droppings before mixing them into the soil makes them safe and beneficial for crop growth.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ okpoi amli, ni eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Shi okpoi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ashishifãi. Okpo mli ŋmeii ni agbiɔ loo afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei adalɛ.

english: Where does the starch in crops like cassava and maize come from as the plant grows?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni starch ni yɔɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ jɛɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Crops make starch inside their leaves using sunlight, water, and air through photosynthesis. The plant then sends this starch down into its roots or grains to store energy, making the crop heavy and nutritious.
ga: Tsei feɔ starch yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ tsei kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ yaa amɛshishifãi loo amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii ni ehaa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops spoil quickly when their outer skin is damaged by birds or farm tools?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ okpoi loo ŋmɔ mli nibii fite kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ?

english: The skin of a root or fruit acts as a protective shield against pests and rot. When pecks or cuts pierce this skin, fungi and bacteria enter easily and feed on the internal starches, causing the produce to decay rapidly.
ga: Shishifã loo aduawai lɛ hiɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ kooloi kɛ fitemɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ ookpa hewolo lɛ loo oofo lɛ, Mold kɛ bacteria boteɔ mli oya ni amɛyeɔ starch ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up during the hot afternoon, but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to save water and protect themselves from drying out. At night and early morning, when the air cools down, the leaves relax and soak up moisture again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Gbi gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Baai lɛ baajɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss and survive drought. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normal tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ ekwɛ baai heei ni ebaakwɛ bulbs ni sa.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants with small fruits instead of a healthy, heavy harvest.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aduawai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, o náa yiblii nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do some of my seeds take a long time to come out of the ground while others sprout in just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of soil moisture, warmth, and proper planting depth to germinate. Seeds buried too deep or planted in dry soil take much longer or fail to sprout entirely.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ, latsaa kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo loo amɛkwɛɛɛ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is overwatered and suffocating the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Te cowpea ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize plants and improves soil fertility.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ fɛo.

english: Is it good for me to water my crops late at night or in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu gbɛkɛ loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering in the evening reduces water loss from evaporation, but watering too late can leave wet foliage overnight, which encourages fungal diseases to grow on your crops.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Shi nu ni awoɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ kome. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa onibii amli lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to quickly steal water, light, and soil nutrients before your planted crops can properly establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Dani tso lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers drop off without fruiting when weather temperatures are too high, when watering is irregular, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over easily when a strong wind blows across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their root systems are shallow, which can happen due to poor soil preparation, overwatering, or crowding that prevents deep root development.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo loo eyi obɔ kɛyashɛ he ni etsĩɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii. Kooloo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my farm soil lose its strength after I plant the same crop for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he waaa beni midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Every crop draws specific nutrients from the soil. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains those exact nutrients completely, so rotating your crops—like planting groundnuts or beans after maize—helps the soil naturally rebuild its richness.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaajie nakai niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I leave dry crop leaves on my field after harvest instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients and kills helpful soil organisms. Leaving dry leaves on the ground creates a blanket that traps soil moisture, prevents heat damage, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leaves above the ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of tuber roots. Loosening the soil deeply and balancing nutrients encourages the plant to store energy underground into big tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛaawo tuber shishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulb agboi amli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or insect attack to save energy. Watering regularly during hot spells and mulching around the roots keeps the plant cool enough to hold its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloo tutuamɔ koni amɛ to hewalɛ. Nu ni oooha bo daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ he lɛ baaye abua. Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting beans alongside my maize help both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to nourish the maize, while the tall maize stalks provide a sturdy support for the bean vines to climb toward the sunlight.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he fiofio.

english: How can I stop my tomato plants from wilting and rotting during heavy rains?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa tomato tsei lɛ koni amɛkagboi ni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Excess water encourages fungal diseases that attack tomato roots and stems. Planting on raised soil ridges allows surplus water to drain away quickly, while spacing plants apart ensures airflow to keep stems dry.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tomato shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ he hewalɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full direct sunlight or strong winds. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby acts as a natural canopy to shelter the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni akɛbaakwɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to powder inside my barn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ sũ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils burrow inside dry grains to eat and lay eggs. Sun-drying your maize until it is completely hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents moisture and bugs from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛye ni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: How do I select the best yam tubers to save as seed yams for the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛto akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛbaadu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Choose small to medium tubers that feel firm, have smooth unbroken skin, and come from healthy plants that produced high yields, as sick or soft tubers will rot in the soil before sprouting.
ga: Halamɔ yitso bibioo kɛyashi teŋgbɛ ni nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ. Eyɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli Enɛ ji akɛ, bulbs ni hela mɔ amɛ loo bulbs bibii lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the roots helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is already moist and plant roots are developed enough to absorb it, usually 2 to 3 weeks after sprouts appear, followed by a second application when the crop starts flowering or making stalks.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ, bei pii lɛ, otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ sɛɛkuu ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes through the leaves inside the central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo ni tsɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the center leaf shoot. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the plant whorl early in the morning or late evening stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turning dark black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular water supply as the fruit grows. Keeping the soil consistently moist through mulching and watering during dry spells helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be beni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is too much direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle heavy, direct heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains next to cocoa trees creates a canopy that shields them from scorching heat while they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa lɛ baa.

english: Leaving too many young shoots, or suckers, forces the mother plant to share its food and water, leading to small plantain bunches. Removing extra shoots leaves energy for the main plant to produce large, heavy fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii loo tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ fe nine Enɛ baaha tso nyɛ lɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu mli. kɛ plantains bibii baa Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves into the sunlight to make food efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to air and light while keeping them off wet ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni ehoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Staking haa baai lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛyaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efuɔ ni egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miida yɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How do I know it is safe to plant my seeds at the start of the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ Ghana?

english: It is safest to wait until the ground receives two or three consecutive heavy rains that soak deep into the soil, rather than planting after the very first light drizzle, so seeds have enough moisture to germinate without drying out.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle hiɔmi ɔ se konɛ dumi ɔmɛ nɛ a ná nu nɛ sa konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a kwɛ̃ nɛ a ko gbi.

english: Why do my young nursery seedlings need to be watered constantly every day during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ nu daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings in a nursery have tiny, shallow roots that cannot reach water deep underground. During hot dry periods, sunlight dries out the topsoil fast, so daily watering is needed to keep the roots moist so the delicate plants do not dry up and die.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli lɛ Hulu la haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔse nu daa gbi koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Koni tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do I need to raise my seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery allows you to protect tiny, vulnerable seeds from harsh sunlight, pests, and heavy rain in a small space where you can easily water and care for them until they are strong enough to survive on the main farm.
ga: Nursery lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ baanyɛ afite lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo nakai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my crops alive when hot weather dries up the soil starting in January?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ January mli lɛ?

english: You can protect your crops during hot dry spells by watering early in the morning or late in the evening, placing shade leaves over young plants, and covering the soil around their base with dry grass to trap moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha amɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ shade baai awo tsei bibii anɔ. ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it better to water my farm in the afternoon when the sun is hot or in the early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening. In the hot afternoon, heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it, and hot droplets on leaves can scorch the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Is it good to leave dry crop waste and plant debris lying on top of my soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni eshwɛ kɛ dumɔwui ahe jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, leaving plant debris on top of the soil acts like a blanket called mulch. It shades the soil from direct sunlight, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil with nutrients.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ niyenii babaoo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetables droop and curl up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpãa shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop in the heat as a natural defense to shrink their surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss. It indicates that the plant is under heat stress and needs moisture once the sun drops.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe ni egbee shi yɛ latsaa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ baaha nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi, ni ehe miihia ni ená ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds completely before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and will steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your young plants. Clearing them gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni hereɔ bo lɛ ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some parts of a farmland stay clean without weeds growing for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli shikpɔji lɛ ekomɛi ahe tseɔ ni jwɛi kwɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When soil is heavily shaded by a canopy or covered with a thick layer of dry plant debris, weed seeds under the dirt cannot receive sunlight. Without light, those weed seeds cannot germinate and grow.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli edɔ waa loo tsei ni egbi ni etse ehe banee lɛ ehà nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la. Kɛji la bɛ Nakai jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Should I burn off all the dry bush and plant remains after clearing my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã tsei bibii ni egbi kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is better not to burn. Burning destroys valuable soil nutrients and leaves the ground naked and dry, whereas letting the cleared organic matter decompose naturally improves the soil's ability to hold water and feed your crops.
ga: Ehi akɛ oooshã. Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbiɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ oha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔ mli lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ nu mli ni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does covering the bare ground around my crop stems help me save water?
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔhamɔ Te tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mikɛ nu akafite?

english: Covering bare soil prevents direct sunlight and dry wind from touching the earth. This keeps the root area cool and wet for a much longer time, reducing the amount of water you need to fetch for your plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ naa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa bo koni okɛjie tsei lɛ baa shi.
