english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the young cocoa with shade and moisture to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves when there is not enough available in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii be mli ni nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Curling cassava leaves are typically caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread the virus from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. he ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ.

english: Beans and cowpeas gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to produce healthy ears, so growing them together feeds the soil naturally.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from producing a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa

english: Why do I have to heap soil into big mounds before planting my yam seed tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabu shikpɔŋ agbo ko naa dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to swell and grow long. Big mounds improve drainage so the tubers do not rot during heavy rains and make digging them up at harvest much easier.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛfuu ni amɛdara be kakadaŋŋ. Gɔji wuji haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni atsaa beni akpaa nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster right after I put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plants in the soil, including weeds. Weeds usually have stronger roots than young crops, so they quickly drink up the extra nutrients unless you clear them out early.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji niyenii kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni jwɛi fata he. Jwɛi fɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa fe tsei bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ oya. Ja ojie kɛjɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry heat spell before the rainy season truly settles in. If you plant too early, the hot, dry ground after that initial rain can bake and kill your sprouted seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hei ni mli edɔ, ni egbi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra water shoots and small branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo nu ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Extra shoots steal nutrients that the tree needs to make cocoa pods. Cutting them off opens the tree to sunlight and airflow, which helps keep fungal diseases like black pod away.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ aba tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa.

english: Why are my pepper fruits getting soft, pale spots on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: This is sunscald, which happens when strong sunlight bakes the fruit directly. It usually occurs when the pepper plant loses leaves, leaving the growing peppers exposed without shade.
ga: Enɛ ji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kpɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ fite. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby provides a natural canopy that protects the young cocoa from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away properly. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nu jogbaŋŋ Kasava ni aaadu yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop roots with dead grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during dry days, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light shower can cause your seeds to germinate and then dry up if rain does not fall again immediately.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baahi shi ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for light, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough resources to produce a large yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso lɛ haa enáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii babaoo.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunshine away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to everything they need to produce healthy fruits and seeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa tsei ni okɛ amɛ yeɔ sharamɔ lɛ naa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I find holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu ko yɛ ŋmãa baa ko mli ni ŋmei bibioo ko kɛ ehe ewo mli lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm that eat young corn shoots. Inspecting your field regularly and using recommended safe pest treatments early stops them from destroying your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa ni okɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni onibii akafite.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil food, while groundnuts and beans naturally add good food back into the soil. Alternating these crops keeps your land fertile without needing to buy extra fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ekɛ niyenii kpakpai baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii nɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant receives uneven amounts of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ tomato.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry spells usually mean the tree is stressed from a lack of water or is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, which the tree needs to make green leaf pigment and food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni faaa yɛ emli loo hɔmɔ miiye lɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛfee baa lɛ mli ŋmɔŋ kɛ niyenii.

english: How does adding fertilizer to the soil help my cocoa trees produce heavier pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Fertilizers feed the soil with concentrated plant foods like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, giving the crop the extra strength needed to grow larger flowers and develop dense, healthy seeds.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ tsei aniyenii ni mli eyi obɔ tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium. Ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛfɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔii wuji. ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Blackened pods are caused by a water-loving fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly when moisture stays on pods for too long in heavy shade or damp rainy weather.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji ŋmeii lɛ hi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more frequently right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain causes crops to sprout soft, fresh green leaves which attract insects looking for easy food, while high humidity creates ideal conditions for pest eggs to hatch.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni miitao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awɔlɔi lɛ baa.

english: What will happen to my crop leaves if I spray chemicals on them during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai shwie amɛnɔ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying during high afternoon heat causes the chemical liquid to evaporate too quickly or scorch the sun-heated leaves, which damages the plant instead of protecting it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo ebaaha tsei ahe tsei ni hulu lɛ eshɛ amɛhe lɛ ashã. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebu ehe.

english: Trees drop flowers when they are short on water, lacking soil nutrients, or attacked by bugs, shedding the flowers to save energy so the main trunk and leaves can stay alive.
ga: Tsei baafɔ̃ kɛ́ nu faaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Eshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi titrii kɛ baai lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do tiny insects help my cocoa flowers become real cocoa pods?
ga: Bɔ ni Kooloo Bibioo Ko Ye Ebua Mi-Cocoa Fɔfɔi lɛ Ni Etsɔ Cocoa Pods Diɛŋtsɛ

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from flower to flower as they crawl around, which fertilizes the cocoa blossom so it can close up and grow into a pod.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi amli muji kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ beni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ abɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekpa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no big shade trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that burn under direct intense tropical sun; taller shade trees block harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow slowly and look thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors, stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil surrounding your main crops so your plants do not get enough nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. O ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ koni o tsei lɛ akaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why does cutting off extra branches from my crop trees help them yield more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni niji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and breeze inside the tree while ensuring all root food and water go straight into growing pods instead of waste leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni miida lɛ mli yɛ baai amli jwɛi najiaŋ.

english: Maize plants need nitrogen to stay dark green and grow tall. Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nutrients because the soil lacks food, or nitrogen fertilizer has not been applied at the right time.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛdara. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia tso lɛ ejaakɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How do cowpea plants help make my soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina tsei aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants decay, they leave this free nutrient behind, acting like natural fertilizer for crops planted later.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛbaashi nɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli tsei.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and gives soil pests a permanent place to live. Changing crops keeps the soil balanced and starves pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi daa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the crop using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the yam produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that lose water fast in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to block harsh heat and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees fall over so easily during small windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit loads at the top. If tiny soil pests damage their root bases or if the soil is too loose, the tree loses balance and pulls out of the ground when wind blows.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii kpata eshishitoo lɛ hiɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse tsɔ. Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain floods the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits around the roots for too long, it cuts off air and encourages water-loving fungi to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ewoɔ hydrophilic fungi hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients needed to hold the fruit to the stem.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni baaha aduawai lɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading plant diseases, or by heat stress during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why does my swamp rice grow well in flooded water while my maize crop dies in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp rice lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nu afua mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice stems have natural internal channels that pump air down to their roots under water, whereas maize roots suffocate and drown quickly when submerged in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo nu ni mli ejɔ mli.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt inside the top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni shwieɔ shi mli Yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The young worms hide inside the central leaves of the plant where they eat the soft parts and leave behind dark waste that looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Amɛyeɔ hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo virus ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale green even when we receive plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔnine eshɛ nugbɔ babaoo nɔ moŋ?

english: Rain provides water, but plants also need food from the soil. Heavy rains can wash away soil nutrients like nitrogen, turning the leaves pale green. Adding compost or fertilizer restores the plant's health.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away during heavy rainy seasons.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs if I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space and resources to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji ni dalɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to use long wooden sticks to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ani oofiɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach direct sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground with sticks allows them to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain farm stop producing large fruit bunches after two or three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ kpaɔ aduawai wuji yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As plantain plants grow, they produce many small shoots called suckers. If too many suckers grow, they steal nutrients from the main plant. Pruning extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots to produce large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ ŋmeii babaoo akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm cut down my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively drink the soil water and fertilizer intended for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a high yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in full sun. Planting shade plants like plantain nearby creates a umbrella that keeps the young cocoa trees cool until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It often happens when soil moisture changes rapidly from very wet to dry, preventing the roots from absorbing calcium consistently.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni edɔ waa kɛyaa nɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ daa.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is good enough for my crops to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi bɔ ni sa ni miŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good soil for crops usually feels crumbly, holds some moisture without turning into a muddy pond, and has a dark brown or black color from rich organic matter. Avoiding places where water collects for days or where the ground is full of hard rocks gives your crops the best chance to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni jɛɔ nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ otsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni nu ebua ehe naa gbii babaoo loo hei ni tɛi ni wa eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛshwere.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and short roots that burn easily under full sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective canopy that keeps the air humid and shields the cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are usually a sign of insect pests like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Inspecting under the leaves and practicing crop rotation or applying manure can help prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ he okadi. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady over a week or two so the ground absorbs enough moisture. Planting after just one isolated rain is risky because a dry spell might follow, causing the new sprouts to dry up in the hot soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hɔmɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize grows fast and is ready to harvest in about three to four months, while cassava grows slowly and stays in the ground longer. Planting them together lets you harvest maize early while giving the cassava room to expand later, maximizing land use.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmã daa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo. Hefatalɔi dumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ alɛɛɔ ŋmei tsu lɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ aná he sɛɛ babaoo.

english: Soil cracks quickly when it lacks decayed leaves and organic matter that hold water like a sponge. Covering the bare ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating the soil's water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ebɛ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa nu hiɔ shi tamɔ sponji. Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni okɛhaa he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ akajɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that encourages leaves instead of fruits. Watering consistently and balanced feeding help flowers stay on and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni woɔ baai hewalɛ koni amɛye aduawai najiaŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil to expand downwards easily. If the soil underneath is hard or stony, the tuber cannot push through and will turn out bent, stunted, or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsɔ Tubers mli ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough local conditions, so their seeds in the soil sprout instantly with rain. Clearing weeds early while your crop seedlings are small prevents the weeds from taking away water, light, and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lɛ amɛtsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Crops pull essential nutrients out of the soil every time they grow. If you plant the same crop on the same plot every year without adding compost, manure, or allowing the land to rest, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot support good yields.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai anɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when excess water drowns the root system. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and healthy growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants grow so many green leaves but very few pods under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants produce too many leaves and few pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Excess nitrogen encourages lush leafy growth rather than flower and pod development.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine woɔ baai ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ podi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large broad leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while cocoa roots get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often a false start followed by dry weather. Seeds that sprout during early rains may dry up and die if the main rainy season has not truly settled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ etsuuu he nii.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani eda lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods shrivel and turn black due to black pod disease caused by heavy rain and shade, or because the tree lacks enough nutrients and water to support all its pods at once.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii diji hela ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. aloo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shikome hewɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop without setting fruit when temperatures get too high, when water is insufficient, or when lack of wind and bees prevents proper flower pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu faaa Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni ŋmeii tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni sa lɛ anaa.

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny insects like aphids or thrips suck sap from the underside of leaves, or when an insect-transmitted virus infects the plant.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ŋmɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo kɛ́ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yeɔ tsei anɔ

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-loving pests and fungal diseases to build up in the soil season after season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Cassava is ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves yellow and shed, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack from expanding tubers.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ yitso ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is packed too hard for roots to penetrate, or when microscopic worms called nematodes attack the tip of the growing tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. aloo beni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that easily burn and dry out under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects young plants from heat stroke and preserves moisture in the topsoil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do you recommend peeling off the outer roots and soil from my plantain suckers before I plant them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ajie kponɔgbɛ shishifãi kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli lɛ dani adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Peeling or 'corm-trimming' plantain suckers removes hidden banana weevil eggs and microscopic root worms (nematodes) that live in the roots. Cleaning them prevents you from transferring harmful pests into your fresh field.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi ni ajieɔ loo ‘ajieɔ amɛyitso’ lɛ jieɔ banana ŋmeii akui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni anaaa lɛ. (nematodes) ni hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Amɛhe ni oootsumɔ lɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okajie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛya oŋmɔji ni akɛ sũ fee lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up in a V-shape before the corn is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ V su mli dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant strips this vital nutrient from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the new top leaves and growing cob.
ga: Abɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyaha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I pour my chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are mineral salts that pull moisture out of plant tissues; placing them directly against the stem will burn the plant tissue and damage roots. Applying fertilizer a few centimeters away in a ring or buried hole lets fine feeder roots safely draw in nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji mineral salts ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛma tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ fãji lɛ ni ebaafite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔ mli loo bu ko ni afu yɛ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up large amounts of soil nutrients, while legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Rotating with legumes naturally refills the soil with nitrogen, keeping the field fertile for future crops.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen afata sũ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe; heavy rain on flat ground fills all soil air pockets with standing water, suffocating roots and inviting fungal pathogens. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɛ nu ni ekã shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii nine. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my yam vines produce much larger tubers when I guide them onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa beni mitsɔɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for underground tuber growth through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts leaves off the ground, spreading them out to catch maximum sunlight while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking elevator lɛ baafo baai lɛ amli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbalamɔ mli koni onine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: What causes small green and brown caterpillars to chew holes right inside the center whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ a-rings lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep central funnel of maize plants to feed on tender expanding leaves. Controlling them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much more during the first four weeks after planting than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni midu lɛ sɛɛ fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small, weak root systems and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Once crop plants grow taller and produce dense leaf canopies, they shade out weeds naturally.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifã bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ dara ni amɛná ŋmeii ni baai lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Amɛbaafee jwɛi lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If I plant my crops very close together so I have more stems on my land, won't I harvest a bigger crop?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni miná ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Planting too closely forces plants to fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin stems and tiny or empty fruits. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build full, heavy ears or tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee toi loo yitso ni tsii, ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I see bees flying around my pepper flowers, and should I chase them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni miibɔle mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mashwie amɛ?

english: Bees are helpful pollinators that carry pollen from flower to flower. Instead of hurting your crop, they help the flowers turn into healthy pepper fruits, leading to a bigger harvest.
ga: Wuo ji ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni woɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli kɛyaa fɔfɔi krokomɛi amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye onibii lɛ awui lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa.

english: What makes the leaves of my cassava plants curl up, turn yellow, and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi? tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni ekpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: This leaf curling is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus starves the plant of energy, so controlling the insects early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Virus haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kudɔ kooloi mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if insects are eating my maize leaves or if the sun is just scorching them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miiye mi ŋmãa baai lɛ loo hulu lɛ miitswa amɛ?

english: Insects leave visible signs like ragged holes or chewed edges on the leaves and tiny droppings inside the leaves, while sun heat makes the leaves dry out or curl up evenly without holes.
ga: Kplukai shĩɔ okadii ni anaa tamɔ buji ni etse loo ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ baa lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ haa baa lɛ mli gĩɔ loo ebɔleɔ ehe pɛpɛɛpɛ ni bu bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field with no taller plants around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides essential shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do crops in one part of my farm grow tall and green while the same crops in another part stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ be mli ni nakai ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ hu feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Soil quality changes across a farm; areas where crops stay short often lack important plant nutrients or do not hold water well, meaning that part of the field needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ bɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa loo amɛhiɛɛɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ he ko he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: How do I know it is the right time to plant my maize after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains have fallen regularly enough for the soil to stay deeply moist for several days, so the seeds get continuous moisture to sprout without drying up.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa bɔ ni sa koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa gbii babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are the green tomatoes on my vines rotting from the bottom before they can even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli ni yɔɔ miwein tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishi dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: Rot at the bottom of tomatoes is often caused by uneven watering or a lack of calcium in the soil during fruit growth, which weakens the skin of the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tomato shishi fitemɔ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ. ni haa aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: Will trimming off some extra leafy branches on my tomato plants help them produce more fruit?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, cutting off non-producing side branches allows the plant to send its energy and water straight to growing large, healthy fruits instead of maintaining extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ sɛɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ kɛya yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e sa nɛ a to baai nɛ piɛɛ he ɔ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when there is plenty of rain for everyone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ miiná nugbɔ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients and sunlight directly from the soil around your crops. Even with enough water, your crops cannot get the food they need if weeds are competing with them.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po yɛ jɛmɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛkɛ kɛji jwɛi kɛ amɛ miitswa akaŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant next season, or will they grow poorly?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Seeds saved from modern high-yielding varieties often lose their strength in the next generation, producing smaller ears and lower yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking helps the leaves make food for the plant, which results in much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the primary food crops need to grow green and healthy. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Will putting rotten leaves and animal dung on my farm really help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani baai ni egbo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, animal dung and decaying leaves turn into organic manure. This manure acts as a rich, natural food for the soil, helping it retain moisture during dry days and releasing nutrients slowly to your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa waa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli

english: What is eating small holes in my corn leaves and leaving tiny worms inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ hoppers lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common caterpillar pest. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended biological controls or safe sprays early in the morning can save your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium and prevents rotten patches.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni haaa amɛfite.

english: How do I select the best cassava stems to cut and plant on my new land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala yucca tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ he hee ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Choose thick, mature stems from cassava plants that are 8 to 18 months old and free from leaf disease or stem holes. Healthy middle portions of the stem grow stronger shoots than thin or damaged tips.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni mli tse ni eda kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 ni bɛ baa hela loo ŋmei mli bu lɛ amli. Tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa fe naagbee ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ni efite lɛ.

english: Which plantain shoots should I dig up from my old farm to plant a new crop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ koni mikɛdu tsei heei?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a heavy base. They grow much faster and produce bigger, healthier bunches than suckers with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmɔlɔ’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni tsii. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ niji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Wait until the soil receives two or three good, heavy rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting after just one light shower can cause your seeds to germinate and then dry up and die if rain stops for a few days.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to survive. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ—amɛjuɔ sũ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. Leaving some taller shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture, protecting young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Koni abu kookoo bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain trunk, they compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ɔ amɛbɔleɔ Plantain tsei babaoo tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for maize growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves stay green and healthy so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmãa shwereɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing on my young maize leaves with small worms hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Kɛ ŋmei bibioo ko ni akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which eats the soft center of the maize plant where new leaves grow. Detecting them early and applying suitable treatments like neem seed extract or recommended insecticides stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baai heei miikwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Ni aaana amɛ mra ni akɛ tsamɔ gbɛ̀i ni sa tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft rot in the soil when it rains heavily for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water starves cassava roots of air and creates conditions where soil fungi thrive, causing the roots to decay. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni efee shihilɛi ni baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ adara Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to catch energy, which feeds the growing underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and leading to bigger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee bɔni afee ni amɛto hewalɛ. ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ foliar helai anaa ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures become too hot, water is inconsistent, or the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Providing regular watering and light shade during extremely hot periods helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests. Using neem oil spray or insecticidal soap helps control these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ anɔ Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebuɔ baai heei ni shwereɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my land yield less crop every year if I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen to the soil and stops crop diseases from building up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni ekpa tsei ahe helai ni buaa amɛhe naa lɛ

english: Why do people spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ amɛbɔleɔ aduawai ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and adds organic food to the soil as it breaks down.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Ehaa jwɛi shwereɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They require shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantain to block harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding air and soil humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛnɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Ehiɛ ehe yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which eats the growing point of the maize plant. Early detection and applying appropriate sprays into the plant whorl early in the morning can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ shwie tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up, twisting, and showing yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and produce a higher total yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout even when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ po?

english: The first rain often does not wet the ground deep enough. If a hot dry spell follows, the soil dries out completely and kills the germinating seed before it can break through the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa ni ebaafite dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have pale yellow or light green leaves instead of rich dark green leaves, or produce tiny fruits despite getting good rain, your soil is low in plant nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local environment and are very efficient at stealing water, light, and soil food from your crops, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jumɔ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: What causes the bottom of my tomato fruits to turn black and rot while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato yibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is expanding rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo enine shɛɔ nu nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiya hiɛ oya lɛ.

english: Why should I pinch off the very first flowers on my pepper plants when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Removing the earliest flowers allows the young plant to direct its energy into growing strong roots and stem branches first, which leads to many more flowers and bigger peppers later in the season.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni jeɔ shishi mra fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi kɛ niji ni wa ni miida lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa anáa fɔfɔii wuji kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny black bugs eat up my harvested maize grains after I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi diji bibii lɛ Yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: These are grain weevils that hatch from eggs laid in the grain. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags or with safe storage dust prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmaa ŋmeii ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmaa mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo vacuum bag loo dust collector mli lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Tso lɛ yɛ kuku lolo?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green leaf growth. It can also happen when too much rain drowns the roots or when weeds steal nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ shwie shishifãi lɛ anɔ loo kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ ju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leaves and tall stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are in heavy shade, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Proper spacing and full sunlight help the plant focus on growing tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ŋmei kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their small flowers before any pods actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani pods lɛ adara diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small portion turn into pods. Heavy flower drop happens when there are not enough tiny midges to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by drought and poor soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ E pɛ ebafeɔ pod. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji tooi bibii ba. Eshɛɛɛ ni ekɛbaawo pollination loo be mli ni hɔmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ miigba tsei anaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the air gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are some of my corn cobs missing seeds or only half-filled with kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii fã pɛ lɛ?

english: Incomplete corn cobs usually happen because of poor pollination caused by hot, dry winds or drought. If the silks dry out before catching pollen from the tassels, those kernels will not form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni edako lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi loo hɔmɔ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ siliki tsɔji lɛ egbi dani emɔ pollen kɛjɛ tsɔji lɛ amli lɛ, Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ko.

english: How do groundnut plants form nuts under the soil after flowering above ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant grows long stalks called 'pegs' that bend downward and push themselves into the dirt, where the nuts safely grow and ripen.
ga: Beni ashɛɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water during intense heat. However, it can also be a reaction to tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ baai kɛ tsei amli helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli hu.

english: Why should I cut down extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete directly with the main plantain tree for food, water, and sunlight. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need plenty of direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves open to sunlight and keeps them off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cowpeas or beans before our main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu cowpeas loo beans dani wɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it directly into the dirt through their roots. When the plant dies, it leaves behind free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow strong. It can also happen if the field is flooded and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: How do I know if my farm land needs extra fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli dani madu nii?

english: If your previous crop leaves looked pale, grew slowly, or yielded smaller harvests than usual, it means the natural nutrients in your soil are finished and need to be replaced with fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ato najiaŋ.

english: Leaves curl inward during high heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant save water and prevent itself from drying out.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ, ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are under stress from prolonged heat, a lack of shade, or when the plant does not have enough water and soil nutrients to feed the developing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli, kɛ́ amɛbɛ hulutsoo, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Tuber rot happens when water stays trapped in the soil for too long during heavy rains, causing the roots to choke and enabling soil fungi to break down the tubers.
ga: Tuber rot baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crop plants grow so small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal these vital supplies away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles eating the plant tissue, which reduces the plant's ability to use sunlight to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji lɛ kɛ bu yɛ baai amli. Enɛ baaha tsei nyɛŋ amɛkɛ hulu la atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain, they steal food and water from the main tree, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: Will removing lower branches from my tomato plants help me get bigger fruits?
ga: Ani tomato tso niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha yibii lɛ adara?

english: Yes, trimming off the extra lower side-shoots forces the plant to direct its energy, water, and nutrients into growing large, healthy fruits instead of unnecessary extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ baai krokomɛi afata he ni he ehiaaa

english: How long does it usually take for me to realize that my cocoa trees have a serious disease like Swollen Shoot?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mileɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hela ko ni naa wa tamɔ bud swelling?

english: It can take anywhere from six months to two years after infection for clear symptoms like swollen branches or red vein patterns on leaves to appear, which is why early inspection is vital.
ga: Ebaanyɛ ehe he fɛɛ he kɛjɛ nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi afii enyɔ yɛ hela lɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ tsei niji ni efu loo ŋmeii tsuji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baaje kpo. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni okwɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down and uproot my cocoa trees when they get sick instead of just spraying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ ni mifolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ beni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofa baashwie nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain viral diseases in cocoa cannot be cured with chemicals; uprooting sick trees is the only way to stop the disease from spreading through roots and insects to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofai atsa helai komɛi ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa koni ekatsɔ shishifãi kɛ kooloi amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: If I uproot sick cocoa trees today, can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same spot immediately?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɛnɛ mijie cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ, Ani manyɛ madu cacao tso hee yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, you should wait a few months after clearing out old roots to treat the soil and plant shade crops first so remaining pathogens die out before new seedlings are introduced.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi beni ojie shishifãi momo lɛ sɛɛ koni okɛtsa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha helai ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ agboi dani dumɔwui heei aba.

english: How can I tell the difference between a cocoa tree that is dying from disease and one that is just suffering from the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tso ni hela miigbe lɛ kɛ cacao tso ni hɔmɔ miipiŋ kɛkɛ lɛ teŋ?

english: Drought causes leaves across the whole farm to dry up and drop evenly, while a disease often causes specific signs like swollen stems, yellow patches, or black rotting pods on individual trees.
