ga: Hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli pɛpɛɛpɛ, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela kɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa, tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo ŋmeii diji ni egboi ni yɔɔ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die so quickly when I plant them in a field without any tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out and burn in direct sunlight; they need shade from plantain or timber trees to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What crops can I plant on my field to make the soil healthy again before I put down fresh cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ dani mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei awo mli?

english: Planting cover crops like leguminous beans or cassava helps break disease cycles, add nitrogen back into the soil, and prepare the land for new cocoa trees.
ga: Dumɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ yardlong beans loo cassava. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ Akɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛhaa kookoo tsei heei.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rainy seasons, especially if the tree canopy is too thick and traps damp air.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji tso lɛ shishi tsɔne lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Will cutting off branches from my cocoa tree reduce the amount of cocoa pods I get to harvest?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha cacao ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: No, pruning dead or overcrowded branches actually increases harvest because it exposes hidden pod spots to sunlight and improves airflow, preventing diseases.
ga: Dabi, tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ ehaa pod hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni atsĩ helai anaa

english: Why are my older cocoa trees giving me much smaller pods now than they did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso ni etsɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, the nutrients in the soil get used up, and the trees become less efficient at feeding pods unless you add fertilizer or prune away old wood.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya. Ni tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ niyenii mli. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo ofo tso momo mli.

english: Are insects like capsids spreading diseases on my farm, or are they just eating the cocoa leaves?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ miigbɛ helai amɛshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo amɛmiiye kookoo baai kɛkɛ?

english: Capsid insects damage the outer layer of young branches and pods while feeding, which leaves open wounds that allow harmful fungal diseases to enter the tree easily.
ga: Capsid kooloi lɛ fiteɔ niji bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛgbɛ fã lɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbele naa ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like fingers during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ niji yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl up, it is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing water through heat. Closing up reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Nɔ ni akɛkpaa lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my newly planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, hot sunlight during their first couple of years. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the bottom leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green, so when nutrients run low, the plant pulls food from its older lower leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Cassava tubers store energy for the plant. If you leave them in the soil past their proper harvest time, the plant starts converting its soft, starchy roots into tough woody fibers to support new stem growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ hewalɛ toɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho amɛkpamɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ, Tso lɛ baabɔi eshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ starch lɛ tsakemɔ ni etsɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni mli wa ni baaye abua tso lɛ shishifãi heei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden shifts between dry soil and heavy watering. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni mli wa teŋ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and thin with very few peppers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they shade each other and fight for sunlight. The plants stretch upward as tall as possible to reach the light instead of spreading out branches to grow flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a gblaa a nine ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a pue fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting shoots in the barn even when there is no dirt or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nugbɔ bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally contain stored food and water inside them. Once their internal rest period ends, the tuber uses its own stored moisture to sprout shoots, signaling that it is time to be planted in the ground.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sweet potato ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji mligbɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tubers lɛ kɛ nu ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the base of my garden plants keep the soil moist for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight from heating the dirt. This prevents moisture from evaporating quickly into the air and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli adɔ. Enɛ haaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms hide inside the central funnel of my maize plant during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the cool, moist funnel of the maize plant during the hot day to protect their soft bodies from hot sunlight and predators. They come out to feed when temperatures drop.
ga: Asraafoi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛgbɔmɔtsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to quickly soak up the first rain and food in the soil. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the water and nutrients your crops need to start strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow before the crop is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food responsible for green leafy growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, so applying fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni haa baai eŋɔlii lɛ daa lɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and naturally breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I water my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil nutrients and water they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They require shade trees or food crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas, keeping them cool and conserving soil moisture while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause waterlogging and flood the ground for long periods, air gets trapped out, causing the tubers to drown and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ baamɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does putting dry grass or dry leaves around the base of my crops help during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the plant roots cool and moist.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the growing crops fight for the same limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving crops proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room to feed and produce a big yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing heat damage and leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii kɛ foliar hela naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the plants from intense direct heat helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juices from the leaves, or passing along a virus. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Why did my maize crop produce very little grain this year compared to last year, even though I planted the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ po

english: Crops react heavily to changing weather patterns every year. Even with good seeds, minor shifts in rain timing, higher sun heat, or dry spells during flowering can disrupt how well the plant forms its grains.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii waa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsake kɛjɛ afi kɛyaa afi. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ moŋ tsakemɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la mli Loo be ni nugbɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and start dropping when floodwater stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi beni nu afua lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it smothers the roots, causing them to rot and preventing the crop from taking up food, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I keep the soil around my vegetables damp for longer when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee tɛŋŋ ni aduawai ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective shade. It stops the hot sun from quickly drying out the soil moisture that roots need to survive.
ga: He ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ ni oooha Onibii ni okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa sũ mli nu ni he hiaa shishifãi koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow faster and greener when I plant right after the very first rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The long dry season leaves natural plant food trapped in the dirt. When the very first rains soak the ground, it releases a sudden rush of nitrogen, giving your young plants a strong, quick start.
ga: Hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũu. Abaajie nitrogen kpo trukaa. Ha odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi oya ni mli wa.

english: Why are my crop yields getting smaller every year even though I work just as hard on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ni mitsu nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ. amɛfee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season to grow. If you plant the same crop every year without adding manure, fertilizer, or resting the soil, the ground gets weak and loses its ability to feed healthy plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: What naturally happens to my farm's soil when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a field where maize was grown before?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsutsu lɛ adu ŋmãa mli lɛ mli?

english: Beans, cowpeas, and groundnuts are special crops that capture good nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they die, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans, cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kpakpa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do insects attack my crops much more heavily during hot, dry weeks than during the rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli fe otsii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: During dry spells, wild bush plants dry up, forcing insects to move to your green farm crops for food and water. High heat also causes many insect pests to hatch and multiply much faster.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsoi bibii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ egbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ kooloi bibii aya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu haa kooloi bibii babaoo fɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout if the soil gets baked hard by the sun right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ hulu shã shikpɔŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sprouting seeds are gentle and need soft, moist earth to push through. When the top soil bakes into a hard crust under the hot sun, the young shoots get trapped underneath and die before reaching the light.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ koni akɛtsi kɛya mli. Beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ. Tsobii bibii lɛ baakpɛtɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them directly under large plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni midu lɛ yɛ dumɔwui wuji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need full daylight to make energy for producing flowers and peppers. When planted under thick plantain leaves, the shade makes the pepper plant stretch upward searching for light instead of growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ pepper. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ plantain baai ni mli tse lɛ ashishi lɛ, hulutsoo lɛ baaha pepper tso lɛ ashɛ ehe koni eyatao la yɛ yibii ni ebaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my mature crops spoil quickly if I leave them in the field too long waiting for extra labor or tools?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni miimɛ nitsumɔ loo nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfata he lɛ?

english: Once a crop reaches full maturity, it stops defending itself naturally. Leaving ripe crops in the field exposes them to field pests, rot from unexpected rain, and high sun heat that weakens the harvested quality.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaakpa ehe hebuu yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ mli fitemɔ fa babaoo aahu akɛ ehaa ŋmaa lɛ mli nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: If I use a tractor to plow my land instead of doing it by hand with a hoe, how will it affect how my crops grow?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ traktɔ tsu nii kɛtsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmei baatsu nii Te ebaana ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Plowing with a tractor loosens hard, compacted soil much deeper than a hand hoe can. This allows crop roots to grow deeper, breathe better, and access underground water, leading to stronger plants and bigger yields.
ga: Trakta ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli shwieɔ shi kwraa fe tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Mumɔ jogbaŋŋ ni onine ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu nɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How does using a motorized knapsack sprayer help my crops grow better than clearing weeds by hand with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: A sprayer lets you apply weed control quickly across the entire farm before weeds can steal light, water, and nutrients from your crops. It also avoids damaging your crops' shallow roots, which often happens when clearing weeds with a cutlass.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Dani jwɛi lɛ baaju la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli. Etsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ hu ahe. of damaged crops Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ dade jieɔ jwɛi.

english: Does harvesting my rice with a machine change the quality of the grains compared to cutting them by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mlihilɛ kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: Machine harvesting cuts and threshes the rice at the exact right time, reducing grain breakage and preventing the rice from spoiling on the field. This results in cleaner, whole grains that attract better buyers at the market.
ga: Nikpalɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni etswaa ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni fãa lɛ shi ni otsi ŋmãa ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ naa Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni he tse ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ waa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow very tall but only produce small, thin cobs that do not bring much money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni ekomɛi ni amɛnáaa shika babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize plants need plenty of nitrogen early in their life to make big cobs. If the soil lacks nutrients or if plants are planted too close together, the crop spends all its energy growing stems instead of filling out the cob.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa tsei yɛ amɛshihilɛ shishijee mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni ekɛbaafata ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow even after I buy and apply chemical fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ oheɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can happen if the soil is too wet, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up food. It can also mean you applied fertilizer at the wrong time or used a type that lacks the specific nutrients your tomatoes need at that growth stage.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa o-tomatoi lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii.

english: When is the right time to feed fertilizer to my crops so it does not go to waste in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly moist and the crops are actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting. If you apply it on dry soil or during heavy downpours, the nutrients will either burn the roots or get washed away by rain.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Niyenii mli nibii baaha shishifãi lɛ ashã loo nugbɔ baaho amɛ.

english: Why are insects still eating my cabbage leaves even after I sprayed pest medicine on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests often hide under the leaves where sprays miss, or they can become used to the same medicine if you use it repeatedly. Spraying under the leaves during cool hours when insects are active makes the treatment far more effective.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi yɛ hei ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ. Aloo, amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔmɔ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ okɛtsu nii shii abɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie baai lɛ ashishi gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii waa lɛ, ebaaha tsofafeemɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants give me bigger tubers when I leave plenty of space between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mishiɔ gbɛ babaoo yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need physical space underground to swell into large tubers. When planted too close together, the leaves shade each other from sunlight and the roots fight for nutrients, resulting in long, skinny tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bɔni afee ni amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting fruit during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from heat stress and lack of soil moisture. Giving the plants sufficient water during flowering keeps the soil cool and enables the plant to hold onto its blossoms to form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni ewo yibii.

english: Why does a crop like cocoa take years to bring in money while maize gives me cash in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii babaoo dani enáa sɛɛnamɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, Corn ha mi shika yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Maize is a quick-maturing seasonal crop that completes its life cycle in 3 to 4 months. Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that spends its first few years building strong roots and branches before it can produce pods continuously for decades.
ga: Abɛi ji be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Cocoa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni heɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani enáa shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa dani enyɛɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Do all the crops I plant on my farm need the same amount of water to grow well?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, different crops require different amounts of water. While some crops can survive in very wet conditions, many others will be ruined if they are left sitting in too much water.
ga: Dabi, tsei srɔtoi biɔ nu babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli moŋ, Shi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baafite kɛji nu babaoo eshwɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if heavy rain leaves too much standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Excess standing water can choke crop roots by cutting off air. If the water stays on the land too long, it can rot the roots and kill the plants.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha tso lɛ agbo.

english: How can I tell if there is too much water on my soil for healthy crop growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: If you see pools of water gathering on top of the ground that do not sink in quickly, or if the ground feels very muddy for days, there is too much water for most standard crops.
ga: Kɛji ona nu ŋshɔ ko ni ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieee shi oya lɛ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nu he akɛ emli efu gbii babaoo Enɛ tsɔɔ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: If my farmland gets flooded, what is the best way to protect my crops?
ga: Kɛji nu eyi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: You need to find a suitable direction and create a path or channel to drain the excess water so it can flow off your farm and leave the land healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ otao gbɛ ni ja ni ofee gbɛ loo gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli koni enyɛ ejɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I remove excess water from my crop field without damaging the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mifiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You can dig shallow drainage ditches leading from the flooded areas toward lower ground or a nearby water pathway to let the water naturally flow away.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛjɛ he ni nu lɛ eyi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ loo nu gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ ehe kɛya.

english: How can I prepare my land before the heavy rains start so water does not spoil my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa koni nu lɛ akafite midumɔ nii?

english: You can dig simple drainage channels around your farm beds ahead of time so that when heavy rains fall, the extra water flows away automatically.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mlɛo. Obɔle oŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Will draining floodwater off my field make my land too dry for crops?
ga: Ani nu afua ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ agbi tsɔ kɛha okwaayeli?

english: No, draining only removes the excess surface water that suffocates crops. The soil itself will remain moist enough to keep your plants healthy.
ga: Dabi, nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ pɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha otso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I plant the same crops on low, watery parts of my farm as I do on higher ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni miduɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: No, because water collects in lower areas. Crops that cannot handle heavy water should go on higher ground, while land with too much water needs to be drained before planting standard crops.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ. Esa akɛ adu tsei ni nyɛŋ adamɔ tsɔne lɛ naa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie hei ni nu fa fe nine yɔɔ lɛ dani adu nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop turn yellow when there is water standing on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the soil has too much water, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to observe how water settles on my field before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makadi bɔ ni nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Checking where water collects helps you know if you need to drain the land first, saving you from losing seeds and crops to waterlogging.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni nu lɛ buaa ehe naa lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ kɛji ehe miihia ni okɛ nu lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshinii ni nu afua lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. It can also happen when soil remains waterlogged for too long, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but only produce small, thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess shade, cassava spends all its energy growing heavy branches and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ starch ato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eniji kɛ baai ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that have tiny bumps on their roots containing good bacteria. These bacteria capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which benefits the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ helai kpakpai lɛ anɔ Helai nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted directly in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn and dry out quickly under direct sun. They need shade from temporary companion crops, like plantains, to shield them while their root system grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off without turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extremely hot daytime temperatures, lack of water, or uneven soil moisture. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy when conditions are difficult.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli latsaa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baawo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over once the fruit bunch starts growing large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go very deep into the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs to be supported with wooden or bamboo props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii afi sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to weed around my yam mounds while the vines are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ ooojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ato be mli ni wain tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Young yam shoots grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Weeding early prevents weeds from stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before the yam vine establishes itself.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani sweet potato wain tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven, making it hard for the plant's roots to take up calcium continuously from the soil.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaya nɔ amɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my healthy green cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and moisture. Raindrops splash the fungus onto the pods, causing them to turn dark and decay rapidly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ewoɔ duŋ ni efiteɔ oya.

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on tender young leaves. The caterpillars hide inside the leaf funnel (the whorl) to feed safely away from sun and predators.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni darako lɛ. Kplukai kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai (rings) amli koni amɛye nii shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on lower parts of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed new growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: During intense heat, pepper plants lose water from their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. They droop to reduce surface area exposed to the sun and usually recover in the evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛgbee shi koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and getting strange yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaf curling and yellow patches are typically caused by cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that feed on the sap of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with small ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward quickly to reach light, leaving little energy to produce large ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee toi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do bean plants remain stunted and refuse to grow big in some parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Stunted growth in beans often happens when soil is too hard for roots to penetrate, when the soil is too acidic, or when root-knot nematodes attack the root system underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni root-knot nematodes lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do crops grown directly under large trees take longer to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to perform photosynthesis and make energy for fruiting. The shade from large tree canopies blocks light, slowing down crop growth and delaying fruiting.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee fotosintɛsis ni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha yibiiwoo. Hɔɔ ni jɛ tso agbo ko yiteŋ lɛ tsi kane lɛ naa. Ehaa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehaa amɛwoɔ yibii sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping flowers without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when extreme heat damages the pollen, or when there is inconsistent watering and too much nitrogen fertilizer given at the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. aloo be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some young cocoa pods turn shriveled and black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii komɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt where the tree discards excess pods it cannot feed, or by fungal infections like black pod disease during heavy rain seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel’s wilt lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye lɛ yɛ. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every season when I plant cassava on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Continuous cropping of the same plant drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my planted cowpea seeds fail to sprout out of the ground after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if planted too deep, if the soil is too dry or too waterlogged, or if soil pests like insect larvae eat the seed before it can break through the soil surface.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When cocoa pods are ripe, their skin changes color from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Tapping the pod gently with your knuckles will also produce a hollow sound, showing the seeds inside have separated from the outer shell.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwere lɛ Ehewolo lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛtsɔ oniji anɔ lɛ, taa tsɔne lɛ he fioo. baaha gbee ni mli ewo muji aba Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbala kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he.

english: What happens if I pull cocoa pods off the branch with my bare hands instead of using a cutting tool?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ miniji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko gbala kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dɛŋdade ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Tearing pods off with your hands damages the bark and the flower cushion where the pod was attached. This cushion is where future flowers and pods grow, so damaging it reduces your tree's ability to produce cocoa in future seasons.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ oniji shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni ŋmeii lɛ ekpɛtɛ he lɛ. Kushin nɛɛ ji he ni wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo yɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to harvest ripe cocoa pods during the main season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should harvest every 2 to 3 weeks during peak season. Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the seeds inside to germinate or rot, which ruins the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do government extension officers insist that we cut down trees infected with Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ afo tsei ni cocoa bloat hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus has no chemical cure and spreads rapidly through mealybugs to neighboring healthy trees. Removing and destroying infected trees is the only established rule to stop the virus from destroying your whole farm and surrounding farms.
ga: Tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛbaatsa kookoo bud hela lɛ. Ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni ji mealybugs lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛfitemɔ ji mla pɛ ni ato koni akɛtsi hela lɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni ebɔle ohe lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ duŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, cold, and shady conditions. Regular weeding, pruning extra branches to let in sunlight, and harvesting promptly prevent moisture from staying on the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni hulu la lɛ abote mli Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akamɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important to prune dead branches and chupons from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tsei aniji ni egboi kɛ cacao ni yɔɔ cocoa tsei amli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the leafy canopy so sunlight and airflow can reach every part of the tree, which lowers disease risk. It also prevents the tree from wasting food on unproductive stems so it can focus energy on growing pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli alɛɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai aba shi. Etsiɔ tso lɛ hu naa koni ekafite niyenii yɛ tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama pods lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans for several days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the bean's seed germ and starts the chemical reaction that creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color. Without fermentation, the beans stay purple, taste extremely bitter, and will be rejected by licensed buying agents.
ga: Fɛ̃i gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ejeɔ tsofa ko ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baakã he ahi ŋmɔtɔ, ebaana ŋmɔtɔ waa, ni mɛi ni heɔ nii ni aha amɛ hegbɛ lɛ baakpoo.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my freshly harvested cocoa beans directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa ehee lɛ? yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Drying cocoa on bare soil exposes the beans to dirt, stones, livestock droppings, and ground moisture that causes mold. Drying on raised bamboo mats or clean tarpaulins ensures high-quality, clean beans.
ga: Kookoo ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa muji, tɛi, kooloi afɔfɔi, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ aba lɛ baa kɔfi yibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ agbi yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ loo tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe tseɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need tall shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ abɔle mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and dry out during the Harmattan season. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and reducing heat stress on young plants.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni egbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my cocoa trees improve my harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi-cacao ŋmɔji lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your cocoa roots. Keeping the farm floor clean ensures all fertilizer and soil richness go straight into expanding the cocoa trees and fattening the pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he tse lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yaa koni amɛha kookoo tsei lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and turning brown during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate like human infants and cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees around them to block the hot sun and retain soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni enyɛŋ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in wet, dark conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air into your farm to dry out moisture and prevent the fungus from thriving.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ mli Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akadara.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves the strength to green up and grow properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does covering the bare ground around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive warm days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔleɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves creates mulch, which acts like a blanket. It shades the dirt from direct sun heat, keeps moisture trapped in the soil longer, and stops weeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwie nɔ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsiɔ muji kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out hard and woody instead of soft and heavy when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo ni amɛhe wa kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots turn woody when plants are left in the ground too long past their harvest time or when they go through extended dry spells without enough moisture during tuber formation.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni eho kpamɔɔ be lɛ he. aloo beni tsei tsɔɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni bulb lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam shoots to climb tall sticks instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for growing big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves high off the muddy ground to catch maximum sunlight while keeping the leaves safe from damp ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa muji lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize ears small and thin when I plant seeds very close together to fit more crops in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same limited food and water in the soil while their leaves block each other's light, resulting in weak plants with tiny yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do plantain suckers take so long to sprout after I plant them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers sprout slowly if old, dead roots and stem damage are not trimmed off before planting, or if planted in hard soil without soft, damp organic matter around the base.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Kɛji akɛ afooo shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ amli dani adu, Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni mli edɔ bɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by erratic watering, extreme heat, or pest damage from small insects like thrips that attack the joint where the blossom attaches.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fãji ni tomato fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why are there small holes chewed into the stems and leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni mikɛyeɔ nii?

english: Those holes are caused by caterpillars such as the Fall Armyworm, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves and feed on the soft growing center of the young maize plant.
ga: Buji nɛɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli lɛ feɔ. ni eyeɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same plot with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa seedlings from sunburn while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK, urea, or decomposed animal manure gives the leaves back their rich green color and helps the plant grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK, urea, loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the main stems become hard and woody. You can gently dig around the base of one plant to inspect the size of the tubers before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmaa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ wa ni eyɛ tsei Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo abɔle tso kome shishigbɛ he koni okwɛ bɔ ni bulbs lɛ da ha dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni elaaje yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf shoot. Checking your farm early and spraying targeted bio-pesticides or neem water into the leaf funnels early in the morning or evening will control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem nu ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye amɛnɔ.

english: This rot is caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady with regular watering and adding wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil helps prevent this condition.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the maize crop, improves soil fertility for the next season, and saves you money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni eye ebua bo ni okɛ shika ato tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are regular, usually after two or three good downpours. The first rain is often followed by a heat spell that can dry out the soil and kill freshly germinated seeds before they establish roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani amɛfee shishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do you recommend covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks sunlight from drying out the soil, prevents weed seeds from growing, and decays over time to add rich organic matter back into your farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa afata he ekoŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to feed and grow large underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and clean, protecting the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhe tseɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant seeds harvested from last year's hybrid maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their vigor and high yields in the second generation, leading to small cobs and unequal plant growth. Buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong growth, uniform ears, and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ he waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa dalɛ ni mli wa baa. Toi kɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ po

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so they don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akafite?

english: You should harvest cocoa pods when they change color completely from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting too early leaves you with underdeveloped beans that lack flavor, while waiting too long causes the seeds inside to germinate or rot.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛtsake amɛhe kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ ŋmeii ni edako jogbaŋŋ ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba. Yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi.

english: Why is it important to gather my harvested cocoa pods at the base of the trees before breaking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abua kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi dani akumɔ amɛ?

english: Gathering pods together at a clean base makes it easier to inspect them for diseases like black pod, sort out healthy ones, and keep the beans clean from soil and dirt when you break the pods open.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmeii lɛ anaa kɛ shishitoo ni he tse lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ kɛji helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ mli, ni ajieɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Ni ha ŋmeii lɛ ahe atse kɛjɛ muji kɛ muji he beni ogbeleɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Is it better to harvest my cocoa pods as soon as a few turn yellow, or should I wait for all of them on the tree to turn yellow?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ oookpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛji kookoo ŋmeii fioo komɛi batsɔ ŋmɔŋ pɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi kookoo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: It is best to harvest ripe pods every two to three weeks as they turn yellow rather than waiting for all of them. Leaving ripe pods on the tree for too long attracts pests like squirrels and increases the risk of diseases spreading.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, moŋ fe ni ooomɛ kɛyashi amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaaho. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, egbalaa ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni ehaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What is the correct way to cut a cocoa pod from the branch so I don't hurt the tree?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ afoɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ tsei aniji amli? Jeee koni eye tso lɛ awui?

english: You should use a sharp sickle or pruner to make a clean cut along the pod stem. Never pull or twist the pod by hand, because pulling damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk, which stops future pods from growing in that spot.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mli wa atsu nii. Koni afolɔ pod lɛ shishi fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kaagbala loo okɛ onine atsɔ podi lɛ anɔ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ agbala lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi akutso ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ baatsi wɔsɛɛ be mli pods lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli.

english: Why do the roots of my cocoa trees sometimes rot, and how can I keep them healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kookoo tso shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cocoa roots rot mainly when the soil stays waterlogged for too long or when underground fungi attack them. You can protect the roots by digging proper drainage channels to remove standing water and avoiding deep digging near the trunk that damages shallow roots.
ga: Cocoa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ titri kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii tutua amɛ. Obaanyɛ obu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ ojie nu ni ekã shi lɛ nɔ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋtayaa ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he, ni baafite shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree naturally thins out pods it cannot feed, or by black pod disease caused by heavy rain and humidity. Pruning excess branches helps air flow through the farm and reduces this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’, ni baa beni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi ni anyɛɛɛ aye lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ black pod hela ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa lɛ mli Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebaaha naagba nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and soft while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ be mli ni mikɛkpeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy conditions. You can control it by harvesting ripe pods promptly, removing infected pods from the farm, and spraying recommended fungicides during the wet season.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ eji black pod hela Ejɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni oookpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my cocoa trees help them bear more fruits?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your cocoa trees need to produce pods. Keeping the base clear ensures the tree's roots get all the nutrients, and it also prevents pests from hiding near the trunk.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa cacao tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ oha shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade trees when they are young, but too much shade causes problems when they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa ehe hulutsoo be mli ni eji gbekɛ lɛ? Shi ani shade babaoo kɛ naagbai baa beni edara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in harsh sunlight, so temporary shade protects them. However, mature trees need sunshine to produce flowers and pods; too much shade creates dark, wet conditions where diseases thrive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, be kukuoo mli hulutsoo baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu kookoo tso lɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Shade babaoo kɛ duŋ, shihilɛi ni mli efɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni helai babaoo shwereɔ yɛ.

english: Some people say low cocoa yield is caused by bad luck, but what practical steps actually bring a good harvest?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ kookoo ni baa shi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, shi mɛɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa ŋmaa kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Low yield is usually caused by poor soil, pests, disease, or old trees. You can naturally boost your harvest by pruning dead branches, applying fertilizer, managing shade, and harvesting regularly to stop diseases from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai loo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa. Obaanyɛ oha odebɔɔ mli yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni ooofolɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookɛwo mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookwɛ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa daa koni helai akagbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and harsh heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees provides a canopy that protects young cocoa from sun damage and preserves moisture in the soil during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ fataa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it safe for me to grow food crops like cassava or maize on the same land with my young tree crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, growing food crops alongside young tree crops provides early harvest and income while your trees mature. However, you must maintain proper spacing so the food crops do not choke or steal all the sunlight and water from the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu yɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe lɛ haa anáa ŋmaa mra kɛ shika be mli ni otsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ koni niyenii tsei lɛ akatsi amɛhe loo amɛkaju hulu la kɛ nu fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant as many crop trees as possible close together on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Planting trees too close together causes them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak trees and lower overall yields. Proper spacing allows each tree enough air and light to grow strong and produce maximum fruit.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune and cut off small side shoots from my crop trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni mafolɔ amɛ lɛ? kɛjɛ mi tsei lɛ amli daa?

english: Pruning removes unproductive shoots and dead branches, allowing the tree to direct its energy into growing healthy fruit. It also improves airflow through the canopy, which lowers the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Does harvesting crop pods forcefully by hand damage the tree's future yield?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii ni mli wa lɛ baafite tso lɛ yibiiwoo ni baajɛ mli aba wɔsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, tearing fruits or pods off by hand can damage the cushions on the branch where future flowers grow. Using clean, sharp tools like a cutlass or harvesting hook protects these flowering points so the tree can produce fruits in upcoming seasons.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, aduawai loo ŋmeii ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee kushin yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ he ni wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔii baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dɛŋdade ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu fɔfɔii nɛɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ awo yibii yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei amli.

english: Why do my crop trees give heavy yields in the first few years but start producing much less after three or four years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli shi ebɔi yibii fioo ko pɛ woɔ yɛ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth with every harvest. Over time, without adding organic compost or fertilizer to replenish the soil, the land becomes exhausted and crop yields naturally decline.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Beni bei hoɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he koni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens to my crop trees when the dry season lasts longer than expected, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu tsei nɛɛ ahe?

english: Extended dry weather causes crops to drop leaves and flowers to conserve water, reducing fruit yield. Mulching around the base of your trees with dry vegetation helps trap moisture in the soil and keeps tree roots cool.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai ni anáa lɛ nɔ ni baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: How do small weeds hurt my fully grown crop trees if the trees are already much taller than the weeds?
ga: Te jwɛi bibii baanyɛ aye mi tsei ni eda lɛ awui amɛha tɛŋŋ? Beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Tree roots rely on shallow feeder roots near the surface to absorb water and nutrients. Weeds steal these essential nutrients and water right from the topsoil, which slows down fruit development even on mature trees.
ga: Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Jwɛi juɔ nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ tsei ni eda po anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and dropping off during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the rainy season can lead to waterlogged soil and root rot or fungal infections. Ensuring proper field drainage and applying recommended fungicides early helps protect your crop leaves from rot.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi baanyɛ agbo loo tsɛŋemɔ hela baanyɛ amɔ amɛ. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akwɛ koni nu atsɔ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaabu otso lɛ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: How many years can a crop tree keep producing good harvests before I need to replace it?
ga: Afii enyiɛ tso ko baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani ehe baahia ni atsake nɔ kroko?

english: With good farm management, weeding, and pruning, tree crops like cocoa can remain productive for 25 to 30 years or more. As trees age past 30 years, yield drops, and they may need rehabilitation or replanting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ajie jwɛi kɛ tsei lɛ, tsei tamɔ kookoo baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛ́ tso ko eye fe afii 30 lɛ, nɔ ni ewoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni asaa tso lɛ loo adu lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn whitish or greenish with mold while in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ eyɛŋ loo eŋɔli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?
