english: Maize molds when it is bagged before drying completely or stored in humid conditions. Tiny fungi grow on the moist grains and produce dangerous poisons called aflatoxins, which can cause severe human health problems like liver cancer when eaten.
ga: Abɛi feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa loo akɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli. Fungi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmaa ni mli efɔ nɔ ni amɛjieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxins lɛ kpo. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai ni mli wa, tamɔ mlɛbo mli kansa aba, kɛ́ mɔ ko ye lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnuts get a dark, dusty powder inside the shell when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ?

english: This dark powder is caused by fungal infection in the soil, especially during dry spells. The mold stays on the seeds and produces invisible toxins that make the groundnuts unsafe for humans and livestock.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ powda ni tsuɔ waa nɛɛ baa. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ tsofa ko ni anaaa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛhaa adesai kɛ kooloi lɛ baa.

english: Is it safe to scrape off the mold from my maize and use the clean part for porridge?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oootsi ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni okɛ fã ni he tse lɛ atsu nii kɛfee ŋmãa?

english: No, because the toxic poisons produced by mold spread deep into the grain even if you cannot see them. Cooking or scraping off visible mold does not destroy these harmful chemicals that damage the liver over time.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɔji ni ŋmei lɛ kɛbaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmaa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛji onaaa lɛ po. Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ mlɛbo lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ ni ahoɔ loo ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do insect holes in my maize cobs make the surrounding grain spoil so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmaa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Pests like weevils create open wounds on the grain while feeding. These wounds allow airborne mold spores to enter easily, leading to rapid decay and poisonous fungal growth on the crop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii feɔ pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Nɛkɛ pilamɔi nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why does drying my harvested crops directly on the bare dirt cause them to spoil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ ni migbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa egboɔ lɛ?

english: The soil contains moisture and microscopic fungi. Laying grains directly on the bare ground allows soil fungi to climb onto your crops, causing invisible molds that lead to spoilage and poisonous contamination.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Dumɔwui ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa onibii anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ko ni anaaa lɛ baa ni ekɛ fitemɔ kɛ muji ni yɔɔ gbeyei baa.

english: How can I tell if my stored maize or sorghum is dry enough to avoid rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa koni ekafite?

english: Grains are dry enough when they crack sharply when bitten or make a clear metallic sound when shaken in a sealed glass bottle with dry salt. Soft or bendable grains still contain water that will breed dangerous molds.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni kɛ́ mɔ ko mɔ lɛ, ebaakumɔ waa. aloo ejie dade gbɛɛmɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto kpo kɛji akɛ akpokpo yɛ glase tsinsii ni akɛ ŋmei ni egbi ewo mli lɛ mli. Nu baanyɛ ahi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ni ebɔle lɛ amli lolo, ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yɔɔ oshara aba.

english: Why do my crops get moldy faster when I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛ́ mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture during wet-season harvesting prevents quick drying. Warmth combined with excess water creates the perfect environment for mold fungi to grow rapidly on your harvest.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbiɔ oya lɛ naa. Dɔlɛ ni akɛ nu ni fa fe nine fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize plants produce weak cobs that turn bad quickly when rain stops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra lɛ?

english: Drought stresses the crop and lowers its natural immunity. Weakened plants are much easier targets for soil and air molds to infect before you even harvest them.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baa shi. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ atswa amɛ hela dani okpa amɛ po.

english: Why do my groundnuts rot in the soil if I leave them unharvested past their maturity date?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ ni akpaaa amɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ lɛ?

english: Over-mature groundnut pods weaken underground, making it easy for soil-borne fungi to invade the pods and release harmful toxins into the nuts before you lift them.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ baabote ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛjie tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui awo ŋmeii lɛ amli dani ajie amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I feed my moldy or spoiled crops to my goats or chickens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji loo efite haa mitooi loo mikooloi lɛ?

english: The poisons in moldy grain harm farm animals just like humans, causing weak growth and organ damage. Additionally, these toxins can pass directly into the animal's meat, eggs, or milk.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli lɛ yɛ oshara kɛha ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ bɔ ni eji kɛha adesai lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa dalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii. Kɛfata he lɛ, nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kooloo loo, ŋmeii, loo mliki mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can I plant other crops or trees on the same piece of land where I am planting my new tree seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei krokomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ tsei ahe dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young tree seedlings protects the seedlings from harsh sunlight, keeps the soil moist, and gives you food and income while the trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa bo niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my newly planted tree seedlings die in the field while others survive and grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ ekomɛi miigboi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings often fail if their roots get damaged during transplanting, if they are planted in dry soil without shade, or if they do not receive enough rainwater during their first few critical weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ amɛnáaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to start planting my tree seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mabɔi tso dumɔwui dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to plant at the very beginning of the major rainy season so the seedlings can use the abundant natural moisture to build strong root systems before the sun and dry season set in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛto shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi dani hulu kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: What happens if I plant my tree seedlings too close to one another on my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to thin, tall trees that produce very little yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: How can I tell if my young tree crops are developing healthily after the first few months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Healthy young trees consistently produce vibrant green leaves, grow steadily in height, develop a firm stem, and show no signs of leaf yellowing or heavy insect damage.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baajie baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ yɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo kooloi ni tsii ni efite lɛ he okadi ko kwraa.

english: Will leaving grass and weeds around my small tree seedlings affect how they grow?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mashi yɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaná amɛdalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like thief plants that steal food, water, and light away from your young seedlings, and they can also harbor pests that damage young leaves.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai bibii lɛ hu amli.

english: Why should I put decomposed manure into the planting hole before placing my seedling in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbo awo dumɔ bu lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Manure enriches the soil with vital nutrients, improves the soil's ability to hold moisture, and gives the fresh roots a gentle, nutritious environment to spread quickly.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni ehaa shishifãi heei lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni mli jɔ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my young seedlings droop and curl up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf drooping is the plant's natural defense to reduce water loss during intense sun exposure, indicating that the seedling needs temporary shade or more moisture around its base.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛba nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ ehe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni bɔle amɛshishigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Is it helpful or harmful if I trim off some of the lower branches from my growing tree crops?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua mi loo ebaaye mi awui kɛji mifo tso ko ni miida lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming lower or dead branches is helpful because it directs the plant's energy toward the main stem and leaves, improves air movement around the trunk, and reduces disease risks.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ejaakɛ etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on the progress of my newly planted seedlings?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa?

english: You should inspect your field at least once a week to catch dead seedlings early for replacement, spot pest outbreaks before they spread, and clear away aggressive weeds.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli koni omɔ dumɔwui ni egboi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mra ni okɛto najiaŋ. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. ni ojie jwɛi ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big forest trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ pɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Forest trees act as natural shields, filtering the light and keeping the air humid so the tender leaves do not dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Ehaa la kpɛɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Koni baai bibii lɛ akagbi

english: Why should I trim the upper branches of shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Trimming high shade branches lets controlled sunlight reach the lower cocoa canopy, encouraging flowering while reducing humidity that causes black pod disease.
ga: Shade ni nɔ kwɔ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni akudɔɔ lɛ shɛɔ kookoo shishigbɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my maize crops stunted and thin when I plant them close to tall plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ midu yɛ plantains kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight to produce energy. The broad leaves of tall plantain trees block sunlight from reaching the maize, causing it to starve for light.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ. Dumɔwui kakadaji lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmãa lɛ he. hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ yɛ la he

english: Why does my soil wash away so easily after I clear a sloping piece of land to plant crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ oya beni mifo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ koni mikɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Clearing trees and natural grass leaves the topsoil exposed directly to heavy rains, allowing water to wash away the rich top layer of soil.
ga: Tsei kɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni naa wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to burn all the cleared bush before planting my yam, or should I leave some trees standing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ ashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii loo esa akɛ ashi tsei komɛi?

english: Burning completely damages beneficial soil nutrients and exposes the ground to extreme heat. Leaving select trees provides natural support for yam vines and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kwraa. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔ waa. Tsei ni ahala lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out very fast after I clear all the weeds and expose the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni mijie lɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly to sunlight through evaporation. Leaving cut grass as mulch covers the soil and traps moisture inside.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi jwɛi ni afo lɛ be mli ni ekɛ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall and spindly instead of growing thick and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiiya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ?

english: When tomato plants do not get enough direct sunlight, they stretch rapidly upwards trying to reach light, making stems weak and thin.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ Tomatoi lɛ baajie amɛhe oya koni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ la lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot and sunny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Excessive heat puts severe stress on pepper plants, forcing them to drop their flowers to save water and keep the rest of the plant alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nyɛ fɔfɔi anɔ ni ashwie shi koni nu akafite ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning brown and falling off while the top keeps growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kã he eyɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: As cassava grows tall and creates upper leaf cover, lower leaves get shaded out and no longer receive sunlight, so the plant sheds them to send energy to the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ da ni eha baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni amɛnáaa hulu la dɔŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ yaafo koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amaje ŋwɛi.

english: What makes crops grow unequally across different parts of the same field after I clear a piece of forest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ? ni ji ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli beni mijie koo lɛ mli he lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Forest land has uneven soil conditions where areas with decayed leaves or old ant mounds hold more nutrients and water than bare soil patches.
ga: Kooi amli hei lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi lɛ ejaaa. Hei ni baai ni egboi loo ŋmeii momoi yɔɔ lɛ hiɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ.

english: Planting seeds too close causes the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know which way is up when I am planting cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okwɛ kɛji oodu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small raised nodes or 'eyes' where leaves used to grow on the stem. These nodes should point upwards toward the sky like little arrows; planting them upside down makes it very difficult for shoots to grow properly out of the ground.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ bibii ni awó nɔ. Yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔi bibii. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that scorch easily under full tropical sun. They require temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from heat and conserve soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ ji koni abu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding balanced fertilizer or well-decomposed manure restores the nitrogen levels so the plants can turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids attacking the tender leaves. Applying an approved organic spray, like neem oil, helps clear these pests so healthy new leaves can expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni tutuaa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni yɔɔ hegbɛ, tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and light shading during hot peak hours encourages flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the heat, and prevents unwanted weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops in the middle of the hot day or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai nu yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots can absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it. Morning watering ensures plants stay hydrated throughout the hottest part of the day without wasting water.
ga: Okɛ nu awo mli leebi maŋkpa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane hulu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni efiteee nu.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles or stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso loo tso ama sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently. Staking keeps leaves dry and clean, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to generate more energy to produce large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhe tseɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Extra small shoots, called suckers, steal water and soil nutrients away from the main mother plant. Pruning them so only one or two healthy shoots remain ensures the main plantain tree receives enough nourishment to yield a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso agbo ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if my crop seedlings are establishing well in the first two weeks after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Look for vibrant green leaves, upright stems, and new leaf buds. If seedlings do not wilt during the sunniest part of the day after two weeks, it means their root system is successfully taking hold in the soil.
ga: Taomɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ, kɛ fɔfɔi heei ni etse. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbooo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ema shi.

english: Why is the first month after planting so critical for my crops' survival?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ni nyiɛɔ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha dumɔwui lɛ ashihilɛ?

english: The first month is when young plants develop their tender root systems and initial leaves. During this period, they are most vulnerable to weeds, pests, and dry spells, so close care determines their long-term growth and yield.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ ji be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ baai lɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Amɛji mɛi ni jwɛi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui fe fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔkwɛmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa baatsɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli dalɛ kɛ nitsumɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are mature enough to survive a short dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli?

english: Once crops reach about three to four weeks of growth and develop deeper root systems, they can access moisture deeper in the soil and handle a few days without rain much better than newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Enɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ daa yɛ aaafee otsii etɛ loo ejwɛ mli ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ. Ni etsuɔ ​​gbii fioo komɛi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ.

english: What stage of crop growth requires the most water and daily attention from me?
ga: Mɛɛ tso lɛ dalɛ fã biɔ nu kɛ mijwɛŋmɔ fe fɛɛ daa gbi?

english: The early seedling stage (first few weeks) and the flowering stage require the most water, as root establishment and seed formation depend heavily on consistent soil moisture.
ga: dumɔwui lɛ ashishijee be Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo (klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo) kɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee be lɛ biɔ nu fe fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ waa.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow two weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves early in growth usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overwatering. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea around two to three weeks after germination helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni daa oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my young seedlings to fall over and die before they reach one month old?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miigboi dani amɛye nyɔŋ kome?

english: Seedlings often collapse due to 'damping-off' disease, caused by soil fungi in overly wet soil, or cutworms severing the tender stems at ground level.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hela hewɔ. ‘Damping’, ni sũ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli edɔ tsɔ loo ni afolɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: How do crops change their appearance when they have recovered from transplanting or stress?
ga: Te tsei lɛ baatsake amɛhefɛo amɛha tɛŋŋ beni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni atsake amɛ loo haomɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops recover, their leaves change from dull or drooping to firm and bright green, and you will notice quick new stem growth within a few days.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ he wa lɛ, baai lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Ni obaana tso lɛ yibii heei ni miida oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: How soon after my crops sprout should I start applying fertilizer?
ga: Beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, te esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii awomɔ oya tɛŋŋ?

english: Most crops like maize respond best when the first top-dressing fertilizer is applied around two weeks after germination, once roots are strong enough to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nɔ aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni amɛje kpo lɛ. Beni shishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Does performing traditional customs or farm rituals actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani kusum nifeemɔi loo kusumii ni afeɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛnyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Traditional customs help bring the community together for shared labor and cultural respect, but crop growth itself relies on physical factors like good soil, water, sunlight, and proper pest management.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi yeɔ ebuaa akutsei lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa koni amɛja nitsumɔ ni amɛbu kusum. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ damɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, hulu la kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to weed around my crops when they are only two weeks old?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaawo jwɛi abɔle he? Miŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛye otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, but you must weed gently by hand or with a small tool, as shallow seedling roots can easily be damaged if you dig too close to the stem.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe baahia ni okɛ oniji loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko atsu nii blɛoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite oya kɛji otsi ohe kɛbɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ.

english: Officer, why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen. The plant moves its remaining nutrients to the newer leaves at the top to stay alive, which tells you the soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to hide inside the shoots of my corn plants and eat holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ayiteŋ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. The moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat the growing center of the plant. Spraying early with recommended insecticides or applying neem extracts can help protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads easily in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches and weeds allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, reducing fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɔ́, kɛ fɔ́ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji kɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ koni eha hulutsoo be kroko lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Ha fungal lɛ dalɛ aba shi

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when they suffer heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. When the plant feels stressed, it sheds flowers to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, beni tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ ko lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn hard like rock whenever the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaje shishi lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter such as compost or decomposed crop leaves. Adding manure and keeping the soil covered with mulch helps retain moisture and keeps the ground soft and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ahe baai ni fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it bad if I plant three or four maize seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: Yes, planting too many seeds in one spot causes the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition results in thin, weak stems and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii waa loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants have tall leaves and thick stems but very tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai kakadaji kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil or planting in overly wet conditions causes cassava to send all its energy to growing top leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ni edaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ haa ŋmei kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant peppers on the exact same piece of land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same diseases and insects. Planting them in the same spot back-to-back lets soil pests multiply and attack your new crop much faster.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli, ni helai kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ yeɔ amɛ. Amɛdumɔ yɛ he kome ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei oya kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and drop off during the dry Harmattan winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during hot, dry weather is the plant's natural way of saving water to survive the drought. Once the rains return, the cassava plant will sprout fresh leaves and grow normally.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hɔmɔ mli lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Kasava tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt very quickly to local soil and draw up water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food away from your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hu shwieɔ shi oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees around my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and retain moisture in the soil, keeping the young cocoa safe until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast around my young cocoa trees compared to older farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mihe lɛ? Mikookoo tsei lɛ darako kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji momo lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees do not have big leaves yet to block the sun, so sunlight directly hits the soil and causes weeds to sprout quickly. Clearing weeds regularly keeps them from stealing food and water from your young crops.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɛ baai wuji ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick and need farm medicine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni ehe miihia ni aná ŋmɔ mli tsofa?

english: Crops show sickness through signs like yellowing leaves, dark spots, holes from pests, or stunted growth. When you see these signs early, applying the right recommended farm medicine or treatment prevents the sickness from destroying the whole farm.
ga: Tsei jieɔ hela he okadii kɛtsɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, he ni edɔ, kɛ bu ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. loo shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Kɛji ona okadii nɛɛ mra Tsofai loo tsamɔi ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akafite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by lack of nutrients, dry weather, or insect attacks. Applying proper crop protection treatments and keeping the soil moist helps the tree hold its flowers to produce healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: This blackening is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal rot that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air flow through the farm, which stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni ji black pod lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni fiteɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do some of my cocoa leaves turn yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the cocoa tree is lacking essential nutrients from the soil or isn't getting enough water. Adding organic manure or proper fertilizers around the root zone helps restore the deep green color and keeps the tree productive.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Organic fertilizer loo fertilizer ni sa ni akɛfataa he lɛ shishifã lɛ haa tso lɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over when the plantain bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbee shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots, so the heavy weight of a maturing bunch can easily pull the whole tree down. You should support the tree by propping it up with a strong wooden pole or bamboo fork under the bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji ni tsii baanyɛ agbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi oya. Esa akɛ okɛ tso ni wa loo ŋmei fɔk ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ shishi lɛ aye abua tso lɛ.

english: Why do so many small plantain shoots sprout around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii No hewɔ lɛ Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe. Mi plantain titri lɛ?

english: These small shoots are called suckers, and if too many grow at once, they steal food from the main tree. Leaving only one or two strong shoots and cutting back the rest helps the main tree produce larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ofo nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa so it weighs more?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo koni efee nɔ ni tsii?

english: Cocoa is fully ripe when the pod turns bright yellow or deep orange. Harvesting pods at full maturity ensures the beans inside are fully developed, juicy, and yield maximum weight when dried.
ga: Cocoa lɛ eshɛ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. Ni aaakpã ŋmeii lɛ amli beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, amɛmli nu ni amɛhaa muji ni fe fɛɛ kɛji amɛgbi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and dry out during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up to reduce water loss when the weather is very hot. Placing dry leaves or grass as mulch around the base of the plantain keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the ground.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi fɔ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant millet together with other crops on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting millet alongside crops like legumes or cassava helps maximize your land, protects the soil from drying out, and reduces the risk of losing all your harvest if one crop fails.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ohaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo. Tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. ni ebaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baafite kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite lɛ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I just mix all my different grain seeds together and scatter them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi futuɔ? Amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee ekome ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: When you scatter mixed seeds randomly, crops grow too close together and fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which makes the plants weak and reduces your final yield.
ga: Kɛji ojara dumɔwui ni efutu lɛ trukaa Tsei lɛ daa ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: What do nutrients like zinc and iron actually do for my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii tamɔ zinc kɛ iron yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Zinc and iron are essential minerals that help crops create green, healthy leaves, produce strong seeds, and convert sunlight into plant food so they can yield well.
ga: Zinc kɛ dade ji nibii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Feemɔ dumɔwui ni mli wa ni otsake hulu la lɛ owo tsei aniyenii mli koni ewo yibii kpakpai

english: How do my crops take up minerals like iron and zinc from the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jieɔ nibii tamɔ dade kɛ zinc kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Crops use their roots to drink in nutrients dissolved in soil water. Keeping organic matter like mulch or compost in your soil helps hold moisture so roots can easily absorb these minerals.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ nu mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nɛkɛ sũ mli nibii nɛɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops are lacking important nutrients like iron or zinc?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ dade loo zinc bɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: When plants lack micronutrients like iron or zinc, their young leaves usually turn pale or yellow between the green veins, and overall plant growth becomes stunted.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii bibii tamɔ dade loo zinc lɛ Bei pii lɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ. ni tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need soil rich in minerals to produce good pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mineral eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require large amounts of soil minerals to build healthy flowers and heavy pods. Rich, fertile soil ensures the trees stay productive for many years.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia mineral babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni baa nii babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii afii babaoo.

english: Why do young cocoa plants dry up and die when planted under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that burn and dry out quickly in full sunshine. They need temporary shade, like plantains, to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does millet survive dry spells better than maize on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Millet has deep, efficient roots and a natural structure that slows down water loss, allowing it to stay green and produce food even when rainfall is very low.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ni haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ewoɔ niyenii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ faaa kwraa po.

english: Is it safe for me to mix different types of fertilizers together before applying them to my soil?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi baafutu? kɛfata he dani akɛwo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Some fertilizers can be safely mixed right before application, but mixing incompatible ones can cause chemical reactions that destroy the nutrients or burn your plant roots.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi afutu mli shweshweeshwe dani akɛwo mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eshãa tsei shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: How does growing legumes alongside grain crops help keep my soil healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally feeding neighboring grain crops like millet without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells as a survival trick to reduce water loss. The plant is not dying; it goes dormant to protect itself and will shoot out fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni akɛba nu ni laajeɔ lɛ shi. Tso lɛ gbooo, eyaa wɔɔhe koni ebu ehe. ni ebaajie baai eŋɔli heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun is hot at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during heat waves to shrink the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside its leaves and prevent itself from drying out during the hottest hours.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ dɔlɛ be mli koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ebaa lɛ mli ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant sheds it to save energy rather than wasting resources on fruit that cannot grow.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔ Kɛ́ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi Tsei lɛ jieɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ aduawai ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants take so much longer to bear fruit when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require full, direct sunlight to manufacture the large amount of food energy needed for fruiting. Under heavy shade, the plant uses all its energy just trying to grow taller to reach light, delaying bunch development.
ga: Hulu la he miihia plantains tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ aba. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛkɛ ni eya ŋwɛi koni ená la lɛ. Enɛ baaha kuu lɛ shweremɔ asɛɛ afo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build chlorophyll, which gives leaves their deep green color and fuels healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my sweet potato roots coming out thin and stringy instead of fat and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes produce thin roots if the soil contains too much nitrogen or is packed too hard. Excess nitrogen tricks the plant into growing big leaves and long vines instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Sweet potato baaná shishifãi bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ lakaa tsei koni amɛná baai wuji kɛ wain tsei kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and stake my yam vines on wooden poles for them to grow big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei anɔ koni bulbs agboi lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to spread its leaves high in the sun to produce plant food. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to full light while protecting them from soil rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná tsei niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Amɛhaa enine shɛɔ la fɛɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ sũ lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but the pollinated flower stem (called a peg) bends downward and burrows into the dirt. The actual nut develops underground in darkness where moisture levels are stable.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Akɛ ŋmeii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs) lɛ shwieɔ shi ni afoɔ amɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nuts lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ duŋ mli he ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi daa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves get wrinkled and curled up, making the whole bush look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Ha jwɛi muu lɛ fɛɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or spreading a virus. The leaf tissue collapses as sap is lost, causing the wrinkled appearance.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Baai lɛ amli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu lɛ mli nu lɛ laaje. kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree as soon as the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa pɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that multiplies rapidly in cool, humid, and rainy weather. Splashing rain carries the fungal spores onto wet pods, where they quickly infect and destroy the beans inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ woɔ fungal spores kɛyaa pods ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Amɛheɔ hela oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth, or that excess water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay short and refuse to grow bigger after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaada agbo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants become stunted when the ground is too hard for roots to expand, when soil nutrients are low, or when microscopic pests in the soil damage the root system.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high daytime temperatures or sudden changes from dry soil to heavy watering.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. aloo tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa nu babaoo nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically the Fall Armyworm, a pest that prefers to hide and feed on the soft, young leaves developing inside the center funnel of corn plants.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ titri nɔ lɛ, enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ni eye baai bibii ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in a field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight; they need nurse plants like plantains to provide shade and trap humidity while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛnɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛná hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant cassava on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously removes the same nutrients from the soil repeatedly without giving the earth time to recover, causing the land to lose its fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ nii dɔŋŋ.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops reduce my final yield?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha minaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your crops, effectively starving your plants and slowing their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants lose moisture quickly through their leaves in hot sun; drooping is a natural defense mechanism to reduce exposure and conserve water until the air cools down.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ shi ni akɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell; if seeds germinate and the dry weather returns, the delicate young sprouts will dry out and die before regular rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food nutrient that gives plants their green strength. This often happens if the soil lacks nutrients or if heavy rains have washed the fertilizer deep beyond the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize in the same field cause them to fight for plant food?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baadu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha tsei niyenii?

english: No, they actually support each other. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which helps feed the neighboring maize and makes the soil richer.
ga: Dabi, amɛfiɔ amɛhe sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When temperatures get too high during hot afternoon sun or dry spells, the plant drops its blossoms to save water and energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my cassava plants when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Cassava tso lɛ beni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly at first and need maximum sunlight and soil moisture. Weeds grow much faster and will steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, leaving your young cassava stunted.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛbiɔ hulu la babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, o-cassava bibioo lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop most of their flowers during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers during dry spells and Harmattan winds to protect themselves from losing precious water. They conserve their energy until steady rains return so they can successfully grow pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu ni jara wa lɛ akafite amɛ. Amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni anyɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the undersides of the leaves. It can also be caused by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips miinu nu kɛjɛ baa lɛ shishi. Tse mli helai ni koolooi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: Why are holes appearing in the leaves of my young cabbage crops overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji je kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars or beetles that feed on tender leaves during the cool hours of the night to avoid daytime heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa kaabeji baai amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the plants to compete fiercely with each other for space, light, water, and nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems that produce very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná he ko, la, nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be a false start followed by weeks of hot, dry weather. If the soil dries out before the seeds establish deep roots, the seedlings will scorch and die.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii komɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ dani dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to swell the tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on tall sticks keeps the leaves exposed to sun and prevents diseases caused by damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ aba. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛbaa lɛ baa.

english: Maize signals it is fully mature when the outer leaves turn brown and dry, and a small black layer forms at the tip where the kernel attaches to the cob, showing that the plant has stopped feeding the grains.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ akɛ edara kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Efeɔ yɛ naagbee he ni dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa edumɔwui lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Why do my ripe cowpea pods burst open on their own while still standing on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni amɛdamɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: As cowpea pods dry out, the outer skin loses water and tightens unevenly. Once fully dry, the pod snaps open naturally to scatter its seeds, which is the plant's natural way of reproducing before you harvest it.
ga: Kɛji tsina ŋmeii lɛ egbi lɛ, hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji egbi kwraa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baajara mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbɛ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii dani okpaa amɛ.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I leave them in the ground for too long without harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa amɛ?

english: If cassava stays in the ground too long after reaching maturity, the tubers lose their starch and turn tough, woody, and fibrous, making them poor for eating and more likely to rot underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ tso kɛ tsɔne. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ aye amɛ, ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn soft and dark on the tree if I leave them unharvested for extra weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛji mishi lɛ ni akpaaa otsii babaoo

english: Overripe cocoa pods lose their thick protective outer skin, making it easy for fungal diseases like black pod and hungry insects to break in and ruin the beans inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewolo ni mli tse ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji kɛ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛfite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my rice grains drop to the ground on their own if I delay harvesting my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji mikpa miŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally weaken the joint connecting each grain to the stem once the seeds mature. If you wait too long, wind or simple movement makes the ripe grains drop off, a process called seed shattering.
ga: Omɔ tsei haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ omɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ateŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ loo nyiɛmɔ fioo ko pɛ baaha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbo. Atsɛɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ akɛ dumɔwui amlijaa.

english: Why do my mature tomatoes soften and spoil so fast if I leave them attached to the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛji mishi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Ripe tomatoes naturally produce a gas called ethylene that speeds up the softening of their flesh. Leaving ripe fruit on the branch keeps this process going until the fruit breaks down completely.
ga: Tomato ni egbɔ lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene, ni haa loo lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya. Kɛ́ ashi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaya nɔ afee nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ kɛyashi aduawai lɛ baafite kwraa.

english: Why do mature crops attract so many pests if left unharvested on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni eda lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni akpaaa amɛ nii lɛ?

english: As crops ripen, they release stronger sweet scents and soft plant tissue, which acts as a natural signal to insects and birds that an easy, nutrient-rich meal is available.
ga: Be ni tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, amɛ jieɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni naa wa kɛ tso fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kpo. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli okadi kɛhaa kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi akɛ niyenii ni afee lɛ mlɛo, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do groundnut seeds start sprouting inside the soil if I do not harvest them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii dumɔwui jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: Once groundnuts reach full maturity, exposure to warm, moist soil tricks the mature seeds into breaking their resting period and growing new roots right inside the pod.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛdara lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ lakaa dumɔwui ni eda lɛ koni amɛfo amɛhe ni amɛwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfee shishifãi heei yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my mature maize cobs turn moldy if rain falls on them before I get to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ dani mikpa amɛ?

english: Dry husks on mature maize hold onto rainwater like a wet cloth, creating a warm, damp space where fungal spores grow quickly and turn the grain moldy.
ga: Abele ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nu tamɔ mama ni efɔ. Enɛ haa he ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Fungal spores lɛ daa oya ni ehaa ŋmãa yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my mature yam tubers spoil underwater if heavy rain floods my farm right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei ni eda lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu shishi kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant parts that need air in the soil to stay alive. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen, causing the tuber tissue to suffocate and rot rapidly.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso lɛ fãi ni hiɛ ka ni he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa tuber fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Can crops like cassava or sweet potato really be turned into flour to bake bread like wheat does?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ afee ashikishaŋ ni akɛshã blodo tamɔ ŋmaa?

english: Yes, cassava and sweet potatoes can be peeled, dried, and ground into fine flour. Mixing this local flour with regular flour allows you to bake bread and pastries using crops grown right here on Ghanaian soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ ajie ŋmei kɛ ŋmei, agbi, ni agbɛlɛ ni afee ashikishaŋ fɛfɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli ashikishaŋ nɛɛ futu daa ashikishaŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ nɔ biɛ lɛ shãa blodoo kɛ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli.

english: Why does wheat struggle to grow in Ghana while our local crops like cassava and yams grow so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ Ghana lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa.

english: Wheat requires cool, temperate weather that we do not have in Ghana. Cassava and yams are native tropical crops naturally built to thrive in our warm weather and local soil conditions.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni wɔbɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ he miihia ŋmaa. Cassava kɛ sweet potatoes ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shikpɔji anɔ ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use orange-fleshed sweet potatoes for baking food products just like regular white sweet potatoes?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Yes, orange-fleshed sweet potatoes grow well in our soil and can be processed into flour or puree for baking, adding extra vitamin A and a pleasant natural sweetness to local bread and snacks.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni abaanyɛ afee lɛ ashikishaŋ loo puree kɛha shãa. Ekɛ vitamin A kroko fataa he ni ehaa maŋ lɛ mli blodoi kɛ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay green and keep growing even during dry periods with little rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni edaa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli po ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a naturally drought-tolerant crop. It drops some leaves to conserve water and relies on the moisture stored in its underground roots to survive dry spells.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Ekɛ ebaai lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he, ni ekɛ ehe fɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting leaves in the shed even when they are not in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ?

english: Yams are living tubers with a natural biological clock. When the rainy season approaches, the stored starch in the yam signals it to sprout and grow a new vine, even without soil or light.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bashɛ Starch ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sweet potatoes amli lɛ feɔ amɛ okadi akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ wain tsei heei. Kɛ́ sũ loo la bɛ jɛmɛ po

english: What changes inside my maize crop as it turns from fresh green ears to dry yellow stalks?
ga: Mɛɛ tsakemɔi baa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛ́ etsake kɛjɛ toi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmãa ni egbi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: As maize matures, the plant moves energy into the seeds, turning simple sugars into hard starch. The green plant naturally dries out so the seeds can be stored safely as dry grain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ tsiɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa dumɔwu lɛ mli. ni otsake sugars ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ owo ashikishaŋ ni wa mli Tsei eŋɔli ni egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni anyɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato shweshweeshwe akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi.

english: Why do my cassava roots go bad within just two or three days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni atsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots lose their skin protection and react quickly with air. This causes internal blue-black streaking and rot unless the tubers are processed or submerged in water within 48 hours.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛhewolo nɔ hebuu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ bluu-diŋŋ mligbɛ ni fiteɔ baa, ja atsu ŋmeii lɛ ahe nii loo awo amɛ nu mli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.

english: How does sun-drying my harvested crops help protect them from rotting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ migbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he?

english: Bacteria and fungi need water to grow and cause rot. Drying crops like cassava, maize, or peppers in the hot sun removes moisture, keeping the food safe to store for many months.
ga: Muawai kɛ ŋmeii taoɔ nu koni amɛdara ni amɛgboi. Nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. ni ehaa akɛ niyenii toɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do green plantains spoil so quickly if I leave them to turn yellow on the tree before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji miha amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Leaving plantains on the tree until they turn yellow allows the natural starches to fully convert into soft sugars, making the fruit ripen very fast and attract insects. Harvesting green gives you much more time to transport and process them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi plantain lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kwraa. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ oya waa, ni egbalaa kooloi bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ o-greens lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná be babaoo ni okɛfã gbɛ ni okɛtsu nii.

english: How does processing my fresh raw cassava into dry flour benefit me compared to selling raw tubers directly?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei hee ni afee lɛ ashikishaŋ ni egbi lɛ he kɛha mi kɛ akɛto ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he?

english: Raw tubers spoil quickly and force you to sell at low market prices. Converting raw cassava into flour prevents spoilage, extends shelf life, and allows you to make higher profits by selling to bakers and processors year-round.
ga: Tubers ni ahoko lɛ fiteɔ oya ni enyɛɔ onɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ashikishaŋ tsake cassava ni ahoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ fitemɔ naa. Extend shelf life Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛtsɔ nihɔɔmɔ ni okɛhaa aboloofeelɔi kɛ mɛi ni feɔ aboloo lɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil so quickly when I store it inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Harvested maize spoils quickly if it is not dried completely before storage because leftover moisture allows mold to grow and attracts insects that eat the grains.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ kwraa dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ adara ni egbala kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to put into storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto?

english: You can test if maize is dry by pushing your thumbnail into a grain; if the grain is hard and leaves no dent, or if it makes a sharp cracking sound when bitten, it is ready for storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbi kɛtsɔ mfoniri bibioo ko ni oootsi awo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii Aloo kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ lɛ gbee ko baa ni efee klalo akɛ abaabua naa.

english: Why do my crops rot if they are piled directly on the ground or against walls inside a storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ato shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ loo akɛkpɛtɛ gbogbo he yɛ nitoohe ko mli lɛ?

english: Dried crops act like sponges and draw moisture directly from damp ground or concrete walls, which creates a wet environment where rot and mold thrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ loo kɔnkrit gbogboi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why should I dry my harvested grains on raised platforms instead of on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ kpoku ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised platforms allow air to flow underneath and around the grains, which dries them faster and keeps them safe from ground moisture, dirt, and crawling pests.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ shishi kɛ ehe, ni no haa egbiɔ oya, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, muji, kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ eyaaa mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers suggest planting a small trial area before trying a new crop on my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu he bibioo ko ni akaa akwɛɔ dani aka akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: A small trial plot lets you observe how a new crop behaves under your local soil and rain conditions without risking your whole farm's income if the crop fails.
ga: small experiment plan Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei feɔ amɛnii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi amli. ni okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shika fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii.

english: How can I observe if a crop variety is doing well during a short dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli?

english: A healthy crop variety will keep its leaves open and green during hot days, while a weaker variety will roll up its leaves, turn yellow, or wilt quickly.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baafo amɛbaai lɛ amli. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbo oya

english: What should I look out for when testing a new maize seed on my land?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mika ŋmãa dumɔwui heei mikwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Watch how fast the seed germinates, how strong the stems grow against wind, and whether the maize cobs fill up completely with healthy grains.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Te tso lɛ mli wa ha tɛŋŋ koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ? Ni ani ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eyi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli obɔ?
