english: What causes small holes and fine powder to appear in my stored grains?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii? Ni ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa ko je kpo yɛ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ mli.

english: The holes and powder are caused by small insects called weevils that burrow into the dried grains to feed and lay their eggs inside.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu kɛ powda baa. Amɛfoɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛna niyenii ni amɛwoɔ wɔji yɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to sort out damaged or broken grains before storing the rest of the harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie dumɔwui ni efite loo ni ekumɔ lɛ amli dani akɛ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ ato lɛ?

english: Damaged grains rot faster and attract pests quickly, which then spread to infect and destroy the healthy grains stored around them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni efite lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai oya. Enɛ baagbɛ hela lɛ eshwa ni efite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato he lɛ. nakai dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why does a grain storehouse need air openings or vents near the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Stored grains naturally release heat and moisture, and air vents let that warm, damp air escape so it does not settle back on the grains and cause mold.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ akabote mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential food crop plants need to grow. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green so the plant can produce strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots mature, the plant stops storing starch in them and begins turning the roots into fibrous wood to support itself. Harvesting on time keeps the tubers soft, heavy, and good for cooking.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmei ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ ni ebɔi eshishifãi lɛ tsakemɔ ewoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli koni ekɛkwɛ ehe. Nikpamɔ yɛ be naa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛtsii ni amɛhi kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden dryness in the soil. Consistent watering during dry spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant seeds closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough food and light to develop large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops if I plant maize on the same farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the ground naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for leaf growth and tuber development. Staking also keeps the foliage away from hot soil and ground pests.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni baai lɛ adara kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ akashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers directs energy into growing big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha oná hewalɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can use them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing normal branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa amɛniji ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that carry plant viruses. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents them from spreading diseases that stunt the crop's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbɛɔ helai ni haa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: What is a certified seed, and why should I plant it instead of saved tubers from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ni awo he odase? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu yɛ bulbs ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Certified seeds are disease-free plant materials grown under controlled conditions by seed specialists. Using them gives your crop a healthy start so you can harvest big, high-quality yams that fetch good prices at the market.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ji tso nibii ni hela bɛ mli ni dumɔwui ahe nilelɔi duɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jara kpakpa baa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ babaoo.

english: How big should my seed yams be when I plant them in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ afee tɛŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Using seed yam pieces that weigh around 500 grams gives the young plant enough stored food and energy to establish strong roots and vines, which leads to a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui bibii ni tsiimɔ aaafee gram 500 tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso bibioo lɛ aná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi kɛ wain tsei ni wa akwɛ̃. Enɛ kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa.

english: Where do extension officers get the clean seed yams that they distribute to us?
ga: Nɛgbɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ náa dumɔwui ni he tse ni amɛha wɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ?

english: Seed producers first plant high-grade parent seeds in special multiplication plots. Once the tubers grow to the right size and pass quality checks, they are distributed to farmers for crop production.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ fɔlɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ hei krɛdɛɛi ni akɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ bulb lɛ eda kɛyashɛ bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mli lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, abaaja aha okwaafoi lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops struggle to give big yams these days if I do not add chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdu sweet potato agbo yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ?

english: Over many years of farming, the soil loses its natural nutrients. Adding fertilizer feeds the soil so your crops get the extra food they need to develop large, heavy tubers.
ga: Okwaayeli afii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa babaoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Is it really necessary to buy farm chemicals when our parents farmed without them in the past?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni wɔhe tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ be mli ni wɔfɔlɔi tsuɔ okwaayeli ni amɛbɛ tsofai nɛɛ?

english: Farming conditions have changed over time, and soils no longer have the natural strength they used to have. Modern inputs like fertilizers and protective chemicals are now needed to help crops yield well.
ga: Okwaayeli shihilɛi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ dɔŋŋ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he Ehe miihia ni aye abua tsei ni amɛná yibii kpakpai.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant good seed yams but choose not to apply any fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kpakpai shi mihala akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko fataaa he?

english: Even healthy seeds cannot produce large yams if the soil lacks nutrients. Without fertilizer, the crop will sprout but may remain small and produce light tubers that are hard to sell.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po nyɛŋ awo sweet potatoes agboi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi ekolɛ ebaafee bibioo ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ waa.

english: Why are agricultural officers asking us to change our old ways of working on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ biɔ ni wɔtsake bɔ ni afeɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔ yɛ blema lɛ?

english: Old methods worked when the soil was naturally rich, but changing weather and tired soils mean those old ways yield less today. Updating your farming methods helps you get higher yields on the same piece of land.
ga: Gbɛ momo lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni miifite Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nakai gbɛi momo lɛ wooo yibii babaoo ŋmɛnɛ. Kɛ́ otsake gbɛi ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oná shika babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Does it matter where exactly on my land I choose to plant my seed yams?
ga: Ani he ni mihala akɛ madu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, planting crops in their recommended soil types and land conditions ensures the seed gets the proper water and drainage it needs to grow properly without rotting.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu kɛ nu ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: How can I ensure the yams I harvest grow large enough to sell easily at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ baafee babaoo bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ mlɛo?

english: Getting large yams requires starting with proper-sized certified seeds and feeding the growing plants with the right fertilizers and protective chemicals throughout the season.
ga: Ni aaaná sweet potatoes agboi lɛ biɔ ni aje shishi kɛ dumɔwui ni dalɛ sa, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ tsofai ni buɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ aha amɛ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Will spending money on farm chemicals and fertilizers bring me more income at harvest time?
ga: Ani shika ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaha maná shika babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Yes, because proper inputs result in larger, healthier tubers. Buyers pay more for big, clean yams, which covers your input costs and increases your total profit.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa yitsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he tse lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni ehaa sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the middle outward, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build green leaves and healthy shoots. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛtee kponɔgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers expand downward and need loose, soft soil to stretch smoothly. If planted in hard or stony soil, the growing tuber hits resistance and bends, so mounding or making deep, loose ridges allows them to grow straight and large.
ga: Sweet potato yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛ nɔ Bulbs ni adu lɛ kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo baakpe ni ebaakumɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ooofee loo ni ooofee lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the farm and water stays in the soil without draining, the roots get choked from lack of oxygen, allowing fungal diseases to attack and rot the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Oxygen bɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa saplings wither and dry up when planted in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally grow under big forest trees. Direct intense sunlight dries out their tender leaves faster than their small roots can suck up water from the ground, causing them to scorch and die without shade plants like plantains.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ agbi oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa baai ni shãa kɛ gbele baa ni tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ shade.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and weak with tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ kɛ toi bibii beni miduɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into growing big cobs, they spend all their energy growing tall to reach for sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛna hulu la.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy wind blows during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the soil surface while bearing heavy bunches of fruit at the top. When the soil becomes soft from rain, the heavy top pulls the shallow roots out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ yɛ nugbɔ hewɔ lɛ Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fã ni tsii lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ja tso fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my garden egg and tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant kɛ tomato ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants often drop flowers during severe hot weather or dry spells to save energy and survive. Extreme heat damages the flower parts so pollination fails, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi. No hewɔ lɛ, pollin lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai efeee.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop as soon as it begins to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft petals that attract pest insects like thrips and pod borers for food. The flowering stage is when the plant is most attractive to pests, so protecting flowers early keeps pods healthy.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers akɛ niyenii. Fɔfɔi be lɛ ji be ni tsei lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ fe fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, bu fɔfɔi ahe mra. Ebaaye ebua ni pods lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my pepper plants even after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to quick growth in poor conditions, whereas pepper plants take time to establish. Weeds quickly steal sunlight and soil food before crop roots can spread out.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be he miihia pepper tsei koni amɛto amɛhe shi. Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes start growing fresh shoots even when stored indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ amɛ toɔ shĩa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes are living plant stems designed to survive dry seasons. Warm conditions inside storage signal to the potato that it is time to wake up and produce shoots, which can be delayed by keeping them cool and dark.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni afee koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ asɛɛ afo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in an open field under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and easily damaged by intense direct sunlight and heat. They require shade crops like plantains or bananas to cover them and keep the soil moist while they build strong roots during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni wa amɛma shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without them killing each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni migbeee mihe?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within 3 to 4 months, leaving the field clear and nutrients available for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmãa ni daa blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow before the crop is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor water drainage. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves their healthy green color back and improves yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the field. Rotating different types of crops restores soil richness naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside our main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ ni wɔdu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ wɔŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for other crops planted in the same field.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit because of extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently damp and protecting plants from harsh winds helps save the blooms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi bibii ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he lɛ bɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: How does the armyworm pest manage to destroy my entire maize farm so quickly?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni cutworm ŋmeii lɛ afite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ oya?

english: Fall armyworms feed inside the central funnel or shoot of young maize plants during the night and cool hours, eating the growing tip and leaves before the plant can mature and produce corn ears.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ loo ŋshɔŋ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi amli gbɛkɛ kɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ dani tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ená ŋmãa toi.

english: Why do weeds make my yam tubers grow small and thin under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miidara bibii ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from the yam plants. Without enough nutrients, the yam vine cannot produce enough energy to expand the tuber underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sweet potato tsei amli. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Nakai nɔŋŋ hu, sweet potato wain tsei nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wither when I pour too much water on the soil during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water floods the small air pockets in the soil, preventing plant roots from breathing oxygen. Additionally, hot water around root zones can stress or burn the plant, causing it to wilt.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ loo eshã amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ agbi.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stalk, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: How can I tell if a disease or pest is attacking my cocoa farm before all my trees get ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko miitutua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ dani akpata tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: You can spot early trouble by checking your trees regularly for strange signs like yellowing or twisted leaves, swollen branches, dark patches rotting on the cocoa pods, or holes in the bark. Catching these signs early helps stop the disease from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona naagbai mra. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ otsei lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ daa kɛha okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ tamɔ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei niji ni efuu, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo bu yɛ tso lɛ mli Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mra Ye obua ni hela akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, overly shady, and wet conditions. Clearing tall weeds, pruning thick branches to let in sunlight, and harvesting ripe pods quickly help prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Shadow kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ, jwɛi shwiemɔ fa. Nibii ni afoɔ ni mli tse koni hulu lɛ ashɛ Ni ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: Where do crop pests go during the dry season, and why do they return so quickly when the rains start?
ga: Nɛgbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Ni mɛni hewɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ oya kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: During the dry season, pests hide inside tree bark, fallen leaves, or nearby bush weeds to survive. Once the rains return and fresh leaves grow, the pests come out of hiding to feed and multiply rapidly on your crops.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. baai ni egbee shi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ni baai heei kwɛ̃ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ he ni amɛtee lɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii ni amɛshwere oya yɛ onibii amli.

english: Why are the chemical medicines I buy for spraying my cocoa not working to kill the pests on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mihe koni mikɛshwie kookoo nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbemɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pest medicines may fail if they are mixed with the wrong amount of water, applied at the wrong time of day, washed away by rain, or if the pests in your area have built up resistance to that specific chemical brand over time.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni esaaa futu mli. Gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa ni nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ebɔi nakai tsofa lɛ he hewalɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: How do I know if an agrochemical company or pest medicine is approved and safe to use on my crops in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji agrochemical loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ahe nitsumɔhe ko ekpɛlɛ nɔ ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Always look for products approved by the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) or the Ministry of Food and Agriculture, and buy directly from licensed agro-dealers rather than uncertified sellers on the street.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ nibii ni Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) loo Niyenii kɛ Okwaayeli He Nitsumɔhe lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ. ni ohé tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ lɛ adɛŋ Moŋ lɛ, ohe kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni he esaaa ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Is it good to spray pest medicine on my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashɛrɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Spraying right before a heavy downpour washes the chemical off the plants before it can work, wasting your money. It is best to spray early in the morning when the rain has cleared and the plants are dry enough to absorb the medicine.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni afɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ahe dani amɛtsu amɛnitsumɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi beni nugbɔ lɛ eho ni tsei lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ tsofa lɛ.

english: What should I do right away if I notice one of my cocoa trees showing signs of a dangerous disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ eko miitsɔɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara?

english: For serious viral diseases like Swollen Shoot, you should cut down and safely remove the infected tree along with surrounding contact trees to prevent the virus from spreading through roots or insects to healthy parts of your farm.
ga: Kɛha helai ni mli wa ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni okɛ amɛ ashwie shweshweeshwe koni hela lɛ akatsɔ shishifãi loo kooloi amli kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers keep advising us to cut extra branches from our mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni fata kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing fresh air and sunlight to reach the inner tree. Sunlight kills harmful fungal spores and helps the tree direct its strength into producing larger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la ashɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Hulu la gbeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does keeping my farm clean from weeds protect my crops from diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tse kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe?

english: Weeds steal nutrients and water from your crops, making the trees weak and easy targets for sickness. Tall weeds also trap damp air around the base of your trees, creating the perfect damp environment for diseases to grow.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni efeɔ nɔ ni helai baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishi, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni baa lɛ baa.

english: If a disease destroys my cocoa farm and I have to replant, how long will it take for new trees to start bearing fruit?
ga: Ni kɛji hela kpata mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ ni ehe bahia ni madu ekoŋŋ hu? Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani tso hee ko baabɔi yibiiwoo?

english: With modern hybrid cocoa varieties, new trees usually start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years, provided they are given good shade from plantains and proper care while they are young.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid henɔi lɛ amli lɛ, bei pii lɛ tsei heei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná hulutsoo kpakpa kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During peak afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. Drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing leaf exposure to the hot sun to save moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa baa lɛ shi yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How can I keep my young crops from dying when the sun and heat become too intense during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mitsei bibii lɛ akagboi beni hulu kɛ dɔlɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can cover the bare soil around the plants with dried grass or leaves (mulching). This keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and protects the young root system from extreme soil heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni ebuɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he.

english: Plants with too little water will wilt, turn brown, and feel dry to the touch. Plants getting too much water will turn yellow, look soft or limpy, and their roots may rot because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air.
ga: Tsei ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbi. etsɔ blɔfo ni enuɔ he akɛ egbi kɛji eta ehe Tsei ni nu babaoo baaná lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo loo egbɔjɔ Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do some crops like cabbage need water every day, while cassava can survive long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ kaabii, he hiaa nu daa gbi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Crops have different root systems and leaf types. Vegetables like cabbage have shallow roots and large leaves that lose water rapidly, while cassava has deep storage roots that reach far underground to collect and save water.
ga: Tsei yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai srɔtoi. Aduawai tamɔ kaabe yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ekɛbua nu naa ni ekɛto.

english: Should I place fertilizer directly around each individual plant or just scatter it across the whole field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso fɛɛ tso he tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛja yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer in a small ring around each individual plant ensures that every crop gets its own full portion of nutrients without feeding nearby weeds or wasting fertilizer on empty soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli Yɛ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ, enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee loo efiteee ŋmɔ mli nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ.

english: How do I make sure I am giving each plant the right amount of fertilizer so I do not burn them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa miiha tso fɛɛ tso? Bɔni afee ni mikashã.

english: Using a fixed measurement, like a specific bottle cap for each plant, guarantees that every single crop gets an equal portion. Giving a plant too much concentrated fertilizer at once pulls water out of the roots and burns them.
ga: Kɛtsɔ susumɔ ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, tamɔ tɔ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ kɛha tso fɛɛ tso. Ehaa nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nine shɛɔ shika ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji babaoo ha tsei yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã amɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice to throw a handful of seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni fa fioo ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ bu kome mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, the crowded plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak crops that yield very little harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend nursing seeds in individual plastic bags before moving them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ helatsɛmɛi dumɔwui awo plastic kotokui srɔtoi amli dani akɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursing seeds individually gives each seedling its own protected space and root room. When transplanting, the root ball remains intact inside its soil portion, preventing transplant shock and root damage.
ga: Dumɔwui akusum haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa he ni abuɔ he kɛ shishifãi ahe. Be ni esa akɛ adu Shishifã bɔɔlu lɛ baahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã lɛ mli. Etsiɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and skinny with pale leaves instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together or under dense tree shade, they stretch upward quickly to search for sunlight. This causes them to become tall, thin, and weak because they lack enough light to build strong stems.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ daraa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛyɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa yɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee tsei ni wa lɛ hewɔ.

english: What happens to my crop roots when rainwater sits flooded on the farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni baa mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe and absorb nutrients. When water sits flooded for days, it displaces soil air, causing roots to suffocate, turn black, and rot.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛnu niyenii mli hewalɛ. Beni nu afua lɛ hi shi gbii babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye esɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need protection from direct sunlight because harsh sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains provides a living canopy that protects them until they are mature and strong enough.
ga: Esa akɛ abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Not all flowers get pollinated by beneficial tiny insects like midges, and cocoa trees will naturally drop excess flowers if they lack sufficient soil nutrients or water to support full pod development.
ga: Jeee fɔfɔi fɛɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli. Tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midge kɛ cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua pod lɛ shweremɔ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives and spreads rapidly in cold, wet, humid conditions where air cannot flow freely through overgrown branches.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni edara fe nine lɛ anɔ atsɔ mli oya lɛ.

english: Will planting my cocoa trees very close together give me a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close causes trees to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak trees, lower overall yields, and higher spread of diseases.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ ba shi ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu tee hiɛ

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, steal vital energy, water, and nutrients away from the main trunk and branches that actually produce the cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ juɔ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri kɛ niji ni feɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer or if they are just suffering from lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu kɛkɛ faaa amɛ?

english: Water-stressed trees wilts quickly during hot afternoons but recover at night, whereas nutrient-deficient trees show pale or yellow leaves and slow growth even when the soil is damp.
ga: Tsei ni nu efo mli lɛ baagboi oya yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaatsa ehe yɛ gbɛkɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni niyenii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ baa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do tiny insects cause the leaves on my young cocoa branches to curl up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii haa mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: These are pests like mirids (capsids) that suck sap from young shoots and pods, injecting toxic saliva that destroys plant tissue and stunts tree growth.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tso lɛ fãji ni tsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressively absorbs moisture and nutrients from the topsoil, leaving young cocoa seedlings starved of food and water.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival mechanism that helps the cocoa tree reduce water loss through leaf evaporation during severe dry periods.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to burn the weeds I cut down or leave them on the soil around my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mifo lɛ loo mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle kooko tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the ground acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, traps moisture during dry spells, and naturally breaks down into food for the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid planting many maize seeds in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni miduɔ yɛ bu kome mli pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ he?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni abele ŋmeii lɛ hu daraaa kwraa.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, keeping them healthy and maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ha amɛná hewalɛ ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the heavy soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without draining away. Excess water suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi to attack and decay them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when tiny insects fail to pollinate the blossoms to trigger fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen koni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaf undersides, or transferring a crop virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai eshwaa

english: Why are my crop leaves chewed up at night even though I see no insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni Ni minaaa kooloi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain crop pests, like cutworms and armyworms, hide underground or under plant debris during the hot day to protect themselves, coming out only in the cool night to eat your crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui komɛi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Okɛ ohe awo shikpɔŋ shishi loo tsei amli ŋmeii ashishi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni obu ohe. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli pɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest every season when I plant maize on the same plot repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa bibioo daa be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every year consumes the exact same nutrients over and over, while also allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni abaadu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baabi niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young crops have tiny root systems. If weeds grow next to them early on, the weeds will steal the soil water, fertilizer, and sunlight before the crop seedlings can grow strong.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifã bibioo ko. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi ekome kɛjɛ shishijee Jwɛi lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la dani dumɔwui lɛ daa waa.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says my soil is too acidic?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ?

english: Acidic soil means your soil has become too sour for crops. When soil is too sour, plant roots get locked up and cannot feed on the nutrients in the ground, causing small crops and pale leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering because the soil is too sour?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Crops growing in sour soil often stay small, grow slowly, and show yellow leaves or reddish-purple edges on their leaves because they cannot draw up plant food from the earth.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ bibii, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛhe ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does it mean to make my soil neutral, and why is that good for crops like pepper and maize?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ ni afee lɛ neutral lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Neutral soil is neither too sour nor too bitter. It creates the perfect sweet spot where roots can easily drink water and absorb all nutrients for a heavy harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hegbɛ, ni jeee nɔ ni mli edɔ loo nɔ ni mli edɔ tsɔ. It creates the perfect sweet spot where the roots can easily drink water and absorb all the nutrients for a large harvest.

english: Why should I bother making compost for my farm instead of buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahao yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mafee lɛ he moŋ fe ni mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Compost is rich natural plant food made from farm waste. It improves your soil's power to hold rain water, feeds your crops long-term, and saves you money on expensive store-bought bags.
ga: Kɔmpost ji tso niyenii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi fee. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Feed ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be kakadaŋŋ Ni ehaa okɛ shika baa shi yɛ kotokui ni jara wa ni oheɔ kɛjɛɔ shwapoi amli lɛ mli.

english: What local waste materials around my village can I collect to build a compost heap?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua maŋ lɛ mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ he lɛ anaa koni mafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can use dry grass, maize husks, animal manure, wood ash, fallen leaves, vegetable scraps, and crushed sea shells. Avoid plastics, meat scraps, and diseased plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi, ŋmãa ŋmãa, kooloi ŋmãa, tso ŋmãa, baai ni egbee shi, aduawai amli ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa ni atswa lɛ atsu nii. tsi ohe kɛjɛ plastic loo ni efite kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe

english: Why do I need to add water to my compost pile while it is breaking down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: The tiny invisible organisms that break down your plant waste into soil food need water to stay alive and work, just like human beings need water while doing hard farm work.
ga: nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli Tsei ni anaaa ni gbálaa otso lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ amli kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia nu koni amɛhi shi ni amɛtsu nii. Taakɛ nu he hiaa adesai beni amɛtsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can ground oyster shells from the coast help my farm soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ oyster ŋmeii ni atswa kɛjɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Oyster shells are full of natural lime. When ground into powder and mixed into soil or compost, they take away the harmful sourness in the land so crops can grow strong.
ga: Akɛ adebɔɔ mli lime eyi oyster ŋmeii lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ́ atsɔ powda nɔ lɛ, okɛfutu shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Ejieɔ acid ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do hard items like shells or bones need to be ground into a fine powder before going into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔ nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmeii loo wui anɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa dani akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large shells take many years to break down, but grinding them into a fine powder allows the soil bugs and rainwater to melt them down quickly so your crops get the food right away.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi wuji lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛfiteɔ. Shi kɛ́ atsɔ mli ni etsɔ powda kpakpa lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya. koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: What happens if I add too much shell powder or lime into my compost pile?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ bark powder loo lime babaoo fata mi-compost pile lɛ he?

english: Adding too much lime makes the compost pile too bitter, which kills the helpful micro-bugs that decay the waste and can damage your plant roots when applied to the field.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ lime babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. ni jieɔ kooloi bibii kɛyaa Sɛɛnamɔ, ni haa jwɛi fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei shishifãi kɛ akɛwo ŋmɔji amli.

english: When is the best time to mix powdered shell lime into my land?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ abonua ŋmɔtɔ afutu mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to add lime powder during land preparation or while making compost weeks before planting, giving it time to mix with rainwater and balance the soil before seeds go in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ lime powder afata he yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo beni afeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii otsii babaoo dani aduɔ lɛ. Ha lɛ be ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ afutu ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome dani dumɔwui lɛ abote mli.

english: Why are buyers overseas so strict about the sprays and chemicals I use on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ mli wa waa yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Overseas buyers use sensitive laboratory machines to test imported cocoa beans for chemical residues. If they detect harmful or unapproved chemicals, they can reject the shipment, which hurts your income and Ghana's reputation as a quality cocoa producer.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayelɔi kɛ laboratori nibii ni he hiaa waa tsuɔ nii kɛkaa kookoo yibii ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ amɛkwɛɔ kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛji ana tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara loo ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpoo gbɛfaa. Enɛ saa shika ni onáa lɛ kɛ gbɛi kpakpa ni Ghana yɔɔ akɛ maŋ ni feɔ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ.

english: How do people outside Ghana know if I used banned or bad chemicals on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mɛi ni bɛ Ghana lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛle kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni agu loo tsofai ni ehiii miitsu nii yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: International buyers take samples from cocoa shipments and test them with specialized machines that can detect even tiny traces of chemicals left inside the dried beans.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ jieɔ kookoo ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ mli nɔkwɛmɔnii ni amɛkɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ana tsofa bibioo ko po ni eshwɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ kaa amɛ amɛkwɛɔ.

english: What happens to our cocoa trade if foreign buyers find chemical traces in our cocoa beans?
ga: Mɛni baaba wɔ kookoo jarayeli lɛ nɔ kɛji majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ na tsofai yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: If foreign tests reveal high chemical residues, entire shipments can be destroyed or rejected. This leads to financial loss for cocoa buyers and can cause international markets to refuse buying cocoa from Ghana.
ga: Kɛji maŋsɛɛ kaa jie tsofai ni eshwɛ babaoo kpo lɛ, abaanyɛ akpata nibii fɛɛ ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahiɛ loo akpoo. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ fiteɔ shika. Ni ebaanyɛ eha majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei lɛ akpoo akɛ amɛbaahe kookoo kɛjɛ Ghana.

english: Are all agricultural chemicals sold in the market safe to use on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli tsofai fɛɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, not all chemicals are approved for cocoa farming. You should only use chemicals approved by COCOBOD because unapproved chemicals leave dangerous residues that fail international safety tests.
ga: Dabi, jeee tsofai fɛɛ ji nɔ ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ akɛ aduɔ kookoo. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni COCOBOD kpɛlɛ nɔ pɛ atsu nii, ejaakɛ tsofai ni ekpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni etsɔko majimaji ateŋ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he kaai amli.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer talks about chemical residue on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ ko wie tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Chemical residue refers to small amounts of farm sprays that remain inside or on top of your crops after you spray them. If you harvest too soon after spraying, these residues remain in the crops.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofa fioo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni eshwɛɔ yɛ onibii anɔ loo yɛ nɔ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji okpa mra tsɔ yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ nibii ni eshwɛ nɛɛ baakã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How long after spraying my farm can I safely harvest my cocoa and food crops?
ga: Beni afɔse tsofa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ Ani manyɛ makpa kookoo kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe?

english: Every farm chemical has a required waiting period (pre-harvest interval) stated on its label. Waiting for this recommended period gives the chemical enough time to break down so it does not leave harmful residues in your harvest.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ be ni ato ni akɛbaatsu nii. (dani ŋmaakpamɔ be) taakɛ atsɔɔ yɛ wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ Be ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii nɛɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ aná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafite. no hewɔ lɛ, eshiŋ nɔ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I prevent farm chemicals from leaving harmful traces in my harvested cocoa beans?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkashi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ amli?

english: You can avoid harmful residues by using only recommended cocoa chemicals, measuring the correct doses, and waiting the full required time between spraying and harvesting your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa nibii ni eshwɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli ni ajieɔ yi pɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Susumɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ he Ni omɛ kɛyashi be ni ato lɛ eho yɛ onibii ni okɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpaa lɛ ateŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant food crops like yam and cocoyam under my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ sweet potato kɛ cocoa yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishi?

english: Yes, planting crops like yam and cocoyam under cocoa trees is a good way to use space and get food, but you must take extra care when spraying your cocoa so those chemicals do not contaminate the food crops underneath.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cocoa ni aduɔ yɛ cacao tsei ashishi lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ he ko tsuɔ nii ni anáa niyenii. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ oofɔ kookoo nɔ koni nakai tsofai lɛ akafite niyenii tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Can the chemicals I spray on my cocoa trees get onto the food crops growing underneath them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ amli?

english: Yes, when you spray cocoa trees, the chemical mist can easily drift down onto food crops like cocoyam or yam growing underneath. This can leave unwanted chemical residues on the food your family eats.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni okɛ tsofa shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ. Tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ anɔ mlɛo. Enɛ baanyɛ ashi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii ni oweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I worry about spray drifting onto yams in my farm if I only intend to sell the cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahao yɛ spray ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ he? Akɛni mikɛ mihe ewo mli akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ kookoo pɛ hewɔ lɛ

english: Even if the cocoa is for export, food crops like yams growing under the cocoa trees absorb those same chemicals. Eating food crops contaminated with farm sprays can cause health problems for your household and local buyers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ cocoa majeɔ maŋsɛɛ moŋ, shi niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa tsei ashishi lɛ shwieɔ nakai tsofai lɛ nɔŋŋ. Niyenii ni aduɔ ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ewo mli lɛ ni ayeɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai aba shiabii kɛ maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell when my maize crop is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize shows clear signs when it reaches maturity: the leaves and husks turn yellow and dry, and the kernels become hard. You can also check for a small dark spot (black layer) at the base of the grain where it attaches to the cob.
ga: Abɛi baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni edara lɛ. Baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii diji (black layers) yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ hu.

english: Does the weather affect how many months my crop will take to reach full maturity?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi saa nyɔji enyiɛ ni eheɔ dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, sunlight, heat, and rainfall directly control crop development speed. Extended drought or reduced sunshine can slow down crop growth and delay maturity, while warm weather with steady rain helps crops mature on schedule.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la, dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kudɔɔ tsei adalɛ oya. Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo hulu la ni baa shi lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be ni ato lɛ naa.

english: Why do some crop plants yield less fruit than others on the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ yibii fioo fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants produce uneven yields due to differences in soil nutrients across the field, unequal water supply, crowding, or pest damage. Giving each plant proper spacing and balanced fertilizer helps every crop yield well.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, nibii ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tsei ateŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛha lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aba yibii kpakpai.

english: Can I save stems from my harvested crop to plant for the next season or share with neighbors?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsei ni mikpa lɛ mli tsei lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli loo mikɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ agba he sane?

english: Yes, healthy stems or planting materials from mature crops like cassava can be saved and cut for replanting or shared with other farmers. You must select strong, pest-free stems to ensure a healthy new crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akpa tsei ni eda, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ amli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni akɛdu ekoŋŋ loo akɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi agba he sane. Esa akɛ ohala tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my crop if I leave it in the field past its full maturity stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho amɛshweremɔ be lɛ he?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field causes grain rot, insect attack, and damage from rain or birds. Harvesting on time preserves food quality and frees up the land for your next farming cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo, kooloi baatutua amɛ, ni nugbɔ loo okpoi baafite amɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be naa lɛ haa niyenii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa gbɛ kɛhaa okwaayeli nitsumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does using a harvesting machine affect my crop output compared to harvesting by hand?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ he?

english: A harvester speeds up the harvest process and reduces labor costs for large fields, though it requires crops to be planted in straight, evenly spaced rows. Hand harvesting is slower but allows you to pick selectively without damaging soft plants.
ga: Nikpalɔi haa nikpamɔ nitsumɔ lɛ yaa oya ni ehaa nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale ni eji akɛ esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee ekome lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo shi ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ofiteee tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant my seeds in straight lines instead of scattering them randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and operating farm machinery much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my crops grow weakly when I use the same land continuously without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ fioo beni mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without resting the land or adding fertilizer drains the soil of essential plant nutrients. Adding compost, manure, or letting the soil rest restored its richness so future crops can grow strong.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa waa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which crops should I plant if I need food in a short time on rented land?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu kɛji niyenii he miihia mi be kukuoo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aha mi lɛ nɔ?

english: Short-season crops like maize, cowpea, okra, and garden eggs mature within three to four months. These give you quick food and fast returns compared to long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, okra kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi haa onáa niyenii oya kɛ sɛɛkuu oya kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso he.

english: What are good food crops to plant if I need to share a portion of my yield with the landowner?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii kpakpa esa akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni mikɛ mishikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ aja miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fã ko?

english: High-yielding food staples like plantain, cassava, yam, and maize are best because they produce large harvests that can satisfy both your family's food needs and your obligations to the land provider.
ga: Niyenii ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ plantains, cassava, sweet potatoes, kɛ corn ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni baanyɛ atsu oweku lɛ niyenii he hiamɔ nii kɛ gbɛnaa nii ni kã onɔ yɛ mɛi ni kɛ shikpɔŋ haa lɛ ahe lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do my tomatoes crush and spoil so quickly when I pack them into deep wooden crates for the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli fãa ni egboɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli kɛha jara lɛ?

english: Overfilling deep crates places heavy weight on the bottom tomatoes, causing them to bruise and burst. Bruised tomatoes release heat and moisture, which speeds up rotting for the entire crate.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ adeka lɛ wo mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tomato ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee mlɛo. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Tomato ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya yɛ adeka lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to pick my peppers so they don't rot before I reach the buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite dani amɛyashɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Harvesting peppers when they reach full size but are just beginning to change color helps them stay firm during transport, giving them a longer shelf life at the market.
ga: Kɛ́ akpaa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛdara shi amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like potassium, which prevents fruit set.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni baaye abua ni tso yibii lɛ akamɔ shi lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: In intense sunlight, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to protect themselves from heat stress and usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overly waterlogged soil that prevents roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ fe nine ni miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer so my crops get the most benefit?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist during early vegetative growth or just before flowering allows roots to easily absorb nutrients when the plant needs them most.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida mra loo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ he hiaa lɛ waa lɛ.

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems, smaller fruits, and a higher risk of fungal diseases due to poor airflow.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii Yibii lɛ ji bibioo. Ni oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa mɔ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to grow weak even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizers directly from the soil before your main crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when heavy soil traps too much water around the roots, creating favorable conditions for soil fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mɔmɔ nu babaoo ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni enɛ haa shihilɛ kpakpa baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do insect holes on leaves affect the size of the crop I harvest?
ga: Te kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Leaves act as solar panels for the plant to make food. When insects eat holes in leaves, the plant cannot produce enough energy, resulting in smaller crop yields.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni haa tsei feɔ niyenii. Kɛji kooloi ye bu yɛ baai amli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantings need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to shield their leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ biɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daa waa lɛ.

english: Spacing crops gives roots enough room to find food and water in the soil, ensures leaves get plenty of sunlight, and keeps plants from competing with each other, resulting in bigger cobs.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna niyenii kɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni etsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkatswa amɛhe akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmei ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is vital food for green growth. Adding compost or appropriate fertilizer will restore the dark green color needed to produce strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa kɛha toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná.

english: Cassava drops leaves naturally during dry spells to protect itself and conserve water. As soon as the rainy season returns, the stem will sprout fresh new green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebu ehe ni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛji akɛ abote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ yitso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the leaves, or a virus spread by insects. Controlling these insects early prevents damage to your crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips miimu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. loo helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa Kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akafite onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for their leaves. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy they send underground to expand the yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛwo yam ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, when water is inconsistent, or when pollinators aren't visiting. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni feɔ pollinating lɛ eyaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Excess rain and cool shade create wet conditions where fungal diseases like Black Pod thrive. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods and reduce rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ haa shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ baa. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baanyɛ ada yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baa shi.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year and encourages pests to settle there. Swapping with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tsake ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so the plant roots can swallow it. Putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn the roots and wastes your money because the crop cannot feed on dry powder.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ami lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã, ni eji shika fitemɔ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to grow strong. It can also happen when the soil has too much standing water, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu damɔ shi babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to leave wide spacing between my seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oshi gbɛ ni da yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed well and grow big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize after them, the maize uses this natural fertilizer to grow faster and stronger.
