ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ŋmãa kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers on my field before planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with big leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and coolness young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and wind in helps dry out the farm and prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack open as the heavy tubers swell underneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca ko eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni tsii lɛ fũuɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes helps leaves catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. It also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing rot and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the full rainy season begins. Planting too early can cause heat to scorch your seeds in the dry soil before steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ anɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open on the sides when heavy rains start after a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ fãa yɛ afãi beni nugbɔ ni naa wa jeɔ shishi yɛ otsi kome ni hɔmɔ eho lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a dry plant suddenly drinks a lot of water, the inside of the tomato fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch. This sudden pressure causes the fruit skin to split open.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ egbi lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu babaoo trukaa. Tomato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ haa aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ fãa.

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients that the plant should be using to produce big, healthy tomatoes. Removing them directs all the plant's energy into making fewer, larger, and higher-quality fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛtsu nii ni ekɛfee tomato agbo ni mli wa. Amɛjiemɔ lɛ heɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo yibii bibii, wuji, ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense sunlight on their own. They require temporary shade crops, such as plantains, to shield their delicate leaves from heat while their root systems establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tswaa amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area. This protects the plant from losing too much water through evaporation during peak heat hours.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Bɔni afee ni ajie baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ shi Enɛ buɔ tsei ahe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small when I plant the stems close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are placed too close together, their root systems compete for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving the plant without enough energy to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizers from the soil faster than crops can, while their broad foliage blocks sunlight from reaching young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ afee. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei bibii ahe.

english: Pepper plants often drop their blossoms when stressed by sudden dry spells, high heat, or nutrient imbalances. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do small suckers keep growing around the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ eda kɛbɔle he fɛɛ. mi plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: Plantain plants naturally produce offshoots called suckers to reproduce. Leaving too many suckers attached forces the main stem to share food, reducing the size of the main fruit cluster.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛfɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie tsei bibii babaoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ aha. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu titri lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: A V-shaped yellowing pattern starting on the lower, older leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen shortage. The plant moves stored nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to feed new top growth.
ga: V-shaped yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse. Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to direct all its energy toward lush stem and leaf growth instead of storing nutrients in underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ woɔ tso ɔ mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree grow thin shoots straight up from the main trunk, and should I leave them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mashi yɛ sɛɛ?

english: Those fast-growing vertical shoots are called chupons. They drain vital water and nutrients away from the main trunk and pod-bearing branches, so they should be pruned off.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni daa oya lɛ akɛ chupons. Amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni woɔ pod lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines try to wrap around nearby trees and sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ehe abɔle tsei kɛ tsei niji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam is naturally a climbing vine that requires vertical support to lift its foliage off the ground, allowing maximum sunlight exposure while keeping leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ nɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha ni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees or plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cool umbrella of shade and retains soil moisture, helping the cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light while protecting them from leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ la ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: When too many suckers grow together, they steal water and soil nutrients from the main stem. Pruning away extra shoots leaves only 2 or 3 strong ones, ensuring the plant produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi koni tso lɛ awo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help the leaves turn green and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crop roots with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the soil cool under hot weather, stops soil water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from growing near your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and stay small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil food, moisture, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow tall and produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are there tiny ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ehiɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest eating the plant's growing point. Applying recommended organic or chemical treatment directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening protects the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yeɔ tso lɛ hei ni edaa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ wo tso lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants often drop blossoms when stressed by extreme weather heat or irregular watering. Giving young plants light shade and watering regularly keeps the soil moist so flowers can form peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo ni okɛ nu wo amɛmli daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is blossom-end rot, caused by dry soil and a lack of calcium uptake. Keeping the soil consistently moist stops the fruit tissues from dying and turning black.
ga: Diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato shishi lɛ ji fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ calcium ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai amli fãji lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ diŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers under the ground are mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by strong, direct heat from the sun. Fast-growing plantain plants produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and humidity they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and grow strong stems. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four maize seeds together in the exact same hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to steal light, water, and soil food from each other. Spacing them out ensures each plant grows thick stems and produces big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni miida lɛ aju la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa tso lɛ shishi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: What causes my young corn leaves to look like someone shot small ragged holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɔ ko ni tu bu bibioo ko kɛtsɔ mli?

english: This ragged damage is caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the growing center of young corn plants and eat the tender leaves before they fully unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ ni etse ehe nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle into the ground instead of sticking them straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle encourages the roots to grow deeper and spread wider on one side, which helps the plant absorb more groundwater and yields larger, easier-to-harvest tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa he kome. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni akpaamɔ waaa.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam plants so the vines can climb them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ fɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up off the dark ground toward the sun. Staking keeps the leaves healthy and exposed to light, which powers the plant to build thick, heavy tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni woɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnaa la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and leathery before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee hewolo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This black spot is caused by irregular watering, which prevents the plant from moving calcium from the soil into the developing fruit. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps prevent this problem.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tsei akajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or dry soil. Giving the soil regular moisture during hot periods helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans on my plot before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Beans and cowpeas extract nitrogen from the air and store it inside the soil through their roots. When the season ends, this natural food remains in the soil to feed the next maize crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmãa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when I water my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that drink the water and suck up the soil nutrients intended for your crops. Even with enough water, your crops stay weak because the weeds steal their essential food.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni shwereɔ oya ni amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaadu nii lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii po bɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi juɔ amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I do not plant plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and cannot withstand direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and preserving soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui waaa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la naa tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my harvest last year yield smaller cobs than the new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid maize varieties lose their strong genetic vigor after the first harvest, leading to smaller cobs and weaker plants. Newly packaged hybrid seeds carry full genetic strength for higher yields and better disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ laajeɔ egbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni mli wa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe hewalɛ fɛɛ ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top remains green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is short on nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever nutrients are left in its older bottom leaves and sends them to the young top leaves and ears to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛkɛyaa baai bibii kɛ toi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show light yellow spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This symptom is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. It reduces the leaves' ability to catch sunlight, which stops the roots beneath the ground from growing large.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ mli. ni ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la lɛ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, pepper plants experience severe heat stress. They drop their flowers to save water and survival energy rather than spending nutrients to develop fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaná dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa. Amɛshɛrɛɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ wala nɔ lɛ he. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo yibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do you advise me not to burn the cleared weeds and bushes on my plot before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and micro-organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops. Leaving cleared vegetation to rot on the field puts valuable nutrients back into the dirt and prevents heavy rain from washing away the soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Tsei ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did my maize plants wither and burn when I placed fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. When placed directly against plant stems, it draws water out of the roots instead of feeding them, causing the plant tissue to dehydrate and burn.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ Egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Ehaa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli nu faaa ni amɛshãa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open around the top after a sudden heavy rain following a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miitswa kɛmiibɔle he lɛ? Top yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: When tomatoes receive a lot of water suddenly after a drought, the fruit inside grows faster than its outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato ná nu babaoo yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Yibii ni yɔɔ emli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with small ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei babaoo amli lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete intensely for sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward trying to reach light instead of building thick stems and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha la, moŋ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds harm my cassava tubers even after the plants have already grown bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ awui lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ eda fe jwɛi moŋ

english: Even if the cassava stems are tall, dense weeds underground suck up the water and nutrients in the soil that the cassava roots need to swell and form heavy tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ koni amɛfu ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The crop moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha gbekɛbii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots under the soil remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build large underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are getting too much water after heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miihe nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ?

english: When soil gets waterlogged, crop roots choke from lack of oxygen. The leaves will turn pale yellow, droop as if they are thirsty, and the base of the stems may feel soft or start to rot.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Gbee shi tamɔ kumai Ni tso lɛ shishi baanyɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo ebɔi fitemɔ.

english: No, planting too closely forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin stems and small or empty cobs, whereas proper spacing gives bigger yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. yɛ be mli ni gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in full direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under intense heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields them from the hot sun while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Weeds act like aggressive thieves that steal water, fertilizer, and light away from your crops. Clearing weeds early lets your crops consume those nutrients without competition.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yitsoŋ wa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ nakai niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or dry soil stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii anyɛ afee.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants full of small holes and ragged edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋwɛigbɛi ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes and ragged leaves on young corn are a sign of pests like armyworms feeding on the tender leaves at night. Spotting this early helps you treat the farm before major damage occurs.
ga: Buu bibii kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii, tamɔ asraafoi aŋmãa ni yeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ni ooona mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ohere oŋmɔ lɛ yiwala dani nɔ ko wulu aba.

english: If I keep seeds from my corn harvest to plant next season, why won't they grow as well as certified seeds?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ tamɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred in laboratories for high strength and disease resistance. Grain saved from a past harvest loses that hybrid vigor, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Certified seeds are specially bred in a laboratory for high vigor and disease resistance. Seeds collected from past harvests will lose hybrid vigor. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my maize field regularly to check on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli daa koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Regularly walking through your field allows you to catch early signs of pests, diseases, or yellowing leaves before they spread across your entire farm, saving your yield before it is too late.
ga: Oŋmɔji amli nyiɛmɔ daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ahe okadii mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. This helps preserve your productivity before it's too late.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which acts as food for healthy leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps keep the leaves green so the plant can grow big ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni hi Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and encourages pests to live there. Switching to crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil a rest and restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender leaves in the center of the plant. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying the right treatments before they multiply protects your young crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni sa tsu nii dani efɔ bii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Too much standing water suffocates cassava roots because air cannot reach them in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess rain to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to catch light and generate energy, which helps grow large tubers underground while keeping leaves away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyashɛ hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the heat is too high, water is inconsistent, or bees aren't around to pollinate them. Regular watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. Aloo ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look very green above ground but have empty pods underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli waa kɛ́ eyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Empty groundnut pods usually happen when there isn't enough calcium in the soil while the nuts are swelling underground. Adding agricultural lime to the soil supplies the calcium needed to fill out the shells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ efuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli lime fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli calcium ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays moist a few inches deep after two or three steady rains, rather than planting after the very first shower, so the seeds don't dry up after sprouting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ 2-3 inches yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ 2-3 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when my crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɔ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots underground that steal water and nutrients away from your crops before your crops can use them, which slows down fruit and grain growth even if the crop is taller.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii. Enɛ haa aduawai kɛ dumɔwui lɛ daa blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants developing tiny holes and looking eaten up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni etamɔ nɔ ni aye lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the leaves at the center of the maize plant during the day and eat the young foliage. Applying recommended organic or chemical insecticides early in the morning or late evening can help protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or whiteflies. These insects feed on the leaves and can spread viruses that distort growth. Spraying with neem oil or targeted insecticidal soap can reduce pest populations.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ yeɔ baai ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni fiteɔ dalɛ amɛshwã. Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry winds, or inconsistent watering. When the plant gets stressed by drought or hot weather, it sheds its blossoms to save energy and water for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛji hɔmɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hao tsei lɛ Eshwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato koni ehi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too closely, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks that fall over easily and produce small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. ni ekɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa

english: Maize draws a lot of nitrogen nutrients out of the soil. Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally restores fertility for the next crop season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: As cassava grows, it naturally sheds its oldest lower leaves to direct water and nutrients to the younger top leaves and the roots underground, especially during dry spells or when soil nutrients are low.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei lɛ da lɛ Ekɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii aya ŋwɛi baai lɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be mli ni sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds lie dormant in the soil waiting for moisture, and once the rain falls, they absorb water and soil nutrients faster than domestic crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛ dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya fe shia dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines stop growing and naturally turn yellow and dry up. This signal shows that the plant has finished transferring its energy down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why must I cover my harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves to ferment before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo ni akpa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba dani egbi lɛ?

english: Covering wet cocoa beans with plantain leaves traps natural heat and allows beneficial microorganisms to ferment the beans. Fermentation removes the bitter pulp and develops the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, emɔɔ dɔlɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni amɛná tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential food plant need to build leaves and stems. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo mli koni akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ edara beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cabbage plants produce loose leaves instead of forming a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form solid heads if they receive too much heat, inconsistent watering, or insufficient nutrients like nitrogen during their early growth stage. Giving them steady moisture and cool shade helps them form firm heads.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji akɛ ekɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli Nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli daa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa amɛyitso hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water and usually recovers by evening once the temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei baagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pod husks turn black and rot before they are mature enough to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and heavy shade during rainy periods. Pruning heavy canopy branches allows sunlight and air flow to dry out the farm and reduce the rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit a virus to the plant. Controlling these insects early and removing severely infected plants stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I stop worms from eating holes in the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms, like fall armyworms, hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant where leaves emerge. Applying recommended treatments directly into the center funnel early in the morning or late evening reaches the pests effectively.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ tamɔ fall asraafoi ŋmeii. Ekɛtee ŋmãa tso ko teŋ he ni baai jeɔ kpo yɛ lɛ. Okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans inside the same farm as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping beans or cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Legumes capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural food source that improves the growth of your maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Legumes mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams soften and rot quickly when I store them inside my rooms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly in dark, closed rooms because of heat and a lack of fresh air circulation. Storing them off the ground on raised wooden racks in a shaded, open-air yam barn keeps them dry and extends their shelf life.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya yɛ tsũi ni mli ewo duŋ ni aŋã mli lɛ amli yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Atomɔ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei ni awó nɔ yɛ atomɔ shĩa ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa egbiɔ ni ehaa esɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or floods the roots so they cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nu, ni eha amɛmumɔ shwie shi.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from underneath the leaves and passing a virus to the plant. It can also happen when the plant rolls its leaves to reduce water loss during hot, dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji tsei shwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛlaajeɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the stem before they get big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal sickness that spreads quickly during heavy rainy seasons when the air is cool and wet. Excessive shade and water droplets splashing from the ground carry the sickness onto the young pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ hela baaba ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without turning into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they get too stressed by high heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. When daytime temperatures get too hot, the pollen dries up and the plant drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, kɛji hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of bush and green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miikwɛ jwɛi kɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich soil, they spend all their energy producing leaves and stems instead of making flowers and pods. Trimming excessive fertilizer helps the plant shift focus to producing seeds.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eshiɔ dumɔwui afeemɔ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava lets you know it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to swell and crack open as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to balance heavy bunches, especially if tiny soil worms called nematodes or root weevils have damaged the roots underground. Staking the trunk with strong wooden forks supports the weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛha niji ni tsii lɛ afee ekome. Titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ŋmeii lɛ, amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Akɛ tso ni mli wa fĩɔ tsɔne lɛ he koni ekɛfi tsɔne lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing out thin and twisted instead of big, thick, and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ agbo, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and stay small when the soil inside the heap or mound is packed too hard, filled with rocks, or not deep enough. Yams need loose, deep, stone-free soil so the tuber can expand downward easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi eyi mli obɔ, loo ekɔɔɔ he eko. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia sweet potato. No hewɔ lɛ, yitso lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi oya.

english: Why does the top of my farm soil turn hard and dry like stone just two days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ wa ni egbi tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Soil hardens fast when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves, compost, or manure. Organic matter works like a sponge to trap moisture and keeps the soil soft, open, and easy for plant roots to push through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo, egbeleɔ, ni ewaaa akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abote mli.

english: How can I know if my crop leaves are wilting because of disease or just because of sun heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela hewɔ ni mitso lɛ baai lɛ miigbo loo hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Plants wilting from simple sun heat will bounce back and look fresh in the cool early morning or evening. If a plant stays wilted or yellow even after a cool night or watering, it is likely being attacked by a soil disease or root rot.
ga: Tsei ni hulu la ni tsoɔ daa lɛ gboiɔ lɛ Baahe ajɔ amɛ ni amɛbaafee tamɔ mɛi ni he ejɔ amɛ yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ egbo loo efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ loo nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ hela loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hu baatutua lɛ.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing holes and rolled edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ amɛhe ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes and rolled leaves in young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central shoot of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ baai ni ebɔle ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking plant sap and transmitting viral diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun, so fast-growing plantains are planted alongside them to provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas in the same field where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollinators like bees to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ hao amɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to grow thick stems and leaves instead of spending energy on flowering and pod formation.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ fɔfɔi kɛ pod peemi he ní.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when the field has poor drainage and stays waterlogged, or when soil pests like nematodes damage the growing tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ jɛmɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni damɔ shi. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes fiteɔ bulbs ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my maize produce very small cobs even though the plants grew tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ moŋ?

english: Tall plants with small cobs occur when the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen right when the cobs begin forming.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ nitrogen, kɛji ŋmeii lɛ bɔi feemɔ pɛ.

english: Plantain plants fall because their root systems are shallow, especially if planted in hard soil or weakened by root-eating pests like nematodes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi tamɔ nematodes lɛ ebɔle ehe.

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees are mature enough to start producing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cacao tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Cocoa trees usually start bearing fruit after 3 to 5 years. You will know they are getting ready when small flowers start appearing directly on the trunk and main thick branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ efee klalo beni fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ.

english: Do older, mature cocoa trees need different care than young trees?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni eda lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe cacao tso?

english: Yes, older trees need less shade than young trees, but they require regular pruning to remove dead branches and let air flow through, which prevents black pod disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ ahe ehiaaa tsɔi babaoo fe tsei bibii. Shi ebiɔ ni afo tsei lɛ ahe daa koni ajie tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ black pod hela lɛ naa.

english: How long does it take for land to stabilize and give good yields after planting tree crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai beni adu tsei sɛɛ?

english: It takes about 3 to 4 years for the soil to settle and the tree roots to establish deeply before you start seeing consistent, healthy harvests.
ga: Eheɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani shikpɔŋ lɛ shwereɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shɔŋŋ dani obɔi yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ namɔ.

english: What warning signs on my crop show that disease is starting to spread?
ga: Mɛɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ akɛ hela lɛ miibɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ?

english: Look out for pods turning black, yellow spots on green leaves, or sudden wilting. Spotting these early lets you remove infected pods before the disease spreads to the whole farm.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii ni etsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai eŋɔli nɔ loo egboɔ trukaa Nibii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow slowly even after I planted them at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Slow growth often means the roots are struggling with poor soil conditions, lack of nutrients, or too much direct sunlight when the plant is still young.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ daa blɛoo lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo miiwuu beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ fioo lɛ.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely. Pods that start as green turn bright yellow, and pods that start as red or purple turn bright orange when ready.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ atsake amɛhe su kwraa. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni pods ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ tsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ orange ni kpɛɔ kɛji amɛfee klalo.

english: What is the best way to harvest cocoa without hurting future yields?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa kookoo ni enaaa wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni abaafee lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Use a sharp pruning hook or cutlass to cut the pod stem cleanly. Never pull or twist pods by hand, as this damages the flower cushion where future pods will grow.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei loo tsɔne ni mli wa atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ pods lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kaagbala loo okɛ onine atsɔ podi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baafite fɔfɔii akushin ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I guide my farm workers so they do not destroy my crops during harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ ŋaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Teach your workers to identify ripe pods properly, cut stems carefully without scratching the tree trunk, and gently gather pods in baskets rather than dropping them roughly on the ground.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ onitsulɔi lɛ ni amɛyoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ akatswa tso lɛ shishi, ni obua ŋmeii lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli moŋ fe ni oooshɛrɛ amɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil is in good condition to support cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ cacao tsei anɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil holds moisture without staying flooded, feels soft and dark with decomposed leaves, and allows water to sink in smoothly during rain.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni nu akabote mli. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ duŋ kɛ baai ni miigboi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ shwieɔ mli oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Why do my crops look weak right after harvest, and how can I help them recover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya nɔ?

english: Trees put a lot of energy into producing fruit, leaving them exhausted after harvest. Applying organic manure or fertilizer and maintaining weed control helps them regain strength for the next season.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ yibii. kɛ tɔlɛ baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Humus loo organic fertilizer kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. The maize plant pulls nitrogen from its old bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Abɛi tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct harsh sun and strong winds. Planting shade trees or plantains around them creates a cooler, moist climate that keeps the young leaves from burning and drying out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo baa. Enɛ baatsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce lots of large green leaves but very small cassava roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi? Cassava shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get enough water. Heat stress stops the flower from forming fruit, so the plant sheds it to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ he haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa. Aloo hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛji hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do plantain suckers with narrow, sword-like leaves grow better than suckers with broad, flat leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Narrow-leaf suckers (sword suckers) have strong, healthy underground roots and food reserves, while broad-leaf suckers (water suckers) have weak root connections and produce smaller bunches.
ga: Narrow leaf suckers (sword suckers) lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni ato. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ (nu mli ŋmeii) lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli.

english: Why do my yams yield bigger tubers when I support the vines with sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso fiɔ wain tso lɛ sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight and air. More sun exposure helps the plant manufacture food faster and store it in the tuber below.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Hulu la babaoo ni anáa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii oya ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea pods rot on the farm when rainfall continues late into the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛyashiɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Dry cowpea pods easily absorb water from rain. Excess moisture creates a warm, wet surface where fungal rot grows quickly and ruins the seeds inside the pods.
ga: Cowpea ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ mli oya. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ, ni efɔ. Fuji ni fiteɔ lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my rice crop so much more during the first month than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young rice plants grow slowly and have small roots, so weeds easily steal their sunlight, water, and nutrients. Once rice grows tall, its own leaves shade out new weeds.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛyɛ shishifãi bibii. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi lɛ baaju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ da lɛ Ebaai lɛ baaha jwɛi heei anɔ.

english: Why are my watermelons forming tiny fruits that turn black and drop off before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Tiny watermelons turn black when bees do not pollinate the female flower properly. Without pollen from a male flower, the plant aborts the unfertilized fruit.
ga: watermelon bibioo Etsɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛji ŋmeii efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi yei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ pollen ko bɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli lɛ Tso lɛ baaŋmɛɛ yibii ni awoko lɛ he.

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the soil, supplying essential nutrients that crops need to grow strong stems, healthy leaves, and produce more pods or fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa, baai ni wa, ni amɛwo pods loo aduawai babaoo.

english: Where exactly am I supposed to place fertilizer around my cocoa trees?
ga: Nɛgbɛ pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he?

english: You should place fertilizer on the ground around the base of the cocoa tree in a circle where the leaves end, so the fine roots underground can easily feed on it.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kakao tso lɛ shishi ji kooloo yɛ baai lɛ anaa. koni shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shihilɛhei lɛ aye mlɛo.

english: Can pouring fertilizer directly against the stem of my cocoa tree harm it?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kookoo tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaná nɔ ko ni ehiii?

english: Yes, piling fertilizer directly touching the stem can burn the bark and roots. It should always be spread in a ring around the base a short distance away from the trunk.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni ekɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: Why can't I just scatter fertilizer randomly all over my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ majara ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Scattering fertilizer everywhere wastes money because weeds will eat the nutrients instead of your cocoa trees, which only absorb food near their root zone.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo he fɛɛ he lɛ heɔ shika ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ moŋ fe kookoo tso lɛ. Enɛ baaŋɔ niyenii ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ pɛ.

english: How will spending money on fertilizer help me make more profit from my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shika ni mikɛbaahe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli?

english: Proper fertilizer use increases both the number and size of cocoa pods your trees produce, resulting in a much larger harvest that earns you more money than the fertilizer cost.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kookoo ŋmeii ni tso lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa babaoo ni baaha oná shika babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ baa.

english: Will using fertilizer help my young cocoa trees start producing pods faster?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛje ŋmɔshi nibii ahe oya?

english: Yes, feeding young cocoa trees proper nutrients helps them build strong roots and branches quickly, allowing them to mature and bear fruit earlier.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ aha cacao tsei bibii lɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni edaa ni ewoɔ yibii oya.

english: How does following proper farming advice prevent me from losing money on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni sa ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ mi gbɛ koni mikafite shika yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Getting proper advice ensures you apply inputs like fertilizer correctly and in the right amounts, preventing wasted materials and protecting your crops from damage.
ga: Ŋaawoo ni sa ni oooná lɛ haa ona nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni sa. Tsi nibii ni afiteɔ lɛ anaa ni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: When is the best time of year to put fertilizer on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo kookoo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the rainy season when the soil is moist, which helps the tree roots absorb the dissolved nutrients easily.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need fertilizer or extra nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii krokomɛi?

english: If your cocoa trees have yellowish leaves, grow slowly, or produce very few pods, it is usually a sign that the soil lacks the necessary nutrients to support them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, eedara blɛoo, loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛye abua cacao tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I put fertilizer on my farm, do I still need to clear the weeds around my cocoa trees?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehe miihia ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ lolo. Cocoa tso loo daabi?

english: Yes, you must clear weeds because they grow faster than cocoa trees and will steal all the fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your trees can use them.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ ohe ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya fe kookoo tsei. Ni ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani otsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant build strong, green leaves to make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eŋɔli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛhoo nii.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large leaves but refusing to form a tight ball in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi efeŋ bɔɔlu yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, irregular water, or during extreme heat. Balanced feeding and steady watering encourage the plant to form a firm head.
ga: Cabbage lɛ yitsoŋ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Nu lɛ ejaaa. aloo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ Niyenii ni ja kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛbulb lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get scorched and stressed easily by direct sunlight. Shade trees protect the seedlings from severe heat and harsh winds while keeping the soil cool and moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛhaoɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Which type of plantain suckers should I choose from an old crop to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain ŋmeii esa akɛ mahala kɛjɛ tso momo ko mli koni mikɛje tso hee shishi?

english: Select 'maiden' or 'sword' suckers, which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. They grow faster and yield bigger bunches than suckers that have wide, flat leaves early on.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Maiden’ loo ‘Sword’ ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ kui wuji fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: Why is it necessary to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tsei ahe tsɔi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises yam leaves off the damp ground to catch maximum sunlight for growth and prevents soil-borne fungal diseases, resulting in much larger tubers at harvest.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo kɛha dalɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akwɛmɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa kɛji akpa.

english: Why does swamp rice require shallow standing water in the field while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni peat rice lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water prevents weeds from taking over the field, stabilizes soil temperatures, and gives rice plants the constant moisture they need to produce healthy tillers.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ ahi shi daa. ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo ŋmãa ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when heat is intense, water is inconsistent, or pests attack the flowers. Keeping soil evenly moist and shielding plants from extreme heat helps fruit set successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli wa waa. Nu lɛ ejaaa. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi yɛ ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ haa yibiiwoo yeɔ omanye.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips, or viruses spread by them. Applying neem oil or appropriate remedies early stops further damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Neem fɔ loo helatsamɔ gbɛ̀i krokomɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni sa Ebaakpa nɔ ni fiteɔ nii krokomɛi.

english: Insects like flower thrips feed on cowpea blossoms before pods can form. Spraying safe, recommended pest treatments at the onset of flowering preserves the blossoms so pods can mature.
