ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips yeɔ cowpea fɔfɔi dani pods feɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready 8 to 12 months after planting, signaled when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil around the stem base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni etsɔɔ be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to plant my maize in neat straight lines instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures each crop gets enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow strong. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you later on.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds and loosen the soil before putting my seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition so your young crops don't have to fight for water and food. Loosening the soil makes it easy for young crop roots to spread out and go deep to absorb nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni odumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbote mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ nii.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Plant maize seeds about 3 to 5 centimeters deep (about the length of your thumb knuckle). If planted too shallow, birds might eat them or sun will dry them out; if too deep, the shoot will exhaust its energy before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 (aaafee otsitsi bibioo lɛ kɛlɛ). Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, Okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, hulu la lɛ baaha amɛgbi. Kɛji amɛmli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, tu lɛ hewalɛ baaho dani eshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my cassava cuttings after the rains begin?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the soil is consistently moist after two or three good rains at the start of the rainy season. Planting in moist soil ensures the cassava stems form roots quickly instead of drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya moŋ fe ni amɛaagbi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up and turn yellow during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during intense heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves. Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is stressed from a lack of water or lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni bɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry or too wet, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are some of my plantain suckers growing very slowly while others right next to them grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida blɛoo waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ miida blɛoo waa lɛ? Amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Slow growth usually means those specific suckers are fighting underground pests like nematodes, lack sufficient water, or are competing with hidden weed roots for soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nakai tsei bibii lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes miiwu ni amɛbɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo amɛkɛ jwɛi shishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes your maize and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their young crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (called mulching) keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you don't need to water as often, and prevents weeds from popping up around your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Locks in moisture No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases specific to maize to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it better for me to harvest my cassava bit by bit instead of digging up the whole field at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fiofio moŋ fe ni mafo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers spoil quickly within two to three days after being dug out of the ground. Leaving unharvested tubers in the soil keeps them fresh until you are ready to sell or eat them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni atsa amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni akpaaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo oye.

english: What happens to my crops if I harvest everything at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Harvesting everything at once can lead to heavy losses from spoilage if you do not have good storage facilities or immediate buyers, and it forces you to sell at lower market prices.
ga: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni oookpa shikome lɛ baanyɛ aha ofite nii babaoo kɛjɛ fitemɔ mli kɛji obɛ he kpakpa ni okɛtoɔ loo mɔ ni baahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni ebaanyɛ onɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops mature at different times even though I planted them on the exact same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ? ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ

english: Crops mature unevenly because of small differences in soil nutrients, sun exposure, water availability across the field, and natural variations in the seeds.
ga: Tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ srɔtofeemɔi fioo ni yɔɔ sũ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ hewɔ. kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔi ni baa dumɔwui amli lɛ

english: Plantains are ready for harvesting when the fingers become full and plump, the sharp angles on the fruit soften, and the flower remnants at the tips dry off completely.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni niji lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Yibii lɛ a-angle ni mli wa lɛ baa shi. ni fɔfɔii lɛ amli fãi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ egbi kwraa.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant new crops too close to existing ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu tsei heei ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plants compete for the same limited nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. Overcrowding starves both old and new plants, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ miiha tsei heei kɛ tsei momo miiye hɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving the space and sunlight for the cassava to grow bigger later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko kɛ hulu la koni ŋmei lɛ adara sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot in the ground when water collects in heavy soil without proper drainage, creating wet conditions that encourage fungal and bacterial rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ahe hewalɛ baa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and dark shade. Pruning tall trees and weeding helps air flow through the farm to prevent rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni eyɛ diŋŋ lɛ. Tsei kakadaji ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil so quickly after I bring them home from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛba shia lɛ?

english: Crops rot fast after harvest if they are bruised during picking, exposed to direct heat, or stored in poorly ventilated bags without airflow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ Aloo okɛto kotoku ko mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bɛ mli.

english: Why do insects still attack my stored maize even after I dried it under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Sun-drying reduces moisture, but insect eggs hidden inside the grains can still hatch during storage unless the grain is treated with approved storage dust or kept in airtight bags.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Shi kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ lolo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ja ashɛre dumɔwui lɛ ahe sũ yɛ he ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ loo akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my land is ready for me to plant new crops this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui heei yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: You can test if your soil is ready by squeezing a handful of moist earth; if it forms a soft ball without dripping water or crumbling instantly, it has the right balance of moisture for seeds to germinate successfully.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni oootsi mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu bɛ mli ni hoɔ loo efoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa aba koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in the first year but start producing less if I plant the same thing in the exact same spot next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ da jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi ebɔi yibiiwoo fioo kɛji akɛ midu nɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants take specific nutrients out of the soil. When you plant the same crop repeatedly in one place, it drains those specific nutrients and attracts crop-specific pests, which is why rotating different crops keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ejieɔ nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ ni egbalaa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I test if the seeds I bought will actually sprout before I plant them all on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can do a simple float test in a bowl of water: healthy, viable seeds usually sink to the bottom, while dead or damaged seeds float to the top and should be discarded.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee buoyancy kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nu tsɛnsi mli - dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni baanyɛ ahi shi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛyaa shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni egboi loo efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: What will happen to my crops if I apply fertilizer when the afternoon sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer during intense heat can scorch the roots and leaves of young crops, so it is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the evening when the soil is cool and moist.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ.

english: How do I calculate how much seed or fertilizer I need to buy for my small plot of land so I do not waste money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ he akɔntaa koni mikafite shika?

english: You should measure the exact size of your land in acres or fractions of an acre and follow recommended spacing guidelines, which tell you the precise weight of seeds or bags of fertilizer required per area.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ he yɛ acre loo acre mli fãi amli. ni onyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ajie he kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ bo dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku ni he hiaa yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ tsiimɔ pɔtɛɛ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its outer leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss through evaporation, allowing the root system to conserve moisture and survive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, forcing them to grow tall and weak instead of building strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii ni he wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do heavy rain downpours right after planting affect my young vegetable crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ saa mi-aduawai bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Torrential rain can wash away topsoil, expose tender roots, or pack the soil so tightly that air cannot reach the roots, causing young seedlings to yellow or rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei bibii feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil, which prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: How does planting plantains next to my young cocoa trees help the cocoa grow better?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Te mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, supplying essential shade and moisture while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong direct sun. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to protect them and keep the soil cool during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines up to catch light and keeps leaves off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. When soil lacks this nutrient or gets waterlogged, the roots cannot feed properly, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ. ni haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally enriches the soil with fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In waterlogged soil during heavy rain, roots cannot breathe and begin to decay, which is why planting on soil ridges or mounds helps drain extra water.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil dries out completely. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to conserve energy and water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves droop in the afternoon heat even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, cabbage leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can drink it up. The plant droops on purpose to shield itself from heat and usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Kaabaji baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the field before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when heavy rain comes right after a long dry spell. The inside of the fruit drinks water rapidly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over if their root systems are weak, planted too shallowly, or damaged by soil pests. Planting deep enough and mounding soil around the base gives stalks stronger anchor support.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ Adu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni ato shikpɔŋ ni abɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ he wa waa.

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved from last year will actually grow before I plant my whole farm with them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds in a wet cloth in a warm spot for a few days. If 8 or more seeds sprout, your seed batch is strong and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Anáa enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni akɛwoɔ mama ni mli efɔ mli yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why should I try a new seed variety on a small patch of my land before planting my entire field with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? dani adu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu

english: Testing a new crop variety on a small plot lets you see how it reacts to your specific soil and weather conditions without risking your entire season's food or income if it performs poorly.
ga: Kɛ́ oka tso hee ko okwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ, ebaaha ona bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he. Ni akɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii loo shika ni anáa lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which helps the plant conserve water and survive extreme heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ba hulu la ni shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the surrounding air moist and protecting the tender leaves from scorching.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Cassava plants drop their lower leaves during dry spells to reduce the amount of water they lose, allowing the plant to survive drought conditions until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shiɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, while making weeding, spraying, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready and healthy enough for planting yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Healthy soil for yams should be dark, loose, well-drained, and rich in organic matter. You can also ask an extension officer to run a soil test to check its nutrient levels.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha sweet potato lɛ afee ediŋŋ, ni egbɔjɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo Obaanyɛ obi o-extension nitsulɔ lɛ ni efee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa koni ekwɛ bɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ ha.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop when feeding the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei lɛ miiye nii?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the delicate plant tissue and roots. It should be applied in a ring or line a few inches away from the stem so the roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo ŋtayaai amli loo ŋtayaai amli yɛ ŋtayaai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ he koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do fall armyworms always hide inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel offers young armyworms tender leaves to eat while shielding them from heavy rainfall, intense heat, and natural predators like birds.
ga: Teŋgbɛ fã lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii yeɔ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi awui tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or develop mold inside my storage room so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa mi-nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize molds in storage when it has not been thoroughly dried in the sun first. Trapped moisture inside the grain encourages mold growth and attracts storage pests.
ga: Abele baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii adalɛ he hewalɛ ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while sheltering the delicate leaves from burning until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow tall. Rain provides water, but without soil nutrients or fertilizer, the plant starves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tsei.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with dense leaves, but yields very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or if the ground is too hard, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my maize rows help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil to feed the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, abaajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like they have small holes and ragged chewed edges overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fã nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the plant during the hot afternoon and comes out at night to eat the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ

english: Why is it better to build raised earth mounds before planting my yams or sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so root tubers can expand easily without meeting hard earth. They also elevate the roots to prevent them from rotting in waterlogged soil during heavy downpours.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akakpe. Amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ hu anɔ koni amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This leaves every plant weak and small rather than giving a few plants enough resources to produce well.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii. Mohu ɔ, ha tsehi bɔɔ komɛ níhi nɛ sa konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a wo ní kpakpahi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without developing into fruits during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures and dry conditions cause the pollen inside tomato flowers to dry up before fertilization can happen. The plant then sheds the useless flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani fɔmɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aba. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni ekɛto nu kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to look weak even after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they quickly drink up the water and eat the fertilizer before your planted crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya dani otso lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: What are the best months for me to start planting cocoa on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mabɔi kookoo dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The main recommended time for you to do your primary cocoa planting is in March and April.
ga: Be titri ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛdu shishijee kookoo lɛ ji March kɛ April.

english: What month should I target for my main cocoa planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should target March and April as the primary period to plant your cocoa seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ohiɛ afɔ March kɛ April nɔ akɛ be titri ni akɛduɔ kookoo dumɔwui.

english: Is March a good time for me to put my new cocoa seedlings into the ground?
ga: Ani March ji be ni hi kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei baawo shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, March and April are the ideal early months to begin planting cocoa on your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, March kɛ April ji shishijee nyɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ oje kookoo dumɔ shishi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: If my cocoa seedlings fail to survive after the first planting, when can I replace them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ hu? Mɛɛ be manyɛ matsake dumɔwui?

english: If you experience issues with your initial planting, June and July are the right months to replant your cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ naagba miikpe yɛ kookoo dumɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ, June kɛ July ji nyɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ odu kookoo hee.

english: When is the second planting window for me to replace cocoa trees that did not grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ be manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ koni mikɛto kokoo tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: The second planting window to replace failed cocoa plants takes place in June and July.
ga: Dumɔ be ni ji enyɔ ni akɛtoɔ kookoo tsei ni efite lɛ najiaŋ lɛ baa yɛ June kɛ July mli.

english: Why would I need to plant cocoa again in June and July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu kookoo ekoŋŋ yɛ June kɛ July mli lɛ?

english: June and July are set aside as a second planting period to fix issues and replant cocoa seedlings that did not survive the first planting.
ga: Ato June kɛ July akɛ dumɔ be ni ji enyɔ koni akɛsaa naagba lɛ ni adu kookoo dumɔwui ni ehiɛɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant cocoa seedlings more than once within the same year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui fe shikome yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, you can carry out planting activities up to three times in a single year through main plantings, replantings, and follow-ups.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofee dumɔ nitsumɔi ni shɛɔ etɛ yɛ afi kome mli kɛtsɔ dumɔ titri, dumɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ nɔ.

english: How many total times can I plant cocoa on my farm before the year ends?
ga: Kookoo enyiɛ manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani afi lɛ aba naagbee?

english: You can plant cocoa up to three times in one year, starting with March-April, moving to June-July for replanting, and completing with follow-ups.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kookoo shii etɛ yɛ afi mli. Kɛjɛ March-April Tsɔɔmɔ yɛ June-July mli koni akɛdu ekoŋŋ ni agbe nifeemɔ lɛ naa.

english: What is meant by doing follow-up cocoa planting on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ aaadu kookoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Follow-up planting refers to additional rounds of planting done after the main and second planting windows, allowing you to plant up to three times in a year.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ dumɔ ni akɛfataa he yɛ dumɔ be titri lɛ kɛ dumɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ shii etɛ yɛ afi mli.

english: What schedule should I follow if I want to plant cocoa multiple times throughout the year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛjianɔtoo esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni madu kookoo shii abɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: You should do your main planting in March and April, handle any replanting issues in June and July, and conduct follow-up plantings to complete up to three rounds before the year ends.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee dumɔwui titri lɛ yɛ March kɛ April mli. Tsuɔ dumɔwui ahe saji ahe nii yɛ June kɛ July mli. ni aya nɔ adu koni agbe kpokpai etɛ naa dani afi lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees not bearing any pods even though I planted them over a year ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko beni midu lɛ nɔ ni fe afi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to establish strong root systems and branches before they can support heavy fruit. Most cocoa varieties take three to five years to start producing pods, so early growth focuses entirely on building a healthy tree.
ga: Cacao tsei he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi kɛ amɛniji ni mli wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii. Kookoo henɔi babaoo heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ fã lɛ kɔɔ tso ni wa ni aaafee lɛ he.

english: I planted my pepper seeds four days ago, but nothing has come out of the soil yet; did my seeds die?
ga: Midu pepper dumɔwui gbii ejwɛ ni eho nɛ. Shi nɔ ko nɔ ko ejeee kpo kɛjɛko shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo. Ani miseshibii lɛ egboi?

english: Pepper seeds naturally take time to germinate, usually taking between 7 to 14 days to push through the soil. They need steady moisture and warm soil during this quiet underground stage before green shoots appear.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ he miihia be dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao nu ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be ni yɔɔ dioo mli dani ŋmeii eŋɔlii lɛ baaje kpo.

english: If I apply double the recommended fertilizer to my maize, will it grow twice as fast and mature earlier?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa he ŋaa akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ toi enyɔ tsu nii lɛ, Ani ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaakwɛ oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: Adding too much fertilizer at once can burn the plant's roots and ruin your crop. Crops grow best when given nutrients in steady, correct amounts at specific stages rather than trying to force rapid growth.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛná niyenii ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni onyɛ dalɛ oya nɔ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with small ears instead of healthy, full grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii baa. Yɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ

english: Why is it necessary to weed my farm early when my crops are still tiny seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwu bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and easily choked out by fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the sunlight, water, and nutrients they need during their most critical starting stage.
ga: Tsei bibii waaa ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ miimɔ amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná hulu, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛshishijee bei ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off some healthy-looking branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots, called suckers, helps the plant direct its main energy and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Side shoots ni ajieɔ Enɛɛmɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why does my tomato crop need much more water when it starts flowering than when I first planted it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi-tomatoi lɛ beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi fe beni midu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: As crops grow bigger and begin forming flowers and fruits, their water needs increase significantly because water is used to build the fruit pulp, whereas seedlings only need enough water to keep roots moist.
ga: Beni tso lɛ daa ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai feemɔ Nu ni ataoɔ lɛ etee hiɛ waa akɛni akɛ nu feɔ aduawai amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready for harvest if the tubers grow underground where I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ hu?

english: Cassava usually takes 9 to 12 months to mature, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛɔ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many of their early flowers before any small fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ fɔɔ oya dani aduawai bibii baa lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can possibly support. The tree drops excess flowers on purpose so it can save energy to feed and grow the remaining strong fruits.
ga: Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to cut down my old, unproductive cocoa trees completely or keep harvesting the few pods left on them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo mi-cacao tso momo ni wooo yibii lɛ kwraa loo makpa ŋmeii fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Removing old, disease-prone trees allows you to clear the land and replant modern, high-yielding cocoa varieties that will produce far more pods in the long run than keeping dying trees.
ga: Kɛji ojie tsei ni egbɔ ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ, obaanyɛ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni odu kookoo henɔi heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni baaha ŋmeii babaoo aba yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli fe tsei ni miigboi ni ooodu.

english: Why does my farm produce very little harvest even though I spend every day working on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifiteɔ shika daa gbi yɛ mli moŋ?

english: Hard work alone cannot overcome aging cocoa trees or tired soil; without proper pruning, clearing overgrown weeds, or replenishing soil nutrients, old crops naturally slow down their yield.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ nyɛŋ aye kookoo tsei ni egbɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ kunim. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa bɛ lɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he Tsei momo lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens to my soil if I leave my farmland uncleared and covered in bush for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ tsei ebɔ he be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Leaving land uncleared allows weeds and wild plants to suck up nutrients, harbor destructive pests, and make it much harder for new crops to establish roots when you finally plant.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni ajieee jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaŋɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei amli lɛ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ teeɔ Ni enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei heei akɛ amɛbaafee shishifãi beni naagbee lɛ odu amɛ lɛ.

english: If I clear all the wild bushes off my plot, won't the hot sun damage the bare soil before my new crops grow?
ga: Kɛji mijie koo mli tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ekpãtãŋ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ hiɛ dani mitsei heei lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Clearing exposes the soil temporarily, but planting temporary cover crops or shade plants like plantains right away shields the ground from heat and preserves the moisture your young crops need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ kpo yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi kɛ́ odu be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How long does a newly planted hybrid cocoa tree take before it starts giving me pods to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii koni mikɛkpa?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees grow faster than older wild varieties and usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years if they get enough shade, water, and care.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya fe koo mli tsei ni etsɛ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛjeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná hulutsoo, nu kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting plantains alongside young cocoa is ideal because the broad plantain leaves provide essential shade for the young cocoa while giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Ejaakɛ plantain baai lɛ mli lɛɛ Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by excessive shade and damp conditions; clearing wild bushes and pruning thick tree branches lets sunlight in and air circulate, which keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi. Tsɔɔmɔ koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ ni ofolɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli koni hulu la abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing flowers that drop off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree lacks nutrients, water, or sunlight, or when pests attack them; feeding the soil and properly managing tree shade helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, nu loo hulu la, loo kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ tso mli ŋmɔlɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: No, you should keep some tall forest trees because young cocoa trees need partial shade to protect their leaves from sunburn, though you should trim heavy branches so enough light reaches the ground.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oha tsei lɛ ahi shi shɔŋŋ yɛ koo lɛ mli ejaakɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo fioo ko koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ koni la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cleared land has good, healthy soil for planting new crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni mijie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛduɔ tsei heei?

english: Healthy farm soil is dark, crumbles easily in your hands, stays moist after rain, and contains decaying leaves or organic matter that feeds young crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kpakpa mli lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Haa ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ hewalɛ.

english: If I spray my crop field with pest medicine, how does that actually help the plant grow better?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Spraying stops insects and diseases from eating leaves and stems. When the plant is protected, it can use all its water and food energy to produce healthy shoots, flowers, and fruits instead of constantly repairing damage.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai aye baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛji abu tsei ahe lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeya nɔ esaa nɔ ni efite lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when insects attack the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua tso lɛ?

english: When insects bite or suck sap from cocoa leaves, the tree gets stressed and cuts off food to the damaged parts to protect the rest of the stem, causing damaged leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ loo amɛnu nu ni jɛɔ kookoo baai amli lɛ Tso lɛ haoɔ ni efoɔ niyenii kɛyaa he ni efite lɛ koni ekɛbu tso lɛ shishi ni eshwɛ lɛ he. Ehaa baai ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: High moisture and humidity encourage mold and fungal spores to grow on leaf surfaces, which blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf and causes spots to spread.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa kɛ fɛ̃i woɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when there is no shade above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots that cannot draw up water fast enough in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains to shield them until their root systems grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do cassava plants lose all their leaves in the dry season but stay alive underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baa fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Shi ani wala yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to stop water from evaporating out of the plant. The roots underground go into a resting state and save energy until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ boteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes when the days get very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out pollen inside the flowers, causing the tree to drop its blossoms because it cannot successfully form seeds or fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn reddish or purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ tsuru loo purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is too cool or lacks enough available phosphorus, which the crop needs early on to build strong root systems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ loo fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa kɛjɛ shishijee koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and woody instead of swelling up with starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee mlɛo ni amɛfee tamɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the ground is too hard for them to expand easily, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the main nutrient the plant uses to store starch in the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee mlɛo oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃. Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛtoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does wild grass grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds have shallow, tough roots ready to absorb moisture immediately, whereas cultivated crops take longer to settle their roots and start expanding after planting.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni wa ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop making new flowers if I leave ripe peppers on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi heei kɛji mishi pepper ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Once a pepper plant holds mature fruits with ripe seeds, it assumes its job of reproduction is complete. Picking ripe peppers signals the plant to produce new flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ pepper tso lɛ wo yibii lɛ, no lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni dumɔwui lɛ hu ekwɛ̃. Abuɔ fɔmɔ lɛ akɛ eshɛ he. Pepper ni ekwɛ̃ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ebaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei.

english: I have just acquired a piece of land to start farming, so how do I know which crops will grow best on it?
ga: Etsɛko tsɔ ni mihe shikpɔŋ koni mikɛje ŋmɔ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Different crops thrive in different soil types and climate conditions. For example, deep loamy soils with good drainage are great for maize and vegetables, while cocoa prefers fertile, well-shaded soil. Checking what grows successfully on neighboring farms or having your soil tested will guide your choice.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi anɔ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa kɛ aduawai. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ hulutsoo kpakpa. Nɔ ni adu jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli lɛ ni oookwɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ni ooofee lɛ baakudɔ nɔ ni ohalaa lɛ.

english: I am retiring soon and want a crop that does not require heavy daily physical labor, so what should I plant?
ga: Etsɛŋ ni mikɛ mihe baawo hejɔɔmɔ mli ni miitao tsei ni biɔ nitsumɔ ni tsii daa gbi. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ madu?

english: Tree crops like cashew or fruit crops like plantain require less daily intensive maintenance once established compared to delicate vegetable crops like tomatoes or peppers, making them easier to manage as you get older.
ga: Tso tsei tamɔ cashews loo aduawai tsei tamɔ plantains biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ pɛ. Kɛ akɛto aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oookwɛ nɔ beni odara lɛ.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant to start making money quickly while waiting for long-term cash crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni mabɔi shika namɔ oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Short-season crops like maize, peppers, tomatoes, or cucumbers mature within 2 to 4 months. Planting these allows you to generate quick income to support your farm while waiting several years for long-term crops like cocoa, oil palm, or cashew to produce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tomato loo kukumba shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 4 mli. Enɛɛmɛi akwɛmɔ haa onáa shika oya ni okɛyeɔ obuaa oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ afii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ kookoo, mu loo cashew nuts.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and look weak when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills the air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen. When nitrogen intake stops, the plant leaves lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni akɛhaa lɛ kpa lɛ, Tse lɛ baai lɛ baaje amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Inspecting under the leaves and treating pests early prevents stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and look thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, water, and space. When weeds grow aggressively, they steal the essential resources your crops need to develop strong stems and leaves.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ ŋwɛi mli beni jwɛi lɛ daraa oya Ebaaju nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otso lɛ koni ená shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Is it a good idea to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within a few months, leaving the field open for the slower-growing cassava to expand its roots and leaves for the rest of the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Ashiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmei lɛ ada blɛoo koni egbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller every year if I keep planting it on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly on the same land exhausts the specific soil nutrients that plant relies on and allows soil-borne pests to build up. Rotating crops or leaving the soil to rest helps restore nutrient levels.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ afite, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aná amɛhe shi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake loo ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time of year to plant my crops so they do not dry up and die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu tsei? Koni tsei lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi?

english: Planting should coincide with the arrival of the rainy season so young plants receive constant moisture to build strong root systems. Watching seasonal weather patterns and planting right after the first major rains reduces drought risk.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ akpã gbee bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akwɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yaa nɔ yɛ be mli lɛ, ni adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ he oshara lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I tell when my maize is fully ripe and ready for harvest so it does not spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard and cannot be easily pierced with a fingernail. Harvesting at this stage prevents field mold and pest damage.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ niji atsɔ mli mlɛo. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the soil unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard after I burn the bush on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa beni mishã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani midu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning removes the natural cover of dead leaves and organic matter that traps moisture. Without this protective layer, the hot sun bakes the bare ground and destroys nutrients needed for healthy crop growth.
ga: Shãa jieɔ baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Yams need deep, loose, and well-draining soil free from big rocks so the roots can swell easily into large tubers without rotting in trapped water.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ebɛ tɛi wuji ahe No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ bulb agboi mlɛo ni amɛgbooo yɛ nu ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mli.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water during dry weather. Once the rains return, fresh green leaves will grow back without harming the tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni efiteee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry period. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die before the regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off when the Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: The Harmattan wind is very dry and strips moisture from the trees. Cocoa trees drop their flowers and young pods to conserve water and protect themselves from dying.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli. Cacao tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil, which prevents the blossoms from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why are small holes in my pepper leaves reducing the number of peppers I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu lɛ ji bibioo lɛ? yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ, ni no haa pepper ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi

english: Insects chew holes in the leaves, which reduces the leaf surface area available to catch sunlight. Without enough sunlight, the plant cannot create enough energy to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Kplukai ŋmɔɔ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli Enɛ baaha baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds while my maize is still small instead of waiting until it grows tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ jwɛi be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi ebaada lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have small roots and struggle to compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives the crop space and food to build strong stalks.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha aná he ko ni adu kɛ niyenii ni akɛfee tsei ni wa.

english: Use the hard, mature middle section of a healthy stem from a plant that is 8 to 12 months old. Avoid the soft top section because it rots easily, and avoid the very bottom section because it takes too long to sprout.
ga: Kɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ tso ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ mli fã ni wa ni eda lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he, ejaakɛ egboɔ oya. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shishigbɛ nɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Should I plant my cassava stem cuttings flat in the soil or standing up at an angle?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu cassava niji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo yɛ koŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cuttings at a 45-degree angle with the buds pointing upward is usually best. This helps the roots grow deep enough to reach soil moisture during dry periods while giving the tubers room to swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ 45 degree angle mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa yitso he gbɛ lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to make ridges or mounds before planting root crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔma ŋshɔkei loo ŋshɔkei dani wɔdu shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges loosen the hard soil, making it easy for roots to expand into large, healthy tubers. They also help rainwater drain away so the tubers do not sit in water and rot.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi ni mli wa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akabote nu mli ni amɛkagboi.

english: Why do my cassava plants rot underground when there is heavy rain on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water collects on your farm without draining, it smothers the roots, causing bacteria and fungi to multiply and rot the tubers until they become soft and inedible.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo lɛ, efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni anyɛɛɛ aye.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to make green leaves. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK will help the leaves turn green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ NPK ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: I noticed caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my maize plants; what damage do they cause?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ ŋmeii miiye mi-abele tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ. Mɛɛ fitemɔ amɛfiteɔ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the heart of the plant where new leaves grow. Destroying this growing center prevents the maize plant from forming healthy ears, so they need to be controlled early with approved sprays or neem oil.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa tso lɛ tsui he ni baai heei ekwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpata he ni aduɔ nii yɛ nɛɛ hiɛ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ akudɔ amɛ mra. kɛ neem spray loo fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ

english: How does leaving weeds around my cassava plants affect the size of my yield at harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te ŋmei tso lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds crowd cassava plants, the crops spend their energy fighting for survival instead of producing large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni jwɛi ebɔle ŋmei tso lɛ he lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ baawu koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmei wuji.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop is ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Most improved cassava varieties mature within 9 to 12 months when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. You can carefully dig up one test stem to check if the tubers are thick before harvesting the rest.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa kaa tso kome mli koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli edɔ dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some cassava tubers taste bitter and prove unsafe to eat straight after boiling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi komɛi mli edɔ ni ehiii akɛ ayeɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ahoo lɛ?

english: Bitter cassava varieties contain higher levels of natural plant chemicals that protect them from pests. These bitter types must be processed through grating, fermenting, or drying into products like gari to remove the bitterness and make them safe to eat.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ fa babaoo yɛ cassava henɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Esa akɛ ajie nɛkɛ tsofai ni mli edɔ nɛɛ, afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo agbi amɛ ni afee nibii tamɔ gari koni ajie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same land, or will one spoil the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo ebaakpata ŋaa kroko ni ato lɛ hiɛ?

english: You can plant them together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly in its first few months. By the time cassava expands and needs full space, the maize is already harvested.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehe hiaa he ko babaoo. Agbɛnɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to plant cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei?

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, dark, well-drained soil that holds moisture without getting waterlogged. If water stays pooled on your land for days after heavy rain, the cocoa roots will rot and the trees will not survive.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing and falling leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are getting too much direct sunlight or not enough water. Young cocoa needs shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect their tender leaves from the harsh sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Cocoa bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce many flowers, but no pods actually grow from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani pods ko bɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them before pods can form. If you spray harsh chemicals at the wrong time or remove all leaf litter from the ground where these insects live, the flowers cannot turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛfee pollination dani pods lɛ afee. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwie shi yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo ojie baai lɛ amli jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree take from planting before it starts producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years, while older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, shading, and soil nutrition help them bear fruit faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing very tall with thin trunks instead of spreading out wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã babaoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees stretch upward searching for light when the shade trees above them are too thick. Trimming excess branches from overhead shade trees lets enough sunlight through so the cocoa trees grow thick trunks and produce pods on their main branches.
ga: Kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛtao la kɛ́ ŋwɛi hulutsoo be lɛ mli tsɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ atsɔ mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ feɔ tso ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmeii yɛ niji wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are some of my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning overhead branches to let in air and sunlight, alongside removing the infected pods quickly, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɔ́, kɛ fɔ́ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What causes swollen, bulged lumps on the stems and branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛniji anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Swollen branches are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread between trees by mealybug insects. Because there is no chemical cure for the virus, infected trees must be cut down to protect the healthy ones nearby.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji cocoa bud virus hela ni efuu lɛ he okadi, ni mealybugs gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa hela lɛ. Esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees dry out and look burned during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ egbi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry months and Harmattan, hot sun and dry winds remove moisture from cocoa leaves faster than roots can pull it from the dry ground. Placing dead leaves or plant materials around the base of the trunk helps keep soil moist.
ga: Yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ kɛ Harmattan lɛ amli lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛjɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi loo tsei ahe nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods smaller and lighter this year compared to my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto tsutsu ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Smaller pods usually indicate that the soil lacks essential nutrients or that the tree suffered from water shortage during pod development. Insect pests like capsids can also suck sap from stems and prevent pods from fully developing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo tso lɛ naa nu ni faaa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids lɛ hu baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli ni amɛtsi pod lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa trees using seeds taken directly from pods harvested on my own farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ makwɛ cacao tsei heei?

english: You can plant farm-saved seeds, but certified hybrid seeds bought from approved seed nurseries grow faster, resist common diseases better, and yield significantly more pods than seeds saved from regular farms.
