ga: Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni ato yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛlɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ni ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ fa kwraa fe dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: How does putting a net mesh over my vegetable farm protect my crops from bugs?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋshɔŋlooi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: A fine net acts as a physical barrier that stops harmful insects like whiteflies and moths from landing on your crops to lay eggs or feed, keeping your vegetables healthy without relying heavily on chemical sprays.
ga: Mesh kpakpa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii anaa. Kaaha amɛtara oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwo ŋmeii loo amɛha niyenii. Ha o-vegetables lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and turn dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from young leaves, or by extreme heat stress where the plant curls its leaves to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Tso lɛ baafolɔ ebaa lɛ mli koni nu akafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants put all their energy into growing tall stems and leafy leaves instead of flowering. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit set.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai amli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Nitrogen kɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wilt and die when the afternoon sun gets too harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ tso waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots that cannot absorb water fast enough to replace what leaves lose in high heat. Providing light shade during the hottest hours helps keep them cool until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaato baai ni elaaje yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up before the cobs are full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi dani ŋmãa lɛ eyiɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from older leaves at the bottom to feed new growth at the top, which reduces your final yield if not corrected with fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ baa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii asaaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and woody even when the plant stems grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ dara waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil to expand its roots. If the soil is hard or compacted, the roots cannot swell into big tubers, causing the plant to put its energy into stem growth instead.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Yucca koni eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashwere ni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow thick, healthy stems.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting cowpeas next to my maize make the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ tsina ŋmei yɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli waa?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Nearby maize plants feed on this added nitrogen to grow greener and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fata he nɛɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my garden egg plants fall off before forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress from irregular watering, severe heat, or a shortage of plant nutrients like calcium that are required to hold and develop the fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ calcium, ni he hiaa koni ekɛma shi ni ewo yibii lɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani mifee klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when sudden heavy rainfall or overwatering occurs after a dry spell. The inside leaves take up water quickly and expand faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo nu babaoo ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe bɔ ni baa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do buyers reject some of my crops at the market even when they look normal to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi yɛ jara nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha mi moŋ.

english: Buyers check for hidden defects like mold, insect holes, or soft spots. Sorting your produce into good and bad batches before going to market ensures you get a fair price and do not waste energy transporting spoiled goods.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ musu, kooloo bu loo hei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ onibii lɛ to kui kpakpai kɛ kui gbohii amli dani eshɛ jara nɔ lɛ, ehaa onine shɛɔ jara ni sa nɔ, ni ofiteee hewalɛ ni okɛ nibii ni efite lɛ yaa.

english: Why should I separate damaged or bruised crops from good ones in my harvest bags immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite loo ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛwo ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: One rotten or damaged fruit carries fungi or bacteria that quickly spread to healthy crops trapped in the same bag. Separating them immediately keeps the rest of your harvest fresh during storage and transport.
ga: Yibii kome ni egbo loo efite lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋmei loo hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ yɛ kotoku kome mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbala amɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi ehee yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or larger shade trees to act as natural umbrellas until their root system is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and large cobs, they stretch upward quickly just to reach light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso agbo. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or a lack of water. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying during harsh weather conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and rot if I leave them in the ground too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stop making starch once mature and begin absorbing excess underground water. Leaving them unharvested causes the starch to break down into water, leading to root rot and poor quality.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ starch feemɔ kɛji ahoo ni ebɔi nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ ni akpaaa amɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli agbala ni etsɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to produce food. Heavy rains can also wash nitrogen away from the root area, causing the leaves to lose color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni tsei kɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ehaa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, sunken spots at the bottom while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii ni ebote shishi yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven, preventing the plant roots from taking up calcium consistently from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry heavy bunches of fruit at the top. Heap extra soil around the base of the plant and use wooden Y-sticks to prop up the heavy stems so wind cannot push them over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Okɛ sũ krokomɛi abɔle tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ tsei ni tamɔ Y atsu nii ni okɛfi tso lɛ shishi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatsɔ mli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into fine dust and spoil inside jute bags after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ sũ bibii ni egboɔ yɛ jute kotokui amli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils eat the inside of the maize, while trapped moisture causes mold growth. Grain must be completely dried before storage and stored in insect-proof bags or treated appropriately.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ corn weevils lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃. Esa akɛ ŋmaa lɛ agbi kwraa dani akɛto ni akɛto kotokui ni kooloi nyɛŋ abote mli loo yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge, bushy leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight and air reach the pods helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Extreme heat or lack of water can cause tomato flowers to dry out and fall off before pollination happens. Keeping the soil constantly moist around the roots helps save the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi dani amɛhe afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, light bunches when many young shoots grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: The extra young shoots (suckers) steal food and water from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii krokomɛi (tso lɛ) juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa plantain lɛ hiɔ shi agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko baama sweet potato wain tso ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which goes down into the ground to build large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the maize crop naturally and keeps the soil healthy for next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that give shade and keep the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a natural protection trick. The plant curls its leaves to reduce the area exposed to the sun so it loses less water through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ ŋaa ni buɔ mɔ he. Tso lɛ baafolɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ lɛ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my orange trees shed many of their young green fruits right after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sudden heavy rainfall after a long dry spell shocks the tree with a rapid intake of water, causing it to drop delicate young fruits. Keeping soil moisture steady through mulching prevents this.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ hosoɔ kɛ nu oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: What is greenhouse farming, and why are some farmers using it to grow vegetables?
ga: Mɛni ji okwaayeli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli? Ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ aduawai?

english: Greenhouse farming means growing crops inside a framed structure covered with protective plastic or netting. It protects high-value crops like tomatoes and peppers from heavy rain, extreme sun, and insect pests so you can produce good quality vegetables all year round.
ga: Greenhouse okwaayeli tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛ plastic loo tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ehà nɔ lɛ mli. Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni naa wa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to set up a greenhouse right away if I want to grow vegetables?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni madu aduawai lɛ, ani esa akɛ mato ŋmɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Setting up a greenhouse requires a big investment. Before building one, you should first make sure you have reliable buyers lined up, as greenhouse crops are expensive to produce and spoil quickly if you cannot sell them immediately.
ga: Ni aaato greenhouse lɛ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ shika babaoo awo mli. Dani obaama nitsumɔhe Esa akɛ okwɛ koni oná mɛi ni heɔ nii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afeemɔ jara wa ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji onyɛɛɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can I grow any crop I want inside a greenhouse, or are there specific ones that work best?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Mɛni he hiaa mi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo ani tso pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Greenhouses work best for high-value, fast-growing vegetables like sweet peppers, tomatoes, and cucumbers. These crops sell at higher prices, which helps you recover the high cost of building and maintaining the greenhouse.
ga: Greenhouses tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ aduawai ni jara wa, ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmei, tomato, kɛ kukumba. Ahɔ̃ɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shika babaoo ni okɛmaa ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What does it mean to have a ready market before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji jarayeli ni asaa he dani ajeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ shishi lɛ shishi?

english: Having a ready market means you have identified or agreed with buyers, such as market women, hotels, or processors, who are willing to purchase your harvest at a specific time and price before you put seeds in the ground.
ga: Ni ooona jarayeli he ko ni asaa he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oyɔse loo okpɛlɛ mɔ ko ni baahe nii lɛ nɔ, tamɔ jarayeli yoo, hotɛl loo nitsumɔhe ko. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhe onibii yɛ be kɛ jara pɔtɛɛ ko mli dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do prices drop so low in the market when everyone in my village harvests at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli jara lɛ ba shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest and sell the same crop at the exact same time, there is more produce than buyers need. This oversupply forces farmers to drop their prices just to sell perishable crops before they rot.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee babaoo fe nɔ ni hɔlɔ lɛ taoɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ nyɛɔ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛba amɛjara shi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya dani amɛfite kɛkɛ.

english: Should I delay planting my crops if there is already too much of that produce in the market?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adumɔ mli kɛji akɛ efa babaoo yɛ jara nɔ momo?

english: Yes, holding off or adjusting your planting schedule helps you avoid harvesting during an oversupply. Planting slightly later allows you to harvest when supply in the market is low and prices are higher.
ga: Hɛɛ, be ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ ni oootsi kɛya sɛɛ loo otsake lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okpa nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni nibii babaoo fa fe nine lɛ. Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli fioo lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nii yɛ be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ faaa ni jara hu yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I check if market buyers actually want the crop I plan to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ miisumɔ nibii ni mito he gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can visit local market centers, talk to crop traders, or ask extension officers about current demand trends, market prices, and which crops buyers struggle to find at different times of the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jarayelɔ lɛ agba sane Aloo bi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ nibii ni ataoɔ amrɔ nɛɛ, jarayeli jara kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ naa naagba yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli lɛ ahe sane.

english: How does joining a local farmer group or cooperative benefit my farming business?
ga: Te okwaafoi akuu loo kuu ko ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mli lɛ baaye abua mi okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Joining a group allows you to combine your harvest with other farmers to attract bigger buyers, negotiate better prices, reduce transport costs, and learn successful farming practices from experienced group members.
ga: Kuu ko ni okɛ ohe woɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi feɔ onibii ni okɛbaahe nii lɛ ekome koni okɛgbala jarayelɔi wuji. Tsɔɔmɔ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ Okɛ gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo aba shi ni okase okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni yeɔ omanye kɛjɛ kuu lɛ mli bii ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why should I follow the farming methods used by other successful farmers in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɔ okwaayeli gbɛi ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Adopting proven techniques from successful local farmers lowers your risk of failure because those practices have already been tested and worked well under your local soil, weather, and market conditions.
ga: Ŋaai ni ana he odaseyeli ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ aŋɔɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ amɛbaafee nɔ ko lɛ baa shi. Ejaakɛ aka nakai nifeemɔi lɛ akwɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ jarayeli shihilɛi ashishi.

english: Why do high-value crops like tomatoes rot quickly if I cannot sell them immediately after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa tamɔ tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: High-value fresh vegetables contain a lot of water and continue to breathe after harvest. In hot weather, they lose water rapidly and decay within days if they are not sold quickly or stored in a cool place.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ aduawai heei ni jara wa waa lɛ amli. ni eyaa nɔ emuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Efiteɔ nu oya ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji akɛ ahɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ oya loo akɛtooo he ko ni mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when there is no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate root systems and tender leaves that lose moisture quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a protective cover that shelters cocoa from heat stress until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and energy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛha hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds lower my harvest even after I apply fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures that your main crop gets all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to spread their leaves into the sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, allowing them to capture maximum sunlight to manufacture food for bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plantain stem for food, water, and soil space. Pruning extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong shoots focuses the plant's energy into producing large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni ahiɛ tso lɛ mli tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ahi yibii wuji ni tsii ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny, ragged holes appearing in the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii ni etse ehe lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are often caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm eating the tender leaves. Spraying with recommended organic or chemical pest control early prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any small fruits start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi efee?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil minerals like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying balanced fertilizer helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil near the base of the plant. Gently digging around one root lets you check if the tubers have reached full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmei ko jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi lɛ eko he blɛoo bɔni afee ni okwɛ kɛji bulb lɛ eshɛ elɛɛmɔ he.

english: How do I know when it is safe to plant my maize seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting right after the first rain is risky because the ground can dry out quickly if the rains stop. It is safest to wait until there are two or three steady rains so the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I not save and replant seeds harvested from my high-yielding hybrid maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their high-yielding strength after the first generation, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests if replanted. Purchasing fresh, certified hybrid seeds each season guarantees strong and uniform crop yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ daa afi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear, open field without any tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I grow my yams under big leafy trees, or do they need direct sunlight to produce good tubers?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato yɛ tsei ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi? Aloo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛná bulb kpakpai?

english: Yams need full, direct sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth. Planting yams under heavy tree shade will cause the vines to stay thin and weak, resulting in small tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ tsei ni tsii lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha wain tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji yitso bibioo

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the maize plant is missing nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Leaf curling is often a defense mechanism against heat and lack of water, but it can also mean tiny insects like whiteflies have transmitted a plant virus to your tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ he. Shi ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ kooloo bibioo ko, tamɔ whitefly, kɛ tso mli hela ko ewo otomatoi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge leafy branches but produce very small roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and leafy green foliage instead of swelling its root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ kɛ akɛto potassium he. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How does putting dry grass around my plantain stems help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi-plantains lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and keeps plantain roots hydrated during dry weather.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa plantain shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: What will happen to my corn if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When corn seeds are planted too closely together, the growing plants compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stems and very small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow much slower and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, effectively starving your plants before they can reach maturity.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Why is it good to trim off some of the side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Removing extra side branches reduces unnecessary foliage that drains plant energy, allowing the tomato plant to direct its nutrients toward producing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa baai ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip inward, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea helps the plant stay green and build large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa ko shishigbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efee V su kɛjɛ enaagbɛ kɛtee mligbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that like maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like peanuts, cowpeas, or soybeans restores soil nutrients and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, loo soybeans. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing lots of big green leaves but failing to produce any flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: This usually happens when pepper plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or high-nitrogen manure. Excessive nitrogen encourages the plant to focus all its energy on leaf foliage rather than spending energy to blossom and produce pepper fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji akɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ babaoo. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ,.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my maize seeds when planting instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ

english: Planting seeds too close forces the young crops to fight with each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough room to absorb what it needs to produce thick stalks and big, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tso lɛ shishifã ni mli wa kɛ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain suckers in the same field as young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and can easily burn or dry out under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that create a shade umbrella to shield young cocoa plants and keep the soil damp during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni akɛwoɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe ŋmɔlɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from my farm before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop seedlings and will quickly steal the sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients that your seeds need to germinate. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a head start without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei dumɔwui. Ni ejuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa odumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal attack called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excessive cocoa branches allows sunlight and air to move through the farm, drying up moisture and stopping the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod hela. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kookoo ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before they turn into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, prolonged dry soil, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and water helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ okɛ muji kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell underground cassava tubers are big enough and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava plants show they are mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground directly around the root base begins to swell and crack open from the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Yucca tso ko tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Trunk lɛ mli bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. kɛ hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines turn brown and dry up completely when the crop is almost mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shweremɔ lɛ?

english: This natural drying of the yam vine signals that the plant has finished growing leaves and is transferring all remaining energy down into the underground tuber. Once the vine dries out completely, the yam tuber is mature and ready for harvesting.
ga: Nɛkɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekwɛ baai ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ miiwo shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni wain tso lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ Agbɛnɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Can I grow rice together with other crops on the same farm?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, upland rice varieties can be grown alongside crops like maize, cassava, or vegetables. This practice, called intercropping, helps you maximize your farmland, reduces the risk of crop failure, and provides continuous harvests throughout the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ shi ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What are the benefits of planting food crops like vegetables alongside my main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ aduawai, ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ he?

english: Planting vegetables like pepper or legumes alongside main grains gives you quick food and income while waiting for your main harvest. Legumes also add nitrogen back into the soil, which helps feed the main grain crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oŋmaa titrii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oná niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmaa titri lɛ. Legumes hu kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii aha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: Is it bad if I keep touching or walking through my rice plants while they are growing?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mitee nɔ mita mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe loo minyiɛ amɛmli be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Yes, frequent walking or disturbing the plants during grain development can break delicate flowering stalks and damage root systems. Once the crop is established and weeded early, it grows best when left to mature with minimal interference.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni nyiɛɔ loo ni gbaa mɔ naa shii abɔ Yɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ, fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Beni adu tsei jogbaŋŋ ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: When should I stop clearing weeds from my rice field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: You should clear weeds during the first 3 to 6 weeks after planting. Once the rice forms a full canopy and begins to flower, walking through the field can damage the stems, so it is better to leave the field undisturbed.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa ni ebɔi fɔmɔ ŋmɔji amli nyiɛmɔ baanyɛ afite ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmɔji lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko akagbala amɛ.

english: How can I check if my crops are healthy without walking through and damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni mikɛnyiɛɛɛ nɔ ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: You can monitor crop health from the farm bunds or field edges by checking leaf color and plant height. Deep green leaves and upright, sturdy tillers show the crop is doing well without needing to step inside.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔ lɛ naa kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ahe su kɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei niji ni wa ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni atsɔ mli.

english: Why do seed officers mention so many different names for rice varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi tsɛɔ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi babaoo gbɛi lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties are bred for specific land conditions. Some varieties thrive in flooded lowlands, while others grow well on dry uplands, resist local pests, or mature faster, allowing you to pick the right seed for your specific land.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ naa. Henɔi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu afua fɔɔ baa lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo edaa oya Enɛ haa ohalaa dumɔwui ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I secure full harvest rights to the crops I plant on rented land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahiɛ hegbɛ ni miyɔɔ akɛ makpãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛha lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always establish a clear agreement with the landowner before land preparation and clearly mark your farm boundaries. This ensures that you have full legal rights to harvest everything you plant without interference when crops mature.
ga: Feemɔ kpaŋmɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ dani osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okadi oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa mla naa hegbɛi fɛɛ ni okɛbaakpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni odu lɛ ni okɛ ohe wooo mli kɛji tsei lɛ eda.

english: Why is standing water good for lowland rice fields even if I don't work on the field every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ hi lolo kɛha ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli be mli ni mitsuuu nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli daa gbi lɛ?

english: Standing water acts as a natural weed control and keeps nutrients dissolved so the rice roots can absorb them easily. Once water levels are regulated, the crop can thrive on its own with minimal daily labor.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni yeɔ jwɛi anɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya. Kɛji akɛ akudɔ nu lɛ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ akwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ daa gbi nitsumɔ fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why should I encourage my young children to come to the farm and listen to agricultural officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mibii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛba ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛbabo okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ atoi lɛ?

english: Involving young people early allows them to learn modern farming methods, soil care, and business skills. This prepares them to manage the farm successfully in the future and keep the land productive.
ga: Oblahii kɛ oblayei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli mra Ehaa amɛkaseɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi, shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ jarayeli he ŋaa. Enɛ saa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ wɔsɛɛ, ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I teach my children to manage rice crops properly for the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔɔ mibii lɛ bɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji anɔ jogbaŋŋ wɔsɛɛ?

english: Bring them along during key farming activities like seed selection, planting, and harvesting so they observe best practices firsthand, learning how to yield good harvests without destroying the soil.
ga: Okɛ amɛ aya yɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ dumɔwui ahalamɔ, dumɔwui, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni amɛnyiɛ nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ asɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kasemɔ bɔ ni ooofee odu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: If one of my cassava plants gets sick and has yellow, twisted leaves, should I pull it out or leave it alone?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eko hela mɔ lɛ ni eyɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ani esa akɛ majie loo mashi yɛ mli?

english: You should pull it out completely and remove it from your farm. Leaving sick plants in the field allows diseases like Cassava Mosaic Virus to spread to your healthy crops through insects, which can ruin your entire harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbala lɛ kɛya he fɛɛ he ni ojie kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa helai tamɔ cassava virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. ni baanyɛ akpata onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil or that heavy rains have washed away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Improving drainage helps the roots breathe again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to remove some of my maize shoots when they germinate too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmãa ŋmeii komɛi kɛji amɛdara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. Thinning them out gives the remaining stalks enough room and nutrients to produce big, full cobs of corn.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afee ŋmeii lɛ bibii lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily in direct sun. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains next to them acts like a shelter, protecting the young cocoa from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Amɛbaafee ekome kɛtsu nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my tomato plants staying short and refusing to grow bigger even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants stop growing when the soil lacks food or when pests are damaging their roots under the ground. Adding manure or fertilizer gives the roots the food they need to push out new stems and fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛtsi tsei kɛ aduawai heei kɛjɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my soil if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Planting it in the same spot repeatedly wears out the soil's strength, leading to smaller harvests each year unless you rotate crops or add organic fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he.

english: Can I grow any crop I want on low-lying, marshy ground, or do certain plants prefer that soil?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Miisumɔ ni ehi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ? Aloo tsei komɛi sumɔɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Different crops prefer different types of land. Crops like rice thrive in wet, swampy soil, while crops like cassava and sweet potato will rot if their roots stay buried in too much water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baafite kɛji akɛ afu amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli.

english: Weeds are aggressive and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Which crops can I plant that grow quickly so I can sell them and pay my children's school fees on time?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu koni mahɔ̃ɔ ni mawo mibi lɛ skul nyɔmɔ yɛ be naa?

english: Fast-growing vegetables like okra, tomatoes, and leafy greens, or short-season maize, can be harvested in 3 to 4 months, giving you quick income compared to long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra, tomato, kɛ aduawai ni baa eŋɔli yɔɔ mli. Aloo, abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kuku yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ baaha oná shika oya kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo mu ŋmãa he.

english: How do I know when my yams are fully mature and ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmeii ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally near the end of the rainy season, it means the yam tubers under the ground have finished growing and are ready for harvesting.
ga: Beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee he lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling, the leaves reduce the surface area exposed to hot sun and dry winds, which prevents the plant from losing too much moisture through sweating.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know if heat is damaging my tomato plants, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dɔlɛ miifite mi-tomato tsei lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aaatsɔ atsĩ naa?

english: Sunburnt tomatoes develop dry, bleached patches on their leaves and sunburn spots on the fruits. You can protect them by using palm fronds for temporary shade, planting shade crops nearby, or avoiding heavy pruning so the crop's own leaves shade the fruits.
ga: Tomato ni hulu eshã lɛ yɛ hei ni egbi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni hulu eshã yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni okɛaatsu nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Aloo tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni afoɔ waa lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni tso lɛ baai lɛ atsĩ yibii lɛ anaa.

english: How often am I supposed to water my vegetable nursery seedlings during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings need water twice a day—once early in the morning before the sun gets hot and once late in the afternoon. Watering during these cooler times allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply without it evaporating immediately.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui shii enyɔ daa gbi. Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni afeɔ leebi dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Ni ekoŋŋ yɛ shwane mli Nu ni ashwieɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieee shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Should I change my watering schedule from every three days to once a week as my pepper plants grow bigger?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsake be ni mikɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ kɛjɛ gbii etɛ fɛɛ gbii etɛ nɔ kɛya shikome yɛ otsi mli beni mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yes, as pepper plants mature and grow deeper root systems, they prefer less frequent but deeper watering. Deep watering once a week encourages roots to stretch down into the soil, making the plant stronger against dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ pepper tsei lɛ daa ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛsumɔɔ nu fioo kɛ nu ni mli kwɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli jogbaŋŋ shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ mli waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: How can I tell male papaya plants from female papaya plants, and will both produce fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ papaya tso nuu kɛ yoo teŋ? Ni ani amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaawo yibii loo amɛwooo yibii?

english: Male papaya plants produce long dangling stalks covered with many small flowers, but they do not produce fruit. Female plants produce single large flowers directly on the main stem that grow into fruits after pollen is transferred to them.
ga: Papaya tsei hii yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni fĩɔ shi kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. Nɔ ni fa shi nɔ ko jɛɛɛ mli baa Yei tsei woɔ fɔfɔi agbo kome yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ni edaa ni efeɔ aduawai beni akɛ pollen lɛ eha amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are many of the flowers on my watermelon vines falling off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants produce both male flowers and female flowers. Male flowers open first to produce pollen and naturally fall off after a day; only fertilized female flowers will swell and turn into watermelons.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ. Fɔfɔi hii fɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛjie pollen. ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ gbi kome sɛɛ. Fɔfɔi yei ni awo amɛ fɔ lɛ pɛ fũuɔ ni amɛfeɔ watermelon.

english: How deep in the soil am I supposed to plant my yam setts when building mounds?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu sweet potatoes yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni miishɛ tɛŋŋ beni miima gɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam seed setts should be planted about 10 to 15 centimeters deep inside the mound with the sprout buds facing upward. Planting too deep delays growth, while planting too shallow exposes the seed to heat and dry air.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15, ni ŋmeii ni miida lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha edalɛ asɛɛ afo. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi.

english: Why do some farmers plant cassava cuttings slanted in the ground while others plant them straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei niji ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi kui komɛi kwɛɔ amɛ ja?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle makes harvesting easier because tubers grow shallowly on one side. Planting upright buries roots deeper, which helps the crop survive drought but makes digging up tubers harder.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ daaa yɛ he kome. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni ja lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli shi ehaa bulbs ni aaafo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa.

english: Why do my neighbor's cowpeas grow much taller than mine even though we planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ kwɔ kwraa fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crop height varies based on seed variety and soil nutrients. Some cowpea varieties are short bush types, while others are long climbing vines. Soil with high nitrogen also causes plants to spend more energy growing leaves and stems.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta baasoro lɛ yɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa. Cowpeas henɔi komɛi ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii kukuji. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Eji wain tso kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ hu haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi.

english: How long can mature cassava roots stay in the ground before they begin to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi?

english: Mature cassava roots can safely remain unharvested in the soil for several months. However, once you harvest and dig them out of the ground, fresh roots begin to rot within two to three days unless processed quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe ni akpaaa nyɔji babaoo. Shi, kɛji okpa amɛ ni otsi amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Shishifãi heei lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja atsu he nii oya

english: How deep should I actually dig the hole when planting my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu mli kɛyashɛ he ni kɛ́ midu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa seedlings need holes about 30 centimeters wide and 30 centimeters deep. If the hole is too shallow, the main root will bend or stay near the surface, making the plant weak and easily dried out during dry weather.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia bu ni amɛlɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 30 kɛ sɛntimita 30 mlibotemɔ. Kɛji bu lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi titrii lɛ ebɔle loo ebɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Does it matter if the soil at the bottom of the planting hole is hard or loose?
ga: Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ dumɔ bu lɛ shishi lɛ mli wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yes, loosening the soil at the bottom of the hole makes it easy for young roots to push deep into the earth. If the soil at the bottom is hard, root growth stops and the plant stays small and weak.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ bu lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ abote sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa Shishifãi lɛ baakpa shweremɔ. ni tsei lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: How should I remove the plastic bag around the seedling before putting it in the ground?
ga: Dani obaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, te esa akɛ ofee tɛŋŋ ojie plastic kotoku lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli?

english: You must carefully cut the plastic polybag off completely from top to bottom without breaking the ball of soil around the roots. If you leave the bag on, the roots cannot spread and the plant will eventually die.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo polybag lɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋwɛi kɛyashi shishi. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ekumɔɔɔ Kɛji oshi kotoku lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɛɛ eshwaaa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso lɛ baagbo.

english: What should I do right after I put the seedling in the hole and cover it with soil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee beni mikɛ dumɔwu lɛ ewo bu lɛ mli ni mikɛ sũ ha nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Press the soil down gently with your hands around the stem to remove air pockets, making sure the top of the soil ball matches the ground level so water doesn't pool around the stem and rot it.
ga: Okɛ oniji atsu nii ni okɛmi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo. ebɔle tso lɛ he koni ejie kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome. koni nu akabua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ he ni efite

english: Can my children help me plant cocoa seedlings, or does it take special skill?
ga: Ani mibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni madu kookoo dumɔwui? Aloo ebiɔ ŋaa krɛdɛɛ ko?

english: Children can assist with light tasks like carrying seedlings, but an experienced person should place and cover them. Rough handling by inexperienced hands can break the soft roots or damage the main stem.
ga: Gbekɛbii baanyɛ aye abua kɛ nitsumɔi bibii, tamɔ dumɔwui ateremɔ. Shi esa akɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ama shi ni amɛha nɔ. Niji ni bɛ niiashikpamɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa baanyɛ akumɔ shishifãi bibii loo efite tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ.

english: Why is it important to measure spacing instead of planting cocoa wherever there is space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni aaadu kookoo yɛ he fɛɛ he ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing, usually 3 meters by 3 meters, ensures every tree gets enough sunlight, ground nutrients, and airflow. Planting too close leads to overcrowding, poor yields, and rapid spread of diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa, ni bei pii lɛ mitai 3 x mitai 3 lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni hoɔ kɛyaa jɛmɛ lɛ Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii eyiɔ shi fe nine, yibiiwoo ni ehiii, kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily burn under direct hot sun. They need temporary shade from plantains or shade trees during their first two years to trap moisture and keep them cool.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i.

english: What is the best time of the day to put my new seedlings into the farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant early in the morning or late in the afternoon on a rainy or cloudy day. Planting in the hot midday sun causes the young seedling to lose water quickly and wilt before root contact is made.
ga: Esa akɛ adu leebi loo shwane mli. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo atatu gbii anɔ Dumɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Should I put chemical fertilizer into the hole at the exact time I am planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo bu lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: No, putting chemical fertilizer directly in the hole can burn the young tender roots. It is better to let the plant establish its roots for a few weeks before applying fertilizer around the outer edge of the plant.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii lɛ. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ tso lɛ gbɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ama shi otsii fioo komɛi dani awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ he.

english: How long will it take after planting before my new cocoa trees start bringing in income?
ga: Kɛ́ adu agbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani kookoo tsei heei lɛ baabɔi shika feemɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing their first pods in about 2 to 3 years under good care, while older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years before yielding a full harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani eshɛ shweremɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he.

english: What happens to my maize crops if heavy rain causes a nearby river to overflow into my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ho kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Excessive water around plant roots smothers them because roots need air to breathe. If floodwater stays on the field for more than two days, the roots begin to rot, causing maize leaves to turn yellow and growth to stop.
ga: Nu babaoo ni ebɔle Tse lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ miɔ lɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu afua lɛ mli nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe gbii enyɔ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ. Ehaa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look burnt and withered right after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ ewo tsei ahe lɛ, amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer directly against plant roots draws moisture out of the roots, drying them out. Fertilizer should always be placed a few centimeters away from the stem when the soil is moist.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds. During the Harmattan, dry air bakes the foliage faster than the young root system can draw water from the soil, causing the leaves to dry up and drop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shãa baai lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without growing any peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures and dry air cause severe stress to pepper plants. To protect themselves from losing too much water, the plants drop their flowers to save energy instead of spending it on developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Koni obu ohe koni nu babaoo akafite. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite yɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall stems with broad green leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen pushes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen tsirɛɔ tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaa kɛ amɛniji ni daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why are my maize plants producing large cobs, but there are almost no corn kernels inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji shi kɛ́ mikpa lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: If maize experiences high heat or dry conditions while flowering, the silk threads dry out. Without wet silks to catch pollen from the top tassels, the cob cannot form kernels.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Siliki lɛ baagbi. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, siliki ni efɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kob lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui.

english: Why do crops growing close to thick weeds grow much slower and turn pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ ahe lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively for light, water, and plant nutrients in the soil. When weeds take most of the soil's nitrogen, your crops cannot make the green pigment needed to feed themselves and grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛye amɛhe ni amɛdara waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers. Staking lifts the vines so the leaves get maximum sunlight and air movement, which also keeps the leaves dry and free from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow much better when I plant them in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil for both crops, while the tall maize acts as a natural shield against hot winds.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛhaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit. It usually occurs when watering is irregular, which prevents the plant from transporting calcium continuously from the soil to the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ be, ni no haaa ekɛ calcium aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I need to till my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani miduɔ nii?

english: Tilling breaks up hard ground so that plant roots can spread easily, absorb water, and reach nutrients in the soil. It also buries weeds and loosens the soil so young seeds can sprout easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya, amɛŋɔ nu, ni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ehaa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui bibii akwɛ̃ oya.

english: If I finish tilling my land, can I let it sit for a few weeks before I plant my seeds?
ga: Kɛ migbe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ naa Ani manyɛ maha ehi shi otsii fioo komɛi dani madu dumɔwui?

english: It is best to plant shortly after tilling. If the land sits idle for too long, rain will pack the soil hard again, washed-away nutrients will be lost, and weeds will quickly return to take over the land.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu beni adu ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ laajeɔ. Ni jwɛi baaku amɛsɛɛ oya ni amɛbaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I end up using more chemical when I spray my farm myself compared to when I hire experienced sprayers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai babaoo atsu nii kɛ́ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛ tsofa miifɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni akɛ mɔ ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni shwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ he

english: Inexperienced spraying often leads to walking too slowly or spraying the same spot twice, which wastes chemical. Experienced sprayers maintain a steady walking pace and use the correct nozzle size to apply just the right amount.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni shwieɔ tsofai anɔ ni amɛbɛ niiashikpamɔ lɛ haa amɛyaa blɛoo tsɔ loo amɛshwieɔ tsofai yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii enyɔ, ni no fiteɔ tsofai. Mɔ ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni shwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ baaya nɔ etsu nii be fɛɛ be. Ni okɛ nozzle lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo mli bɔ ni sa lɛ mli.

english: Spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cool and quiet. If you spray in the heat of the afternoon, the chemical evaporates into the air quickly or dries up before the crop can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni efee dioo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ shwane mli lɛ Tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if I have applied too much chemical on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo miitsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: If crop leaves start turning yellow, drying out at the edges, or curling up shortly after spraying, it means too much chemical was applied, which causes chemical burn and weakens the plant.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbi, loo amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ eshishigbɛi lɛ ahe beni afɔ amɛ tsofa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai babaoo etsu nii tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsofai shãa tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are my crops growing poorly even though I put a lot of physical effort into clearing the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ mihe wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii babaoo mli moŋ?

english: Physical effort in clearing land removes surface competition, but crops also need nutrients in the soil, proper spacing, and adequate moisture to grow well. Good land clearing must be followed by proper soil feeding and maintenance.
ga: Gbɔmɔtsoŋ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni akɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ekwɛmɔ ni sa sɛɛ.

english: Does leaving my farmland to rest without crops for a season help it produce better later?
ga: Ani kɛ́ miha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, allowing land to rest (fallowing) gives the soil time to naturally regain lost nutrients, restore organic matter, and improve its structure, which leads to healthier crops and better yields in the next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha ejɔɔ ehe (ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ) lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛnáa niyenii ni elaaje lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akuɔ sɛɛ akɛbaa ni ahaa egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yaa hiɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibii kpakpai baa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when the soil on my farm becomes very hard and compacted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard, plant roots cannot breathe or stretch out to collect groundwater and nutrients. This starves the crop, causing the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
