ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛbua shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I hire labor to clear weeds by hand or if I spray weedicides?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mihe nitsulɔi ni amɛkɛ amɛdɛŋ atsu jwɛi ahe nii loo amɛshwie tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ?

english: Hand weeding protects young, sensitive crops from chemical damage and keeps the soil intact, but it takes time. Weedicides save time and physical labor, but must be applied carefully so they do not injure your main crops.
ga: Nine ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni fiteɔ nii ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite Shi eheɔ be Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ haa be kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ baa shi. Shi esa akɛ okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ekafite oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ.

english: Why is it important to spray chemicals at specific times in the crop's life instead of whenever I have spare time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashwie tsofai anɔ yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashihilɛ mli moŋ fe ni aaashwie nɔ be fɛɛ be ni be ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Crops are vulnerable to pests and weeds at specific growth stages, such as early seedling stage or flowering. Applying chemicals at the right stage protects the plant when it needs it most, while spraying off-schedule wastes money and effort.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi yɛ amɛdalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli, tamɔ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ. loo fɔfɔi Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ otso lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be ni ato lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaabi shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain trees on the same farm with my young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi-kookoo gbekɛ lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed for leafy growth. It can also happen if the soil is waterlogged and drowning the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ batsɔ nu ni shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my field as soon as I bury the seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii kɛji mifu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the seeds germinate and sprout leaves—usually two to three weeks after planting—so the young roots are strong enough to actually absorb the fertilizer.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni baai lɛ akwɛ̃—bei pii lɛ, yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ—koni shishifãi bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It traps moisture in the dirt so it doesn't dry out fast in the hot sun, and it also stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ muji lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop their flowers before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, sudden dry spells, or a lack of water, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, trukaa ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nu ni bɛ, ni no haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops droop and look dead during the afternoon sun even if it rained yesterday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ nyɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing too much moisture, but recovers as the air cools down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni efiteɔ lɛ he. Shi ebaahi shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars keep appearing inside the inner leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yaa nɔ amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft center leaf funnels of maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended treatments into the funnel kills them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, naturally tough plants that adapt very easily to poor soil. They steal water, space, and food away from your crops, which is why clearing them early is important.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa, adebɔɔ mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ oya. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to dig up so it doesn't spoil in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ kɛ́ ashɛ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ, egboŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off. Leaving cassava in the dirt past 15 months makes the roots woody, hard, and prone to rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli nyɔji 15 lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tso, amɛhe wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm regularly instead of leaving all the monitoring to my farm hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi kwɛmɔ fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Walking your field personally allows you to catch early signs of disease, pest attacks, or nutrient deficiency on your crops before the damage spreads across the entire farm.
ga: Kɛ́ bo diɛŋtsɛ onyiɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he okadii mra. dani nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and look droopy during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni gboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce moisture loss; it is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛtoɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dɔlɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to protect them from heat and soil drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small, thin roots when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo beni miduɔ shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too closely, their roots compete aggressively for soil space, nutrients, and water, which prevents the tubers from expanding properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa shikpɔŋ, niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haaa yitso lɛ mli alɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are attacking my young maize crop before my leaves get completely eaten?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall cutworms miitutua mi-baby corn lɛ dani aye mibaai lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Early fall armyworm damage shows up as small ragged holes or light-colored patches on young leaves, along with sawdust-like waste inside the central leaves of the plant.
ga: Cutworm fitemɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli mra lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ buji bibii. ni bɛ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Su ni mli tse yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ Kɛfata jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around my plantain stem instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Plantain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal water and soil food from the main mother plant, which causes the main plant to produce smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and dark green but give me small cobs when I use too much nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuɔ nii

english: Excess nitrogen forces the plant to focus all its energy on growing leaves and stems rather than putting energy into growing strong flowers and big grain cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛkwɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui wuji lɛ,.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from uneven watering, very hot weather, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings and take over the garden so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miida oya fe mi tsei lɛ amli dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛyeɔ abɔɔ lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to harsh soil conditions, allowing them to absorb water and fertilizer faster than young crop seedlings can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ afee.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are mature enough to harvest under the soil without pulling them up too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ oyaiyeli gbalaaa amɛ?

english: Groundnuts show maturity above ground when their leaves start turning yellow, and when you check a sample pod, the inner shell lining changes from white to dark brown.
ga: Peanuts baajie shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ kpo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ okwɛ sample pods lɛ mli lɛ Mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ eyɛŋ kɛya ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure near the base of the plants will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is already moist after rain, during the early stage when plants are growing fast. Applying fertilizer to dry soil wastes it because plants require water to drink up nutrients through their roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ daa oya. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji fitemɔ ejaakɛ tsei he miihia nu koni amɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaves of maize plants. Applying targeted organic pest treatments or recommended sprays directly into the center funnel early in the morning stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ awo tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the leaf sap. Spraying the leaves with neem oil solution or insecticidal soap gets rid of the insects and allows new leaves to grow flat and normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai heei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee nɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping scattered shade trees or planting temporary plantains next to young cocoa provides the cool shade and moisture required for them to survive their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade ni gbɛ eshwa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe Ebaaha shade ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my plantain bunches growing very small when there are many young shoots coming out from the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots (suckers) grow around one main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from each other. Pruning extra shoots so only two or three remain gives the main plant full strength to produce large stems and big fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo (ŋmeii) daraa yɛ tso titri kome he. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ afo tso lɛ yibii 2-3 pɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwo tsei agboi kɛ aduawai agboi.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits in flat soil for too long without draining, smothering the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rains to drain away from the roots safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by high heat, long dry spells, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil constantly moist with regular watering and mulching helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛgbiɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before planting my seeds instead of planting early in dry dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu mra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to germinate and stay alive. If you plant in dry ground after just one light rain, the seeds may sprout but quickly dry up and die before the real rainy season begins.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi. Kɛji odu yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ nɛ fioo yɛ lɛ, shikome pɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow slow and skinny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early in the season leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is this blue fertilizer that other farmers are using, and how does it help my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji bluu ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni te ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: The blue fertilizer is usually a compound fertilizer containing key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. It provides balanced plant food that helps crops build strong roots, grow healthy leaves, and produce higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bluu ŋmɔshi nibii ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli ni niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli. Ehaa tsei niyenii ni ja ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa. ha baai lɛ mli awa ni ewo yibii babaoo

english: Can I damage my crops if I give them too much fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafite miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine?

english: Yes, giving too much fertilizer can burn plant roots and scorch the leaves, leading to stunted growth or plant death. Crops need just the right amount of nutrients, and excessive feeding can also spoil the surrounding soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eshã baai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ekolɛ tso lɛ edaŋ kwraa loo ebaagbo. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa he miihia tsei. Ni niyenii ni ayeɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that your plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. It can also happen when soil becomes waterlogged, preventing roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and bushy with leaves, but produce very little fruit or grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ?

english: This usually happens when plants receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like phosphorus and potassium. Excessive nitrogen makes plants focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of flowering and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo fe niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: What causes my crop flowers to fall off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Flowers drop when plants suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of proper nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni sa ni anáaaaaa Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Crops draw nutrients out of the earth every growing season. If you continuously farm the same piece of land without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer to replenish the nutrients, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛji akɛ oya nɔ otsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite.

english: How do I know if my soil is hungry and needs extra plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehe miihia ni maná tsei niyenii krokomɛi?

english: Hungry soil produces weak plants with pale or yellow leaves, thin stems, and small harvests. A simple soil test or observing slow growth patterns on your farm will tell you if the soil needs organic matter or fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ aná baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Aloo bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different farm chemicals together to spray at once?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ baafutu koni mikɛshwie nɔ shikome?

english: No, mixing chemicals without guidance can cause chemical reactions that damage your crops, harm your health, or make the products ineffective. Always check product labels or consult an officer before mixing.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aba. Eyɛ oshara kɛha ohewalɛ. loo eha nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ akatsu nii Kwɛmɔ nibii ni aŋma yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo bi najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko dani okɛfutu.

english: How should I store leftover farm chemicals and fertilizers so they do not spoil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni amɛkafee yaka?

english: Store all farm inputs in a cool, dry, and locked room away from direct sunlight, moisture, food, and children. Moisture can harden fertilizers, while heat can reduce the strength of crop chemicals.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni aŋã he ko ni hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ, niyenii, kɛ gbekɛbii akabote mli tɛ̃ɛ. Fɛ̃i baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do certified seeds from the agrodealer grow better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and treated for high yield, uniform growth, and disease resistance. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over time, resulting in weaker plants and lower yield.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsu he nii koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. uniform growth kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Lower leaves turn yellow when maize plants do not get enough nitrogen from the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant stay fully green and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, but avoid heavy downpours. Applying right before a heavy storm washes the fertilizer away, while applying in dry soil can burn plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ni akɛbaatsu nii dani ahum lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but drop most of them to save energy for the healthiest pods. Extreme heat, drought, or a lack of tiny pollinating insects like midges can cause even more flowers to fall.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo pollinators tamɔ midge ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi babaoo agbo.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or a sudden dry spell. High temperatures stop proper pollination, so the plant drops its flowers to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo hɔmɔ ni ba trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa pollination ni sa lɛ kpaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans between my corn rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they feed the soil and supply free fertilizer to neighboring corn plants.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni amɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This competition leads to weak, thin stems and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the stem grows thick and lower leaves dry up and fall off. You can test by gently digging around the base of one plant to check if the roots are thick enough before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ egbɔjɔ. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋtayaa ni oootsi blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Abɔle tso kome shishi koni akwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting in storage before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ nitoohe dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams enter a resting period after harvest, but naturally wake up when air warmth and humidity increase. This humidity signals to the tuber that it is time to start growing new shoots for the next planting season.
ga: Sweet potatoes yaa ŋmɛlɛtswaa mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi amɛteɔ shi yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su naa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Nɛkɛ fɛ̃i nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje ŋmeii heei ashishi kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do armyworms attack the deep central leaves of my corn plants at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the central leaf funnel during hot daytime hours to stay cool and hide from birds. At night, they come out to feed on the tender young leaves that are softest to eat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Bɔni afee ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ amɛjeɔ kpo ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛye.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can lie asleep in dry soil for years. The moment the first rain falls, they absorb water faster than crop seeds and explode into rapid growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Eŋɔɔ nu oya fe dumɔwui ni etswaa kɛyaa oya.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant produce food to swell the tubers underground. Keeping leaves off the wet ground also prevents leaves from rotting.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afuu. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, the buds on the cassava stem must point upward toward the sky. Planting stem cuttings upside down makes it difficult for shoots to grow and reduces the yield of roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, ehaa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpea or groundnuts on the land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally enriching the ground for the next crop without needing to buy extra commercial fertilizer immediately.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jara yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients deep away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when temperatures get too high, when plants don't get enough water, or when bees and wind are not present to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies feeding on the sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to apply granular fertilizer when the soil is dry or after rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ granular fertilizer awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after rain. Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil so crop roots can drink it; applying it on hot dry soil can burn your plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ.

english: How do weevils end up in my dried maize bags even when I seal them tight?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii abote mi-ŋmã kotoku ni egbi lɛ mli kɛji mikɛ mihe wo mli jogbaŋŋ po?

english: Weevil insects often lay tiny invisible eggs inside the maize grains while the corn is still drying on stalks in the field. Once stored inside sealed bags, those eggs hatch into adult beetles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miigbi lolo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ladybugs ni eda.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen in the soil or are stressed by too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps make the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo haa amɛhaoɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe waaa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good. Beans trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves soil fertility without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofa babaoo awo ŋmãa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight because it burns their delicate leaves and dries out the roots. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or cassava during their first two years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my crops make them grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiha amɛmiidara blɛoo waa.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, they choke the roots and prevent your crops from getting the nourishment they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ebaatsi otso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight and prevents them from rotting on damp soil. More sunlight helps the plant build bigger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many small suckers grow around the main plantain tree, they fight with the main tree for food and water. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ he lɛ Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ekɛ tso titrii lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do groundnut flower stems bend down and push into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but the nuts must grow underground. After the flowers are fertilized, the stems naturally push down into the earth so the groundnut pods can safely develop hidden beneath the soil.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni awo fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water. As long as the leaves recover in the cool evening, the plant is just managing the heat.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsei miikwɛ dɔlɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather is too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen wo mli babaoo, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest since the tubers are buried?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa kɛjɛ be mli ni afu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is getting ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ eesaa ehe beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from strong sunlight when they are small. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them protects their delicate leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni ooodu yɛ masɛi Enɛ baabu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to thrive.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the middle out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on corn usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow big. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight so their leaves can make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents diseases and helps the tubers underground grow bigger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting. You can test by carefully digging up one stand to check if the tubers are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shidaamɔhe lɛ mli ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji yitso lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny green bugs sticking to the undersides of my pepper leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Koni amɛhi mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those bugs are aphids, which suck the sweet sap out of your plants and cause leaves to curl and stunt growth. Spraying them with soapy water or an approved neem oil spray helps clear them off.
ga: Nakai kooloi lɛ ji aphids. ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛdara. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie enɛɛmɛi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ yɛ tomato nɔ.

english: Why do my root crops rot in the soil when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can flood the soil and choke the plant roots so they cannot breathe. Planting crops on raised earth mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu afua ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stop growing fast even when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the plant food, fertilizer, and water straight out of the soil. Clearing weeds early leaves all the good nutrients in the ground for your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaashi niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aha otsei titrii lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cool. Applying fertilizer under hot sunshine can scorch the plant leaves and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings grow tall and weak instead of strong and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma dumɔwui bibii Mine lɛ miida ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When young seedlings do not get enough direct sunlight or are planted too closely together, they stretch upwards fighting for light. Giving them adequate space and sunlight early on allows them to develop thick, sturdy stems that can support future heavy yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei bibii lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye la he akaŋ. Ni aaaha amɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la mra Enɛ haa amɛnáa tsei ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii wuji wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to put a shade cover over my young cocoa trees when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihaa kookoo tsei bibii ahe beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense full sun. Providing shade with palm fronds or temporary nurse crops like plantains protects their tender leaves and keeps the soil moist while their root systems are still developing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lolo lɛ.

english: How early should I start applying fertilizer to my maize plants after they sprout?
ga: Beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mabɔi mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Young maize plants require early feeding, usually about two weeks after sprouting. Nutrient availability during this early growth stage is critical because it builds strong roots and thick stems, directly setting the foundation for the size and number of corn ears produced at harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni aha ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ niyenii mra. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mra be mli lɛ he hiaa waa ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa baa. Enɛ ji shishitoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛha ŋmãa toi ni anáa yɛ kpamɔ ko mli lɛ dalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ.

english: Does giving my crops good plant food when they are young really affect my harvest months later?
ga: Ani niyenii kpakpa ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni amɛdara lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Yes, proper early feeding establishes the health and growth capacity of the crop. Just like young animals, crops that receive good nutrition from the onset grow bigger, healthier structures capable of producing abundant fruit, grain, or tubers when mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛhaa mra Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etswa hewalɛnamɔ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni akɛbaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ama shi. Nakai eji yɛ kooloi bibii hu ahe. Nibii ni aduɔ ni nine shɛɔ niyenii kpakpa nɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ baaná shishitoo ni da, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo aduawai, dumɔwui loo ŋmeii babaoo kɛji amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many times a day should I water my newly transplanted tomato seedlings?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mitato dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ nu yɛ gbi kome mli?

english: Newly transplanted tomato seedlings should generally be watered twice a day—once in the early morning and once in the late afternoon. This prevents delicate roots from drying out in the harsh midday heat until the plant fully establishes itself in the soil.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ tomato dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ anɔ nu shii enyɔ daa gbi. Shikome yɛ leebi maŋkpa kɛ shikome yɛ shwane mli. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi tso lɛ baatswa shi kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Should I feed my cassava plants fertilizer all at once or divide the application over time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ fɛɛ awo mli shikome loo majara mli yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Dividing fertilizer application into stages—once shortly after sprouting and another a few weeks later—provides a consistent supply of nutrients, helping the plant build strong early top growth first and then develop large underground tubers.
ga: Jaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Shikome yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua tsei ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ ŋwɛi dalɛ ni mli wa shishi mra. Kɛkɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods as a natural defensive behavior to save water. Once the rains return, the plant quickly grows new leaves and resumes feeding energy into its underground roots.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ woɔ baai heei oya ni ebɔi hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or inadequate soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save energy and protect its overall survival during difficult growing conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛwala fɛɛ he yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young crops as soon as they emerge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mi dumɔwui lɛ adara kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ.

english: Young crops are weak competitors. Fast-growing weeds quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during the crop's crucial early growth window, which can permanently stunt the crop's overall development.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ ji akaŋshilɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishijee bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ fɛɛ shweremɔ naa kɛya naanɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cowpea plants turning yellow and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young cowpeas usually signal early pest damage or a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Addressing root health and controlling early pests ensures the leaves stay green and produce food for plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite mra loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shishifãi ahe hewalɛnamɔ he nitsumɔ kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa niyenii kɛhaa tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees turn yellow and curl when exposed to harsh direct sunlight without enough shade, or when they lack vital soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby provides a protective canopy while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu sũ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Watering plants consistently at their roots early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves twisting up into tight, wrinkled balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ etsɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding on the sap. Spraying the underside of the leaves early with neem oil or recommended organic solutions stops these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baai ni egbɔjɔ ni efite lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ekpaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is my maize staying small and pale yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow, stunted maize is a clear signal that the soil is starved of nitrogen, which the plant needs to build strong stem tissues and green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the stems will quickly boost growth.
ga: Abɛi ni ji yellow dwarf lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ama tso lɛ shishi fãji ni mli wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔle Stem shishi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts together with my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and fix it directly into the soil through their roots. This acts as a free, natural fertilizer for your maize while covering the earth to prevent weeds and hold moisture.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen gas naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli koni jwɛi akafee nɔ ko ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest grow as well as new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ tamɔ dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong growth and high yields during their first season, but saved seeds lose those special high-yield traits in the next generation. Buying certified fresh seeds every planting season guarantees full strength and maximum harvest.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni eha amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛsu ni ji ultra-high-yielding lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baaha hewalɛ ni fa kɛ ŋmaa babaoo aba.

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots with small, narrow spear-like leaves and a broad base. These have much stronger energy reserves and roots than 'water suckers' with broad leaves, leading to faster growth and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword suckers’, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni amɛshishi lɛ mli kwɔ. Enɛɛmɛi yɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa babaoo fe ‘nu ni shwieɔ’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, ni no haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ plantain ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put long sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tso nine kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make energy for developing big underground tubers. Staking the vines elevates the leaves away from ground weeds and shade, directly increasing the size and weight of your harvested yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni baa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akashɛ jwɛi kɛ hulutsoo he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes in my young maize leaves with caterpillars hiding inside the tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Mikɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ miiye.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a hungry caterpillar that hides inside the leaves where fresh shoots emerge. Applying recommended pest controls or dropping clean ash into the central shoot early in the infestation destroys the worms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ baai ni ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe ŋaawoo lɛ tsu nii loo okɛ sũ ni he tse shwie tsei lɛ ateŋ mra yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ eba lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn black and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water settles around the roots in poorly drained or heavy clay soil, creating ideal conditions for fungal rot. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off harmlessly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu fee ehe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔshiimɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Is it better for me to clear my farm land using manual labor or heavy machinery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ niji loo tsɔnei ni tsii baatsu nii ni mikɛjie ŋmɔshi shikpɔji lɛ?

english: Using manual labor helps preserve the topsoil structure and prevents severe erosion, especially on land that is fragile or already degraded, whereas heavy tractors can compact the soil if used incorrectly.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ ni naa wa baa. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ loo efite nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, traktɔi ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How can I restore the health of my farm land if the soil is weak and depleted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛji egbɔjɔ ni efite?

english: You can restore degraded soil by applying organic compost or animal manure, planting cover crops like legumes that fix nitrogen, and avoiding excessive burning of vegetation on the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen lɛ he. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei babaoo ni ashãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he

english: Why should I process my harvested crops instead of selling them fresh right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu mikpamɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ akɛ ehee?

english: Processing your produce—such as fermenting and drying cocoa beans—prevents spoilage, increases shelf life, and allows you to sell at higher prices to factories and specialized buyers.
ga: Onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe nitsumɔ, tamɔ kookoo yibii ni ooofee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ egbimɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite. Ha shihilɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha okɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ ahɔ̃ɔ nitsumɔhei kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii krɛdɛɛi lɛ.

english: What makes my harvested crops rot so fast after I pick them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni haa mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops rot quickly post-harvest due to excess moisture, high heat during storage, rough handling that bruises the skin, and keeping them in poorly ventilated bags or rooms.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ, nitsumɔ ni mli wa ni fiteɔ hewolo lɛ ni akɛtoɔ kotoku mli loo tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli

english: Why are my young cocoa saplings turning yellow and drying up in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun; they require shade plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do weeds affect my crops if I do not clear them regularly?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ tsuuu nii daa?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and water away from your crops, while also hosting pests and diseases that can damage your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ ahe jɛɛhe.

english: How often do I need to inspect my farm for crop diseases?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji tsei ahe helai yɛ mli?

english: You should walk through your farm at least once a week to spot early signs of crop sickness, such as leaf spots or unusual insect activity, before it spreads to the entire field.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli koni okwɛ mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hela, tamɔ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii anifeemɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto. dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Can I grow other crops on the same field while waiting for my tree crops like cocoa to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping with fast-growing food crops like plantain, cassava, or maize provides immediate food and income while providing temporary shade for your maturing trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cassava loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ni eda lɛ náa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko.

english: How do I know if my crop is not getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Crops lacking soil nutrients often show slow growth, thin stems, pale or yellowing leaves, and delayed flowering or pod formation.
ga: Tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa blɛoo, amɛyɛ tsei bibii, kɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. kɛ fɔfɔi loo pod feemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Does applying animal manure work better than using chemical fertilizers on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves long-term soil health, structure, and water retention, while chemical fertilizers provide a quick nutrient boost; combining both gives crops both immediate nourishment and sustainable soil quality.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ, egbɛjianɔtoo kɛ nu ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he oya. Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ nɛɛ fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct heat and the dry Harmattan wind. Providing shade plants like plantains or gliricidia keeps the ground moist and shields the young leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ Harmattan latsaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ naa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo glicidia ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they steal food and water from the main tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plantain grows large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha plantains titrii lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting cassava stems with the buds pointing downward forces the new shoots to grow into the dark soil first before bending upward. This wastes the plant's stored food energy and results in fewer, smaller cassava tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei ni aduɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ baaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ dani amɛba ŋwɛi. Enɛ baafite tso lɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmei shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do I need to put strong sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei niji ni wa awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need their leaves spread out in direct sunlight to manufacture food. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground away from diseases and exposes them to sunlight, helping the tuber grow large underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ helai shɛɔ amɛhe, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is necessary for keeping leaves green and healthy so the plant can grow big, full cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ ada kɛyashɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my other crops die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli shi tsei krokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Ani minɔ lɛ baagbo kɛji nu afua ba enɔ?

english: Rice plants have internal air tubes in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots underwater. Standing water also smothers competing weeds without harming the rice.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni eyeee ŋmãa lɛ awui.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get too hot or don't get enough water. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural way of saving energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni haa edaa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turning soft and black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, which usually happens when water supply to the plant goes up and down unpredictably.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yaa ŋwɛi ni eba shi yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny lumps on their roots. When the plant dies, this nitrogen breaks down into the dirt, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ fiteɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Heavy rain will quickly wash away loose fertilizer into roadside gutters or wash it deep into the ground where the crop roots cannot reach it, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ he nubui amli lɛ oya loo etswaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Efiteɔ omɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ oshika.

english: If only female insects lay eggs in my crops, why should I try to kill the male insects?
ga: Kɛji kooloi yei woɔ ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ magbe kooloo nuu?

english: Female insects cannot produce eggs that hatch into crop-damaging worms unless they mate with male insects first. Killing the males stops the mating process, which prevents the females from multiplying and destroying your harvest.
ga: Kplukai yei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo wɔji ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ja amɛkɛ kooloo ko ni ji nuu ko bote gbalashihilɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Nuu lɛ ni agbeɔ lɛ haa ekɛ ehe woɔ gbalashihilɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi yei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do those bottle traps I see hanging in mango trees actually work to protect crops?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tɔ mli ni mina ni akɛkpɛtɛ mango tso he lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The traps contain a special smell or bait that tricks male insects into flying inside thinking they are meeting females. Once inside, they get trapped and die, stopping them from mating with females in your farm.
ga: Amale lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛlakaa kooloi hii koni amɛfo kɛbote mli, ni amɛsusu akɛ amɛkɛ yoo ko miikpe. Kɛ́ oyabote mli lɛ Amɛbaatsi amɛhe ni amɛgboi. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ yei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ.

english: Why do some pest traps attract only male flies instead of catching all the insects in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni akɛtswaa ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii hii pɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These traps use a specific scent that mimics a female insect looking for a mate. Because only male flies are searching for that scent, they are the ones attracted to the trap, leaving the males unable to fertilize any female flies.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ pɔtɛɛ ko ni kaseɔ kooloi yei ni miitao hefatalɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii hii pɛ taoɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ agbalaa amɛ kɛyaa tsɔne lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii hii nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ ŋmeii yei abɔ.

english: Why do my ripe mangoes have tiny worms inside them when the skin looks fine from the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Female fruit flies use a tiny needle-like tool on their bodies to pierce the skin of the fruit and lay eggs deep inside. When those eggs hatch, tiny worms emerge and feed on the inside of your mangoes.
ga: Fruit flies yei kɛ nibii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii. Yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, amɛfoɔ aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ amɛwuji lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo ni amɛyeɔ o-mango lɛ loo lɛ.

english: Do male flies cause direct damage to my mango fruits?
ga: Ani ŋmeii hii yeɔ mi mangoi lɛ awui tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, male flies do not puncture the fruit or lay eggs inside it; only female flies cause direct damage. However, male flies must be controlled because they fertilize the females that destroy the fruit.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii hii boteŋ aduawai lɛ amli loo amɛwoŋ ŋmeii yɛ mli. Fɛ̃i yei pɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa tɛ̃ɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ akudɔ ŋmeii hii ejaakɛ amɛkɛ ŋmeii yei ni fiteɔ aduawai lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why does a small insect problem on my crop farm suddenly become thousands of pests within a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe naagba ko batsɔ kooloi akpei abɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Insects reproduce very quickly once they mate. A single female fruit fly can lay hundreds of fertilized eggs at a time inside your crops, causing the pest population on your farm to explode rapidly.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ oya waa kɛ́ amɛbote gbalashihilɛ mli. Yibii yibii amli ŋmei yoo kome baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni afɔ lɛ yɛ onibii amli yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ baaya hiɛ oya.

english: Can a female fly still destroy my mango crop if she does not find a male fly to mate with?
ga: Ani ŋmeii yei baanyɛ afite mi mango tso lɛ lolo? Ni kɛji akɛ enaaa ŋmeii hii komɛi ni ekɛ amɛ aaabɔ hu?

english: Without mating with a male fly, a female fly cannot lay eggs that hatch into worms. Even if she drops unfertilized eggs, they will not hatch to rot your fruit.
ga: Kɛ amɛkɛ ŋmeii hii ebɔko ŋmeii yei hu nyɛɛɛ amɛwo ŋmeii ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Kɛji eshɛrɛ ŋmeii ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ eshwie po lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ efoŋ ni eha oyibii lɛ agbo.

english: When is the best time for me to put up pest traps on my mango farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mato tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɔnei yɛ mi mango ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to set up your traps early before the fruits mature. Removing the male flies before the female flies start looking for mates prevents any breeding from happening as your crops grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooto tsɔne lɛ mra. dani aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃ Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii hii lɛ kɛjɛ mli dani ŋmeii yei lɛ je shishi amɛbote gbalashihilɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akabote gbalashihilɛ mli be mli ni otsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the spoiled fruit on my farm is caused by fruit flies or something else?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ aduawai ni efite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii loo nɔ kroko?

english: If your mangoes become soft, rot from the inside out, or drop from the tree early and show tiny whitish larvae or worms inside when opened, it is a clear sign of fruit fly damage.
ga: Kɛji o-mango lɛ mli yɛ bɔdɔɔ Rot kɛjɛ mli kɛje kpo Aloo egbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ oya ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ mli. Yɛ mli beni agbele No ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii efite.

english: Is it possible to completely stop insects from laying eggs inside my mangoes without spraying heavy chemicals on the fruit?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsĩ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ mango mli ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii shwieee aduawai lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, by using smell-based traps to catch male flies across your orchard, you can drastically reduce the male population. Without males around to mate, female flies cannot produce living eggs to ruin your fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔnei ni akɛmɔɔ ŋmeii hii ni foɔ otso yibii abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ oha hii ayibɔ aba shi waa. Kɛji nuu ko bɛ ni baafɔ lɛ, ŋmeii yei hu nyɛɛɛ amɛwo ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛkɛfite oyibii lɛ.

english: Why do people attach a branch from a good mango tree onto a strong local mango tree base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ mango niji kpakpai fĩɔ maŋ lɛ mli mango tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Joining a branch from a sweet, high-yielding mango tree onto a strong local tree base lets you grow sweet, marketable mangoes much faster while using the tough local roots to survive dry weather.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ mango tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ŋɔɔ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fata maŋ lɛ mli tso shishitoo ni mli wa he lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ mango ni ŋɔɔ ni abaanyɛ ahé lɛ oya kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Can I use any random local mango tree as the bottom base when joining mango trees together?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mango tso ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ atsu nii akɛ shishitoo nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei lɛ miibɔ he?

english: Yes, strong wild or local mango trees make great base trees (rootstocks) because their roots are well adapted to the local soil and drought, even if their own natural fruit is small or sour.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli loo maŋ lɛ mli mango tsei ni wa lɛ feɔ shishitoo kpakpai (shishifãi) ​​ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi. Kɛji akɛ ebɔɔ su yibii lɛ ji bibioo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ po.

english: Does joining a branch onto a tree make it give mangoes faster than growing one from seed?
ga: Ani tso ni akɛwo mli lɛ baaha mango aba oya fe bɔ ni ajɛɔ dumɔwui amli akwɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, a mango tree grown from seed can take up to seven years to produce fruit, but a tree made by joining a branch from a mature sweet tree can start bearing fruit in just two to three years.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, mango tso ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii kpawo dani ewo yibii. Shi tsei ni akɛ tso ni ŋɔɔ ni eda ni afolɔ mli lɛ fee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli.

english: Will the fruits on my joined tree taste like the sweet branch top or the sour local tree base?
ga: Ani yibii ni yɔɔ mihefatalɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baafee tamɔ tsei niji ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ayiteŋ loo tsei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: The fruit will take on the exact taste, size, and sweet quality of the upper branch you attached, not the local base tree roots.
ga: Yibii lɛ naa ŋwɛi nine ni okɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ, elɛɛmɔ, kɛ eŋɔɔmɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Jeee jɛmɛ tso ni ji cone lɛ shishifã ji no.

english: Why did the mango branch I tied onto my tree dry up and die instead of growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango nine ni mikɛfi tso lɛ he lɛ gĩ ni egbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaada lɛ?

english: If the cuts on the top branch or base tree are rough or uneven, the inner layers cannot touch smoothly to share food and water, causing the newly attached branch to dry out.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ ŋwɛi nine loo shishigbɛ ni afo lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee Mligbɛ fãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ koni amɛja niyenii kɛ nu. Ehaa tsei niji ni akɛkpɛtɛ he ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: How do I pick the right branch from a sweet mango tree to join onto my local tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso nine ni sa kɛjɛ mi mango tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ mimaŋ tso lɛ afata he?

english: You should select a fresh, healthy branch from the ends of a high-yielding tree that has strong, firm buds ready to open, rather than an old dry branch or a soft young leaf.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei niji heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni etswa shi shiŋŋ ni esaa amɛhe koni amɛwo niji lɛ ashishifãi amli. Yɛ tsei niji momo ni egbi loo baai bibii najiaŋ

english: How long does it take for a newly attached mango branch to take root and start growing?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango ni akɛwo tso mli ehee lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni ebɔi dalɛ?

english: If the cuts are made smoothly and tied tightly, the upper branch will join with the base tree and start pushing out fresh green buds within three to four weeks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ, niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baafata tso lɛ shishi ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli.
