english: Why do farmers wrap plastic tightly around the spot where they join two tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ plastic fĩɔ he ni tsei niji enyɔ kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ he waa lɛ?

english: The plastic wrap holds the two cut pieces firmly together so they can heal into one tree, while keeping air and rain out so the cut doesn't rot or dry up.
ga: Plastic ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha fãi enyɔ lɛ afee ekome jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni anyɛ akwɛ amɛ tamɔ tso kome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ koni pilamɔ lɛ akafite loo ekagbi.

english: What happens if rainwater gets inside the joint where I tied the cuts together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nu bote fã ni mikɛ fã lɛ fĩɔ lɛ mli?

english: Water trapped inside the wound can attract fungus and rot the cut surfaces, which stops the two parts from joining successfully.
ga: Nu ni etsi pilamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii ni efite he ni afo lɛ. ni haa fãi enyɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsake amɛhe

english: Should I cut off green shoots that grow out from the bottom base of my joined mango tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei eŋɔli ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mango tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, you must prune away all shoots coming from below the join line, otherwise the base tree will feed its own wild branches instead of sending food to your sweet mango top.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni ofo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he lɛ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ baaye lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛya omango ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and hot dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural leaf canopy that protects young trees from sun burn and keeps moisture in the ground.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my plantain stems with dry grass and fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around plantains, known as mulching, stops weeds from growing, keeps the soil moist during hot weather, and slowly breaks down into natural food for the plant roots.
ga: Ale ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ Plantain he lɛ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and small worms inside the center stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves. Checking fields early and applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract directly into the central funnel of the plant kills these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni adu lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Apply the first round of NPK fertilizer about two weeks after planting when the shoots appear, and follow up with a Urea top-dressing around four weeks later when the corn is waist-high to boost grain growth.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsi enyɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. ni okɛ urea ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ aaafee otsii ejwɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ etsitsi nɔ lɛ koni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Should I plant my cassava stick cuttings flat in the ground or slanted upright?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu yucca tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ja nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle or vertically into soil mounds helps roots push deep down, resulting in larger and more plentiful cassava tubers compared to laying them completely flat.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ 45-degree angle loo ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛfa babaoo. Kɛ akɛto fumɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ he

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden sticks to tie up my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji akpɛtɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he kɛ́ eda lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines keeps the leaves lifted up to receive maximum sunlight, which gives the plant energy to develop large, heavy tubers underground instead of wasting energy trailing on hot soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ awóɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aná. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs agboi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli

english: How can I make my farm soil richer without buying expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Mixing well-rotted animal manure, composted crop residue, or green manure crops into your soil improves its structure, holds water better, and supplies essential plant nutrients naturally.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo ni akɛ tsei amli ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ futuɔ mli Loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔne lɛ aya hiɛ. Nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa haa tsei yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotten at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium uptake in the plant. Watering your garden regularly and adding compost or agricultural lime helps solve this issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni nyɛɛɛ aná tsei amli lɛ. Nu ni oooha abɔɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How do I know that the soil has enough water for me to start planting my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aje dumɔwui ashishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Wait until you receive two or three heavy, soaking rains that wet the ground down to at least the depth of your hand, ensuring seeds have continuous moisture to germinate without drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni naa wa. Pellets enyɔ loo etɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ onine. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why does rice need so much water to grow compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in very wet conditions because their roots are special and can breathe under shallow water. Keeping water in the field also stops normal land weeds from growing and choking your crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa yɛ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmu yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ shishi. Nu ni ooohiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ daa lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛmiimɔ onibii amli.

english: What is the difference between upland rice and lowland rice?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa teŋ?

english: Upland rice is bred to grow on flat or sloping dry land using only natural rainwater, while lowland rice is planted in swampy areas or valley bottoms where water collects and stays on the field for long periods.
ga: Akɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nu tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ gɔŋji amli ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ loo hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi loo jɔɔ lɛ amli hei ni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to broadcast my rice seeds directly into the field or nurse them first before transplanting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo matsa amɛ dani mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Nursing seeds first gives young plants a strong, healthy head start in a protected space. When you transplant them into the main field, they can resist weeds and heavy rains much better than seeds scattered directly on the ground.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ ahe waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ hei ni abuɔ he lɛ. Kɛji okɛwo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ jwɛi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does a single rice seed grow into a big clump with many different stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa wu kome daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmãa wulu ko ni tsei sɔrɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally produce side branches from the main base called 'tillers.' Good soil and proper spacing allow one seed to shoot out many tillers, which means more heads of rice and a bigger harvest for you.
ga: Omɔ tsei woɔ niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ kɛjɛɔ shishitoo titri ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ 'trakta' lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa dumɔwu kome kwɛ̃ɔ tsei babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ ŋmãa babaoo kɛ ŋmaa babaoo kɛha bo.

english: Why do I need to clear all weeds from my field before setting out my young rice plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young rice seedlings. If you leave them in the field, they will steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your rice, leaving your crop weak and thin.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe ŋmãa dumɔwui bibii. Kɛji oshi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants starting to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your rice is hungry for nitrogen or that the soil is waterlogged without proper drainage. Adding the right fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can feed itself again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-rice lɛ loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I split my fertilizer application into different times instead of putting it all in the ground at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aja ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo bei srɔtoi amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootswa lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ.

english: Rice plants need food at specific life stages. Applying early food builds strong roots and leaves, while applying later food helps the plant fill out thick, heavy rice grains instead of wasting fertilizer early on.
ga: Omɔ tsei biɔ niyenii yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Niyenii ni ayeɔ mra lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni akɛhaa sɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa ni mli wa ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni afite ŋmɔshi nibii mra

english: Why do flocks of birds suddenly start attacking my rice field when the plants flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi akui jeɔ shishi amɛtutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ beni tsei lɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: As the rice grains begin forming inside the heads, they fill up with a sweet, milky liquid that birds love to eat. You must guard the field or use scare devices during this liquid stage before the grain hardens.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmaa bɔi feemɔ yɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ Ebaayi kɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni tamɔ mliki ni okpoi sumɔɔ ni amɛye. Esa akɛ obu ŋmɔ lɛ he loo okɛ nɔ ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe atsu nii yɛ nu mli dani ŋmaa lɛ mli awa.

english: Your rice is ready when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the stalks turn a clear golden-yellow color and the heads bend downward. Harvesting too early leaves you with soft grains, and waiting too late causes grains to shatter on the ground.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo beni o-rice lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ batsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. ni ŋmã yitso lɛ efo shi Kpãa mra tsɔ baaha oná dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Ni kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ akumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why must I dry my freshly harvested rice immediately before putting it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani mikɛwo kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Wet rice heats up fast and creates moisture inside storage bags, which causes mold to grow and rots the grain. Sun-drying lowers the water content so your rice stays fresh, clean, and safe to store or sell.
ga: Omɔ ni efɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii daa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa nu ni he hiaa koni o-rice lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehe atse, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛto loo ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving drainage helps the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them first naturally fertilizes the soil so your next crop grows bigger and stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafee agbo ni ehe wa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young maize shoots. Catching them early and applying the right biopesticide or neem extract can protect your crop before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni edara lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often because of irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium properly to the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the small shoots and suckers growing out from the main stem of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ

english: Suckers steal food and water from the main tree without producing good pods. Pruning them off directs all the tree's energy into making large, healthy cocoa pods and improves airflow to prevent disease.
ga: Suckers juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛjieee ŋmeii kpakpai. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii agboi ni mli wa. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai akabote mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tso ko ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves to reach maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni ebaatsi helai anaa koni amɛkaya shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I leave dry grass and crop waste around the stems of my plantain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ? Midumɔwu lɛ tso lɛ

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil moist, reduces heat on the roots, blocks weed growth, and turns into rich compost as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha la ni tsoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛji egbo.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Proper watering and providing light shade during extremely hot periods can stop flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛ. Nu ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day or season to apply fertilizer so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo be mli ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, early in the morning or late in the evening. Avoid applying right before a heavy downpour, as rain will wash it away, or during dry weather when it can burn the roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. leebi loo gbɛkɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ he ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ baaho lɛ. loo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi, ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I clear all the big shade trees away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture faster than their small roots can drink it.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin tubers when I plant the stem cuttings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ naa ŋmeii ni mli tseee waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients, space, and water, leaving the plant with very little energy to grow thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, ŋwɛi kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmei tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra baby shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many baby shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother plant, which causes the main tree to take longer to grow and produce smaller bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii loo bibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani edaa ni ewoɔ kui bibii.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape on older maize leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency, which means the soil lacks the main nutrient the plant needs to build healthy green leaves.
ga: V-shape yellowing ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my plot make my next crop of maize grow better and greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akafite lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes trap nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots, which releases natural fertilizer into the soil when the plants die.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli, ni no jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating quickly and keeping the plant roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden poles instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth, and keeping them off the ground prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. kɛ ehiɛ ni akɛaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni helai akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaa lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits during the very hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High heat causes heat stress in tomato plants, making pollen sticky or sterile so flowers cannot be fertilized, prompting the plant to drop them to save water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato tsei amli. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ashɛrɛɔ tomato tsei ashwieɔ koni akɛbu nu he.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves or spreading a viral leaf curl disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ loo ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rainy day of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period, and if the soil dries out completely after the seed sprouts, the young seedling will die of thirst.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, kumai baagbe tso bibioo lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to burn my land after clearing it, or should I leave the cleared grass to rot on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã mishikpɔŋ lɛ beni mijie lɛ sɛɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni he tse lɛ ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it destroys rich nutrients and kills helpful living organisms in the soil. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose creates mulch that holds soil moisture, keeps the roots cool under hot sun, and naturally adds fertility back to your land.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, eha fɔmɔ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize crop, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize actually helps both crops. Cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to nourish the maize, while the tall maize stalks provide partial shade and support for the cowpeas.
ga: Cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa tsina ŋmãa lɛ fã ko kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why do farmers recommend planting plantain suckers beside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain plants grow very fast and produce large, broad leaves that shade young cocoa plants, keeping the soil moist and protecting them during their delicate first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni eyɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips down before the corn stems fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi dani abele tsei lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their dark green color so the plant can grow big corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce giant stems and huge leaves, but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ tso wulu kɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted in rich, low-lying wet soils, it spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. Proper spacing and balanced fertilizers encourage the plant to send its food down into expanding tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii amaje shi kɛya bulbs ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get consistent water while flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist during the flowering period stops the plant from getting stressed and dropping its blooms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akahao ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi.

english: I noticed dark, rotting spots spreading across my cocoa pods during the rainy season—what causes this?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii diji ni egboi yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Mɛni kɛ enɛ baa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that multiplies in cold, wet, and humid air. Pruning overcrowded cocoa branches lets sunshine and wind inside the canopy to dry out the leaves, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo kokoo tsei lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to look curled up and yellowish with green patches?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. You can avoid this problem entirely by planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ okpa naagba nɛɛ kwraa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi eha he odase lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy fresh packaged hybrid maize seeds instead of just saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni akɛwo kotoku mli ehee lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the next generation, producing uneven plants and far lower yield. Buying fresh certified seeds each planting season guarantees strong, disease-resistant plants that yield maximum grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ, ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ, ni dumɔwui babaoo aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they get cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are stored in warm places without good airflow where fungi thrive. Handle yams gently when digging them up, discard damaged tubers, and store the healthy yams in a raised, shaded, and well-ventilated barn.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli yɛ he ko ni ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ lɛ. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii kɛfo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Shĩ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ ashwie. Ni okɛ sweet potatoes ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ato ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when experienced farmers say I should use 'face water' to mix my crop chemical powder?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ‘nu’ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsofa powda lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Face water' refers to clear, fresh flowing water from a clean stream or tap. Using clean water ensures the chemical powder dissolves properly without mud or dirt weakening its effectiveness on your crops.
ga: Nam Na’ tsɔɔ nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ faa ni mli tse loo nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ mli. Nu ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. ni muji loo muji bɛ mli Enɛ baaha tsofa powda lɛ nitsumɔ yɛ onibii anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it bad to use dirty standing pond water when mixing chemical powder for my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ okɛ nu ni mli ewo muji baatsu nii beni okɛ mi-corn powder lɛ futuɔ lɛ?

english: Dirty or stagnant water contains mud and organic debris that react with the chemical powder, reducing its strength and clogging your spray equipment when treating your crops.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo ni ekã shi lɛ yɛ muji kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kɛ tsofa powda feɔ ekome. Ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ powda lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. kɛ clog spray nibii kɛji akɛ atsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii.

english: Why can't I just dust the dry chemical powder directly onto my crop leaves without using water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ tsofa ni egbi lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛkɛ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry chemical powder alone cannot spread evenly across the leaves and can easily burn your crops. Water is needed to carry and dilute the chemical so the plant can absorb the protection safely.
ga: Tsofa powda ni egbi pɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã baai lɛ fɛɛ mli ni eshãa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya. Nu he miihia koni akɛ tsofai lɛ aya ni akɛwo mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hebuu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is flowing stream water preferred over still, muddy water for preparing crop sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ asumɔɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ faa mli fe nu ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ dioo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he saamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Flowing water is constantly moving and generally clearer. Clear water allows the powdered treatment to dissolve completely so it can protect your crops effectively without chemical breakdown.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni bei pii lɛ, emli tseɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Nu ni mli tse yeɔ ebuaa ni tsofafeemɔ powda lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa. Ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsofai efiteee.

english: What is the proper step-by-step way to mix my powdered chemical with water before spraying my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ tsofa powda futuɔ nu mli dani akɛ cacao woɔ mɔ mli?

english: You should first pour a small amount of clean water onto the powder and stir thoroughly until it forms a smooth liquid, then add the rest of the required water so no hard lumps remain.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse fioo awo powda lɛ nɔ ni okɛfutu kɛyashi ebaatsɔ nu ni mli tse. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ afata he bɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii ni wa akashwɛ.

english: Why do I need to start with just a small amount of water when dissolving my crop treatment powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi nu fioo pɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii koni mikɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofafeemɔ powda lɛ?

english: Starting with a small amount of water allows you to break up lumps easily and create a uniform paste. If you pour all the water in at once, the powder may float and clump together.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu fioo ko je shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ogbala ŋmeii lɛ amli mlɛo ni ofee ŋmeii ni tamɔ krim. Kɛji okɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ wo mli shikome lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nu lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe afee ekome.

english: Why is thorough stirring so important when I am preparing powder treatments for my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsake mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miito tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ?

english: Stirring ensures that the powder mixes completely throughout the liquid so that every vegetable plant gets an equal and correct dose of protection during application.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ, ehaa powda lɛ futuɔ nu lɛ mli fɛɛ kwraa. Enɛ haa aduawai tso fɛɛ tso naa hebuu ni sa ni sa yɛ nitsumɔi lɛ ateŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if I mix too little water with the chemical powder?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma powda fioo pɛ futu mli?

english: Using too little water makes the mixture overly concentrated, which can scorch, spot, or burn your crop leaves instead of protecting them from pests or diseases.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai lɛ ashã, ana, loo ashã. Mohu ɔ, e buɔ a he kɛ jeɔ koolohi loo hiɔhi a he.

english: Why does my powdered crop medicine sink to the bottom of the bucket if I let it sit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsofai ni akɛfee powda lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa tanki lɛ shishi kɛji mishi amɛ pɛ?

english: Powder treatments do not fully melt like sugar; they stay suspended in water. Thorough stirring mixes the powder fine enough to stay suspended so it sprays evenly onto your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ powda fee lɛ shwieee shi kwraa tamɔ sugar. Amɛfoɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha powda lɛ afee fɛo bɔ ni sa ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afɔse oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can I prepare my powdered crop treatment using any liquid I find, or must I use actual water?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu fɛɛ nu afee tsofai ni akɛfee powda? Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana yɛ? Aloo ehe miihia ni okɛ nu atsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You must use actual fresh water because crop powders are formulated to mix safely only with clear water, ensuring the chemical works correctly without damaging your plants.
ga: Nu kpakpa he miihia bo diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afee tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ koni akɛ nu ni mli tse pɛ afutu mli shweshweeshwe. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee otsei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and cannot handle full, direct sunlight or harsh winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu hulu la ni eyi obɔ, ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he nii. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli shade aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu Cocoa he kɛyashi ebaatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars crawling inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ni shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The caterpillars feed on the young leaves and inside the central shoot, which slows down growth and reduces maize yield if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai yeɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the raised buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down delays growth, confuses the plant shoots, and reduces the number of big tubers you harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha edalɛ asɛɛ afo. futumɔ tsei ahe ŋmeii ni oha ŋmeii wuji ni okpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a plant usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Rain alone is not enough if the soil lacks nutrients, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer is necessary.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nugbɔ pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: This sudden collapse is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil. The bacteria enter the roots and block the tubes that carry water inside the stem, causing the plant to dry up and die even when the soil has water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bacteria boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli po.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large, heavy yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain stem to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi plantain shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow forces them to steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Pruning them to leave only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Ha ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ ada fe nine. ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ mli Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1-2 pɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ atsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without developing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually from extreme heat, very dry air, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa, loo nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize improves soil health. Legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize while giving you a secondary food crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa, ni eji niyenii ni ji enyɔ hu.

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that drink the water, absorb the fertilizer, and block the sunlight that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get full access to all the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nu, amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ naa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main plant food. This often happens in worn-out soil or after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my farm helps my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest groundnuts and leave the roots to decay, they release that trapped fertilizer into the soil for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei ni oha shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Amɛjieɔ ŋmei ni emɔ mli lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall green stems above ground but only small tubers under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ tsei eŋɔli ni nɔ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much leafy fertilizer (nitrogen) and not enough root fertilizer (potassium), the cassava puts all its power into building leaves and tall stems instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ baai amli ŋmɔshi nibii (nitrogen) babaoo ni shishifãi amli ŋmɔshi nii (potassium) faaa lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ woɔ tso nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when tiny pests damage the blossom. Consistent watering during hot dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up from the edges inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ emligbɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when water gets trapped around the roots and rots them, or when a soil disease blocks the water channels inside the trunk. Because water cannot reach the top, the leaf tips starve and dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ebɔle he. shishifãi ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ loo kɛ́ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsi nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Ejaakɛ nu nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋwɛi. Hɔmɔ eye baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my harvested pepper fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom while ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni eshishigbɛ shwieɔ shi beni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: These dark spots are called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot move calcium to the growing fruit fast enough, which usually occurs when watering is irregular during dry weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ oya bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: The first rain only wets the top layer of dirt while deep soil stays dry. If the rain pauses for a week or two right after, your newly sprouted seeds will burn and die in the hot, dry soil.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my yam seed setts are still underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi be mli ni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than yam sprouts and steal all the water and light nearby. Clearing them early ensures that when the fragile young yam sprout emerges, it doesn't have to fight weeds to survive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe sweet potato tsei. kɛ nu kɛ kane ni bɛŋkɛ ni ajuɔ Ajieɔ lɛ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet yam tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo. Ehe ehiaaa ni awuu ashi jwɛi koni anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra branches growing on the trunk of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra branches block sunlight and trap moisture inside the tree canopy, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases like black pod thrive. Pruning lets air circulate and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing pods.
ga: Niji ni fata he lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ awo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get tiny holes and powder in them after a few weeks in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ sũ lɛ? Hii kotoku lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs on the grain before harvest or climb inside bags if the maize is not completely dry. Keeping the maize very dry and using proper airtight storage starves the insects of air and water so they cannot multiply.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ dani akpaa loo amɛkwɔɔ kɛboteɔ kotokui amli kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa. Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa lɛ mli egbi waa ni akɛ vacuum ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ nu mli lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ eha yibɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: When maize is planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of using energy to grow big cobs, they spend all their energy growing tall to reach the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow starting from the tips during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen. Maize takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛyeɔ ŋwɛi baa heei. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off and turn yellow during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to rest and keep its tubers alive under the soil until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni egbiɔ koni akɛbu nu he. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my yam farm produce thick green vines with plenty of leaves but tiny yam tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani sweet potato ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter early on, the yam plant uses all its energy to build green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo mra lɛ, Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaato niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai eŋɔlii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter when I harvest them after a long period without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ akpa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Drought causes cassava plants to produce extra natural protective chemicals called cyanogenic glucosides. These chemicals protect the plant from pests during water stress, but they make the root taste bitter.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa ŋmei tsei feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ amɛ cyanogenic glucosides. Tsofai nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ nu mli haomɔ be mli. Shi ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the tiny cocoa pods on my trees shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. A cocoa tree thins out its own young pods when it does not have enough water, soil nutrients, or canopy shade to support every pod to full maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ baatswa ni amɛfee ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ nu bɛ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear away the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers act like hungry children stealing water and food from the main plantain tree. Removing them leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the mother plant to grow large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi, ni no baaha tso nyɛ lɛ ada ni etsɔ plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without growing into tomatoes when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form fruit. The plant then drops the unpollinated flowers to conserve water and energy until temperatures cool down.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ amɛwooo yibii. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and staying small instead of spreading wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa babaoo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense response when tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites attack the underside of the leaves, or when a virus infects the plant and stunts leaf growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ he kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites tutua baa lɛ shishi. Aloo kɛ́ hela ko gbɛ eshwa tso ko mli ni eha baai lɛ ekwɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants keep producing long leafy vines without putting out flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo wain tsei ni baai kakadaji ni fɔfɔi bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas will delay flowering if the soil has too much nitrogen or if they receive too much water early on. The plant stays focused on growing stems and leaves instead of shifting energy to make flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpea baaha fɔfɔii lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo aha lɛ nu babaoo mra. Tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a tsakeɔ he wami konɛ a kɛ pee fɔfɔi kɛ tso.

english: Staking holds yam leaves up high into the sunlight, which allows the leaves to catch maximum light to make food that grows a large tuber underground.
ga: Ni ooohiɛ sweet potato baai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii ni daa ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: What does it mean if a buyer asks me to grow organic crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko ni heɔ nii lɛ bi mi akɛ makwɛ tsei ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Organic farming means growing crops naturally without using synthetic chemical fertilizers or weedicides, relying instead on animal manure, compost, and natural pest controls.
ga: Organic okwaayeli tsɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsuuu nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ a hɛ fɔ koolohi a ngma, ngmɔ, kɛ adebɔɔ mi nɛ a gbeɔ koolohi a nɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpea in my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is burning dry grass and stalks on my land bad for my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys essential soil organisms and burns away natural organic matter that holds water, leaving your soil dry, hard, and infertile over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewaa ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning low branches lets air and sunlight in to keep pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get small black holes and insects when stored in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Ni kooloi bibii kɛ́ akɛto kotokui amli?

english: Those insects are grain weevils that lay eggs when grain is still damp. Thoroughly sun-drying your corn until hard before storing it in clean, airtight bags keeps them out.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji ŋmaa ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui beni ŋmaa lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ. Ha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo vacuum bag ni mli tse mli koni ekabote mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells to reduce water loss. The plant goes to sleep to protect the roots underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsei lɛ baawɔ koni amɛbu amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the flower pollen so fruits cannot form. Covering the soil with mulch keeps the ground cool and helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai nyɛɛɛ afee. Mulching haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if a plantain sucker is healthy enough to transplant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantain suckers lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsake amɛ?

english: Choose suckers that have narrow, sword-like leaves and clean white roots without any dark spots or holes, which indicates freedom from stem borers.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishifãi yɛŋ ni he tse ni he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ loo bu bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii komɛi bɛ ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: How does putting dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops help them during dry periods?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ tɛŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like an umbrella for the soil, blocking direct sunlight so water doesn't evaporate quickly, keeping the soil moist for your crops much longer.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni okɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shwieee oya. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil become dry and cracked just a few days after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni egbɛ eshwa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: Soil without enough organic matter loses moisture quickly under direct heat. Adding decayed manure or compost acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto rainwater so your crops have a steady water supply.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baafite oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water. By rolling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the burning sun and dry air, helping the plant save the little water left in its roots.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje mli. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Baai lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ fioo kpo kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhereɔ nu ni eshwɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during severe dry spells to reduce water loss. Without leaves, the tree uses less water and preserves its main stem and root system to stay alive until rain returns.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsei ni bɛ baai lɛ kɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛshishifã titri lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before growing any peppers when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani eduɔ pepper yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they enter survival mode. The plant drops flowers because it knows it lacks the water needed to nourish growing peppers, saving its energy to survive.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Amɛbaaya wala shihilɛ mli. Tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ ele akɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ. ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and dying during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the plant sacrifices its older bottom leaves to send what little water and nutrients it has left to the fresh top leaves and young fruits.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Tso lɛ kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ nu fioo kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ aya baai heei kɛ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Which food crops can I plant that will still produce food if rainfall becomes very short this year?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu ni baaha niyenii aba lolo kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo kwraa afi nɛɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, sorghum, millet, and cowpeas have deep root systems or naturally low water needs, allowing them to withstand long dry spells far better than crops like maize or leafy vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ amli babaoo fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai.

english: How does planting shade trees around my farm help my crops when water is scarce?
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha he fɛɛ he lɛ Te miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ be mli ni nu faaa lɛ?

english: Shade trees reduce the ground temperature and block harsh winds that dry out the field. This lowers the amount of water your crops lose to the hot air, keeping the surrounding soil damp for longer.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha nu ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I plant my seeds on raised mounds or on flat ground if I expect little rain this season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ kɛji akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ baanɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Planting on flat ground or in small depressions helps retain rainwater right around the seeds. High mounds expose more soil surface to the sun, making the earth dry out much faster during dry spells.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo hei bibii ni gbɛ yɔɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to water my vegetable crops with grey water from washing dishes at home when rains fail?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ nu ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ tsɛnsii ni ahoɔ yɛ shia lɛ mli lɛ baafɔ mi aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ?

english: Yes, water from household washing can be used if it does not contain strong bleach or harsh chemicals. It is best poured directly onto the soil at the base of the plant rather than on the leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni jɛɔ shĩa mli nibii ni afɔɔ he lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛji akɛ bleach ni mli wa loo tsofai ni mli wa bɛ mli. Esa akɛ afɔse ashwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni aaashwie baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain floods the soil and prevents roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is wet from rain before applying fertilizer to my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water so the roots can drink it in. If you put fertilizer on dry ground, it can burn the plant roots or sit on top of the dry soil where the crop cannot use it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ ashã loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This leaves every plant underfed, resulting in small fruits and lower yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii baa ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, moist conditions. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores onto pods, especially when trees have too much shade and little airflow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores lɛ nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. They suck the sap out of the young leaves and can spread plant sicknesses that cause twisted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahe helai ni haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with excess water for too long. The heavy water drowns the root system and encourages soil rot diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Muji lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni etutua bulb lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or dry soil stress. Extreme weather prevents the flower from forming seeds, so the plant sheds the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do I need to remove tall weeds around my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, soil food, and sunlight meant for your plants. Even with plenty of water, crops choked by weeds will stay weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ nu babaoo po yɛ Dumɔwui ni jwɛi ehà nɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbɔjɔ ni efee bibii.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines to climb up tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tso ko koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high to catch full sunlight with their leaves. Sunlight helps the vine make food, which travels down to build big, heavy yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa wain tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain sucker take almost a whole year before it shows its fruit stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani ejieɔ aduawai ahe ŋmeii akpo lɛ?

english: Plantain stems must grow many big leaves to gather energy first. The plant uses its first 8 to 10 months to build strength before it has enough power to produce a bunch.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai wuji babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛbua hewalɛ naa. Tso lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 lɛ dani enáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing water in extreme heat. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism telling you that it is experiencing heat stress and needs moisture.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni kɛɔ bo akɛ tso lɛ miina dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni ehe miihia ni ená ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting too much water on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When tomato plants receive too much water, their lower leaves turn yellow and look wilted even though the soil is wet. Overwatering drowns the roots by cutting off the oxygen they need to breathe.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbo, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmu lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable roots with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating rapidly under the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting sunlight to sprout.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu la shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the tall trees on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifo tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because intense heat burns their young leaves and dries out their roots. Taller trees provide necessary shade and humidity for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ shãa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall leafy stems but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso ni baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to direct all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of food storage. Balanced nutrients help the plant focus energy on growing large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛtoɔ akɛ niyenii. Niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling downward like cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips sucking nutrients from under the leaves. Treating the plants early stops leaf damage and restores normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ mra Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil and improves maize growth without requiring extra commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛheɔ jarayeli lɛ afata he.

english: Yam vines climb to catch maximum sunlight for leaf manufacturing of food. Staking keeps leaves exposed to light and off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and producing bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛfee baai kɛha niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa.

english: Why do flowers drop off my garden egg plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ eggplant yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from high heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Maintaining steady soil moisture and allowing bees into the field helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ naa tso lɛ he amanehulu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmeii ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛboteɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my cocoa pods before the whole pod turns black and rots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔi ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots are early signs of Black Pod disease caused by excess wetness and humidity. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees allows air to dry the pods and prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Black spots ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ni ji black pod ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ amli jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct sunlight while their root systems develop. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide fast shade to protect young cocoa plants, while also giving you food and income before the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo oya koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa bo dani cacao tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Will my plantain plants block too much light from my cocoa trees as they both grow bigger?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ baatsi la babaoo ni jɛɔ mikoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: In the early years, plantains provide helpful shade. However, as cocoa trees grow taller and mature, you need to prune or remove older plantain stems so the mature cocoa gets enough sunlight to produce heavy pods.
