ga: Yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ, plantains haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi, beni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni ofolɔ loo ojie tsei ni egbɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo ni eda lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the main trunk instead of on the tips of thin branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni ewoɔ niji bibii lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow flowers directly on their thick trunk and major branches. This unique trait, called cauliflory, allows the tree to support the heavy weight of growing cocoa pods without breaking thin branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei niji wuji anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Atsɛɔ su nɛɛ akɛ kɔlifloa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ etereɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe muji ni tsii ni ehaaa niji bibii lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and turn yellow during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and store high amounts of water in their soft stems. During dry periods, the plant sheds its outer leaves to conserve moisture inside the stem so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛtoɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Will my plantain stalk produce another bunch of fruit after I harvest the first one?
ga: Ani mi-banana tso lɛ baawo aduawai krokomɛi beni mikpa klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, an individual plantain stem produces fruit only once in its life. After harvesting, you cut down the main stem so the plant's energy flows into the small suckers growing at the base to produce the next harvest.
ga: Dabi, plantain tso fɛɛ plantain tso woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ eshihilɛ mli. kpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaabi ni ofo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ koni tso lɛ hewalɛ atsɔ mli kɛya ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ koni ekɛ ŋmaa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba

english: Why do some of the small, young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani etsɔ agbo.

english: This can happen naturally when a tree discards excess pods it cannot feed, known as cherelle wilt. However, if many pods turn black quickly, it may be caused by black pod disease, which spreads easily in wet, overly shaded conditions.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛrɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ ashwie. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo batsɔ ediŋŋ oya lɛ, ale lɛ hu akɛ cherry wilt, ni ŋmeii diji hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha enɛ aba.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots from my field to plant new crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha tsei heei?

english: Select 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a broad base. These shoots grow faster, establish stronger root systems, and produce larger bunches than 'water suckers' that have broad leaves early on.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud,’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ofee tsei akui wuji fe ‘tsei ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ mra.

english: How many months should I expect to wait from the time my cocoa tree flowers until the pods are ready to harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛjɛ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: It generally takes about five to six months for a cocoa flower to develop into a fully mature, ripe pod ready for harvest, provided the tree gets adequate moisture and pest protection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni eda kwraa, ni esa akɛ akpa. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ ná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my goats and pigs directly onto my farm crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ too kɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure is too strong and can generate high heat as it breaks down, which burns young crop roots. It is best to heap and dry the manure for a few weeks to let it decompose before spreading it near your crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔ hee mli wa tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ dɔlɛ babaoo aba kɛji efite. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa ni ogbi otsii fioo komɛi koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani okɛgbɛ ashwã otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does keeping farm animals like goats help improve the crops I grow on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tooi akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Animals convert crop scraps and farm weeds into nutrient-rich manure. Adding this decomposed manure back into your soil improves moisture retention and provides free nutrients for plantains and cash crops without buying expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Koolooi tsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ ku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui kɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, reduces leaf diseases, and helps the plant grow larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe helai aba shi, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer can fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants and leaves the soil richer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the surface and leaves the soil hot underneath. If steady rains do not follow, the heat bakes the seeds in the ground before they can grow roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli dɔɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ shãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: Curling leaves in pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that hide under the leaves, sucking out the plant's sap and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. shwieɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl into the tight center leaf funnel of the plant to feed on the soft growing tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛ ye fãji ni miida blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot if heavy rains soak my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing underground fungal decay and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular, as the heat stresses the plant into dropping blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Ejaakɛ latsaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly full of small holes and ragged edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii trukaa lɛ? Ni ŋwɛigbɛi ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant leaves. They hide deep in the central whorl of young maize, and treating them early with approved sprays or ash prevents them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ amɛ ewo ŋmãa abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. kɛ amɛ tsamɔ mra. kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: This quick dying while green is often caused by Bacterial Wilt, a soil disease that blocks the tubes carrying water inside the stem. The bacteria live in the soil for years, so you need to plant resistant seed varieties or rotate crops like maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbele ni baa oya yɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jɛɔ bacteria wilt, ni ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu gbɛfaa paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ mli. Muawai hiɔ sũ lɛ mli afii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni odu dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ nii loo otsake ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do all the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the air gets too hot, when humidity drops, or if the plant receives too much nitrogen fertilizer. High heat causes stress, making the plant save its energy by releasing the buds instead of producing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi loo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ baa. Ehaa tsei kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry periods to conserve water. Dry winds and low water levels force the tree to reduce moisture loss through its foliage, though proper shade trees help reduce leaf drop.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ baa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛlaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be ni sa baanyɛ aye abua ni baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi moŋ, shi.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting in the storage barn before the planting rains even begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural clock (dormancy period). After resting for a few months post-harvest, biological signals tell the yam it is time to sprout, regardless of whether it is still in storage or planted in the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa (wɔɔ be) beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji amɛyɛ nitoohe lolo loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall with deep green leaves but end up with small ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ebaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ toi bibii lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen helps the leaves and stems grow fast, but crops need phosphorus for strong roots and flowering, and potassium to fill out large corn grains.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi tsei he miihia fɔsfɔs koni amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ fɔfɔii aba. kɛ potassium ni akɛbaawo ŋmãa wuji amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves start turning yellow around the edges and curve downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf borders usually mean potassium deficiency in the soil or damage to the root system from microscopic soil worms called nematodes. Roots unable to feed properly cause the outer leaf edges to dry out first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ahe tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha baa lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbi klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell of one or two weeks. Sowing seeds immediately means they will germinate, but the young seedlings will wither and die in the dry soil before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji otsi kome loo enyɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Shi tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I leave them after heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains soak the ground and submerge the roots in stagnant water, oxygen gets trapped out, causing the starch roots to decay and rot rapidly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ woɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Oxygen lɛ efo mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ starch lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why does planting cowpeas between my main crop rows make the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ midumɔ ŋtayaai titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients, the plant pulls energy from its lower leaves to feed new growth, causing the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does using animal manure help my crops grow better without damaging them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee amɛ?

english: Well-rotted animal manure acts like slow-release food for the soil. It feeds beneficial soil microbes, helps the soil hold water, and releases nutrients slowly so your crops can grow strong without getting burned.
ga: Nibii ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii fiofio Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara waa ni shãaa amɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear rotten fallen leaves and crops away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotting plants attract pests and trap dangerous fungal spores. Keeping your farm clean prevents diseases from spreading to healthy crops, just like keeping a house clean keeps a family healthy.
ga: Tsei ni egboi lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Taakɛ bɔ ni oshia lɛ mli tsemɔ haa oweku lɛ náa hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: This powdery substance is a fungal disease that thrives in humid, damp air. It spreads when leaves stay wet for too long, blocking sunlight from reaching the leaf and weakening the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ powda nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji baai lɛ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: Leaf curling is a survival trick plants use to conserve water. By curling, the leaves reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Leaf curling ji yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Curling haa baai ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain water sits in the farm without proper drainage, it drowns the roots, causing rotting bacteria and fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive dry spells?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts as a blanket (mulch) that protects the soil from direct sunlight. It keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture so your crops don't dry out quickly between rains.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. (Mulch) ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni onibii akagbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or drought stress. The plant feels it doesn't have enough resources to raise a fruit, so it sheds the flower to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ aduawai bɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshi fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do young cocoa plants need to be planted next to plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ darako ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do some of my groundnut shells end up empty inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔji lɛ amli efee efolo kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods usually happen when the soil lacks calcium during the pod-filling stage. Without enough calcium, the plant forms the outer shell but cannot develop the nut inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni awoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji calcium faaa Tso lɛ feɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei shi enyɛɛɛ efee ŋmei ni yɔɔ emli lɛ.

english: Which of the common crops I grow needs the most water to yield well?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni afɔɔ namɔ ni miduɔ lɛ he hiaa nu fe fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Crops like maize, tomatoes, and cabbage consume a lot of water throughout their growth, especially during flowering and fruiting, compared to drought-tolerant crops like cassava or cowpea.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ abele, tomato, kɛ cabbage kɛ nu babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei he.

english: Do my crops need the same amount of water when they are seedlings as when they start flowering?
ga: Ani nu ni fa bɔ ni dumɔwu ko he hiaa beni ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ nɔŋŋ he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: No, young seedlings need light and frequent moisture just to establish roots, but crops reach their highest water intake when they are flowering and developing fruits or seeds.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia la kɛ nu ni mli edɔ shii abɔ koni amɛná shishifãi. Shi tsei naa nu babaoo fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui.

english: Which crops can still produce a decent harvest if the rains end early on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ awo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lolo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra?

english: Cassava, millet, and cowpeas have deep roots and natural survival mechanisms that allow them to draw water from deep in the soil and produce yields even during low rainfall.
ga: Cassava, millet kɛ cowpea yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ gbɛi ni haa amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo po.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my crops too much water or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu miiwo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli babaoo loo fioo tsɔ?

english: If crops get too little water, their leaves wiltingly curl, dry up, and turn brown; if they get too much water, leaves turn pale yellow and root rot develops because roots drown without air.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ naa nu fioo tsɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baa tsɔ, amɛbaa gbi, ni amɛbaa tsɔmɔ asarasu. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: Is there a specific time before harvest when I should stop watering my vegetables?
ga: Dani Abaakpa Ani be ko yɛ ni esa akɛ makpa mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ?

english: Yes, reducing or stopping watering shortly before harvest helps crops like onions, watermelons, and root vegetables mature properly, improves crop sweetness, and prevents rotting.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔtsemɔ loo akpamɔ be fioo dani akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sabolai, watermelon, kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ha tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔ aya hiɛ ni otsi fitemɔ naa

english: If I use a small water pump on my farm, how do I prevent the high water pressure from washing away my topsoil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu pɔmp bibioo ko tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nu ni fa babaoo lɛ naa koni ekafɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can regulate the water flow by attaching drip pipes, sprinkler nozzles, or directing water into small furrows so the water soaks gently into the root zone without carrying soil away.
ga: Obaanyɛ okudɔ bɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ ehaa lɛ kɛtsɔ paipi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. sprinkler nozzle Aloo okɛ nu awo ŋshɔ bibioo ko mli. koni nu lɛ Ashɛre fiofio kɛbote shishifãi lɛ amli ni ejieee sũ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during hot afternoons to shrink their surface area and slow down water loss, which is a natural defense to protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha ohe akagbi.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly during the harmattan season even when I irrigate them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: The harmattan breeze brings extremely dry air and low humidity, which sucks moisture rapidly from both crop leaves and the soil surface much faster than normal weather.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa ni hulutsoo be fioo baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why does water sit on top of the ground in some parts of my field while soaking in instantly in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi yɛ be mli ni efoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil holds water on the surface because its particles are very tight, whereas sandy soil has large spaces that allow water to drain down almost immediately.
ga: Shikpɔji ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi yɛ amɛmli nibii bibii ni mli wa waa lɛ ahewɔ. Shi shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ hei wuji ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the roots of my crops help keep water in the soil?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective blanket that shades the ground from hot direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation and keeping the root area cool.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do my crop leaves get scorched and turn brown after I spray them with pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Crop leaves burn when chemical mixtures are too strong or applied during the intense heat of the day. Mixing chemicals at the correct strength and spraying early in the morning or late evening prevents leaf damage and ensures the plant stays healthy.
ga: Tsei ahe baai lɛ shãa kɛ́ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo akɛwo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ amɛhe yɛ bɔ ni sa mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite, ni ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does mixing chemical sprays with dirty or muddy water make them fail to protect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nu ni mli ewo muji loo sũ mli lɛ ebuuu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Dirt and clay particles in muddy water bind to the active ingredients in farm chemicals, neutralizing their power before they can protect your crops against pests and diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ sũ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ kɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai amli lɛ kpaa gbee. Tsɔɔmɔ amɛ hewalɛi lɛ dani amɛbu onibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods as a survival trick to reduce water loss through evaporation, keeping the main stem and roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni edara bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight; they need shade trees like plantains or forest trees to shield them from sunburn and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is a key food crops need to build strong green leaves and produce heavy grains.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are dying from a disease or from chemical burn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo tsofai ni akɛshãa mitso lɛ baai lɛ miigboi?

english: Disease spots usually expand gradually with yellow rings or fungal spores around them, whereas chemical burns appear rapidly within hours of spraying as dry, uniform spots where the spray droplets landed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ahe tsɔi lɛ baa fiofio. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni shãa lɛ jeɔ kpo oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ. Eji he ko ni egbi, ni ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ po.

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, making it sticky and inactive so flowers fail to pollinate and naturally drop off the plant instead of forming tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollin ni amɛgbee shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, moŋ lɛ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Tubers rot underground when soil is overly waterlogged or infected with soil fungi, which attack the tubers when air cannot reach the root zone.
ga: Tubers fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛtutuaa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of developing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do fall armyworms always attack the tender center funnel of young maize plants first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central leaf funnel of young maize is soft, easy for worms to chew, full of concentrated nutrients, and provides moisture and shade from the hot sun.
ga: Abɛi abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaaye, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo.

english: What makes cash crops like cocoa take several years to yield fruit compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni haa shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he?

english: Perennial tree crops like cocoa focus their early years on building deep root systems and strong trunks to support long-term production, whereas annual crops like maize complete their entire life cycle within a single season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo ji nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ daa afi tamɔ ŋmãa gbeɔ amɛshihilɛ be fɛɛ naa yɛ be kome mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield many pods in one season but very few in the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally experience yield fluctuations because heavy pod production exhausts the tree's nutrient reserves, requiring a lighter season afterwards to rebuild energy for future flowering.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ naa tsakemɔi yɛ amɛ yibiiwoo mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi. Ni eheɔ be ni mli tseee dani anyɛɔ anáa hewalɛ hee kɛha fɔfɔii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and leaf drop during dry periods is the cocoa tree's survival mechanism to reduce water loss and protect its main trunk from severe heat stress.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni kookoo tsei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbuɔ tso titri lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Excessive rainfall can wash away pollen or cause fungal infections that make cocoa flowers drop off early, preventing them from developing into healthy pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen lɛ loo ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya lɛ aba. Etsiɔ shweremɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ naa.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp shade, damaging pods before they mature.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kpatamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees have swollen stems and pale leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi ashishifãi efuu ni amɛbaai lɛ hu yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and pale leaves are signs of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is transmitted by tiny insects called mealybugs and restricts the flow of nutrients throughout the tree.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni efuu kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo bud hela lɛ efuu. ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs. ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I plant temporary shade plants like plantain alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide necessary shade and moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees planted under dense forest canopy produce fewer pods than trees in partial sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ shishi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe tsei ni hulu lɛ fã ko shɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: While cocoa needs protection from harsh sun, too much shade starves the tree of the sunlight needed for photosynthesis, which reduces flowering and pod production.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ abu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he moŋ. Shi hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa tsei aná hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ podi ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do cocoa pods change color from green or red to yellow or orange when they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: The color change indicates that the seeds inside are fully developed and accumulating the natural sugars necessary for proper fermentation.
ga: Kɛ́ su tsake lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edara kwraa, ni amɛbua adebɔɔ mli sugar ni he hiaa koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: What happens to the crop if I harvest cocoa pods before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Unripe cocoa beans lack sufficient sugar content, leading to poor fermentation, flat flavors, and low-quality beans that buyers may reject.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni eshɛko lɛ bɛ sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ŋɔɔɔɔ. kɛ kɔfi ni ehiii kwraa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpoo.

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food maize needs to make strong green leaves, so when it runs out, the plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ená baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ etee lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing tall with huge bushy leaves, but the tubers underground are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich poultry manure, it puts all its energy into growing big leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ woɔ zugba sisi sisi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct full sunlight and hot winds. They need big shade trees or plantain plants above them to block the intense sun and keep the soil moist while their roots are still young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei wuji loo plantains ni haa amɛnáa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to stretch and expand into long, straight tubers. Mounding loosens the soil, improves drainage so the yam does not rot in heavy rain, and allows the tuber to grow big without hitting hard ground.
ga: Atomɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni ekɛgbala ni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ tsei kakadaji ni ja. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaawo lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. improve drainage No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, egbooo. ni ehaa yitso lɛ daa ni etswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: Why should I remove the extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie suckers ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around the mother plantain, they will steal water and soil nutrients from her, resulting in smaller bunches of plantains and weak stems that fall over easily.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ lɛ dɛŋ. Enɛ haa plantains bibii shwieɔ shi. Ni tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagbee shi oya.

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads fast in damp, cool shade. Splashing rain carries the fungus from the ground onto the pods, causing them to turn black and decay if there is no air flow through the farm.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and turn light yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Whiteflies thrive in dry, warm weather and suck sap from tomato plants, passing the leaf curl virus into the crop as they feed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Whiteflies lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ. kɛ nu ni jɛɔ tomato tsei amli lɛ ni amɛnuɔ ni amɛhaa leaf curl virus lɛ yaa tsei lɛ amli beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any pepper fruits begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or water stress. If the weather becomes too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo nu he haomɔ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do small insects bore holes and leave white dust inside my stored maize grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu ni amɛshiɔ sũ yɛŋ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These holes are caused by maize weevils that lay eggs inside dry corn kernels. Once hatched, the young insects eat the inside of the grain and leave dust behind if the maize was not thoroughly dried or treated before storage.
ga: Abele ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ afɔ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baaye ŋmaa lɛ mli ni amɛshi sũ yɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb water before the hot sun causes evaporation, while giving the wet leaves time to dry off quickly, which prevents leaf fungus from attacking the crop.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai ni efɔ lɛ be ni amɛgbi oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ akatutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, or that heavy rains washed the fertilizer away before the roots could take it in. Applying fertilizer in splits at the right growth stage and close to the root zone helps the plant absorb all the food it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajara mli lɛ wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni edaa lɛ mli, ni ebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eŋɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani makwɛ tsei?

english: You can tell by observing your soil's color and how well previous crops grew. Dark, rich soil usually holds nutrients better, while light, sandy, or exhausted soil shows poor crop growth and requires added manure or fertilizer to produce a good harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛi hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ŋã loo sũ ni mli edɔ tsɔɔ tsei adalɛ ni ehiii lɛ. Ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni aná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the stems and leaves grow tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant spends all its energy growing leafy branches instead of storing food below ground. A balanced nutrient blend helps the plant focus on expanding its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei aniji kɛ baai moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa eshishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist at the base of the plant protects the blossoms so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves roll up as a defense mechanism to prevent water from evaporating too quickly in hot sun. Covering the ground around the plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu akatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, shady, and overcrowded farms. Pruning thick branches lets sunlight in and reduces humidity, which stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni efɔ, ni hulu enyɔ shi, ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Niji ni mli tse lɛ afolɔ Ha hulu la abote mli ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Planted too closely, crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, causing them to grow thin, tall, and weak with small yields. Proper spacing gives every crop enough room and light to yield heavily.
ga: planted too close Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni kɛlɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa lɛ baa. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tsei fɛɛ aná he ko kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to germinate out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil dries out completely, or if insects eat them underground. Planting seeds at a depth equal to twice their size into moist soil gives them the best chance to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa, loo kɛji kooloi ye dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tamɔ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How does excessive rainfall hurt my yam crops growing in the field?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ saa mi sweet potato tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too much water can saturate the ground, cutting off air to the soil and causing yam tubers to rot underground. Building raised mounds or high ridges allows excess water to drain away safely.
ga: Nu babaoo baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface and cannot always support a heavy fruit bunch during high winds. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden or bamboo fork prevents the tree from snapping before harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni jeee be fɛɛ be amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni mli wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ dani akpa.

english: How will using land clearing machines help my farm compared to using only my cutlass and hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto dade kɛ shɔvel pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Machines allow you to clear larger plots of land quickly and prepare deep, loose soil. This saves you heavy physical labor, saves time, and helps crop roots grow deeper to absorb more water and nutrients for better yields.
ga: Mashiŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ shikpɔji wuji anɔ oya ni osaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ. Enɛ haaa oná gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ, be, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii babaoo koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops absorb nutrients from the soil every season to grow. If you do not replenish the soil using organic manure or fertilizers, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller harvests over time.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be koni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ okɛ humus loo humus wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baafee bibioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Will adding more chemical fertilizer automatically make my crops grow faster and produce more?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha mitsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Applying too much fertilizer can burn the crop roots and damage the soil. Crops only need a balanced amount applied at the right time to grow healthy and yield well.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ji tsofai ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I leave some big trees standing when clearing the forest to plant my cash crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni damɔ shi beni mijieɔ koo lɛ mli kɛha mishika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Large forest trees provide critical shade that protects young crops from scorching sun heat, keep the soil moist, and protect your farm from strong winds that can break young plants.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dɔlɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I earn money from my land while waiting several years for long-term tree crops like cocoa to start producing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ afii babaoo koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ daa tamɔ kookoo lɛ abɔi ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ?

english: You can plant short-term food crops like plantains, cassava, or maize between your young tree crops. These quick crops provide early food and income while also sheltering the young tree crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ plantains, cassava loo ŋmãa yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ oya nɛɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long without proper drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and stay asleep in dry soil, waiting for the first rain to sprout quickly. They compete aggressively with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil food.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ amɛmiimɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are insects damaging my crop leaves more during the hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Many crop pests multiply rapidly in warm, dry weather because heat speeds up their lifecycle. Furthermore, thirsty insects attack crop leaves to get the moisture hidden inside them.
ga: Kooloi babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa amɛshihilɛ yaa oya. Kplukai ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ hu tutuaa tsei ahe baai koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain spoil or get attacked by insects so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi bibii tutuaa amɛ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: If grain is stored with too much moisture inside, fungi and insects thrive in it. Thoroughly drying your grain under the sun before storing it in sealed, dry bags keeps pests out and preserves its market value.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui to ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, Fungus kɛ kooloi baakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi dani akɛwo kotokui ni egbi ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha amɛ jara ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can smallholder farmers like me get access to affordable farming machines and subsidized inputs in our community?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ aná okwaayeli tsɔnei ni jara waaa kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Joining a local farmer group or cooperative allows you to register with district agriculture offices. Governments and organizations usually distribute subsidized machinery, seeds, and fertilizers through recognized farmer groups.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu loo kuu ko mli lɛ, ebaaha okɛ ohe awo Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔyelii kɛ gbɛjianɔtoi jaa tsɔnei. dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa kɛtsɔɔ okwaafoi akui ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that create shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leafy stems above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or heavy rainfall early on, it puts all its energy into growing branches and leaves above the ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ shishijee mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei niji kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do groundnut flowers sink into the dirt after they bloom instead of producing fruit on the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ, moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a special way of growing where the flower pollinates above ground, then grows a long stalk called a peg that burrows into the soil to safely form the peanut pod underground.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛdaraa ni akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant capture light better, which produces larger and healthier yam tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ he. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn plants need to build strong stems and leafy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Why do the leaves on my hot pepper bushes curl up into cup shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee kɔɔpoo lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding on the undersides of leaves and sucking out the plant juices, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers keep dropping off the stem without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are not enough bees and wind to shake the pollen inside the flower to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baanyɛ atswa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center funnel of my corn plants eating holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, common pests in Ghana that hide inside the central funnel of young corn plants to feed on soft growing leaves before the plant can produce corn cobs.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai dani tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmeii.

english: Why can paddy rice survive in standing water while my vegetables die if flooded for two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu afua lɛ ye gbii enyɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes that carry oxygen from the leaves down to the roots under water, whereas vegetable roots drown because they cannot breathe in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai ashishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough moisture for planting without using expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii ni akɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can dig down a few inches, scoop up a handful of soil, and squeeze it in your hand. If it forms a ball that holds together without dripping water, the moisture level is good for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ muji ni okɛwo oniji amli lɛ ni okɛmimɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko ni yɔɔ kokroo ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Fɛ̃i hi kɛha shweremɔ.

english: Why do the seeds I buy from the agricultural extension officer stay healthier than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mli nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Seeds provided by extension officers are produced under clean conditions and monitored naturally to ensure they are free of infections, giving them strong built-in protection against common farm diseases.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli tse mli, ni akwɛɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ana akɛ hela ko bɛ mli. Enɛ haa hebuu ni mli wa ni ama awo mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I am buying for this planting season are clean and disease-free?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛha nɛkɛ shweremɔ be nɛɛ mli tse ni hela bɛ mli?

english: Good seeds come from certified sources where parent plants are carefully monitored using natural methods to guarantee that no hidden diseases are passed down into the seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai jɛɔ hei ni awo he hewalɛ ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni ana akɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ko eboteee dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: What does it actually mean when officers say seeds have been monitored before bringing them to our community?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ onukpai kɛɛ akɛ akwɛɔ dumɔwui amli dani akɛbaa wɔ akutso lɛ mli?

english: It means experts closely inspect the plants while they are growing to catch and remove any sickness early, ensuring that only healthy, disease-free seeds reach your farm.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋaalɔi kwɛɔ tsei anɔ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ helai ni amɛjie amɛ kɛjɛ mli mra. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ pɛ shɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young crops sometimes get sick right after sprouting, and how can I stop this from happening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ hela mɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enɛ naa koni ekaba?

english: Early crop sickness often comes from disease organisms already living inside poor-quality seeds; using tested, disease-free seeds ensures your crops start life healthy and grow without early attack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai ni baa mra lɛ jɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ehiii amli momo lɛ amli. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko etutuaa amɛ mra.

english: Is it possible to protect my farm from diseases without spending money on expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe ni afiteee shika yɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting disease-resistant seed varieties and using natural field management techniques allows your crops to naturally resist diseases without needing heavy chemical treatments.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo he ŋaai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai ni tsii he ehiaaa.

english: If I plant clean, disease-resistant seeds, do I still need to do extra work during cultivation to keep them healthy?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni he tse ni helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni matsu nitsumɔ kroko lolo yɛ dumɔ be mli koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: While clean seeds naturally withstand major diseases, keeping your field free of weeds and giving plants proper spacing helps preserve their natural protection throughout the growing season.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai ni naa wa nɔ moŋ, shi kɛji akɛ jwɛi bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ni okɛ tsei lɛ to he ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni adebɔɔ mli hebuu ahi shi yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Will disease-free seeds still produce a good yield if my land does not have very rich soil?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni hela bɛ mli lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy seeds have a strong starting foundation and efficient root systems, which helps them survive better and produce reliable yields even under tough soil conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shishijee shishitoo ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa po nɔ.

english: Why are extension officers introducing these new crop seeds to us gradually instead of bringing them all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ jieɔ dumɔwui heei nɛɛ akpo amɛtsɔɔ wɔ fiofio moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee amɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: New seed varieties are supplied gradually so officers can carefully monitor how well they adapt to local farm conditions and ensure no unexpected diseases affect your land.
ga: Dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Akɛhaa koni onukpai lɛ akwɛ bɔ ni nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ nɔmimaa aha akɛ helai ni akpaaa gbɛ ko baaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does it take so long for new, improved seed varieties to reach our village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani dumɔwui heei ni asaa amɛhe lɛ shɛɔ wɔ akrowa lɛ?

english: Seed producers spend considerable time testing and monitoring new seeds naturally across different seasons to guarantee they are completely disease-free before sharing them with farmers.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ be babaoo amɛkaa adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui heei amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛ yɛ bei amli. Enɛ ji koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ hela bɛ amɛhe kwraa dani akɛ amɛ aha okwaafoi.

english: Can diseases spread to my crops if my neighboring farmer plants low-quality, unmonitored seeds?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ du dumɔwui ni ehiii ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, crop diseases can travel through wind, water, and insects from nearby fields, which is why extension officers encourage entire farming communities to adopt clean, monitored seeds together.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ kooloi ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ okwaafoi akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is your maize plant's natural defense against heat and drought. The plant rolls its leaves to hide part of its surface area from the hot sun, which helps cut down on water loss through evaporation until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ ehiɛ fã ko ato hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from severe heat or water stress. When the soil is too dry or the air is too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save water and keep itself alive rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baawo yibii heei lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly after a tractor plows my field when the ground is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni traktɔ lɛ etsu nii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plowing wet soil crushes the natural air pockets in the ground, causing heavy soil compaction. This creates hard layers underground that make it very difficult for crop roots to breathe, spread, and absorb water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi fã ko ni wa baa ni ehaa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu, amɛja, ni amɛŋɔ nu.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with friendly soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When these plants die, they leave behind natural nitrogen fertilizer that nourishes your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow and dying while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Because nitrogen can move inside the plant, the corn takes this nutrient away from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the young green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen baanyɛ aya tsei amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli. ni otsu lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyaye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge stem leaves but produce very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, cassava puts all its energy into growing green leaves on top instead of swollen roots underground. Loose, well-balanced soil encourages the plant to store food in the roots instead.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baa eŋɔli nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi ni efuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ja jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct sun. The large trees provide living shade that keeps the air humid and shields the young cocoa leaves from intense sunlight until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo, amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ ni amɛbuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli waɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall, thin, and weak when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight. The plants put all their energy into stretching upward to outgrow their neighbors for light, making them tall and fragile with weak stems.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya fe amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ koni amɛtao la. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛshishifãi hu bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout and cover my farm so much faster than my planted crop seeds after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and can germinate instantly with the smallest amount of moisture. Cultivated crop seeds usually need specific planting depths and slightly more time to wake up and grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo fioo ko pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ biɔ dumɔ mlibotemɔ pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ be fioo ko ni fata he koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I bury them very deep in the soil to wait for rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni mimɛ nugbɔ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they exhaust all their stored food energy trying to push up through the heavy dirt before they ever see sunlight. Plant seeds at the correct shallow depth so they can reach the surface quickly after taking in moisture.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Niyenii ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani ena hulu la lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi oya beni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for tree crops to start producing fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ tso tso ko heɔ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Many improved varieties of tree crops take about 3 years to start bearing fruit, though maximum yield is usually reached as the trees fully mature over the following years.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni asaa amɛhe lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ, bei pii lɛ, anáa yibiiwoo ni fe fɛɛ beni tso lɛ daa yɛ sɛɛ mli afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do some crops take three years to produce while vegetables take only a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ afii etɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni aduawai heɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tree crops need time to build strong roots and branches to support years of harvesting, whereas short-term crops focus all their energy on quick growth and immediate seed production.
ga: Be he miihia tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi amli lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baaye abua afii babaoo ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa amɛdalɛ oya kɛ dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my fruit crop is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miyibii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most fruits show readiness through changes in skin color, firmness, sweet aroma, or when they loosen easily from the branch.
ga: Yibii babaoo jieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛtsɔ amɛhewolo nɔ su tsakemɔi, amɛhewalɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ, loo kɛ́ amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough for growing perennial fruit crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha aduawai ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ adumɔ?

english: Perennial crops need deep, well-drained soil and adequate seasonal rainfall, which an agricultural extension officer can test before you plant.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa. ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ aka amɛkwɛ dani odu

english: What kind of crop should I choose if I want something that gives good money but doesn't take too many years to start yielding?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ ohala kɛji oosumɔ nɔ ko ni woɔ nyɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ shi eheee be babaoo ni ekɛbaatsu nii?

english: You can look for improved hybrid tree crop varieties that start yielding within 3 years, or intercrop young trees with short-term cash crops like plantain or vegetables.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona tsei sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 mli, loo okwɛ tsei bibii ni shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains loo aduawai yɔɔ mli.

english: Is it guaranteed that I will make money if I plant a fast-yielding tree crop on my empty land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo nɔmimaa akɛ maná shika kɛji midu tsei ni woɔ yibii oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Profits depend on good farm management, protecting crops from pests, labor costs, and having a reliable market to sell to after harvest.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ damɔ ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo, kɛ jara ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I make income from my land during the three years while waiting for my tree crops to start fruiting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afii etɛ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ni tsei lɛ abɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: You can plant short-term food crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between the young trees to generate income and food while the main crop grows.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ koni eha shika kɛ niyenii aba be mli ni ŋmãa titri lɛ miida.

english: If a crop produces beautiful and healthy-looking fruit, does that automatically mean it will give a high yield?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii fɛfɛji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii babaoo kɛjɛ ehe?

english: Fruit appearance shows good health, but total yield depends on overall tree nutrition, proper spacing, disease control, and using high-yielding seed varieties.
ga: Bɔ ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ kpakpa. Shi yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ damɔ tso lɛ niyenii fɛɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ, helai ahe nitsumɔ, kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Where can I get reliable seedlings that are guaranteed to bear fruit within three years?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaawo yibii yɛ afii etɛ mli lɛ yɛ?

english: You should buy certified seedlings from recognized government nurseries or accredited agricultural centers to ensure they are healthy and quick-yielding varieties.
ga: Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ nɔyeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei loo okwaayeli hei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ amɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii mra.

english: Do I need to care for young crop trees during the first three years before they start producing fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi?
