english: Yes, regular weeding, watering, and pest protection during the first three years are essential to help the young trees establish strong roots for high future yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa, nu ni akɛhaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia koni eye ebua tsei bibii ni amɛma shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ kɛha yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do maize crops grow so much better in districts like Sekyeredumase and Nkoranza compared to other places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei tamɔ Sekyeredumase kɛ Nkoranza kɛ akɛto hei krokomɛi ahe lɛ.

english: Areas like Sekyeredumase and Nkoranza have very rich, fertile soils and balanced rainfall patterns that naturally supply maize with the constant water and nutrients it needs to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Hei tamɔ Sekyeredumase kɛ Nkoranza yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii waa ni baa nii. ni eyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni ja Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii haa ŋmãa lɛ daa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the land I chose is good enough to produce a bountiful harvest of maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mihala lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Good land for maize has deep, loose soil that drains water easily after rain and does not get waterlogged. If weeds and natural grass grow tall and dark green on the plot, it shows the soil has high fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni mli kwɔ. Ehaa nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli kɛji jwɛi kɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi dara ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii waa.

english: How can I tell when my maize crop is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he kwraa kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn dry and straw-colored, the silks on top of the cob turn dark brown, and the kernels feel hard and firm when pressed with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee tamɔ jwɛi. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nineshi tsɔne miimɔ nɔ.

english: What happens if I harvest my maize too early before it is completely ready?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ mra tsɔ dani efee klalo kwraa?

english: Harvesting maize too early means the grains will have too much water inside, causing them to shrink as they dry, and they will rot or mold easily when stored.
ga: Abele ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo baahi ŋmaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛgbi. ni ebaagbo loo ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛ akɛto

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to hide their surface area from the sun, reducing water loss through evaporation during intense heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main plant food. If the yellowing starts at the leaf tips and moves along the middle, applying nitrogen fertilizer will restore the green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmã he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ ni amɛtee teŋgbɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my maize stalks produce two big cobs while others only produce one small cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ toi wuji enyɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo kome pɛ.

english: A stalk produces multiple good cobs when it receives plenty of sunlight, space, water, and nutrients. If plants are crowded or short on water and plant food, the stalk focuses all its energy on making just one smaller cob.
ga: Tso kome baawo ŋmeii kpakpai babaoo kɛji akɛ aha lɛ hulu la, he ko, nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Kɛji tso lɛ eyi obɔ loo nu kɛ tso niyenii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmei bibioo kome.

english: Why is it bad for my yield if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants grow too close together, their roots fight each other for soil food and water, while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight, resulting in thin, weak stalks with very poor cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: How can I make sure my maize crop spreads out uniformly across my field for a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-ŋmãa lɛ aja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Planting in straight, properly measured rows with consistent spacing between seeds gives every single plant equal access to sunlight, air, soil nutrients, and water.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni asusu he jogbaŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ po yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii anɔ. kɛ nu pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why should I buy certified seed instead of just planting grains saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to produce uniform, strong plants that resist diseases and yield much heavier cobs. Grains saved from previous harvests lose their vigor and result in smaller, unequal cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni wa, ni yaa nɔ daa. Helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ ni amɛwoɔ cob ni tsii fe no kwraa. Ŋmãa ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ.

english: Yellowing starting from the tip and moving down the middle of older maize leaves usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed for green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi yɛ ŋmeii baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara lɛ

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil around them for too long without draining away, suffocating the roots and allowing harmful fungus to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni haaa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ada.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from taking over your bed.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha otsu lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on the same field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but groundnuts are special crops that capture food from the air and feed it back into the earth, restoring the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmei ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agbo ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my corn plants produce very small cob sizes when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to build big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from fresh leaves, or by a sickness carried into the plant by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ hela ni jɛ nakai kooloi lɛ amli lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or a lack of insects to move pollen around inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before applying granular fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmeii ni ji granular fertilizer awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer granules need moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink them in; putting dry fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots or simply waste the fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do mangoes grown here in Ghana taste sweeter and sell better than those from neighboring regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana biɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ fe nɔ ni jɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ghana’s unique weather provides the ideal balance of bright sunshine and dry periods during flowering. This helps mango trees build up higher natural sugar levels, giving Ghanaian mangoes exceptional sweetness and high market value.
ga: Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli fɔfɔii lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa mango tso lɛ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar ni fa babaoo baa. Enɛ haa Ghana mango lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa, ni ejara wa waa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do my mango tree flowers keep falling off before turning into real fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop when the tree experiences dry spells, strong winds, or attack by small pests like thrips. Keeping the roots moist during early flowering and protecting the farm from common pests helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo be, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips. Kɛ́ ahã shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ mra lɛ, ni abuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fɔɔ baa lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my mango tree yield a huge harvest this year, but almost no fruits the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ afi nɛɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, ani eshwɛ fioo ni abaawo yibii?

english: After producing a heavy harvest, the tree gets exhausted and spends its remaining food to rebuild itself. Pruning old branches after harvest and applying rich manure helps the tree bear good fruit consistently every year.
ga: Beni akpa yibii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ he baajɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛma ehe ekoŋŋ. Niji ni egbɔ ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai daa afi.

english: Why are my ripening mangoes developing soft spots with small worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by fruit flies laying eggs under the mango skin while the fruit is still on the tree. You can protect your harvest by hanging fruit fly traps in your farm and clearing away fallen fruits from the ground.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ mango lɛ shishi be mli ni aduawai lɛ kã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookɛwo oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ooojie aduawai ni egbee shi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my young mango trees when setting up a new farm?
ga: Kɛ́ ato ŋmɔ hee ko shishi lɛ, te esa akɛ adu mango tsei kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Mango trees need wide spacing—about 10 meters apart—so their branches and roots do not fight for food and light. Giving them enough room ensures every tree receives direct sun to produce heavy harvests.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 10, no hewɔ lɛ tsei niji kɛ shishifãi kɛ amɛhe wooo niyenii kɛ la he akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tsei fɛɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do my fruit trees produce fewer fruits when they grow under the shade of bigger trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni amɛdaraa yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Fruit trees need direct sunlight to make food for growing flowers and fruits. Under deep shade, the tree wastes its energy growing tall branches toward the light instead of bearing fruit.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ lɛ shishi Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛɔ niji kakadaji ni kwɛɔ la lɛ hiɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off some branches from my mango tree when they look completely healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mango tso lɛ niji komɛi? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni eye emuu?

english: Cutting selected branches opens up the middle of the tree to let sunshine and fresh air pass through. This prevents plant diseases and forces the tree to put energy into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhalaa tso lɛ mli lɛ haa gbɛ ko baa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my land has good soil for growing long-term tree crops like mangoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mango?

english: Tree crops need deep soil where roots can reach far down and water drains easily. If rainwater sits on your land without draining for days, the soil will retain too much water and rot the tree roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he ko ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ta oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli gbii babaoo. Sũ lɛ baaha nu babaoo ahi shi ni ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the green leaves on my crops turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate the plant is missing nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are suffocating from too much standing water. Feeding the soil with compost or manure restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds make my crops grow slow and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves by soaking up the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment required to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii julɔi kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient, or the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves roll up and get covered in tiny bugs during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Cover yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava leaves curl during dry weather because pests like cassava green mites suck the sap from the leaves when heat stresses the plant. Spraying neem oil water or preserving natural predator insects helps control these pests.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ ejaakɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cassava green mite lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ cassava baai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ́ dɔlɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and develop twisted, wrinkled leaves at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpa shweremɔ ni ehiɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Twisted and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses they spread. Controlling these insects early with organic or approved sprays prevents damage to new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ kudɔmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if insects are not visiting to pollinate them. Keeping soil moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young plantain trees bend over and fall down easily when the fruit bunch grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni kuu lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and no strong wooden trunk, so heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Supporting the stem with sturdy forked wooden props prevents winds and heavy fruits from uprooting the plant.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbɛ tso ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso yibii bibii ni tsii ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni akɛ tsɔnei ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie tso lɛ kɛjɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of green leafy vines but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miikwɛ wain tsei babaoo ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to grow leaves instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air, so they need phosphorus nutrients rather than high-nitrogen fertilizers to make pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ fɔsfɔs babaoo fe nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to build a strong stalk and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii ni sa, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yam in the exact same field where I harvested yam last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Planting yam continuously in the same soil depletes specific nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and rot diseases to multiply. Rotating yam with crops like legumes or cereals restores soil health and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa. Sweet potatoes ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmaa tsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan winds strip moisture from leaves faster than young roots can take water from dry soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa plants from harsh sun and dry winds.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem as tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Stem base beni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ

english: Why do some crops need to be planted in a nursery first instead of directly on my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tsei komɛi klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Nursery planting protects delicate seeds and young plants from harsh weather, pests, and heavy rain while they are weak, ensuring only strong and healthy seedlings are moved to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Can I make money by raising crop seedlings in a nursery to sell to other farmers?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná shika kɛtsɔ tsei dumɔwui ni makwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, running a nursery to sell healthy seedlings is a good business because many farmers prefer buying strong, ready-to-plant young crops rather than risking growing them from seed themselves.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ ni agbeleɔ koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ji jarayeli kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okwaafoi babaoo sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ adu ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooŋɔ oshara ni ji bo diɛŋtsɛ otsei ni oootsɔ dumɔwui anɔ lɛ,.

english: How do I know when seedlings in my nursery are ready to be planted out on the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings are ready when they have developed a firm stem, a few strong leaves, and a good root system that can hold soil together without breaking easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. baai fioo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi kpakpai ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ sũ lɛ ekome ni ekumɔɔɔ mlɛo.

english: What else can I get from my harvested crops besides selling them raw at the market?
ga: Mɛni kroko hu manyɛ maná kɛjɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli kɛfata ni mikɛbaahɔɔ lɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ he?

english: Many crops can be processed into higher-value products like cooking oil, seed cake for animal feed, and leftover residue that can be recycled for farm use or fuel.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni afee nibii ni jara wa waa tamɔ fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii. Dumɔwui keeki kɛha kooloi aniyenii kɛ nibii ni eshwɛ ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ koni akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli loo akɛ tsofa.

english: Is it better for me to sell my crops fresh after harvest or process them into oil first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehee beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ loo mafee amɛ fɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Selling fresh gives you immediate cash without processing costs, but processing allows you to store the product longer and sell at higher prices based on specific customer demands.
ga: Nibii heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ haa onáa shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo ko fataaa he. Shi bɔ ni atsuɔ he nii ahaa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii lɛ toɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ bɔ ni mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ hiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ yɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: What can I do with the solid waste or press cake left behind after extracting oil from my crops?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ jwɛi loo keeki ni eshwɛ beni mijie fɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The press cake is very valuable as protein-rich feed for livestock like pigs and poultry, while organic crop residue can be composted into rich soil fertilizer.
ga: Abuɔ keeki ni atswa lɛ waa akɛ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein kɛha kooloi tamɔ tsinai kɛ kooloi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee tsei ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ sũ ni baa nii.

english: Can the nuts or seeds I harvest be eaten raw as well as processed into oil?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aye ŋmeii loo dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ ŋmɔŋ loo afee amɛ fɔ?

english: Yes, many oil-bearing nuts and seeds can be consumed raw or roasted directly as food, or crushed and processed into oil depending on what buyers in your area want.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ aye ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui babaoo ni mli ewo mu lɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ashã amɛ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ niyenii. loo atswa ni afee lɛ fɔ Edamɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I process my whole crop harvest into oil all at once or wait until buyers place orders?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ni mafee lɛ fɔ shikome loo mamɛ kɛyashi mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baabi?

english: Processing based on customer orders is often safer because it prevents fresh crop oil from spoiling in storage and avoids spending money on processing before a buyer is confirmed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaatsi tsofa ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ mli fɔ hee lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he dani mɔ ni heɔ lɛ lɛ aná nɔmimaa.

english: Why do some buyers ask for fresh raw crops while others want processed oil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ ni aha amɛ nibii heei yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi biɔ ni aha amɛ mu ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ?

english: Different buyers have different business needs; household consumers and local food vendors often buy raw fresh crops for cooking, while commercial buyers look for processed oil and cake for manufacturing.
ga: Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ jarayeli he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni yeɔ nii yɛ shia kɛ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ niyenii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ heɔ niyenii ni ahoo koni amɛkɛhoo nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ taoɔ mu ni afee lɛ srɔtoi kɛ keeki ni afee lɛ.

english: What are the main basic stages I need to follow to produce a successful crop from start to finish?
ga: Shishijee gbɛi titrii Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyashi naagbee?

english: Successful crop production relies on three main stages: cultivating and preparing the land, planting healthy seeds or seedlings properly, and harvesting mature crops carefully at the right time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni yeɔ omanye lɛ damɔ gbɛi titrii etɛ nɔ: ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ. Dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ ni akpaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do people say I should sweep or clear the floor under my cocoa trees like I clean my home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ mafo loo mafo shikpɔŋ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi tamɔ bɔ ni mijieɔ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing the ground under your cocoa trees removes hiding places for pests and fungal diseases like black pod. Keeping the farm floor clean prevents damp conditions that make your trees sick.
ga: He ni osaa o-cocoa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baaye abua ni ejie nɔ ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akahã otsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ.

english: What is 'Aproka' in cocoa farming, and how does it affect my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Aproka’ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii amli? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Aproka' refers to clean-weeding or thoroughly sweeping the ground beneath your cocoa trees. It prevents weeds from stealing fertilizer and water from your cocoa roots, helping your trees grow stronger.
ga: Aproka’ shishi ji ni atsumɔ jwɛi loo atsumɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it harmful to leave old, rotting cocoa pods on the ground under my trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni miifite lɛ yɛ mitso lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, leaving diseased or rotting pods on the ground allows fungal spores to spread back onto healthy hanging pods whenever it rains, leading to heavy crop losses.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni egboi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fĩ shi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ waa.

english: How often in a year do I need to clean and clear the undergrowth on my cocoa farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni matsumɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe yɛ afi mli?

english: It is best to clean under your cocoa trees 3 to 4 times a year, especially right before the heavy rains start, to stop weeds from choking the trees and to control pests.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsumɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Bɔni afee ni jwɛi akakpɛtɛ tsei lɛ ahe, ni akɛye kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anɔ

english: How does clearing thick brush beneath cocoa trees help them breathe and produce more?
ga: sweeping thick brush Te kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi shihilɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛmu ni amɛwo yibii babaoo amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Removing thick brush increases airflow around the tree trunks. Better air movement dries out excess moisture quickly after rain, which stops fungal diseases from multiplying.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie brɔshi ni mli tse lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ. tso lɛ shishi Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Can simply keeping my cocoa farm floor clean increase my yield without using expensive chemicals?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehe atse lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, regular farm sanitation reduces pest and disease pressure naturally. By saving pods from rotting, you harvest more cocoa beans without spending heavily on chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni oooha ŋmeii lɛ akafite Enɛ baaha onyɛ okpa kookoo ŋmeii babaoo ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why does humidity or damp ground make my cocoa pods turn black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo loo hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a water mold that thrives in dark, damp conditions. When the farm ground is messy and wet, the mold grows quickly and splashes onto lower pods.
ga: Nu mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli he lɛ mli efee basabasa ni edɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni eshwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees yielding more pods than mine when we share the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ akutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe wɔ cacao tsei lɛ be mli ni wɔkɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Higher yields often come down to daily management practices like regular farm cleaning, prompt removal of sick pods, and proper shade control rather than just soil quality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ daa gbi nitsumɔ nɔkwɛmɔ nifeemɔi, tamɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ daa nɔ. Nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ oya kɛ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Jeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpakpa pɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to adopt a new cocoa maintenance method I learned from another farmer in my village?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ gbɛi heei ni mikase kɛjɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Learning from successful local farmers is a great practical step, but it is always good to confirm with an extension officer to ensure the practice suits your specific land and tree age.
ga: Nikasemɔ kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ o-extension officer lɛ ama nɔ mi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nifeemɔ lɛ sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ tso lɛ afii.

english: How does managing light and shade inside my cocoa farm change how pods develop?
ga: Te kane kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ pod lɛ shweremɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Balanced light helps cocoa trees make energy for pod growth, while reducing heavy shade prevents moisture buildup that causes pods to rot before they mature.
ga: La ni ja yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ haa pod lɛ dalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ shi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the afternoon sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which prevents the plant from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa tree leaves turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during prolonged dry spells to reduce water loss and protect the trunk from heat stress, though proper shade and mulching can help keep leaves green.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ yitso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli moŋ, shi.

english: Why do my soya bean plants produce flowers that fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Soya beans naturally shed a portion of their flowers if the weather is too hot or if the soil lacks moisture during flowering, as the plant conserves energy for fewer, healthier pods.
ga: Soybeans baajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ toɔ kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my young maize plants to turn a purple or reddish color?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple loo etsuru?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually indicate that the plant is struggling to absorb phosphorus from the soil, often due to cool soil temperatures or poor root establishment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ejie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo shishifãi ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the thick main trunk instead of just on thin leafy branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso titri ni mli tse lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on their main trunk and thick branches because mature cocoa pods are heavy, and the solid trunk is strong enough to support their weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsii ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ amɛtsiimɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my rice stalks fall flat on the ground just before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over—a problem called lodging—when the stalks grow too weak, which usually happens if too much nitrogen fertilizer is used or if seeds are planted too close together.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbee shi - naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ lodging - kɛji ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii loo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Do my soya bean crops need the same heavy chemical fertilizer that I give to my maize field?
ga: Ani tsofai ni tsii ni mikɛhaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ nɔŋŋ he miihia mi-soybean tsei lɛ?

english: No, soya beans belong to the legume family and can make much of their own nitrogen fertilizer from the air through helpful bacteria living on their roots.
ga: Dabi, soybeans yɛ legume weku lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ efee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my lowland rice turn yellow and stop growing if the field dries out for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa shweremɔ kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbi gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice roots are designed to absorb nutrients while underwater; when the soil dries completely, the roots temporarily lose the ability to take up nitrogen properly.
ga: Afee ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ nu shishi lɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nitrogen jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn dark brown, shrivel up, and die before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egboɔ ni egboɔ dani edara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods shrivel due to black pod disease or natural thinning; high humidity and damp conditions encourage fungal diseases that destroy the pods early.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ ŋmeii diji hela loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi kɛ ŋmeii helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya baa.

english: Why do my crops wilt early in the morning even when the soil received good rain two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ egbiɔ leebi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil often means the roots are rotting or waterlogged, which prevents oxygen from reaching the roots and stops them from drawing water up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa nu lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet for too long, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or lack water. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready to harvest so it does not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni egbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off. Leaving tubers in waterlogged soil after maturity causes them to lose starch and turn watery or rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afite ni amɛbaafee nu loo amɛbaafite.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes go soft and spoil so quickly on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ mitee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes keep ripening and breathing after being picked. Harvesting them during the hot afternoon heat or packing them in deep, unventilated baskets traps heat, causing them to spoil much faster.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ ekwɛ̃ lolo ni amɛmiimu beni ajie amɛ sɛɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa loo yɛ tsɛnsii ni mli kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ baaha hulutsoo ahi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, egboɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do the improved seed varieties grow faster than my traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ daa oya fe mishishijee maŋ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to put energy into fast growth and early fruiting. Local varieties are naturally tough and built to survive unpredictable conditions, which makes them grow at a slower pace.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaadara oya ni amɛwo yibii mra. Kuu lɛ mli kooloi lɛ ahe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ama amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why do my vegetables grow tall and thin with small leaves when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ baai bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plant stretches upward quickly to get light, making the stem thin and weak.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe oya koni eha la lɛ abote mli. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning shade trees and weeding helps sunlight dry the cocoa pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the crop conserve moisture and prevent water loss during hot hours.
ga: Cowpea shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaaa nu lɛ afite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing thin and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ mli tse ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to push down and expand easily. If the soil is hard, stony, or not mounded properly, the tuber struggles to push through and becomes misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tubers he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe oya ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo ebɛ gɔŋji kpakpai lɛ, Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛbaafite.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with sturdy bamboo props helps keep the trees upright during strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Ha amɛfee nɔ ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their leaves from getting burned by direct heat and to keep the soil moist. Large shade trees or food crops like plantains protect young cocoa from intense sunlight until they are strong enough to handle full exposure.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ akashã amɛbaai lɛ. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves grow green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni efee eŋɔli ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dryness. Keeping the soil moisture steady and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛhe egbi waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers using sunlight on their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf rot caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. ni etsĩɔ baai ni sũ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my pepper plants help them survive hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Covering the dirt around your plants with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct sun, stops soil water from evaporating, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ebɔle Tsei ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are small worms eating the leaves hidden inside the center of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the soft center part of the maize stalk where they are safe from the sun while eating the fresh growing leaves. Spraying early when the plants are young protects the growing tips.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ateŋ he ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ mra be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I put fertilizer on my farm after it rains instead of when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink it in. If applied to dry soil during bright sun, the chemical fertilizer can evaporate into the air or burn the dry plant roots.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo eha tso shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year give me smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients naturally back to the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally have stronger roots designed to grab available water and food instantly before cultivated crops can. Removing them quickly gives your planted crops a chance to drink and grow first.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Afee amɛ koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ dani tsei ni miida lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ oya lɛ, ehaa odumɔi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛdaraa klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and lose water quickly through their soft leaves. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to shelter them from severe sun until their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: These pests are likely fall armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of maize. Early detection and applying recommended treatments into the leaf center protect the growing tip so the plant can develop healthy ears.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mɔ. ni kɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ Mra ni ana Ni tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will restore the healthy green color needed for growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas make my farmland better for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When the plant leaves and stems decay, they leave behind rich nutrients that nourish the next crop planted there.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛbaashi niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when left in standing water because waterlogged soil cuts off the air roots need to breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ foɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does covering my garden bed with dried grass keep my crops healthy in the dry season?
ga: Te abɔɔ mli saatsoi ni akɛ jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from the hot sun. It traps moisture in the soil longer and prevents the earth from cracking and drying out root systems.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fãa ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I need to clear away extra young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant grows big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can capture maximum sunlight to grow bigger tubers under the soil. It also keeps leaves away from wet ground pests and diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛmɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ hu ahe.

english: Why is it bad practice to apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away off the surface of the farm into streams before roots can absorb it, wasting your money and starving your plants of needed nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eheɔ bo shika ni ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants face extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Giving plants steady, consistent water and protecting soil moisture keeps the flowers healthy enough to form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa, ni abuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛto tomato shishi.

english: This is usually Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies and spread through infected planting stems. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and selecting healthy stems for your next planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji ŋmei mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ni halamɔ tsei ni wa kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes in the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize leaves. Inspecting your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem tree extract directly into the center leaf whorls helps stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air, along with removing infected pods immediately, helps keep the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants shrinking and twisting tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying your pepper plants early with soapy water or diluted neem leaf oil removes these pests and lets new, healthy leaves grow.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem baa mli fɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ baashwie pepper tsei anɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ni eha baa heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food needed for leaf growth. Applying fertilizers like NPK or mixing well-rotted animal manure into the soil gives the plant the energy it needs to grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, reduces the need for expensive chemical fertilizers, and gives you two different harvests from one piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. ni amɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the soil dries out or when the afternoon sun gets too hot. Keeping the soil moist through regular morning watering and covering the soil around the plant with dry grass helps flowers stay attached and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso shwane mli tsɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha nɔ daa leebi kɛ sũ ni okɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi adu koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and drop in the afternoon but wake up again the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi ni ooote shi ekoŋŋ enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water into the air faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Adding dry grass or wood shavings around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the ground for longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ jwɛi loo tso ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when their fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ eyibii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and struggle to hold up heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy fork-shaped bamboo or wooden pole prevents the tree from snapping before the fruits mature.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni tamɔ fɔk loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ dani tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Underground rot happens when rainwater collects in heavy soil and cannot drain away, suffocating the roots. Planting yams on tall mounds or raised ridges with good drainage keeps water flowing away from the tubers so they stay firm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: My old cocoa farm is not producing pods like before, so how do I start over and restore the land?
ga: Mi-cocoa ŋmɔ momo lɛ wooo pods tamɔ tsutsu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te abaafee tɛŋŋ aje shishi ekoŋŋ ni aku sɛɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Rehabilitating an old cocoa farm involves cutting down unproductive or diseased trees, clearing the land, and planting fresh, disease-resistant seedlings alongside fast-growing shade crops to rebuild a healthy farm.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kookoo ŋmɔji momoi ni aku sɛɛ asaa lɛ he ji tsei ni wooo yibii loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ afolɔmɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni odu dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ ahe koni otswa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa tree when it is growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi amli be mli ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents dampness that causes diseases and encourages the tree to spend its energy growing big cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ naa, ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu kookoo ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Should I leave fallen dry leaves on the ground around my crops or sweep them away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni egbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ? Miŋmɔshi nibii loo shwiemɔ kɛtee?

english: You should leave healthy dry leaves on the ground because they form a carpet that keeps the soil cool, traps moisture during dry weather, and decays into natural plant food.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛfeɔ kapɛti ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in wet, dark, and humid weather. Clearing weeds, removing rotten pods promptly, and letting sunlight into the farm help stop the fungus from destroying your crop.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni egbo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni kɛ́ oha hulu la kpɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What should I do if the branches of my cocoa tree start swelling and the leaves turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ kookoo niji lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Swelling branches are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is carried by tiny insects called mealybugs. The infected tree must be cut down completely so the disease does not spread to healthy trees.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ lɛ mealybug tsɔne. Esa akɛ afolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What causes tiny dark spots and sap leaking on my young cocoa stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? And milk leaked on my young cocoa stem.

english: This damage is caused by small insects called capsids or mirids that suck the juice from young stems and pods. Applying recommended crop sprays at the right time protects your farm from them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ enɛɛmɛi ahe.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is too weak to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your plant leaves look pale or yellow instead of deep green, or if trees produce very few pods despite good weather, your soil is running low on essential plant nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. Aloo, kɛji akɛ otso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kpakpa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otso lɛ miiho oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Trees naturally drop extra flowers, but losing too many happens when the tree lacks water or nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔii krɛdɛɛi. Shi nɔ ni laajeɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ ebɔle he. Fɔfɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their skin changes color completely from green to yellow, or from red to orange-yellow, showing that the beans inside are mature.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhewolo lɛ tsakeɔ kwraa kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ nɔ lɛ. loo kɛjɛ etsuru mli kɛtee yellow-orange Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the crops I actually planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to the local soil and weather conditions, so they sprout aggressively. They quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ mra.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli?

english: These are pests like the Fall Armyworm. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they feed on the tender growing center of the corn plant, which stunts its growth if left untreated.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida blɛoo lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Will planting my cassava stems very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he kroko lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba?

english: No, planting cassava stems too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives the root tubers enough room underground to grow large and thick.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect the plant from losing moisture in hot weather. When the soil becomes too dry, the plant drops its leaves as a survival mechanism to keep its main stem alive.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers, but the flowers fall off before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei yɛ fɔfɔi shi amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when soil moisture is irregular. Without consistent watering and proper pollination by insects, the plant drops its blossoms instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii haaa lɛ nu daa ni ekɛ pollination haaa lɛ, Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I bury my maize seeds very deep in the ground when I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: If buried too deep, maize seeds run out of stored energy before the seedling can push through the soil into the sunlight. Planting them at a shallow, correct depth helps them sprout fast and strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ŋmãa dumɔwu lɛ eto lɛ baa shi dani dumɔwu lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does planting beans alongside my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Maize feeds on this natural soil food, helping it grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi yeɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni edaa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do seeds developed by agricultural researchers perform better than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Researcher-developed seeds are specifically bred to fight off local diseases, withstand dry spells, and produce bigger yields. Over time, saved seeds can lose these strong traits, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni niiamlitaolɔi lɛ fee lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛwu ashi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ shiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo Beni be hoɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite sui nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo.

english: Is it better to protect my crops before pests show up, or should I wait until I see insects eating the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai aba? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi mana kooloi ni yeɔ baai?

english: Preventing pests and diseases early through proper field hygiene, crop rotation, and preventive spraying is much easier and cheaper than trying to cure a full outbreak after your crop yield has already suffered damage.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ mra kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni sa nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ Kɛ tsofa ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ he nitsumɔ waaa ni ejara waaa fe bɔ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni otsa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni efite momo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Keeping the field clear of weeds and spraying early with natural remedies like neem oil prevents these insects from settling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛji akɛ jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akakpɛtɛ ohe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant moves the limited nitrogen it has to the new top growth, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛyaa ŋmeii heei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and dry up during their first dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and cannot survive full, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young trees from sun damage and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow weak stems and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do some vegetable farmers cover the bare soil around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni kwɛɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from evaporating soil water, keeps root temperature cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting enough light to sprout.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa hulu la lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rain water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot temperatures, dry soil, or uneven watering, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi, tamɔ latsaa ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even after I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you apply.
