ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: How long does cassava usually take in the ground before it is mature enough to harvest and sell?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei fɔɔ ye yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani edaa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Cassava typically takes between 9 to 14 months to fully mature depending on the variety. Harvesting too early results in small roots with low starch, while leaving it too long can make the tubers woody and unmarketable.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 14 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni starch faaa yɛ mli lɛ baa. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take almost a year before they produce a full bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani midumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantains grow in stages, spending their first 6 to 9 months building strong roots and leaf structures before they can support a heavy stalk of fruit, which then takes another 3 to 4 months to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli, ni amɛkɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 lɛ maa shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani edara kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does leaving dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: This practice, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the earth. It keeps moisture in the soil from evaporating under the hot sun, prevents weeds from growing, and adds nutrients as it decomposes.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during damp, rainy periods. Clearing heavy shade, pruning dense foliage, and harvesting mature pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Shade ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ Baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akpaa oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat hole patterns into my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms. They hide inside the center of young maize plants and feed on foliage, which can weaken or kill the plant if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ loo egbo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why is it better to buy fresh certified seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du wuhi nɛ o to ngɛ jeha nɛ be ɔ ngmami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist diseases, tolerate dry weather, and yield larger crops consistently, whereas saved seeds from hybrids lose their vigor and produce smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops regularly while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be fɛɛ be beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from young crops, which causes crop growth to slow down or stunt early on.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mra.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be dug up from the mounds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli?

english: Yams are generally mature when the vines and leaves start turning yellow and drying up at the end of the rainy season, signaling that energy has transferred completely into the underground tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Okadi akɛ hewalɛ etsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kwraa.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot quickly at the bottom before they even ripen on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifite oya yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when plants don't get enough calcium or experience uneven watering while fruit is forming, causing the base of the tomato to breakdown.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo amɛnáaa nu yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifɔ lɛ. Ha tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Where can I get reliable cocoa seedlings to replant my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana kookoo dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can get improved and disease-resistant cocoa seedlings from official seed production divisions or government agricultural research stations in your district, which ensure higher survival rates than uncertified sources.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kookoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa wala yibiiwoo ni fa fe jɛɛhei ni bɛ odaseyeli lɛ he nɔmimaa.

english: You should speak with an extension officer to select certified hybrid varieties that are suitable for your area's rainfall, mature early, and can resist major local diseases like Swollen Shoot.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-extension agent lɛ awie koni ohala hybrids ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni sa kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ni edaa oya ni baanyɛ ateshi helai ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ tamɔ crown swolling lɛ.

english: Why did my entire cocoa farm dry up and die during the last dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩ ni egbo yɛ naagbee hɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees lack deep roots and will dry out under severe sun if they do not have adequate shade trees or enough soil moisture to protect them through long dry periods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: What steps should I take if a disease destroys most of the trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji hela kpata tsei ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo ahiɛ?

english: You need to cut down and remove all affected trees to stop the spread, clear the land properly, and replant using disease-resistant hybrid seedlings under proper shade.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ojie amɛ koni okpa gbɛfaŋnɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa shishi.

english: Why is cocoa farming so stressful and difficult in the first few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ haa mɔ haoɔ ni ewaa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees require intensive care, including providing shade, controlling weeds, removing pests, and protecting seedlings from extreme heat before they are strong enough to produce pods.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni fata he ji hulutsoo ni akɛhaa. jwɛi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Is it better for me to plant cocoa seeds directly into the soil or use nursery seedlings?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu kookoo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛ ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Using nursery seedlings is much better because the young plants already have strong, developed roots, giving them a higher chance of survival in the field compared to raw seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ dumɔwui baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni edara momo. Enɛ haa hegbɛ babaoo ni akɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my newly planted cocoa seedlings struggling to grow on my old farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Old farmlands often lose important soil nutrients and organic matter over time, so the soil needs to be restored with proper land preparation and plant nutrition before planting new cocoa.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni etsɛ lɛ laajeɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani adu kookoo hee.

english: How can I prevent my cocoa plants from rotting and dying during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can prevent pod rot and plant decay by pruning extra branches to let light and air pass through, managing shade levels, and spraying approved fungicides during rainy periods.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi pod rot kɛ tso lɛ fitemɔ naa kɛtsɔ niji krokomɛi ni ooofolɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni shade lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do some cocoa farms nearby produce plenty of pods while mine struggles to yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ miifee pods babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi-mine lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ lolo ni ekɛwo lɛ?

english: High-yielding farms usually use certified hybrid seedlings, maintain regular weed and pest control, prune dead wood, and ensure proper shade management throughout the year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli tsuɔ nii. Kwɛmɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ daa. ŋmɔ tsei ni egboi ni okwɛ koni akwɛ hulutsoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ cacao tso hee ko masɛi?

english: Yes, planting temporary shade crops like plantain gives your young cocoa protection from the hot sun while providing you with food and income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. Once the rains return, the stem will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up like small tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll inward during intense afternoon heat to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, which stops moisture from escaping too fast and protects the crop from heat stress.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya tsɔ lɛ naa. ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my yam plants need climbing stakes to produce big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ ŋtayaai anɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose as many leaves as possible to sunlight. The sunlight helps the leaves manufacture energy, which flows down to build thick, healthy tubers in the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ feɔ bulbs ni mli wa ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my sweet potato crop producing so many healthy leaves but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miiwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh manure, the sweet potato plant spends all its energy growing lush green leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to grow big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni sweet potato tso lɛ baatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛba shi koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves fold up tightly together when night falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut leaves close up naturally at night to trap moisture, reduce water loss in the cool night air, and protect delicate young leaves from dew and cold temperatures.
ga: Peanut baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe gbɛkɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ha nu ni fiteɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ebuɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily once the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like timber trees; they rely on shallow root networks. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top becomes unbalanced, so propping the plant up with sturdy wooden poles is necessary to support it.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishifã ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Aduawai lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ ji asymmetrical. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ni akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ he miihia kɛha sɛɛfimɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when there is sudden water stress. Severe heat prevents the flower from pollinating, so the plant sheds the flower to preserve its strength.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli.

english: Why are my green oranges falling off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tangerine lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Citrus trees shed small, undeveloped fruits when they suffer from irregular watering, poor soil nutrients, or when fruit flies lay eggs inside the young fruits, causing them to rot internally and fall.
ga: Orange tsei jieɔ aduawai bibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdarako moŋ, shi amɛnaa piŋmɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ aduawai bibii amli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa amɛmli fiteɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded farms during the rainy season when air cannot flow freely between the trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants crumpling up and twisting as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Wrinkled or distorted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaf surfaces, which damages the growing leaf tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo etsake lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni miida lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger trees or planting shade crops like plantains creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa trees from burning and helps the soil retain moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni eda lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa trees, or will it harm them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii adu ŋmei? Aloo ebaaye kookoo tso lɛ awui?

english: Cassava roots feed heavily on soil nutrients and grow aggressively, which can starve young cocoa trees. It is better to intercrop with plantains or bananas because they provide shade without competing heavily for the same root space.
ga: Cassava shishifãi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ plantains loo banana adu amɛ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli he ko babaoo he.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield a heavy harvest one year, but very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ?

english: Cocoa trees use up massive amounts of energy and soil nutrients to produce a large harvest. If the soil is not replenished with fertilizer or organic matter, the trees become exhausted and take time to recover before producing heavily again.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ehe baahia ni ekɛ be atsu nii dani enyɛ ewo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why must I harvest my cocoa pods immediately after they turn fully yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the beans inside to germinate or rot. Overripe pods also attract pests and diseases that can destroy the quality of the harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I leave my farm unattended for a few months after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ he?

english: Unattended farms become overgrown with weeds that steal water and nutrients. Disease spores like black pod spread rapidly without control, and pests multiply, which weakens the trees and severely reduces future yields.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsuuu he nii lɛ mli jwɛi ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi eyi ŋmɔji amli. Helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ. ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ tee hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni ebaaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, consume water and food that the main tree needs. Removing them ensures all energy goes into developing healthy stems and cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and humid weather. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi krɛdɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their tiny flowers without making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, afeee pod?

english: Flowers drop when the tree faces extreme dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or lacks beneficial insects for pollination. The tree sheds its flowers to save energy to stay alive during harsh conditions.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ yashɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ amli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha pollination ni bɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa trees curling up and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling brown leaves are often a sign of heat stress combined with sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids). These insects attack young shoots and block water flow within the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji hulutsoo he haomɔ he okadi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids). Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ tutuaa ŋmeii bibii ni amɛfiteɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm's soil is too tired to feed my crops properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops show pale or yellowing leaves, slow stem growth, and thin fruits despite getting enough rain, the soil has run out of essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ daa fiofio. Ni aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy new improved seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are carefully bred by researchers to resist local pests, tolerate dry weather, and produce much higher yields compared to traditional seeds that lose strength over time.
ga: Niiamlitaolɔi baadu dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: How can I be sure that a new crop variety being sold to me is safe and officially approved for farming in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ aha mi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Officially approved varieties must go through field trials and get inspected and certified by the country's Variety Release Committee before they are legally released to farmers.
ga: Esa akɛ aka tsofai srɔtoi ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli. ni maŋ lɛ mli Tsei Srɔtoi Ajiemɔ Ajinafoi Akuu lɛ kwɛɔ mli ni amɛhaa amɛhe odaseyeli dani amɛjieɔ amɛhaa okwaafoi yɛ mla naa.

english: Why do some cassava plants stay healthy while others in the same field get ruined by cassava mosaic disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi yɛ hewalɛ waa nɛkɛ? be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni cassava mosaic hela kpata amɛhiɛ lɛ?

english: Different varieties have different natural defenses; plant breeders specifically develop disease-resistant varieties so the crop can fight off infections while growing.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu sɔrɔtoi. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ awuu ashi helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do certain maize plants stay green during a dry spell while my traditional maize leaves turn brown and wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mishishijee ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ blɔfo ni amɛgboi.

english: Drought-tolerant varieties are bred to grow deeper roots and conserve water, allowing them to survive and keep growing even when the rain stops for a few weeks.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛshwereɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo po.

english: If I plant an improved crop variety this season, can I save seeds from the harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It depends on the seed type; if it is a hybrid variety, saving the seeds will result in weak plants and low yields next season, so you need fresh certified seeds each time.
ga: Edamɔ dumɔwu henɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛji eji dumɔwu ni akɛfee ekome lɛ Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni oná dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do some new yam varieties mature in five months while my regular yam takes up to eight months to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato henɔi heei komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ heɔ nyɔji kpaanyɔ dani akpaa.

english: Breeders develop early-maturing varieties to help farmers harvest early in the season, enabling them to sell when market prices are high and avoid late-season droughts.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ fee kooloi srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛkpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mra. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara lɛ nɔ wa lɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ he.

english: Will consumers in my local market accept the taste and cooking quality of these new crop varieties?
ga: Ani mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ baakpɛlɛ bɔ ni nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei nɛɛ ŋɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni ahoɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ nɔ?

english: Before any new variety is released to farmers, expert committees test it for taste, boiling quality, and storage life to ensure local consumers will want to buy and eat it.
ga: dani ajie tsofai heei kpo atsɔɔ okwaafoi lɛ Nileelɔi akuu ko baaka tsofai lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ, bɔ ni afeeɔ dãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni ehiɔ shi ehaa lɛ amɛkwɛ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baasumɔ ni amɛhe ni amɛye.

english: Will a new high-yielding crop variety grow well on my land if I do not add fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli?

english: New varieties are stronger, but because they produce more fruit or tubers, they need adequate soil nutrients; feeding the soil helps the plant reach its full yield potential.
ga: Srɔtoi hee lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Shi akɛni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii babaoo hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛ yibiiwoo ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do agricultural researchers make these new plant varieties in the laboratory?
ga: Te okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfeɔ tsei srɔtoi heei nɛɛ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli?

english: Researchers create new varieties by crossing two strong parent plants—such as combining one with sweet tubers and another that resists diseases—and selecting the best offspring over several years.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi feɔ tsei srɔtoi heei kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni wa ni amɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛtsɔ eko ni bulbs ni ŋɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛ ekroko ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ohala seshi ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to follow specific row spacing when planting a new maize seed instead of broadcasting it as usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã tamɔ bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Improved varieties need accurate spacing so each individual plant gets enough sunlight, ground moisture, and air, preventing overcrowding so every stalk produces a big cob.
ga: Esa akɛ ato tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ ji koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso yɛ ŋmei agbo.

english: If I clear an old piece of land that hasn't been farmed since my childhood, is the soil automatically rich enough for planting?
ga: Kɛji mijie shikpɔŋ momo ni mitsuuu nii yɛ nɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shikpɔŋ ni baa shi kɛha dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Land left untouched for many years usually gathers rich organic matter, but the soil underneath can also be compact, overly acidic, or hiding root pests. It is best to clear carefully and test or mix the topsoil before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ashi efolo afii babaoo lɛ ji he ko ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ acid tsɔ. loo okɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui awo shishifãi lɛ amli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oka loo okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu.

english: Why do crops grow tall and green in one spot on my farm, but stay small and yellow just a few meters away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ekɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai fioo komɛi pɛ.

english: Soil content varies across the same land because of hidden differences underground, such as gravel pockets, poor water drainage, or low nitrogen levels. Adding compost or manure to the weak spots helps balance crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ falɛ srɔtoi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ naa. Yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ tɛi ni hoɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. loo nitrogen ni faaa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ adalɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to burn the bushes I clear from my land or leave them to rot on the farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo maha amɛgbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys rich organic nutrients and beneficial soil organisms. Leaving cleared brush to rot naturally as mulch keeps the soil cool, retains moisture, and feeds your crops over time.
ga: Shãa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse oya. Shi efiteɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ha brɔshi ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Wait until the major rainy season establishes with two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil deep down, rather than planting after the very first light shower which can leave seeds to dry up and die.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ aje shishi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa. Moŋ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔnɛmɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What happens to my farm if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and causes crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to smaller harvests each season.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ fioo pɛ baaba yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant cassava or beans together with my maize instead of planting only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa moŋ fe ŋmãa pɛ?

english: Mixing crops protects your farm because legumes like beans trap nitrogen in the soil to feed the maize, while growing different crops ensures you still harvest food even if one crop suffers from pests or weather.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni oduɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii lolo lɛ, Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yeɔ amanehulu po.

english: Can I plant new crops on the exact spot where I just cut down old, dying cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tso hee yɛ he ni mifo cacao tso momo ko ni miigbo lɛ?

english: You can, but you must first clear out or burn the old stumps and roots, because decaying old tree roots underground can harbour fungal diseases like root rot that will attack your fresh seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ehe miihia ni ojie loo oshã tsei akutsei kɛ shishifãi momoi, ejaakɛ tsei shishifãi momo ni miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ ŋmeii tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni baatutua odumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: Why do my young crop leaves wilt and burn even when there is water in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Young plants have delicate root systems that cannot absorb water fast enough to match hot, direct sunlight; providing temporary shade with palm fronds or nurse crops like plantain keeps them cool while roots grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains ha hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why are insects attacking the roots of my yams underground when the vines on top look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi sweet potato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi nɛɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Soil pests like yam beetles and nematodes live hidden underground in the earth and feed directly on tubers; treating the seed yams or soil before planting prevents this hidden damage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ sweet potato ŋmeii kɛ nematodes hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ atsa sweet potato dumɔwui loo shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ naa.

english: How can I keep my crops from drying up when the dry season starts earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, reduces evaporation, and keeps crop roots cool during dry spells.
ga: Mulching around Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ehà otso lɛ shishi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. They require temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter them until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛhi amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are the leaves on my green pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso eŋɔli lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the plant juice and spreading viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot, when watering is irregular, or when there is poor pollination due to a lack of gentle breeze or insects.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni pollination lɛ ehiii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when heavy rains last for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain in heavy soil fills up all air spaces, effectively suffocating the cassava roots and allowing waterborne fungi to invade and rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku fɛɛ kotoku nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the top weight easily pulls the shallow roots out of soft, wet soil unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu agbo ko dara lɛ, Muji ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya. ja tso nibii fiɔ sɛɛ

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads rapidly in high humidity, heavy rain, and shade where air cannot circulate freely around the trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he lɛ. tsei lɛ yɛ heyeli mli

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn before the next planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break their resting phase (dormancy) when room temperatures and air humidity rise, signaling to the tuber that it is time to grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ (dormancy) yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji tsu lɛ mli latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tee hiɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tsei heei.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with little caterpillar droppings inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli buji ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the tender central whorl of the maize plant before the cob develops.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into a liquid form that roots can absorb. Putting fertilizer on dry soil keeps it trapped on top and can burn plant roots when rain finally comes.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ nu ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpɛtɛ ŋwɛigbɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ́ naagbee lɛ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I saved from my last harvest will actually sprout before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu amɛ?

english: You can test your seed viability using a simple water test or moist cloth test. Put a handful of seeds in a bowl of water; healthy seeds that will grow usually sink to the bottom, while hollow or damaged seeds float to the top and should not be planted.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu mli kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo aka bɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi amɛha lɛ okwɛ. loo kaa kɛ mama ni mli efɔ Okɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ kɛ nine awo nu tsɛnsi mli. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛyaa shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji loo ni efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ.

english: Why do some improved hybrid seeds perform better than the traditional seeds I get from my local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred in laboratories to resist local diseases, handle heat better, and produce higher yields. However, they require careful watering and soil management to reach their full potential, unlike traditional seeds which are hardier but produce smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ yɛ laboratorii amli koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ dɔlɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo, ni amɛbiɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ blema dumɔwui ni wa shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I rush to plant immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ? Klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Rushing to plant after the first light rain is risky because the soil might not have enough deep moisture to keep seedlings alive if a dry spell follows. It is safer to wait until the rains are steady so your seeds don't dry up and die under the hot sun.
ga: Asusuɔ oyaiyeli ni akɛyaaduɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ he akɛ eji oshara Enɛ ji akɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do crops that grow easily in the wet forest areas struggle to survive when planted in the Savannah regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔji yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops in the Savannah face hotter temperatures, lower humidity, and longer dry periods than in forest zones. Crops planted in the Savannah need to be drought-resistant varieties with deep root systems to survive the harsh sun and limited rainfall.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ Savannah lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kpeɔ. hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe koo lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ Savannah lɛ anyɛ akpee hɔmɔ naa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself from extreme heat and drought. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto water inside its stem.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ahi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil, or that water is logged around their roots. Applying organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very tiny fruits when I put too many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo nɛkɛ lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition forces them to grow tall and weak trying to reach the sun, leaving them with no energy to produce big fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛfee mɛi ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haaa amɛnáaa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every year drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crop with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the dirt naturally, keeping the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if my plants are already bigger than the weeds?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ dara fe jwɛi lɛ momo?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizers from deep in the soil before your crop's roots can reach them. Keeping the field clear ensures all the nutrients go directly into feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fɛɛ aya niyenii ni okɛbaahã onibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get insects so quickly after I put them in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ŋmeii shwieɔ nɔ beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil in storage if they are not dried completely before being stored, as leftover moisture attracts mold and weevils. Drying your grains under the sun until they are hard and crack when bitten will protect them from insects and rotting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ baagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbala kɛji akɛ amɛye lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning under the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves overheat easily and lose water too quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains around them provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ amli dɔɔ fe nine ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop fail to form big cobs if it does not rain when the flowers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ efeee ŋmeii wuji kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Maize needs the most water during its flowering phase to transfer pollen and fill out the grains. If dry conditions occur at this critical time, the cobs will remain small or develop empty spots without corn kernels.
ga: Nu he hiaa ŋmãa fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli ni ekɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi ba yɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baakã he afee bibioo loo ebaana hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmei ŋmei ko bɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave the soil flooded or waterlogged for extended periods, the roots suffocate and succumb to fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu loo nu shwie shi be kakadaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots coming out from the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: When a plantain tree produces too many young shoots, all of them compete for the same food and water in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni dumɔwu lɛ ná ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niji ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better and give bigger tubers when I support the vines with stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei fiɔ wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the wet ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber, while also improving airflow around the plant to prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni eha amɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ ehe lɛ yaa hiɛ. tsei koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm make my crops perform better than planting on bare land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Repeated harvesting drains essential plant food from the ground. Animal manure restores vital nutrients like nitrogen and improves the soil's ability to hold moisture for crop roots.
ga: ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ Ejieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koolooi ashishifãi haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or beans helps make the soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same patch of ground for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil strips away specific nutrients it needs to thrive and creates an environment where maize pests and diseases build up in the soil.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ ekwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ edɛŋ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot periods as a defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss, though it can also be a sign of insect pests like whiteflies transferring leaf viruses.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ aba shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ baanyɛ afee tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ hu he okadi moŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they face extreme heat, lack sufficient soil moisture, or suffer from insect damage before pollination can occur.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ lɛ dani pollination baa

english: Can I use chicken manure to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, chicken manure is rich in nutrients like nitrogen that feed your crops. However, it is very strong, so you should let it dry out or mix it with dry plant waste to compost it first so it does not burn your plants' roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmɔtɔ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ fa babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe wa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oha egbi loo okɛ tsei ni egbi ni etse lɛ afutu mli koni efee ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekashã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or dried manure, and ensuring excess water can drain away, helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fataa he. ni okwɛ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving green powder inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda eŋɔli yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center leaves (funnel) of the plant to feed, so applying recommended treatment directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening will help protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when water gets trapped around the roots in heavy or poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Keeping a consistent watering schedule and mulching the base of the plant helps keep soil temperatures steady.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni atoɔ daa kɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops make the harvest bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your plants full access to these resources so they can grow faster and produce more yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛná nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ. Koni tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo

english: How do I know if the soil is moist enough to plant seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dig down about a hand's length into the soil; if you can squeeze a handful into a ball that stays together without dripping water, the soil is moist enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ aaafee tso kome kɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji obaanyɛ okɛ nine kome awo bɔɔlu ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with crops like cowpea or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Abɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my vegetable plants look small and weak when the soil becomes hard and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Hard, packed soil stops plant roots from expanding and breathing, making it hard for them to absorb water and plant food. Loosening the topsoil around the plants helps roots spread and grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkamu. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu ni amɛdu niyenii. ŋwɛi sũ ni bɔle Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Is it harmful to my crops if plastic bottles and general rubbish are left buried in my farm soil?
ga: Ani ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji akɛ afu plastic tsɛnsii kɛ jwɛi ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plastic waste does not decay like dead leaves. When plastic bottles are buried in the farm, they create barriers that block crop roots from spreading to find water and nutrients, and they can trap unwanted stagnant water around root zones.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, plastic jwɛi lɛ fiteee tamɔ baai ni egboi lɛ. Beni afuɔ plastic tsɛnsii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Plastic tsɛnsii feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. ni ebaanyɛ emɔ nu ni damɔ shi ni ataooo lɛ he kɛbɔle shishifã lɛ he.

english: Should I clear away every single tree and bush when preparing my farmland for planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛji misaa miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛha dumɔ?

english: No, clearing absolute everything leaves your soil completely bare and unprotected. Leaving some beneficial trees provides shade, protects the topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains, and keeps the land cool.
ga: Dabi, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ooojie lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuuu he. Kɛ́ oshi tsei komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ agbele lɛ, ebaaha oná hulutsoo. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ

english: Why does plastic rubbish gathered along the farm edge cause water logging around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plastic jwɛi buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ? Ni ehaa nu shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Plastic bottles and trash block natural drainage paths where rain is supposed to flow away. When water gets trapped by trash, it spills over into your farm and creates standing water that can cause crop roots to rot.
ga: Plastic tsinsii kɛ jwɛi tsiɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ he ni esa akɛ nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ nɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ jwɛi he lɛ Nu baaho kɛbote oŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ehaa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ baa.

english: Why is the government encouraging us farmers to plant trees on our farms through the Green Ghana initiative?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ miiwo okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu tsei yɛ wɔŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔ Green Ghana nifeemɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The initiative aims to restore lost forests and soil fertility. Trees planted on farms help bring rainfall, shade tender crops, prevent soil erosion, and build a healthier environment for long-term farming.
ga: Oti ni ato he gbɛjianɔ nɛɛ ji ni aku sɛɛ aha kooi ni elaaje kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ. Tsei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ akanɛɛ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hulutsoo Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ofee shihilɛ ni hi kɛha okwaayeli ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Will planting trees alongside my food crops steal all the food and water from my crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni miduɔ yɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Not if you select the right trees and space them properly. Deep-rooted shade trees draw water and nutrients from deep underground where crop roots cannot reach, and their fallen leaves rot to provide free organic fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Jeee nakai kɛji ohala tsei ni sa ni okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shade tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni tsei lɛ ahe baai ni egbee shi lɛ baagboi koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: When is the best time for me to plant new tree saplings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant tree saplings right at the beginning of the main rainy season. This allows the young trees to establish strong root systems in moist soil before the hot dry season arrives.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wither very fast after I remove all shade trees from around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Without shade trees to block direct sunlight, the soil heats up rapidly and soil moisture evaporates into the air quickly, leaving young crops stressed and dehydrated.
ga: Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ oya ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ haoɔ ni nu hu faaa amɛmli.

english: Why do my crops planted right by the dusty roadside seem to struggle more than crops in the middle of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ gbɛ ni sũ eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ he lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Roadside crops get covered in dust, which blocks sunlight from reaching their leaves and prevents them from making food efficiently. They also suffer from higher heat exposure along cleared roadside corridors.
ga: Muji ehà tsei ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Amɛná dɔlɛ ni mli wa hu yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do shade trees help my farm survive during the hot dry season?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees act as natural windbreaks to stop dry winds from drying out your plants, and their overhead canopy keeps the ground temperature lower so the soil retains water much longer.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha otsei lɛ agbi. ni tsũ lɛ yiteŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops planted under light tree shade behave differently than crops planted in wide open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Crops in open sunshine get full light to grow fast if they have enough water, while crops under light shade stay cooler and conserve moisture better, making shade ideal for delicate or young plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ baaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛji amɛyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo tsei bibii.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during prolonged dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normal tubers.
ga: Cassava baagbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ bulbs ni sa.

english: Very high temperatures can cause tomato pollen to become sticky or sterile, preventing pollination. Without pollination, the flowers cannot form fruit and drop off. Providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps lower plant stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa baanyɛ aha tomato pollen lɛ afee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi loo nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. Bɔni afee ni akafee pollination Kɛji pollination bɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tsei lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ anɔ haomɔ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks nutrients before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If previous crops on the same land showed pale yellow leaves, thin stems, or very small yields, the soil is likely low in key nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost before planting helps restore soil richness.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni tsɔ hiɛ ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-corn lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside or in rotation with maize, they naturally feed the soil with fertilizer that maize needs to grow strong.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu kɛfata ŋmãa he loo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ Amɛkɛ ŋmãa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by viruses they carry. Controlling these insects early with neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ amli Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ Neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaves rolled up with caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: This is typical damage from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the central funnel of the maize plant and eats the leaves. Applying targeted biological or chemical treatments directly into the funnel early stops them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni eyeɔ baai lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra kɛyaa gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite he ni shweremɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need support to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then sent down to build large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ bɔni afee ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ he lɛ aná babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee yam ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young maize plants early rather than waiting until they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mibi lɛ ŋmãa duɔ mra. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ agbɔ lɛ,.

english: Young maize plants grow slowly at first and easily get overpowered by weeds. Early weeding removes competition for soil moisture, fertilizer, and sunlight so the crop gets off to a healthy start.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli, ni jwɛi yeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la he lɛ kɛyaa koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Hybrid maize seeds are specially bred for high yields in the first generation. If you plant the seeds harvested from that crop, the second generation loses those high-yielding traits, leading to uneven growth and small ears.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafite esu ni haa yibiiwoo babaoo lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ toi bibii baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem due to swelling tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ shishi yɛ yitso ni efuu lɛ hewɔ.

english: How should I prepare my plantain suckers one by one before putting them in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa plantain tsei lɛ aŋkroaŋkroi dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: To prepare plantain suckers, carefully trim off the old roots and clean any damaged tissue from the base of each sucker individually. This removes pests and diseases, giving the young plant a fresh, healthy start to establish strong new roots.
ga: Yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ahe saamɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɛ shishifãi momo lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni otsumɔ fãji ni efite kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli srɔtoi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie kooloi bibii kɛ helai kɛya. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa hewalɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi heei ni mli wa.

english: Can I plant plantains alongside my young tree seedlings to protect them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni mabu amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting plantains next to young tree seedlings is an effective farming strategy. Plantains grow quickly and produce large, broad leaves that provide vital shade and retain soil moisture, protecting fragile tree seedlings from harsh sunlight.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi. Dumɔwui ji okwaayeli gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Buu tso dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why does my pawpaw plant grow so tall and thin when other crops are nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo be mli ni tsei krokomɛi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants are very sensitive to competition for light. When other crops grow close to a pawpaw, the pawpaw rapidly stretches upward to match or exceed the height of neighboring plants so it can reach direct sunlight.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ nuɔ akaŋshii he waa kɛha la. Kɛ tsei krokomɛi dara yɛ tsitsii lɛ ahe lɛ, tsitsii lɛ shwereɔ oya koni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ he loo eteke nɔ koni eha hulu la lɛ ashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it bad to plant other crops very close to my pawpaw tree?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu tsei krokomɛi yɛ mi-pawpaw tso lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, planting crops too close to a pawpaw can stress it. Pawpaws do not tolerate heavy root or light competition well, so keeping adequate clear space around the base of the pawpaw tree ensures it stays healthy and stable.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsitsi lɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ aná haomɔ. Pawpaw ekpɛlɛɛɛ shishifãi ni tsii loo akaŋshii ni waaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, he ni bɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ ni oooha Okɛ shishitoo ni sa aha o-pawpaw tso lɛ baaha tso lɛ mli awa ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my pawpaw plant is struggling because of neighboring crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mipapaya tso lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahewɔ?

english: If a pawpaw is struggling due to nearby crop competition, it will grow unusually tall and slender with a weak base, or show sparse leaf growth as it spends all its energy stretching upward for sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ naji lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ lɛ Edaraa ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ kɛ shishitoo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Aloo jiemɔ baai ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ adalɛ kpo beni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa ehe koni emɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: How do my crops behave when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Taller or more aggressive crops will shade out smaller ones, causing plants to stretch, grow weak stems, or yield less fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ loo ni yɔɔ basabasa fe tsutsu lɛ baaha amɛfee bibii. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baatsɛ, eshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, loo ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: How do I know the correct distance to leave between different types of crops on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni ka ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Correct spacing depends on how tall and wide each crop grows at maturity. Fast-growing or shade-sensitive crops need enough room so their leaves and roots do not overcrowd neighboring plants.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ damɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ elɛɛmɔ nɔ beni edara lɛ. Tsei ni daa oya loo ni nuɔ hulutsoo he lɛ he miihia he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ akayi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli fe nine.

english: Why do some of my crops try to grow taller than the plants next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally detect shade from surrounding vegetation. When a plant senses neighboring crops blocking its light, it redirects its energy into growing height so its leaves can reach full sunlight.
ga: Tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ miitsi la naa lɛ Etsɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ebaa lɛ aná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant temporary crops and long-term trees in the same field at the same time?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo kɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe abɔ?

english: Yes, combining fast-growing temporary crops like plantains with slow-growing permanent trees is a great practice. The temporary crops yield food and income early on while providing shade to help the permanent trees grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains kɛ tsei ni daa blɛoo ni akɛaafata he lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa koni eye ebua tsei ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I choose plantain to plant alongside my young cash crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala plantains ni mikɛdu yɛ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains are ideal companion plants because they grow fast, provide high, wide leaf canopies for shade, and improve microclimate humidity without permanent root interference for your main cash crops.
ga: Plantains ji tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya. Ha jwɛi lɛ tsei ni mli kwɔ, ni kɛlɛ ni eha hulutsoo. ni oha microclimate humidity lɛ aya hiɛ ni ogbaaa oshika ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ ashishifãi ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ anaa.

english: If I harvest the leaves of my cassava plants to make soup, will it affect the growth of the tubers under the ground?
ga: Kɛ mibua ŋmei baai anaa koni mikɛfee shwiili lɛ, ani ebaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Taking too many leaves can reduce root growth because leaves act like food factories for the plant. If you harvest only a few outer leaves from mature cassava plants, the tubers underground will continue to grow big and strong.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ejaakɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛji okpa kponɔgbɛ baai fioo komɛi pɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baaya nɔ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Are there specific types of cassava I should grow if I want rich, green leaves for cooking?
ga: Ani ŋmei pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miitao baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii?
