english: Yes, certain sweet cassava varieties produce larger, tender leaves that stay green longer and are ideal for cooking, while other varieties focus mainly on root size.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei henɔi komɛi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi lɛ Baasusu shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he titri.

english: Is it safe to eat fresh cassava leaves directly from the farm, or do I need to process them first?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooye ŋmei baai heei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ atsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Raw cassava leaves contain natural compounds that must be broken down before eating. Washing, pounding, and boiling the leaves thoroughly removes these compounds, making the leaves safe and nourishing to eat.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni esa akɛ akumɔ mli dani aye lɛ yɛ cassava baai ni ahoko lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ ahe, atswa amɛ, ni ashã amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Will my cassava plant grow new leaves after I cut some off to make stew?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tso lɛ baaná baai heei beni mifo ekomɛi koni mikɛfee stew sɛɛ?

english: Yes, a healthy cassava plant will naturally sprout fresh leaves from its stem as long as it receives adequate water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛjɛ amɛtso lɛ shishi, kɛji amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my food crops turning yellowish instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant is missing important soil nutrients like nitrogen or needs more water. Dark green leaves show that the plant is healthy and receiving proper food from the soil.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu babaoo he miihia lɛ. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni enáa niyenii ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I make my farm soil richer so my crops give me stronger and more nourishing yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa, ni niyenii yɔɔ mli babaoo?

english: Adding organic matter like animal manure, compost, or decayed leaves feeds the soil, giving your crops the vital nutrients they need to grow strong and healthy food.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egboi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii. Ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni mli wa ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Does the way I care for my crop plants change how nourishing the harvest will be for my family?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ mihaa lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni mikwɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ mihaa miweku lɛ?

english: Yes, crops grown in fertile soil with proper water and care store more natural nutrients and vitamins, resulting in a richer, healthier food harvest for your family.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ ni nu kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baahiɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ vitamini babaoo mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oweku lɛ baakpa niyenii ni jara wa, ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: What should I do if insects are eating and destroying the leaves on my cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji kooloi ye mi-cassava baai lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ?

english: Damaged leaves reduce the plant's ability to feed itself. You can protect the leaves by applying safe organic mixtures, such as mild ash solutions or neem extracts, to keep insects away.
ga: Baai ni efite lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni enyɛ eye ehe niyenii. Obaanyɛ obu baai lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ashwishwɛ ni mli ejɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii koni kooloi akabote mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava plant is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off while the base of the main stem thickens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi beni tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Can I grow leafy green vegetables together in the same farm with my young cassava plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsei ni yɔɔ baai yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, you can plant short-season vegetables between cassava rows during the first few months after planting before the cassava grows tall and shades the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu aduawai ni heɔ be kuku yɛ ŋmeii akutsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ. Dani ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ,.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. It can also happen when the soil stays too waterlogged or when plants don't get enough water during dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too hot, when plants experience water stress, or when there is a lack of proper plant food in the soil. Extreme heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ loo be mli ni tsei aniyenii ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rains keep changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje tsei afeemɔ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi lɛ?

english: Rather than planting after the very first rain, wait until you get two or three steady rains that soak deep into the soil. Seeds planted in soil with deep moisture have a better chance of surviving if there is a short dry spell right after planting.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ amɛaahi shi kɛji amɛná be kuku ni nu egbi. Beni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and get scorched under direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates a cooler environment that protects young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller harvests now compared to when I first cleared the bush years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni mijie ŋmeii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Growing crops on the same soil year after year removes essential plant nutrients without giving the land time to recover. Adding manure, compost, or rotating with crops like beans helps restore life and fertility to tired soil.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wala kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will putting extra chemical fertilizer on my crops make them grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much chemical fertilizer can burn the plant roots and ruin the crop. Plants only absorb what they need, so using the correct small amount at the right stage of growth gives the best result.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛmli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ shika bibioo ni sa lɛ tsu nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside maize helps the soil. These plants naturally capture nitrogen food from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfata ŋmeii ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei nɛɛ mɔɔ nitrogen niyenii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I can dig them up to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ atsa amɛ ni akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when water sits around the roots in heavy soil without draining away, or from fungal diseases spread by insects. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ebɔle he. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli loo helai ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa Shishifãi ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I intentionally planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive harsh conditions and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early while your planted crops are small prevents the weeds from choking out your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ni ooofee bibii lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my stored maize get eaten by small insects even when kept inside bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ? Akɛto kotoku mli?

english: Insects like weevils often lay tiny eggs on maize grains while they are still drying in the field. If the maize is bagged while still slightly damp, those eggs hatch inside the warm bags and the insects multiply quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ be mli ni egbi lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Kɛji akɛ awo ŋmãa lɛ kotoku mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo lolo lɛ, Nakai ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the tips even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make food. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep down into the soil beyond the reach of young roots, so adding compost or fertilizer helps put food back where roots can drink it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm improve my crops better than just watering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni mikɛwoɔ mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the microscopic organisms living underground that break down plant food and release invisible nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. It also helps the soil hold onto rainwater longer so your crops do not dry out quickly.
ga: Koolooi ashwiei haa nibii bibii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei aniyenii ni ejieɔ niyenii ni anaaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni onibii akagbi oya.

english: How do deep roots help my cassava plants survive the long dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Even when the top of the farm looks completely dry and cracked, water remains hidden deep underground. Cassava grows long taproots that push deep into these hidden damp layers to draw up water, keeping the plant green during drought.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ, shi nu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lolo. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋshɔi ni mli ewo nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. ni oha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I bury my maize seeds too deep under the ground when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Seeds need a small amount of trapped air and warmth near the soil surface to sprout. If buried too deep, the young shoot runs out of stored energy before it can reach the surface light, causing it to rot underground.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ni amɔmɔ amɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, oblahii kɛ oblayei bibii lɛ baafite amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani la baanyɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi. ni haa egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and turn yellow when I cannot see any big insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni onaaa kooloi wuji komɛi yɛ?

english: Tiny, almost invisible insects like whiteflies carry microscopic viruses from plant to plant. These invisible germs live inside the plant's sap and block food movement, causing leaves to curl even without large insects chewing on them.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni eshwɛ fioo ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ whiteflies lɛ hiɛɔ helai bibii ni anaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Nɛkɛ helai ni anaaa nɛɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ niyenii lɛ gbɛfaa naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kooloi wuji po shwieee amɛ.

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit while it is growing, which usually happens when watering is irregular. When soil jumps between being very dry and very wet, the roots cannot consistently absorb and push this invisible mineral up to the fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nɛkɛ mineral ni anaaa nɛɛ ni amɛtsi kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on the same land make my next maize crop grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work with friendly bacteria in their root nodules to pull nitrogen gas out of the air and turn it into soil food. When the cowpeas are harvested, this hidden nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpea kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ejie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa tsina ŋmãa Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act as living umbrellas, providing temporary shade and keeping the air around the young cocoa moist until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ cacao tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa ni enáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny, almost invisible insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If the farm ground is too dry or cleared completely of damp leaf litter, these insects cannot survive, leaving flowers unpollinated so they drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Kplukai ni miihe ashɛ ni anaaa amɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges Koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli he lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo eyɛ baai ni mli efɔ fɛɛ lɛ, Kplukai nɛɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds keep sprouting in my farm even after I cleared all the visible plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mijie tsei fɛɛ ni anaa lɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep buried in the soil for months or years without dying. Clearing the land exposes these hidden seeds to sunlight and moisture, which signals them to wake up and grow all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nyɔji loo afii babaoo ni amɛgbooo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ baate shi ni amɛdara shikome.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants often drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden soil dryness. The heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to save water and survival energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi trukaa. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the ground isn't dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko yɛ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than roots can draw water out of the soil. Drooping is the crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf area facing the sun and conserve moisture.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ latsaa be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa baai ni kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi ni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, the individual plants compete aggressively against each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving all of them thin and undernourished.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to dig out extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: Having too many young suckers around one mother plantain tree forces them all to fight for the same soil food and water, which results in smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Ni aaaná tsei bibii babaoo ni bɔle dumɔwu kome he Ni enyɛɔ amɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: How do weeds reduce my farm yield even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water and fertilizer right out of the soil before your crop's roots can absorb them, starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ. ni hɔmɔ aye nyɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas that keep the air cool and preserve moisture for the young seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmeii ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I stake the vines with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛ mikɛ tso tswa wain tso lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture plant food, while keeping the leaves away from wet soil diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ wo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni akɛtsu nii yɛ tsei aniyenii feemɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the soil during periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess rainwater fills all the tiny air pockets in the ground, suffocating the roots and creating moist conditions for rotting fungi to attack.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa koni ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ atutua.

english: Why should I trim off lower branches and side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ amɛsɛɛ tsei lɛ?

english: Trimming away extra shoots and leaves forces the plant to direct its food and water energy straight into swelling and ripening the fruits, rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu hewalɛ ni haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Cocoa pods change color from green or red to bright yellow or orange when they are fully ripe. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the beans inside have fully developed their sugars and rich flavor.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kwraa yɛ amɛ sugars kɛ flavor lɛ mli.

english: Does leaving ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long affect the beans inside?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaana kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, if left on the tree for too long, the seeds inside the pod will begin to germinate and sprout, or the pod will rot, making the beans useless for sale.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Aloo ŋmeii lɛ baagboi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why is it important to use a sharp cutlass when harvesting cocoa pods instead of breaking them off by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ kaklai ni naa wa atsu nii lɛ? Koni akpa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niji baakumɔ amɛ

english: A clean cut with a sharp tool prevents tearing the flower cushion on the tree stem. Damaging this cushion stops new flowers and pods from growing in that same spot in future seasons.
ga: Kɛ akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ oya ŋmɔɔ nibii ni he tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ fɔfɔi akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mligbalamɔ naa. Pincushion nɛɛ ni afee lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ he kome yɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli.

english: Can I harvest both green and yellow cocoa pods at the same time to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa kookoo ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: No, harvesting unripe green pods produces flat, bitter beans with little sugar, which leads to poor fermentation and a lower price from buyers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni sugar fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ jara baa shi.

english: How should I open my cocoa pods so I do not destroy the beans inside?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ agbele kookoo ŋmɔ mli ni akpataaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ?

english: It is best to strike the pod with a blunt wooden club or tap it carefully around the middle with a cutlass without slicing deep, so you break the outer shell without damaging the beans.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ tso ni mli tseee atswa pod lɛ. Aloo okɛ tsɔne atswa teŋgbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafo mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ atse ni efiteee ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour my freshly harvested cocoa beans directly onto the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ kookoo ni akpa ehee lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing beans directly on bare soil exposes them to dirt, fungal spores, and insects, which can introduce dampness and cause mold to ruin your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii wo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná muji. Mold spores kɛ kooloi bibii, ni baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ akpata onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why is it better to dry cocoa beans on raised bamboo mats rather than flat on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ hi fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised platforms allow air to circulate under and around the beans, helping them dry faster and more evenly while keeping them safe from farm animals and ground moisture.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛhe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ekome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛ koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: What happens to cocoa beans if I put them out to dry without fermenting them first?
ga: Mɛni baa cocoa ŋmeii anɔ kɛji migbi amɛ ni mikɛwooo mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Unfermented beans will stay slate-grey, taste very bitter, and lack the rich chocolate aroma buyers look for, which reduces the crop's market value.
ga: Beans ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ slate-gray, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa, ni ebɛ tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha jarayeli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How does rainy weather during the drying period affect my harvested cocoa beans?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ saa mikookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess rain and humidity slow down drying, causing wet cocoa beans to absorb moisture, clump together, and grow harmful mold.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine haa kookoo yibii lɛ agbiɔ fioo. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. abua amɛhe naa ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara ni jeɔ kpo

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo po akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and overly wet conditions with poor air circulation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get sunburned easily if exposed to full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that give shade and keep the air humid so the cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la oya kɛji amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ aba koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for the crop. Staking lifts the vines high into the light and keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal rot and helps the tuber grow bigger.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ mli, ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afite ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planted too closely, crop roots compete for the same water and nutrients underground, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin, weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tse shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores nitrogen and brings back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with natural nitrogen.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my plants help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwo tso shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the earth so plants survive dry spells, keeps the ground cool, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. koni tsei anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni eha jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong, aggressive roots that steal water and plant food from the soil faster than farmed crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from starving your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ basabasa. ni juɔ nu ni eduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on tender corn leaves. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended safe pest control measures or ash mixtures protects the plant before the heart of the maize is destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo sũ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ahe dani ŋmãa lɛ tsui lɛ afite.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. Look for the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, along with visible cracks in the dry soil near the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ ŋmeii ni anaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɛŋkɛ tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely. Providing regular watering during dry spells cools the plant down and allows the flowers to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli ajɔ, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Yam plants are vines that naturally climb toward sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil to prevent fungal diseases and helps the plant catch maximum sunlight to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eha tso lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow small and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand downward easily. If your soil is hard, compact, or stony, the tuber struggles to push through, resulting in stunted, misshapen tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaawa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How long can I leave mature yams in the ground before they spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi ŋmɔtɔ ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ dani efite?

english: Yams can stay safely underground in dry soil for a few months during the dry season because the tuber goes dormant. However, once the next rains begin, the tuber will start sprouting and quickly lose its eating quality.
ga: Sweet potatoes baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ ehiɔ shi. Shi, kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ je shishi lɛ, The tubers lɛ baabɔi shweremɔ oya ni amɛ sui ni ayeɔ lɛ baaje mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn yellow while the crop is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When nutrients in the soil run low, the plant moves food from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my corn plants look weak when I plant many seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one spot, the young plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting fewer seeds per hole gives roots enough space to grow strong stems.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ yɛ he kome. Tsei bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tso ni wa.

english: How does hot, dry weather affect my maize when the cobs are forming?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ saa mi-ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji eba fɔfɔii ahe?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry out the sticky silks on the maize cob, which prevents pollen from fertilizing the flowers. This causes cobs to develop missing or incomplete rows of grain.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baaha siliki lɛ afee nɔ ni wa. yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ nɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pollen lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmãa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ loo eshɛɛɛ he.

english: What is the best way to store my harvested maize so weevils do not destroy it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ŋmeii akafite?

english: Insects thrive on moisture. You must dry your maize cobs thoroughly in the sun until the seeds are very hard before putting them into airtight bags or dry storage cribs to keep pests away.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Kwɛmɔ ni ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani okɛwo vacuum bag loo dry storage cot mli koni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why does my cassava take almost a full year to mature while my maize takes only three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ heɔ nyɔji etɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is a fast-growing grain crop designed to produce seeds above ground quickly. Cassava is a root crop that slowly collects food energy over many months to store in thick underground roots.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni daa oya ni afee koni ewo dumɔwui oya yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Cassava ji tso ko ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni Buaa niyenii hewalɛ naa fiofio yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli koni ekɛto eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas act as natural helpers by taking nitrogen from the air and putting it into the soil. This enriches the soil and provides natural food for your maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa o-corn tsei lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why do crops yield better in the major rainy season compared to the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa fioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: The major rainy season brings longer, more consistent rainfall that keeps the soil moist throughout the crop's growth cycle. The minor season is shorter with unpredictable rains, which can interrupt plant growth.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni yaa nɔ daa baaba. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ kuku ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Is it good to plant cassava or vegetables on land where heavy digging and mining took place?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ mli waa lɛ nɔ?

english: Land that has experienced heavy digging loses its nutrient-rich topsoil and may contain harmful residues or hard subsoil, making it very hard for crops to grow deep roots or absorb the food they need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie shika babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ baafite sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ekolɛ sũ ni eshwɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo sũ shishi ni wa yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaawo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Feeding the soil with compost, manure, or fertilizer restores the nutrient balance so the leaves turn dark green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, shielding fragile young leaves from burning heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ebuɔ baai bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense against extreme heat; the leaves roll up to conserve internal water and prevent moisture loss from excessive sunshine.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ahi mli ni amɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni fe nine mli baa lɛ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops compete against each other for light, soil water, and nutrients. They stretch upward to fight for sunlight instead of growing thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild species adapted to survive in harsh local soils. They absorb available soil food and water much quicker than domestic crops, which is why regular clearing is needed to prevent them from choking your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni atsake lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ jɛmɛ shikpɔji ni mli wa lɛ anɔ. Amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ daa koni ekɛtsi oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize every year if I grow maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to rest. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy enough to support cash crops like cashew or oil palm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cashew nuts loo palm oil?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, soft to dig, holds water well after rain, and contains living organisms like earthworms, which show that the soil is rich in organic nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, kɛ́ atsa lɛ, ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli.

english: Why are the flower blossoms falling off my pepper plants before any peppers start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips that damage the sensitive flower stems.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why do dark brown spots spread across my cassava leaves during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-cassava baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall and high moisture create damp conditions where fungal diseases thrive and spread easily from leaf to leaf through splashing water droplets.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa hulutsoo shihilɛi baa. Fungal helai daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps improve my soil for the next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvest is done, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ naa Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or straw help my crops survive hot days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from heating up the earth. This keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly, and helps your crops retain moisture longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni etsi jeŋ dɔlɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya Ni eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and how does it hurt the crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni te eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Those holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on young leaves. If left untreated, they can eat into the growing centre of the maize plant, preventing it from producing healthy stalks and ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye nii kɛya hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akaná ŋmeii kɛ toi ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam plants turning yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves early in the season usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage around the roots, which prevents the yam plant from absorbing the nutrients it needs to build tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ehiii, ni no haaa sweet potato tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why can my cassava plants stay green during the dry season when my other crops dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Beni mitsei krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Cassava is a naturally drought-hardy crop that drops its outer leaves to conserve water and relies on deep root systems that extract moisture stored far below the soil surface.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eshiɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he, ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu babaoo ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my sorghum seeds after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil is wet at least hand-deep after two or three steady rainfalls. Planting too early after a light drizzle can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni ewooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient water during flowering, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small even when there is plenty of sunshine for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water and fertilizers from under the ground long before they grow tall enough to block sunlight from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest produce less grain than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwu ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from commercial varieties lose their hybrid vigor in subsequent generations, leading to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower disease resistance compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ jarayeli mli lɛ laajeɔ hybrid hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli, ni no haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my stored grains develop small insects inside the bag even when I dried them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ kooloi bibii yɛ kotoku lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Insect eggs are often laid on grains while they are still in the field. If the grain is not dried to a very low moisture level and stored in sealed, airtight bags, those hidden eggs hatch and multiply inside the stored bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kooloi bibii awoɔ dumɔwui anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashɛɛɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi waa ni akɛto vacuum bag ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green leaves. When there is not enough food in the soil, the plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does putting chemical fertilizer directly touching my pepper stems make the plants dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that pull water out of plant tissue. Placing fertilizer right against the stem sucks moisture directly out of the plant, causing the stems and roots to burn and dry up.
ga: Nuŋtɛi ni mli eyi obɔ ni jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The maize stretches upward to reach the light, spending all its energy on height instead of making big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abɛi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa kane lɛ he. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeetswa ŋmei agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots store soft starch for food. If left in the ground past maturity, the plant converts that soft starch into tough woody fibers to strengthen itself as it gets older, making the roots hard to cook and eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo toɔ akɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaadara jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ nakai ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa koni amɛwo amɛhe hewalɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo shishifãi lɛ ni aye.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during the hottest days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen so the flowers cannot form seeds or fruit. When the plant senses a flower will not produce fruit, it drops the flower to save energy and moisture for cooler days.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ tomato ŋmɔtɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui loo aduawai. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii Amɛbaashi fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ hulutsoo he yɛ gbii ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon even when the ground has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: On hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. Curling up reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant hold onto its water until the evening cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do cowpeas make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work with beneficial organisms in the ground to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny bumps on their roots. When the cowpea plant dies, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that travels down to swell the tuber underground. Staking spreads the leaves high off the ground where they catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil dampness.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi lɛ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ. Staking gbɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ lɛ, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do pests attack and chew my cabbage leaves much faster during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-cabbage baai lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ mra kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather helps pest eggs hatch faster and creates larger insect populations. Also, because leaves have less water during dry periods, pests must eat double the leaf material just to get the water they need to live.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. ni ekɛ kooloi bibii babaoo aba. Kɛfata he lɛ, akɛni baai lɛ bɛ nu babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ aye baai lɛ amli nibii ni fa fe shii enyɔ koni amɛná nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get moldy and rot if I bag them immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli beni mikpaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain trapped water inside them. If you seal them in a bag without sun-drying them first, that trapped water creates heat and moisture, which is the perfect environment for mold and rot to grow.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu ni efo mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo kotoku mli ni okɛ hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ ji he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and turn yellow during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to trap moisture and protect themselves from extreme heat. When the soil is dry, the plant cannot absorb enough nitrogen and water, which causes the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nitrogen kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do tomato leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, tomato leaves evaporate water faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. This causes temporary wilting during peak afternoon sunshine, but the plant usually recovers once temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Kɛji edɔ waa lɛ Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he waa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon temperatures, dry winds, or erratic watering. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ na nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi wala mli.

english: Which crops can handle hot and dry weather similar to the climate in Burkina Faso or Northern Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ akpee shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ Burkina Faso loo Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ naa?

english: Crops like sorghum, millet, cowpea, and groundnuts have deep root systems and tough leaves that allow them to survive in hot, dry conditions with very little water compared to crops like maize or cabbage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli wa ni haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo kaabe he.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay alive during long dry seasons when other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to stop water loss and relies on energy stored in its thick underground roots, remaining dormant until the next rains arrive.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛkpa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii. Kɛtsɔ shi ni ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ Kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans alongside my cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for nearby crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow much faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild and very hardy, meaning they react instantly to moisture and absorb nutrients quickly, whereas cultivated crop seeds take more time to break dormancy and establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ basabasa waa ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ, amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfoɔ ŋmiŋmi ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to start growing vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi aduawai adumɔ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, breaks apart easily in your hands, retains water without waterlogging, and contains organic material like decayed leaves or earthworms that feed plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu ato ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to multiply and attack my crops more heavily during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayi fa babaoo ni amɛtutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heat accelerates insect reproduction cycles, and dry conditions weaken crop leaves, making it easier for pests like aphids and mites to feed on plant sap.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa kooloi afɔmɔ yaa oya. ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu.

english: Why should I avoid pouring water directly over crop leaves in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ he?

english: Water droplets left on leaves in bright sunshine act like magnifying glasses that can burn the leaves, and wet leaves in high heat encourage leaf-fungus diseases to spread quickly.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo ni baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ. Ni baai ni la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baaha baa mli ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and die after heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods your field and water sits for too long, it cuts off air to the soil. Plant roots need oxygen to breathe and absorb nutrients; without it, the roots begin to suffocate, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to stall.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmɔji lɛ amli hoɔ nu ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ baafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ yaa wɔɔhe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the soil stays waterlogged for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu gbii babaoo nɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to develop properly. When rainwater sits in the soil without proper drainage channels, harmful fungi and bacteria thrive in the wet earth, causing the tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa bɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu lɛ. Mold kɛ bacteria ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: How does digging channels around my field help my crops survive storm season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ahum be mli?

english: Channels and gutters collect heavy rainwater and direct it safely away from your plants. This keeps the soil from getting oversaturated, protecting root systems from rotting and stopping topsoil nutrients from washing away.
ga: Funnels kɛ gutters buaa nugbɔshiimɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛtsɔɔ lɛ gbɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etse tsɔ. Ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he, ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that catch strong wind and shallow roots that hold onto the soil. When heavy rains soften the soil, the roots lose their grip, making it easy for the heavy plant to pull out of the muddy ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he nii, kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Ehaa tsei ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: How does using piped irrigation affect how fast my pepper plants grow in the dry season?
ga: Te paipii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa bɔ ni pepper tsei lɛ daa oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During the dry season, plants slow down their growth to save moisture. Piped irrigation supplies a steady, controlled amount of water directly to root zones, allowing the pepper plants to keep feeding and fruiting continuously without stress.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Nu ni akɛ paipii tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni akudɔɔ lɛ yaa shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa pepper tso lɛ yaa nɔ eyeɔ nii ni ewoɔ yibii ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open when I give them plenty of water after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ tswaa kɛ́ mikɛ nu babaoo ha amɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a tomato plant goes dry for too long, the skin on the fruit toughens. If it suddenly receives a large flush of water from heavy rain or sudden irrigation, the inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Yibii lɛ ahiɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ trukaa lɛ, nu babaoo ni jɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ trukaa lɛ mli ba. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai lɛ amli fãmɔ.

english: How does regular, controlled watering help fertilizer work better on my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛhaa mi daa ni akudɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa mi-aduawai lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve into a liquid state that roots can absorb. Steady, controlled watering keeps the soil moist enough to dissolve fertilizer without washing the nutrients so deep into the earth that roots cannot reach them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ nu ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ aahu akɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and young pods when the rainy weather is too extreme?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɔfɔii kɛ amɛbii bibii lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme rain and high dampness create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like black pod. Moisture stress and sudden temperature drops also cause the cocoa tree to shed flowers and small pods to conserve energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji. Humidity haomɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi trukaa lɛ hu baanyɛ aha cacao tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot days, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. Wilting is a temporary protective reaction where the plant closes its pores to conserve water until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbimɔ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni nu lɛ ahi mli kɛyashi hulu lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my young rice seedlings wash away or get buried after heavy downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ, nu hoɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ loo ashɛrɛɔ amɛ ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Without controlled water pathways, heavy rain creates strong surface currents that strip away topsoil and carry light seedlings with it. Proper water control structures slow down the water flow so seedlings stay rooted.
ga: Kɛji nu gbɛi ni akudɔ bɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ yaa. Nu he gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi lolo.

english: Is it safe for me to cut or prune my crops if I am growing them on a hillside or mountain?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji midu yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, pruning or cutting your crops on higher or sloped ground does not harm them. It helps manage their growth so they can settle well and take firm root in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa loo ofolɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ eyeee amɛ awui. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ amɛdalɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛto amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Will trimming excess growth from my plants on high ground ruin my harvest?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ fãi ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: No, you haven't done anything wrong by trimming crops on higher land. Cutting back extra growth encourages the crop to direct its energy into taking strong root in the ground.
ga: Dabi, ofeee nɔ ko ni ejaaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ofoɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Dalɛ kroko ni abaaba shi lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo shishifãi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do my crops behave differently when planted on a slope compared to flat ground?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔji anɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Crops on high ground naturally seek to establish themselves deep in the soil, and routine cutting or maintenance helps them adapt to the sloped terrain without damaging their growth.
ga: Gɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto amɛhe shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ loo akwɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ni efiteee edalɛ.

english: How does flowing water help my crops grow better than standing water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni ekã shi lɛ?

english: Flowing water makes it easier for crops to drink and absorb essential nutrients continuously, which keeps the plants active and moving forward in their growth.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu be fɛɛ be ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ni eyaa hiɛ yɛ dalɛ mli.

english: What should I do to care for my crops if my farm is in a wet or swampy area?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nu yɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ?

english: When crops are in water, you must support them by managing the water flow properly so the plants get enough moisture to drink without suffering from stagnant conditions.
ga: Be ni tso lɛ yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ Esa akɛ oye obua tsei lɛ kɛtsɔ nu lɛ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛnuɔ nii ni shihilɛi ni ŋmɛɔ shi lɛ akapiŋ amɛ.

english: How does controlling the movement of water across my land benefit my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔyeli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Directing the way water flows helps your crops steadily drink and take in nutrients, which propels their overall development and health forward.
ga: Nu lɛ ni hoɔ lɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai daa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hiɛyaa fɛɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do crops planted near a moving stream seem to feed and grow more actively?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni adu yɛ faai ni hoɔ oya lɛ ahe lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: The natural movement of water brings fresh nutrients right to the plant roots, allowing them to drink easily and advance steadily through their growth stages.
ga: Nu lɛ adebɔɔ mli nyiɛmɔ kɛ niyenii hee baa tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ anuɔ nii mlɛo ni ayaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to guard and protect the water sources near my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabu nu ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ he ni mabu he lɛ?

english: Protecting your water sources ensures a clean, continuous flow of water, which is necessary for your crops to drink and thrive over time.
ga: Onu jɛɛhe lɛ he ni ooobu lɛ haa nu lɛ mli tseɔ ni eyaa nɔ ehoɔ. Enɛ he miihia koni onibii lɛ anu nu ni amɛdara yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What does it mean to provide protection for the water on my land?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he buu lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Providing protection for water sources means creating buffers or barriers around streams and ponds so the water can flow cleanly and keep nourishing your crops.
ga: Nu jɛɛhe ko he ni abuɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ afee buffer loo gbɛtsii nii ko ni ebɔle he. faai kɛ ŋshɔi Enɛ baaha nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli atse ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does keeping my farm's water channels clear help my plants survive dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mihaa efeɔ faŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli?

english: Maintaining clear water pathways acts as a guardian for your supply, ensuring that smooth water flow reaches your crops so they can drink continuously and keep growing.
ga: Nu gbɛi ni mli tse lɛ akwɛmɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii ni okɛhaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shɛɔ onibii ahe. Bɔni afee ni amɛya nɔ amɛnu dãa ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their delicate leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that protects the young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants need to build strong stems and keep their leaves green, so adding compost or fertilizer helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛhe shi ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What should I do if I notice one cassava plant has twisted leaves while the others look healthy?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ eko baa lɛ etsake? Yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Twisted or yellow-patterned leaves on cassava usually signal Cassava Mosaic Disease. Uprooting and destroying that single infected plant immediately prevents tiny insects like whiteflies from spreading the disease to your healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela. Kɛ́ otsi tso kome ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shishi ni ofite lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji anaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkagbɛ hela amɛshwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need both air and moisture to sprout. If soil stays waterlogged right after planting, the seeds drown from a lack of air and rot before they can grow roots.
ga: Dumɔwui he hia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i fɛɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my cassava cuttings very close together?
ga: Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build large tuber roots, resulting in a heavier total yield.
