ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ baaya hiɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer ears of maize every time I plant maize on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa toi fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to settle in permanent breeding spots. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ toɔ he ni amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ daa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face sudden heat stress or lack water. The plant discards flowers to save its strength until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ. Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa edaa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and look weak even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as competitor plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops usually grow into weaker plants that yield much less food than the parent crop. Purchasing fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong growth and uniform yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo kwraa fe fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa anáa dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why should I cut off the low, old branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishi kɛ nɔ ni egbɔ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing lower branches prevents soil-borne diseases from splashing onto the leaves during rain. It also helps the plant direct its energy toward producing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akashwie baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei hu ni amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa crops struggling even though I plant them the same way my parents taught me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ miitswa lɛ? Ni madu nibii ni mifɔlɔi tsɔɔ mi lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Climate change has altered weather patterns in Ghana, bringing unpredictable rains and higher temperatures that stress traditional cocoa plants and make old farming routines less effective.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ etsake kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɛ Ghana. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ baa. Enɛ haa kusum cacao tsei lɛ anɔ haoɔ. ni ehaa okwaayeli nifeemɔi momo lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Does changing weather really affect how insects behave on my farm?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ baaná kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ajeŋba nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, rising temperatures and changing rainfall patterns create ideal conditions for pests to multiply faster and spread to new farms more easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔji heei amli oya.

english: Why am I seeing so many new bugs on my cocoa trees in recent years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi heei lɛ? Ayɛ shweremɔ babaoo yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afii nɛɛ amli.

english: Changes in climate have brought new pest populations into areas where they were not common before, allowing them to thrive on vulnerable crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kooloi bibii heei miiba hei ni tsutsu lɛ anaaa amɛ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa lɛ amli.

english: What makes cocoa trees get sick and lose their pods?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hela ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ?

english: Cocoa trees get sick when fungal infections or viruses attack them, especially when weather conditions are humid and the plant variety lacks natural defense against those diseases.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hela kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutua amɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni tsei srɔtoi lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nakai helai lɛ ahe.

english: How does disease spread so quickly from one tree to another on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela ko gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Disease spores travel through water droplets, farm tools, and pest insects that move from sick trees to healthy ones, spreading rapidly if the trees are not resistant.
ga: Helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai tsɔɔ nu mli nu mli. okwaayeli he nibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashi.

english: What does it mean when an officer says a cocoa variety is 'strong'?
ga: Kɛ́ onukpai kɛɛ akɛ ‘eyɛ kookoo henɔi lɛ amli’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: A strong cocoa variety has been specially bred with natural defenses that allow it to withstand diseases and harsh weather better than older varieties.
ga: Akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ fɔɔ cocoa henɔi ni wa lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe henɔi ni etsɛ.

english: Is the Amazonian cocoa variety still a good choice for my farm today?
ga: Ani Amazon cocoa ji nɔ ni hi lolo kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ ŋmɛnɛ?

english: No, Amazonian cocoa is an older variety that struggles to resist the newer diseases and tougher climate conditions present in Ghana today.
ga: Dabi, Amazon cocoa ji tso ko ni etsɛ ni miitao ni edamɔ helai heei kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ Ghana ŋmɛnɛ lɛ naa.

english: How do I choose the best type of cocoa seed to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kookoo ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should look for modern hybrid varieties specifically developed by agriculture research centers to resist local diseases and survive changing weather.
ga: Esa akɛ otao ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ fee tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli.

english: What will happen if I keep planting old cocoa seeds instead of buying new disease-resistant varieties?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo yibii momo yɛ kookoo henɔi heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ahemɔ najiaŋ?

english: Old cocoa varieties lack the strength to fight off modern pests and diseases, which will lead to lower yields, dying trees, and lost income over time.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawu amɛshi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai. Enɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aba shi, tsei agboi, ni shika ni anáa lɛ hu afite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Where can I find crop varieties that won't die easily when disease enters my village?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana tsei ni gbooo mlɛo kɛji hela bote mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Disease-resistant seed varieties are produced by certified government extension offices and cocoa research institutions that test seeds for strength before distributing them.
ga: Nɔyeli nitsumɔhei ni yaa hiɛ kɛ kookoo he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei ni aŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Enɛ baaka dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ akwɛ dani ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why does my rice farm need so much standing water compared to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi babaoo kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in wet conditions and have internal airways that let their roots breathe underwater. Keeping water in the field also creates a natural barrier that stops most weeds from growing and competing with the rice.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ daa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ mli, ni amɛyɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni tsiɔ jwɛi babaoo naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa lɛ akaye akaŋ.

english: Why can rice survive heavy rain flooding while my cassava rots in the water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa je nu afua ni naa wa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa fite yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice stem tissues act like tiny snorkels that transport oxygen from the leaves down to flooded roots. Cassava roots lack this feature, so prolonged flooding cuts off their oxygen, causing the tubers to suffocate and rot.
ga: Omɔ tso mli fãji tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ paipi bibioo ko. ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ yaa shishi kɛyaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu afua ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ

english: Why do birds attack my rice farm right when the grains start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ be mli pɛ ni ŋmaa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Before rice grains harden into rice, they fill with a sweet, liquid starch known as the 'milk stage'. Birds find this milky liquid very nutritious and easy to digest, which is why they target the farm during early grain formation.
ga: Dani ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmãa lɛ Esa akɛ amɛkɛ nu mli ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘milk stage’ lɛ afata he. Okpoi naa akɛ nɛkɛ nu ni tamɔ mliki nɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ waa ni ehaa amɛyeɔ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni akɛ amɛhiɛ fɔ ŋmɔji anɔ yɛ shishijee dumɔwui akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Rain gives the plant water, but it does not supply the essential soil nutrients needed for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu. Shi ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haaa.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for light, air, and nutrients. They stretch upward as fast as possible to reach sunlight instead of growing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my farm when the ground is damp rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbi lɛ?

english: Crops cannot eat solid fertilizer; they absorb nutrients dissolved in water through their roots. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn the root system or cause the nutrients to blow away.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa. Amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛjieɔ niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya.

english: Weeds are native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh local conditions. They absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing weeds early is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why does strong wind and rain reduce my crop harvest when the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi kɛ́ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering is the stage when plants transfer pollen to form seeds and grains. Heavy rain and wind knock flowers off the stem or wash pollen away, preventing the crop from producing grains or fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be mli ni tsei tsɔɔ pollen mli koni amɛfee dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi loo efoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui loo aduawai.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it back into the soil. Planting them after grain crops like rice refreshes the land's fertility naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield smaller crops than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their vigor over generations and may carry hidden pests or diseases from the past season. Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to ensure high germination, disease resistance, and good yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Ni ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stalks too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other, and their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil. Giving them enough space allows each plant to form larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ baatsi hulu la naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain plants grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ yɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaf shade and retain moisture, acting like protective umbrellas for the young cocoa during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa baa lɛ mli hɔɔŋ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are hungry for soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If your maize leaves start turning light green or yellow, especially starting from the tips in a V-shape, the plant is lacking nitrogen and needs fertilizer or compost to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Titri lɛ akɛni ŋmãa lɛ naagbee ji V hewɔ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa awo mli koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on my farm before I plant maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the ground so your next crop, like maize, has rich soil to feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni eyeɔ.

english: These are pests like Fall Armyworm that hide in the growing center (funnel) of the plant where it is soft and moist. They feed on young leaves, which can destroy the plant's ability to grow if not managed early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli (cone) lɛ mli, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni baanyɛ afite tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes mud carrying fungal spores onto the leaves, and the wet leaves create the perfect environment for fungi to grow. Taking off lower leaves touched by soil can help stop this spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni hiɛ fungal spores lɛ anɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni sũ eshɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akpa nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct heat, preventing water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves turn yellow when the soil stays flooded with water for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When soil stays flooded, water fills up all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and causing the leaves to turn yellow and droop.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lolo lɛ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why did some of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if planted too deep for the shoot to reach the light, if the soil was too dry, or if insects and ants ate the seeds in the ground before they could germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni la akabote mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I remove the tiny side shoots growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, jiemɔ

english: Trimming extra side shoots forces the plant to send its water and energy directly into making big, healthy tomato fruits rather than growing useless extra leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ koni ewo tomato yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water around their roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps them get back their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni amɛdara waa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu kroko hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids (akate). Proper shade management, pruning, and protecting the trees from pests help flowers stay on and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirid (akatate) shade management pruning Ni tsei ahe ni abuɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato plants stop making fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive heat damages tomato pollen, causing flowers to dry out and fall off before fruit can form. Providing light shade and watering early in the morning helps keep the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ baafite tomato pollen lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afee tsei lɛ hulutsoo ni awo amɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible. When the leaves get maximum sunlight, the plant creates more food, which leads to much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Beni baai lɛ náa hulu la babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ baafee niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: The extra shoots (suckers) steal food and water from the main fruiting tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree has enough strength to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi (tso lɛ) juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Giving each plant proper space allows it to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so much slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the food and space they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha otsei lɛ niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by hungry caterpillars feeding on your crop. Inspecting your plants regularly and spraying early with natural neem oil solutions or safe insecticides can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛyeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo. Abaanyɛ akpa tsei nɛɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist for several days. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell immediately follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni egbo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do insects easily destroy the vegetables I plant on my open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo lɛ?

english: On an open farm, pests can freely fly in and attack your crops. Growing inside a structure like a greenhouse creates a physical wall that prevents insects from getting inside to destroy your produce.
ga: yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni agbele mli mli lɛ, ŋmeii yɛ heyeli ni amɛfoɔ kɛboteɔ mli ni amɛtutuaa onibii. Kɛ́ okwɛ̃ yɛ tsɔne ko tamɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I stop bugs from eating my crops without using too much chemical spray?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa ni mikɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can plant your crops inside a greenhouse. The building acts as a protective shield that keeps insects out so they cannot reach your growing plants or harvested produce.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsuji tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkashɛ tsei ni miida loo nibii ni akpaa lɛ ahe.

english: Can an enclosed farm building really protect my harvested produce from pests?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsũi ni agbe naa lɛ baanyɛ abu mikpamɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because insects cannot easily penetrate an enclosed greenhouse structure, keeping both your growing plants and your harvested produce safe from pest damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kooloi bibii nyɛŋ abote tsũi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni agbe naa lɛ amli mlɛo. Ha otsei ni miida lɛ kɛ okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite amɛ.

english: Why is it so hard to protect my outdoor crops when the weather becomes too hot or dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mabu mi kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When you plant outside in the open, you cannot control the weather or sun conditions. A greenhouse gives you full control over the climate inside so extreme weather does not harm your crops.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ Onyɛŋ okudɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ. Greenhouses haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ yeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Is there a way for me to control the atmosphere around my plants so they grow better?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makudɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? mi tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, growing crops in a greenhouse allows you to manage and control the internal environment, unlike open-field farming where you are at the mercy of natural weather patterns.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni oookwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni okwɛɔ nɔ. Ejeee tamɔ ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli ni agbele naa he ni oyɔɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ amɔbɔnalɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do crops planted in the open field suffer more during heavy rain or severe heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ naa amanehulu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Open fields expose crops directly to bad weather that you cannot manage. Inside a greenhouse, you control the climate conditions, protecting the crops from harsh external environments.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni agbele naa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni onyɛɛɛ okwɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ amli. Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli Obaanyɛ okudɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ahe

english: Is it possible for me to grow tomatoes during the dry season when rain is scarce?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ tomato yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Yes, by using a greenhouse, you control the growing environment inside. This allows you to plant and harvest crops at any time of the year regardless of rain patterns outside.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ greenhouse ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ okudɔ shihilɛ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nibii ni okpaa yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ he

english: How can I produce fresh vegetables continuously without waiting for the traditional rainy season?
ga: Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔya nɔ wɔwo aduawai heei ni ehe ehiaaa ni wɔmɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni wɔfeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Planting inside a greenhouse lets you grow crops all year round because you are no longer dependent on outdoor seasons or uncontrollable weather.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ejaakɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ kponɔgbɛ bei loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: What is the main difference between planting crops inside a greenhouse and planting outside in my open field?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ amɛdumɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ teŋ?

english: Outside, you cannot control weather conditions or keep insects away easily. Inside a greenhouse, you keep destructive pests out and can control the climate to grow crops at any time you want.
ga: Yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ, onyɛɛɛ okudɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mlɛo loo otsi ŋmeii kɛjɛ he. Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli Obaanyɛ ojie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ. Ni obaanyɛ okudɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ koni okwɛ tsei be fɛɛ be ni osumɔɔ.

english: How does a greenhouse allow me to plant crops outside of their normal farming season?
ga: Te greenhouse lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ tsei yɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ lɛ mli?

english: A greenhouse lets you adjust and maintain the right environment for your plants, meaning you do not have to rely on traditional outdoor seasons to get a good harvest.
ga: Greenhouse haa onyɛɔ otsakeɔ shihilɛ ni sa kɛha otsei lɛ ni okwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ kusum nifeemɔ ni ji kponɔgbɛ be lɛ nɔ koni onine ashɛ kpamɔ kpakpa nɔ.

english: How do I calculate how much seed I need to buy for one acre of maize land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha ŋmãa shikpɔŋ ni ji acre kome lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Every crop has a recommended planting distance. For maize, proper spacing means you will need about 8 to 10 kilograms of good seeds to cover one acre without crowding the crops.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ he ni esa akɛ adu yɛ. kɛha ŋmãa Gbɛ ni sa tsɔɔ akɛ obaahiɛ dumɔwui kpakpai aaafee kiloi 8 kɛyashi 10 ni okɛha acre 1 ni okɛ tso lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: Is it better for me to expand my farm to more acres or try to get more harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ acre babaoo nɔ loo mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni makpa nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: It is usually better to focus on doing proper spacing, weeding, and soil feeding on your current small land first. Managing a small land well yields more profit than spreading your labor thin across many acres.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama gbɛ ni sa nɔ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ niyenii haa yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ nɔ. yɛ ogbɛnɛ klɛŋklɛŋ Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔkwɛmɔ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ fe nitsumɔ ni ooogbɛ ashwã acre babaoo nɔ.

english: Seeds need constant moisture to wake up and grow. If you plant in dry soil after just one light rain, the seeds can dry out and die under the hot sun before the main rain arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, shikome pɛ Dumɔwui hu baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba.

english: How can I check if my soil is in good condition to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli koni mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Good planting soil should be dark, crumble easily in your hand without forming a hard lump, and feel moist. If earthworms are present in the soil, it is a sign that the ground is healthy and ready.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ afee diŋŋ. Efoɔ mlɛo yɛ nine mli ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. ni ehaa mɔ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni efee klalo.

english: What basic steps do I need to follow to prepare my land before putting seeds in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You must first clear the weeds and bush, loosen the topsoil so roots can spread easily, clear big roots or rocks, and create ridges or planting holes before dropping your seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii kɛjɛ ohe klɛŋklɛŋ. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Jiemɔ shishifãi loo tɛi wuji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. ni afee ŋmeii loo dumɔ bui dani adu dumɔwui

english: How deep should I bury cassava cuttings when I am planting them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava stems should be buried about 10 centimeters deep at a slanting angle into loose soil so the roots can anchor firmly and produce big tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ afu ŋmei tso lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 10, yɛ koŋ nɔ, awo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ amɔmɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops at different stages instead of giving it all at once during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mli shikome yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Young seeds cannot handle too much food at once and can burn. Splitting the fertilizer allows the plant to get nutrients gradually when growing leaves, flowering, and forming fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ aye niyenii babaoo yɛ be kome mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai fiofio beni eshiɔ baai, ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth, or that too much water is trapped around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Aloo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall with weak stems and produce very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients needed to hold the fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛkpa aduawai lɛ ni bɛ

english: How do I know if my maize farm is receiving too much water from heavy rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When maize gets too much water, the soil loses air and the plant's roots begin to drown. You will notice the leaves turning pale yellow starting from the bottom, and the entire plant will stop growing taller.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ná nu babaoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaana akɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ shishigbɛ. ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baakpa shweremɔ

english: What will happen to my cassava roots if floodwater covers my field for three days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii etɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. If covered by standing water for more than two or three days, the underground tubers will rot quickly and turn soft and smelly, making them unharvestable.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ nu ni damɔ shi fe gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ha nɔ lɛ Tubers fiteɔ oya ni efeɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ. ni haaa anyɛ akpa nii

english: Which crops can I safely plant in low-lying land that collects floodwater during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rice and certain varieties of cocoyam are naturally adapted to wet conditions. Their roots can handle standing water and wet soil better than crops like cassava, maize, or cowpeas.
ga: Omɔ kɛ kookoo henɔi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋmɛ nu ni damɔ shi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa.

english: Can I still plant tomatoes during the dry season if I have access to a water dam nearby?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛji miyɛ nu ŋshɔ ni bɛŋkɛ mi?

english: Yes, dry season farming is very profitable with dam water. Because there is less pest pressure and higher market demand during the dry period, watering your tomatoes regularly from a dam will yield healthy crops and better sales.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ he baa sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛtsɔ nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ faaa, ni jarayeli nibii hu taoɔ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomatoi lɛ amli daa kɛjɛ faa ko mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaahɔɔ hu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is water collected from rain runoff and stored in a dam safe to pour on my food crops?
ga: Ani nu ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli ni akɛtoɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ koni akɛshwie miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, stored surface runoff is generally safe for crops. However, it is best to apply the water directly to the soil around the roots using bucket or drip irrigation rather than pouring it over the leaves to prevent spread of soil-borne fungi.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hoɔ ni ato lɛ ji nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, shi kɛlɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ nu lɛ baatsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Root kɛ baagi loo drip nu ni hoɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ kɛ pue baai ɔmɛ a nɔ konɛ tsɛŋemɔtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a ko ngmɛɛ zugba a mi.

english: How often should I give water to my vegetables during the hot dry months using stored water?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni ato lɛ awo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Vegetables usually need water every day or every two days during the hot dry season. Water them early in the morning or late in the evening so the soil stays moist and the sun does not evaporate the water quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu he hiaa aduawai daa gbi loo daa gbii enyɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Okɛ nu awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni hulu la lɛ haŋ nu afee ŋmɔtɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers as a defense mechanism to conserve energy and water when soil gets dry. Once regular watering resumes, the plant will produce new flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi. Kɛji akɛ nu shwie nɔ bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ ni ebaawo yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's way of reducing its exposure to hot sunlight to prevent water from evaporating out of its leaves. It is a sign that the plant is trying to protect itself from losing moisture.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu akajɛ baa lɛ mli. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it better to water my plants early in the morning rather than at mid-day when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi fe gbi mli beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets the roots absorb moisture before heat builds up. Mid-day watering causes most of the water to evaporate instantly into the hot air before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbi mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I check if the soil on my farm has enough moisture before planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Take a handful of soil from a few inches below the surface and squeeze it into your fist. If it holds its shape as a soft ball without crumbling or dripping water, the soil has the right moisture for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ aaafee 2-3 inch lɛ ni okɛmimɔ otsitsi mli. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ tamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ, nu ni shwieɔ shi loo nu ni shwieɔ shi bɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Should I dig up my entire farm land before planting my crops during the dry season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo he fɛɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani madu nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Not always. Digging up hard, dry soil breaks its natural structure and allows the remaining moisture to evaporate quickly into the air, leaving the soil drier than before.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa ni akuɔ mli lɛ baafite adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Can I plant my crops directly into the ground without digging up the whole field first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yes, this practice is called minimum tillage or zero-tillage. By making small holes only where seeds go, you leave the good soil and natural organic matter undisturbed to nourish your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ minimum tillage loo zero tillage, ni ji bu bibii ni afeɔ yɛ he ni dumɔwui lɛ yaa lɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is too dry to start plowing or tilling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: If the ground is hard, dusty, and creates thick dust clouds when disturbed, it is too dry. Tilling dry soil turns it into fine dust that easily blows away in the wind or washes away with the first rain.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ sũ babaoo, ni ekɛ sũ atatui ni mli tse baa kɛji akɛ agba enaa. Etsɔɔ akɛ egbi tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ sũ bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɛyaa oya loo ejieɔ kɛyaa kɛji nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɛ.

english: How does digging up my field in dry weather affect my soil quality?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ ni akuɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ saa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Digging exposes the deeper, moist soil to the hot sun, drying it out completely. It also exposes buried beneficial organisms and roots to intense heat, reducing natural soil fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli agbi kwraa Ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shishifãi hu shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ baa shi.

english: Why is it helpful to leave old weeds and plant leaves lying on top of my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi jwɛi ni madu baai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving plant remains on the surface acts like a protective blanket. It shades the soil from the harsh sun, keeps the ground cool, retains water, and turns into free natural fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Tso mli jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛji efite.

english: Is it bad practice to clear and burn all the grass on my land before planting?
ga: Ani jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii ni mikɛshã dani midu lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo?

english: Yes, burning destroys the valuable top layer of organic material that feeds your crops and holds moisture. It leaves the bare soil exposed to burning sun and heavy rain erosion.
ga: Hɛɛ, shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ ahiɛ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ awo hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What can I do to keep moisture in my soil when the hot sun is drying out my field?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa miŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ?

english: You can cover the ground around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a method called mulching. This shields the earth from heat and drastically reduces how fast water escapes from the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii. Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa bɔ ni nu hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly during sunny days even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: When soil is left completely bare, direct sunlight heats the ground and evaporates water instantly. Adding a surface layer of plant materials keeps the soil cooler so water stays near the roots longer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni nu lɛ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is the top layer of my farm dirt so important for crop growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ lɛ?

english: The top layer contains rich organic material from decomposed leaves and plants, holding most of the soil's nutrients and moisture. Protecting this top layer ensures your seeds get the best start.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni jɛ baai kɛ tsei ni egboi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛi hebuu nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my land has good natural soil before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ kpakpa dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Good soil is usually darker in color, feels slightly soft, stays moist under surface leaves, and shows signs of decaying plant matter or earthworms, indicating high natural fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ su ni tsuɔ waa. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo fioo Ekwɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi baai lɛ ashishi ni ana okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso mli nibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii efite Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo fa babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa stems do not dry out before their roots are well established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ akagbi dani shishifãi lɛ ama shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the leaves at the top are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to keep its fresh top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ŋwɛi baa lɛ ahi shi ehee.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or pest attacks. When the plant feels weak or hot, it drops flowers to save its remaining energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ loo edɔ lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani wɔdu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special crops that trap food from the air and store it in the soil through small balls on their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural food left behind and grows much better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa. Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do I harvest small, thin crops when I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because they are sharing a limited amount of food, none of the plants get enough to grow large.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛjaraa niyenii fioo ko pɛ Tse ko bɛ ni baanyɛ adara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my cassava crop continue to stay green and alive even when the rain stops for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, tough roots that can dig deep into the earth to find hidden groundwater. It can also shut down its growth and drop a few leaves during long dry spells to conserve water until the rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa. Ebaanyɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ena shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi dalɛ naa hu ni amɛshwie baai komɛi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, wrinkled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or thrips are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice. This damage distorts the leaves and stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips he okadi. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ekɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes to give me big yam tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni enine ashɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the energy required to make large tubers. Climbing high on stakes lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ mli, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: Why does cutting off some extra branches from my garden eggs or tomatoes help the plant grow bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni niji krokomɛi ni fata mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo tomatoi ahe lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: When a plant has too many leafy branches, it wastes its energy feeding leaves instead of fruit. Removing non-essential shoots forces the plant to send all its water and nutrients directly into growing larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo tsɔ Ebaafite hewalɛ kɛji eye baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds always grow much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that naturally adapt to harsh conditions, allowing their roots to steal water and fertilizer faster than farm crops. If weeds are not removed early, they rob your crops of the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ wɔjieee jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, Amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green leaves and strong growth. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ kpakpa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or right before a gentle rain. The moisture helps dissolve the fertilizer so the roots can absorb it, but avoid putting it down right before a heavy storm, which can wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko baanɛ. Fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shi kaakɛwo mli dani ahum ni naa wa aba, ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass—known as mulching—keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young maize, and how can I stop it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Those holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which are small caterpillars that hide inside the growing tip of the plant. You can control them by spraying recommended bio-pesticides or chemicals early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves or spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or insecticidal soap helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli loo ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi afɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that easily burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and maintaining soil moisture while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leads to thin, weak stems and a smaller overall harvest compared to plants that have enough space to spread their roots.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ hu baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaale akɛ egbɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi gbee.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences stress caused by extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil, which prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haaa fɔfɔi awo yibii

english: Why do my crops grow weak and tall when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɔ lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they stretch upward to fight each other for sunlight. Because they spend all their energy growing tall to reach the light, their stems stay thin and weak, and they produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ amɛtso lɛ mli tsei ni amɛhe waaa. ni amɛwoɔ nibii fioo

english: Why is my tomato plant growing very big with many leaves, but not producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on making leafy branches instead of flowers. Reducing nitrogen and using fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to start fruiting.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei niji kɛ baai afeemɔ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Nitrogen ni ajieɔ lɛ shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do improved crop varieties yield heavy harvests even with less fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ tsu nii po lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to use soil nutrients more efficiently and resist local diseases. Instead of wasting energy fighting sickness or making unnecessary tall stems, they put most of their strength into building heavy, rich grains and fruits.
ga: Abaafɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ hela loo tsei kakadaji amamɔ he ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ. Akɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo feɔ ŋmaa kɛ aduawai ni tsii ni fa babaoo.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap. This damages the leaf structure and stops the plant from making food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers rot underground mostly when water stays trapped in the soil without proper drainage, or when soil insects bite into the tuber and allow fungal diseases to enter. Planting on raised mounds helps excess water drain away.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ŋmɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛha ŋmeii helai bote mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out watery and thin instead of thick and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji nu ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become thick and heavy when they store starch from healthy leaf activity. If you harvest too early, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, the roots cannot fill up completely, leaving them thin and watery.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa beni amɛtoɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anitsumɔ kpakpa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji okpa mra tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ awo mli ekoŋŋ kwraa. Ha efee mlɛo ni efee nu.

english: Why are my maize cobs small and missing many grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛmli ŋmeii babaoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs wind to move pollen from the top flowers to the silks on the cob. If the farm experiences extreme heat or drought during flowering, the silks dry up before pollination is complete, leaving empty gaps on the cob.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia ŋmãa koni ejie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ yiteŋ kɛya siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Siliki lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani pollination lɛ baa naagbee. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ baa ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover my soil with dried leaves instead of burning my farm clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã ŋmɔ lɛ ni ehe tse lɛ?

english: Dry leaves act as a protective blanket for your soil. They block direct hot sunlight, keep moisture in the ground longer, and slowly decay into rich organic manure that feeds your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni ekɛhaa otsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Hybrid seeds get their high yield from a special cross between two distinct parent plants. That strength is lost after the first harvest, so planting those saved seeds next season results in uneven growth and much lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ateŋ tsakpaa krɛdɛɛ nɔ. Nakai hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nikpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and improves your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but produces tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ waa, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant spends its energy growing stems and foliage instead of roots. Using balanced organic matter or fertilizers containing phosphorus and potassium encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai moŋ fe shishifãi. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni edaraa.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally improves soil fertility and gives you a double harvest from one field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nii ni fa fe ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ toi enyɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight or strong dry winds. Leaving tall shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the tender cocoa plants and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes into the young leaves at the top of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young maize foliage. Identifying them early and applying recommended natural sprays like neem leaf extract or approved insecticides prevents them from destroying your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni gbeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem tso mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my vegetable bed dry out and harden so quickly after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa ewaa oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast when exposed to direct sun and heat. Covering the bare ground around your plants with dried leaves or grass (mulching) holds water in the soil longer and prevents hard crusting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits developing dark, sunken rotten spots at the bottom before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding crushed eggshells or lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋshɔŋloo loo lime ni atswa lɛ ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, prolonged drought, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and light shade during the hottest part of the day encourage flowers to stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine Nu ni awoɔ daa ni haa hulutsoo be fioo. Yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains right when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli beni aduawai wuji lɛ eje kpo pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and heavy bunches make the plant top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with sturdy bamboo props or wooden stakes prevents wind and heavy fruits from pulling the tree down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa tsei lɛ tsiimɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni wa loo tsei ni akɛfee tso lɛ fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala tso lɛ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden poles instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate food for growing big tubers underground. Staking raises the foliage off the damp ground, boosting growth and protecting leaves from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: If I plant two different crops close together, will their roots fight each other for food?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Ani amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ?

english: Crops planted too close together can compete for water and nutrients, but combining certain crops like legumes with grains actually helps because legumes add nitrogen to the soil that feeds neighboring plants.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Shi tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmaa ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow deep roots while others spread out near the top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: Deep roots allow crops to search for underground water during dry periods, while shallow roots are designed to quickly catch surface rainfall and absorb nutrients from compost or topsoil.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni afee shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees produce better leaves when I grow plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ woɔ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under intense sunlight, so broad-leafed plants like plantains act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and holding moisture in the air.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I plant maize and cowpea on the exact same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe abɔ?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Cowpea covers the ground to keep soil moist and adds nutrients, while tall maize grows straight up without blocking light from the low cowpea plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Okɛ tsina ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ afata he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni etsĩii tsina ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crops now than it did when I started farming it twenty years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops over many years continually removes nutrients from the earth; without adding organic manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil gradually gets exhausted.
ga: Afii babaoo ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite fiofio.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to grow demanding crops like oil palm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ tamɔ mu tso?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, feels crumbly and soft when wet, holds moisture well after rain, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo kɛji efɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni egboi ni eshwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbers that need support to spread their leaves towards sunlight, allowing the plant to make maximum energy to feed and expand the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛdara ni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees dry up quickly when I don't clear the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantains lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho oya be mli ni minyɛɛɛ mafo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizers from your plantains, starving the trees and causing their leaves to turn brown and dry up early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ o-plantains lɛ amli. Ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without producing peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside pepper flowers so they cannot form seeds, causing the plant to shed the useless flowers to save its strength.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ebɔ dumɔwui. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my plantain suckers if I transplant them during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Young suckers lack deep root systems to find deep soil water, so planting them during hot, dry weather usually causes them to dry out and die unless heavily watered.
ga: Suckers bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛkɛtaoɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi, ja awo amɛ nu babaoo.

english: Officer, what is the difference between breeder seed and foundation seed when we talk about yams?
ga: Official Fɔlɔ dumɔwui kɛ shishitoo dumɔwui Kɛji awie ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ, mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ?

english: Breeder seed comes directly from the crop researchers who created the variety—it is like the original mother plant. Foundation seed is the offspring grown directly from that mother plant to produce clean, healthy seed in larger quantities.
ga: Breeder dumɔwui jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amlitaolɔi ni bɔ amɛ lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji shishijee nyɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ Shishijee dumɔwui ji seshibii ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I bother buying foundation seed yams instead of just replanting pieces of my old harvested yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe shishijee dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ mikpamɔ momo lɛ aku sɛɛ akwɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Foundation seeds are raised from clean mother plants and are free from hidden diseases and pests, giving you a much healthier crop and better yield than reusing old, infected yam tubers.
ga: Akwɛɔ shishijee dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso ni he tse mli. ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo fe ni okɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baatsu nii ekoŋŋ.
