english: What makes a 'mother plant' so special when crop researchers are multiplying seeds?
ga: Mɛni haa ‘tso nyɛ’ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa beni ŋmɔshi nibii amlitaolɔi miigbɛ dumɔwui amɛshwã lɛ?

english: The mother plant, or breeder seed, holds the pure and strongest characteristics of a crop variety, such as disease resistance and high yields, which it passes down to all the young seeds produced from it.
ga: Nyɛ tso loo dumɔwu ni jɛ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ Eyɛ sui ni he tse ni mli wa fe fɛɛ yɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ, tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. ni akɛhaa dumɔwui bibii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ.

english: How do the leaves on my yam plant actually help the yam growing underground to get bigger?
ga: Te baai ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Yam leaves catch sunlight and mix it with water and nutrients to make food for the plant. This food travels down through the stems and fills up the underground tuber, making it grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ mɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii futuɔ mli koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Niyenii nɛɛ fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. feemɔ agbo

english: How long does it take after planting for a yam plant to produce small seed tubers?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani sweet potato tso ko woɔ dumɔwui bibii ayitsei beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It takes about four months of healthy growth for the leaves to make enough food to form well-developed small seed tubers underground.
ga: Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ dani baai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha dumɔwui bibii ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ ayitsei aba shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If insects eat the leaves off my yam vines, will it affect the yam tubers underground?
ga: Kɛji kooloi ye mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ, ani enɛ baaná shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, because the leaves act as small food factories for the plant. If insects destroy the leaves, the plant cannot produce enough food to feed and swell the underground tuber.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ejaakɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii nitsumɔhei bibii kɛha tso lɛ. Kɛji kooloi bibii kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ehi shi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How big or heavy should a small seed yam tuber be for me to plant it?
ga: Te dumɔwui bibii ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ dara loo amɛtsii ha tɛŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu?

english: A small foundation seed yam weighing around 10 grams is ideal because it contains enough stored food energy to sprout strong shoots while being efficient to plant.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui bibii ni tsiimɔ aaafee gram 10 lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni he wa akwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Can I grow small seed yams in nursery containers or special soil mixtures instead of directly in the main field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui bibii ni ji sweet potatoes yɛ tsɛnsii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsɛnsii krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, growing seed yams in controlled nursery media helps protect the young roots and tubers from soil-borne diseases, producing very clean and uniform mini-tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ buɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa yitso bibioo ni he tse waa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: How can I produce a large quantity of seed yams to sell to other farmers in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee ŋmeii babaoo ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You start by obtaining healthy foundation seeds, planting them carefully to multiply them into many small tubers, and then selling those clean tubers to farmers as high-quality planting material.
ga: Ojeɔ shishi kɛtsɔ shishitoo dumɔwu ni mli wa ni ooona lɛ nɔ. Aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná bulb bibii babaoo, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ bulb ni he tse lɛ ahaa okwaafoi akɛ dumɔ nii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is the harvesting time for small seed yams the same as big market yams?
ga: Ani ŋmeii bibii ni ji dumɔwui bibii lɛ heɔ be ni akɛkpaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, small seed yams can often be harvested earlier, around four months, once they reach the target seed size, whereas market yams are left in the ground longer to grow into full size.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, akpaa sweet potato dumɔwui bibii lɛ nyɔji ejwɛ pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛshɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he lɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ashiɔ jarayeli sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ ni eshɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do small weeds affect my crops even when my trees are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ dara momo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from your crops' roots. Clearing them regularly ensures all the soil's nutrients go directly into helping your crops grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha onine ashɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Is it really necessary to clear weeds before I plant my crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ dani adu tsei?

english: Yes, clearing weeds before planting gives young seeds and sprouts a clean start. If weeds are left in the ground, they will grow faster than your crops and choke them before they can get established.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee blɛoo kɛ shishijee dumɔwui ni he tse. Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛbaatsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni amɛbaagbe amɛ dani amɛba shi.

english: What does it mean to work the land properly before planting?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ ni aaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani adu nii lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Working the land means breaking up hard, packed dirt, removing rocks and roots, and loosening the soil. This allows plant roots to spread easily, absorb water better, and take in food from the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mligbalamɔ. Tɛi kɛ shishifãi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How does digging and loosening the soil help my crops give a better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mifoɔ ni mifoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Loosening the dirt softens hard soil so young roots can penetrate deep into the ground. It also helps rainwater soak into the earth instead of washing away the topsoil.
ga: Muji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is depleted and losing its strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo ni mihewalɛ miiho?

english: Depleted soil often turns pale, becomes hard, and produces crops with yellowish leaves or tiny harvests. If crops grow very slowly even when there is good rain, the soil has likely lost its nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewaa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baai yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo yibiiwoo fioo pɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu baanyɛ afite niyenii mli hewalɛ nii.

english: How can I make my tired land fertile again so my crops produce well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ekoŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: You can restore tired soil by adding organic matter like poultry manure, compost, or fertilizer, and by letting the land rest or planting soil-building crops like beans.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ kooloi ashishifã, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ, kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe loo tsei ni maa shikpɔŋ, tamɔ ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crop harvests getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When you grow crops on the same piece of land year after year without adding food back into the soil, the crops use up all the natural nutrients, leaving the soil exhausted.
ga: Beni oduɔ tsei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ.

english: What main conditions do my cocoa trees need to thrive and produce many pods?
ga: Mɛɛ shihilɛi titri he hiaa mi-cacao tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Cocoa trees need rich, fertile soil, proper shade when they are young, regular clearing of weeds, protection from pests, and adequate moisture to bear healthy pods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ ni baa nii babaoo he miihia kokoo tsei. Shade ni sa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa Ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my young crops seem to struggle to grow during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops struggle when the soil lacks organic matter to hold moisture. Adding compost or leaving cleared weeds around the base of plants as mulch helps keep the soil moist and cool.
ga: Tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo jwɛi ni he tse ni ashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my cocoa trees help keep them healthy?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi-cacao tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ehaa tɛŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Thick weeds around cocoa trees trap damp air, creating a home for harmful pests and diseases like black pod. Clearing the ground allows air and sunlight to flow around the trees.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli tse ni bɔle kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. Amɛfeɔ shia kɛhaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen in the soil or too much shade, they spend all their energy growing tall and bushy leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas need full sunlight and balanced soil to trigger flowering and pod growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ lɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Cowpeas he miihia hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the tubers and encouraging fungal growth. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither and die after just a few hot, sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young seedlings have shallow roots that quickly dry out when the top layer of soil loses its moisture in direct heat. Covering the bare ground around your seedlings with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps moisture.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ fo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ wo mli tɛ̃ɛ. He ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa dumɔwui ahe kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does lowland rice need to stay in water while maize dies if water stays on the farm too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ ahi nu mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa gboɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice stems have special internal air channels that let oxygen travel down to its roots even under water, while maize roots drown and rot without dry air in the soil. Standing water also prevents weeds from choking out the rice plants.
ga: Omɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akatsi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the young flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, a lack of soil nutrients, or attacks from tiny insects like mirids. Keeping shade trees overhead and controlling pests helps the flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Shade ni yɔɔ yiteŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the sap, or by a viral infection carried by these pests. Using neem oil spray or soapy water early on helps control these insects before they damage the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla tsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite baai lɛ.

english: This black soft patch is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding wood ash or lime to the soil prevents this damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni akɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily when heavy rains and strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and very heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy and easy for wind to push over. You can protect them by propping up the fruiting stems with strong wooden bamboo poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ ewoɔ lɛ oya. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni okɛbaafi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to spread their leaves fully toward the sun. When you stake yam vines off the ground, the leaves capture maximum sunlight to manufacture the food needed to expand the underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo kwraa kɛha hulu la lɛ. Kɛji odu sweet potato wain tso kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: What makes Pona yam so popular and expensive compared to other yam varieties in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni haa Pona yam lɛ ehe gbɛi waa ni ejara wa waa kɛ akɛto yam henɔi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ahe?

english: Pona yam is highly valued in the market because of its sweet taste, dry mealy texture when boiled, and quick cooking time, though it requires good soil and careful storage to prevent rot.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji potato yams lɛ jara wa waa yɛ jara nɔ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ ahoo lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli egbi. Ni eheɔ be oya dani ehoɔ, eyɛ mli akɛ ebiɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ he ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekafite moŋ.

english: Does the size of the seed yam I plant determine how big my harvested yam will be?
ga: Ani bɔ ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ dara ha lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni sweet potato ŋmaa lɛ baafee agbo ha?

english: Larger seed yams store more food energy to help the vine grow strong early on, which can lead to bigger yields, but soil fertility, water, and proper spacing matter just as much.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui wuji toɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo koni eye ebua wain tso lɛ ni edara waa mra. Enɛ baanyɛ aha nitsumɔ babaoo aba. Shi shikpɔŋ babaoo, nu kɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ hu he hiaa nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers sometimes plant two or three small seed yams together in one mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ okwaafoi duɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ji dumɔwui lɛ? Dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛfee ekome yɛ ŋtayaa kome mli?

english: Small seed yams have limited energy stored inside them, so planting two or three together ensures the sprout gets enough combined strength to produce a strong vine and a good harvest.
ga: Hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo wain tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Is it better to plant small whole yams or cut a large yam into seed pieces?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmeii bibii ni eye emuu loo ooofolɔ ŋmeii wuji amli ni ofee dumɔwui?

english: Whole small yams are protected by their unbroken skin and resist rot better in dry soil, while cut pieces (minisetts) give you more seeds from one yam but need wood ash or treatment so they do not rot.
ga: Hewolo ni etseee lɛ buɔ sweet potato muu lɛ he ni eshiɔ fitemɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni afolɔ (mini sets) lɛ baaha dumɔwui krokomɛi aba fe ŋmeii kome lɛ, amɛbiɔ tso sũ loo tsofafeemɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: How can I check if a seed yam is in good condition before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli dani madu?

english: A good seed yam should feel firm to the touch, have intact skin with no soft spots or mold, and show healthy buds or 'eyes' near the top stem end ready to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa kɛji mɔ ko ta he. Eyɛ hewolo ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni ebɛ he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ŋmeii, ni eyɛ ŋmei loo ‘ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naagbee, ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃.

english: How does lifting and staking yam vines off the ground help the crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ sweet potato wain tsei ni ooowo nɔ ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves into full sunlight so the vine can produce more energy to feed the tuber underground, while also keeping leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbiɔ baai lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: What kind of soil do I need if I want my yams to grow smooth and shapely?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni o-sweet potato lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee fɛo lɛ, Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ he hiaa?

english: Yams grow best in deep, loose, well-drained sandy loam soil that allows the tuber to expand easily downward without hitches or excess water that causes rotting.
ga: Atomɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shishi oya ni amɛtsiii amɛhe loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa amɛgboi.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning yellow and drying up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early yellowing is usually caused by lack of soil nutrients, fungal leaf spot diseases, or drought stress, which stop the tuber from growing to its full potential size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mra. Fungal leaf spot hela loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ mli baa Enɛ haaa yitso lɛ adara kɛyashɛ egbɛfaŋ.

english: How can I store my harvested yams so they do not rot or shrink quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato koni amɛkafite loo amɛkagbɔjɔ oya?

english: Store yams off the ground in a shaded, well-ventilated traditional yam barn, tying them vertically on racks so cool air circulates around each tuber.
ga: Okɛ sweet potato ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ blema sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Akɛ amɛ fĩɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ adeka nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ abɔle ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he.

english: Why do yam prices go up so much a few months after the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato jara yaa hiɛ waa yɛ nyɔji fioo ni nyiɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During harvest, the market is flooded with yams so prices drop, but as months pass, supply decreases because many stored yams rot or sprout, making remaining fresh yams far more valuable.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ Jarayelihe lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, no hewɔ lɛ jara baa shi. Shi beni nyɔji lɛ hoɔ lɛ, Nibii ni Akɛhaa lɛ hu eba shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni ato lɛ egbo loo ekwɛ̃. Ehaa yams hee ni eshwɛ lɛ he hiaa waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha eŋɔli lɛ su lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds like I used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding, while making weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or water stress, which prevents proper pollination. Watering consistently and keeping the soil moist helps the plant hold onto its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and showing yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this and protect your yield.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ otsi oŋmɔshi nibii anaa ni obu he.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ Mi tso shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sunlight, stops water from evaporating quickly, keeps plant roots cool, and enriches the soil as it decomposes.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the growing center of the maize. Applying approved treatments or neem extracts early prevents the pest from destroying the plant before it produces corn.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ dani amɛwo ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same spot where I planted tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni midu tomato yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Pepper and tomato belong to the same plant family and share the same diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot year after year lets pests build up in the soil, so rotating with crops like cowpeas keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the roots expand beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to grow stronger, resist local diseases better, and yield significantly more grain than saved seeds, which lose their strength and vigor over repeated plantings.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara waa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ dumɔwui babaoo baa fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ afite kɛjɛ dumɔ ekoŋŋ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a cool shelter and retains soil moisture until the cocoa roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my oil palm trees turn yellow and dry up before the rest of the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani baai krokomɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Bottom leaves turning yellow usually means the palm tree is lacking potassium or nitrogen in the soil, forcing the plant to pull food away from old leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli koni eye ebua shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make leaves grow, or that heavy rain has logged the soil and choked the roots from taking up food.
ga: Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye niyenii.

english: Why should I add dried animal manure to my farm when chemical fertilizer works much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi afata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ? Be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kwraa?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the crop immediately for one season, but animal manure improves the soil structure like a sponge, helping it hold onto water and natural nutrients over many years.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be kome. Shi kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil space, and water, resulting in thin stems and very small tubers instead of a big harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ ŋmaa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: How do I choose the right part of a cassava stem to plant for a good shoot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni madu koni ewo ŋmeii kpakpai?

english: The middle portion of a mature, healthy cassava stem works best because the soft top rots easily in the dirt, and the bottom base stem takes too long to sprout new buds.
ga: Kasava tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot of my young corn plants and chewing the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ amli ni amɛmiiye baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the tender funnel leaf of young maize to feed on the soft tissue while staying safe from sunshine and chemical sprays.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ni ji ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, which cripples the leaves and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food, while also keeping leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases from spoiling the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbiɔ baai lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no insects or wind around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains around them protects the young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɔ. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer or when water stays stagnant around the roots for too long. Feeding the soil with nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can grow heavy ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo kɛ́ nu lɛ ehi shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada waa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to remain healthy. When heavy rains cause waterlogging, air cannot reach the underground tubers, which leads to fungal infections and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. The plant discards the blossoms to save water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny sucking pests like whiteflies or mites feeding under the leaves and transmitting viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the plant foliage flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce large tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground toward the sun and prevents soil-borne diseases from spreading to the leaves through damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo bulbs agboi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest them, that stored food remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to dry up much faster during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gĩɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal soil moisture and plant nutrients faster than your main crop can. Removing weeds keeps the available groundwater strictly for your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Why should I choose plantain suckers with narrow leaves instead of wide leaves when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala banana tsei ni baai lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ́ midu?

english: Suckers with narrow, needle-like leaves have strong underground energy reserves to build new roots. Suckers with wide leaves lose too much water through evaporation and struggle to survive transplanting.
ga: Suckers ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shishifãi heei anɔ. Suckers ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. ni esa akɛ ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi kɛ́ ajie lɛ awo mli

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry and there is no rain expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni nugbɔ enɛko lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only drink fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil leaves the chemicals concentrated near the roots, which can scorch and destroy the plant.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afee ekome yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients needed to make the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen naturally out of the air and trap it in their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. The plant automatically shifts its limited nitrogen to the younger leaves at the top to survive, causing the older leaves at the bottom to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni faaa lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow very large leaves but refuse to form a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai wuji waa shi ekpooɔ akɛ ebaafee yitsei ni yɔɔ kokroo ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or experience extreme heat. Excess nitrogen encourages the plant to put all its energy into leafy stem growth rather than wrapping its leaves tightly together into a head.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ ajie eyitso kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ baai lɛ abɔ he shiŋŋ ni efee yitso

english: Tomato flowers fall off when air temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences sudden drought stress. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed flowers to save its water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do some of my watermelon flowers die off without producing any watermelons at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ ni amɛwooo watermelon ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants produce separate male and female flowers. Male flowers open first to attract bees and fall off naturally after releasing pollen; only female flowers—which have a tiny mini-fruit at their base—will turn into watermelons after bees pollinate them.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi hii fɔ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛgbala wuobii ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni amɛjie pollen lɛ sɛɛ. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ yɔɔ ni woɔ yibii bibii. Yɛ shishigbɛ pɛ ji he ni etsakeɔ efeɔ watermelon beni ŋmeii efolɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants stop bringing out new flowers after I pick the first few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi beni mikpa klɛŋklɛŋ shii fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Okra stops producing fresh flowers if old pods are left to get too big and hard on the stalk. The plant assumes its life cycle is complete and directs energy into seed production rather than making new flowers.
ga: Roselle baakpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ kɛji akɛ ashi fɔfɔi momoi ni dara tsɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ buɔ eshihilɛ be lɛ akɛ egbe naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui afeemɔ he nii moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi heei.

english: What happens to my pepper crops if I plant the seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely forces pepper plants to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stems that easily break, poor airflow that invites diseases, and far fewer peppers per plant.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fãa oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni kɛ helai srɔtoi baa Ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ tso kome mli.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunlight on as many leaves as possible to build large tubers underground. Staking keeps the foliage off damp soil to prevent leaf rot and exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni amɛkafite, ni ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo.

english: Cassava drops leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick to prevent water loss through leaf evaporation. The plant stays alive underground and rapidly sprouts new leaves once rainy weather returns.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo gbɛ koni nu akafite yɛ baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Tsei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛwoɔ baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do groundnut pods sometimes turn out empty with no nuts inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells happen when there is a lack of calcium in the topsoil while pods are expanding. Groundnut pods absorb calcium directly from the dirt around them to form the solid seed inside.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni pod lɛ miigbɛ eshwa lɛ. Peanut ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ muji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. koni ekɛfee dumɔwui ni wa yɛ mli

english: How does growing vegetables inside a protected greenhouse change the way crops grow compared to an open field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni tsei lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ni mli tse he?

english: A greenhouse controls rainfall, wind, and pests while maintaining steady heat and moisture. This shelter allows crops like tomatoes or sweet peppers to grow continuously, produce higher yields, and avoid common outdoor diseases.
ga: Greenhouses kudɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa. Nɛkɛ shĩa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato loo ŋmei. Yaa nɔ eda Ha nibii ni anáa lɛ babaoo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for plant growth. Applying well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the healthy green color and improves plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni eha eŋɔli su ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because their delicate leaves burn easily in full direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or keeping some large forest trees provides living cover and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo koo mli tsei wuji ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ wala ato ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy, soggy soil for long periods. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra rainfall to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun. When yam leaves get plenty of sunlight, the plant manufactures more food, which results in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ he. Kɛji sweet potato baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo aba. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-cereal ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This natural process fertilizes the soil and helps nearby crops like maize or sorghum grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele loo ŋmãa, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plants do not receive consistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the plants helps protect the blossoms so they can produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo tomato.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that transmit leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these insects early using insecticidal soaps or neem oil prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ hela ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect the way my crops grow?
ga: Te Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind rapidly pulls moisture out of both plant leaves and the topsoil, causing crops to dry out quickly. Mulching crop beds with dry grass or leaves helps trap soil moisture during these dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ oya. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii gĩɔ oya Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nɛkɛ hulutsoo bei nɛɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just planting the grain I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests and diseases while producing high yields. Saved hybrid seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests and lower crop quality.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Young crops have short roots and small leaves, making them weak competitors against fast-growing weeds for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks ensures your crops get all the food they need to start strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛha jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nu ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually right after weeding early in the rainy season. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots, while applying it right before heavy rains can cause it to wash away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Shi kɛ́ okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, strong sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Retaining selected tall trees or planting fast-growing plantains provides the essential shade and cool air cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ baaha aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ mli kookoo he miihia waa koni anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes completely dry while the plant is flowering. Providing regular water and light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ lɛ. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛtsɔmɔ tomatoi.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight for soil food, water, and sunlight. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with very small tubers underground instead of yielding big, heavy cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmei tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa. Yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii najiaŋ

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to make food efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases while allowing the plant to develop larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛhoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ a-funnels lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on tender young maize leaves inside the central shoot. Catching them early and treating them with suitable organic or recommended chemical sprays prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my harvest yields even if I make sure my crops get enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients, light, and root space. Even with plenty of water, weeds deprive your crops of the essential food needed to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Kɛ nu babaoo po yɛ mli lɛ, Jwɛi hu jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa bo koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my main crops help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, feeding neighbor crops like maize or cassava without requiring as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ babaoo tsuuu nii

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain plant, they all compete for the same food and water, leading to small bunches. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems that produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛshiɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome he akaŋ. kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei bibioo Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha plantain tso agbo ni tsii aba.

english: Officer, why do the leaves on my young seedlings dry up and burn during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛmiishã yɛ nɛkɛ shwane ni mli edɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plant leaves burn easily under strong sun heat. Keeping the soil moist and providing light shade or cover prevents intense heat from scorching tender leaves before the plant develops strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo loo he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa koni ekashã baai bibii lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around the base of their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) protects plant roots from extreme sun heat, keeps moisture trapped in the soil, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it difficult for my maize seeds to grow up when the farm soil is hard and packed down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa akɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need soft, loose soil so air can circulate and the young shoots can easily push upward and rise out of the ground to reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya ni amɛte shi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛyamɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: How does mixing compost or animal manure into my land help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Manure makes heavy soil lighter and softer, which helps the ground hold water better, allows plant roots to breathe, and feeds the crop steadily as it grows.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ blɛoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ muɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer placed directly against stems can burn or 'scorch' the plant tissues and roots, leading to yellow leaves, damaged stems, or plant death.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo ‘ashã’ tso lɛ fãji kɛ shishifãi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, loo tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Can using the wrong weedkillers in my farm cause long-term problems for my soil?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, using improper or harsh chemicals can leave bad residues in the soil, damaging young crop roots and killing beneficial organisms that keep your soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni esaaa loo ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashi nibii gbohii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. efiteɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Officer, how deep should I bury my seeds when planting during the dry season?
ga: Nitsulɔi Te esa akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ha tɛŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds slightly deeper during dry weather protects them from the scorching heat near the soil surface and helps them reach deeper moisture to sprout safely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mli fioo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni mli kwɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are too close, they compete with each other for heat, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin plants that give very low yield.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ dɔlɛ, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa baa.

english: Why are extension officers encouraging us to try new farming techniques instead of only using old methods from back in the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔka okwaayeli gbɛ̀i heei wɔkwɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ gbɛi momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: New farming techniques are designed to handle changing weather conditions, improve soil health, and prevent crop damage, helping you get a larger harvest from your land.
ga: Afee okwaayeli he ŋaai heei koni akɛkpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What key signs should I look out for on my farm to know if my crops are developing problems?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii titri esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ?

english: Regularly check your crops for yellowing leaves, dark leaf spots, pest holes, or wilting. Spotting these signs early lets you treat diseases or water problems before the whole crop fails.
ga: Kwɛmɔ onibii amli daa kɛha baai ŋmɔŋ, baai ni tsuɔ, kooloi awuiyelɔi bu, loo ŋmɔtɔ. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa helai loo nu he naagbai dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though the rains are falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, or fall armyworms are feeding on the young leaves and taking away their nutrients. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or treating early for pests will help bring back the green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo fall armyworms lɛ miiye baai bibii ni amɛmiiye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off during the dry season, and does it mean my crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive the heat. The crop is not dead; the roots underground stay healthy and will sprout new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nibii ni adu lɛ gboko lolo. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when there is too much or too little water, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding compost helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni nu babaoo loo fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical medicine on my crops during the middle of the day when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ wɔkɛ tsofai shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Spraying under strong midday sun causes the chemical medicine to evaporate into the air before the plant absorbs it, and the heat combined with the chemical can burn your crop's leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni dɔlɛ ni akɛ tsofai lɛ fataa he lɛ baanyɛ ashã otso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if an insect on my plant is damaging my crop or helping it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifite loo amɛmiiye mibua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Harmful pests actively chew holes in leaves, bore into stems, or make leaves curl up by sucking sap. Beneficial insects, like ladybugs and spiders, hunt those bad pests and do not chew on your crops.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ baai amli, amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi, loo amɛhaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ. Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ladybugs kɛ spiders Taoɔ nakai kooloi fɔji lɛ. Ni kaaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. The crowded branches also trap moisture, which encourages black pod disease to spread quickly.
ga: Kɛji adu cocoa ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Niji ni mli tse lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow long and thin with very few leaves when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Vegetables like peppers and tomatoes need direct sunlight to grow strong and bushy. Under dense trees, they stretch upward searching for light, making them tall, weak, and poor at bearing fruit.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi lɛ, amɛkpã amɛhe kɛmiitao la. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛfɔɔɔ yibii wooo.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that travels in water droplets. Raindrops splash the fungus spores from the soil onto lower pods, and the high humidity helps the disease spread rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nyiɛɔ nu mli ŋmɔtɔi amli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to absorb rainwater and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and water from your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly in storage after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ mli beni mifo mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot in storage if their skin gets cut or bruised by farm tools during harvest. Fungi and bacteria enter through these small wounds, especially if stored in warm, damp, or unventilated places.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ okwaayeli nibii shwie amɛhewolo nɔ loo atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Fungi kɛ bacteria boteɔ pilamɔi bibii nɛɛ amli, titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, loo he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer (like urea) will help bring the green color and healthy growth back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ urea) fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are these small green caterpillars eating holes inside the tops of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli nɛɛ ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the center leaves (the funnel) of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended organic neem oil or approved insecticides will save your crop yields.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai (funnels) lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni kɛ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it important for me to leave big shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees prefer partial shade, especially when young, because intense full sun burns the leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Shade trees protect cocoa from excessive heat, maintain soil moisture, and shield them from heavy wind damage.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ eji gbekɛbii Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa sũ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baafite lɛ naa

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small fruits when too many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: Those side shoots are called suckers, and they steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. You should prune away extra suckers, leaving only 2 or 3 strong ones, so the main tree has enough energy to grow big fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ afã tsei nɛɛ akɛ suckers ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni oshi ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni eha tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots under the ground are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. You can carefully dig around one plant to check if the tubers are thick and firm before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Akwɛ tso kome mli jogbaŋŋ koni ana kɛji ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi kɛ ŋmeii dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose as many leaves to sunlight as possible. More sunlight helps the leaves make food, which flows down to grow large, healthy yam tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛha hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Efoɔ kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and uneven water supply while the fruit is growing. Watering your tomatoes regularly and adding wood ash or calcium to the soil prevents these spots from forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ kɛ nu ni falɛ ni ejaaa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo calcium wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaa.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough regular water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha tso lɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (called mulching) acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from drying out the ground. It keeps the soil cool, retains water longer, and stops weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi ni egbi Mulching (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait until the rains settle properly before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: If you plant after just one early rain, the soil might dry up quickly during a dry spell, causing your seeds to die after sprouting. Waiting for the major rainy season to settle ensures there is consistent soil moisture for the seeds to grow safely into strong plants.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ mɛmɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa koni dumɔwui lɛ adara shweshweeshwe ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are yellowing because of a nutrient shortage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: When crops lack key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, they cannot produce green chlorophyll properly, causing older bottom leaves to turn yellow while upper leaves remain green. Applying the right soil fertilizer provides the food plants need to regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua niyenii tsei ni amɛná su ni mli kwɔ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why shouldn't I dump chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against a plant stem can burn the tender plant tissues and damage the roots. Fertilizer should be buried in the soil a few centimeters away from the plant stem so the roots can safely reach out and feed on it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo ni aye amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it best to put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry or after rain?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil so plant roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, but not during heavy downpours which can wash the fertilizer away from your farm.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know which chemical spray is right for killing weeds without harming my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni efiteee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Weedkillers are split into non-selective chemicals that kill all plants and selective chemicals designed for specific crop types like maize or cassava. Using a selective herbicide formulated for your specific crop ensures only the weeds die while your crop stays healthy.
ga: Ajara tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ amli awo tsofai ni halaaa ni gbeɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ tsofai ni halaa ni afee aha tso pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Kɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa jwɛi pɛ gboɔ yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects keep attacking my vegetables even after I spray them with pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa mi aduawai lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ.

english: Pesticides only work well if applied at the correct dose, at the right time of day, and targeted at the specific pest damaging your crop. If you use the wrong chemical or spray in mid-day sun when pests are hiding, the chemical can evaporate without killing the insects.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli. yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni sa mli ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ kooloi pɔtɛɛ ni miifite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii Yɛ hulutsoo be mli he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. Tsofai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ la ni egbeee kooloi lɛ.

english: Can I mix two different crop chemicals together in my knapsack sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ afutu yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Combining different agricultural chemicals without professional advice can cause them to react, neutralizing their effectiveness or creating a mixture that burns your crops. Always apply chemicals separately unless the manufacturer labels explicitly state they can be safely mixed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai srɔtoi fata he ni ŋaawoo ni he esa bɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛfee nɔ ko. Neutralize efficiency Aloo afee nɔ ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsofai atsu nii srɔtoi. Ja mɔ ni fee lɛ wolo lɛ tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaafutu.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and weak instead of producing thick stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ?
